english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and the plants remain short and thin. Adding organic manure or appropriate fertilizers restores essential nutrients like nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shi kuku ni amɛbaafee mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes competition among the crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow strong roots and yield larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa tsei ateŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly when the Harmattan weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds bring dry, hot air that evaporates moisture quickly from both the soil and leaf surfaces. Placing dry leaves or grass as mulch around the base of your plants helps retain soil moisture during this season.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture deep into the root zone before the hot sun causes evaporation, keeping the plants cool and hydrated through the warmest parts of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow cassava together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving space, water, and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ŋmɛɔ gbɛ koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ atsɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and suckers from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage, allowing it to direct its water and nutrients into producing bigger flowers and healthier fruits.
ga: Kpojiemɔ kroko ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa fɔfɔii wuji kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Flowers fall when plants suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees needed to transfer pollen so the fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya koni aduawai aba lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do tiny green insects cluster under my plant leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiiha amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: These are pests like aphids that suck vital sap from the undersides of leaves, causing them to curl and stunt plant growth until treated with appropriate pest controls.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do some tree crops require so much soil moisture compared to smaller vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo fe aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Large trees have broad leaves that release a lot of water vapor into the air throughout the day. To replace this lost water and stay healthy, the tree's roots must constantly pull up large amounts of water from deep in the soil.
ga: Tsei wuji yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni jieɔ nu lasu babaoo kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Koni akɛto nu ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ ni aná hewalɛ kpakpa. Esa akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ agbala nu babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Is watering my trees regularly enough to guarantee a healthy crop yield?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ daa lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba?

english: No, watering alone is not enough. You must continuously inspect the trunk and leaves for pest infestations, diseases, and nutrient shortages, as water cannot protect a crop from insect damage.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Esa akɛ okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu nyɛŋ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: How do I know if pests are damaging the inside of my tree trunks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifite mitso lɛ mli?

english: Look for small holes in the bark, saw-dust-like powder at the base of the tree, or branches that suddenly wilt. These are clear signs that stem-boring insects have chewed their way inside the trunk.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ sũ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. loo tso nine ni gboɔ trukaa Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ efo tso lɛ mli.

english: What steps can I take to stop insects from boring holes into my farm crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni kooloi akafo bu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Keep the area around the crop clean, prune dead or weak branches where pests like to hide, and apply recommended protective trunk washes or natural pest deterrents to keep boring insects away.
ga: Ha he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he atse, ni ofolɔ niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtee lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ stem cleaner loo adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why are my tree leaves wilting even when the soil around the farm is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Leaves often wilt despite wet soil if stem-boring insects or root diseases have damaged the inner vessels of the plant, preventing water from traveling up from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo shishifãi ahe helai efite tso lɛ mli tsɛnsi lɛ, Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important for tree crops to develop deep root systems after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Deep roots anchor the tree firmly in the ground to protect it from strong winds, while also allowing the crop to reach moisture deep underground during dry periods.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a newly transplanted crop seedling has successfully established its roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: A seedling is well-established when it starts growing fresh green leaves and stem shoots, showing that its roots are taking deep root and absorbing nutrients from the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛbɔi baai kɛ tsei eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between trees when planting my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni da yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots and branches spread out wide as they grow. Giving them space prevents trees from fighting each other for soil nutrients, sunlight, and underground water.
ga: Tso shishifãi kɛ eniji gbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he akaŋshii.

english: How does a crop with a wide branch spread help protect my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni amɛniji lɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: A wide leaf canopy creates shade over the land, which keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and protects the soil surface from heavy rainfall erosion.
ga: Kpoji lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Do mature tree crops with deep roots still need regular inspection by the farmer?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni okwaafoi akwɛ tsei ni edara ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ amli lolo?

english: Yes, mature trees still need regular monitoring because insects can bore into older wood and diseases can build up quietly, which can kill a mature tree if left unchecked.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei ni edara lɛ amli lolo daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii baanyɛ atsɔ tsei momo amli ni helai baanyɛ aba dioo. Enɛ baanyɛ agbe tsei ni eda lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an important food it needs to grow strong, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings grow better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo kookoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller crops like plantains create shade, keep the ground cool, and hold moisture in the soil for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil, resulting in thin stalks and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer, which causes the plant to protect itself instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ ehe nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing thin and woody instead of big and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, well-drained soil to expand easily; if the land is hard or too compacted, the roots cannot swell properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kwraa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's fluids, damaging leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai lɛ adalɛ awui

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil food, but cowpeas and groundnuts put natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ babaoo aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up, so the plant wilts temporarily to conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main stem, so removing them leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii nɛɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than most crops, so they drink up the water and eat the soil nutrients before your main crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground so they catch full sunlight and stay safe from soil fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye niyenii. Staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aha ni ebu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding manure or NPK fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients needed to turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Under strong sunshine, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its leaf pores and preserve water, usually recovering once the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛgbala baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the branches and leaves are growing very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe tseee nɛkɛ be mli ni eniji kɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives heavy rains early on, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa mra. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when they lack water, nutrients, or shade, allowing the tree to save its energy for the pods it can successfully feed.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii loo hulutsoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant drops flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and open instead of forming a hard, round ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ bɔɔlu kokroo ni wa?

english: Cabbages need consistent water and proper spacing to form tight heads. If they are crowded or face irregular watering, the leaves grow loose instead of wrapping tightly around the center core.
ga: Nu he miihia cabbage daa ni akɛto he jogbaŋŋ koni cabbage yitsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji gbɔmɛi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ, Baai lɛ etse amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔle ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunch is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots carrying a very heavy top load. Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes can damage these roots, making the plant unstable until strong winds push it over if it isn't supported with a prop stick.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni jatsu ni tsii yɔɔ amɛmli. Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ damɔɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswaa kɛhoɔ ehe kɛji akɛ tso ko fiii shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep producing pods at different times instead of ripening all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ shikome lɛ?

english: Many local cowpea varieties keep growing, flowering, and making new pods continuously as long as rains continue. This allows farmers to harvest food over several weeks rather than all in a single day.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsina ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo yaa nɔ amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa niyenii yɛ otsii babaoo mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ

english: People in my village say the February dry season always kills cocoa trees. Is that true?
ga: Mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ February mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ gbeɔ kookoo tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be. Ani eji anɔkwale?

english: That is not entirely true. While the February dry season is very harsh, cocoa trees that receive some rainfall or proper care beforehand can survive the heat without dying.
ga: No jeee anɔkwale kwraa. Eyɛ mli akɛ fɛ̃i be ni baa yɛ February mli lɛ mli wa waa moŋ. Shi cacao tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa loo akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo.

english: If a little rain falls right before the dry season starts, will it really help my cocoa trees survive?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua kookoo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: Yes, even a small amount of rain reaches the tree roots and provides essential moisture, making the cocoa strong enough to withstand the upcoming dry spell.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ fioo po shɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ edaaa hɔmɔ ni miiba lɛ naa.

english: Why is the month of February usually so dangerous for cocoa farms in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ February ji oshara kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: February is typically the peak of the dry season when weather conditions are hot and dry, making it easy for unprotected or unwatered cocoa trees to suffer from heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, February ji be ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Kookoo tsei ni abuuu amɛhe loo awoɔ amɛ nu lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa dɔlɛ he haomɔ waa.

english: Does rain water actually reach deep enough into the soil to protect my cocoa trees during a drought?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ koni ebu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Yes, when rain falls, water sinks into the soil where the root system absorbs it, storing up energy that helps the tree endure dry periods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ. Etoɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdamɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ bei anaa.

english: Is it better to treat my cocoa farm before the dry season starts or wait until the heat hits?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi loo ooomɛ kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ?

english: It is best to take protective measures before the dry season arrives so your trees stay strong and resilient before the heat causes serious harm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hela naa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba koni otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi amɛhe dani latsaa lɛ kɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I do not give them any treatment before the dry weather arrives?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba?

english: If you do not take preventive steps or manage your farm properly, the strong dry weather can cause leaf loss, lower your harvest, or even damage the trees beyond recovery.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuuu nii loo okwɛɛɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Shihilɛ ni mli egbi waa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afite, eha yibiiwoo aba shi, loo efite tso lɛ po aahu akɛ enyɛŋ ehi shi.

english: Why do some farms survive severe dry weather while neighboring farms in the same village die off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni yɔɔ akrowa kome mli lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Farms survive when farmers apply recommended practices and preventive treatments early, while farms left without care suffer heavy damage from the sun.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛji okwaafoi lɛ nyiɛ nifeemɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛ tsamɔi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ asɛɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni ashi amɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ ko lɛ, hulu lɛ fiteɔ amɛ waa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are starting to have a problem from dry weather before it is too late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ dani eshɛɔ sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: Look out for early signs like drooping leaves, yellowing foliage, or premature leaf fall; noticing these early allows you to get help before the trees dry out completely.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ni gbeeɔ shi, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo baai ni laajeɔ oya. Nibii nɛɛ akadimɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná yelikɛbuamɔ dani tsei lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: When should I contact an extension officer to help me with my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ extension nitsulɔ ko abɔ koni eye ebua mi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should reach out as soon as you notice early signs of trouble or when preparing your farm for severe weather changes, rather than waiting until the trees are dying.
ga: Esa akɛ oyana amɛ pɛ kɛji ona naagba ko he okadi mra loo beni osaa oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tso lɛ agbo

english: If my neighbor's cocoa farm is suffering from the dry season, can the same treatment used on my farm help him?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai kpe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Ani tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ?

english: Yes, standard preventive techniques and proper field treatments taught by extension officers work across cocoa farms to protect trees from harsh weather conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsamɔi ni sa ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkɛbu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry when the sun is very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under hot direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving bigger trees gives them the protection and cooler environment they need to survive and grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛma shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hebuu kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves green and produces bigger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua baabii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped in the soil because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and hiding inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli ni akɛtee tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn plants. Checking your farm early and applying neem water or approved pest treatments directly into the leaf funnel will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baawo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Giving your plants regular water and covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food before your crops can get them. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting gives your main crops a strong start without any competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii titri lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ he.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on all their leaves to feed the tuber growing underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and stay safe from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni eye ebua amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Fertilizer works best when crops are actively growing and the soil is slightly moist. Applying a small amount a couple of weeks after sprouts appear, and again around flowering, ensures the plant uses the food when it needs it most.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Okɛtsu nii fioo fioo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas together with maize helps the soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsina ŋmãa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that pull natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. This feeds both the cowpeas and the nearby maize, keeping your soil healthy for longer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize seeds so small insects do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi bibii akafite amɛ?

english: Insects multiply quickly in moist grain, so drying your maize under the sun until the seeds are very hard is the most important step. Storing dry seeds in airtight bags or clean sealed containers keeps insects out and prevents mold.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ oya yɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo fɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ni ooogbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ mli wa waa lɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku mli loo nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I plant to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ madu koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: The middle part of a mature, healthy cassava stem works best. The top tip is too young and rots easily, while the bottom base is too old and hard to sprout fast.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã, he ni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ naagbee lɛ ji gbekɛ tsɔ lolo ni egboɔ oya. Shishigbɛ shishigbɛ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ewa akɛ ebaada oya.

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these have narrow, sword-like leaves and a large bulb at the base. They grow faster and produce stronger bunches than suckers with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ bulb agbo ko yɛ shishigbɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛmli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. When vines spread on the hot ground, leaves overlap, get shaded, and are exposed to soil diseases, resulting in smaller yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Beni wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ, ni ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ekɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip and moving down the central vein mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Kaadi ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni etsɔɔ teŋgbɛ line lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop harvested, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum baatswa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertilizer down into deep soil or off the field entirely before crop roots can drink it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after rain, not right before heavy rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ kwraa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Jeee dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out quickly. They require plantain trees or temporary shade crops to shelter them during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites living under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or a recommended insect spray stops these pests and helps new leaves grow normal again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi fɔji nɛɛ anaa, ni ebaaha baai heei akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot, when plants don't get enough water, or when too much chemical fertilizer makes the plant grow stems instead of fruit. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizer keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better if I weed early instead of waiting for weeds to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛji mijie jwɛi mra yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with young crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds when they are small lets the crop get all the nourishment early on when it needs it most to grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ amɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ mra. Be ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my crops fail to grow well even though people say any land in Ghana is good for farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli moŋ?

english: Not all land has the same health. Soil quality varies across Ghana depending on past farming practices, erosion, and nutrient levels. Soil needs specific nutrients and organic matter to support healthy crops, so depleted land will produce poor yields until it is restored.
ga: Jeee shikpɔji fɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ srɔtoi yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Edamɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni eho, shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii aba kɛyashi be mli ni abaanyɛ asaa amɛ.

english: Maize requires rich soil with plenty of water and nutrients to thrive, while cassava is a resilient crop that can survive and give decent yields even in sandy or low-nutrient soil where maize would fail.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ po nɔ, he ni ŋmei baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crop yields every year when I plant the exact same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil every season. Rotating different crop types gives the soil time to recover and prevents pests and diseases from building up.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa ŋmeii kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn light yellow while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen or that water is logging the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color to feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli loo nu miibote shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni anyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani etsɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed, usually due to extreme midday heat, lack of soil moisture, or an imbalance of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛ enɛ baa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ejaaa

english: Why do my sweet potatoes grow a lot of thick green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the crop uses all its energy to grow lush foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In high heat, tomato leaves evaporate water faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps the root area cool and conserves soil moisture.
ga: kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Organic mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They require partial shade from nurse plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without making fruits when I plant them close to large forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii beni midu yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward searching for light when shaded by large trees, spending all their energy on height rather than building thick stems, strong roots, or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ashishi. Okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni oootswa tsei ni mli tse. Shishifãi loo aduawai ni mli wa

english: Why do my grain crops grow better when I plant beans or cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special root structures that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why are market buyers rejecting my produce even when some of my crops look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kpooɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: When a disease spreads through a farm, even crops that look clean on the outside can carry hidden infections or spoil very quickly during transport, causing buyers to reject the entire batch to protect their business.
ga: Beni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Nibii ni adu ni tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ po baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛfite oya beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Ha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo nibii fɛɛ ni amɛheɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ nitsumɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it hard to sell my cocoa beans when there is a plant disease outbreak in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ kookoo yibii lɛ? Be mli ni tsei ahe hela ko baa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: During disease outbreaks, buyers and exporters become extra strict because infected pods produce poor quality beans that fail international trade standards.
ga: Yɛ hela ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ mli wa titri. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni baa shi ni kɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli he mlai kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my crops stop bearing fruit after their leaves start turning yellow and wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa yibiiwoo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves act like food factories for your plants. When sickness damages the leaves, the plant loses its energy to make food, causing it to drop its flowers and stop producing fruits.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he kɛha otso lɛ. Kɛ hela kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why does my harvested crop rot so quickly before I can get it to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: If your plants contract diseases while growing in the field, micro-organisms continue to multiply inside the harvested produce, causing fast decay once the crop is picked.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ ná hela be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Microorganisms lɛ baaya nɔ amɛfa babaoo yɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto.

english: How can a plant disease ruin the whole harvest on a farm that usually produces high yields?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko afite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Aggressive crop diseases move quickly through healthy plants. Once inside the plant's system, the disease blocks nutrients and water, killing both young shoots and mature produce before harvest.
ga: Tsei ahe helai ni naa wa lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya. Kɛji akɛ ebote tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ Hela tsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu naa. Gbemɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fɛɛ dani okpa.

english: Why do even my best-fertilized crops get sick when a disease hits our farming community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ po yeɔ hela kɛ́ hela ba wɔ okwaayeli akutso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer helps crops grow strong, but it cannot make them immune to contagious plant viruses or fungi, just like good food alone cannot stop a human from catching a flu.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa waa. Shi enyɛŋ eha gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anyɛ atsu nii. Tamɔ niyenii kpakpa pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsĩ adesai anaa koni amɛkaná flufla.

english: Can diseases spread from my neighbor's farm onto my field?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plant sicknesses travel easily between nearby farms through the wind, flying insects, shared farm tools, or rainwater running from one field to another.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo. koolooi ni foɔ kɛ okwaayeli nibii loo nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli

english: What should I do immediately if I notice some plants on my farm are getting sick?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: You should carefully remove and destroy the infected plants away from your field so the sickness does not spread to the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are catching a disease before my whole farm gets damaged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emɔ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ afite?

english: Look out for early warning signs such as unusual spots on leaves, stunted growth, sudden leaf dropping, or stems wilting during cool mornings.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ hei ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ baai anɔ. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ trukaa baai ni gbeeɔ shi Aloo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gboɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli.

english: Can I plant new crops right away in a field where my previous crops died from a sickness?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hela gboi yɛ mishishijee tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli?

english: No, planting immediately is risky because disease germs can live on in the soil or old roots and will quickly attack your new young seedlings.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, oshara yɛ he ejaakɛ helai baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi momo lɛ amli. ni ebaatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting nurse crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa trees can survive their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains ni akwɛɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are running out of nitrogen, which is a key food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the crops are still growing helps keep the leaves green and boosts yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil base around the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko edara kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shishitoo lɛ Tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist continuously and planting during cooler periods helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly after I put them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast when exposed to too much moisture, heat, or direct sunlight. Storing them on raised racks in a shaded barn with plenty of moving air keeps them dry and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, dɔlɛ, loo hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Too he gbɛjianɔ yɛ shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa egbiɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying with organic pest sprays or soapy water early on helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Akɛ organic insect spray loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the topsoil before the crop roots can drink it in, wasting your money and leaving the crop hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I cut and plant to get a heavy bunch?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei lɛ esa akɛ afo ni adu koni amɛná ŋmeii ni tsii?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong base—grow faster and produce bigger, healthier plantain bunches than water suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Klante tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi, kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa. Edaa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas in the same farm as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil naturally. This helps fertilize your maize crop for free while protecting the ground from weeds.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni o-abele lɛ akafee nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot away during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather. Pruning heavy cocoa branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm reduces moisture and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ waa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: If the rains stop early in the season, can I water my yams myself to keep them growing?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli Ani manyɛ mawo mi-sweet potato lɛ nu koni ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, yams respond very well to extra water during dry spells. Giving them water when the rain stops keeps the plants active and allows the tubers underground to keep growing bigger.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes tsuɔ nu ni fa fe nine he nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Will watering my crops during a dry period actually increase my harvest, or is it a waste of effort?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo eji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ?

english: Watering during dry periods is very effective because crops are simply waiting for moisture to keep growing. Giving them water when there is no rain keeps them producing yield instead of staying dormant.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miimɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛkɛ koni eya nɔ eda. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya wɔɔ.

english: Is it better to give my crops a little bit of water every day or a lot of water once a week during dry times?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Giving a deep soaking once or twice a week is better because deep water reaches the deep roots of crops like yams, encouraging them to grow stronger than frequent, shallow watering would.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ wo mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu lɛ shɛɔ tsei shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ daa waa fe nu ni akɛhaa amɛ shii abɔ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster right after it rains compared to when I hand-water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ minine shwieɔ nu lɛ he?

english: Rainfall covers the entire field evenly, washes dust off the leaves, and cools the air. This allows the plants to take in water through both their leaves and roots, giving them an immediate growth boost.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsuɔ sũ he kɛjɛɔ baai ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi fɛɛ anɔ. Ha tsei akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How does good rainfall affect the size of my yam tubers underground?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainwater fuels the growth of the leaves above ground. Strong, healthy leaves use sunlight to produce food, which is then stored in the underground tubers, making the yams heavy and large.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa baai lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii ni efee agbo.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my yams right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early ensures young yam shoots take full advantage of the natural moisture in the soil, allowing the roots and vines to become strong before any mid-season dry spells happen.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi kɛ wain tsei lɛ dani hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines look weak and stopped in growth when it doesn't rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekpaa dalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, yam plants rest to conserve energy and survive the heat. They are not dead, but simply waiting for water so they can resume active growth.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Sweet potato tsei lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Amɛ gboko lolo. Shi mɛ kɛkɛ ni nu lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can my yams recover and grow again if they look yellow and dry during a mid-season drought?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni eda ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, yam plants are tough. As soon as you water them or rain falls again, the plant will revive, produce new green leaves, and continue growing its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato ji tsei ni wa. Kɛji okɛ nu shwie nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ. baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ kpo Ni eyitso lɛ tee nɔ eda.

english: How can I tell if my yam leaves are dry because of lack of rain or because it is harvest time?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ egbi yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ loo kpamɔ be ni eba lɛ hewɔ?

english: If leaves wilt during the middle of the growing season when it is hot and dry, the plant needs water. If leaves dry out naturally at the end of the season when the tuber is fully mature, it is simply ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gboi yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ji be ni mli edɔ kɛ be ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tsei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gĩ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee beni bulbs lɛ edara kwraa lɛ. Efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Does rainwater do something special for my yams that well water or tap water cannot do?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu feɔ nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko kɛhaa mi sweet potatoes lɛ ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo pɔmpi mli nu nyɛŋ afee?

english: Rainwater naturally contains small amounts of nitrogen from the air and is free of added chemicals or high salt levels, making it the cleanest and most natural food source for crop growth.
ga: Nitrogen fioo ko ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ nu mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsofai loo ŋoo ni fa babaoo bɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni he tse fe fɛɛ ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei daa.

english: Why is it important to prepare my land well before sowing soybean seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu soya dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation loosens the soil, making it easier for soybean roots to grow deep, absorb nutrients, and sprout evenly across your field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa soybean shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ mlɛo

english: How do I know the right time to sow my soybean crop during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu soybeans yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Sowing should happen right after the rains become steady so the seeds get enough moisture to germinate without drying out in early dry spells.
ga: Esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How close together should I plant my soybean seeds to get the best harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-soybean dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni maná yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Proper seed spacing prevents plants from competing with each other for sunlight, air, and soil water, leading to healthier crops and more pods.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: When is the right time to apply the first batch of fertilizer to my soybean field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mi soybean ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Applying your first fertilizer early, usually shortly after the seeds sprout, gives young plants the immediate boost they need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa mra Bei pii lɛ, beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Will my crop still yield well if I apply fertilizer but do not get enough rain?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shi nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve and reach the roots. Without adequate rain, plants cannot take up the nutrients, which limits overall growth.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ babaoo lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa dalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How much harvest can I realistically expect from one hectare of soybean farm?
ga: Nikpamɔ enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ soybean ŋmɔ hectare kome mli?

english: With good land preparation, timely fertilizer application, and adequate rainfall, you can target at least 3 metric tons of soybean per hectare.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Obaanyɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ̃ soybeans ni ji mɛtrik tɔn 3 nɔ yɛ hectare kome mli kɛ hoo lɛ.

english: What causes soybean pods to stay empty or produce very small beans?
ga: Mɛni haa soybean ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: Empty or small pods usually happen when plants lack water during flowering or when the soil lacks enough nutrients to feed the developing seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are some of my young soybean plants growing slowly compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida blɛoo kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Slow early growth often happens if the seeds were planted too deep, if the soil is too hard, or if the initial fertilizer was missed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee lɛ, daalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɛɛ ohe

english: How can using a mobile phone app help me manage my soybean farm better?
ga: Te mobile app ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ mi-soybean ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A farm app helps you track your exact field size, monitor key planting dates, and record input use so you can manage costs and timing efficiently.
ga: Fam app lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ gbii ni he hiaa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ. ni aŋmala nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ awo wolo nɔ Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okwɛ shika nɔ ni oto be he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure the exact size of my field before buying seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ he dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: Knowing your exact land size in hectares ensures you buy the correct quantity of seeds and fertilizer, saving money and avoiding wasted inputs.
ga: Kɛ́ ole oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ yɛ hectares mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohéɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, okɛ shika toɔ ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni afiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: When maize leaves roll up, the plant is trying to protect itself from losing water in the heat. It is a natural stress response showing that the crop needs moisture and is conserving what it has until the temperature drops.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli haomɔ hetoo ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbuɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ he kɛyashiɔ hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my pepper crop actually needs more water before I start irrigating?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo he miihia mi-pepper tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ dani mabɔi nu shwiemɔ?

english: Push your finger about two inches deep into the soil near the plant root. If the soil feels dry and crumbles away without sticking to your skin, the crop needs water; if it feels cool and sticks together, the plants still have enough moisture.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ egbi ni ekumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nu he miihia tsei. Kɛji enu he akɛ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough nitrogen from the soil, they move nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, causing those lower leaves to turn yellow and eventually fall off.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves when the dry weather sets in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be ba lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to stop water from evaporating through the foliage. This helps the crop save energy and preserve underground roots until reliable water returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow much better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering shade and keeping the air humid so the cocoa survives its early stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my bean plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or dry conditions during the flowering stage cause plants to panic and shed their blossoms to save energy, preventing them from holding onto and growing fruit pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ gbeyei ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakpɛtɛ aduawai ashishifãi ahe ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and weak with small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo awo bu kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they fight for the same water, light, and nutrients. They stretch upwards trying to reach light instead of using their strength to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does water stay on top of my soil for hours instead of sinking down to the roots when I water the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo kɛyashɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard or compacted soil forms a thick crust that blocks water from penetrating. Loosening the top layer of soil with a hoe helps water flow down deeper to reach the root zone where crops can drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋtayaa shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ anu nu yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes split open on the farm right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When plants take in a sudden large amount of water after being dry, the inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo trukaa beni amɛgbi lɛ sɛɛ Tomato loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are my cabbage seedlings leaning towards one side of the nursery bed instead of growing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ fã kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally bend towards the direction of the strongest sunlight to make food. If big trees or walls block light on one side, the crop will stretch sideways toward the open sky.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa he ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji tso agbo loo gbogbo ko tsi kane lɛ naa yɛ fa kome lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ afã kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni agbele naa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen nutrients or are sitting in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen helps plants produce green pigment to feed themselves, so applying urea or well-composted manure will restore their green color and help them grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkɛyeɔ amɛhe niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize, will they steal food from the main crop?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Ani amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa titrii lɛ amli?

english: No, legumes like cowpeas and beans actually feed the main crop because their roots pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, which enriches the ground and helps nearby plants grow better.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛji niyenii titri ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: I planted soybeans to sell for poultry feed, but why are the pods producing very tiny seeds?
ga: Miduɔ soybeans koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ akɛ kooloi aniyenii. Shi mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ?

english: Small seeds occur when soybean plants do not get enough water during the pod-filling stage or lack soil phosphorus. Giving plants sufficient water during flowering and adding phosphorus fertilizer at planting builds larger, fuller seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii baa kɛji soybean tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni awoɔ pod lɛ mli loo phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni okɛ fɔsfɔs wo mli beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛye emuu.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa mi lɛ?

english: Underground rotting happens when water stays around the roots for too long or when soil pests bite the tubers, allowing fungi to enter. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away and prevents root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɔ amɛyitsei. ni ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mli Ni aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What makes my cocoa trees drop all their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛnáa ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience sudden heat, prolonged dry spells, or attacks by sucking insects like mirids. Maintaining shade trees on your farm protects the cocoa blossoms from drying out.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ba trukaa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tutuamɔi kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ luster ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even though they look fresh in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ehee leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes leaves to lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it, making the plant droop temporarily. Adding dry grass or straw mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil moist and root zone cool.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do dark black spots spread across crop leaves whenever continuous heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash soil containing fungal spores onto wet leaves, and high moisture allows the fungus to grow rapidly into dark spots. Spacing plants well allows air to flow through and dry the leaves faster to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds just as the fruit bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli tamɔ aduawai ni edara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and pests like stem borers or root nematodes can destroy their root hold, making tall trees top-heavy. Propping the trees with sturdy wooden poles and controlling soil pests keeps them standing until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes baanyɛ afite shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Tsei ni akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ewo mli lɛ adumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by a plant virus carried by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Removing infected plants quickly and using sticky traps or proper sprays controls whiteflies and protects the healthy crops.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ tsɔnei ni sa ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye ŋmeii yɛji anɔ ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when I apply water and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, root space, water, and fertilizer intended for your plants. Clearing weeds during the first four weeks after planting gives your crop the upper hand to establish strong growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shweremɔ ni mli wa ni amɛbaafee lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and can burn easily. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way I point the cassava stem when I insert it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei wo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to bend upward to reach the light, which wastes energy and leads to lower tuber production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ baaha amɛkoto amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tuber ni afeɔ lɛ faaa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants build green leaves, so when it runs low, the plant moves what remains to its newest leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.
