english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil natural bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize used up.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi waa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heatwave or a short dry period. Sowing too early causes seeds to sprout and then die from lack of moisture before the rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight for photosynthesis, which provides the plant with energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe banee ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Small holes inside the central leaves of young maize are typical signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant. Early detection allows you to treat the whorls before the crop is severely damaged.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa he ko ni da dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, making the pollen sterile so the flowers cannot be fertilized. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Ehaa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔ. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I break down and grind hard soil clods before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ mli ni mafolɔ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Breaking hard soil into fine pieces makes it easier for delicate young roots to push through, search for water, and absorb nutrients. It also helps seeds get uniform contact with moist soil so they sprout evenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli bibii bibii Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ abote mli, amɛna nu, ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpaa gbee po bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build strong green leaves. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop most of its leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmatha be lɛ mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally when water is scarce to prevent moisture from escaping through the foliage. The plant goes into a resting state while keeping its tubers safe underground until the rains return.
ga: Yucca baajie ebaai lɛ ashwie shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by heat stress. These pests feed on the leaves and can spread viruses that disrupt the plant's normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa bɔ ni sa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not hold deeply into the ground. When a heavy bunch grows, top-heaviness pulls the stem down, which is why farmers use wooden props or stakes to support them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Muji ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaafoi kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of tall stems and leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or not enough direct sunlight, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo hulu la ni fa tɛ̃ɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Amɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baa tsei yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why does my maize produce small, incomplete cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeee emuu kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, individual maize plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves each plant with insufficient resources to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Abele tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso bɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my yam vines right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, wild root systems adapted to grab water and soil nutrients instantly after rainfall, while cultivated crops take more time to recover and draw up nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpãa gbee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni adu amɛ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cowpea plants without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping in cowpeas is commonly caused by insect pests like blossom thrips feeding on the tender flowers, or by extreme heat stress preventing proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cowpea nɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I mark or tag the healthiest crop plants on my farm before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makadi loo makadi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Marking your healthiest and highest-yielding plants helps you remember which ones to collect seeds or cuttings from for the next planting season, ensuring your future crops inherit those superior traits.
ga: Kɛ́ okadi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaiɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni esa akɛ okɛto kɛha shweremɔ be ni baa lɛ. Enɛ haa owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná nakai sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ gboshinii.

english: Can I save seeds from any crop in my harvest to plant next season, or does it matter which specific plant they come from?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli. Yɛ mikpamɔ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo tso nɔ̃ ni nakai dumɔwui lɛ jɛ mli lɛ he hiaa?

english: Seeds inherit traits directly from their parent plants. Collecting seeds only from your strongest, disease-free plants gives you better harvest results, while saving seeds from weak plants leads to poor yields.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ sui kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni helai bɛ mli lɛ pɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmaa kpakpa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some cassava plants on my farm yield huge tubers while others planted at the same time right next to them yield very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni aduɔ tsei komɛi yɛ he kome yɛ amɛhe Yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ?

english: Individual plants carry unique genetic traits, just like human children inherit different traits from parents. Some individual plants are naturally stronger at absorbing soil nutrients and resisting local pests than others.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ fɔmɔ su pɔtɛɛ ko. Taakɛ adesai abii lɛ náa sui ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ amɛfɔlɔi ahe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei komɛi ahe wa fe ekrokomɛi yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛheɔ, ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: If I take suckers from my best plantain tree, will the new trees produce the exact same high yield as the mother plant?
ga: Kɛji mihala ŋmeii kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ Ani tso hee lɛ baawo yibii babaoo tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ?

english: Yes, planting materials like plantain suckers or cassava cuttings are direct genetic copies of the parent plant, which means they will reliably carry the exact same good traits as the mother plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmei ni afo lɛ ji fɔlɔ tso lɛ fɔmɔ sui tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ baaná sui ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to get weaker and produce smaller yields when I replant seeds saved from the same crop line year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tso kome mli lɛ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Replanting seeds from the same small family line repeatedly causes seed degeneration or inbreeding depression, making plants weaker over time. Introducing fresh, high-quality seeds or rotating stock prevents this loss of strength.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ weku bibioo kome mli lɛ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha amɛfite loo amɛhao yɛ fɔmɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo nibii ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hewalɛ ni baa shi nɛɛ naa.

english: What happens if I plant two different varieties of maize right next to each other on the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa srɔtoi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Wind carries pollen between nearby crops, causing them to cross-pollinate. The harvested seeds will become a mixed variety, which can alter the desired kernel color, taste, or grain quality in the next generation.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pollen yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ cross-pollinate. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ bafeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko. ni baanyɛ atsake dumɔwui lɛ ahe su, amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ, loo amɛhilɛ-kɛhamɔ ni ataoɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I save and plant seeds harvested from high-yielding hybrid maize to get the same great harvest next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ ato ni madu koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, seeds produced by hybrid crops lose their uniform vigor in the next generation and split into unpredictable traits, which usually leads to lower yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. ni aja mli awo sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why is it important for me to keep records of where I bought my crop seeds and their variety names?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma he ni mihe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ kɛ amɛmli srɔtoi lɛ agbɛi lɛ?

english: Keeping track of seed varieties helps you remember which specific types perform well on your soil, how much fertilizer they require, and which suppliers provide reliable seed quality.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni oookwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okaiɔ dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ enyiɛ he hiaa bo? Ni mɛɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ haa?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they face environmental stress, such as intense sunshine, lack of water, or poor soil fertility. Providing shade and consistent moisture helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i haa fɔfɔi lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my watermelon vines produce many flowers, but very few of them actually turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai?

english: Watermelons produce separate male and female flowers on the same vine. Bees must carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers for fruit to develop; without insect activity, female flowers dry up and fall off.
ga: Watermelon woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ koni aduawai aba. Kɛji kooloi bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi yei lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I bought are grain crops like maize or rice before I put them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ji ŋmaa nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa? dani adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Grain seeds like maize, rice, and sorghum usually have a hard outer shell and a single seed leaf when they sprout. Checking the shape, size, and seed texture helps you identify the grain type so you can plant it at the right depth and spacing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa kɛ dumɔwui baa kome kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ, amɛdalɛ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oyoo dumɔwui lɛ ahenɔi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛ ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Light early rains often do not soak deep into the soil. If the soil dries out quickly after planting, the seeds absorb just enough water to start germinating but then dry out and die before they can push through the soil surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛje kwɛ̃mɔ shishi shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young grain crops turning yellow and stunt-growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves early in the season usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen helps crops stay green and grow leaves, while excess water prevents roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. yɛ be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu.

english: Why do my crop plants grow very tall and thin, but then fall over before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni egbɔjɔ shi egbeeɔ shi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Plants grow tall and weak when they are planted too close together and have to fight for sunlight, or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer. When heavy winds or rains arrive, these weak stems break easily under the weight of the crop.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. aloo kɛ́ onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa Nɛkɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ fãa oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are the plants at the edges of my farm bigger than the ones growing in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ dara fe tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops at the edges get more sunlight, fresh air, and less competition for soil water and nutrients than plants crowded together in the center of the field.
ga: Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ naa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa Ni akaŋshii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe lɛ faaa fe tsei ni abua naa yɛ ŋmɔ ko teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops flower and produce grains at different times on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth happens when seeds are planted at different depths or when parts of the field retain more water and nutrients than others. Planting seeds at a uniform depth ensures they all germinate and mature together.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. aloo be mli ni ŋmɔ ko mli hei komɛi hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo fe ekrokomɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do I know my grain crop is fully ready so a combine harvester can harvest it without destroying the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kwraa? No hewɔ lɛ, ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa ni efiteee ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Grains are ready for machine harvesting when the leaves and stalks have completely dried and turned brown, and the seeds feel hard when pressed with a fingernail. Harvesting while grains are still soft or wet can crush the crop and jam the machine.
ga: Afee klalo kɛha tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmaa lɛ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei miimɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni edɔ loo edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni eha tsɔne lɛ atswa.

english: Will bringing a heavy combine harvester onto my farm spoil the soil for the next planting season?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii ni tsii ni akɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy harvesters can press down wet soil and cause soil compaction, making it hard for future crop roots to grow deep. Using machines when the soil is dry prevents severe compaction and protects your land for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔnei tsu nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa naa, ni ebaabu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains small and light even though the plants looked healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Grains stay small if the crop lacks water or key nutrients like potassium during the flowering and grain-filling stage, or if heat stress occurs right when the grains are developing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafee bibii kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni awoɔ mli lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ba be mli ni dumɔwu lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my crops in straight rows or just scatter the seeds across the field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ loo aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop proper space to grow, makes weeding much easier, and allows farm machines like combine harvesters to pass through the field without crushing plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ni sa ni ekɛda. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni ehaa okwaayeli mli tsɔnei, tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkuuu ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and attracts specific pests. Rotating maize with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do people say I should plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide quick shade and hold soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ oya ni amɛhiɛɔ sũ lɛ mli nu. Buu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves and grass around the stems of my crops instead of clearing and burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie ni ashã

english: Leaving dry plant material on the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. It prevents water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and slowly breaks down into compost to feed the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe nibii ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ latsaa be mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early when my cassava plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Beni ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Removing them early ensures your young cassava gets all the food and space it needs to produce big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ajieɔ ŋmei lɛ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmei bibioo lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmei wuji.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant does not get enough water consistently. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɔ́ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb upward so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food for the plant, which leads to much larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni akwɔ nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la haa anyɛɔ akɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ahaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season in Ghana?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out the hot ground and cause your seeds to spoil before they sprout.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha hei ni edɔ lɛ agbi ni eha odumɔwui lɛ agboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I pick the right part of a cassava stem to cut and plant for a strong harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso ni abaafolɔ ni adu koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: Use the firm, middle section of a healthy stem rather than the soft green top or the old woody base. Stems cut to about 20–30 centimeters with multiple visible nodes sprout the fastest.
ga: Okɛ tso ni mli wa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ yi mi tomi nɛ ngɛ tsɔi loo tso sisi tomi momo nɛ tsu ní. Afoɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashɛɔ aaafee 20–30 cm, ni ŋmeii babaoo ni anaa lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ.

english: What is making holes in the center leaf funnels of my maize with small black droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli ni ŋmei diŋ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Checking your field early and putting recommended pest control measures directly into the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees to filter the sun and keep the air humid until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛjie hulu la lɛ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can capture light efficiently and make food. When vines lie on the ground, leaves stay shaded, get dirty, catch fungal diseases easily, and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhoo nii. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baakã he ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, amɛhe baawo muji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baamɔ amɛ oya. ni amɛwoɔ yitsei bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded in a single spot, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil water, and food. Because no single plant gets enough nutrients, they all stay weak and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei eyi he kome Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves and strong stalks. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's growth helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that extra plant food remains in the dirt to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tse niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small caterpillars hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo kone mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, an insect pest that feeds on the soft center of the maize plant. Spraying approved treatments directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening helps clear them out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread plant viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents the virus from spreading and damaging your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily even when there is no heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees collapse when tiny worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects damage their root systems underground. Without strong roots anchoring the plant, the heavy stem cannot support the weight of the growing bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kpata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi ni tsii lɛ po nyɛŋ afi tso lɛ kuu ni miida lɛ muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells as a survival mechanism to save water, not because the plant is dead. The root tuber below ground stays alive and healthy, and the plant will shoot fresh green leaves as soon as rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Jeee akɛ tso lɛ gbo hewɔ. Tubers lɛ baahi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ni tsei lɛ baatswa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the soil moisture steady and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young cocoa trees are lacking key nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or they are receiving too much harsh sunlight without enough shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hulu la ni naa wa babaoo eshɛ ehe ni ebɛ hulutsoo be ni sa.

english: Why should I only use approved chemicals on my cocoa farm instead of cheap ones from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ pɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni jara waaa ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ baatsu nii

english: Unapproved chemicals can burn your cocoa trees, kill the harmless midges that pollinate your flowers, and leave dangerous residues that stop buyers from accepting your cocoa beans.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã cacao tsei. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni bɛ awui ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. ni eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsiɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakpɛlɛ o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that thrives in cool, damp, and shady conditions, spreading rapidly from pod to pod through rainwater drops.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they do not have enough water and nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects called midges in the soil to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee pollination.

english: What happens if I let my cocoa trees grow as tall as they want without trimming them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha kookoo tso lɛ da bɔ ni esumɔɔ ni mifolɔko tso lɛ he?

english: Trees that grow too tall waste energy on unnecessary leaves and branches instead of making pods, making it hard for air to circulate and extremely difficult for you to harvest or spray.
ga: Tsei ni daa tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ Ni ewaa waa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakpa loo oooshwie nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too closely, their roots fight over water and fertilizer underground, while their top leaves block each other from getting the sunlight needed to produce pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ enaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to put fertilizer on my farm at specific times instead of anytime I buy it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ bei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli be fɛɛ be ni mahe lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer at the right time—such as right at the beginning of the rainy season—helps roots soak it up immediately, whereas applying during severe dry spells or heavy downpours wastes the fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya fitemɔ.

english: Why do tall weeds around the base of my cocoa trees slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunshine, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa tree, while also creating a hiding place for dangerous pests like rats and capsids.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ capsids lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe.

english: How do small bugs like capsids damage my cocoa trees?
ga: Te kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ fiteɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Capsids bite into young cocoa shoots and green pods to suck out juices, leaving dark, burnt-looking patches that dry out leaves and cause young pods to die.
ga: Capsids lɛ ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋmei diŋ ko ni tamɔ nɔ ni shã. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ agboi.

english: Why should I avoid harvesting cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ he be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe cocoa pods do not have enough sweet juice inside their beans, which prevents proper fermentation and leaves you with bitter, flat cocoa beans that sell for low quality.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni edako lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa. Ni enɛ haa onáa kookoo ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and increases your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small maize cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes maximizes sunlight exposure and keeps the leaves away from wet soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ woɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Managing these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can continue producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ aya nɔ ewo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In soggy, waterlogged soils without good drainage, the roots suffocate and rot-causing soil fungi attack the tubers, making them soft and spoiled.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomato lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. Regular watering and providing partial shade during very hot periods help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it good practice to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full, hot sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaves that shade young cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce the overall amount of harvest I get?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunshine away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil food and light they need to grow fast and give you a bountiful yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, a key soil nutrient required for green leaf growth, or that excess standing water is drowning the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and the plant to stop growing tall?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle ehe ni tso lɛ miikpa shweremɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: How do I know if my cocoa pods are suffering from Black Pod disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ black pod hela?

english: Black Pod disease shows up as a small brown spot on the cocoa pod that rapidly spreads until the entire pod rots, turns black, and produces a white powdery fungus in wet weather.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ. etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni ekɛ powder fungi yɛŋ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain plants provide essential shade and moisture while the cocoa roots establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: How do I select the right cassava stems to use for my next planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa kɛha midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Choose clean, mature stems from disease-free plants, using the middle section of the stem and cutting pieces that have 4 to 6 strong, undamaged eye buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni he tse ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Okɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ afo mli. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave spacing between my tomato plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tomato tsei lɛ abɔle he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing lets air flow freely around tomatoes to prevent fungal leaf rot and ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients to produce larger fruits.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tomato lɛ he jogbaŋŋ koni fungal baa lɛ akafite. ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil for the next crop without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crop with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsei ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Mulching with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly under hot sun, stops weeds from growing, and adds organic plant food as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ fataa he kɛji amɛgboi.

english: How can I tell underground yam tubers are ready for harvesting without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and stems of the vine turn yellow and naturally dry out, signaling that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni wain tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers from my plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi plantain ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for the same water and nutrients, which slows down growth; removing extra suckers focuses energy into producing a large, healthy bunch on the main plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them out in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily in direct heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛná wɔɔhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How long does it usually take for newly planted cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees typically start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, while traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, pruning, and soil care help them mature faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Weeding pruning Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize matures quickly and is harvested in about 3 to 4 months, leaving space and nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ kɛ niyenii haa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy after a resting period. Warm temperatures and light in the barn signal to the yam that it is time to grow, causing it to use up its stored energy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. He ni mli edɔ kɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potatoes akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making any peppers during dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or drought as a survival mechanism to conserve water and energy until moisture conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Root rot occurs when soil stays too wet, allowing fungi to attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why does my tomato crop produce plenty of leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato woɔ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowers. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: As cocoa trees age, overgrown canopy branches block sunlight and soil nutrients get depleted. Pruning old branches to let light in and feeding the soil rejuvenates older trees.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, ŋwɛi niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Niji ni egbɔ ni aaafolɔ koni la abote mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ baaha tso momo lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak, thin stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective umbrella that shields the young cocoa from the hot sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why does the soil on my farmland dry out so quickly even after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter, such as decayed leaves or manure, cannot hold water effectively. Adding compost or leaving dry crop foliage on the soil helps trap moisture so your crops can drink longer between rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli, tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ato nu jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he loo okɛshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mli bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa babaoo lɛ? dumɔwui yɛ bu kome mli

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the plants compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow into strong plants while others stay small and produce light bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi ji bibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Selecting 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves—gives you plants with stronger roots and higher vigor, leading to larger plantain bunches compared to shoots that start with broad leaves.
ga: Tsobii bibii’ ni ji tsei bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ halamɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui agbo ko baa kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni jeɔ shishi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, naturally enriching the soil and feeding nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele.

english: Why is it harmful to spread fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil causes high chemical concentration around the roots, which burns and damages the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai babaoo baa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ashã ni efite nii.

english: Curled and yellow cassava leaves are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the plant's funnel to feed on soft leaves. Early detection and applying targeted botanical or chemical controls save the yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ana mra ni akɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant lacks calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil switches repeatedly between very wet and very dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa teŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster and have aggressive root systems that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to sweep or clear the weeds away around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi jwɛi lɛ?

english: Clearing the space around the base of your cocoa tree stops weeds from stealing food and water from the crop, while also preventing pests and diseases from nesting near the trunk.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ni ajieɔ Cacao shishitoo lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai akafee amɛ ŋtayaai yɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ he.

english: How wide of a area around my cocoa tree stem should I keep clear of debris and weeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsumɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Te kookoo tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ji tɛŋŋ?

english: You should clear a circle about one meter wide around the base of the trunk so that any manure or water you add goes straight into the soil where the feeder roots are located.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee kooloo ko ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee mita kome kɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu fɛɛ nu ni okɛbaafata he lɛ aya shikpɔŋ ni niyenii halɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I use chicken droppings as fertilizer for my cocoa crop, and how does it help?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii akɛ ŋmei kɛha kookoo tsei? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa?

english: Yes, chicken droppings are a rich organic fertilizer that adds essential nutrients like nitrogen to the soil, helping cocoa trees grow strong branches and produce good yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, eyi mli obɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ niji ni wa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Where exactly around my tree should I place animal manure when feeding my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ahe kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha?

english: Place the manure in a ring around the base of the tree under the canopy, where the fine roots spread out underground to absorb food.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ abɔle he. Tso shishi ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ Baagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ niyenii atsu nii.

english: Is animal manure like chicken dung safe to use on my farm compared to bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani kooloi amli ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli ni aheɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, animal manure is safe and improves soil health long-term by building up organic matter, though it should ideally be dried or aged slightly so it does not burn delicate young roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni etswaa lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ ebaahi lɛ, esa akɛ agbi fioo loo atsa lɛ koni ekashã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ moŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover chicken manure with soil after putting it near my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ sũ aha tsina ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Covering manure with soil stops the sun from drying out its nutrients and burning them off into the air, keeping the food locked in the ground for the tree roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agbi ni ekɛshã kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: What happens if I leave chicken manure sitting open on top of the ground without covering it with soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tsina fɔmɔ kotoku yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ muji ehaaa nɔ?

english: If left uncovered, heavy rain can wash the valuable manure away before the plant can use it, or the hot sun can bake it and waste its nitrogen content.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ni akɛteeee lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii. Aloo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo ni nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why does fertilizer or manure need to be in direct contact with the soil to work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpe tɛ̃ɛ koni etsu nii lɛ?

english: Direct contact allows soil microbes and moisture to break down the manure so that its nutrients dissolve into a form that the plant roots can swallow.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa sũ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ami.

english: How does rain help the manure I put around my cocoa trees work better?
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ he lɛ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rain dissolves the nutrients inside the manure and carries them deep down into the root zone, allowing the tree to drink in the plant food easily.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ekɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaanu nii akɛ tsei niyenii.

english: Should I apply my chicken manure right before the rainy season starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ awo mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Yes, applying manure just as the rains begin ensures there is enough moisture to wash the nutrients down into the soil without heavy downpours washing the manure away.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from the maize I buy at the local market to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ dumɔwui ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain bought from the market is usually meant for cooking and may produce weak plants or very small yields. Certified planting seeds are specially bred and treated to resist local pests and produce strong, high-yielding crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii ni ebaanyɛ ewo tsei bibii loo nɔ ko fioo pɛ aba. Akwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by hot weather, lack of water, or missing nutrients like phosphorus. Ensuring consistent watering and proper soil nutrients helps the flowers stay on and grow into tomatoes.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Is it harmful if I weed or disturb the soil very close to my pepper plants while they are flowering?
ga: Ani ebaaye mi awui kɛji mijie jwɛi loo migba shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yes, weeding too close damages the delicate surface roots when the plant needs stability most. Distracting or damaging the plant during flowering causes it to drop its blossoms instead of producing pepper pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala tso lɛ naa loo ofite lɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee pepper pods.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants experience transplant shock when moved directly into harsh sunlight. Transplanting them late in the afternoon and watering them immediately gives them the cool night to settle into the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baaná shoofeemɔ kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shwane mli ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ beni ebashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do wild plants grow easily on uncultivated land, but improved cassava varieties need clear fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ lɛ mlɛo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmei henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ?

english: Wild plants are naturally tough but yield very little food. High-yielding crop varieties direct all their energy into producing big roots, so they cannot compete with weeds for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Koo mli tsei lɛ ahe wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ shishifãi wuji ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crops if I do not feed the soil with any fertilizer or manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time as crops grow. Without extra feeding from fertilizer or well-rotted manure, crops become yellow, grow slowly, and yield very little food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛji niyenii kroko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo mli baa lɛ bɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Does giving my crops a double batch of fertilizer at the start make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ ji shii enyɔ fata ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaha eda oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once can burn the roots and kill the plants. Crops need light, balanced feeding at specific stages, such as early growth and flowering.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Tsei biɔ niyenii ni waaa, ni ja yɛ bei komɛi amli, tamɔ amɛdalɛ mra kɛ fɔfɔi.

english: How do I know the exact time my fresh maize is ready to harvest so it doesn't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa hee lɛ esa akɛ akpa koni ekafite?

english: Fresh maize is ready when the silk turns brown and dry, and squeezing a seed produces a milky liquid. Leaving it longer makes the kernels hard and dry, turning it into dry grain instead.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji siliki lɛ batsɔ blɔfo ni egbi. Ni kɛ́ amimɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa nu ni tamɔ mliki baa. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛgbi, ni no baaha dumɔwui ni egbi aba moŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crop fields in staggered weekly batches instead of planting everything on one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu otsi fɛɛ otsi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ najiaŋ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting in batches means your crops mature at different times. This gives you a continuous supply to sell or eat over two to three months, rather than everything maturing at once and spoiling.
ga: Ni oookwɛ yɛ kui amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa onáa nibii ni okɛbaahɔɔ loo oyeɔ daa nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baaho shikome ni efite lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the field without draining away, it starves the roots of air, causing them to rot and kill the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ e puɛɔ nɛ e gbeɔ tso ɔ.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa tree when it is already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji kɛji tso lɛ etswa shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra or dead branches lets sunlight and air reach the healthy parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and helps the tree focus its energy on growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of year for me to trim my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo cacao tsei?

english: Trimming is usually done right before the main rainy season begins, around February to April, so the tree can use the coming rains to quickly grow fresh leaves and set new pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afoɔ tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Aaafee February kɛyashi April Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ baai heei oya ni amɛfee ŋmeii heei.

english: What are those fast-growing shoots coming out from the bottom of my cocoa trunk, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii ni daa oya ni jɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Those shoots are called suckers or water sprouts. They steal food and water from the main tree without producing good pods, so you should remove them early to keep the main tree strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo nu ŋmeii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛwooo ŋmeii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ojie amɛ mra. Koni tso titri lɛ awa

english: How does cutting back heavy leaves stop my cocoa pods from rotting on the tree?
ga: baai ni tsii ni afoɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Thick leaves trap damp air around the pods, which causes fungal diseases like black pod. Trimming opens up the canopy so wind and sun can dry the pods quickly after it rains.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no kɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbeleɔ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start forming small pods around April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii bibii shweremɔ lɛ? Aaafee April mli?

english: Cocoa trees react to the early rains that usually start around April. The water gives the tree the strength it needs to turn its flowers into young pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli, ni bei pii lɛ ejeɔ shishi yɛ April mli lɛ he nii. Nu haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔii bibii.

english: Why do many flowers drop off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks nutrients, water, or light, it naturally drops extra flowers to save energy for a few strong pods.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso ko bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, loo la lɛ, ebaashɛ fɔfɔi krokomɛi ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing smaller pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older and overcrowded with branches, they spend more energy maintaining wood and leaves instead of feeding the pods, which makes the pods smaller.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni eniji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii kɛkwɛ tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ

english: Who can come to my farm to help me trim my cocoa trees properly if I am afraid of damaging them?
ga: Namɔ baanyɛ aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaye ebua mi ni mafolɔ mikoo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Ni kɛji mishe gbeyei akɛ makpãtã kookoo tso lɛ hiɛ hu?

english: The Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) sends trained extension staff and official pruning teams into farming communities to help farmers prune their trees correctly without harming them.
ga: Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ tsuɔ mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa okwaayeli akutsei amli. Koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛfolɔ tsei jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyeee amɛ awui

english: Will clearing all big trees around my cocoa farm make the cocoa pods grow faster?
ga: Tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Ani mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ adara oya?

english: No, removing all shade trees exposes young cocoa to harsh sunlight and hot winds, which burns the leaves and weakens the tree's pod production.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ajie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ aná kookoo bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow more pods after I clear the weeds and tidy up the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mijie jwɛi ni mifee mibɔɔ lɛ mli fɛo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water from the soil. Clearing them leaves all the nourishment for the cocoa tree, giving it the extra strength needed to produce plenty of pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛhe lɛ, niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ adɛŋ lɛ shiɔ. Enɛ haa enáa hewalɛ kroko kɛha pods babaoo feemɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers spoil so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to spoil within 2 to 3 days after harvest because they contain high moisture and continue to breathe rapidly. Once cut from the stem, natural chemical breakdown occurs unless the tubers are processed or dried quickly into products like konkonte.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ mumɔ ni yaa nɔ oya lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni fiteɔ lɛ baaba. Ja afee tubers lɛ oya loo agbi amɛ ni afee nɔ ko tamɔ conconte.

english: What causes cassava tubers to become watery and poor for making konkonte flour?
