ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi feɔ nu ni esaaa akɛ akɛfeɔ con conte ŋmɔtɔ?

english: If cassava is harvested right after heavy rainfall or before it reaches full maturity, the starch content drops and water content rises. This makes the tubers soggy and difficult to dry into high-quality konkonte.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmei yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Starch lɛ falɛ baa shi ni nu lɛ falɛ baaya hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ewaa akɛ amɛaagbi ni amɛfee conte ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the correct way to measure fertilizer so I do not ruin my crop field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni asusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Using simple standard local measurements, such as a specific bottle cap or a small tin per plant, ensures balanced distribution. Applying too much fertilizer burns crop roots, while applying too little leaves crops starved of essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli susumɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tɔi pɔtɛɛ loo tsinsii bibii tsu nii yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni aja mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of leaves above the ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or fertilizer. Nitrogen encourages the plant to grow bushy stems and leaves instead of storing energy in the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nitrogen woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaato hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Infected plants cannot process sunlight efficiently, which reduces their overall growth and tuber size.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu hulu la lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha yitso lɛ dalɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: What causes stem rot in my cassava field before harvest time comes?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji amli dani kpamɔ be shɛɔ?

english: Stem and root rot occur when soil holds too much water without proper drainage. Fungal diseases thrive in waterlogged soil and attack the damp stem bases under the earth.
ga: Stem kɛ root rot baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Fungal hela lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni etutuaa tso lɛ shishi ni efɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops turn yellow right after the main rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Heavy, continuous rains can wash away surface nutrients like nitrogen or drown root systems in flooded soil, preventing the roots from taking up air and nutrients properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nitrogen loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops survive dry weather better than others on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava develop long taproots that stretch deep into the earth to draw groundwater, whereas shallow-rooted crops can only access moisture near the surface, which dries out fast.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ pɛ. ni baagbi oya lɛ

english: Why do my dried cassava pieces develop mould and insects when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni egbi lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii baa kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If cassava pieces are bagged before they are completely dry to the core, trapped moisture creates a warm, damp environment where mould spores grow and storage pests reproduce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei fãi lɛ wo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa kɛyashɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ daa yɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my crops take longer to mature during a dry year compared to a wet year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli kɛ akɛtoɔ afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Water carries soil nutrients up through the plant. When water is scarce during a drought, the plant slows down its growth and food production processes to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei anɔ. Beni nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees above them to shield them from sun scorch while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the ground. If seeds sprout and the soil dries up immediately, the young shoots will wither; it is safer to wait until the rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli tsɔnei lɛ?

english: Those are fall armyworms, which target the tender growing point of maize plants. Catching them early with neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments stops them before they destroy the crop's growing core.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ mli fã ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into small cups and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually brought by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies that suck sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and stopping fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi aduawai lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects in the soil without draining away, or when infected stem cuttings were planted. Planting on ridges helps drain excess rainwater away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. aloo beni adu tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ Dumɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow in a V-shape during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer solves this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily whenever strong rain winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ baatswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall when too many suckers grow around one main stem, weak roots from poor soil, or nematodes attacking the root base. Pruning extra suckers keeps the main plant anchored and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui baagbee shi kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe. single main trunk Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo nematodes yɛ ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ Shishifãi krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make energy. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing the leaves to sun while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni atsĩɔ helai ni baa sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from sudden water dry-outs. Consistent watering at the roots during flowering helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nu fite trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my vegetables staying small when I plant them in small wooden boxes instead of the open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tso adeka bibioo ko mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ?

english: Crop roots need room to spread out to find water and food. When grown in small boxes, the roots quickly get trapped and run out of space and nutrients, which stops the top of the plant from growing big.
ga: He ko he miihia tsei shishifãi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔni afee ni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ adu yɛ adeka bibioo mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ oya. ni he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ edaaa.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it keep insects away from my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: A greenhouse is a sheltered structure covered with special plastic or fine mesh netting. It acts as a physical wall that stops flies, beetles, and other destructive pests from entering and eating your crops.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛ plastic krɛdɛɛ ko loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ehà nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa. Kaaha amɛba ni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil food. They waste energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and strong leaves.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa la mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do tiny flies make the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiha mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like whiteflies suck the vital juices out of young leaves and spread plant sicknesses. This damage causes the leaves to twist up, preventing the plant from making food and growing properly.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get rotten leaves when I cover them tightly with plastic sheets without leaving air holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ni fiteɔ beni mikɛ plastic ŋmɔji ha amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni mishiii kɔɔyɔɔ bu ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops need fresh air to breathe and dry off. Tightly covering them traps heat and moisture, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases quickly breed and rot the leaves.
ga: Tsei taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛgbi. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ ni amɛfite oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They temporarily droop to save water and usually bounce back once the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaakoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu nu he. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji shwane mli fɛ̃i eba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I do not plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get scorched by strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees act like umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture the young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Yellow bottom leaves mean the soil is running low on essential food like nitrogen. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send the remaining nutrients to feed the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni ji baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. When the plant feels weak, it drops its flowers to save its own life instead of spending energy making fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ egbɔjɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink the water and eat the soil nutrients meant for your crops. Even during heavy rain, the weeds steal the food first, leaving your crops hungry and slow to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaadu nii lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli lɛ, Jwɛi baaju niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara fiofio.

english: If I buy yam seeds that grow very well in Techiman, will they automatically give me the same good yield if I plant them on my farm in Tamale?
ga: Kɛ mihe sweet potato dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Techiman lɛ, ani sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai ni tamɔ nɛkɛ aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Tamale lɛ mli

english: Not necessarily. Crops adapt to the specific rainfall, sun, and soil conditions of their local environment, so a variety that thrives in Techiman may not give the same high yield when moved to Tamale.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Techiman lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee Tamale.

english: Why can't I just clear any piece of land anywhere in Ghana and plant yams on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo shikpɔŋ yɛ Ghana he ko ni madu sweet potato yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams require specific soil types and climate conditions to grow well. If you plant them in an area where the environment does not suit them, the crops will not thrive or yield good tubers.
ga: Sweet potato biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji odu yɛ he ko ni shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ esaaa tso lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ loo ebaawooo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why does a yam variety like Adwira perform so well in some towns but fail to grow properly in other places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Adwira sweet potatoes lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maji komɛi amli shi amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are naturally suited to specific regions. What makes Adwira thrive in one town—such as its soil depth and rainfall pattern—might be missing in another town's environment.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ ji nɔ ni sa kɛha kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni haa Adwira shwereɔ yɛ maŋ ko mli, tamɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ebaanyɛ elaaje kɛjɛ maŋtiase shihilɛi krokomɛi amli.

english: My friend in Nyankpala gets huge harvests with his yam seeds, so if he gives me some of those seeds, will they grow just as well in my town?
ga: Minaanyo ni yɔɔ Nyankpala lɛ ná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ e-yam dumɔwui lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji eha mi nakai dumɔwui lɛ Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crop seeds perform based on their local environment. Unless your town shares the exact same climate and soil features as Nyankpala, the seeds might not perform as well on your land.
ga: Dumɔwui feɔ amɛnii yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ naa. Ja omaŋ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ su tamɔ Nyankpala pɛpɛɛpɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I relocate to a different region in Ghana, can I bring and plant the exact same crop varieties I used to grow in my home village?
ga: Kɛji mifã kɛtee kpokpaa kroko nɔ yɛ Ghana Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni adu yɛ mimaŋ akrowa lɛ nɔŋŋ aba?

english: It is better to check first. Every region in Ghana has unique weather patterns and soil characteristics, so crops that worked in your old village might struggle in a new region.
ga: Ehi akɛ oookwɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Ghana kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ e kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ sui. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nyɛ akrowa momo lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa yɛ kpokpaa hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it true that every crop has specific places in Ghana where it naturally grows best?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ Ghana ni ekwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yes, Ghana has different ecological zones. Crops naturally produce their highest yields in regions where the local rainfall, temperature, and soil naturally match what the plant needs.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana yɛ eko-zonii srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, latsaa, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahiamɔ nii kpãa gbee lɛ.

english: How do I know if the land I have in my village is suitable for growing yams before I spend money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ dani mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he?

english: The best sign is to observe if yams are already planted and thriving in that specific area, or speak with an agricultural officer who knows which crops suit your local environment.
ga: Okadi ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okadi kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nakai he pɔtɛɛ lɛ. Aloo okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni le ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ agba sane.

english: How should I choose which crop variety to plant on my farm for the best harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná ŋmaa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Always select varieties that are proven to thrive in your specific locality, rather than choosing a variety just because it is famous for doing well in a distant part of the country.
ga: Halamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohala tsina ko ejaakɛ eyɛ gbɛi kpakpa akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ,.

english: Why would the exact same seed type grow tall and healthy in one district but stay small and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ he ko, shi eyɛ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Plants react strongly to their surroundings. Even with good seeds, an environment that lacks the right weather or soil nutrients for that specific plant will stunt its growth.
ga: Tsei yɛ henumɔi ni mli wa yɛ amɛshihilɛhe lɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ moŋ Shihilɛ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛha nakai tso lɛ bɛ mli lɛ baatsi edalɛ naa.

english: Why did my yam crop produce very small tubers even though I bought high-quality seed yams from a major farming market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miiwo tuber bibii waa beni miheɔ sweet potato ni ji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelihe wulu ko lɛ?

english: Seed quality is only half the picture. If those seed yams were meant for a different climate zone, moving them to your farm's different soil and weather conditions can cause poor tuber growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe saji ji mfoniri lɛ fã pɛ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi krokomɛi Amɛjie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tuber lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight. If they get too much direct sun, their leaves burn and turn yellow. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji onine shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo nɔ. Baai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing lots of tall leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leafy stems instead of expanding tubers. Reducing nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant focus its energy on swelling the roots underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing these small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Enɛɛmɛi ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to build big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them dry, which prevents leaves from rotting on wet ground and leads to much bigger yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ nitsumɔ babaoo baa

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen naturally out of the air and put it back into the ground. This feeds the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Be ni miha tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Nakai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Too many young suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and light. Cutting back extra suckers so only two or three remain allows the main tree to feed big, full bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni eshi baai enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei niji wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium uptake. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering allows the plant to draw up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni anáaa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani mifee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or severe dryness. Providing shade, mulching the soil to hold moisture, and watering during dry spells prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa he. Ha hulutsoo, mulch koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Ni nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, suppresses weeds, and enriches the soil as the dry leaves break down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ baai ni egbi lɛ fite

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my seeds as soon as I plant them or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo dumɔwui lɛ amli nu kɛji adu amɛ pɛ loo aaamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seedlings need to develop roots before they can take in food. Putting chemical fertilizer directly on seeds at planting can burn them, so it is best to wait two to three weeks after sprouting when roots are ready to drink the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi dani amɛye nii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshã, no hewɔ lɛ mɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaanu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on dry soil or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when put on moist soil after a rain because water dissolves the fertilizer so the roots can drink it in. Putting fertilizer on completely dry soil can burn the crop's roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing cassava about 1 meter apart in all directions leaves enough room under the soil for big roots to expand without competing with neighboring plants for water and nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tapioka lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee mita kome yɛ gbɛi fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa aha shishifãi wuji lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juice out of the leaves, or by sicknesses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruit grows on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, which stresses the plant and prevents the flowers from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do strong winds easily break or push over my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ fãa loo etsiɔ mi plantains lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad, heavy leaves that catch the wind like a sail. Planting them close together in blocks or putting strong wooden poles next to them helps support them against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsii ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛi. Dumɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ blɔkii amli loo okɛ tsei ni wa awo amɛhe. Ebaaye ebua ni efi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry out, showing that the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy into the tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito bulb ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of green leaves but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants put all their energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of making flowers and bean pods. Cowpeas need little to no nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, Cowpeas biɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ loo eko kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crops regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients from the earth. Rotating different crops, especially beans or groundnuts, helps put fresh nutrients back into the ground and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi titri lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii hee aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear small weeds from my farm if my crops are already much taller than them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? shi miŋmɔ lɛ mli Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even small weeds drink water and steal valuable nutrients from the soil that your tall crops need to grow big fruits and grains, so removing them ensures your main crops get full nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni he hiaa otsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ aduawai kɛ ŋmaa wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any small tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when they do not get steady water. Providing regular watering and light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing very thin even though the leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing big leaves above ground instead of expanding roots below. Using balanced fertilizers rich in potassium helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my watermelons rotting while they are still attached to the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi lɛ miifite be mli ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ kpãa gbee lolo lɛ?

english: Bottom rot on watermelons happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by irregular watering routines or overly dry soil during fruit formation.
ga: Watermelon shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that hide under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects when weather is dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning brown before it is time to dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani be shɛɔ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up and wither at the end of their lifecycle when the plant has finished storing all its energy into the tuber underground, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naagbee beni tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow much better when planted alongside maize instead of on a separate plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi moŋ fe ni adu amɛ yɛ saatsoi srɔtoi anɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which nourishes nearby maize plants while the sturdy maize stalks provide a natural frame for the cowpeas to climb.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni wa lɛ haa tsina ŋmãa lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛkwɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain or banana alongside them creates living shade and keeps the air cool and moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaafee shade ni ekɛ shade baaha. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn ears grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and healthy. When the soil runs low on food, the plant steals nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the newly growing upper leaves and corn ears, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai lɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi heei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if I plant them in dry soil before the rains fully start?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ kwraa?

english: If seeds get just a tiny sprinkle of rain, they will break open and start to sprout. However, if the main rains fail to continue, the heat and dry soil will dry out the weak young roots, killing the plant before it can grow.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná nugbɔ fioo pɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa ni amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Shi, kɛji nugbɔ titri lɛ eyaaa nɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ dani enyɛɔ edaa.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow after I keep them under a tree for a few weeks before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi otsii fioo komɛi dani midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava stems are alive and contain water and stored food. If stored too long before planting, they dry out and lose the energy needed to push out new roots and shoots once buried in the ground.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛbua nu kɛ niyenii naa. Kɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani adu lɛ Ebaagbi ni hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaje mli.

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, making it impossible for the flowers to fertilize and produce seeds. When a flower cannot form fruit, the plant drops it to save its remaining water and nutrients.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo dumɔwui. Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller maize harvests every year if I grow maize on the same plot repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ?

english: Maize drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus out of the soil every season. Growing it in the same spot repeatedly empties the soil's pantry and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii he saamɔ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee efolo. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ.

english: Why do yam vines need to grow on tall wooden stakes instead of spreading along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the food that makes tubers grow big underground. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, preventing decay from damp soil and helping the plant capture light.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking elevator lɛ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli fitemɔ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ la

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow tall and thin with very light yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. When weeds surround a plant, the crop stretches upward rapidly to fight for sunlight, leaving it with weak, thin stems and little energy to produce food or fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaawo niyenii loo amɛwo yibii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaf undersides or spreading a virus. The damaged leaves cannot make food properly, which halts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni haa tsei kpaa shweremɔ

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve the soil for other crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family and work with natural soil organisms to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested and its roots rot, that nitrogen stays behind to fertilize the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, Nitrogen baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni ekɛwo tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava harvests now compared to ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same land removes essential plant nutrients from the soil over time. Without giving the land a rest to recover or adding compost or fertilizer, the soil becomes depleted and cannot support big yields.
ga: Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baajie tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji oŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ.

english: Why is it good for my farm if I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei fata ŋmei he lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and naturally put it into the soil. This feeds the neighboring maize plants and leaves the soil healthier for future planting seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa bei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry up, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. When a flower isn't fertilized, the plant drops it to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tso baafi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking allows the leaves to spread out high in the sun, which sends more energy down into the ground to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee yitso ni da.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit. When you leave too many side shoots growing around the main trunk, it weakens the base, making it easy for wind to tip the heavy plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji akɛ oshi sɛɛ ŋmɔji ni bɔleɔ tsitsi wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shishitoo lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deeper into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei amli niyenii titri Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: The middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem works best because it has strong buds and enough stored food. Stems that are too young dry out quickly, while stems that are too old take too long to sprout.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ niyenii ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsoi ashishifãi ni darako tsɔ lɛ baagbi oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni egbɔ tsɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and dark dirt inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms. They crawl into the center funnel of the plant where young leaves are growing and eat them before they open.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ. Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni baai bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if I make sure to give my farm enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa eha ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root system is deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, cools the plant roots, and stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient in the soil that helps plants build strong leaves and grow green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ naa baai ni wa ni amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ eŋɔli.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the ground is moist, so the heat doesn't burn the roots or evaporate the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, la ni tsoɔ lɛ shãaa shishifãi lɛ loo ehaaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ la.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same specific food out of the soil and gives pests that love that crop a permanent place to live and multiply.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he ko ni amɛhi shi daa ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the suckers growing around one plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛreɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ?

english: If you leave too many suckers, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil, which leaves the main stem weak and results in very small bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha plantains bibii akui aba.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches lets fresh air and sunlight pass through the tree, which prevents damp diseases like black pod from growing on the pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni mli ewo fɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji akakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, which suffocates the roots and causes fungi to grow and spoil the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is causing holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing center of the plant and eat the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crop yield smaller at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops, leaving your crops weak and unable to produce full fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and turn into dust after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ sũ beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Maize grains contain hidden insect eggs or attract pests like maize weevils if they are not dried properly before storage. These insects multiply quickly in warm grain, eating the inside of the seeds and leaving behind hollow shells and dust.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi ŋmeii amli loo egbala kooloi bibii tamɔ abɛi ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ faa oya yɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ.

english: Why does my stored rice start smelling sour and growing white mold even though I harvested it dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmãa ni ehaa ŋmãa yɛŋ baa eyɛ mli akɛ Akpa ŋmãa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Even if rice feels dry on the outside, it can still hold hidden moisture inside the grain. When kept in damp or closed spaces without enough airflow, this trapped moisture causes mold to grow and spoil the crop.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmã lɛ egbi moŋ Shi ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nu ni emɔ mli nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know that my maize is completely mature and ready to be harvested so it doesn't rot later?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, sɛɛ mli lɛ, egbooo.

english: Maize is mature when the husks turn brown and dry, and a tiny dark spot appears at the base of the grain where it attaches to the cob. Harvesting at this exact stage prevents field insects and rains from damaging the cobs.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shishi yɛ he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ nugbɔ naa koni amɛkafite ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains fall off onto the ground before I can even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani mikpaa lɛ?

english: Rice grains drop naturally—a process called shattering—if the crop is left in the sun for too long after maturing. Harvesting as soon as 80 percent of the panicles turn golden yellow prevents you from losing grain on the soil.
ga: Ŋmãa lɛ baagbee shi yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shwiemɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, Kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ amli oha mlijaa 80 pɛ ni etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested maize cobs get very hot when I stack them together in a big pile inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ waa beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmãa agbo ko mli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still 'breathes' and releases moisture and heat. When stacked tightly in a room without fresh air, this trapped heat creates sweat, which makes the grains rot and attracts beetles.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ ‘muɔ’ lolo ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ ato tsu ko mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ kɛ latsaa baa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa jɛmɛ.

english: How can building a raised crib off the ground protect my harvested crops better than keeping them on the floor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ maa lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmaa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe ni akɛto shikpɔŋ?

english: A raised crib allows air to flow freely around the cobs to dry them naturally while keeping ground moisture, rats, and crawling pests away from your harvest.
ga: Hamɔk ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ohe jogbaŋŋ. cob to dry naturally Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does keeping maize in regular fertilizer sacks cause it to spoil faster than using airtight storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli daa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ vacuum woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Regular woven sacks allow insects and moist air to enter freely. Airtight storage bags block out oxygen, which suffocates any insects inside and prevents mold from growing without using chemical powders.
ga: Baagi ni akpɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ boteɔ mli oya. Vacuum kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii

english: Why does my stored rice turn yellow or dark instead of staying clean and white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni he tse ni eyɛ futafuta lɛ?

english: Rice changes color when it is stored while damp or exposed to heat and moisture. This color change happens because heat destroys the quality of the grain, reducing its market value and altering its taste.
ga: Omɔ tsakeɔ su kɛji akɛto be mli ni edɔ loo akɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ baa ejaakɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ jara nɔ ni otsake nɔ ni ŋɔɔ

english: Why do insects attack my stored grain faster during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in humid air because moisture helps their eggs hatch and speeds up their growth. High humidity in the air during rainy months makes stored grains absorb moisture, turning them into ideal food for pests.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmaa ni ato lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔshiimɔ. Ebafeɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why do traders offer me very low prices when I try to sell just two or three bags of maize at a time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi haa mi jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ beni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa kotokui enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Traders spend a lot on transport and prefer buying large quantities at once. When individual farmers combine their harvests into one large supply, traders pay better prices because it saves them time and transport costs.
ga: Jarayelɔi fiteɔ shika babaoo yɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii babaoo shikome. Beni okwaafoi aŋkroaŋkroi kɛ amɛnibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛfeɔ nibii babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ. Jarayelɔ lɛ baawo jara ni hi fe no. Ejaakɛ ehaa be kɛ shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree usually take before it starts giving me pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take about 3 to 5 years to start producing fruit, while improved hybrid varieties can start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years if given proper water, shade, and soil care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔi feemɔ yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná nu, hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that dry out easily under intense sun and low rainfall. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains and placing dry leaves around the base keeps the soil moist and protects them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa, ni akɛ baai ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop easily when the tree experiences water stress from lack of rain, or during extreme hot weather. The tree drops flowers to conserve energy and water so that the main plant can survive.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up and fail when the rains stop coming for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize relies heavily on steady soil moisture to draw nutrients. Without rain, the plant cannot feed itself, causing the leaves to roll, yellow, and dry up before forming healthy ears.
ga: Abɛi damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ eye ehe niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni egbi dani ebɔ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Which growth stage of my maize crop suffers the most if rain does not fall?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ fã baaná he sɛɛ fe fɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Maize is most vulnerable during the flowering stage—when the tassels and silks appear—and during grain filling. Drought at this time prevents kernels from forming properly, leading to empty or sparse cobs.
ga: Abele ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ. Beni ŋmeii kɛ siliki jeɔ kpo kɛ be mli ni akɛ dumɔwui fataa he lɛ Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yaka loo amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Is there any way I can protect my crops when the rains fail for weeks?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ otsii babaoo?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil longer. You can also plant drought-tolerant seed varieties that require less water to mature.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ŋmɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni biɔ nu fioo dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ hu.

english: Why do my crops yield so little harvest even when I spend so much hard work on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpamɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard work alone cannot produce a high yield if the soil lacks nutrients, or if poor seeds and lack of water affect growth. Combining your hard work with soil testing, proper fertilizers, quality seeds, and weed control will boost your yield.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ aha yibii babaoo aba kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ saa dalɛ he. Kɛji akɛ okɛ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ fata shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni sa ni akɛbaafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he kaa he Kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does planting maize on the same piece of land year after year lower my harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha miŋmãa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, planting maize on the same plot continuously drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nutrients to the soil and improves future yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize seeds when the weather is unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui? Be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait until the main rains have fully set in and soaked the soil deeply, rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can leave seeds to dry out in hot soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ titri lɛ baagbee shi kwraa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do market centers like Techiman run out of maize and charge high prices when our rains fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli he ko tamɔ Techiman lɛ ŋmãa faaa ni amɛbiɔ jara babaoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When poor rainfall causes crop failure across major farming regions, the total supply of harvested maize drops significantly. High demand combined with low supply causes shortages and drives market prices up.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ yɛ okwaayeli hei wuji lɛ Abele ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa. Nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo kɛ nibii ni baa shi lɛ haa nibii ni faaa lɛ baa ni ehaa jara nɔ jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to block the harsh heat and keep the surrounding air cool while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground prevents rotting and gives the plant the energy needed to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the bottom and move upward usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ni eyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when soil stays soaked in water for too long. Poor soil drainage causes waterlogging, which leads to fungal infections that rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil exposed to the direct sun loses moisture rapidly. Covering the bare ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) blocks the heat and keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. He ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough nourishment to produce good cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo cob kpakpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support heavy weight against strong winds. Prop sticks are needed to physically prop up the trunk once the heavy fruit bunch develops.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ nibii ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ anɔ. Tso ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ he miihia koni ekɛfi tso lɛ shishi be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Curled, twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking the sap from new leaves, or by plant viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures are too high or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe. koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi amli ni ekɛ amɛ awo mli

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Applying too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of flowering and making bean pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsina ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni efee bean pods lɛ

english: Why do my young seedlings seem to struggle and die more easily than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mitsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants have delicate root systems and soft stems, making them very vulnerable to harsh weather, diseases, and pests. They require close attention and care in their early weeks until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe waa. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaya mli shɔŋŋ

english: What are the early signs that my small crops are sick and need treatment?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ hela mɔ lɛ ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ?

english: Common signs include yellowing leaves, drooping or wilting stems, dark spots on leaves, and stunted growth. Catching these signs early allows you to apply the right treatment before the entire crop is lost.
ga: Okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ji baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni sa tsuɔ nii dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: Do young crops need extra water compared to older plants?
ga: Ani nu kroko he miihia tsei bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, young crops need frequent and gentle watering because their roots are short and stay near the surface where soil dries out quickly. Mature crops have deeper roots that can draw moisture from deeper under the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu shii abɔ kɛ blɛoo. Akɛni eshishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛbɛŋkɛ sũ lɛ hiɛ hewɔ lɛ, sũ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: How often should I check on my crops after planting them in the field?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ?

english: In the first few weeks after planting, you should inspect your field every day or two. Regular checks help you spot pest attacks, water shortages, or diseases early enough to save the plants.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli daa gbi loo gbii enyɔ. Nibii amlipɛimɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ. nu ni faaa loo hela oya bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ yiwala.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around very small plants right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Small seedlings cannot compete with weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. If left unattended, fast-growing weeds will quickly choke young plants and kill them.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baagbe tsei bibii oya ni amɛbaagbe amɛ.

english: Why should I raise some seeds in a protected nursery before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he dani mikɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery allows you to give tender seeds full protection, regular water, and daily care in a small space. This ensures only strong, healthy plants are transferred to the larger field.
ga: Nursery lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ odumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kwraa. Ha lɛ nu daa. kɛ daa gbi kwɛmɔ yɛ he bibioo ko Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: How do I know my young seedlings are strong enough to survive being transplanted to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have formed 3 to 4 true leaves and developed a sturdy green stem. This shows they are tough enough to handle open field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu shihilɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni agbele naa lɛ ahe nii.

english: Can strong sunlight kill my newly planted young seedlings?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: Yes, harsh direct sunlight can scorch tender young shoots and evaporate soil water rapidly. Providing temporary shade using leaves or palm fronds helps young seedlings survive their first few weeks.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni eha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo tsei ahe tsei ahe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do insects attack new green shoots more than the older leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fe baai momoi lɛ?

english: New shoots and small leaves are soft, sweet, and easy for insects to bite and chew. Protecting these tender growing points is essential to keep the plant alive.
ga: Tsofai heei kɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ŋɔɔ, ni ewaaa akɛ koolooi baamɔ ni amɛye. Nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ he miihia waa koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Is it safe to apply chemical fertilizer directly to small seedlings right after they sprout?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Strong fertilizers applied too close to delicate seedling roots can burn them. It is best to enrich the soil before planting or wait until the young plant has established a healthy root system.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani odu loo omɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ ebɔi shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Can I use the same cutlass to clear healthy crops right after cutting sick ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nakai dade nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: No, using the same cutlass transfers plant disease germs directly into the cuts of healthy crops. You should always clean or heat-treat your tools after working on sick plants before moving to healthy areas.
ga: Dabi, nakai dagger ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha tsei ahe helai ahe nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe loo okɛwo la mli be fɛɛ be beni okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ dani okɛ amɛ aya hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: I only have one cutlass on my farm, so how can I stop it from spreading crop diseases?
ga: Miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ dade kome pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekagbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã?
