english: If you cannot afford extra tools, you must wash your cutlass thoroughly with soap and clean water or pass the metal blade through a flame after trimming sick crops before touching your healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji onyɛɛɛ okɛ nibii krokomɛi awo mli lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ samla kɛ nu afɔ o-knife lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Aloo okɛ dade tsɔne ko atsɔ la lɛ mli beni ofo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ dani ota otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do with my pruning shears right after harvesting diseased crop branches?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa tsei aniji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Immediately wash the tools to remove plant sap and dirt, then disinfect or heat-treat them so that leftover disease germs do not stay on the metal to infect crops during the next use.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ojie tso lɛ mli nu kɛ muji. No sɛɛ lɛ, feemɔ amɛ steril loo shã amɛ la. Enɛ ji koni helai ni eshwɛ yɛ dade lɛ nɔ lɛ akabote ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni akɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do plant diseases move from one section of my farm to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli kɛyaa fã kroko mli?

english: Diseases travel easily on infected farm tools, footwear, hands, shared harvest baskets, or plant sap. Moving from a sick area of your farm straight to a healthy area carries the disease germs along with you.
ga: Hela tsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii, tokotai, niji, ŋmaakpamɔ tsɛnsii ni ajaa, loo tsei amli nu lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛ́ oshi he ko ni hela yɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee he ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ekɛ hela lɛ baa.

english: Why should I inspect my healthy crops before I inspect the sick ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani makwɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Inspecting healthy crops first prevents you from accidentally carrying disease spores on your hands, clothes, or tools from the sick plants into your healthy crop fields.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote oniji, otadei, loo nibii ni jɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ oshara mli kɛya tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops suddenly fall sick after I prune them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ trukaa beni mifolɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning leaves fresh open wounds on plants. If you prune with dirty tools that carried germs from sick plants, those disease germs easily enter the open wounds and infect the crop.
ga: Afoɔ baai ni agbele, pilamɔi heei yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni he tseee ni yɔɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli helai lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ Nakai helai lɛ baanyɛ abote pilamɔi ni agbele mli lɛ amli mlɛo ni amɛwo tso lɛ mli hela.

english: Can carrying my harvested crops in dirty sacks spread diseases to my other fields?
ga: Ani mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ kotokui ni mli ewo muji amli lɛ baanyɛ agbala hela kɛya miŋmɔji krokomɛi lɛ amli?

english: Yes, sacks or baskets that touched diseased plants carry microscopic disease spores. Reusing them in healthy fields rubs those spores onto uninfected crops and spreads the sickness.
ga: Hɛɛ, kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baabɔ he lɛ mli helai bibii ni anaaa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela lɛ emɔko amɛ lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa.

english: Is it safe to borrow farming equipment from a neighboring farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofa ŋmɔ mli nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli?

english: If your neighbor’s farm has plant diseases, their tools can carry those germs to your crops. You should always wash and treat borrowed tools before using them on your own field.
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ahe hela Amɛ nitsumɔ dadei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nakai helai lɛ kɛya onibii amli. Esa akɛ ofɔ nibii ni okɛfa lɛ ahe ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be dani okɛtsu nii yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli.

english: Is it safe to move soil from an area where crops died to help my new crop seedlings?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie shikpɔŋ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbo yɛ lɛ koni eye ebua mi tso hee lɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: No, soil where crops recently died often harbors hidden disease germs or pests that will attack and destroy the roots of your new seedlings.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ hiɛɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enɛ baatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni efite amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I take cassava cuttings from a farm plot that has some sick plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afoɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔji ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Even if a particular stem looks healthy, it might already carry the disease internally. Planting stem cuttings from a field with sick plants spreads the sickness directly into your new plot.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ Shi nakai tso lɛ hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛ mligbɛ helai baa. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã osɛɛ hee lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sun. Without shade from companion plants like plantain or shade trees, sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil, preventing proper growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ahe lɛ, Hulu la baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. tsiɔ dalɛ ni sa naa

english: Why do my maize plants have small holes in the leaves and missing centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni teŋgbɛ ko bɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical controls early inside the leaf whorl protects the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛyeɔ wala nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Baa lɛ mli ŋtayaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni edara lɛ he.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the base of the stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efuɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruits develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress caused by high afternoon temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering at the root level helps protect the blossom set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I cut down the small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ Midumɔwu titri lɛ he?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers allows them to steal nutrients and water from the main tree. Pruning so only two or three suckers of different sizes remain ensures the main stem produces large bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi suckers enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni dalɛi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ panicles agboi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they enrich the soil with natural fertilizer that helps the next crop grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to grow leaves high above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which travels down the stem to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni eyatao niyenii ni egbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli eshwa

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the plant juices and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the stunt in growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Etsiŋ dalɛ naa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before heat causes it to evaporate, giving the plants the water they need to endure hot afternoons.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I leave weeds in the field during the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops compete directly with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks gives young crops full access to resources needed to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Officer, I am expecting to harvest around six bags of maize from my field, but how can I know for sure if my land will actually produce that much?
ga: Ofisa Mikpaa gbɛ akɛ makpa ŋmãa aaafee kotokui enumɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo nakai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: While good rain is important, your actual yield depends on plant spacing, timely weed control, and proper fertilizer use. You can estimate your harvest by counting the average number of healthy cobs per plant across a small test area on your farm before harvesting.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nugbɔ kpakpa he miihia. Shi yibiiwoo diɛŋtsɛ ni obaaná lɛ damɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Obaanyɛ obu kpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso kome mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane yɛ kaa he bibioo ko lɛ nɔ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani okpa

english: Why do some of my neighbors get many bags of corn while my field yields very little even when we plant during the same week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ ekomɛi naa ŋmãa kotokui babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu yɛ otsi kome mli moŋ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to soil fertility, seed quality, and crop care. Using certified seeds, applying fertilizer at the right growth stages, and keeping weeds down during the first six weeks make a huge difference in harvest output.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ fɛo ha lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ahe kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enumɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ mli.

english: Is it bad for my final harvest if I start picking and eating some of my green maize early before the entire farm is dry?
ga: Ani minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ baafite kɛji mibɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ŋmɔmɔ kɛ yeli mra? Dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbi?

english: Harvesting a few fresh cobs for home eating is fine, but every cob picked early reduces the final weight of dry grain you can sell later. If your main goal is to harvest full bags of dry grain for sale, it is best to leave the crop to mature completely.
ga: Ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmeii heei fioo komɛi ato koni oye yɛ shia. Shi ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei ni ahala mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei ni egbi ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ naagbee muji lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ oti titri ni ma ohiɛ ji ni okpa dumɔwui ni egbi kotokui ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ agbɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so that the cobs do not rot on the stalks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa nii? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite?

english: Corn is ready for dry harvest when the leaves turn brown, the outer husks dry out completely, and a small black spot appears at the base of each kernel where it connects to the cob. Harvesting at this point prevents rotting and pest attack.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi kwraa. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni kɛ ŋmei lɛ tsa lɛ shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Can I plant my corn in small batches at different times so I can harvest fresh corn continuously over a longer period?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmãa bibioo ko. yɛ bei srɔtoi amli bɔni afee ni akpa ŋmãa hee be fɛɛ be yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, this is called staggered planting. By planting small sections of your farm two to three weeks apart, your crops will mature at different times, giving you a steady supply of fresh corn for eating or selling.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. fã bibioo ni aduɔ Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli egbala kɛ otsii 2-3 lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa hee ni okɛyeɔ loo ohɔ̃ɔɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your corn lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow strong and green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea, or adding well-rotted manure, will help the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When the rains become unpredictable, what simple practice can I use to keep my corn crops from drying up in the field?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ baa shi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ manyɛ mikɛ nifeemɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni ŋmãa tsei akagbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can practice mulching by spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of your plants. This layer shades the soil, reduces evaporation, and keeps moisture in the ground longer during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni oookɛshwie otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: If I harvest my corn and put it straight into sacks right away, will the grain spoil?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa ni mikɛwo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ baagbo?

english: Yes, it will spoil. Freshly harvested corn still contains moisture. If you bag it immediately, mold will grow and the grain will rot. You must spread the cobs out to dry thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are hard before shelling and bagging.
ga: Hɛɛ, ebaafite. Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Mold baakwɛ̃ ni ŋmãa lɛ baagboi. Osumɔɔ ni ogbɛ ŋmei lɛ oshwã ni oha egbi jogbaŋŋ. Agbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani ajieɔ amɛhe ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli.

english: How can I protect my stored bags of dry corn from being destroyed by weevils?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa kotokui ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii akafite amɛ?

english: Make sure the corn is completely dry before storage. You can store the grain in hermetic (air-tight) bags like PICS bags, which suffocate insects without needing heavy chemicals, or mix approved storage dust into the grain before bagging.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛto. Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku, ni baaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii. Aloo okɛ sũ ni ato ni awo he odase lɛ afutu dumɔwui lɛ amli dani okɛwo kotoku mli.

english: What is the best way to mark my farm boundaries clearly so neighbors do not mistake my crops for theirs?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makadi miŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni akutsoŋbii lɛ akatɔ̃ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ amɛ nɔ.

english: Planting clear living borders such as cassava rows, lemongrass, or boundary trees like teak around the edges of your field helps clearly mark your land so everyone in the community knows where your farm ends.
ga: Husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei, lemongrass, loo husu tsei tamɔ teak ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni otsɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli faŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ale he ni oŋmɔ lɛ naagbee yɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping them cool and moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa cacao tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential nutrient that helps plants stay healthy, grow strong stems, and produce green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kpakpa, amɛshishifãi lɛ wa, ni amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji aba lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the vine to make food efficiently, which helps produce larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛhoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni afee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes to appear on the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These insects feed on the growing leaves and stems, which can severely reduce your harvest if not managed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onitsumɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they feed the soil and restore nutrients that the maize crop took away.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhaa niyenii ni ŋmãa ejie lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to be dug up and harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ atsa ni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the dirt quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing and competing for nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha muji lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛkayeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any small peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi eda?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinators like bees, which prevents the blossoms from developing into actual fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ, ni no haaa ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt in the hot afternoon but look healthy again the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hewalɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull it from the soil. The leaves shrink to reduce water loss, and overnight they recover as moisture builds back up.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebaahe ejɔ ehe nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye ngmɔ ngmlɛfia nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller plants and weaker yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, tolerate dry weather, and produce higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the plant pulls the nutrient from its older, bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, causing the lower leaves to yellow and die.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. They require living shade trees or companion plants like plantains to shelter them from extreme heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni hiɛ ka loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. In waterlogged soil, standing water starves the tubers of oxygen and promotes fungal growth, causing the cassava roots to rot beneath the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oxygen ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ he, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry, hot winds prevent tomato flowers from pollinating properly. When flowers remain unpollinated or experience extreme heat stress, the plant naturally drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination loo amɛhe ejɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small fruit when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough food to grow thick stalks and produce large yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my stored yam tubers sprouting stems before the planting season even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ po baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy after a period of rest, especially when exposed to warmth and high humidity. Heat signals to the yam that it is time to grow, causing early sprouting in storage.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ akɛ ehe wo he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ tsɔɔ atomɔ lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting into cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree when the weather becomes wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain and dark, humid environments create the ideal setup for Black Pod disease. Raindrops splash fungal spores onto the pods, which quickly infects them and turns the pod and beans black.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ black pod hela baa jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look pale even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that consume water and fertilizer much quicker than your crops can. If weeds are not cleared, they absorb the nutrients intended for your crops, leaving your plants starved.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few of them turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen moved from flower to flower by tiny insects or human hands to set fruit. If the flowers are not pollinated, they cannot form pods and simply fall off the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi biɔ pollen ni kooloi bibii jieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli. loo gbɔmɔ niji koni ekɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aba Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pods ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Madam, what is hand pollination, and how does it help my cocoa farm yield more pods?
ga: Yei, mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ená pods babaoo?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using tweezers or a brush. It ensures almost every flower develops into a full pod, significantly increasing your harvest.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ tweezers loo brɔshi nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi daa ni etsɔɔ fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ. Ehaa nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: What causes the small flowers on my cocoa tree to dry up and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ bibii? Yɛ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Flowers drop off due to lack of pollination, prolonged dry spells, or damage from tiny pests. Keeping the farm properly watered and ensuring pollination helps the flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pollination ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii efiteɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to prune or trim branches from my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps the tree direct its strength into producing pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when planted under shade from plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ plantains tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing plantains beside them creates natural shade umbrellas that keep the soil moist and protect young cocoa leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: How does galamsey mining near my farm affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Te galamsey ni akuɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Illegal mining washes topsoil away, destroys natural water sources, and leaves chemicals in the ground. This damages the soil quality, making it difficult for tree roots to take in nourishment.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhei ni eshiɔ tsofai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer to help my cocoa pods grow bigger?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn yellow, tree growth slows down, or pods remain small and weak, your soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tsei lɛ daa blɛoo. aloo ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cold, overly damp, and shaded environments. Clearing farm weeds and trimming branches lets air flow in to dry the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ tsɔ, edɔ, kɛ hulutsoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Okwaafoi amli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Can I continue growing heavy food crops like cassava inside my farm when my cocoa trees grow big?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Beni mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Food crops can be grown with cocoa when trees are young, but once cocoa trees mature, heavy food crops compete with them for soil nutrients, water, and direct sunlight.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ kookoo adu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ. Shi kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda Niyenii tsei ni tsii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: How can I arrange my farm so that I can easily maintain it alone without hiring extra help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikome too manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe yelikɛbuamɔ kroko?

english: Planting crops in neat, straight rows with clear walking paths makes weeding, hand-pollinating, spraying, and harvesting faster and much easier for a single person to manage.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tɛ̃ɛ, tɛ̃ɛ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ haa jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yaa oya kwraa ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mɔ kome.

english: Why did my young maize plants burn and die after I put chemical fertilizer like urea right around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai tamɔ urea ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers like urea contain strong salts. Putting them directly against the plant stems draws water out of the roots and burns the crop. You should always place fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in a ring or shallow groove.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea lɛ mli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo ŋtayaa ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli.

english: If I keep using chemical fertilizers on my land every season, will it damage my soil over time?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii daa afi Ani ebaafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Continuous use of strong chemical fertilizers without adding organic matter can make the soil acidic and hard, killing useful soil organisms and making it harder for crops to feed in the long run.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ tsu nii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee shiŋŋ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaana niyenii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why does my maize still turn yellow even after I apply urea fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ urea woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, but urea needs moisture to work. If the soil is too dry or flooded with heavy rain, the fertilizer evaporates or washes away before the plant roots can drink it in.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Shi urea he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsu nii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, Ŋmei baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ebaatsɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Can I mix animal manure with chemical fertilizers when preparing my land for planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi afutu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ koni mikɛsaa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, combining manure with small amounts of chemical fertilizer improves the soil structure and helps the ground retain moisture so your crops can absorb the chemical nutrients more effectively.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa fioo ko futu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool and the soil is moist. Applying chemicals under strong midday sun causes them to evaporate into the air instead of helping your crops.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulu ni naa wa ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to save water and protect themselves from drying out during hot weather. The plant goes to rest and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Tsei lɛ baahe amɛhejɔɔmɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin with tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to grow tall and weak instead of producing big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to reduce water loss when the sun is very intense, but persistent leaf curling can also be a sign of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a disease.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa. Shi baai ni yaa nɔ efoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni miigbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted after I spray weedkiller on the grass around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Even if you do not spray crops directly, chemical weedkillers can travel through the soil or drift in the wind, causing stress to the crop's root system and temporarily slowing down its growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa shwieee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ po. Shi tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Can an individual smallholder farmer like me get free advice or soil help from government extension officers?
ga: Ani okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana ŋaawoo loo shikpɔŋ he yelikɛbuamɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛ nɔyeli extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ?

english: Yes, local district agricultural offices have extension officers whose job is to support individual farmers with free guidance on soil management, fertilizer application, and crop health.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ yɛ extension officers ni amɛnitsumɔ ji ni amɛye amɛbua okwaafoi aŋkroaŋkroi kɛ ŋaawoo ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛnamɔ he.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants compete for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. This results in weak, thin stalks and very small or poorly filled corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo ni ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put stakes or wooden poles next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei loo tsei awo sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up off the ground toward the sunlight. Getting plenty of sunlight helps the leaves make food, which is sent down to grow a large, healthy yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni atsu kɛba shi koni amɛyadu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) forces the mother plantain tree to share its food and water. Removing extra suckers allows all the nutrients to go into growing a single, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛja niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii akuu kome ni tsii.

english: As cassava plants pass their mature harvest stage, the plant converts soft starch into tough fibers to support its heavy stems, making the tubers tough, fibrous, and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛkɛfi amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. Rotating crops or adding organic manure restores those missing nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do cowpeas or beans help improve the land for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha tsina loo ŋmeii aha he ni miyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, providing a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ mli lɛ, tsa nɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when heavy rain sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the field for too long, it pushes air out of the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young or exposed cocoa trees shed leaves to conserve water when it gets dry. Without shade trees to protect them from the scorching heat, the intense sunlight damages the leaves and causes them to drop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii loo ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai koni nu ahi mli kɛ́ amɛgbi. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbee shi.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the heat is too extreme or when the soil dries out completely. High temperatures can prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to discard the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo eba loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tso lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by severe heat causing the leaf to fold over to protect its water supply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu nu ni hoɔ lɛ he lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but only produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo yɛ shishi pɛ

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil or fertilizers, it puts all its energy into growing green leaves and stems instead of feeding the roots. To get big tubers, the plant needs balanced soil with enough potassium, which directs food down into the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei eŋɔli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. koni ená yitso agbo Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli. ni kɛ niyenii baa shi kɛyaa yitso lɛ nɔ

english: How can I know that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem. Also, as the underground tubers swell and grow bigger, you will notice cracks forming in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, beni ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ, Obaana ŋmeii ni miifee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning dark blue inside and rotting just two days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi bluu ni mli edɔ yɛ emli ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled out of the ground, its roots react quickly with air and begin to break down internally within 48 to 72 hours. To prevent this, only harvest what you can immediately process, sell, or consume, or keep the tubers covered in moist soil until needed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ebɔi fitemɔ yɛ emli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ Nikpamɔ nɛɛ naa lɛ, nɔ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsu he nii, ohɔ̃ɔ, loo oye amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Aloo okɛ bulb lɛ ato shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛyashi ehe baahia.

english: What makes some of my harvested cassava tubers taste bitter while others from the same field taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi krokomɛi Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Cassava naturally produces compounds that make it bitter as a protection against insects and animals. When the crop experiences stress, like prolonged drought or poor soil, it produces higher levels of these compounds, making the roots taste bitter.
ga: Cassava feɔ nibii ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi. Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ, Ebaajie nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ babaoo kpo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yields when I plant cassava on the same plot two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws a large amount of nutrients, especially potassium, out of the earth as its tubers grow. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil's strength, so rotating it with crops like beans or resting the field allows the land to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, titri lɛ potassium, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmɔji ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How does leaving crop leaves and stems to decay on my field help my soil become more fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miha baai kɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ fite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Decaying plant material acts as natural compost. As the leaves break down, they release stored nutrients back into the soil, feed beneficial soil organisms like earthworms, and help the ground retain water during dry periods.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji baai lɛ fã Ejieɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in between my young cassava plants, or will they steal nutrients from my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Planting groundnuts or cowpeas between young cassava actually helps your crop. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the young cassava while keeping weeds down.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei bibii ateŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmei bibii niyenii ni egbeɔ jwɛi hu.

english: Cassava leaves curl up in hot, dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat. However, it can also be a sign of sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or spider mites, which multiply quickly during the dry season.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni edɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, amɛ baanyɛ afee okadi hu kɛha koolooi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies loo spider mites. ni fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ

english: Will cutting stems from my growing cassava plant to share with my neighbor reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ ni mifoɔ koni mikɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ agba he sane lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, cutting off stems and leaves reduces the plant's ability to capture sunlight. Leaves act as food factories that feed the roots below ground, so removing them early forces the plant to spend energy regrowing shoots instead of swelling its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni afoɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ baa shi. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei ni haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ni ajieɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Which direction should I face the buds on my cassava cuttings when I bury them in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ ofu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be buried with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots must bend around to grow upward, which wastes the plant's energy and leads to weaker sprouts and lower yields.
ga: Esa akɛ afu cassava niji ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle Tsofɔi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ. ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do I need to expose my young nursery seedlings to full sunlight a few days before planting them in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi dani madu amɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This process is called 'hardening off.' Young seedlings grown under shade are delicate. Exposing them to full sun in small amounts gradually builds up their strength so they do not wither or break when transplanted into the harsh field environment.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Harding off’ Dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shade mli lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli fioo lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee shoo fiofio. Wo lɛ hewalɛ Enɛ ji koni amɛkagbo loo amɛkaku kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni mli wa waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees tear into strips when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are naturally designed to split along their veins during high winds to allow air to pass through easily, which prevents the entire tree from being blown over or snapping at the main trunk.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbala amɛhe yɛ amɛ fãji lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ atswa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo akumɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ he.

english: Why should I remove the tiny side branches growing out from my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Removing these small side shoots forces the plant to send its energy and nutrients to the main stem and flowers, resulting in stronger growth and larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Nibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomatoi lɛ daa waa ni tomatoi lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my maize all at once or in small amounts at different times?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli loo fioo fioo yɛ bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Applying fertilizer in small, split doses ensures the growing plant receives nutrients when it needs them most, and prevents heavy rains from washing away unused fertilizer before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii fioo ni ajaa mli awoɔ mli lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ni miida lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to capture more sunlight for growth while protecting the leaves and developing tubers from rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do cocoa farmers plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide temporary shade and retain moisture in the soil, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature and strong enough to survive full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya haa hɔɔŋ be kukuoo mli ni amɛ hiɛɔ sũ lɛ mli fũu mli. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation during hot sunny days, and protects the topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. ni ebuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Why should I pull out extra seedlings if three maize seeds germinate together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui krokomɛi kɛji akɛ ŋmãa yibii etɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When too many plants grow in one spot, they compete for water, sunlight, and soil food, making all of them thin and weak. Removing the weaker ones leaves the strongest plant to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko da babaoo yɛ he kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo he.

english: Why do small green oranges drop off my tree long before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop excess young fruit when they lack sufficient water or nutrients, or when stress causes the tree to shed extra weight to keep the main tree healthy.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo beni haomɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine bɔni afee ni ehiɛ tso titri ni mli wa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to cassava roots if I leave them in the soil for too long past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmei shishifãi anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ?

english: If left in the ground too long, cassava roots become woody, tough, and lose their starch, making them poor in quality for cooking or selling.
ga: Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso, amɛhe wa ni amɛfiteɔ starch. Enɛ haa niyenii ni ahoɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or excessive waterlogging around the roots, which prevents the plant from absorbing necessary nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer before the plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during downpours.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ beaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look wrinkled in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing moisture during hot conditions, but if the leaves stay curled permanently, it usually means sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids are attacking the plant.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa hu? Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ miitutua tso lɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomatoi lɛ amli tsɔi diji kɛ tsɔi ni ebote shishi dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is expanding.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã lɛ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on my cocoa trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp environments. Continuous rainfall and thick shade retain moisture on the pods, allowing fungal spores to multiply and spread rapidly.
ga: Fungs ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your main crops and improves soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa otsei titrii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too hard for the sprout to push through, or if too much water rots the seed before it can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ atsɔ mli, Aloo kɛji nu babaoo ha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my watermelon plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop without forming fruit if there are not enough bees around to pollinate them, or if the plant is stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: How do I know my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do fresh tomato prices drop drastically in the market during peak harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato hee jara baa shi waa yɛ jara nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: During peak harvest, many farmers bring fresh tomatoes to market at the same time. Because fresh tomatoes spoil quickly without cold storage, farmers must lower prices to sell their crates fast.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ tomato hee miiba jara nɔ yɛ be kome too mli ejaakɛ tomato hee fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awooo friji mli. Esa akɛ okwaafoi aba jara shi bɔni afee ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ adekai oya.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away the nutrients from around the plant roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no seeds inside even though they grew plenty of flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ fɔfɔii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil while the pods are forming, or when the soil is too hard for the plant's flowering stems to enter the ground properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miifee lɛ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do all the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience stress from dry weather, intense heat, or insect pests like mirids. The tree drops the flowers to save energy when conditions are not good for growing fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui tamɔ pollen mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi ehiii kɛha aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When the bunch grows heavy, the root system cannot hold the weight, especially during strong winds or when the soil is very soft from rain.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni kuu lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ muji lɛ Shishifã lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ waa kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting inside the barn before the rain even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ po bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural sleeping period after harvest. Once that period ends, warm temperatures signal to the tuber that it is time to wake up and grow shoots, even if it is not yet planted in moist soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ nakai be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ tsɔɔ bɔlb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ aduko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lolo po.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining away. Excess water starves the roots of air and allows fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ hɔmɔ aba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni eha ŋmeii lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why does my maize stop growing taller even though we are receiving plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Too much rain can flood the root zone and drown the roots by removing the air they need to breathe. Excess water also carries away plant food deeper into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu kɛ tsei aniyenii yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus carried into the farm by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my developing tomato fruits turn black and soft while growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium. This usually occurs when watering is irregular and the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my crop yields if there is enough space on the land for all plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei fɛɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops underground for water and fertilizer, and above ground for sunlight. Even with space, weeds grow faster and drink up resources before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ona hulu la Eyɛ mli akɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ moŋ Jwɛi hu daa oya ni amɛyeɔ nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why is the government advising us to plant extra shade trees on our cocoa farms because of the changing weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miiwo ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Changing weather brings higher temperatures and harsh sunlight. Shade trees protect cocoa plants from intense sun stress, lower the temperature on the farm, and help keep the soil moist during dry periods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa baa. Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: How do big trees planted inside my farm actually help my cocoa crops when the weather gets hotter?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ?

english: Big trees block direct scorching sunlight, drop leaves that turn into natural manure, and slow down water evaporation from the soil, preventing your cocoa trees from drying out during hot spells.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo Etsiɔ kookoo tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa farm if the weather keeps getting hotter and I do not plant shade trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu? Ni miduuu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ?

english: Excessive heat and dry weather cause cocoa leaves to burn and drop early, flowers to fall off before fruiting, and pods to dry up, which severely reduces your overall yield.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni baanyɛ aha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why should I plant plantain together with my young cocoa seedlings on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains ni cacao tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as temporary umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture to young cocoa trees while giving you early food and income.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: Won't plantains steal water and food from my young cocoa trees if I plant them close together?
ga: Ani plantains lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When spaced correctly, plantains protect the young cocoa from heat and help keep the soil cool, which provides far more benefit than the small amount of nutrients they share.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ sa lɛ, Plantains buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo fe niyenii fioo ni amɛjaraa lɛ.

english: Is using plantain for shade on my cocoa farm the same as planting permanent forest trees?
ga: Ani shade dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, plantain provides quick, temporary shade for the first 2 to 3 years of a cocoa tree's life, whereas permanent trees provide long-term shade and protection against severe weather for decades.
ga: Dabi, plantains haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: What kind of trees should I look for to plant on my cocoa farm to fight changing weather?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ matao koni madu yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni mikɛwu ashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ?

english: You should plant tall forest trees with high branches that spread out wide—such as Terminalia or Newbouldia—because they provide good shade coverage without crowding the cocoa roots below.
ga: Esa akɛ odu koo mli tsei kakadaji ni amɛniji kakadaji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, tamɔ Terminalia loo Newbouldia, ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo kpakpa ni amɛhaaa kookoo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ayi obɔ kɛteke nɔ.

english: Should I plant shade trees at the exact same time I plant my cocoa seedlings, or should I plant them earlier?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ madu lɛ mra?

english: It is best to plant your shade trees or plantains early or alongside your young cocoa so that their protective shade is already growing by the time the cocoa faces harsh sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔwui mra loo yɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ebu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ kookoo nɔ.

english: Why does the ground under big trees stay moist even when there has been no rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: The leaf canopy of big trees blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, while fallen leaves trap moisture in the soil like a natural blanket.
ga: Tsei wuji ahe shade lɛ tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa egbi. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ mɔɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ adebɔɔ mli kuntu.

english: Does full sunlight help cocoa trees produce more pods than trees growing under shade?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Full sun can produce more pods initially if you use a lot of fertilizer, but under hot, changing weather conditions, unshaded cocoa trees get stressed quickly, get sick easily, and die much younger.
ga: Hulu ni eyi obɔ baanyɛ aha pods babaoo aba shishijee mli kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii. Shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, kookoo tsei ni bɛ hulutsoo lɛ haoɔ oya, hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and die when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? ni baanyɛ aha hulutsoo abɔle tso lɛ he

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baa ni mli tse lɛ he koni ekashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower part of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves the remaining nitrogen up to feed new green leaves, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and low moisture stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to preserve energy and water rather than spend resources developing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi haa tomato tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why do I need to thoroughly dry my harvested corn before packing it tightly into big storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui wuji ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grains trapped in bags with leftover moisture generate heat and sweat, creating ideal conditions for mold, dangerous toxins, and grain-boring insects to spoil the entire harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli ni nu ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa baa. ni feɔ shihilɛi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: The heavy rain creates high humidity and damp conditions that spread fungal spores (Black Pod disease) across the farm through water drops splashing on pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi ni gbɛɔ fungal spores (black pod hela) eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pods lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and rot if I leave them in the ground too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, tsei ni fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?
