english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, the plant begins storing less starch and converts its roots into tough fibers to survive, making them susceptible to soil-borne fungi and decay.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmei fioo ko toomɔ ni ebaatsɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli ŋmei ni wa koni ehi shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting inside the storage barn even before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock (dormancy period). Once that rest period ends after a few months, warm barn temperatures trigger the seed to sprout automatically.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa (wɔɔ be) beni nakai wɔɔ be lɛ baa naagbee yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my corn make the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil for crops like corn to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛtsu nii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit, which damages the leaf tissues as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni kɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during strong winds when they are carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii wuji miifã gbɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; they rely on shallow root networks near the surface. The heavy weight of the fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy and easy for wind to pull out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdamɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Tso yibii akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ haa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ, ni ehaa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key food it needs to grow strong. The plant moves available nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, showing it needs fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ he miihia bo.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer tender growing leaves inside the plant funnel. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the leaf whorls can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or soapy water helps clear these pests so healthy leaves can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem mli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛje kpo.

english: Why do my cocoa pod husks turn black and dry up on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp weather and thick shade. Clearing weeds around the tree base and pruning excess branches allows sunlight and dry air to stop the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa. Jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when rain stops and starts unpredictably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni ebɔi nɛmɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Rather than planting after the very first rainfall, wait until the rain is consistent and the soil stays moist up to hand depth for a few straight days. This prevents seeds from germinating and drying out if rain pauses.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ nine mli gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruits are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Planting suckers deeper into the ground and supporting the stems with sturdy wooden stakes keeps them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ mafo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water collects around them in hard or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain off easily so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Kasava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow crooked and small instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand downward easily. Hard or stony soil blocks the tuber's growth, forcing it to bend or stay small, so clearing stones and heaping soft topsoil into tall mounds gives best results.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ tuber dalɛ naa. ni nyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe loo efee bibioo No hewɔ lɛ, tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atoɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ baaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants get stressed by high afternoon heat or dry soil, which prevents proper pollination. Watering plants consistently at the base helps keep the flowers healthy enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ shishi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I pick my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Green cocoa pods contain immature seeds with poor oil and sugar content, leading to bitter, low-quality cocoa beans. Waiting until pods turn bright yellow or orange ensures full development and better beans for market.
ga: Dumɔwui ni edarako ni fɔ kɛ sugar faaa yɛ mli lɛ yɛ green cocoa pods lɛ amli. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa kwraa ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa jara nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK and improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby can help lower temperatures so the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Young cocoa pods (cherelles) often dry up and turn black due to natural thinning or fungal diseases like black pod. Pruning heavy tree branches to let sunlight and air into the farm reduces this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahewɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them thin, weak, and produce much smaller yields than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and support my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ afi mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb sticks so their leaves can catch sunlight to build big tubers underground. Weeds block sunlight and steal nutrients, reducing the size of your final harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei aniji anɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Jwɛi tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Extra suckers steal food and water from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a much bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a natural umbrella to protect them for their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after light rain, but never during heavy downpours. Moist soil helps roots absorb nutrients immediately, whereas heavy rain washes expensive fertilizer away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the growing centers of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that destroys maize growing points. Spraying the recommended pest treatment early in the morning directly into the center funnel of the plant stops them quickly.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ hei ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaha amɛkpa oya.

english: Should I pour fertilizer at the base of my crops or spray it directly on the leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi loo mikɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It depends on the fertilizer type and your crops' immediate needs. Granular fertilizers applied at the soil base nourish plants slowly through their roots, while liquid foliar fertilizers sprayed on leaves give plants a quick nutrient boost during critical growth stages.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa onibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fiofio kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii oya yɛ be mli ni edaa waa lɛ.

english: Can crops absorb food through their leaves if I spray liquid fertilizer on them?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie amɛnɔ?

english: Yes, plant leaves have tiny pores that can absorb liquid nutrients directly. This method, called foliar feeding, is useful for quickly correcting nutrient deficiencies, though crops still need healthy soil and root feeding to thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe baai yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ foliar feeding. Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ oya. Shi kɛlɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ shishifã niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know which type of fertilizer is best for the soil in my local area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different soil areas lack different nutrients. You can look at leaf signs—like yellowing leaves which often mean a lack of nitrogen—or ask your local extension officer for a soil test to know the exact fertilizer blend your land needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ bɛ niyenii srɔtoi. Obaanyɛ okwɛ okadii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Aloo bi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ extension agent lɛ ni efee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa koni ele bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiamɔ nii ahe nii eha.

english: What is a mist blower machine, and why would I use one instead of a manual knapsack sprayer?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ afua nɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ enɛ atsu nii yɛ tsɔne ni akɛ niji shwieɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: A mist blower is a motorized sprayer that uses air to blast chemicals into fine droplets. It helps you cover large land areas and tall crop canopies much faster and more evenly than a hand-pumped sprayer.
ga: Mist blower ji tsɔne ko ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai anɔ ni akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsofai bibii anɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohaa hei wuji kɛ tsei akutsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ oya ni efeɔ ekome fe nine pɔmp ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ.

english: How many times in a season am I supposed to spray chemical treatments on my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Spraying frequency depends on the specific chemical, pest pressure, and crop type. Always follow chemical package instructions or extension advice, because spraying too often wastes money and can harm your crops or the soil.
ga: Bɔ ni afɔɔ tsofa lɛ afɔ̃ɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ damɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Pest pressure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahenɔi Be fɛɛ be lɛ Nyiɛmɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi loo sɛɛkuu gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ asɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, eheɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ eye onibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: What safety precautions should I take when spraying agrochemicals on my field?
ga: Mɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi esa akɛ mafee kɛji mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Always wear protective gear like boots, gloves, and a nose mask. Avoid spraying on windy days to prevent fumes from blowing back onto you, and never spray during hot midday sun, which can burn plant leaves.
ga: Wo hebuu nibii tamɔ atadei, glɔvs kɛ hiɛ he mask be fɛɛ be. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ nɔ koni lasu lɛ akaku esɛɛ kɛba onɔ. Ni kaashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How do I clean and maintain my spraying machine so it lasts a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ mi-sprayer lɛ he ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Rinse the chemical tank with clean water after every use and run clear water through the nozzles to prevent clogs. Regularly check seals and filters for wear and tear, and store the machine out of direct sunlight.
ga: Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tanki lɛ he kɛji okɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛ nu ni mli tse atsɔ tsɔne lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɔne lɛ naa. Kwɛmɔ seals kɛ filters lɛ daa kɛji amɛfite. ni oha tsɔne lɛ akashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What are biological fertilizers, and how are they different from regular chemical ones?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Biological inputs are made from natural sources like beneficial microbes, plants, or organic waste. They build long-term soil health and are safer for the environment, whereas chemical fertilizers provide immediate nutrients but can wear out soil over time.
ga: Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tsei, loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ nii amli. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ekolɛ ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to prune my tree crops, and how does cutting branches help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mitsei lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes dead, weak, or overcrowded branches. This opens up the tree so sunlight and air can reach all parts, reducing diseases and encouraging the plant to put its energy into producing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ajieɔ. Enɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa helai baa shi ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ awo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the best time of day or season to prune my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbi lɛ mli be loo be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaakpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Pruning is best done early in the morning or during dry periods. Cutting during dry weather allows wounds to heal quickly without inviting fungal diseases, while cool morning hours reduce stress on the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei lɛ leebi loo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ehaa pilamɔ lɛ tsaa oya ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, leebi ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves turning yellow and dropping before the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is stressed, either by a lack of nutrients in the soil, water shortage, or an early stage of a disease like Cocoa Swollen Shoot. Identifying the cause early helps you treat the plant before the disease spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. kɛji akɛ eji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni faaa loo helai ni yɔɔ shishijee mli, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu, ni oyoo nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni otsa tso lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning trees allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baakpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why does an extension officer recommend cutting down an entire cocoa tree if only a few branches look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Certain viral diseases, such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot, spread throughout the entire tree's sap system before all leaves show physical signs. Removing the whole sick tree stops insects from carrying the virus to neighboring healthy trees.
ga: Helai komɛi ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli fɛɛ dani baai lɛ fɛɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii akpo. Kɛ́ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii ni kɛ hela lɛ aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need taller plants like plantains growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture needed for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ehaa hulutsoo ni emɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth and drop leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya ni amɛbaa fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds suck water out of plants quickly. Crops shed leaves naturally to conserve water in their stems and roots so they can survive the dry season until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛto nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the thick trunk of the tree instead of on the thin outer branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers and pods on their main trunk and thick branches because these sturdy parts are strong enough to support the heavy weight of full cocoa pods as they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ fãi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɛɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii lɛ he kɛji eda kwraa.

english: How does cutting off healthy branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes excess leaves and branches that consume energy without producing pods. Trimming them directs the tree's water and nutrients straight to flowering areas and developing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni yeɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efeee lɛ. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa hei ni fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, while their tops block sunlight from reaching each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to yield a full harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ayiteŋ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa.

english: How do weeds growing on the ground harm my cocoa trees if they aren't touching the leaves?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkɛ baai lɛ ebɔko?

english: Weed roots underground aggressively soak up water and soil food meant for your crops. Weeds on the ground also hold trapped moisture, creating a damp environment where harmful fungi can easily breed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi jwɛi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afɔ yɛ mli mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Tired soil produces plants with slow growth, pale leaves, and small pods even when there is enough rain. Adding fertilizer restores essential nutrients to the ground so crops can grow strong again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo, ni amɛbaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted even after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe moŋ?

english: If the soil is too dry, too acidic, or if roots are damaged by underground pests, the crop cannot absorb food. The fertilizer will just sit unused on top of the dirt, wasting your money.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Eyɛ acid tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii. Fertilizer baata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsuuu nii. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: How can I stop the fertilizer I apply from sitting on top of the dry soil and getting wasted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-fertilizer lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni efite?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve and enter the roots. Always mix fertilizer lightly into damp soil or apply it just before a light rain so the plants can actually drink it in.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli fioo. Aloo okɛwo mli fioo dani nugbɔ anɛ koni tsei lɛ anu nu diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why have my crops completely stopped growing even though the rains have been good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lolo?

english: When roots are attacked by invisible pests like nematodes or fungus, they lose their ability to take in water and nutrients from the soil, causing the plant to starve in the middle of plenty.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ nematodes loo fungi lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei babaoo

english: What causes the stems and tips of my crops to turn soft and start rotting?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛnaatsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ?

english: Rotting in plant stems is usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases that thrive when there is too much water sitting around the roots or when plants are crowded too closely together.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green plants losing their shiny look and becoming dull and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves lose their healthy green shine when the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when diseases damage the plant's internal pipes that carry food from the soil.
ga: Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji hela fite tso lɛ mli tsɔnei ni kɛ niyenii yaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the growing eyes on my stored seed yams turning dull and rotting before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ hiŋmɛii wuji ni amɛgboɔ dani be ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam eyes rot when stored in hot, dark, humid places where fungi and rot-causing insects multiply, killing the growing tip before it ever gets into the ground.
ga: Sweet potato buds lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ fa babaoo yɛ lɛ. ni ogbe ŋmeii ni miida lɛ dani amɛgbee shikpɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are developing a sickness before the whole farm gets destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ fite?

english: Look out for early signs like dull leaves, slow growth, wilting during cool parts of the morning, or dark spots on stems; catching these signs early lets you remove sick plants before disease spreads.
ga: Taomɔ mra okadii tamɔ baai ni edɔ kɛ dalɛ blɛoo. Egbɔjɔɔ gbɛkɛ mli leebi loo eyɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ Omɔ okadii nɛɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the immature fruits falling off my crops before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni ekwɛko lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Crops drop their immature fruit when they are under severe stress from drought, nutrient loss, or disease; the plant sheds the fruit to save its own life.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛyibii ni eshɛko lɛ kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shishi. Yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo hela ni baa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baajie eyibii lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark and dropping off the branches while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ amli edɔ ni amɛmiigbee niji amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is often Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that attacks cocoa pods in wet and heavily shaded conditions, causing the pods to rot, turn black, and drop off.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji black pod disease Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni tutuaa cocoa pods yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa pods lɛ fiteɔ, efeɔ ediŋŋ, ni egbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are my vegetable plants dropping all their flowers instead of turning them into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, lack of water, or insect damage, which prevents successful pollination and stops fruit from forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ trukaa, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo koolooi fitemɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does putting crops inside a sheltered house help them grow better than planting outside?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shia lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: A greenhouse protects delicate crops from extreme weather, direct scorching sun, heavy rain, and destructive pests, creating a controlled environment where plants can grow faster and yield higher quality produce.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ he ni tsei baanyɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting tall shade trees or plantains alongside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the ground until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo loo lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their dark green color and helps the plant build food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy with plenty of green leaves, but leaves me with tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eshi mi kɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or excess water, it puts all its growth energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ mli kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make my next crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and deposits it naturally into the soil through their roots, fertilizing the land for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal valuable water, sunlight, and ground nutrients right out of the soil before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu ni jara wa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay green longer during a hot dry spell if I cover the soil around them with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch, which shades the earth and stops the sun from evaporating precious ground water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni ehaaa hulu la atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they experience water stress, as the plant protects itself by saving energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my young maize leaves right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn baa lɛ trukaa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures and humidity after early rains cause armyworm eggs to hatch rapidly, and the tiny caterpillars feed heavily on soft, young maize leaves as their main food source.
ga: He ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Eyeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ akɛ niyenii titri ni jɛɔ mli baa.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves in maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space prevents overcrowding and allows the roots to expand into larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ anaa, ni ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing disease and leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Koni hela kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves scorching and turning brown in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside young cocoa shields the leaves from sunburn and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana kɛ cocoa bibii lɛ, ebaabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ mabɔle plantain tso wulu lɛ he?

english: You should leave only 2 or 3 strong suckers of different ages around the main stem. Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tsei bibii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he. Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by viral infections spread by small insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Using neem oil spray and keeping the soil consistently watered helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies mli kɛbaa loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii ni okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and mulching around the roots help keep flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can also dig up a few pods; if the inside of the shell has dark brown veins, the groundnuts are ready to harvest.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ pods fioo komɛi hu atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or dried leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, traps soil moisture so crops survive longer dry spells. It also keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: I am seeing small green caterpillars eating my maize leaves, why are they appearing so fast?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miiye mi-abele baai lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ eje kpo oya nakai lɛ?

english: These are likely pests like Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the underside of leaves. They reproduce quickly in warm weather and attack young, tender leaves because they are easy to eat.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli. Amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛtutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeli waaa.

english: Why is the spray chemical I bought not killing the insects on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Pesticides often fail if they are mixed with dirty water, applied in full sunshine when pests are hiding, or used at the wrong dosage. Using the same chemical repeatedly can also cause insects to build resistance to it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji futu mli. Kɛtsu nii yɛ kpo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli. loo akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni esaaa mli Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi aná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai.

english: Why shouldn't I place dry fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong salts that need moisture to break down. When placed directly touching the stem on dry soil, the high salt concentration draws water out of the plant and burns the roots and stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni biɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani efite. Beni akɛ tso lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni eshãa shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and burnt after I applied fertilizer to save them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli koni eye ebua amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once or putting it on crops when the soil is very dry causes fertilizer burn. Crops need moist soil so the roots can safely drink diluted nutrients without getting scorched.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome loo okɛ tsei fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia tsei bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much water, which smothers the roots and prevents them from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani eda ni etsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: In extreme heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water and usually recovers by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yield when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of using their energy to produce big fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soil and dry conditions. They are aggressive feeders that steal water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Amɛji niyenii yelɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow well if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain warms up the dry soil, but it is often followed by a long dry spell. If young seeds sprout right away, their delicate roots will dry up and die before the main rainy season fully sets in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and stop growing when the river overflows onto my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ beni faa lɛ hoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When floodwater covers your land for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Without air, the roots drown and cannot absorb food or nutrients from the earth, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to stop growing.
ga: Kɛ nu afua nui ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ kpaɔ daamɔ.

english: Are there specific crops I can plant near riverbanks that will not rot when the water rises suddenly?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ faa lɛ naa ni fiteŋ kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa?

english: Crops like rice and sugar cane are naturally built to handle wet ground because their stems can transport air down to their roots under water. Tubers like yams and cassava will rot quickly if left in standing water.
ga: Abɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eye ebua hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Tubers tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava baafite oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them near the river in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ faa lɛ masɛi leebi?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's way of protecting itself from losing water. During very hot hours, heat pulls water out of leaves faster than roots can drink it, so the plant curls its leaves to shield itself from the strong sun.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my land is dry enough for planting after heavy rain flooding?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa kɛ nu afua sɛɛ?

english: You can test your soil by taking a handful and squeezing it into a ball. If the soil crumbles easily when you press it lightly, it is ready for seeds; if it forms a sticky wet ball or drips water, planting now will cause seeds to rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nine ni oooŋɔ ni okɛmimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya beni onyɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ. Kɛji akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ loo nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ bianɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Why do crops grow much faster on land where floodwaters recently left behind thick mud?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida oya waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ, ni eshiɔ muji ni mli edɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Floodwaters carry rich mud called silt from upstream, which is full of naturally decayed leaves and minerals. This mud acts like a strong natural fertilizer, giving your new seeds rich food to start growing quickly.
ga: Nu afua lɛ kɛ muji ni fa babaoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ sũ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baa, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, eyi kɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ shika tsuru. Nɛkɛ muji nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa. Ha odumɔwui heei lɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛje shishi amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants fall over easily after heavy rain makes the ground near the river soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ egbɔjɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes too muddy, roots lose their firm grip on the earth. Additionally, plants in very wet ground keep their roots shallow near the surface instead of growing deep into the soil for strong anchor support.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo muji tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Mohu ɔ, du kɛ ya zugba a mi saminya konɛ e ná he wami.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but very small tubers when I plant it right beside the riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei yɔɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Riverbank soil often contains high amounts of nitrogen from flooded material. Too much nitrogen encourages cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall green leaves instead of storing energy underground in big tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ni jɛɔ nibii ni nu ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ faai lɛ anaa lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ yucca tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ zugba a sisi ngɛ yi wulu ko mi.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them in dry soil before the main rainy season officially begins?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: If seeds absorb only a small amount of moisture from light early rains, they will begin to sprout inside the soil. However, if full rains do not follow immediately, the intense heat will dry out and kill the young sprout before it reaches the surface.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ŋɔ nu fioo pɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shishijee be lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast on my tomato leaves during the humid rainy period near the river valley?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tomato baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni bɛŋkɛ faai jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungus thrives in warm, damp air with high humidity. River areas hold heavy moisture in the air during rainy weather, which creates the exact wet conditions leaf diseases need to multiply and spread quickly across your farm.
ga: Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli. Faa hei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni foli helai ni yɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. In nature, they rely on taller trees to act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the ground moist and protecting delicate leaves from sunburn while roots develop.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he beni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential food crops need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rain or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after light rain. If you apply it right before a heavy downpour, the rushing water will wash the fertilizer off your field before the crop roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the earth and keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is making tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark waste in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant and eat the tender green leaves, which can weaken the crop if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai eŋɔli bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling up and twisting into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. They suck the juice out of the leaves and can spread plant sicknesses that twist the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahelai ni fiteɔ dalɛ hee lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a broad, open sunlit field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to block the intense heat while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant feels too stressed, it sheds flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ tsɔ lɛ, Ebaajie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They stretch upward trying to reach the light, making them weak and spindly.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Ha efee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and you see cracks forming in the dirt around the base of the stem from the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii ni eba yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni jɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ efuu yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the mound before they can grow any leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani baai baa lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot when the soil is overly waterlogged without good drainage, or if the seed tubers already had small wounds or insect damage that let disease in before planting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji dumɔwu lɛ yitso lɛ yɛ pilamɔ bibioo ko loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ hela baa dani adu.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and thin when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight over the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed well and grow strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii kpakpa kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: How do weeds hurt my pepper crops even if I give the field plenty of water?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmɔji lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil nutrients, water, and space directly from your crops. Even with sufficient water, the weeds crowd the peppers and starve them of essential soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ he ko mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Jwɛi hu buaa amɛhe naa kɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: My cassava leaves are turning yellow and curling up, does this mean the plant is sick?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ?

english: Yes, leaf yellowing and curling are signs of plant illness, often caused by tiny insects spreading viruses or a lack of soil nutrients. Just as humans show fever when sick, plants change leaf color and shape when unhealthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso hela he okadii. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛbaa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Taakɛ adesai jieɔ atridii kpo kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei tsakeɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛhe su kɛji amɛbɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is adding fertilizer to the soil the same thing as giving medicine to a sick crop?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛaawo sũ mli lɛ kɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, fertilizer is like nutritious food that feeds the soil to keep crops strong, while pesticides or fungicides act as medicine to cure specific insect attacks or fungal infections.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa kɛha kooloi pɔtɛɛ ni tutuaa loo ŋmeii helai.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Taller shade trees or plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the young plants cool and moist until they are mature enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop their leaves during the hot afternoon but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ ni ja ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: During very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Drooping is their natural way of protecting themselves to save water until the weather cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ obu ohe koni okɛbu nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why does my farm produce fewer crops each year if I plant on the exact same plot without letting the soil rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the earth. Farming continuously without giving the soil a rest period or adding organic matter leaves the soil tired and empty, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ ni efee efolo. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize, or will they harm each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa loo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: They actually help each other. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer that feeds hungry crops like maize.
ga: Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do my crops fail to grow properly if I sow seeds right before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Seeds need consistent water in the soil to sprout and grow strong roots. Planting right before the dry season leaves the soil too dry, causing seeds to fail to germinate or young sprouts to die of thirst.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni hoɔ daa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni shishifãi ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi tsɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ loo tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ kumai hewɔ.

english: Why do some crops like vegetables yield food in a few months while tree crops like oil palm take years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi tamɔ aduawai woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei fɔ heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Vegetables have short life cycles and put all their energy into fast growth and quick fruit production, whereas tree crops invest their early years in building deep roots and strong trunks before producing fruit for many years.
ga: Aduawai wala be kukuoo ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii oya. Yɛ be mli ni tsei heɔ be yɛ shishijee mli koni Koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛwo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil and attack future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my rice fall over flat on the ground just when the grains are ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging. It happens when stems become too weak to hold heavy rice heads, usually because of planting seeds too close together, applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, or strong winds.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa beni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmãa ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing the flowers from setting fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii saminya.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during hot afternoons to save moisture. By reducing the surface area exposed to direct heat, the plant prevents itself from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulutsoo baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni abaajie lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baatsi ehe naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with tiny harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to reach the light instead of building thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fa tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la he, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do cassava roots rot and turn watery inside the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays flooded and cannot drain water. Roots need air in the soil to breathe, and standing water starves them of oxygen.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting grains saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmaa ni abua naa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose strength and yield potential over time. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, grow evenly, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why do weeds grow aggressively when my crops are small but slow down when my crops grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ daraaa lɛ? Shi ani esɛɛ tsɛɔ be mli ni mitsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Weeds need direct sunlight to germinate and grow. As your crops grow larger, their leaves form a broad shade over the dirt, blocking light and stopping weed growth naturally.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara Amɛbaai lɛ feɔ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ la naa ni ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my corn leaves and dark powder in the middle leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It feeds on young maize leaves and hides inside the center whorl during the day, leaving behind ragged leaf holes and dirt.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Shi bu yɛ baai ni etse kɛ muji amli yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to make leaves green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the soil when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around them because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ fee ekome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus carried by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and make the plant sick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hela mɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds before the fruit bunches are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy tops, and tiny worms in the soil called nematodes often eat away the roots, making the plant unstable.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ. ha tsei akafee shiŋŋ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water, dropping blossoms to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Gbee shi koni okɛ hewalɛ ato koni onyɛ ohi shi.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the barn even when I haven't planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ kwraa?

english: Yam tubers are living stems that naturally break dormancy after a period of rest, using the water and nutrients stored inside themselves to start growing new shoots.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato yɛ emli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjeɔ ŋmeii heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: Why do I get less harvest every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa nii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs without giving the soil time to rest or recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field help the crop I plant next season grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts work with good bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving free food in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow better when water stays on the field during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?
