english: Standing water keeps the soil soft for rice roots to spread easily while naturally smothering weeds that would otherwise steal light and food from the rice.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ hu yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are buyers refusing to purchase my rice harvest this season even though the crop yielded well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahɔɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmaa lɛ hi moŋ?

english: When many farmers harvest and bring the exact same crop to market at the same time, the market gets flooded. This oversupply makes buyers slow down purchases and drives prices down until the excess grain is cleared.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nu baaho jara lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ nibii ni amɛheɔ lɛ, ni ehaa jara baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmaa ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Should I rely on the government to buy all the rice I harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nɔyeli lɛ nɔ koni ehe ŋmãa fɛɛ ni akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, government buying programs have limited budgets, fluctuating quotas, and specific buying schedules. Relying solely on state purchases can leave you stuck with unsold crops if they reach their buying capacity.
ga: Dabi, nɔyeli lɛ nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ bɛ shika babaoo. Nɔyeli nibii ni aheɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ akã shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he ni abaanyɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller rice grains when I replant immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa bibii beni miduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Replanting immediately without letting the land rest strips the soil of essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Without time to recover, the soil leaves the next crop malnourished, resulting in weak plants and smaller grains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ashiii he ko ni eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji be bɛ ni akɛbaatsake Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant and harvest perfume rice three times on the same field in one year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ shii 3 yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: While perfume rice matures quickly enough to allow three cycles in a year, doing this continuously exhausts the soil's fertility and builds up crop pests, leading to declining yields over time unless heavily managed.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ daa oya bɔ ni sa ni eshɛɔ shii etɛ yɛ afi mli moŋ, shi nakai feemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa ŋmeii baa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ja atsu he nii waa

english: How long should I leave my rice field to rest before planting the next set of seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maha ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe dani madu dumɔwui akuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Giving your field a rest period of a few weeks or rotating it with leguminous crops like cowpeas allows the soil to rebuild organic matter and breaks pest and disease cycles before the next planting.
ga: Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ otsii fioo komɛi loo okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli dani aduɔ nɔ kroko.

english: What crop can I plant after my rice harvest to make the soil rich again?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Planting leguminous crops such as cowpeas, groundnuts, or beans after rice traps nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for your next grain crop.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does perfume rice grow and mature faster than my regular local rice varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ daa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya fe mimaŋ ŋmãa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Perfume rice varieties are bred specifically to have a short growth cycle. This means their natural genetic behavior allows them to flower and produce grains quicker than traditional long-duration local rice.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara be kuku. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ su lɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui oya fe blema maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops mature unevenly when I plant them late around July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ edaaa pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ July naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting around July catches the changing pattern of the rainy season. Inconsistent rainfall during the crop's establishment phase causes seeds to germinate at different times, leading to uneven growth across the field.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ July he lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ ehaa lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ tso lɛ shishitoo be mli lɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why does my stored perfume rice lose its sweet scent after keeping it for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛto lɛ he ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: The natural aromatic compounds in perfume rice evaporate when exposed to warm air, light, and humidity. Proper drying and storing the grain in sealed, airtight bags are necessary to preserve the aroma.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, la, kɛ hulutsoo mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ he miihia waa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if the plants lacked nutrients while forming seeds, or if the harvested grains were dried unevenly under harsh hot sun before milling.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ dumɔwui lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ agbi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ dani ashɛreɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is stopping the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu yɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: Extreme heat or lack of water stresses the tomato plant, causing the flowers to dry up and fall off before they can be fertilized and turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by small insects like whiteflies spreading the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which weakens the plant and reduces the growth of tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ sinava hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ sinava mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuberous lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do holes appear in the leaves of my cabbage crops early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the soft foliage, which reduces the plant's ability to catch sunlight and grow a solid head.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baa lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la lɛ shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha amɛfee mɛi ni yitsoŋ wa.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak, thin stalks and small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do cocoa farmers plant plantain trees on the same land with young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in strong sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide wide leafy shade to protect the cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on a piece of land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, refreshing the land for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with seeds already adapted to your soil, allowing them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than newly planted domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛyɛ dumɔwui ni etsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni adu ehee yɛ shia lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly under the sun before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moisture left in harvested grains causes dangerous mold to grow and attracts pests like weevils, which can destroy your entire harvest while it is stored.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, ni baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow strong. Adding manure or a nitrogen fertilizer when the soil is moist will restore green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ eda waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination. Do not apply in dry soil because it can burn the plant roots, and avoid applying right before heavy rains so it doesn't wash away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kaawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni akafɔ.

english: Which direction or position should I place cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ loo he esa akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ?

english: Plant cassava stems at a slanted 45-degree angle with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Ensure at least two to three nodes are buried underground so strong roots can form while leaves sprout above.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmei yɛ 45 degree angle mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kwɛmɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, afu ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni wa aba yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ daa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra small branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Pruning removes weak branches that waste the tree's food without producing pods. It also allows sunlight and breeze to flow through the tree, which keeps humidity low and protects pods from black pod disease.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egbɔjɔ ni fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tswaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ black pod hela he.

english: What is eating small ragged holes inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-cone lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the young leaves. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract early in the morning or evening when they are active can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning soft and black before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium or water while forming fruit. Watering regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and dry out quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water through their broad leaves in hot, dry air. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass mulch keeps soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu akatsɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in dry soil waiting for the first rain. Once water hits them, they germinate quickly to capture sunlight before crop seeds can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ amɛmiimɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ nu tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and builds up maize-specific pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen naturally in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni efee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ Okɛ ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaakɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which helps them make food for large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni fungal leaf helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my land makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly. Giving your tomatoes steady watering and a bit of shade during the hottest part of the day helps them hold onto their flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ha otomatoi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves, creating a living umbrella that provides essential shade and keeps the air humid for the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into thick tubers. If planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall stems with small, thin tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni eyɛ yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture deep down before the sun gets hot enough to evaporate it. Evening watering leaves wet moisture on the leaves all night, which can cause fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ. dani hulu lɛ mli adɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaatsɔ la Nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni baanyɛ ekɛ fungal leaf disease aba.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crop is still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and cannot fight against aggressive weeds for soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the resources they need to grow strong root systems.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap. Spraying the leaves with a mix of mild soap water or neem oil drives away the insects and allows new leaves to grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Small insects called weevils lay eggs inside the seeds around harvest time, and their young eat their way out during storage. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers keeps oxygen out so the pests cannot survive.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ni amɛbii lɛ baaye kpojee lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off naturally, leaving mostly top leaves. You can also test by carefully digging up one root; if it is firm and full of starch inside, the whole field is ready.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi ŋwɛi baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Obaanyɛ oka lɛ okwɛ hu kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ ashikishaŋ babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo.

english: What does potassium do for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni potassium feɔ kɛhaa mi kakao lɛ?

english: Potassium helps cocoa trees grow strong trunks, resist diseases, and produce larger, heavier cocoa pods, which leads to a much richer harvest.
ga: Potassium yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa, amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ cacao tsei wuji ni tsii. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer like potassium?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ potassium?

english: If your cocoa trees produce small pods, have weak stems, or turn yellow at the leaf edges, it usually means the soil is running out of essential nutrients like potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ, eyɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni bɛ hewalɛ loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium.

english: What is the best way to make my cocoa crop thrive and produce more yield?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi cacao tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Feeding your trees proper soil nutrients like potassium, keeping weeds clear, and ensuring good shade management will allow your cocoa to thrive and produce maximum pods.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa, tamɔ potassium haa tsei, ni haa jwɛi lɛ mli tseɔ. Ni shade nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa baaye abua ni cocoa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ pod yibii babaoo aba.

english: Can proper plant nutrients help my cocoa trees survive dry weather?
ga: Ani tso mli niyenii ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, nutrients like potassium help cocoa plants manage water inside their stems and leaves, making them much stronger against drought and harsh sun.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ehe wa waa yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Is it worth discussing farm finances with my family to buy fertilizer for my cocoa?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ akɛ weku lɛ baasusu ŋmɔ mli shika he koni akɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kookoo?

english: Yes, talking with family or supporters to secure funds for small farm inputs like potassium fertilizer can multiply your yield, making the investment well worth it.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ weku loo mɛi ni yeɔ amɛbuaa lɛ awiemɔ koni ana shika kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii bibii tamɔ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebaanyɛ eha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Ha shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ afee nɔ ni sa

english: How do small investments in farm inputs help my farming business grow?
ga: Te shika fioo ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Buying essential items like quality fertilizer or proper pruning tools directly improves crop health, turning small costs into bigger harvests and higher income.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi loo nibii ni sa ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahemɔ baaha otso lɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ shika bibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ awo nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo babaoo kɛ shika ni fa babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods stay small instead of growing full and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛdara kwraa ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Small pods often happen when the soil lacks key plant foods like potassium during the flowering and pod-growing season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii titrii, tamɔ potassium, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ be mli.

english: Does harvesting cocoa year after year weaken the soil on my farm?
ga: Ani kookoo ni akpaa afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ?

english: Yes, every cocoa pod harvested takes away nutrients from the soil. Replacing nutrients like potassium ensures the land remains fertile for future crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo tso fɛɛ tso ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some cocoa farms give continuous good yields while others fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu nyɛɛɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Farms that yield well are routinely supplied with soil nutrients like potassium and kept healthy, whereas neglected soil loses its power to support good crop growth.
ga: Okwaafoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii tamɔ potassium yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: What simple steps can I take as a beginner to start improving my cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛi bibii komɛi ni manyɛ matsɔ nɔ akɛ shishijee mɔ koni mabɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ?

english: Start by clearing weeds around the base of your trees, pruning dead branches, and applying nutrients like potassium to nourish the roots.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ooojie kɛ niji ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do some seeds like oil palm or soybean give us rich oil when crushed, while maize seeds do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei fɔ loo soybeans, Eyɛ mli akɛ ehaa fɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ aŋmɔ Be mli ni ŋmãa dumɔwui haaa?

english: Certain seeds store their energy reserves as fats and oils rather than starches. When crushed or heat-treated, these oil-bearing seeds release those concentrated fats, which can then be collected and used for cooking.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtoɔ lɛ toɔ yɛ fɔ kɛ fɔ mli moŋ fe ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ atswa loo awo la mli lɛ, Dumɔwui ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ jieɔ fɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ amɛhe. ni abaanyɛ abua naa ni akɛhoo nii

english: Why is red palm oil so deep red in color, and does that mean it is good for cooking food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ red palm oil lɛ ji red palm lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ehi kɛha nihoomɔ?

english: The deep red color comes from natural nutrients called carotenes, which the human body turns into Vitamin A. This red color shows that the oil carries high nutritional value for healthy growth and vision.
ga: Su tsuru ni mli kwɔ lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ carotene lɛ mli. ni adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ vitamin A Su tsuru nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔ lɛ mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛha dalɛ kpakpa kɛ hiŋmɛigbelemɔ.

english: If I harvest all the beans and oil-bearing seeds from my farm, does that take goodness away from my soil?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo mu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaajie kpakpafeemɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes. As crops grow, they draw vital nutrients out of the earth and lock them inside their fruit and seeds. When you harvest and carry those crops away, those nutrients leave the field, meaning you must feed the soil again with compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ tsei dara lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛ yɛ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui amli. Kɛ́ okpa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni okɛ amɛ tee lɛ, Nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baashi ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do bean plants help make my soil richer for other crops like maize?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Beans belong to a special family of plants that work with helpful microbes in the earth to pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This creates natural plant food that fertilizes the ground for nearby crops.
ga: Beans fata tsei akuu krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young bean plants turn pale yellow and grow weak when they are under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Plants use sunlight like food to build up their leaves and stems. Without direct sunlight, the plant cannot make energy through its green leaves, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la tamɔ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni amɛ baa kɛ amɛ tsei lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ amɛfee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I bury my bean seeds very deep in the soil when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-beans lɛ futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: A seed only contains a tiny package of stored energy to push its shoot up through the dirt. If planted too deep, it runs out of food energy and dies in the dark soil before its leaves can reach the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Niyenii hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crop seeds and leaves more during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa midumɔwui kɛ tsei ahe baai yɛ nugbɔ be mli fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Moisture and warm temperatures create the best environment for insect eggs to hatch quickly. The rain also makes plant leaves soft and tender, giving pests plenty of fresh food to reproduce rapidly.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kooloi bibii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ oya. Nugbɔ hu haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa niyenii hee babaoo ni amɛkɛbaafɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers without forming any pods when the sun becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to the crop, making the pollen dry out so flowers cannot form seeds. To save its remaining water and protect itself from drying up completely, the plant naturally drops its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. gĩ pollen lɛ Fɔfɔ lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Enɛ baaha nu ni eshwɛ lɛ akaje mli, ni ebaaha ohe akagbi kwraa. Tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop is drowning from too much rain water in the farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely waterlogged, plant roots cannot breathe oxygen from the dirt. This causes the roots to rot, making the leaves turn yellow, go soft, and wilt even though there is water everywhere.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu eyi mli obɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my harvested crop seeds spoil and grow mold if I store them right after harvesting without drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikɛto beni mikpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni migbiko lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested seeds hold a high amount of natural water inside them. Mold spores and bacteria need moisture to thrive, so storing damp seeds encourages mold to grow rapidly and rot your harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli. Fungal kɛ bacteria mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ahe hewalɛ, ni ebaaha onibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my crops seem to get sick more often during the hot, dry season instead of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela shii abɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli moŋ fe hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot and dry conditions put stress on plants, making them weaker and more vulnerable to certain heat-loving diseases and pests, whereas regular rain helps plants stay hydrated and strong.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni sumɔɔ latsaa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Can strong sunlight and hot weather cause diseases to suddenly break out on my farm?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, extreme heat can weaken crops and create the exact warm environment that certain dormant plant germs need to rapidly multiply and show symptoms.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ aba ni tsei amli helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi aya hiɛ oya ni amɛjie hela lɛ he okadii akpo.

english: Why do I see fewer crop sicknesses during the heavy rains compared to sunny periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto hulutsoo be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cooler temperatures during the rainy season slow down the growth of heat-seeking plant germs, and extra water helps the plants maintain their natural defenses.
ga: He ni mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei amli helai ni taoɔ dɔlɛ lɛ daraaa fioo. Ni nu ni fa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu mli.

english: Does intense sunshine kill crop diseases or does it make them worse?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai loo eha amɛhe afee shoo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: While sunlight can dry up moisture that some fungi need, severe heat can also dry out and stress your crops, making it easier for dry-weather diseases to attack them.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, hulu la lɛ haa fɛ̃i, ni ŋmeii komɛi taoɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbi ni ehao amɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baatutua mɔ.

english: Is it possible for plant diseases to travel through the air to my farm?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ tsei ahe helai baatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many crop diseases are caused by microscopic spores that float in the air and can easily be carried by wind from neighboring farms to your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛba onibii amli lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a disease on my farm is carried by the wind?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli?

english: Airborne diseases usually spread quickly across large sections of your field at the same time, especially during windy or dry periods, rather than starting in just one isolated patch of soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ oyale lɛ mli hei babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooje shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kome pɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops from illnesses that spread through the air during sunny weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Planting tall trees or crops as windbreaks around your farm boundaries can block windborne spores, and keeping crops well-watered reduces heat stress.
ga: tsei kakadaji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ koni etsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne ni ebɔle Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Ni kɛ́ aha ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to pay attention to which season a crop illness appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe helai baa lɛ?

english: Tracking seasonal patterns helps you predict when a disease will strike so you can spray preventive treatments or adjust planting dates before the risky weather starts.
ga: Be mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ asɛɛdii baanyɛ aye abua bo ni otsɔɔ be ni hela baaba. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa loo otsake gbi ni okɛbaadu lɛ dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why does a crop illness disappear during the rains only to return when the sun comes back out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai lɛ laajeɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji hulu lɛ tso pɛ?

english: Some disease organisms do not die during rainy periods; they simply go dormant because conditions are too cool, and then wake up as soon as warm, sunny weather returns.
ga: Helai komɛi gbooo yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Amɛwɔ pɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, te shi kɛji hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: What steps can I take to prepare my crops for the hot period when diseases usually attack?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ be mli ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ? bei pii lɛ ebaa koni ebatutua

english: You can prepare by providing shade where possible, applying mulch to keep the soil cool and moist, and applying appropriate preventive treatments before the hot weather sets in.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa ohe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni oooha kɛji ebaahi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ mulch atsu nii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa atsu nii dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in my young maize leaves, and how does this affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. If left unchecked, they destroy the leaf area needed for the plant to make food, drastically reducing crop yield or killing the plant early.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Efiteɔ baa he ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ afee niyenii lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa loo ehaa tsei lɛ gboiɔ mra.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Excessive moisture and poor air circulation allow fungal spores to spread rapidly across pods, causing them to rot before ripening.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny and bunched together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This distorted growth is often caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit. As these pests feed on plant juices, they stunt growth and stop the plant from developing fruit properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa nɛɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu. Amɛbaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When the weather gets too hot or dry, pollination fails, and the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Ni tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. The plant puts all its energy into building tall stems and green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of older leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow, so when the soil runs low, the plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to keep the young growing leaves alive.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni baai bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up during the hot afternoon sun and open back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural self-defense mechanism against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to sunlight, conserving its internal water so it does not dry out during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and very heavy tops. If microscopic worms called nematodes or root rot fungi weaken the roots, strong winds can easily push the heavy plant over, especially when the soil is wet and loose.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei ni tsii kɛho mlɛo. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward light, increasing photosynthesis while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa kane lɛ he. Ehaa fotosintɛsis yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry straw or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko woɔ mli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi.

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the root area cool, stops weeds from taking over, and adds nutrients to the soil as the dry leaves decay.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ baai ni egbi lɛ fite.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow and dry up at the tips before the crop is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen or isn't getting enough water. Giving the rice nitrogen fertilizer at the right growth stage keeps the leaves green so they can feed the growing grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo ŋmãa mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni akɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but very few grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ nɛkɛ lɛ? Baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo?

english: When rice gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing tall leaves instead of seeds. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium helps the plant focus on building heavy, healthy grain heads.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmãa babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kakadaji amli yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni wa lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why does rice need to grow in standing water, and will it spoil if the water stays too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Rice plants thrive in shallow standing water because it prevents weeds from growing and keeps soil temperature steady. However, you must drain the field a few weeks before harvest so the plants mature evenly and the stems don't rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ejaakɛ enɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do birds suddenly start invading my rice farm when the heads start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi miibɔi mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli tutuamɔ be mli ni yitsei lɛ miibɔi feemɔ lɛ?

english: When rice grains begin to form, they fill with a sweet, milky liquid that birds love. This 'milky stage' lasts about two to three weeks, so you need to scare birds away until the grains harden into solid rice.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmaa bɔi feemɔ Kɛji akɛ aha okpo lɛ niyenii pɛ lɛ, nu ni ŋɔɔ ni tamɔ mliki ni okpoi sumɔɔ lɛ baayi mli obɔ. ‘Mliki fã’ nɛɛ heɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okɛ okpoi lɛ akabɔ he kɛyashi ŋmaa lɛ baatsɔ ŋmãa ni wa.

english: How can I tell the exact time my rice is ripe so I do not waste my yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ baashɛ koni mikafite mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Your rice is ready when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a golden-yellow color and the lower parts of the stem begin to dry. Harvesting too early leaves you with light, undeveloped grains, while waiting too long causes grains to fall off onto the ground.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do some of my rice stalks produce light, empty husks with no grain inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ? Ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ mli?

english: Empty husks happen when the plant experiences drought during its flowering stage or gets attacked by insect pests like stem borers. Without enough water and nutrients during flowering, the husk cannot fill up with grain.
ga: Bark ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ nyɛŋ ahi dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why must I dry my harvested rice before taking it to be processed by a machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi dani mikɛ tsɔnei atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested rice contains too much moisture, making the grains soft. If soft rice goes into a milling machine, it gets crushed into paste; drying the grain makes it hard enough for the machine to peel the outer skin off cleanly.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo tsɔ. Ha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo Kɛji ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tee ŋmãa lɛ mli Agbɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni efeɔ ashikishaŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɔne lɛ akɛ ebaajie kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when they are threshed and processed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Be ni afeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Rice grains break easily if they were harvested when over-ripe or dried too fast under harsh direct sunlight. Drying your harvested crop slowly in thin, shaded layers hardens the kernels and keeps them whole.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ tsɔ loo amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko wo tsei ni akpa lɛ amli fiofio lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni ebaaha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I put the leftover rice straw and husks back into my farm soil after processing?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ beni atsu he nii agbe naa lɛ?

english: Yes, rice straw and husks are rich in plant matter. Plowing straw back into the soil or composting the husks improves soil fertility and helps the soil hold moisture for your next crop season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ tsei wala. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ ku sɛɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo okɛ jwɛi lɛ fee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my rice seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When rice plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. This causes weak, thin stems that produce fewer and smaller grain stalks compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni woɔ dumɔwui bibii fioo kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during the dry season even when I water them a little bit every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu fioo haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Light daily watering only wets the top layer of soil, encouraging shallow roots. Deep, less frequent watering encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where moisture stays longer.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ fioo daa gbi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni afɔɔɔɔ lɛ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do farmers in dry Asian countries manage to grow crops successfully even when rain is scarce?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Asia maji ni nɔ egbi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: They rely heavily on efficient water management techniques like drip irrigation, rainwater storage ponds, and soil mulching to ensure minimal water is wasted and crops get steady moisture.
ga: Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nu ni hoɔ, nugbɔ nu ni akɛbuaa nu naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ waa koni amɛkwɛ akɛ nu fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the air is cool, allowing water to soak deep into the soil for the roots rather than evaporating quickly in the afternoon sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to reduce their exposed surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out under high heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my crop turn yellow and drop off when dry weather lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the crop sheds its older lower leaves to reduce its overall water demand so it can keep its stem and young growing leaves alive.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛba nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ shi. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ tsei bibii kɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How does heavy flooded water in my farm affect the roots of my cassava crops?
ga: Te nu afua ni naa wa ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess standing water cuts off air to the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot, which prevents the crop from absorbing food and water properly.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: What simple technique can I use to keep water in the soil from drying out too fast under the hot sun?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni baatsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the ground and lowers soil temperature.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ baa shi.

english: Does adding animal manure to my farm help the soil stay moist longer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil, improving its ability to hold onto water so your crops have access to moisture even during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do some farmers make raised earth mounds or ridges before planting instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa gɔji loo ŋmeii dani amɛduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges improve water drainage during heavy rains to prevent root rot, while keeping the topsoil loose for roots to spread easily.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei haa nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why do some crops need deep soil to survive drought better than crops with shallow roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ he hiaa tsei komɛi koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops with deep taproots can reach water stored deep underground during long dry periods, whereas shallow-rooted crops only rely on topsoil water that dries out quickly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu pɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and curling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛkɛbu amɛtso lɛ he tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of mature bunches, especially in wet soil. Supporting the stem with strong wooden or bamboo stakes helps hold the plant upright during storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua panicles ni eda lɛ ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Tso loo ŋmeii ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Yellowing from the bottom up is a sign that your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava produce long stems and leaves above the ground, but tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of storing starch in the root tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight for food production while keeping them away from damp soil diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why are the flower buds on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells cause heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to save water and energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nyɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ajie nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get dark spots on their leaves after a long rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Frequent rain splashes soil bacteria and fungi onto the lower leaves, creating a moist environment where foliage diseases like blight quickly spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli helai tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why did the edges of my crop leaves dry up after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ beni akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer directly against the stem or roots draws moisture out of the plant, causing leaf burn. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the plant stem in a ring.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni shãa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby provides protective shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa tree establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ maa ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to produce energy for stem and root development. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant yield larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai taoɔ hulu la babaoo koni ena hewalɛ kɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Soil pests like root nematodes can also weaken the base, so supporting the main stem with a bamboo pole prop helps keep the plant upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ root nematodes baanyɛ aha shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso fiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have bushy green leaves, but when I dig them up, the tubers are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Shi be ni mitsa lɛ, mina akɛ yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Soil needs balanced nutrients with enough potassium to encourage thick tuber growth below the ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli koni eha tuber ni mli tse lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni akpa ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When planted after heavy-feeding crops like maize, they naturally restore fertility to the soil without cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheee nɔ ko.

english: Heavy rains flood the soil surface and create runoff that carries loose fertilizer away into streams or neighboring fields before plant roots can absorb it. Fertilizer is best applied to moist soil when light rain or steady moisture is expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ ni ehaa nu hoɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ aya faai loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ fioo. aloo eyɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites feeding on the underside of leaves and transferring plant viruses. Treating the plants with organic neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil spray loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look wilted in the hot afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The leaves temporarily wilt to reduce surface area and conserve moisture, usually springing back up by evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkwɛɔ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between wet and dry. Consistent watering and mulching around the base keeps soil temperatures steady and preserves flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ daa Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and flowering at the top, but no corn ears are growing on the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiwo fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa toi ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Maize plants fail to produce ears when they lack sufficient nitrogen or suffer from water stress right when the central silk and tassels emerge. Proper feeding and moisture at the flowering stage are critical for ears to form.
ga: Abɛi tsei nyɛɛɛ afee toi kɛji amɛbɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛnaa nu mli haomɔ kɛji siliki kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ je kpo. Niyenii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be mli fɔfɔii lɛ ahe miihia kɛha toi feemɔ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantains alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade, protecting young cocoa seedlings from harsh direct sunlight while maintaining soil moisture.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yes, but you need proper spacing so the cassava does not block sunlight from the young plantain suckers or compete too heavily for underground nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni oná gbɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ akatsĩ hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ plantain dumɔwui lɛ ahe loo ekɛ ehe akawo niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up to conserve moisture when water is scarce. Adding organic mulch around the base helps keep the soil moist for longer.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji nu bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the mother plant for water and nutrients. Removing them allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing a larger fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai akui wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my plantain plant is mature enough to start producing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: A plantain plant usually reaches maturity and begins flowering after producing 30 to 40 healthy leaves, which takes about 8 to 12 months depending on soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi kɛji amɛná baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ 30 kɛyashi 40, ni enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm smaller and lighter than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Small bunches usually indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium or organic matter, which can be improved by adding compost or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting suckers too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weaker stems and smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni jwɛi lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall over when pests like nematodes or stem borers attack the roots and underground stem, destroying the plant's anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested plantains from ripening too fast before I take them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi plantain lɛ naa koni akakpa mra tsɔ dani akɛya jara nɔ?

english: Store harvested plantain bunches in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area, and keep green bunches separated from already ripened fruits.
ga: Kɛ plantain tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ogbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛjɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the growth and root health of my plantain crop?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While heavy rainfall encourages leaf growth and fruit development, excess standing water in poorly drained soil can rot the roots and damage the crop.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Shi nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Do my cocoa trees really breathe air like humans and animals do?
ga: Ani mi cacao tso lɛ muɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ adesai kɛ kooloi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees have tiny, invisible openings on their leaves that allow them to breathe in gases from the air. They use this air along with sunlight to stay alive and grow, just as humans need air to live.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni anaaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa cacao tso lɛ muɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛhi shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do crops feed themselves if they do not have mouths like us?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ amɛhe aha tɛŋŋ? Be mli ni obɛ naabu tamɔ wɔ?

english: Crops drink water and suck up nutrients from the soil using their roots. Their green leaves then use sunlight to turn that water and soil food into energy, which acts as their food.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ amɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I spend time just walking through my cocoa farm to look closely at the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli koni mana tsei lɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are living things that show signs when they are sick or thirsty. Walking through your farm regularly helps you spot problems like pests or leaf diseases early before they kill the tree.
ga: Cacao tsei ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni jieɔ hela he okadi kpo kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ loo kumai ye amɛ. Nyiɛmɔ ni ofeɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona naagbai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsei ahe helai mra. dani tso lɛ baagbo

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die so easily if I leave them without care for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are tender like newborn babies. Their roots are shallow and cannot reach deep groundwater yet, so even a few days of harsh sun or weed competition can dry them out completely.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. No hewɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi po ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo jwɛi akaŋshii baanyɛ aha amɛgbi kwraa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are thirsty during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai yeɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When cocoa trees lack water, their leaves will start to droop, turn yellow, or curl up at the edges. This is their way of showing that they are stressed and losing moisture too fast.
ga: Beni nu bɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ baabɔi shwiemɔ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ebɔle eshishigbɛi lɛ ahe Enɛ ji gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wither under the hot afternoon sun but wake up in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Shi te shi leebi?

english: In hot afternoon sun, plants lose water faster than their roots can drink it from the dirt, so they droop to save energy. Overnight, the roots catch up on drinking, making the leaves firm again by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ nii ni anuɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Can soil get tired and weak just like a human being?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ tamɔ adesai?

english: Yes, as crops grow year after year, they pull goodness and nutrients out of the earth. If you do not give the soil a rest or add manure and organic matter, the ground becomes tired and can no longer feed new crops well.
