ga: No ji anɔkwale, beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa afi fɛɛ afi lɛ. Amɛjieɔ kpakpafeemɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ je lɛ mli. Kɛji ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii heei jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe kookoo dumɔwui ni midu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are very quick at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because your cocoa seedlings are delicate, weeds will easily crowd them out if you do not clear the farm.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, o-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ waaa. Ebaafee mlɛo akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaho kɛji ojieee oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my cocoa tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers need proper water, good soil health, and tiny insects to turn into pods. If the tree is weak, sick, or lacks water, it will shed its flowers because it does not have enough strength to carry pods.
ga: Nu ni sa he miihia fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛ kooloi bibii ni baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji tso ko bɛ hewalɛ, hela mɔ lɛ, loo nu efo emli lɛ, ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt it, or does it help the tree live better?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baafite lɛ loo ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning extra or dead branches does not hurt the tree; it helps it. Removing unnecessary branches allows air and sunlight to reach the healthy parts and prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeee tso lɛ awui; eyeɔ ebuaa. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or is getting drowned by too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eefo nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fataa he Dumɔwui ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, groundwater, and soil food. Giving each seed its own space allows the roots to spread and grow full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I have to make big mounds of soft earth before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ babaoo dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into long, thick tubers. If planted in hard ground, the tubers cannot grow easily, leading to small, bent, or stunted yields.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni etsɔ tsei kakadaji ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ adara mlɛo. Enɛ haa nibii bibii, ni ebɔle loo ni egbɔjɔ baa.

english: Cassava leaves fold up in intense heat to save water from evaporating. As long as the leaves recover in the evening, this is a natural protective behavior that helps the crop survive dry periods.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ la ni naa wa mli koni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra stems (suckers) draw water and nutrients away from the mother tree. Removing all but one or two suckers ensures all the plant's energy goes into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi (suckers) gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii agbo kome ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits start rotting on the bottom when the vines touch the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ wain tso lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil carries tiny fungal spores and dampness that infect tomatoes when they lay directly on the earth. Staking tomato stems off the ground keeps the fruits dry and protected from soil rot.
ga: Fungal spores bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ aha tomatoi aná hela kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tomato tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do armyworms hide and eat inside the heart of my maize stalk instead of outside on the big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworms seek out the softest, newest tender leaves at the center of the stalk because it provides rich nutrition and protects them from sunlight and birds while they feed.
ga: Armyworms taoɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after a very heavy rainstorm hits right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain hardens topsoil into a tight crust that small sprouts cannot push through, or floods the soil so seeds choke from a lack of air. Planting at the right depth protects seeds from getting trapped.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tsei bibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. impenetrable Aloo nu afua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a open, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni mɛi yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sun because their tender leaves burn easily and their small roots cannot suck up water fast enough. They need fast-growing crops like plantain planted nearby to act as living umbrellas and provide shade for the first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ hu shãa. E nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ dumɔwui, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings upside down forces the new buds to grow downward into the dirt before turning upward. This wastes the plant's energy, making it weak and severely reducing the size and number of tubers you harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni okpaa lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​baa shi waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This struggle leaves you with tall, skinny stalks that easily fall over and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ta nɛɛ haa onáa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight to make food. Staking spreads the leaves out so they catch maximum sunlight, which feeds the underground tuber and makes it grow thick and heavy.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni efee niyenii. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves too much standing water in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Why does putting dry chicken manure on my land make my vegetables grow better than planting in plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi fata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa nɔ lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in natural plant food like nitrogen and phosphorus that feeds the crops as it breaks down. It also improves the soil structure so it holds moisture longer during dry days.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã lɛ mli tsei niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛfiteɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds in my farm slow down the growth of my crops so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like silent thieves on your farm; they suck up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops and block daylight. Clearing them early removes this obstacle so your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark green dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the funnel of the maize plant where it eats the newest leaves before they unfold. Spraying targeted treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyeɔ baai heei fe fɛɛ lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛmamɔ hiɛ lɛ shwie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsofa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear rotten cocoa pods and dead leaves away from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie kookoo ŋmɔji ni efite kɛ baai ni egboi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Old, rotten pods carry the spores of the black pod disease. If left on the ground or tree, rain drops will splash the disease from the decaying pods onto healthy fresh pods, destroying your farm's output.
ga: Pods ni egboi lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛ black pod hela lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tso nɔ Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni egboi amli kɛyaa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. ni fiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, sudden periods of drought, or lack of soil nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water and suffocating the plant roots. Adding manure or fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rain water stay trapped on top of my field instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil or heavy clay prevents water from soaking into the earth. Mixing organic matter like dried leaves or compost into your soil helps loosen it up so water can drain naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ haaa nu abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli atse bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli kɛjɛ ehe.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sun. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid enough for cocoa trees to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Hefatalɔi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. The plant drops flowers to save energy and protect itself until water and cooler temperatures return.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ba amɛnɔ. Tsei baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Maize consumes specific nutrients heavily every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil, leads to lower harvests, and encourages pests. Rotating with crops like groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi waa daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu atsɔ ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi ni ekanya tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatswa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my main crop make the soil richer?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots decompose, they leave behind free plant food that nourishes nearby crops.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water and soil food much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi hɔmɔ ni yeɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Keeping fields clear of infested plants stops the insects from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do tiny beetles destroy my stored maize grains even inside a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli po lɛ?

english: Grain beetles (weevils) thrive if grain is stored while still damp. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun before storing it prevents insect eggs from hatching and destroying your harvest.
ga: Grain beetles (moths) baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto lɛ, no tsiɔ kooloi bibii akui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ̃ ni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and twisting even though I don't see any insects eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves twist and turn yellow because of tiny, invisible germs called viruses, which are often carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Even though you cannot see the germ with your eyes, it multiplies inside the plant's sap and stops it from producing good tubers.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ helai bibii ahewɔ. Atsɛɔ nibii ni anaaa lɛ akɛ virus. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Bei pii lɛ, amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ onyɛɛɛ okɛ ohiŋmɛii ana helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ moŋ, Shi eshwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli ni ekpaa ŋmeii kpakpai feemɔ.

english: My neighbor's maize farm is dying from a sickness; how can I keep that sickness from jumping over to my own field?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miigbo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nakai hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plant sicknesses can travel through the wind, splashing rain, insects, or even on tools and clothes. You can protect your farm by planting a border of tall grass, removing sick plants immediately, spraying early, and avoiding walking straight from an infected field into your healthy field.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ nitsumɔ dadei kɛ atadei po amli. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ adumɔ akɛ husu nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ mra ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛmiiya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why does the extension officer tell us to cut down a whole cocoa tree when only a few branches look swollen and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo cocoa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni niji fioo komɛi pɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efuu ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease is caused by a virus that travels throughout the inside of the tree. Even if only one branch shows swelling, the entire tree is already infected, and tiny mealybugs will carry that virus from your sick tree to all the healthy cocoa trees around it if it is not removed.
ga: Cocoa bloat hela lɛ jɛɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso nine kome pɛ jieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ efuu moŋ, shi No mli lɛ, hela lɛ emɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ momo. kɛ mealybugs bibii Ekɛ hela lɛ jɛɔ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ajieee

english: Why do my tomato plants get dark spots on their leaves and rot much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔi diji ni amɛgboiɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity and wet leaf surfaces, which are perfect conditions for fungal sicknesses to grow. Fungal spores float through the moist air and splash up from the soil onto leaves, quickly multiplying and causing black spots and rot.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni efɔ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ adalɛ. Fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Amɛshwereɔ oya, ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How did Fall Armyworms destroy my whole maize field in just a few days when I only noticed a few caterpillars last week?
ga: Bɔ ni Fall Armyworms lɛ Kpata Mi-Abɛi Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ Fɛɛ Hiɛ yɛ Gbii Fioo Komɛi Amli Otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ mina.

english: Fall Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs at once, and when the caterpillars hatch, they grow very quickly and eat constantly. A small group of tiny worms can turn into thousands of hungry caterpillars in just a few days, consuming an entire field if not treated early.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ shikome. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Edara oya ni eyeɔ nii daa. Kplukai akuu bibioo ko baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii akpei abɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli. Eheɔ he fɛɛ he kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why should I clear weeds around the edge of my farm if they are not directly touching my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ? Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ

english: Weeds act as hidden breeding grounds for pests like whiteflies and aphids, as well as plant viruses. Insects feed on the wild weeds, pick up diseases, and then fly into your farm to spread those diseases directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ whiteflies kɛ aphids fɔɔ yɛ. Virus ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ Kooloi yeɔ koo mli jwɛi, amɛheɔ helai, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfoɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛgbɛ nakai helai lɛ amɛshwã onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I cut stem cuttings from my old cassava plants that produced small tubers, will those cuttings grow into healthy new plants?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso momo ko nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani nakai niji lɛ baatsɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: No, if the original plant was weak or infected with a virus, the stems carry that same sickness inside them. Planting infected stems passes the illness straight to the new crop, so it is better to buy certified disease-free stems for planting.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ shishijee tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo hela ko emɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ emli. Tsoi ni hela emɔ amɛ ni miida lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya tsei heei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni awo he odase akɛ ooodu.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep wilting and dying in the exact same spot in my farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Certain plant diseases live in the soil for many years even after the old plants are gone. When you plant peppers in that same infected dirt, the soil germs enter the roots again and block the tubes that carry water up into the stems.
ga: Tsei ahe helai komɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, kɛ́ tso momo lɛ etee po. Kɛji odu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, Helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ ni amɛtsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Can using my cutlass on a sick plant pass the sickness to my healthy crops?
ga: Ani mi-dagger ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie hela lɛ kɛya miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, sap from a sick plant sticks to your cutlass blade when you cut or prune. When you cut a healthy plant next, the germs enter the fresh wound, which is why you should wash your tools with soap or clean them over a flame between uses.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛ́ ofo amɛ loo ofo amɛ. Kɛji okɛ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baabote pilamɔ hee lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ samla loo la ni mli tse afɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe yɛ be ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ lɛ.

english: If I pick off and burn the first few spotted leaves I see on my plantain plants, will it help save the rest of the crop?
ga: Kɛ miŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ baa he ni minaa yɛ dumɔwu ko nɔ lɛ ni mishã lɛ, Ani ebaahere ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ayiwala?

english: Yes, removing and burning early spotted leaves reduces the total amount of fungal spores or germs on your farm. This stops the sickness from multiplying and spreading to nearby healthy suckers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ojie baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ ni oshã amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi. Enɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is a nurse crop, and why should I plant one next to my delicate young crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔs tso? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu yɛ midumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe?

english: A nurse crop is a fast-growing plant grown alongside delicate seedlings to shelter them from harsh sunlight, strong winds, and soil erosion while their roots establish.
ga: Nurse tsei ji tsei ni daa oya ni daa yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi beni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛhe lɛ he.

english: Is it better to harvest my crops early for quick money or wait longer for them to mature?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra? Koni oná shika oya loo omɛ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Waiting for crops to reach full maturity yields significantly heavier total produce weight and higher quality, bringing in much higher total income than small early harvests.
ga: Ni aaamɛ ni tsei lɛ adara lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shika fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ fa fioo fe shishijee ŋmaa lɛ.

english: How can I set up my farm layout now so that it is easier to manage when I grow older?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ bianɛ koni mafee nɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ beni midaa lɛ?

english: Investing in low-maintenance perennial tree crops and proper spacing early on reduces heavy labor needs later in life, allowing the farm to yield high returns even when physical strength declines.
ga: Ni akɛ shika awo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esaaa kwraa lɛ amli kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nitsumɔ ni tsii ni he hiaa yɛ wala naagbee lɛ baa shi. Ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ naa shika babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ baa shi moŋ.

english: Why should I cut away healthy branches or early flowers instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji loo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Removing excess flowers or branches directs the plant's energy and water into the remaining produce, resulting in larger, heavier, and healthier harvests rather than many tiny, low-value yields.
ga: Fɔfɔi loo niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ kɛyaa yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nibii ni dara, ni tsii, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe nibii bibii ni jara waaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my whole farm at the same time on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in staggered batches ensures a continuous harvest over time, spread-out labor, continuous cash flow, and protection against losing everything if bad weather hits at once.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ yaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. nitsumɔ mlijaa shika ni yaa nɔ kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni baafite kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ ba shikome.

english: How does feeding my soil proper nutrients increase the actual weight of my harvest in kilograms?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni niyenii ni sa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ kilogram mli?

english: Balanced soil nutrients help plants build stronger cell walls and store more water, sugars, and starches in their fruits, directly increasing harvest weight and overall yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa wala yibii gbogboi ni mli wa. ni ehiɛɔ nu, sugar, kɛ starch babaoo yɛ aduawai lɛ amli Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Will letting my land rest without crops for a season actually help me get more yield later?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mahã mishikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli yɛ be ko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Resting land allows soil organic matter to rebuild naturally and restores nutrient levels, resulting in much higher overall crop yields when you start planting again.
ga: He ni ajieɔ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ehee ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ fa babaoo kɛji oje dumɔ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: If I crowd more crop seedlings closer together, will I harvest more crop weight overall?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa tso lɛ fɛɛ muji babaoo?

english: No, crowded plants compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to stunted growth and lower total harvest weight compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa fioo ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I plant fast-growing vegetables or long-term cash crops like cocoa and oil palm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo shika ni anáa be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei fɔ?

english: Combining short-term food crops for immediate cash with long-term cash crops creates immediate income to survive while building long-term wealth for the future.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni akɛaafata he koni akɛfee shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ shika ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa anáa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛha wala kɛ agbɛnɛ hu be kakadaŋŋ mli ninamɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be.

english: How does good storage right after harvest prevent me from losing overall crop weight?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni nibii kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsĩ minaa koni mikaba tso lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ shi?

english: Proper pest-free and dry storage prevents moisture loss, rotting, and pest damage, ensuring you do not lose kilograms of yield before selling at the market.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ naa. fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Enɛ haaa ofite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ kilogrami babaoo dani okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base early in the season keeps the leaves green and boosts yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shishigbɛ lɛ he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, this stored nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji tso shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ashiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm early and applying an approved control measure directly into the leaf center (whorl) prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ (rings) lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite he ni ŋmɔji lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing properly during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack during dry, hot weather. Spraying with neem oil or recommended insecticides keeps these insects away so leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Baai lɛ baafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep scorching and dying when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive harsh direct sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby provides protective shade and keeps the air humid while the cocoa establishes.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo aba koni ebu he ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do I know when it is safe to plant my seeds after the first rain of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain can be misleading because the ground may dry up quickly if rains stop for weeks. It is best to wait until the soil is wet down to about wrist depth so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni lakaa mɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into full sunlight, which helps the vine manufacture food to build big underground tubers, while also preventing soil diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the field during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much water, cassava roots cannot breathe and fungi spread quickly. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni ŋmei lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) prevents sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without producing any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry up before insects or wind can pollinate them. Mulching to keep roots cool and ensuring regular watering helps flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce wide leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close to each other, their root systems compete for the same underground space, soil nutrients, and water, which prevents the tubers from swelling into thick roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu kɛyashi amɛbaafee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green, so when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my land make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested, that natural nitrogen remains in the soil to nourish the following crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa tsei lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry chemical fertilizer on my crops during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into a form that plants can drink up safely. If applied to dry soil, concentrated fertilizer salts draw moisture out of plant roots, causing root burn and damaging the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni tsei baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Eshãa shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the central growing whorl of my young maize plants so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms seek out the tender, soft, and nutrient-dense inner leaves at the core of young maize plants where they can easily feed and shield themselves from predators.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ taoɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna niyenii yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even after I have added fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing and aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can absorb them, depriving your main plants of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa yɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees produce fewer pods if I leave the extra water shoots on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji mishi nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Water shoots, or chupons, are fast-growing branches that consume large amounts of nutrients and water from the main tree without producing cocoa pods, taking away energy needed for flowering and fruit development.
ga: Buds, loo chupons ji tsei niji ni daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high or when the plant experiences severe water stress, causing the plant to abort flower production to save its own moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe. Enɛ haa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔii feemɔ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli nu lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield less than new certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Hybrid crop seeds are bred to produce a high yield only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their specialized vigor in the next season, resulting in smaller harvests and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ faaa, ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: What does it mean when people talk about 'hybrid' maize seeds?
ga: Kɛ́ mɛi miiwie ‘hybrid’ ŋmãa dumɔwui ahe lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are created by crossing two distinct, high-performing parent plants. This combination creates a seed that grows stronger, resists diseases better, and produces a much higher yield than traditional seeds.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛtsɔ nyɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ haa dumɔwui ni daa waa lɛ baa. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ

english: What is an OPV maize seed, and how is it different from other seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji OPV ŋmãa dumɔwui ni te amɛsoro amɛhe yɛ dumɔwui krokomɛi ahe amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: OPV stands for Open-Pollinated Variety. These plants are pollinated naturally by wind or insects. Unlike hybrids, seeds harvested from an OPV crop can be saved and replanted for a few seasons without a big loss in yield.
ga: OPV damɔ shi kɛha Nɔ ni Akɛwoɔ Mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei nɛɛ amli. Esoro lɛ yɛ hybrid srɔtoi lɛ ahe Abaanyɛ ajie dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ OPV tsei amli lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ bei 2-3 mli ni yibiiwoo lɛ fiteee babaoo.

english: How do I decide whether to buy hybrid seeds or OPV seeds for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mahe hybrid dumɔwui loo OPV dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Choose hybrid seeds if your goal is the highest possible yield and you can afford to buy new seeds every year. Choose OPV seeds if you have a lower budget and want the option to save your own seeds to replant next season.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛji oti ni ma ohiɛ ji yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ. Ni obaanyɛ ohe dumɔwui heei daa afi. Halamɔ OPV dumɔwui kɛji oyɛ shika fioo. Ni oosumɔ ni okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui lɛ ato koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Why are hybrid maize seeds more expensive to buy than regular seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa lɛ jara wa fe daa dumɔwui ni aheɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds require specialized scientific research and careful manual work by seed companies to produce every year. While they cost more upfront, the extra grain they yield usually covers the cost and brings in more profit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui nitsumɔhei lɛ tsuɔ koni amɛfee daa afi. Shi kɛlɛ, nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ jara wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shika he nyɔmɔwoo ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa.

english: Why is it recommended that I buy fresh maize seeds every season instead of just saving some from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mihe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei daa be lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ to ekomɛ kɛ je nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi.

english: Fresh commercial seeds give you the strongest growth and maximum yield. Over time, saved seeds lose their vigor, get infected with hidden pests or diseases, and produce smaller cobs.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui heei yeɔ ebua bo ni odaraa waa ni ohaa yibii babaoo. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji bibii

english: What will happen if I harvest maize from a hybrid crop and plant those harvested grains again next year?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ tso ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli ni midu ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: If you replant seeds saved from a hybrid crop, the new plants will grow unevenly, produce much smaller cobs, and give you a poor harvest because the hybrid strength is lost after the first generation.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome mli lɛ Tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa. kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii ejaakɛ hybrid vigor lɛ laajeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my OPV maize harvest to plant during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi OPV ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can save seeds from an OPV harvest for 3 to 4 seasons. To get good results, select seeds only from the healthiest, strongest plants in your field, dry them properly, and store them securely away from pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ OPV kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato bei 3 kɛyashi 4 koni onine ashɛ yibii kpakpai anɔ. Halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ amli. Egbi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛto he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do seeds that I store in my house sometimes fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ shĩa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Seeds stored at home often absorb humidity from the air, get damaged by tiny insects like weevils, or lose their energy due to heat. Store-bought certified seeds are specially treated and dried to make sure almost every seed sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Kplukai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ loo hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni agbiɔ koni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do all the maize plants in my neighbor's hybrid field grow to the exact same height while mine look uneven?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ hybrid shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he kome yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ daaa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds come from uniform genetic parents, so every plant grows at the same speed and height. This uniformity allows all the plants to share sunlight equally and mature at the exact same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jɛɔ fɔlɔi ni yɔɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli lɛ adɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ daa oya kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome. Nɛkɛ ekomefeemɔ nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ jaa hulu la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli.

english: Are hybrid maize crops better at surviving dry spells than local maize varieties?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern hybrid maize varieties are specially bred by scientists to withstand heat and dry weather, allowing them to produce a good harvest even when the rains are unreliable.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa srɔtoi babaoo pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ po.

english: What happens to the soil when I clear forest land to plant crops like corn?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mijie koo mli shikpɔŋ koni mikɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Forest soil is naturally rich in organic nutrients, but removing the forest trees exposes the bare earth to direct sunshine and heavy rain. This causes the ground to bake hard and heat up, making it harder for soil to hold water without proper care.
ga: Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi tsei ni afoɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa waa ni edɔɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ eeehiɛ nu mli kɛji akwɛɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to provide extra water when I start planting on a newly cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu kroko aha kɛ́ aje dumɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly cleared land loses its natural tree shade, causing sunlight to dry out the topsoil quickly. Providing water helps young crop roots establish themselves in the soil before the intense heat dries them out.
ga: Hei ni ajie amɛ ehee lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli tso ŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hulu la haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani la ni naa wa lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my corn crops grow and yield better?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii kpakpai eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer works like food for plants, supplying essential minerals like nitrogen and phosphorus. These minerals help corn grow thicker stems, dark green leaves, and larger, fuller ears of corn.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa shika tsuru nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Nɛkɛ minerals nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmãa toi lɛ bafee wuji

english: Why do my corn plants get burnt or die if I put fertilizer on dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated chemical salts. Without water to dilute these salts, the fertilizer pulls moisture out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, which scorches the plant leaves and kills the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji nu bɛ ni akɛbaahã ŋmeii nɛɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer at the exact same time I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait until the seed sprouts and forms roots—about two weeks after planting—because fresh seeds without roots cannot absorb fertilizer, and strong chemical contact can ruin the sprouting seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. (aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ) ejaakɛ dumɔwui heei ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli waa lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is fertilizer useless to my crops if there is no rain or water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehiaaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ loo nu bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots cannot feed on dry chemical powder. Water is necessary to dissolve the fertilizer into liquid food that the roots can drink up and transport to the leaves.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye tsofa powda ni egbi. Nu he miihia koni akɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni etsɔ nu ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu ni amɛkɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ miipiŋ?

english: Crops suffering from water stress will roll or curl their leaves inward to trap moisture, look pale or yellowish, droop heavily during the afternoon, and stop growing tall.
ga: Tsei ni nu mli haomɔ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baafolɔ loo amɛbaafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya mli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Egbee shi waa yɛ shwane mli ni ekpa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ.

english: Why do my young seedlings need water more frequently than full-grown plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shii abɔ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, delicate roots that stay near the top of the soil where heat dries water fast, whereas mature plants have long roots that can drink water stored deeper underground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni dɔlɛ haa nu lɛ gĩɔ oya lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni baanyɛ anu nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves droop during the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than the roots can drink it up. As long as the soil stays damp underneath, the plants will recover once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo yɛ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ beni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I prevent water from evaporating too quickly from my soil during hot days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, traps soil moisture, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ abɔle shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, intense sunlight. They require partial shade from companion plants like plantains or shade trees during their first two to three years to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color and improves growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil wears out specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water sits around them for too long because the soil lacks proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away freely and protects the roots from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso ko masɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs light on its leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and keeps them from catching diseases from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. ni etsĩ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ anaa

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which eats maize leaves from the inside out. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract sprays can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks by small insects like thrips. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and providing light shelter during intense heat helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni la akabote mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for longer during the dry hot season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the open soil around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—prevents the sun from drying out soil moisture quickly and keeps the root area cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso shishifãi ahe kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la naa, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is poor and needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Poor soil often looks pale, forms hard crusts, grows poor weeds, or produces stunted crops with yellowish leaves. Adding animal manure or organic compost before planting improves soil richness and structure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efeɔ ŋmei ni wa Jwɛi gbohii komɛi yɛ. loo amɛwoɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow small and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei titrii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures your main crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I soak my maize seeds in clean water before planting them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo nu ni mli tse mli dani madu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking seeds in water gives them early moisture to soften their outer coat and release oxygen inside the seed. This wakes the seed up quickly so it can sprout faster, even if the dry soil lacks enough rain at first.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra. Koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baate dumɔwui lɛ oya koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi po lɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaa.

english: Can I soak my vegetable seeds in a simple water mixture at home to help them sprout without buying expensive shop chemicals?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ aduawai dumɔwui awo nu ni akɛfutu mli mlɛo mli. Ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ shia koni eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofai ni jara wa yɛ shwapo mli?

english: Yes, soaking seeds in a simple water or liquid mixture at home allows moisture and air to enter the seed coat naturally. This triggers fast and uniform sprouting without needing costly commercial chemical boosters.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu loo nu ni akɛfutu mli yɛ shia lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya, ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ afata he.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout when I plant them too deep under heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply cannot get enough air or gentle sun warmth from the surface. Without enough oxygen reaching the seed under the heavy dirt, it suffocates and fails to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ loo dɔlɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli blɛoo lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Ebaafo ni enyɛŋ eda kɛjɛ mli.

english: Do my crop roots need air to grow, or is rain water enough for them?
ga: Mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛdara. Aloo ani nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ?

english: Crop roots need both air and water to stay healthy. Good soil allows water carrying dissolved oxygen to reach the roots so the plant can breathe and take up nutrients continuously.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu fɛɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu ni mli ewo muji ni hiɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tsei nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai daa.

english: Why do my cassava and pepper plant leaves turn yellow when water sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu edamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When standing water covers your field for too long, it pushes all the trapped air out of the soil. Without oxygen, the roots choke and stop feeding the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni emɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does adding water to dry animal manure help turn it into good food for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛfataa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi he lɛ haa efeɔ niyenii kpakpa kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Moisture from water provides oxygen and the right environment for tiny friendly organisms in the manure to feed, break down the waste quickly, and release nutrients for your crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ shihilɛ ni sa kɛha nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. ni ji naanyobɔɔ yɛ kooloi afɔfɔi amli kɛha niyenii Gbalamɔ jwɛi oya ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa onibii amli

english: How does keeping my soil moist help my tomato plants stay cool during the hot Ghanaian sun?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Moist soil holds onto water that absorbs and regulates heat from the sun. As the crop drinks water from the damp soil, it releases moisture through its leaves to cool itself down naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛ nu toɔ, ni no gbalaa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ. Beni tsei nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ Ejieɔ nu ni mli efɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the cool morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso?

english: Watering in the cool morning allows the soil to absorb moisture and supply oxygen to the roots before the midday sun hits, protecting the crop from heat stress throughout the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ dani hulu lɛ nyɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do soil bugs and worms multiply so quickly right after the first major rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The combination of warm soil and fresh rainwater creates ideal moisture and oxygen conditions that trigger insect eggs buried in the soil to hatch rapidly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu ni mli tse ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa. Enɛ baaha kooloi bibii ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ̃ oya.

english: Does wet soil cause pest eggs in the farm dirt to hatch faster?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ oya?

english: Yes, damp soil provides the exact moisture and oxygen pest eggs need to wake up and hatch quickly, which is why pest numbers often rise right after heavy rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛfɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow when there is water trapped in my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: While rice needs water to grow, standing water that becomes completely still stops fresh oxygen from reaching the roots. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients properly, causing the leaves to turn yellow and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nu ni yɔɔ lolo ni etsɔ nu kwraa lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa lolo. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Can I plant rice during the dry season in Ghana, or must I always wait for the main rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu omɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana? Aloo esa akɛ wɔmɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa be fɛɛ be?

english: You can plant rice during the dry season if you have access to an irrigation system or a reliable water source nearby. Without constant watering, dry weather will cause the rice crop to wither before it can produce grains.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji oyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Kɛji akɛ nu haaa amɛ daa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ dumɔwui.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural shield against the hot sun. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat, helping it hold onto internal moisture until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too high, or when the plant experiences water stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the flower to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tomato tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants look very green and healthy, but refuse to bring out flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ? Shi ekpoo akɛ ebaajie fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes pepper plants focus all their energy on growing thick stems and leafy green foliage instead of flowers. Adding phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni mli eyi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I add animal manure or compost to my farm soil instead of using chemical fertilizers alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Organic matter like compost feeds the living soil organisms, improves the soil's ability to hold moisture during dry spells, and keeps the soil soft so roots can spread easily, making chemical fertilizers work much more effectively.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ehaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers stay very small even when the plants above ground look tall and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ cassava tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eda moŋ, shi.

english: Cassava plants planted too close together compete for sunlight and nutrients, causing the plant to spend all its energy growing tall instead of storing starch in underground tubers. Proper spacing gives roots room to swell.
ga: Cassava tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa gbɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do garden eggs and vegetables start rotting quickly at the roots after sudden heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. This wet, warm environment allows harmful soil fungi to grow fast and attack the weakened roots, causing rapid root rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ha kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa oya ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same farm plot where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koolooi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: How is buying certified seeds different from just saving and planting seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kɛdumɔ he lɛ he?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist common local diseases, survive dry weather better, and grow uniformly, whereas saved seeds often lose their strength and yield less with every new planting.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni edaa be fɛɛ be Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ tso hee fɛɛ tso hee.

english: Can I use the same spray chemical on my maize farm to clear weeds in my tomato bed?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ agbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, different crops react differently to chemicals. A weedkiller designed for maize can burn or destroy delicate vegetable crops like tomatoes because every agrochemical is formulated for specific plant types and specific targets.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ tsofai ahe yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee aha ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo efite aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato. Enɛ ji akɛ, afee agrochemical fɛɛ agrochemical kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ oti pɔtɛɛ ko.

english: Is there one general chemical I can buy at the market that will solve all my crop problems?
ga: Ani tsofa kome yɛ ni afɔɔ namɔ ni manyɛ mahe yɛ jara nɔ ni baatsu miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe naagbai ahe nii?

english: No single chemical works on every crop or problem. Crop chemicals are specialized—some only kill specific insects, others target plant diseases, and others control weeds. Buying a chemical meant for everything often damages crops or wastes your money.
ga: Tsofa kome pɛ bɛ ni tsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ loo naagba fɛɛ naagba. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ ŋaalee krɛdɛɛ ko. Kooloi srɔtoi komɛi gbeɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi pɛ. Ekomɛi ji nɔ ni akɛma tsei ahe helai anɔ. ni henɔi komɛi yeɔ jwɛi anɔ. Tsofai ni ooohe kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ afitemɔ loo efiteɔ shika.

english: Can I mix two different pest chemicals together to save time when treating my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mli?

english: It is dangerous to mix chemicals unless the product label explicitly says it is safe. Combining incompatible chemicals can trigger a reaction that burns your crop leaves or stops the chemicals from working altogether.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yɛ oshara. Ja nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛaafata he lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko aba ni shã otso lɛ baai lɛ loo eha tsofai lɛ akatsu nii kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off after spraying weedkiller near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava plants are sensitive to broad-spectrum weedkillers. If the chemical mist drifts onto the cassava leaves, it disrupts the plant's internal processes, causing yellowing and leaf loss because the chemical was not designed for cassava safety.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ nuɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi srɔtoi lɛ ahe waa. Kɛji tsofai ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmei baa lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaafite tso lɛ mli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai ni afeee kɛha ŋmei shweshweeshwefeemɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why does my pepper farm look stunted even after spraying a strong chemical I was told works fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie nɔ po lɛ? Akɛɛ mi akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii oya.

english: Using a chemical that is not specifically approved for pepper crops, or applying the wrong dose, stresses the plant. Instead of protecting the pepper, the chemical slows down its growth and damages its roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha pepper tsei loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ekɛ haomɔ baaba tsei lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsofai lɛ baabu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he Moŋ lɛ, tsofai lɛ ha edalɛ ba shi ni efite eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my watermelon flowers drop off after I spray to get rid of caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa shwie nɔ koni mikɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ?
