english: Some insect chemicals are too harsh for plants when they are flowering or setting fruit. Spraying a chemical not formulated for blooming crops causes plant stress, leading to flower drop and poor yield.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha tsei kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi loo amɛwo yibii. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii.

english: How do I choose the right chemical when bugs start eating my cocoa leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofai ni sa kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɔi mi-kokoo baai lɛ yeli?

english: You should consult an extension officer or check approved product lists for cocoa. Cocoa trees need specific insecticides registered in Ghana that target destructive pests like mirids without damaging the tree or leaving harmful residues in the cocoa beans.
ga: Esa akɛ oyabi onitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ loo okwɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ afee kookoo lɛ. Cocoa tsei biɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni gbeɔ kooloi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ yɛ Ghana. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ pollen lɛ anɔ. ni efiteee tso lɛ loo eshiŋ nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why didn't the weedkiller I bought kill the stubborn grass in my rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mihe lɛ egbeee jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Because rice itself is a type of grass, weedkillers used in rice fields must be highly specific to target unwanted weeds without harming the crop. A general grass killer will either destroy your rice or fail if it is the wrong formula.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ ji jwɛi henɔ ko. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ pɔtɛɛ waa koni ekɛtutua jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baafite oŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛbaafee nɔ ko kɛji akɛ amɛji tsofai ni ejaaa.

english: How can I tell if a crop chemical sold in Ghana is safe to use on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Approved chemicals carry standard labels showing the exact crops they are safe for, the specific pests or weeds they control, and official registration details. Avoid unlabelled liquids or sellers claiming a single bottle treats every crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ woji ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha lɛ. Nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo jwɛi ni tsofai kudɔɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ woloŋmaa he saji fitsofitso Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo jarayelɔi ni kɛɔ akɛ tɔ kome baanyɛ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Does plant fertilizer work the same way as agrochemicals that kill pests?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ bɔ ni okwaayeli mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, fertilizers feed the soil and the plant to encourage healthy growth, while pest chemicals target specific insects or fungal diseases. Every product has a distinct purpose, so pest chemicals cannot act as plant food.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ kooloi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Esoro yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ nibii fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii akɛ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on rice usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients or are sitting in stagnant water that lacks fresh oxygen for the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii loo eyɛ nu ni ekã shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my rice field has too much or too little water for the crop to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fa tsɔ loo ebɛ nu tsɔ kɛha tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Rice likes soil that stays wet and flooded with a few centimeters of water during early growth, but if the water completely covers the plants or dries up and cracks the soil, growth will stall.
ga: Omɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu ni falɛ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi eyi mli obɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shi kɛji nu lɛ ha tsei lɛ anɔ kwraa loo egbi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fã lɛ, Dalɛ baakpa.

english: Can I keep seeds from my current maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa amrɔ nɛɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can save seeds from traditional local varieties if you dry them properly, but saved seeds from hybrid varieties will produce much smaller harvests if replanted.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli kusum mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ ato kɛji ogbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo bibioo kwraa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested beans at home so that insects do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato shia koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Drying beans completely in the sun and storing them in airtight containers or sealed triple-layer bags starves insects of air and stops weevils from multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni akɛwo mli shii etɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant that will still survive if the rains stop early this year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni baahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa afi nɛɛ shishijee mli?

english: Drought-hardy crops like cowpeas, cassava, and millet have deep roots or short growth cycles that allow them to yield food even when rain is low.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ cowpea, cassava kɛ millet lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ni haa amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains waterlog the soil without good drainage, causing fungal diseases to attack the wet roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni no haaa nu atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ baa.

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings after I clear and plant my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil food faster than young crop seeds can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ afee.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops grow better than using no fertilizer at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛwooo mli kwraa lɛ?

english: Animal manure slowly feeds the soil with natural plant nutrients and helps the earth hold onto rainwater longer for root absorption.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi baafee fiofio Ekɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin plants with small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ.

english: How do I know when my rubber tree is mature enough for me to start cutting it for latex sap?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔmɔ kɛha nu lɛ?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when the trunk reaches about 50 centimeters in circumference at knee-to-chest height, which usually takes 5 to 7 years of growth. Tapping a tree too early will stunt its growth and lower the total amount of rubber it produces over its lifetime.
ga: Rɔba tsei efee klalo kɛha gbee kɛji tso lɛ shishi lɛ shɛ aaafee sɛntimita 50 yɛ ebɔlemɔ he kɛjɛ etsitsi nɔ kɛyashi etsitsi nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani edaa. Kɛ́ otswa tso ko mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ. ni ekɛ rɔba ni afeɔ yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my rubber tree produce much less sap when I tap it in the hot afternoon instead of early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ mli nu lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ́ mitswa lɛ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli moŋ fe leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Trees lose water quickly through their leaves under the hot afternoon sun, which lowers the internal fluid pressure inside the bark. Tapping early in the cool morning when pressure is highest allows the latex sap to flow freely and yield much more.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ otswa leebi ni hulutsoo be mli ni nɔnyɛɛ lɛ fa fe fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya ni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and hot sun dry out the soil quickly, causing young cocoa trees to drop leaves to save water and survive. Providing shade trees like plantains and watering young seedlings helps protect them from dying during these dry months.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ agbo koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe koni amɛkagboi yɛ nɛkɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ nɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to grow when I plant them under deep tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need direct, bright sunlight to make energy and grow fast. Planting them under deep shade starves the leaves of sunlight, which slows down growth and leads to small, weak bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni ekwɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye baai lɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ekɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa

english: Why do my cassava plants grow bigger roots when I plant them on land where I previously grew cowpeas or beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When cassava is planted after them, it feeds on this stored natural fertilizer, helping it grow thicker, healthier roots.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oodu ŋmei Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni ato nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to space out my maize seeds instead of putting three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaagbala ŋmãa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni akɛ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ baafata he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded in one hole, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant its own room to feed and grow large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo bu kome mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil get hard like concrete after rain, making my crops look pale and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Mahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Heavy rains wash away topsoil and pack tight soils together, trapping the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb water easily. Adding compost or animal manure mixes air into the soil and helps roots breathe and uptake nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ ji koni akɛmɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛkamu loo amɛkaŋɔ nu mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and getting green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a sickness spread from plant to plant by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers prevents the sickness from spreading across your field.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛha lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Will trimming off the lower branches of my crop trees hurt them or help them produce better?
ga: Ani mitso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaaha ewo yibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary lower branches actually helps the tree by directing its food energy upward toward growing strong main branches and bigger fruits, while also letting airflow through to prevent disease.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ eniyenii hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa niji titrii ni he wa kɛ aduawai wuji amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ mli koni helai akabote mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even during the rainy season when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the nutrients and plant food out of the soil before your crop roots can reach them. Even with rain, your crops become hungry and turn yellow if weeds are competing for that soil food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tips usually mean the maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or the roots are struggling to get water to feed the plant properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Aloo shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná nu ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of rain, or attack by tiny insects like mirids, or simply when there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutua amɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves, but the stems underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much rich manure or nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its strength growing thick stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: What makes the bottoms of my garden eggs and tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ?

english: This black rotting at the bottom of the fruit is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the ground, often caused by irregular watering during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top. Without wooden bamboo stakes to support the stem and good soil mounded around the root base, strong winds can easily knock them down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ, ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abua naa ebɔleɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa amɛ shi oya.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside the barn even before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally wake up after resting for a few months after harvest. The warm, humid air in the storage barn signals to the tuber that it is time to start growing a new plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes baate shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ tsɛnsii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje tsei heei ashishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni mikpamɔ lɛ hu faaa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce a big yield.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do wild weeds keep growing fast on my farm even when my crops are struggling to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi miida oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher than cultivated crops and are better at quickly drinking up available soil food and water, which starves your main crops if the weeds are not cleared early.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii titri lɛ kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop in the hot afternoon sun even though it rained in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes plants to lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the wet soil. The plant droops to protect itself from drying out and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe koni ekagbi, ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies crawling on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni shwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing so big even though I didn't add any chemical fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraa waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efataaa he moŋ?

english: Cassava plants naturally store extra starch in their roots as a survival habit. When the soil is loose and gets good rainfall during the early months, the root system expands easily and bulks up naturally using stored soil nutrients.
ga: Taakɛ eji wala su lɛ, cassava tsei kɛ starch ni fa fe nine toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually makes my yam tubers grow very long and fat under the ground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee shwiili yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams expand underground when the soil in the mound is soft, deep, and well-drained. Sunlight hits the leaves to create energy, which flows down to build a heavy tuber if the soil moisture is just right.
ga: Sweet potatoes baagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la lɛ tswaa baai lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ bulbs agboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ja.

english: Why do some maize stalks in my farm grow very thick while others right next to them stay thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ waa lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ Egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa lolo?

english: Differences in stalk size happen when nutrients or water are distributed unevenly in the soil. Stalks get thicker where there is more decaying plant matter or better water retention near their roots.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nu lɛ mli eja yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni tso lɛ fiteɔ babaoo loo bɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does pouring extra water around the base of my crop make the fruit grow larger, or can too much water ruin it?
ga: Nu kroko ni akɛbaawo Mitso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adara. Aloo ani nu babaoo baanyɛ afite lɛ?

english: Moderate, consistent moisture carries nutrients into the fruit to help it swell. However, flooding the base chokes the roots of air, which can rot the root system and cause the fruit to drop or become watery.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli tse ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛya aduawai lɛ amli koni eye ebua lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa, shi kɛlɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha aduawai lɛ agbo loo etsɔ nu.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ mli leebi lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon air pulls water out of leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant droops to protect itself from heat, but it usually recovers once the sun goes down.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it better to apply water directly to the soil around my plant rather than wetting the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni mawo baai lɛ amli nu lɛ?

english: Roots are the mouth of the plant that drink water and absorb soil food. Keeping leaves dry prevents fungal diseases from growing on them while ensuring moisture goes straight to the roots.
ga: Shishifãi ji tso daaŋ ni nuɔ nu ni eŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can my farm produce heavy harvests relying only on rainwater and natural bush fallow without chemical inputs?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ jwɛi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, decaying leaves and old plant roots break down into rich organic matter that feeds the soil. This natural food helps the soil hold moisture and feeds the crops over time to produce good yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe baai ni egboi kɛ tsei shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Peppers drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or too much nitrogen in the soil which forces the plant to make leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Chili peppers jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nugbɔshiimɔ trukaa. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow even though the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Yellow leaves in wet soil mean the roots are suffocating from too much standing water, preventing them from taking up plant food. Poor drainage damages root health even if water is abundant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ po.

english: Why do young cocoa pods dry up and turn dark on the stem before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, which happens when the cocoa tree naturally sheds excess young pods it cannot support due to stress, food competition, or dry weather early in the season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ nɛɛ ji cherel wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ shwie dumɔwui bibii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. yɛ stress niyenii he akaŋshii loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ hewɔ

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for healthy green growth, or that the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain, which prevents the roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like potassium needed for fruit setting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to absorb moisture and soil nutrients faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava maximizes land use; maize grows fast and matures in three to four months, while cassava grows slower underneath and is harvested much later in the year.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo. Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ, ni akpaa lɛ babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the main rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should plant after the soil has received enough rainfall to stay consistently moist for two to three days, ensuring seeds have enough water to germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ odu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi, koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant the seeds harvested from my hybrid maize crop for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong performance only in their first generation; seeds harvested from that crop will produce uneven growth and significantly lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ daalɛ ejaaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi waa.

english: How does dried chicken manure help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure adds organic matter that improves soil structure and water retention while slowly releasing vital nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that feed the plant over time.
ga: Kokoo ŋmei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ mli nibii kɛ nu ni hiɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ fataa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni haa tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: What causes crop roots to rot and turn soft underground during continuous rains?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei shishifãi fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Root rot occurs when standing water fills all the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for harmful fungal diseases to attack the plant.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni baatutua tsei lɛ.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on the leaves of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in warm, humid weather when crops are planted too closely together and lack proper airflow.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do insects attack my crops more aggressively during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Insects seek out green crops during dry periods to feed on plant sap for hydration and nutrients when other wild vegetation has dried up.
ga: Kplukai kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛye tsei lɛ amli nu koni amɛha amɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai beni koo mli tsei krokomɛi egbi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leaves but producing tiny roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai kakadaji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing big leaves on top instead of expanding its tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why is it beneficial to leave dry plant leaves and grass on the ground around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi tsei ahe baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass and leaves around your crops acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It traps moisture so the ground stays wet longer, prevents weed growth, and turns into organic fertilizer as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni ashiɔ yɛ he ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my crops after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three strong, steady rains before planting. Planting right after the very first light shower can kill your seeds if the sun returns and dries out the soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa dani oduɔ nii. Kɛ́ odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe odumɔwui lɛ kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a larger yield from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the stems thin and weak, resulting in smaller harvests than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ faaa fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from high heat and keeping the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Can I spread sickness from one crop to another just by using my cutlass across the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ hela ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛya ekroko mli kɛtsɔ dade nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, plant diseases caused by tiny germs or fungi stick to your cutlass blade, boots, or hands. If you cut a diseased plant and then use the same cutlass on a healthy plant without cleaning it, the sickness transfers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo ŋmeii kɛbaa. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ o-blade, o-boot, loo onine he. Kɛji ofo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ nakai dade lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni otsuuu he. Abaajie hela kɛya he kroko.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the tight center funnel of the plant to eat the soft inner leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛwoɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even if I clear them out after the crops grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ amɛ beni tsei lɛ eda lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and water early on. Stunting a crop's growth when it is young prevents it from recovering fully later, even if weeds are removed afterwards.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli mra. Kɛ́ tso ko dalɛ tee hiɛ fioo beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaná hewalɛ kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli po.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil and get infested with insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fite ni helai emɔ mi beni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains rot and attract weevils if they are put into storage before drying completely. Excess moisture inside the grain allows fungi to grow and creates a ideal breeding environment for insect pests.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baagboi ni ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear and prepare my cocoa farm before the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni masaa amɛhe dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing your farm before the dry season helps protect the trees from extreme weather, reduces bushfire risks, and ensures the trees retain enough strength to develop healthy buds and flowers later.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa oŋmɔ lɛ he dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Ha koo mli la ni baa lɛ aba shi ni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I just prune or clear my cocoa farm whenever I have spare time during the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mafo mli be fɛɛ be ni maná be ni mikɛtsuuu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: It is better to follow a set schedule. If you wait and do farm maintenance too late in the cycle, you might disturb the trees right when they are trying to produce flowers, which reduces your total yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooonyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji omɛ ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli lɛ Obaanyɛ ogbala tsei lɛ anaa kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why is proper timing before the dry season so important for cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni sa dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Proper timing allows cocoa trees to rest and store nutrients safely during dry weather, putting them in the best position to burst into flowers when the right month arrives.
ga: Be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ cacao tso lɛ woɔ he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛji nyɔŋ ni sa lɛ bashɛ.

english: At what point in the year should I expect flowers to start showing on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli yɛ afi lɛ mli esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ fɔfɔi baabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: In a standard annual growth cycle, major flowering usually begins around the eleventh month after the initial seasonal growth and preparation period.
ga: yɛ afi mli dalɛ be ni sa mli Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji 11 lɛ mli yɛ be mli dalɛ kɛ hesaamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when I start seeing tiny white flowers growing on my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: No mli lɛ mibɔi fɔfɔi bibii yɛŋ namɔ. Mɛni ji mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ shweremɔ tsɔɔ?

english: Tiny flowers on the trunk mean the tree is entering its reproductive stage. If these flowers are successfully pollinated and cared for, they will grow into young pods over the following months.
ga: Fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibote fɔmɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ aye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi nɛɛ amli ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ nyɔji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How long does the full development cycle take from flowering to full pod growth?
ga: Be enyiɛ shweremɔ be lɛ fɛɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛyashiɔ pod lɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ?

english: The main flowering stage begins around the eleventh month, progresses through the twelfth month, and completes its full annual cycle over a 12-month period.
ga: Be titri ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji 11 lɛ mli, ni eyaa nɔ kɛyashiɔ nyɔŋ ni ji 12 lɛ nɔ, ni egbeɔ afi mli fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ naa yɛ nyɔji 12 mli.

english: Why do cocoa trees seem to produce flowers at specific times instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond naturally to weather changes like rain and dry spells. The dry period acts as a trigger so the tree concentrates its energy to flower in a specific peak month.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Be ni nu bɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kanyaa mɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ nyɔji ni fɔfɔi lɛ fa babaoo lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa flowers if the farm experiences a sudden harsh dry spell?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa?

english: A severe dry spell without proper pre-season preparation can cause fragile flowers and tiny pods to dry up and fall off before they can mature.
ga: Hɔmɔ be ni naa wa ni asaaa he jogbaŋŋ dani be lɛ baa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni waaa kɛ ŋmeii bibii afɔlɔ. Amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are on track for a good flowering season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kpakpa mli?

english: If you cleared and prepared the field on schedule before the dry weather, you will see strong, healthy flower buds popping up along the trunk and main branches around the eleventh month.
ga: Kɛji ojie jɛmɛ ni osaa he lɛ yɛ be naa dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli agbi lɛ, Obaana fɔfɔii ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome lɛ he.

english: Does delaying my farm work past the recommended schedule hurt my harvest?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsi sɛɛ kɛho be ni awo he ŋaa lɛ he lɛ baaná mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Yes, delaying farm work disrupts the tree's natural timeline. If you miss the key maintenance window, you risk damaging delicate flowers during the eleventh and twelfth months, leading to fewer pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ kɛyaa sɛɛ lɛ gbalaa tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli be he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe wooo tsɔsemɔ be ko mli lɛ Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaafite fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ nyɔji 11 kɛ 12 lɛ amli, ni no baaha ŋmeii fioo pɛ aba.

english: Why does the chemical spray I bought fail to clear the pests eating my leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni miheɔ lɛ ejieee mihe nibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mihe lɛ?

english: Pesticides can fail if they are mixed with too much water, applied during the hot afternoon when insects hide under leaves, or if the insects in your farm have built up resistance to that particular chemical over time.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ akɛ nu babaoo futu mli. Ye shwane ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ná nakai tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Curling and yellowing leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by a lack of balanced nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo niyenii ni ja ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting at the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bottom rot on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering or dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Tomato shishi fitemɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa loo egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii lɛ? Shi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava put all its growth energy into stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ baai amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack enough shade during dry weather, experience sudden heat stress, or lack tiny pollinating insects in the farm to turn flowers into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ. Piŋmɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli trukaa Aloo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsake fɔfɔii lɛ amɛfee ŋmeii

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields if I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete underground for water and soil nutrients while their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in weak, overcrowded plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ feɔ shoo.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground year after year.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after light rain, placing it near the root area and covering it slightly with soil, rather than applying right before heavy downpours.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Okɛma he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the sunny afternoon even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water to the hot air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself until the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ gbiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ehe kɛyashi hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing cocoa with the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka, ni ehaa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying NPK fertilizer or compost early on will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ oya, ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra Ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water or proper nutrients. Ensuring regular watering during dry spells and adding manure helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn sticky?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant's juice and leave a sticky liquid behind. Spraying with neem oil or soapy water can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛshiɔ nu ni mli tse yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds take so long to come out of the ground after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both water and loose soil to sprout. If the soil is too dry, too hard, or if the seeds were buried too deep, they struggle to push through the surface.
ga: Nu kɛ sũ ni mli tse fɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ewa tsɔ, loo kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if I give my plants enough fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha mitsei lɛ po?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. If weeds are present, they steal the fertilizer away before your crops can soak it up through their roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop and wilt during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves when it is hot. If the roots cannot pull up water fast enough from the soil, the plant wilts to save moisture, though it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baagboi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ moŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my corn seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, which results in thin stalks and tiny, weak corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dry out, and when you open a pod, the inside shell wall has dark veins and the seeds are full and firm.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele pod lɛ Mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ gbogbo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in cold, wet conditions. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and airflow helps prevent this disease.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpods ji nɔ ni kɛ helai diji ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain floods the soil, preventing roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop feeds on and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores food to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain in Ghana is often a 'false start' followed by a dry hot spell. If seeds sprout and the soil quickly dries out, the delicate seedlings will wither and die before the full rainy season begins.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ fɔɔ kaa "shishijee amale" ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why should I avoid planting my seeds very close together to try and fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ he koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes the stalks grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller harvests than properly spaced crops.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo fe be mli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and turn small?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant sickness. It can also be the plant's reaction to extreme sun and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ efee bɔ ni tso ko feɔ enii ehaa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hu mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around the roots for too long, suffocating them and encouraging water-loving fungal diseases. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ hydrophilic fungal hela he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their tiny green pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani eda?

english: This drop, called cherelle wilt, often happens naturally when the tree produces more pods than it can feed with available water and nutrients. However, severe pest attacks or prolonged dry weather can make the problem much worse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko wo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ aye. Shi kɛlɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha naagba lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my garden egg plants produce plenty of blossoms, but the blossoms fall off without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers fall when plants experience heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. It can also happen if beneficial insects like bees are not visiting the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haaa ená hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my yams turn out crooked and split instead of growing smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams bend and split when the young growing tuber hits hard, compact dirt, rocks, or heavy clay beneath the surface. Digging deep mounds with soft, loose soil lets the tuber expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejaraa kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni akɛ sũ ni mli tse tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers put dry grass on top of the dirt around their vegetable roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ amɛ aduawai shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from drying out quickly under the hot sun, and stops weeds from stealing plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves towards sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch maximum light, which helps the plant produce energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which feeds the maize while helping to suppress weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I burn the dry weeds on my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the topsoil that feed your crop roots, leaving the ground dry and weak over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Growing maize in the same spot continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and causes crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields each season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the plant stems instead of spreading it across the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly near the root zone ensures your crop absorbs most of the nutrients immediately, rather than wasting fertilizer on nearby weeds or letting it wash away in heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai lɛ ateŋ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ loo oha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aho lɛ.

english: What causes the small ragged holes inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves (the whorl) of young maize plants during the night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and collapse suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni efoɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden drooping in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, where tiny germs attack roots damaged by waterlogging or poor drainage, stopping the plant from taking up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baa. he ni helai bibii Etutuaa shishifãi ni nu ni hoɔ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ efite lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my seed leaves turn yellow and dry up when I plant immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The early rain is often just a false start followed by a short hot dry spell. Without continuous soil moisture, young seedlings burn quickly in the hot sun and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ji amale shishijee kɛkɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji hulutsoo be kukuoo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ bɛ. Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees do not have deep root systems yet and cannot tolerate direct intense heat; they need temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them from scorching weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and keep the soil moist, acting as temporary protective covers while the cocoa trees grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer supplies the food the maize needs to keep its leaves green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aye kooloi niyenii. Koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil. This enriches the land and helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger without exhausting the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and soft during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and dark, unpruned farms. Pruning dense leaves lets sunlight and wind into the farm, drying out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ ni afolɔɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and leaves to spread out and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and slowing down growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraa fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by extreme heat stress or tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Mulching the soil to keep roots cool and managing insect pests can help the leaves return to normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mulching ni akɛbaahã shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua baa lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ adu sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground toward sunlight helps the plant capture light energy efficiently. This extra energy is redirected downward to make the underground yam tubers grow larger and heavier.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ la hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my soil protect my vegetables during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni ebaaha nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi

english: Why does resting my piece of land for a year make the soil produce better crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ afi kome lɛ haa ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous farming drains vital minerals from the soil. Letting the land rest gives natural vegetation time to grow, rot, and restore organic matter and nutrients back into the dirt for future planting.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ shika tsuru ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛdaraa, amɛfiteɔ, ni amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛtsu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to support new top growth, so adding nitrogen fertilizer will help the whole plant stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni eye ebua ŋwɛi dalɛ hee. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food. Putting up stakes lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant channel more energy into growing big tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛhoo nii. Pinching baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the bed with mulch helps lower soil temperature and keeps the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas make my farmland better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plant dies after harvest, it leaves that nitrogen in the soil, acting as free food for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji cowpea tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi nakai nitrogen lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-cornmeal ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away so the roots do not sit in soggy mud.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ emɔɔɔ muji ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I remove small sucker shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra sucker shoots fight with the main plantain tree for water and plant food from the soil. Removing most of the small suckers leaves more energy for the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii krɛdɛɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ Efã babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and getting wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaf surfaces. Spraying the plants with neem oil or a suitable farm chemical kills the insects so new leaves grow out smooth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni sa shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition results in tall, thin stems with small or missing ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo ni bɛ.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to be pulled out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry out. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown spots, the nuts are fully mature and ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong sunlight and can dry out easily. Planting plantains alongside them provides essential shade and keeps the soil cool and moist during the cocoa trees' first few years of growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Kookoo tsei ni aaadu yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their rich green color and helps the plant produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔtɔ wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe under water. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather or dry soil. Giving the plants consistent watering and protecting them during the hottest sun helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni obu amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my farm soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?
