english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it inside the soil through tiny leaf-like roots. When you harvest them, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop you plant, like maize or vegetables.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ. ni tamɔ baai Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do I have to use wooden sticks to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto wooden sticks lets sunlight reach all the leaves easily so the plant can make food for growing large tubers. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal rot and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe mlɛo. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ afee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni akwɛ̃ɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and spoil during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a plant sickness caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Trimming off extra shade tree branches lets light and air dry out the crop, which helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tso hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hi ji akɛ, aaafo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the extra farm space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ ŋmɔ mli he kroko kɛji ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi mabɔle he lɛ? Mi ŋmɔshi nibii shishifãi?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, retains water longer, and stops unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars, often called armyworms, feed on tender young leaves to grow. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying safe sprays or ash into the center of the plant leaves stops them before they ruin the entire leaf crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ asraafoi ŋmeii. Ye baai bibii koni amɛdara. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo sũ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom leaves upward when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food that keeps plants green and healthy, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay green and grow large ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná toi wuji.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the young leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying with neem oil or targeted insect treatment helps protect the leaves so they can grow flat and absorb sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaabu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe hulu la lɛ.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Giving the plants steady, regular water helps the fruits grow firm and healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni ekwɛɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil for too long, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my watermelons split open while they are still growing in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack when a long dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain or heavy watering. The fruit drinks up water so fast that the inside grows quicker than the skin can stretch, causing the rind to burst open.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ nuɔ nu oya aahu akɛ loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off instead of forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry winds, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. Keeping tall shade trees on your farm protects the delicate flowers from harsh wind and direct heat so they can turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni baatutua amɛ Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above ground but grow the nuts deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi eduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a long stem called a peg that pushes itself down into the soil. Once buried, the tip expands into the pod, which is why loose, sandy soil makes it easy for the pegs to enter the ground.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji afu lɛ, naagbee lɛ yaa pod lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers when I let them trail on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii beni mihaa amɛnyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo stake lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers. Staking holds the vines up high so every leaf catches maximum sunlight, while trailing on the damp ground causes leaves to shade each other and rot.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ogbala lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ atsĩ amɛhe naa ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings survive better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the air humid around the young cocoa until it is strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Kakao tso lɛ ji gbekɛ kɛyashi ehe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha hulu la ni naa wa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my maize crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ haa mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, which helps the hungry maize plants grow bigger and greener.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa trees to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can help replenish the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars destroying the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni makpãtã mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ahiɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms that hide inside the central funnel (whorl) of maize plants to eat the tender leaves. Applying recommended biopesticides or soapy water into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nu ni akɛ samla wo mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my maize help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means their roots work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ niyenii.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and inactive, preventing the flowers from getting pollinated. Keeping the soil well-watered and providing partial shade can reduce heat stress on the plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollination Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eha hulutsoo be fioo ko aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds harvested from my hybrid maize crop for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield only in their first planting season. Seeds saved from that harvest will produce weaker plants with smaller cobs and lower yields compared to fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shweremɔ be lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. Amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I space my yam mounds far apart instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi sweet potato ŋtayaai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each yam plant has enough room for its tubers to expand deep into the soil. It also stops plants from competing with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa sweet potato tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli

english: Why should I cut off the extra straight shoots growing out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those straight shoots, called water suckers, drain valuable water and nutrients away from the main tree. Removing them allows the cocoa tree to focus its energy on producing flowers and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni ja nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa cacao fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout when I plant them during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moist soil to trigger stem buds to form new roots and leaves. If planted in bone-dry soil, the stems lose their stored moisture quickly and dry out before roots can grow.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ afomɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni ewo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kɛ baai heei. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ nu ni ato lɛ oya ni amɛgbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so many days to come out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have tough outer shells and require consistently moist, warm soil to soften the seed coat and start growing. If the soil surface dries out or gets too hard, the seeds will sprout very slowly or fail to sprout at all.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni eha dumɔwui lɛ ahewolo lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo waa loo amɛkwɛ̃ŋ kwraa.

english: How long will my new coconut trees take before they start producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso hee lɛ baawo yibii?

english: Improved hybrid coconut varieties usually start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 7 years. Proper weeding and regular feeding during the early years help them produce much faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi ni kɛlɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ afee amɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do I need to leave large spaces between my coconut seedlings when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ agbo yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need wide spacing—about 7 to 8 meters apart—so their wide fronds can capture full sunlight and their roots have enough room to pull water and nutrients from the soil without competing.
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ gbɛ ni da. Amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8 bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Ni shishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting short-term food crops or legumes between young coconut trees maximizes land use and gives you income while waiting for the trees to mature. Just keep intercrops at least one meter away from the tree trunks.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni ekɛ shika aba yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ha tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mita kome pɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let tall grass grow around the base of my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal moisture and nutrients from young crops, harbor pests like rodents, and create a major bushfire risk during the dry Harmattan season.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Eji he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ, ni ekɛ koo mli la he oshara kpele baa yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli.

english: Why are young green coconuts falling off my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoobii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is usually caused by long dry spells, a lack of soil nutrients like potassium, or sap-sucking insects attacking the young flowers and nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ oya lɛ baa ji ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni tutuaa fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: What causes the lower leaves of my young crop to turn yellow and droop?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is logged around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or compost helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is making holes and V-shaped cuts on the fronds of my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo baa lɛ mli ewo bu ni etsɔ V-shaped?

english: This damage is caused by the Rhinoceros beetle boring into the young growing shoot. You can reduce them by clearing rotting wood and compost piles near the farm where they breed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji rhinoceros ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ mli lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Do my young coconut trees need watering during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni awo mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, young coconut trees under two years old need extra water during the dry season to protect their leaves from burning and keep them growing continuously.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tsei bibii ni eyeko afii 2 lɛ he miihia nu kroko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How can I tell if my soil is fertile enough for a heavy crop harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Dark, rich soil that holds moisture well and breaks easily in your hand is fertile. If crops grow slowly or look pale, mixing organic manure into the soil will improve its structure and nutrient content.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo loo efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha egbɛjianɔtoo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I select the best seedlings to ensure my farm gives a high yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ koni maná yibii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Choose strong seedlings with thick stems, deep green leaves, and fast sprout growth from registered nurseries. Healthy seedlings build strong root systems quickly after field planting.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. ni edaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baafee shishifãi ni mli wa oya beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ.

english: What is the main reason I should start my crop seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly into my main field?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri hewɔ ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A nursery provides a controlled environment that protects delicate young seedlings from harsh weather, heavy rains, intense sun, and pests while they are weak, ensuring only healthy and strong plants get moved to your main field.
ga: Nurseries haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my nursery seedlings often wither and die shortly after I move them into the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock, which happens when delicate roots are damaged or suddenly exposed to hot sun without enough moisture; shading the young plants and watering them immediately after moving helps them survive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite loo hulu la ni tsoɔ trukaa ni naa wa waa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ afee tsei bibii lɛ shade ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ amɛshi amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Is it better for me to buy certified seed packets from the market or just plant saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ahe paketii ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jara nɔ loo madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds from reputable agro-dealers are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases, germinate more reliably, and produce higher crop yields compared to saved seeds, which lose vigor over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ gbɛi kpakpa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe. ni baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How can I tell if the seeds I want to buy at the local market are good quality before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni mahe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: Good seeds should be uniform in color and size, dry, smooth, and free from insect holes, cracks, or mold, preferably coming from sealed packages with a clear expiry date.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee ekome yɛ su kɛ amɛdalɛ mli, ni amɛgbi, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko, kɛ́ ebaahi lɛ, amɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli ni atsĩ naa mli, ni be ni amɛbaafite lɛ hu ahi shi faŋŋ.

english: How do I know which specific fertilizer to buy at the agro-dealer shop for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mahe yɛ nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Different crops require different nutrients at specific stages; for example, leafy growth needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer, while root and fruit growth need phosphorus and potassium, so matching the product to your crop type is essential.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, baai lɛ adalɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ biɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he miihia waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing crops turning light yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or excessive soil moisture that suffocates the roots and stops them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize plants fall over easily when strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops fall over when their root systems are weak, which often happens if seeds were planted too shallow, spaced too closely together, or lacking potassium in the soil to build strong stems.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee tsei ni wa

english: How does adding compost or organic manure to my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Te ŋmɔ mli sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Compost works like food for the soil by improving its ability to hold water during dry spells and slowly releasing essential nutrients that feed crop roots over a long period.
ga: Kɔmpost tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ nɔ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage me to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã amɛhe lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every plant enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with nearby crops, while making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do crop protection sprays work to keep insects from eating my farm produce?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni kooloi akaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop protection products work either by killing pests directly on contact or by making the plant leaves poisonous or unpleasant for insects to feed on, protecting the plant's health.
ga: Nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji amɛshɛ he lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai ni afee ni amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo nɔ ni esaaa akɛ kooloi yeɔ lɛ nɔ. koni akɛbu tsei ahewalɛ he

english: Is it possible for my crop plants to get too big and fat from the food in the soil?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ agbo tsɔ ni ená fɔ kɛjɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, just like animals, plants can overeat if there is too much rich nutrient or heavy food in the soil. This causes them to grow excessively large leaves and stems instead of producing good fruit or tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tamɔ kooloi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei baanyɛ aye nii fe nine kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo niyenii ni tsii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni dara tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii loo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce giant leaves and thick stems, but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When crops get too much heavy, starch-rich food or fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves above ground. To get big tubers, you need to balance their food instead of giving them too much heavy material.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná yitso agbo Esa akɛ okɛ niyenii ni oyeɔ lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni okɛ nibii ni tsii baawo ohe fe nine.

english: What happens if I put too much cassava waste into my farm soil as fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmei babaoo fata miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɛ ŋmei?

english: Cassava is very rich and heavy. Adding too much at once causes plants to grow oversized and weak, so it is better to take just a small amount of cassava waste and mix it with lighter garden soil or leaves.
ga: Cassava ji nii babaoo ni eyɛ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ babaoo fata he shikome lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ daraa fe nine ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋɔ ŋmei fioo ko pɛ ni okɛfutu abɔɔ mli sũ loo baai ni mli tseee lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plants grow so tall and big very quickly, but fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiidara oya nɛkɛ? Shi egbeeɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa?

english: Rapid overgrowth happens when soil has too much rich food. The plant grows big stems too fast without building strength, making it weak. Mixing lighter inputs into the soil helps plants grow strong and sturdy.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe nine. Tso lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ emaaa shi. ha egbɔjɔ Nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How should I use rich plant materials like cassava peelings when making plant food?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ ŋmei ni ajie lɛ atsu nii aha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mifee niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee?

english: Because cassava peelings contain a lot of heavy food that can make crops overgrow, you should only use a little bit and mix it thoroughly with dry leaves or light compost before applying it to your crops.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni tsii babaoo yɛ ŋmei ni ajieɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adara tsɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli fioo dani okɛwo onibii amli.

english: Why is it better to mix small amounts of rich manure into soil rather than adding a large pile at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ agbo afata he shikome lɛ?

english: Dumping a lot of rich food at once makes crops gorge and grow unnaturally large without producing good fruit. Mixing small portions into the soil gives them a steady, healthy diet.
ga: Niyenii babaoo babaoo ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ shi yɛ be kome mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ nii ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni nɔ ko kpakpa jɛɛɛ mli baa. fãi bibii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛná niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if I am feeding my soil too much heavy organic material?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo miiha shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: If your plants develop unusually thick stems and oversized, dark green leaves but fail to flower or form tubers, they are getting too much heavy food. You need to dilute the soil with lighter materials.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli tse yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi enyɛɛɛ efɔ fɔfɔi loo efee bulbs lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni tsii tsɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ nɔ ko ni mli tseee awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop my crops from focusing only on growing big leaves instead of giving me a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai wuji pɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai?

english: You can control crop growth by reducing heavy, rich inputs. Mixing small amounts of nutrient sources evenly into the soil prevents the plant from getting oversized and encourages it to focus on producing fruits.
ga: Obaanyɛ okudɔ tsei adalɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni tsii ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni oootsi shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii nɛɛ fioo ko futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ agbo tsɔ, ni ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Can high-energy foods in the soil delay when my crops produce fruit?
ga: Ani niyenii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha be ni heɔ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii lɛ asɛɛ afo?

english: Yes, when crops receive too much high-energy food like heavy cassava compost, they keep growing bigger and bigger instead of flowering. Balancing the soil food encourages timely flowering and fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei niyenii ni haa hewalɛ babaoo tamɔ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. Tso lɛ baada agbo ni efee agbo. yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ja lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ yibii baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the best way to feed my crops so they stay a manageable size and produce well?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ he ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: The best approach is moderate feeding. Take a little bit of rich food or organic waste, mix it evenly with general farm soil, and feed the plants gradually so they grow healthy without becoming overgrown.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni aha lɛ niyenii ni sa. Ye niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fioo. Okɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ fɛɛ afutu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tsei lɛ niyenii fiofio koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods each year even when the rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Over time, cocoa trees take up nutrients from the ground to grow leaves and pods. If those nutrients are not replaced, the soil becomes tired and exhausted, making it impossible for the trees to produce full harvests.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbaa kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ atsakeee nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its power to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ?

english: Tired soil often becomes hard, light in color, or fails to hold water after rain. Crops grown in it will have pale yellow leaves, slow growth, and yield small or diseased fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ fɔɔ kaa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ehiɛɛɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. shwereɔ blɛoo ni ewoɔ aduawai bibii loo helai

english: Is it possible to bring an old, tired piece of farmland back to life for cocoa planting?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔji ni egbɔ ni etɔ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ koni akɛdu kookoo?

english: Yes, soil can be rejuvenated by adding organic nutrients. These natural materials restore the soil's structure, bring back useful soil organisms, and replenish food for plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni okɛ niyenii afata tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe

english: Why does cocoa grow better in rich, dark soil compared to dry, hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa he lɛ?

english: Rich soil contains organic matter that acts like a soft sponge. It holds water and food around the cocoa roots, allowing the tree to drink and feed easily throughout the year.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ eeenu nu ni etao niyenii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is organic fertilizer, and how is it different from chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni te esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Organic fertilizer comes from natural plant and animal sources. Unlike chemical fertilizers that only give a short burst of plant food, organic fertilizer builds up the soil structure for long-term health and keeps the land fertile for years.
ga: Organic fertilizers jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛ kooloi amli. Esoro tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni haa tsei niyenii be kukuoo pɛ lɛ ahe. Organic fertilizers haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii afii babaoo.

english: Will applying fertilizer to my farm actually help me get better returns for my hard work?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua mi diɛŋtsɛ ni maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ minitsumɔ ni wa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, feeding your soil restores its vitality, which leads to stronger trees, larger pods, and higher crop yields. This means you harvest more from the same piece of land for the work you put in.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ baaye abua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ baa. pods wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaakpa babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛha nitsumɔ ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: How does feeding the soil help cocoa trees fight off sickness and bad weather?
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Just like well-fed people get sick less often, cocoa trees growing in nourished soil build strong roots and trunks, making them more resilient against dry spells and diseases.
ga: Nakai nɔŋŋ hu mɛi ni yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hela mɔmɔɔɔ amɛ tsɔ. Kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shishifãi kɛ tsei ni wa waa. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, not just water. Rain and water help the plant drink, but if the soil lacks key nutrients, the plant starves and its leaves lose their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. Jeee nu pɛ Nugbɔ kɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni baai lɛ baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods dry up and turn black on my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa?

english: When soil lacks vitality, a cocoa tree does not have enough energy to support all its pods. To save itself, the tree drops or aborts young pods before they can mature.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Cacao tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛkɛ. koni obu ohe lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shi loo eshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa.

english: What actually happens underground to crop roots when the soil becomes rich again?
ga: Mɛni baa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛdu shishifãi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bafee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: In rejuvenated soil, plant roots can spread deeper and wider without hitting hard dirt. This allows the roots to absorb more water and nutrients to support heavy pod growth.
ga: yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aku sɛɛ ato lɛ mli Tso shishifãi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni enáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, an essential food for the plant. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the green color return and restore normal growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots work with friendly soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, creating a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for the same limited supply of soil water and nutrients, while their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in weak plants.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo pɛ, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantain trees next to them creates living umbrellas that offer shade and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Tso lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch maximum sunlight for growth, while also keeping the leaves off the hot, wet ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni edɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ ahe.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows deep into the center of young corn plants to eat the soft, developing leaves before the stalk grows tall.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my pepper leaves after several days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity and splashes mud onto the leaves, which spreads fungal spores that attach to the damp plant tissue and cause spot diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ muji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbɛɔ fungal spores ni kpɛtɛɔ tso mli fãji ni mli efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ eshwaa ni ekɛ helai ni baa he kome lɛ baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or lack of water, which stresses the plant and prevents pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if it rains for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the ground waterlogged for too long, the roots suffocate and soil fungi attack them, causing rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ. kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when the trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over when carrying heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa nɔ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo aduawai babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a survival mechanism to minimize water loss through evaporation during extreme heat. This helps the plant save moisture until the temperature drops in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni laajeɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the plant is suffering from drought stress. The plant sacrifices its older leaves to send remaining water and nutrients to the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ miina hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ebaai momo lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Flower drop happens when the crop experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium. Without steady moisture and food, the plant cannot support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ be fɛɛ be. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and fall over easily when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, causing them to stretch upwards quickly. This makes their stems thin and weak instead of thick and sturdy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water from my farm channel?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔ mli nu lɛ mli?

english: Overwatered crops often show pale yellow leaves, soft or rotting stems, and stunted growth because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo náa amɛ lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo egbo. kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why does irrigation water sit on top of my land instead of sinking into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ taa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water sits on the surface when the soil is heavily compacted or contains high clay content. Adding organic matter like compost helps break up the dirt so water can drain down to the roots.
ga: Nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ babaoo yɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ muji lɛ koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Is it bad if I irrigate my vegetables during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering under intense sun causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and hot wet leaves can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain plants grown beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide shade and cool air, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do weeds growing near my crop roots slow down my plant's growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds act like thieves on the farm; their roots spread fast and steal water, fertilizer, and light that your crop needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium, usually caused by uneven watering that prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow from the middle, even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves stay green and strong. Heavy rain can wash nutrients out of the topsoil, leaving the plant without enough food to make green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket. It keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so water doesn't evaporate quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni nu akafo oya yɛ latsaa mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do crops like groundnuts and cowpeas help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that capture food from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, that stored food remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛmɔ niyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and dropping off during the Harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lose water quickly through their leaves when the sun and wind are harsh. Without enough shade trees or soil moisture to protect them during dry months, the leaves burn and fall off to keep the main stem alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu he yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Too many young suckers fight with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and food from the soil. Leaving only two or three strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Abifabii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but give me tiny tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi beni okpa lɛ ni okɛ yitso bibioo ko ha mi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants get too much shade, the cassava spends all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of sending that food down into the soil to build big, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ jamɛ a niye ní ɔ kɛ yaa zugba a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when there is too much water at once. Extreme heat or water stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to protect itself from dying.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nu babaoo yɛ be kome mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices out of young leaves, or by tiny germs transferred by those insects that stop the leaves from expanding naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai bibii ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small dark powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ powda bibioo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and dark powdery dirt inside the center leaf funnel are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the growing tip of the stalk where it is moist and chew on the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Buu ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa ni amɛfɔ bii yɛ mli.

english: How do I take proper care of new young cocoa seedlings before I plant them into my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kookoo tsei bibii heei lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need consistent shade and regular watering, but avoid waterlogging the soil. Keep them in polybags under a canopy of palm fronds or shade cloth to protect them from harsh sun and strong winds until they are strong enough to be transplanted at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ nu daa. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Okɛ amɛ awo polybag mli yɛ ŋmei tso loo mama ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ shishi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsake amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa plants dying when I plant them in full, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant food crops like cassava or plantain together on the same land with my cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-kookoo lɛ?

english: Plantains are great to plant with young cocoa because they give needed shade. However, heavy feeders like cassava can aggressively steal nutrients and water from the young cocoa trees, so they should be spaced carefully or kept at a safe distance.
ga: Plantains hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii akwɛmɔ ejaakɛ amɛhaa amɛnáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ aju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I plant new cocoa trees on the exact same field where my father grew old cocoa for decades?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mitsɛ du kookoo momo mli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, but old farm land often loses its nutrients and may harbor hidden pests or diseases in the soil. Before planting new trees, you must clear out old infected roots, nourish the soil with organic manure or fertilizer, and allow the field time to recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ, ni ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ mli. Dani obaadu tsei heei lɛ, esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni oha ŋmɔ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time and way to prune my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni matsɔ nɔ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning is best done just before the rainy season starts. You cut away unwanted shoots (basal chupons), diseased branches, and dead wood to let air circulate and sunlight reach the lower trunk, which helps prevent rot and encourages healthy pod growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Ofoɔ tsei ni ataooo (basal chupons), tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ, kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he ni hulu la lɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbo ni ewoɔ pod lɛ hewalɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients, or are attacked by pests like mirids (capsids). Ensuring the soil has adequate moisture, applying recommended nutrients, and controlling insects helps the tree hold onto its flowers and form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutua amɛ. Ehe hia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii Kɛ kooloi bibii ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to turn yellow and fall off during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, is receiving too much direct sunlight, or is infected with a disease like cocoa swollen shoot virus. Checking for pests and adding rich compost or fertilizer usually helps restore green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛ enɔ tsɔ, loo ená hela ko tamɔ cocoa bud swelling virus. Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha tsei ahe tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small black ants crawling all over my cocoa pods, and do they harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji bibii ni miiho yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Ants themselves often do not eat cocoa, but they are attracted to sugary honeydew produced by mealybugs. Mealybugs spread harmful diseases like the swollen shoot virus, so seeing many ants is usually a warning sign that mealybugs are present and need treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ yeee kookoo. Shi amɛsumɔɔ wuo ni ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ feɔ lɛ. Mealybugs gbɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ bud shwiemɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii babaoo ni anaa Bei pii lɛ amɛji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ mealybugs yɛ ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if my farm gets continuous heavy rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo?

english: Excess rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like Black Pod disease to spread rapidly. Proper tree spacing, regular weeding, and frequent pruning help air dry out the farm faster after rain, keeping pods safe from rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ shii abɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni pods lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is good enough for growing healthy crops without buying expensive testing equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ adumɔ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa ni akɛkaa nii lɛ?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, holds water well without staying flooded, breaks apart easily in your hand, and is full of earthworms or decaying leaf litter. Soil that is pale, hard, or overly sandy will struggle to produce high yields without extra organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ, ehiɛɛɛ nu, ni efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni miifite eyi mli obɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni wa, loo ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo ni nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, a key food crops need to grow. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little food it has from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni adu Beni nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow very tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight. The plants stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light before their neighbors, which makes them grow tall and weak, making them easy for wind to blow over.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei baafee tɛ̃ɛ oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ la ni yɔɔ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why is my maize producing flowers and tassels when the stalk is still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When crops experience extreme stress, such as prolonged dry weather or very poor soil, they sense that they might die. To survive, the plant stops growing tall and rushes to make flowers and seeds early while it still can.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ Amɛnu he tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi. koni ehi shi Tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ oyaiyeli yaa fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ dumɔwui mra. Be mli ni ebaanyɛ eba mli lolo lɛ

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread between plants by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from making food properly, which results in very small cassava roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate them, or if the tree is under stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛhe fɔfɔi. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam rot happens when water sits in heavy soil without proper drainage. The wet soil smothers the tubers and allows harmful germs and fungi in the soil to attack and rot the yam before harvest.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ nɔ ni ehaa helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛgboɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the next season's maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap natural food from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why did my pepper plants wither and die after I placed fertilizer directly against the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like strong salt. Placing it directly against the plant stem or main root sucks moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, which burns the roots and causes the plant to dry up.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Enɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my tomato plants help them survive hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil, called mulch. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeping water near the roots much longer and keeping the root area cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulch lɛ he. Etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Weeds have strong roots that drink water and steal plant nutrients from the soil much faster than your crops can. Even with rain, the weeds eat up the food in the ground before your crops get a chance to reach it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ anu nu ni eju tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛyashɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn reddish or brownish when they first start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ etsuru loo ŋmɔtɔ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves naturally produce reddish pigments to protect themselves from harsh sunlight before they mature, develop green chlorophyll, and turn into tough green leaves.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Eha klorofil eŋɔli ni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and survive heat stress. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or soil moisture is inconsistent, which prevents proper pollination and fruit setting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves in the late afternoon or under strong sunlight to reduce water loss through evaporation and protect themselves from heat.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above ground but the nuts grow under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, their stems elongate and push down into the soil where the pods safely form and mature.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Eshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown before I dig up the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry out when the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the tuber, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo ni amɛbaagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni tsei lɛ gbeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to fruit when I leave many of them on one stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ tsei babaoo yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow on one plantain stool, they compete for nutrients and water; cutting back extra suckers allows the main plant to grow faster and produce bigger bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain ŋmeii kome nɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dying after I cleared all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from larger trees to protect their delicate leaves from direct sun damage and keep the surrounding soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my pepper crops so they don't fight for space?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkaye he ko he akaŋ?

english: Spacing pepper plants about 50 centimeters apart gives each plant enough space to capture sunlight, receive proper airflow, and absorb soil nutrients without spreading diseases easily.
ga: Ha pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50, ni oha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ aná. Na kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni helai egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die shortly after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often suffer from transplant shock or heat stress if planted in direct sunlight or dry soil. They need gentle root handling, initial shade, and moist soil to establish themselves safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ blɛoo. Shade kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni akɛma shishifãi shweshweeshwe

english: When is the best time of the year for me to start planting cocoa on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The ideal time to plant is at the start of the main rainy season (around April to June in Ghana). This gives young crops plenty of natural water to grow strong roots before the harsh dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Hɔmɔ be lɛ (aaafee April kɛyashi June yɛ Ghana) haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ be ni naa wa lɛ baashɛ.

english: Is it good for me to leave large trees on my farm when planting new cocoa?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo hee lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving temporary shade trees protects young cocoa plants from intense sunlight and heat, helps retain soil moisture, and keeps the young leaves from burning.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baa bibii lɛ akashãa

english: What makes my cocoa trees flower well and turn those flowers into healthy pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ehaa nakai fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy pod formation requires steady rainfall, good soil nutrients, and tiny natural insects like midges that pollinate the flowers so they can mature into pods.
ga: Pod kpakpa feemɔ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some flowers drop off my cocoa trees without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping usually happens during dry periods, when soil nutrients are low, or when beneficial pollinating insects are killed by harsh spraying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Be mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo be mli ni agbeɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, deep, well-draining, and rich in decomposed organic leaves that retain water without staying flooded after rain.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni eyɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ ni haa nu hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni nu afua akafee lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot faster during heavy rains?
