ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates wet, humid conditions where fungal spores (black pod disease) thrive and spread quickly across the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni fungal spores (black pod hela) lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ pod lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt the plant or help it produce more?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning off dead or crowded branches helps the tree by letting sunlight and fresh air flow inside, which reduces rot diseases and encourages better pod growth.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebaaha ebɔle emli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ he okadii lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from the base of my young crops so frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil food away from young crops, causing them to grow slowly and stay weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: How does applying fertilizer to my soil give me a bigger cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa kookoo shweremɔ yaa hiɛ?

english: Fertilizer restores key soil food like nitrogen and potassium that plants consume over time, giving mature trees the strength to produce more flowers and heavy pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea after weeding helps the plants turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that destroys maize leaves. Inspecting your farm early and spraying an approved insecticide into the center of the plants will protect your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni fiteɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie otsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: The best practice is to apply NPK fertilizer about 2 weeks after planting during your first weeding, followed by a top-dressing of Urea 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the crop is growing rapidly.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ jwɛi shwiemɔ be lɛ mli. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni adu tsei lɛ beni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balancing your fertilizer use will help the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to turn black and rot at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant roots absorb calcium and keeps the fruits healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm in the morning or afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate quickly, wasting water and stressing the plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Nu ni afiteɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava early if cassava is already a tough crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cassava mra Kɛji akɛ cassava ji tso ko ni ewa akɛ aaakwɛ momo?

english: Young cassava stems grow slowly during their first three months and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for light and soil nutrients. Weeding early lets the cassava build strong underground roots.
ga: Kasava tsei bibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni etswaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil in your mounds is hard, stony, or packed tight. Making deep, soft mounds with loose topsoil gives the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes baatswa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ okpɔŋɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli etse lɛ, ebaaha tuber he lɛ alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves dry up and burn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lose water quickly under direct hot sun during the Harmattan. Planting shade trees like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and reduces water loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my land is healthy enough to support good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or organic matter. If soil is light, dry, and hard, adding compost or poultry manure will improve its richness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waaa, egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready to harvest so it does not spoil in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa lɛ akɛ efiteee yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the husks turn dry and brown, and the cobs droop downward. Looking for a tiny dark mark (the black layer) at the base of the grain kernel also shows it has stopped growing and reached full maturity, preventing mold during storage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ gbee shi Kɛji ootao hyperpigmentation bibioo (black layer) yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi lɛ, no hu tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni edara. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How does drying my harvested cocoa beans on raised mats make them better for sale?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ tsɔji ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Drying cocoa on raised bamboo or wooden mats allows air to circulate beneath the beans, helping them dry evenly while preventing contact with ground dirt and mold. This preserves bean quality and secures a better price at market.
ga: Cocoa ni agbiɔ yɛ ŋmei loo tsei ahe lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo yibii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, muji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akashɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa amɛjara hu hiɔ shi yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve moisture and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing its underground roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the ground with nutrients for the next crop, like maize or vegetables.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ abele loo aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and sensitive to direct sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger shade trees on the farm protects young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds in organized rows ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without overcrowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso baaná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaaa eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become excessively hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop unfertilized blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow twisted and small while others grow long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji bibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require soft, deep soil to expand smoothly underground. If the soil is hard or compacted, the growing tuber hits resistance and twists around obstacles, resulting in stunted or deformed shapes.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tuber ni miida lɛ kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo kpeɔ ni ebɔleɔ gbɛtsii nii ahe, ni no haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo efiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin even when I plant healthy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for light, space, soil nutrients, and water. When weeds grow unchecked, they steal essential food from the soil, leaving your crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha la, ŋwɛi, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot when rain water sits around them for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to stay alive. When standing water covers the roots for too long, it drowns them and creates an environment where destructive soil fungi thrive and rot the root system.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ko baa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: I could not work on my farm for weeks and weeds have overgrown everywhere; can my crops recover if I weed the farm now?
ga: Minyɛɛɛ matsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii babaoo ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ kwraa. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bianɛ?

english: Yes, many crops like cassava, maize, and cocoa are resilient and can recover once you clear the weeds. Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients, so clearing them allows the crops to access sunlight and nutrients again to restart healthy growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi pɛ. Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ekoŋŋ koni amɛje hewalɛ kpakpa shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for my soil to cut overgrown weeds with a cutlass and leave them on the ground or to burn them after clearing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafo jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni mikɛ dade aaashi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo mashã kɛji ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: It is usually better to cut the weeds and leave them on the ground as mulch. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose enriches the soil with organic matter, keeps the ground moist, and protects it from erosion, whereas burning destroys valuable soil nutrients and beneficial organisms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Which staple crops in Ghana are tough enough to survive long periods without regular care or maintenance?
ga: Mɛɛ tso titri ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ loo asaaa lɛ daa?

english: Cassava and plantain are among the most resilient crops in Ghana. Cassava stores water and food in its underground tubers to survive periods of neglect and drought, while plantains have strong underground stem structures that keep them alive until regular care resumes.
ga: Cassava kɛ plantain ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana. Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ be mli ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tso ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaakwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will a farm that was left unmaintained for a few months give as much harvest as a farm that was weeded regularly?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ ni ashi lɛ nyɔji fioo ko ni mɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baawo yibii tamɔ ŋmɔ ni ashwieɔ jwɛi daa lɛ?

english: Yields will usually be lower because neglected crops suffer from nutrient competition and stress during crucial growth stages. However, clearing the farm, weeding thoroughly, and applying fertilizer can still save a significant portion of your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni aku hiɛ ashwie amɛnɔ lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii kɛ haomɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okpa fãi ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: How often should I clear weeds around my young cocoa trees using my cutlass to keep them healthy?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ cacao tsei bibii kɛ dade tsuɔ nii koni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees generally need weeding about three to four times a year. Clearing a wide ring around the base of each young plant keeps aggressive weeds from choking its shallow roots while ensuring it gets enough light and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ aaafee shii etɛ kɛyashi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ ni bɔle tso bibioo lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baa lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, enaa la kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do insect pests and plant diseases spread so fast when a farm becomes bushy and unkept?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya beni ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds create a dark, humid environment where insect pests can hide and breed without being seen by predators. Bushy farms also block fresh air movement, trapping moisture on leaves, which helps fungal diseases multiply rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ feɔ duŋ ni edɔ. he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi amɛhe ni amɛfɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ enaaa amɛ Okwaafoi ni bɛ deka lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yaa lɛ naa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Do weeds really steal food and water from my crop roots underground, or do they just block sunlight?
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds do both. Underground, weed roots aggressively absorb soil moisture and fertilizer nutrients before your crops can reach them, while above ground, tall weeds block sunlight, preventing your crop leaves from making food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa otso lɛ baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii.

english: If I use my cutlass to trim off dead or overgrown branches from my crop trees, will it harm them or help them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ mitso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ Ani ebaaye amɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ?

english: Pruning dead or weak branches helps your crops. Removing inactive parts forces the plant to direct its energy and nutrients strictly toward growing healthy new leaves, flowers, and fruits.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua onibii. Nibii ni tsuuu nii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkudɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with very few leaves when heavy weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward rapidly when surrounded by taller weeds in a struggle to reach sunlight. This survival response uses up the plant's energy on stem height rather than developing thick stems, strong roots, or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji jwɛi ni kɛlɛ ni miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Nɛkɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo nɛɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa. Shishifãi loo aduawai ni mli wa

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my crops turning yellow after being covered by thick weeds for a while?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni mli tse ehà nɔ be fioo lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow and drop off when they are shaded from sunlight and cannot perform photosynthesis to feed the plant. Once you clear the surrounding bush and sunlight reaches those lower branches again, fresh green leaves will grow back.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji hulu la eshɛ amɛhe. ni enyɛɛɛ efee fotosintɛsis ni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei Beni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ. Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow tall. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn dry weeds and stalks on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that keep soil fertile and moist. Leaving crop leaves to rot naturally acts like food for the soil and protects it from drying out under the hot sun.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ baa nii ni ehaa enɔ fũuɔ. Tso baai ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, natural restoring soil fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers need shade trees or plantain shade when planted next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and provide natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit combined with uneven watering. When water supply bounces between very dry and very wet, the plant cannot move calcium to the base of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ hoɔ yɛ nu ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa teŋ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ ashishi.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Infected plants cannot process sunlight efficiently, causing stunted growth and lower root yield.
ga: Cassava Mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni ŋmeii yɛŋ bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. plant sap sucker Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu hulu la lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer beetles eat and destroy the root system beneath the ground, leaving the heavy plant without anchors.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem-boring beetles lɛ ye amɛ ni amɛfite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta bɛ he

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high temperatures, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce only leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai pɛ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I know that my underground cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn black and dry up prematurely before the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during warm, humid rain showers. It attacks leaves and stems, stopping the plant from making food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Fuji hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Etutuaa baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Ekpaa tso lɛ ni ehooɔ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. Keeping shade trees in your farm and covering the soil around roots with dry grass (mulching) retains soil moisture and keeps cocoa trees healthier during the dry spell.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ jwɛi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ anáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my young maize plants staying short and turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowish, stunted maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs to grow strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season supplies the nutrients needed for deep green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ awa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but excessive standing water fills up all the air spaces and starves the roots of oxygen. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainfall to drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. Shi nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo shweshweeshwe.

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Watering your plants consistently at the base in the early morning helps them retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips living under the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf extract or targeted pesticide under the leaves stops these insects from damaging the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi amli lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give very small bunches when many shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) growing from the same root compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones directs all the energy into making a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii (tso lɛ) babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for building big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines so leaves get maximum sunlight and keeps them away from hot, damp soil that can breed fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ naa.

english: Why do my other crops grow better when I plant groundnuts in the same farm with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ da jogbaŋŋ beni midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding neighboring crops like maize without extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop completely at midday even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Midday heat causes plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it, so they wilt temporarily to protect themselves. Placing mulch over the soil and ensuring deep watering keeps roots cool and minimizes midday droop.
ga: Gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ehe. Mulching kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do cowpeas produce pods so much faster than crops like cassava or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have a short growth cycle designed to survive in areas with short rainy seasons. They bloom and form pods within a few weeks to complete their life cycle before the soil dries out, making them ideal for quick harvests.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ dalɛ be kuku, ni afee koni ehi shi yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa dani shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nikpamɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my cassava stems after the dry season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu ŋmei tsei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the major rains start and the soil stays moist about a hand-length deep for a few days. Planting in dry soil causes the cassava cuttings to dry out and die before they can sprout roots.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi nɛ waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi tamɔ tso ni dalɛ ji tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tso lɛ agbi ni egbo dani shishifãi akwɛ̃.

english: What causes tiny green worms to eat holes in my cabbage leaves, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Yeɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli bu lɛ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. You can control them by spraying organic neem leaf extract or approved biopesticides early before the insects multiply and ruin the cabbage heads.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni woɔ amɛwuji amli lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Dani kooloi bibii lɛ baafa ni amɛfite kaabe yitsei lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, usually from dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Watering regularly and placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ mli. Nu daa ni okɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni aduawai aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast in my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when wounded during digging or when kept in hot, damp, airless rooms. Storing undamaged yams on raised wooden racks in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn stops rotting fungi from growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ epila yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ atomɔ ni mli ewo muji ato tso adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni mli ejɔ, shade, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daalɛ kpaa.

english: Will I harvest more corn if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with tiny or empty cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce large, full ears.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii. loo efolo Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha toi lɛ adara ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is the white powdery dust spreading across the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni ji sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly in warm, humid weather when plants are crowded. Spacing your plants for good airflow and removing affected leaves early prevents it from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli ni ojie baai ni ena hela lɛ mra. Enɛ ji koni akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from selected parents to give high yields only in the first generation. Replanting seeds saved from that harvest causes the next generation to grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi ni ahala amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cowpea crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to quickly grab water and nutrients from the soil faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks gives cowpeas a head start to spread their leaves and naturally shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsina ŋmei lɛ aje baai lɛ agbɛfaŋ ni eha jwɛi heei lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and severe heat. Without enough shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees, intense sunlight scorches their leaves and drains moisture, causing them to dry up and curl.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaajie nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged. Maize needs nitrogen to produce green chlorophyll for healthy growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil eŋɔli lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: If my cassava plants start flowering, does it mean the tubers underneath are ready for harvesting?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: No, flowering simply means the plant has reached maturity above ground. Tuber growth develops underground on its own timeline based on crop variety and soil conditions, usually taking 9 to 12 months regardless of flowering.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ tsɔɔ kɛkɛ akɛ tso lɛ edara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tuber dalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebe mli ni edamɔɔ tso lɛ henɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 ekɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus transmitted by insects. As these pests suck sap from the leaves, they distort the leaf growth and stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛhaa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines start dying off and turning yellow towards the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up when the tuber underground has fully matured. The plant transfers all its remaining nutrients down into the tuber and goes dormant to survive the dry season.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ bulb lɛ mli ni eyaa wɔɔhe koni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into growing a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo (tsei lɛ) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni daraa ni tsii waa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over so easily when heavy rains and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is shallow or the stalk is weak, often caused by planting seeds too close together or lacking potassium in the soil. Strong winds easily uproot top-heavy plants with weak anchorage.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie tsei ni tsii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ ashishifãi oya.

english: Why do my garden eggs start turning black and rotting from the bottom while still hanging on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miibɔi diŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛkã jwɛi lɛ anɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is often blossom-end rot caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering, or a fungal infection from soil splashing onto fruits low to the ground. Mulching the soil and consistent watering help prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ ni jɛɔ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ mli baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli baa. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains start showing small powder-filled holes inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi bu bibii kpojiemɔ lɛ? Akɛ powda eyi kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli

english: Holes and powdery dust inside stored grains mean grain weevils are infesting your harvest. Weevils lay eggs inside dried kernels, and the hatching larvae eat their way out from the inside.
ga: Buu kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmaa mli ŋmeii miifite oŋmɔshi nibii. Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi mli. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye nii kɛjɛ mligbɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are thirsty and need water before they start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye mi-ŋmã lɛ ni nu he miihia lɛ dani egbo?

english: Maize leaves will roll up tightly like straws during the heat of the day to save water. If you see the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning or late in the evening, your crop is under heavy water stress and urgently needs water.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu akafite. Kɛji ona baai ni ebɔle ehe leebi loo gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ nu afua mli ni nu he miihia amɛ oya.

english: What will happen to my crop leaves if the dry season starts early and I run out of water?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi mra ni nu fite mi?

english: Without water, crops cannot pull nutrients up from the soil into their stems and leaves. The plant will try to save itself by shedding lower leaves, causing them to turn yellow, dry up, and fall off.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ agbala niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ baai amli. Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsa ehe kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I give water to my vegetables without wasting the few buckets I fetch from the stream?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-vegetables lɛ nu ni mikɛ baagi fioo ni mijie kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ efiteee?

english: Instead of splashing water over the whole field where the sun evaporates it, pour water slowly directly around the base of each stem, or use perforated plastic bottles buried near the roots to feed water straight to where the plant drinks.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ he ni hulu lɛ efo lɛ, shwiemɔ nu lɛ blɛoo ni okɛbɔle tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo okɛ plastic tsinsii ni mli ewo muji ni afu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛya he ni tso lɛ nuɔ nu yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly after it rains, and how can I keep it moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu yɛ mihe?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun through evaporation. Covering your farm soil with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a shade cover that keeps the ground cool and traps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛyaa hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ baawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I capture rainwater on my farmland so the soil stays wet during dry weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ bɛ lɛ amli?

english: You can dig small basins or create half-moon shallow trenches around your crops. When rain falls, these basins hold the water on your farm instead of letting it run off, giving it time to soak deep into the soil around your plant roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubui bibii loo ofee nubui ni tamɔ nyɔji enyɔ ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ nubui nɛɛ baaha nu ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ejo foi. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my farm crops in the middle of the day or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering at mid-day causes most of the water to evaporate instantly in the hot sun before the crop roots can drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ mli babaoo atsɔ la amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanu nu

english: Do all crops on my farm need the exact same amount of water to grow well?
ga: Ani nu falɛ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, crops have different water needs. Leafy vegetables like spinach need light water frequently because of shallow roots, while crops like cassava develop deep roots that allow them to survive longer periods without rain.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ nu he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach lɛ he miihia nu ni waaa, ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm that can survive if the rains are very small this season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas are naturally hardy and use water very efficiently. They can tolerate dry weather much better than water-heavy crops like cabbage or tomatoes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wa ni nu hu shɛɛɛ he. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni nu tsii tamɔ kaaba loo tomato.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. When roots cannot breathe oxygen, they begin to rot and can no longer send food to the leaves, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ Amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha baai lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither instantly when I move them from the seedbed to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ trukaa beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young transplants suffer from shock because their soft roots get damaged and dry out in the open sun. Watering them well before moving them and planting them late in the afternoon gives the roots a cool night to settle into the soil.
ga: Oblahii kɛ oblayei ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ naa shoofeemɔ he amanehulu beni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni oooha lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ ni adu yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i gbɛkɛ ni akɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their leaves earlier than usual during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi mra fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to save water when the weather becomes unusually hot and dry. While dropping leaves is a natural defense against heat stress, losing too many leaves weakens the tree and reduces the number of cocoa pods it can carry.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he moŋ, shi baai babaoo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ayibɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ awo lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi

english: How does changing rainfall pattern affect the right time for me to plant new crops?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ saa be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ tsei heei lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When weather patterns change, rainy seasons may start late or end earlier than expected. Planting immediately after the first light rain can burn seeds if a dry spell follows, so it is best to wait until steady, consistent rains begin before planting.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi sɛɛ mli loo ebaagbe naa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni ebaaya nɔ dani odu.

english: Are there new cocoa varieties that can survive dry weather better than the old ones?
ga: Ani kookoo henɔi heei yɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli fe henɔi momo lɛ?

english: Yes, hybrid cocoa varieties developed by agricultural research institutes grow faster, start bearing pods earlier, and are specifically bred to handle heat and dry spells better than older traditional cocoa varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee hybrid ni Okwaafoi Ahe Nibii Amli Taomɔ Nitsumɔhe lɛ fee lɛ daa oya. Ejeɔ shishi efeɔ pods oya. Ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛtsu dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the sunshine gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot withstand direct, strong sunlight. Without shade from larger plants like plantains or tall trees, the strong heat dries out the seedlings faster than their roots can take up water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ adɛŋ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Can I plant food crops alongside my cocoa trees to protect my farm if the weather damages the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ kookoo tsei ahe koni mikɛbu miŋmɔ lɛ he? Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ fite kookoo lɛ

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa provides shade for the cocoa while giving you food and income. This protects your farm income if harsh weather affects one specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cassava ni akɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baaha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ mli shika ni onáa lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ saa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko he.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil for my cocoa trees when rainfall is low?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aha kookoo tsei lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around the base of your cocoa trees with fallen leaves, dry grass, or plant remains helps trap moisture in the soil and protects it from direct sun heat, keeping the roots cool during long dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbee shi, jwɛi ni egbi, loo humus shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I know if my old cocoa trees are too old to produce good pods anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmeii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce high yields for 25 to 30 years. If old trees produce mostly small pods, have hollow or diseased trunks, and produce very little even with good rainfall and care, it means the tree is aging and needs to be replaced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ tsei ni mli ewo muji loo helai ni ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake.

english: What makes cocoa pods turn black and rot during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excessive moisture and humidity create ideal conditions for Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus spread through water splashes. Dense shade and trapped moisture prevent air movement, allowing the disease to spread rapidly across pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Shade ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. It directs the tree's energy into growing big, healthy pods rather than feeding unnecessary leaves, while reducing moisture that causes plant diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei ahe niyenii ni he ehiaaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer or if low yield is just due to hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Heat stress usually causes leaves to curl, dry up, and fall, while nutrient deficiency causes entire leaves to turn pale or yellow between the veins while remaining on the branch. Applying fertilizer helps strengthen the tree to handle climate stress better.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, yɛ be mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fãji lɛ ateŋ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow leaves, so adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves. Spraying the plants with soapy water or appropriate neem oil treatments can help clear them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni sa shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or lacks enough water. Ensuring consistent watering during the flowering period helps the tree retain its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo trukaa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ nu haa tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know if my soil is moist enough to plant cassava cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei?

english: Cassava cuttings need damp soil to sprout roots. A good test is to squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a soft ball without water dripping out, the soil has the right moisture for planting.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kaa kpakpa ji ni ajie sũ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu ko hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Small plantain bunches usually happen when too many suckers are left growing around the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers so only two or three remain allows all the food and water to go into making bigger bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains bibii lɛ feɔ kɛji ŋmeii komɛi eshwɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe. Nyɛ tso ni fa tsɔ Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi koni niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ aya ni efee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do my cabbage plants remain loose instead of forming hard, tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head tightly when they lack consistent water or face high temperatures. Regular watering at the root level encourages the inner leaves to pack tightly together.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa loo ekɛ ehe wo he ko ni latsaa waa. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam rot in the soil occurs when water gathers around the tubers in flat or heavy clay ground. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away from the tubers so they stay dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato shikpɔŋ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu shwie shi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatsumɔ?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, usually three to four months after planting. You can gently dig up one stem to check if the tubers are full and firm.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso lɛ shishi blɛoo. Koni ana kɛji yitso lɛ eyi ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is standing water important in my lowland rice field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa lolo yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A shallow layer of water prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice for food, while giving the rice plants the steady moisture they need to grow full grains.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛye niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ nuɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛdu ŋmaa.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease in another part of Ghana will reach my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko ni yɔɔ Ghana fã kroko lɛ baashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop diseases can travel through wind, infected farm tools, or moving plant material. Extension officers track these disease movements across districts to warn farmers before the sickness reaches their local farms.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. okwaayeli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsei ahe nibii ni tsiɔ amɛhe Extension nitsulɔi lɛ nyiɛɔ helai nɛɛ asɛɛ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ koni amɛbɔ okwaafoi lɛ kɔkɔ dani hela lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ amɛkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: What basic steps can I take to protect my farm if a plant disease is reported in my district?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ abɔ tso hela ko he amaniɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect your farm by regularly cleaning your cutlasses and boots, clearing infected plants early, keeping weeds down, and using disease-resistant plant varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ o-daggers kɛ o-boots lɛ ni oootsumɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Should I wait until I see sickness on my cocoa trees before taking steps to protect them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ aná hela dani mafee nɔ ko koni mabu amɛhe?

english: No, prevention is much easier than curing a farm disease. Taking protective actions like proper spacing, weed control, and shade management before signs appear keeps your crops strong enough to fight off infections.
ga: Dabi, hela naatsii waaa kwraa fe helai ni atsaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Nifeemɔi ni tsiɔ hela naa tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shade nɔkwɛmɔ dani okadii lɛ baaje kpo. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai.

english: Can crop diseases spread from one type of plant, like cocoa, to a completely different plant like plantain or cassava?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ tso kome, tamɔ kookoo mli kɛya tso kroko kwraa, tamɔ plantain loo cassava nɔ?

english: Most diseases target specific plant families, so a cocoa virus usually will not make a plantain tree sick. However, some pests and soil fungi can live on surrounding plants and spread to your main crops.
ga: Helai babaoo yeɔ tsei aweku kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo hela lɛ haaa plantains hela amɔ amɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii komɛi baanyɛ ahi tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa onibii titrii lɛ amli

english: Why do many farmers plant plantain and cassava on the same farm with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantain and cassava grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade to protect tender cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you food and income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Cassava kɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Will planting cassava near my young cocoa trees steal too much nutrients from the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava needs a lot of nutrients and can compete with cocoa if planted too close. Giving proper distance between your cassava cassava and young cocoa ensures both crops get enough food and light.
ga: Cassava biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ cocoa abɔ akaŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha Tapioca kɛ kookoo ni mli tse Enɛ baaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does planting plantain help keep the soil healthy for other plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have broad leaves that shade the ground, which reduces water evaporation from the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents heavy rain from washing away the fertile topsoil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it risky for me to start a new farm right next to an old, abandoned cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ aaaje ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni ashi lɛ?

english: Yes, old or abandoned cocoa farms often harbour lingering pests and diseases like swollen shoot virus. Setting up a new farm right next to them makes it easy for those hidden diseases to cross over to your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji ni etsɛ loo ni ashi amɛ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. Okwaafoi hee ni ato yɛ Okwaafoi lɛ ahe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nakai helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ akɛ amɛbaatu kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crops planted close to the bush seem to catch diseases more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai oya lɛ?

english: The wild bush can shelter insects, fungi, and wild plants that carry diseases without showing obvious symptoms. These pests easily jump from the bush into your cultivated farmland.
ga: Koo mli tsei baanyɛ ahi koo mli tsei, ŋmeii, kɛ koo mli tsei ni hiɛ helai ni amɛjieee okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛyaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: How do extension officers know which areas in Ghana have crop diseases and which areas are clean?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ ale hei ni tsei ahe helai yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ kɛ hei ni he tse?

english: Officers visit farms across different regions, inspect crop health, collect plant samples, and map out where diseases are active so they can advise farmers on high-risk and safe planting zones.
ga: Amralofoi yaa ŋmɔji amli yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ Kwɛmɔ tsei ahewalɛ Bua tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa ni ofee shikpɔŋ he mfoniri ni tsɔɔ hei ni helai baa. Koni ekɛ ŋaawoo aha okwaafoi yɛ okwaayeli hei ni yɔɔ oshara waa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ahe

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and build big cobs, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to build up in the ground. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture for planting seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball in your hand. If it holds its shape without dripping excess water, but crumbles easily when squeezed lightly with a finger, the soil has ideal moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi. Shi efiteɔ oya ni kɛ́ okɛ oniji ŋmɔ mli blɛoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long, leading to fungal diseases. Planting cassava on ridges or mounds in well-drained soil prevents excess water from suffocating the roots during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding on the underside of the leaves. These pests damage the young leaf tissue and can pass viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ fiteɔ baa bibii lɛ ahe fãji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are caterpillars eating up my cabbage leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ye mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves are soft and nutritious, attracting moths and butterflies that lay eggs on them. When the eggs hatch into caterpillars, they eat constantly to grow fast, requiring early hand-picking or organic pesticides like neem spray to control them.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii Amɛbaaye nii be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara oya. Esa akɛ akɛ niji aŋɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shishijee. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, tamɔ neem spray, atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but shed most of them because the tree lacks the water, nutrients, or energy to support every flower turning into a full pod.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii loo hewalɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ahi shi ni efee dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off without producing fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ yibii ni ewooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat causes tomato pollen to become dry and sterile, preventing fertilization. Without fertilization, the plant drops the flower to save energy for when cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔmɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight, which the leaves use to make food for growing large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf spot diseases and allowing maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Akɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi baa he hela naa ni oha hulu la lɛ aba enɔ babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, light, and soil water. Leaving only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small sucker ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Sucker kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo kɛ sucker bibioo kome Enɛ baaha nitsumɔhe wulu lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small buds or nodes along the stalk. You must plant them with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the plant grows properly above ground rather than getting stunted.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo nodes, yɛ tso lɛ he. Osumɔɔ ni odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Koni tso lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to grow big, heavy yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Minɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: These holes are caused by pests like Fall Armyworms or stem borers. They chew into the growing center of the plant, which stops leaf growth and can destroy your entire harvest if not treated early.
ga: Kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworms loo stem borers ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ dalɛ kpaa, ni ebaanyɛ efite onibii fɛɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.
