english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy enough to bear pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ pepper yibii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots draw up the calcium needed for firm, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná tomato ni wa ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and attracts corn pests. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni egbalaa ŋmãa mli kooloi kɛbaa ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply NPK fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after germination, so the roots can absorb the food before heavy rain washes it away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afɔ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant yields a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii babaoo, babaoo, ni tsii aba.

english: Why does my rice crop dry up and die so fast whenever rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have very shallow root systems that cannot reach deep groundwater during dry spells. They require continuous moisture around the root zone, which is why lowland valley fields are ideal for rice farming.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Amɛmiitao nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, no hewɔ ni ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave diseased or pruned leaves lying around my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi baai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni afolɔ amɛhe lɛ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔji lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Leaves removed from sick or overgrown plants can still harbor fungal spores and pests. Leaving them under trees allows rain to splash diseases back onto healthy crops, damaging your future harvest.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛdara fe nine lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lolo. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ gbɛɔ helai eshwaa. Ku osɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli Enɛ fiteɔ owɔsɛɛ nibii ni obaafee lɛ.

english: What should I do with diseased leftover pods still hanging on my cocoa trees after harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ eshwɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: You must remove and dispose of all leftover or mummified pods away from the farm. Leaving them on trees allows fungi like black pod to survive through the dry season and infect the next crop.
ga: Esa akɛ oye mumified pods ni eshwɛ loo mummified pods fɛɛ nɔ kunim ni ojie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does keeping my crop harvesting area clean help protect the quality of my cocoa seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ he ni akpaa nii lɛ he tseɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mi-kookoo lɛ he?

english: A clean harvest area prevents dirt, dead leaves, and harmful microbes from mixing with your fresh seeds. This ensures your crops process smoothly without contamination or spoilage.
ga: Nikpamɔ he ni mli tse lɛ baatsi muji naa. baai ni egboi kɛ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛfutu odumɔwui heei lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni muji loo fitemɔ bɛ mli.

english: What is the sticky white substance inside a fresh cocoa pod, and why does it feel like okra?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ, ni mɛni hewɔ enuɔ he tamɔ okra lɛ?

english: That sticky substance is natural fruit pulp rich in sugars and water. It coats the seeds to protect them while inside the pod, much like the natural mucilage found in okra plants.
ga: Nɔ ni ŋmɛɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ ni sugar kɛ nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Etamɔ adebɔɔ mli muji ni anaa yɛ gumbo mli lɛ.

english: Why do fresh crop seeds have a slimy coat on them when I take them out of the pod?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: The slimy coat retains essential moisture and protects the delicate seeds from drying out before they are ready to germinate or be fermented.
ga: Mucilaginous coating lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does the sticky pulp surrounding fresh cocoa beans need to melt away during processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii heei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: As the sticky pulp ferments and turns to liquid, it generates heat. This heat penetrates the beans, killing the seed embryo and unlocking the rich chocolate color and flavor needed for sale.
ga: Beni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ nu. baaha dɔlɛ aba Dɔlɛ nɛɛ boteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. gbeɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni egbeleɔ tsokolate sui ni jara wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔi ni he hiaa kɛha jarayeli lɛ naa.

english: When is the right time to start processing seeds after removing them from the pods?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ shishi beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: Seed processing should begin shortly after pod breaking while the sugary pulp is fresh. Delaying processing allows unwanted rot or mold to set in, reducing the quality of your beans.
ga: Esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔ shishi beni ŋmeii lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji ehee lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ atsake nitsumɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛbua ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe hilɛ baa shi.

english: Why must I separate unwanted leaves and plant material from my seeds during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe nibii ni ataooo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Leaving trash and leaves among fresh seeds traps excess moisture and brings decay, which ruins seed taste and causes buyer rejections at the buying depot.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi kɛ baai yɛ dumɔwui heei ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ahi mli ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ amɛ yɛ he ni amɛheɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do with empty crop husks left over after collecting my harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni eshwɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Empty husks should be collected, moved away from live crop trees, or composted properly. Leaving wet piles of husks near living trees creates a breeding ground for rot and pests.
ga: Esa akɛ abua ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ naa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe. aloo feemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ ni abua naa yɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why is it important to trim off unnecessary leaves from my crop canopy before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni he ehiaaa kɛjɛ mi ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Trimming dense leaves allows air and sunlight to dry out excessive moisture around pods, preventing fungal diseases from ruining the pods before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite tsei lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and need shade to survive. Without bigger trees or plantains to block the heavy sunshine, the direct sun burns the young leaves and dries up the water in the soil before the roots can drink.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei bibii ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunshine to catch light and make food for the yam underground. If the vines lay flat on the ground, the leaves rot from soil moisture and get eaten easily by bugs.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha sweet potato ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food that keeps plants green and healthy. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the new leaves, leaving the older leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei amli. Ha baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts on the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull natural plant food out of the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them alongside maize feeds the soil naturally so your maize can grow bigger.
ga: Peanuts ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Dumɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni oŋmãa lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off completely during the dry season, and does it mean my crop is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo?

english: Your cassava is not dead; dropping leaves is a survival trick it uses to save water when the ground gets hot and dry. As soon as the rains return, the plant will quickly grow fresh leaves and keep growing tubers underground.
ga: O cassava ɔ gbo we lolo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nu nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ ni tso lɛ woɔ baai heei oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my corn seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until you have had two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the dirt. If you plant after just one small rain, the top soil will dry out quickly and kill the tender young sprout before the next rain arrives.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egbeɔ tsei bibii dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids hiding under the leaves. They suck the sap out of the plant and pass along plant sicknesses that cause the leaves to twist up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei ahelai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. When stressed by heat or water, the plant drops its flowers to protect itself instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo loo nu he Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ, tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛkwɛ ehe.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not hold deeply into the ground. When the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, strong winds can easily pull the tree down unless you support the stem with a strong wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu ko ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni wa tsu nii ni okɛfi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal the food and water in the soil right away before your crop roots can catch them. Even with lots of rain, your crops stay hungry because the weeds are taking the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi baaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if my land has a lot of stones under the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If cocoa roots hit hard stones underground, they cannot grow down deep to reach water and nutrients. This weakens the tree and can cause it to dry up and die, especially during dry seasons.
ga: Kɛji kookoo shishifãi lɛ tswa tɛi ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛyashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha egbi ni egbo, titri lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, loose, and dark with rich nutrients, allowing roots to go down without hitting hard rocks, gravel, or waterlogged clay.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ duŋ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni tɛi ni wa, tɛi bibii, loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ etswaaa amɛ.

english: Should I remove rocks and stones from my planting holes before putting in seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tɛi kɛjɛ dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani mikɛ dumɔwui afata he?

english: Yes, clearing stones from planting holes gives young roots space to spread easily and tap deep into the ground for moisture and stability.
ga: Hɛɛ, tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo. ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shiŋŋfeemɔ aha.

english: How deep should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need to be planted in deep holes—about 30 to 45 centimeters deep—so that the base is well covered with soil to give the plant strong support against heavy winds.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi yɛ bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli, ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 30 kɛyashi 45, koni shikpɔŋ aha shishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to cover the base of a newly planted plantain sucker completely with soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ sũ aha tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ashishi kwraa lɛ?

english: Covering the base properly keeps moisture around the roots, protects the sucker from pests, and ensures the stems grow deep and sturdy in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ aha shishigbɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaabu ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ewaa

english: How deep should a young cocoa seedling be placed in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ akɛ kookoo tsei bibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: A cocoa seedling should be planted at the same depth it was in its nursery bag, ensuring the main taproot points straight down without bending.
ga: Esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ akɛ taproot titri lɛ ama shi tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain on the same farm with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade, protecting young, tender cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and soil drying out.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Will plantain plants steal food and water from my young cocoa trees if I plant them together?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji mikɛ amɛ fee ekome?

english: If spaced correctly, plantain plants help cocoa by providing shade and maintaining soil moisture, outweighing any small competition for nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni jɛkɛ lɛ ja lɛ, Plantains baaye abua kookoo lɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni ekɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ko fioo fe akaŋshii kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seedlings die a few months after I plant them on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa often dies due to lack of shade from harsh sun, poor root growth caused by stony soil, or planting in shallow holes that dry out fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo ni amɛnaaa lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ Aloo dumɔ yɛ bu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya.

english: How do deep roots help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Crops with deep roots can reach water trapped far below the surface, allowing them to stay green and alive even when rain has stopped for months.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná nu ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji babaoo po.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and intense light. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a natural canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water during peak sunshine. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture when the air is hot and the soil is dry.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi.

english: Is it better for my tomato crops if I give them heavy water once a week or light water every day?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mi tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo ha lɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli loo nu fioo ko daa gbi?

english: Light daily watering keeps roots near the soil surface where they dry out quickly. Deep waterings done less frequently force tomato roots to grow deep into the soil to find moisture, making the crop stronger during dry spells.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli fioo daa gbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni no haa amɛgbiɔ oya. Nu ni afɔɔɔ shwiemɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha tomato shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why do the roots of my vegetable crops rot when water sits on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, it pushes air out of the soil and starves the roots of oxygen, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ.

english: Why does irrigating my crops early in the morning work better than watering them at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering at noon causes much of the water to evaporate into the hot air before the roots can take it in. Early morning watering gives the soil time to absorb moisture so plants can drink before the heat sets in.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anu nu dani la lɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks sufficient nitrogen. The corn plant copes by pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sending it to nourish the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge stems and green leaves but only tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus its energy on leafy top growth instead of storing food in the underground roots. A balanced soil food supply encourages the plant to build thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni mli tse.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny with small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light, leaving them too weak to form big, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I clear all the tall trees from around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act as a natural canopy that keeps the young seedlings cool and retains moisture in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without producing any peppers when weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to pepper plants. To survive, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and moisture rather than spending resources to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. koni ehi shi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my onion plants produce seeds at the top instead of growing big bulbs underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ miiwo dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Onions form seeds early when they experience sudden weather stress or irregular watering. The plant senses danger, assumes it might die, and rushes to reproduce seeds rather than expanding its bulb.
ga: Sabolai feɔ dumɔwui mra. Kɛ amɛna kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ Tsei lɛ nuɔ oshara he. Asusuɔ akɛ ekolɛ egbo. ni amɛfee oya koni amɛgbɛ dumɔwui amɛshwã yɛ bulbs ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How long does a newly planted mango tree take to settle in and start growing properly on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni adu ehee lɛ baahi shi ni ebɔi dalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: After planting, a young mango tree usually takes about 3 to 6 months to establish its root system firmly in the soil before it starts showing strong new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mango tsei bibii lɛ, amɛheɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛjeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishi.

english: What basic care do my mango trees need once the young seedlings are planted in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ mi mango tso lɛ biɔ beni aduɔ dumɔwui bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly planted mango trees need regular watering during dry spells, clearing of weeds around the base so they do not steal nutrients, and protection from roaming farm animals.
ga: Mango tsei ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi koni ekaju niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni ebu ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe

english: How do I know when my mango trees are mature enough to start producing healthy fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi mango tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ womɔ?

english: Grafted mango trees typically begin flowering and bearing good fruit around 3 to 4 years after planting, once their trunk is thick and branches are strong enough to support the weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eniji lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does doing crop farming well mean for a beginner like me who wants good yield?
ga: Mɛni tsei akwɛmɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ kɛha mɔ ko ni jeɔ shishi tamɔ mi ni miitao yibiiwoo kpakpa lɛ?

english: Doing farming well means choosing quality seedlings, spacing trees correctly, weeding regularly, applying proper organic or chemical fertilizers, and controlling pests before they cause damage.
ga: Okwaayeli jogbaŋŋ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahalaa. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ dani amɛfiteɔ nii.

english: How can proper trimming of my crop trees protect them from common diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa?

english: Pruning or trimming dead branches opens up the tree canopy, allowing sunlight and air to flow through, which keeps leaves dry and reduces fungal diseases during the rainy season.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi ni afolɔ loo afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What other useful things can I produce from my mango crop besides selling fresh fruit in the market?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi yɔɔ mango tso lɛ he kɛfata aduawai heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he?

english: Beyond selling raw fruits, mangoes can be processed into dried fruit slices, natural juices, jams, or mango puree, which allows you to sell products even when the harvest season is over.
ga: Kɛfata aduawai ni ahoo lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he lɛ, abaanyɛ afee Mango hu ni afee aduawai ni egbi lɛ fãi. Adebɔɔ mli tso yibii amli nu, jam loo mango puree Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ eho po.

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil so quickly, and how can processing help me save my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni te nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: Fresh fruits spoil quickly because of warm weather and natural ripening; processing excess fruits into dried snacks or juices preserves them for many months without spoilage.
ga: Yibii heei fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai ni fa fe nine lɛ fee niyenii ni egbi loo nu lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehi shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee.

english: How can starting a commercial mango farm create job opportunities for young people in my village?
ga: Te mango ŋmɔ ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ baaha oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ aná nitsumɔ hegbɛi amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: A commercial farm needs ongoing labor for land preparation, planting, weeding, harvesting, and processing the fruits, which provides steady employment for youth and women in the community.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmɔji biɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, dumɔ nii, jwɛi, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ. kɛ aduawai ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa oblahii kɛ oblayei kɛ yei ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Is mango farming a reliable long-term business for a farmer here in Ghana?
ga: Ani mango okwaayeli ji nitsumɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, tree crops like mangoes provide a long-term income stream because once the trees are established, they continue producing fruit every year for several decades with good maintenance.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli tamɔ mango haa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where can I get technical guidance and support to successfully run a large farming project?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni kɔɔ ŋaa he koni manyɛ matsu okwaayeli nitsumɔ wulu ko ni yeɔ omanye yɛ?

english: You can get expert guidance through local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) extension officers, district farmer cooperatives, and agricultural training organizations operating in your region.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona ŋaawoo ni he esa kɛjɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) Extension Nitsulɔ, Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi Akuu lɛ dɛŋ. kɛ okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I pick my coconuts when they are still very green, will they still mature properly at home?
ga: Kɛji obua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ anaa Ani shia lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Yes, green coconuts will continue to mature after harvest. As long as you keep them in a cool, shaded place, the fruit inside will naturally dry out and mature over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni okɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my green fruits ripen much faster when I pile them close together after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ mikɛto amɛhe beni mikpa amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested fruits release a natural, invisible ripening gas. When fruits are piled together, this gas gets trapped around them and causes the whole pile to soften and turn color much faster.
ga: Yibii ni akpa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni anaaa lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ ato aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ Gas nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fɛɛ feɔ blɛoo ni etsakeɔ ehiɛ su oya kwraa.

english: How can I know if my green crops are mature enough to be harvested early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ mra?

english: Mature green crops feel heavy for their size, have a firm skin, and reach their full shape. If picked too young, they will wither instead of maturing properly.
ga: Tsei eŋɔli ni eda lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa yɛ amɛdalɛ hewɔ. yɛ hewolo ni mli wa ni eyɛ su ni yeɔ emuu Kɛji ohala akɛ obaafee gbekɛ tsɔ Amɛbaagbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara kwraa.

english: Why is it better to place my harvested crops under a shade tree instead of leaving them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ baawo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Direct sunlight heats up harvested crops and bakes the moisture out of them quickly. Shade keeps the crop cool, prevents water loss, and keeps the crop fresh for a much longer time.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa fɛ̃i lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Tsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: How long can I safely leave green coconuts sitting in a shaded area before they go bad?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shweshweeshwe yɛ shĩa mli dani amɛfite?

english: Green coconuts stored in a cool, shaded place can safely rest for up to two months while slowly drying and maturing without spoiling.
ga: Kokooi eŋɔli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ, ni amɛgbi fiofio ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do some of my harvested crops decay quickly if I put them straight into warm bags after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛwo kotokui ni mli edɔ mli beni mikpa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops still breathe and produce heat. Trapping that heat inside warm bags creates moisture and heat, which makes mold and rot grow very quickly.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Dɔlɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa oya waa.

english: Why do farmers leave certain harvested crops in a shaded room for weeks before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shiɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkpa lɛ yɛ tsũi ni mli ewo hulutsoo mli otsii babaoo dani amɛkɛbaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Resting crops in a shaded, dry area lets their outer skin harden and cure. This natural protective layer prevents disease from entering and extends how long the crop stays fresh.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo he ko ni hulu enyɔ shi ni egbi lɛ, ebaaha hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli awa ni etsa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabote mli, ni ehaa be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi ehee lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my crops lose so much weight after sitting for a few days after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ be mli ni mita shi gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once a crop is detached from the root, it can no longer draw water from the soil. It constantly loses water through evaporation into the air, which causes it to lose weight and shrink.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Enyɛŋ ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Efiteɔ nu be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ la ni efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do young plants and harvested fruits spoil faster during the dry, hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High heat speeds up the internal breakdown of the fruit and causes rapid water loss, making both growing plants and harvested food age and spoil much faster.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli fiteɔ oya ni ehaa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni miida kɛ niyenii ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my crops turn bad if I store them on wet ground under the shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: While shade protects crops from heat, damp ground allows fungi and bacteria to crawl into the crop's skin, causing rot even if the temperature is cool.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he moŋ, shi hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ po.

english: What is a liquid fertilizer, and how is it different from the usual dry fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he?

english: Liquid fertilizer is plant food concentrated in liquid form that you dilute with water and spray onto crops or soil. Unlike dry granules that dissolve slowly in the soil, liquid fertilizer provides quick nourishment that plants can absorb right away.
ga: Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ji tso niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni okɛ nu shwieɔ mli ni okɛshwieɔ onibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio lɛ ahe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ oya.

english: Can liquid fertilizer completely replace solid fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Ani nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa najiaŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, liquid fertilizer is meant for quick feeding through the leaves, while solid fertilizers build long-term nutrient rich soil. Using solid fertilizer at planting and liquid fertilizer during fast growth gives your crops the best balance.
ga: Dabi, afee nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha foliar oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tsu nii yɛ dumɔ be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ oya lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Yes, spraying liquid fertilizer directly on crop leaves is called foliar feeding. Leaves have tiny openings that absorb nutrients faster than roots, making it great for giving sickly crops a fast boost.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ foliar feeding. Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shishifãi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ oyaiyeli.

english: Why does the time I choose to apply fertilizer matter so much for my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni mikɛhalaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Crops need specific nutrients at critical stages, such as root development or flowering. Applying fertilizer at the right time ensures the plant uses the nutrients to grow bigger fruits or grains instead of wasting them.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa amli pɛ, tamɔ shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ loo fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaafite amɛ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops before or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or right after light rain. If you apply it right before heavy rain, the water will wash the fertilizer away before your crops can feed on it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo sɛɛ. Kɛ okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ.

english: What time of day should I spray liquid fertilizer on my maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ afɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early morning or late evening when the sun is gentle. If you spray during the hot afternoon, the heat will evaporate the liquid quickly and can burn the plant leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nii ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How do I know the right stage in my crop's life to give it extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fã ni sa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ mli koni mikɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ afata he aha?

english: Crops usually need their first feed 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting to grow strong leaves, and a second feed just before flowering to help form healthy seeds or fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ taoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ niyenii yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni aha lɛ niyenii shii enyɔ nɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi koni eye ebua ni ewaje dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow, and will fertilizer fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ asaa enɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crop is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying the right fertilizer early enough restores healthy green leaves so the plant can make energy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baatsu nii mra ni Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on them at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn crop roots and cause leaf edges to dry up and turn brown. Too many nutrients at once can shock the crop and cut down your final harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ agbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe afee shoo ni eha onaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: How fast should I expect my crops to change after I apply a liquid fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsake oya ha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo mli sɛɛ?

english: Because crops absorb liquid through their leaves quickly, you should start seeing greener and stronger leaves within 3 to 7 days after application if weather conditions are good.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ oje shishi ona baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni mli wa yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni okɛtsu nii lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from direct sun and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start producing big bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi aduawai wuji womɔ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly in the ground, making the heavy plant top-heavy when fruiting. Propping up the main stem with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles supports the weight and prevents wind from knocking them over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fioo, ni no haa tsei ni tsii lɛ feɔ tsii kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa to tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi muji lɛ sɛɛ ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekatswa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow green and produce large cobs. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer fixes this issue.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my other crops help my soil?
ga: Cowpeas loo beans ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe Te minɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decompose, they release nitrogen into the soil, naturally fertilizing neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛwo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Burying or covering the fertilizer slightly with soil near the base of the plant stops heavy rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fu loo akɛha nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop roots with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) shades the soil from heat, reduces water evaporation during dry spells, suppresses weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich organic matter.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni woɔ yibii

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that transmit viruses from plant to plant. Controlling whitefly populations with insect nets or recommended treatments prevents the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii gbɛɔ tomato baa curl lɛ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ Whitefly ayibɔ ni akudɔɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are tiny green caterpillars eating holes into the growing center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid in the funnel of the maize plant. Checking leaves early and applying appropriate natural remedies like neem oil or recommended treatments kills them before they destroy the crop center.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii tsei amli lɛ amli. Akwɛ baai lɛ amli mra ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni sa tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaha nakai baai lɛ agboi dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do pests keep attacking my cocoa trees even after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: If crop medicines are not mixed at the exact recommended dosage or applied at the right time of day, they will not effectively kill the pests. Following proper application instructions ensures the chemical works as intended.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ futuuu bɔ ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ loo akɛtsuuu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Nakai tsofai lɛ nyɛŋ agbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni sa ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Mixing different chemicals without proper advice can weaken their power or create a toxic mix that burns your crop leaves. Always consult an extension officer before combining agrochemicals.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛ́ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eba tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ shi loo efee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ dani okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ afata he.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops have tiny holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on young leaves. Spraying recommended insecticides directly into the center leaf whorl early in the morning or late evening helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray my farm again a few weeks after the first treatment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofafeemɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The initial spray usually kills adult pests but may not destroy their unhatched eggs. A follow-up treatment breaks the pest breeding cycle by killing newly hatched insects before they lay more eggs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ. Shi ekolɛ ekpataaa ŋmeii ni afɔko amɛ lɛ ahiɛ. Tsofai ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni efɔ ehee lɛ agbemɔ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees scorching and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from sun damage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ baa.

english: Why do many of the small cocoa pods on my tree shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Small pods often turn black due to fungal infections like black pod disease or lack of soil nutrients. Regular pruning to let in sunlight and applying recommended fungicides protects young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ black pod hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli daa koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ, ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and the whole trunk falling over easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This is often caused by root damage from pests like nematodes or trunk borers weakened by fungal disease. Plant healthy, treated suckers in well-drained soil to prevent this breakdown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers ni fungal hela egbɔjɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Dumɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni atsa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge leafy stems but yields very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium. Using balanced plant nutrients encourages the plant to channel energy into expanding its roots into big tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni daa fe nine lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje koni amɛgbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too closely causes them to fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to develop full cobs.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds hidden underground sprout whenever sunlight and rain hit fresh soil. Mulching or planting cover crops shades the ground and prevents dormant weed seeds from getting the light they need to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ. Mulching, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. La ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha shweremɔ lɛ ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ

english: This usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in that spot. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiishã yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains protect the young trees from harsh sun and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out, allowing the plant to generate more energy to feed and expand the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or lack of water. Keeping the soil moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nu ni faaa yɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ehaa tomato fioo ko pɛ.

english: This happens when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, which encourages leaf and stem growth instead of fruit production. Excessive leaf growth distracts the plant from making flowers and fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ woɔ baa kɛ tso yibii adalɛ he hewalɛ moŋ fe aduawai ni baajɛ mli aba. Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Seeds need sustained soil moisture to germinate and survive. It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down, rather than planting immediately after the very first light rainfall.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se.

english: Why do cassava leaves start curling up and showing yellow patterns during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the plant, reducing its ability to grow thick tubers.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ baa shi.

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. They naturally feed the neighboring maize plants and help keep the soil fertile.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions and quickly grab water and nutrients from the soil. Because they grow faster, clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and light from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: If I stop buying and using chemical fertilizers on my maize, will my crops still grow big and healthy?
ga: Kɛ mikpa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ hemɔ kɛ nitsumɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baadara lolo ni amɛhe wa?

english: Yes, crops can grow very well using natural compost, animal manure, or decayed plant leaves. These organic foods feed the soil gently, helping plants grow strong while keeping the soil rich for future seasons without costing you extra money.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ waa kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei lɛ ni amɛfiteee shika babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn yellow, and how can I fix it without buying expensive store chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa yɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen. You can feed them naturally by making compost from food scraps, dried leaves, and livestock manure, which provides the exact nutrients your plants need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Obaanyɛ oha amɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ, baai ni egboi, kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading poultry or cow manure in my farm soil help my cassava grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts like a soft sponge that holds rainwater in the dirt so plant roots do not dry out. As it breaks down, it slowly releases natural plant food into the ground, helping cassava roots swell and grow larger.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni tsei shishifãi akagbi Beni efiteɔ lɛ, ejieɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio. Eyeɔ ebuaa cassava shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do some extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas in my field before I plant my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural plant food directly out of the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave free nitrogen in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Is there a way I can protect my cabbage from insect pests without spraying dangerous chemical poisons?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mi-cabbage lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara shwieee nɔ?

english: Yes, you can make a natural pest spray by crushing neem leaves or hot pepper and mixing them with warm water and a little soap. Spraying this on your plants drives pests away without leaving toxic chemical residues on your food.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛtsɔ neem baai loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni okɛ nu ni mli edɔ kɛ samla fioo baafutu mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ enɛ shwie otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote ohe ni tsofa fɔŋ ko akashi oniyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Can spraying too many chemical pest medicines on my tomatoes make the harvest unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ babaoo ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Yes, heavy chemical sprays leave poison residues on the fruit that do not wash off easily and can cause illness when eaten. Switching to organic insect traps and natural leaf sprays keeps your tomatoes safe and healthy to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewa akɛ abaafɔ he, ni kɛ́ aye lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba. Kɛji otsake kɛtee organic bug zappers kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha o-tomato lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly in the hot sun, and how can I keep the ground moist longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Bare dirt loses water fast under the hot sun. Covering the ground around plant stems with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a shade blanket that traps moisture in the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Muji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year if I keep planting the exact same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil until the land becomes weak. Rotating different types of crops each season gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its natural nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: I see earthworms living in my farm soil; are they damaging my crop roots or helping them?
ga: Mina shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ani amɛmiifite mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua amɛ?

english: Earthworms are a sign of rich, healthy soil. They dig tiny tunnels that allow air and rainwater to reach crop roots easily, and their droppings create rich, free organic food for your plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he okadi. Amɛfo gbɛ bibioo ko. No haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe oya. Ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Is it better for my soil if I burn the dry weeds when clearing my land, or should I leave them to rot?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi ni egbi beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo esa akɛ maha amɛgboi?

english: Leaving weeds to rot in the field turns them into natural compost that feeds the soil. Burning destroys important soil nutrients, kills friendly living organisms in the earth, and leaves the soil dry and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ aha jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kpatamɔ bɔɔ nii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Flower drop usually happens when weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks moisture and nutrients. When extreme heat hits, tomato plants get stressed and drop blossoms to conserve energy rather than trying to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii bɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my onion plants producing flowers instead of developing big bulbs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ bulbs wuji ni amɛbaakwɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When onion plants flower prematurely, it is called bolting. This happens when the plant experiences sudden temperature changes or water stress, making it think it is dying, so it quickly produces seeds to reproduce instead of expanding its bulb.
ga: Kɛji onion tsei lɛ fɔ mra lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ bolting. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hulutsoo tsakemɔi trukaa loo nu mli haomɔ. Ehaa osusuɔ akɛ eshwɛ fioo ni ebaagbo. No hewɔ lɛ, ewoɔ dumɔwui oya koni ekɛfɔ yɛ bulbs ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants look strong in the morning but wilt completely under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa leebi shi amɛgboiɔ kwraa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables wilt in the hot afternoon because their leaves lose water faster through evaporation than their roots can pull from the soil. If they recover by the next morning, it means the roots are working, but your soil may need organic mulch to stay cool and hold water longer.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ohe wa bo enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miitsu nii. Shi ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ he baahia koni ehi shi fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or from a virus spread by whiteflies. These insects suck sap from the leaves, causing them to distort and lose color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe su lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular—switching between too dry and too wet—which prevents the plant roots from absorbing calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛtsɔ nu ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni efɔ tsɔ lɛ ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can planting garlic close to my other vegetables help protect them from bugs?
ga: Galiki ni aduɔ yɛ aduawai krokomɛi ahe Ani minɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, garlic acts as a natural pest repellent. The strong smell of garlic confuses and repels pests like aphids, beetles, and caterpillars, making it a great companion crop to protect vegetables like peppers and tomatoes.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, galiki tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Garlic he ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa mɔ yiŋ feɔ lɛ kɔshikɔshi ni eshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aphids, ladybugs kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa galiki feɔ nanemɛi tso kpakpa ni buɔ aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato he.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant right before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when they receive a sudden, heavy supply of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are my pepper fruits remaining very small and not growing hot or spicy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper buds lɛ ji bibii ni edɔɔɔ loo edɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper size and heat depend on heat, sunlight, and proper feeding. If pepper plants receive too much shade or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, the plant will grow lots of leafy stems instead of focusing its energy on big, spicy fruits.
ga: Pepper dalɛ kɛ edɔlɛ damɔ dɔlɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pepper tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Tso lɛ yɛ shishifã ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma tso yiblii nguahi nɛ a ngɛ mi ɔ nɔ.

english: Onions tell you they are mature when their green leafy tops start to turn yellow and fall over on their own. Once about half of the tops in your field have collapsed, the bulbs have finished growing and are ready to be harvested.
ga: Sabalai kɛɔ bo akɛ amɛdara beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Beni aaafee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fã efo lɛ. Bulb lɛ egbe shweremɔ naa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I plant the garlic cloves I buy from the market directly into my farm soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu galiki ni ahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: You can plant market garlic cloves, but imported varieties from store shelves may be treated with chemicals to stop sprouting or might not thrive in tropical heat. It is best to use local garlic cloves adapted to your area's climate.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu galiki ŋmeii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. Shi henɔi ni akɛbaajɛ shwapoi amli lɛ baanyɛ abi tsofai ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli galiki ni sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do agricultural officers cut down my whole cocoa tree when only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ mi kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ be mli ni baai fioo pɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa diseases like Swollen Shoot spread invisibly inside the trunk and roots long before showing on all branches. Cutting down the whole tree is the only way to stop the virus from travelling through the roots and air to destroy the surrounding healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Cocoa helai, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu lɛ, gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni anaaa nɔ. dani nine fɛɛ nine baaje kpo Tsei muu fɛɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni efite tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If one cocoa tree in the middle of my farm gets sick, will all my other trees automatically catch the disease?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome Kookoo tsei krokomɛi Ani amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaaná hela lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not automatically, but the trees closest to the sick one are at very high risk. Removing the infected tree quickly along with the immediate neighboring trees creates a safe barrier that stops the sickness from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: jeee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Shi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ helatsɛ lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara mli babaoo. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot where a diseased tree was just cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is better to wait and clear the area thoroughly first. The insects and roots that carry the disease can stay alive in the soil for a while and easily infect young, delicate seedlings planted too soon.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni ojie jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kplukai kɛ shishifãi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be ko ni amɛye dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: How do crop diseases move from my neighbor's farm to my own cocoa farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko jɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Plant diseases usually travel through tiny insects like mealybugs carried by the wind, infected plant sap stuck on shared farm tools like cutlasses, or through connected root systems underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa lɛ amli. Tso mli nu ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ daggers, loo kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni tsa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Can using the same cutlass on different trees spread sickness across my farm?
ga: Ani dade kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei srɔtoi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, when you cut a sick tree, infected sap sticks to your cutlass. Using that same blade on a healthy tree introduces the disease directly into its trunk, just like using an unwashed needle.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ Nu ni hela emɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ okpɔŋɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ nakai baai lɛ nɔŋŋ wo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ hela lɛ baa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nakai eji yɛ ŋmeii ni ahooo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu he.

english: What simple daily steps can I take on my farm to prevent crop diseases from breaking out?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Daa gbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei ahe helai akagbɛ ashwã?

english: Keep your farm clear of heavy weeds, prune extra leaves to let sunlight reach the soil, remove dried or rotting pods immediately, and clean your farm tools regularly.
ga: Ha jwɛi ni mli ewo muji akafee oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai krokomɛi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egbi loo ni egbo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe tsemɔ daa
