english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is dying from a disease or just suffering from dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miigbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛkɛ miipiŋ amɛ?

english: Dry weather usually makes leaves turn brown and drop off evenly across the whole farm. A viral disease causes swollen stems, strange red or pale leaf patterns, or pods that turn black unexpectedly even when there is enough rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Virus helai haa tso lɛ mli fũuɔ. Baai lɛ yɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Aloo pod lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: Are small insects like ants and mealybugs on my cocoa trees harmful to my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, mealybugs suck the juice from cocoa stems and carry deadly viruses from sick trees into healthy ones, while ants protect these mealybugs from danger, helping the disease spread faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, mealybugs lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei amli lɛ ni ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ buɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ awuiyeli he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Who should I inform in my village if I suspect a strange new crop disease on my farm?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ mabɔ he amaniɛ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli? Ni kɛji misusu akɛ tso hela hee ko eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: You should immediately report it to your local Agricultural Extension Officer or Cocoa Extension Assistant so they can examine the farm, confirm the issue, and help you stop it before it affects other farms.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ enɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo kookoo he nitsulɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛma naagba lɛ nɔ mi, ni amɛye amɛbua bo ni okpa dani ená ŋmɔji krokomɛi anɔ hewalɛ.

english: How long should I wait before replanting my farm after diseased trees have been removed?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni madu miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ beni mijie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should generally wait several months after removing the sick trees and destroying their root systems to ensure all disease-carrying insects have died off before putting new seedlings in the ground.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ nyɔji babaoo beni ojie tso ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kooloi ni hiɛ hela lɛ fɛɛ egbo dani okɛ dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant beans together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmeii feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the maize plants, helping them grow taller and stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa amɛ.

english: Why does planting beans on my land make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Beans have special microscopic organisms on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the bean plant dies, this stored nitrogen remains in the earth, enriching the soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans yɛ nibii bibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni anaa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: What will happen to my corn if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, groundwater, and soil food. This competition causes the stalks to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs and a lower total yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa cob lɛ feɔ bibioo ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my bean plants fall off without turning into bean pods during very hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause heat stress in bean plants. To protect themselves from losing too much moisture, the plants drop their flowers to save energy rather than spending resources to produce pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ŋmeii tsei amli. Koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee pods.

english: Why does my corn grow tall and thin with small cobs when it is shaded by tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni tsei kakadaji lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Corn needs full, direct sunlight all day to create food through its leaves. When grown under shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light, which drains its energy and leaves little strength to build thick stalks or large cobs.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni enyɛ etsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ efee niyenii. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. ni baajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ mli ni ehaaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the corn plant is starving for nitrogen or water in the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their healthy green color and helps them make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli.

english: How do weeds growing around my corn plants affect how much grain I will get at harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi ŋmãa tso lɛ saa dumɔwui abɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, rainwater, and soil nutrients away from your corn plants. If weeds are left to grow, your corn gets fewer resources, which stunts its growth and significantly reduces the amount of grain you can harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nugbɔ nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ O-ŋmãa lɛ baaná nibii fioo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I tell when my corn is fully mature and ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Corn is ready for harvest when the outer husks wrap tightly around the cob, turn dry and papery brown, and the silks at the top become completely dark brown and dry to the touch.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ ebɔle ŋmei lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa egbiɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ wolo. ni siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbiɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he.

english: Why does my stored corn get ruined by insects and mold shortly after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stored corn spoils quickly if it is put into bags or granaries before it is completely dry. Any remaining moisture creates a perfect home for mold to grow and attracts hungry insects like grain weevils.
ga: Abɛi ni ato lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku loo ŋmɔ mli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ. ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii.

english: Can I save the corn seeds from this year's harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can plant saved seeds, hybrid corn varieties lose their vigor after the first generation. Replanting saved seeds often results in weaker plants and lower yields compared to purchasing fresh, certified seeds each season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni ato moŋ, Shi ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he waaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How do I know if the land I want to clear in the village has good soil for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni mafolɔ mli yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa?

english: Good soil for maize is usually dark brown or black, feels slightly moist, and drains water well without turning into a swamp. You can also look at the existing wild plants—if natural weeds and shrubs are growing tall and dark green, the soil is fertile.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋshɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hu. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall stems with plenty of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or when crops are planted too close together. The cassava spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my tomato crop if the rainfall stops suddenly while the plants are producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Without water during flowering, tomato plants get stressed, drop their blossoms, and fail to set fruit. Any fruits that do manage to grow may develop black, rotten bottoms known as blossom-end rot due to lack of moisture.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ, fɔfɔii lɛ baashwie shi, ni amɛwooo yibii. Yibii fɛɛ yibii ni baa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ diŋ ni fiteɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field without one crop destroying the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni tso kome efiteee ekroko lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works very well. Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in about three months, while cassava grows more slowly and expands into the empty space after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni akpa abɛi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaf funnels of my young maize plants covered in tiny holes after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ehà mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ? Beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which hatch as soon as the rains start and feed on young, soft leaves. They hide deep inside the leaves during the hot day and eat the plant at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tsei gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster after I clear my farmland by burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa beni mijie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ shãa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning clears the tall grass on top, but the heat awakens buried weed seeds and leaves bare soil exposed to sunlight, allowing weeds to sprout rapidly. Burning also destroys valuable organic matter that crops need to stay strong.
ga: Shãa lɛ jie jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agbo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shi latsaa lɛ teɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Ehaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya Shãa hu fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that spread a virus while feeding on sap. The curling shows that the plant is losing nutrients and cannot produce food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa be mli ni enuɔ mliki Curling tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite, ni enyɛɛɛ efee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my farm so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is already damp after a light rain, but never during a heavy downpour. Placing the fertilizer in small holes near the roots and covering it with a bit of soil prevents rain from carrying it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ bu bibii amli Abɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akafɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings dry up and die right after I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by moving delicate seedlings into hot, harsh sunlight without giving them time to adjust. Moving plants late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps their roots survive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ajieɔ kɛyaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni ahaaa amɛ be ni amɛkɛtsake amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shwane mli ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I tell when my yam tubers under the ground are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Yam is ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the soil naturally turn yellow and dry up completely. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its starch inside the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava stems keep growing very tall, but when I harvest, the tubers under the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lolo shi kɛ́ akpa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on growing leaves and tall stems instead of building tubers underground. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant put energy into growing big roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ shishifãi wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaf tips usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and produce heavy cobs. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni tsii aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: I want to try planting soybeans for the first time, but how do I know if my farm soil is good enough for them?
ga: Miisumɔ ni maka soybeans ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha amɛ?

english: Soybeans are very supportive crops because they can pull their own nitrogen food directly from the air into the soil using tiny bumps on their roots, so they grow well even in poorer soils where maize might struggle.
ga: Soybeans ji nɔ ni woɔ mɔ hewalɛ waa ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ nodes bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ agbala amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya sũ lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni ehiii po nɔ ni ŋmãa baanyɛ abɔi ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my cassava so it doesn't rot or go woody inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Enɛ ji koni akafite loo tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting; harvesting too early gives small roots, but waiting too long makes the roots hard, fibrous, and prone to rotting in wet soil.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baajɛ mli aba. Shi kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ, amɛfee ŋmeii, ni amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Is it better to plant my maize seeds as soon as the very first rain falls, or should I wait?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ, aloo esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: It is best to wait for the rains to become steady and moisten the soil deeply, because a single early rain followed by a dry hot spell can scorch and destroy your freshly germinated seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome ni ahum ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers plant soybean in the same field where they planted maize the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ soybean yɛ ŋmɔji ni adu ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Planting soybean after maize is called crop rotation; soybean enriches the soil with natural nitrogen, breaks insect breeding cycles, and restores fertility for the next season's maize crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ soybeans ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ. Soybeans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Efoɔ kooloi bibii afɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ekɛ fɔmɔ baa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the leaves right in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of young maize plants; catching them early with recommended pest control measures keeps them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting up and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects; using disease-resistant cassava stems from certified suppliers is the best way to keep your farm clean.
ga: Nɛkɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe nɛɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni jɛɔ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury soybean seeds when I am planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-soybean dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Soybean seeds are relatively small, so they should be planted shallowly, about 2 to 3 centimeters deep, so the young sprout can easily push through the soil surface to reach sunlight.
ga: Soybean dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ, aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3, koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why does planting high-yielding improved seeds give a bigger harvest than saving seeds from my own farm last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adumɔ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds from agricultural research are specially bred to resist local pests, withstand dry spells, and yield more food, whereas seeds saved year after year lose their vitality and get weaker.
ga: Atsɔ okwaayeli mli niiamlitaomɔ nɔ atsake dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting a rubber tree before I can start collecting latex from it?
ga: Kɛ́ odu rɔbɔt tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi latɛs lɛ naabuamɔ?

english: Rubber trees take about 5 to 7 years of growth before their trunks become thick enough to be tapped safely for latex without damaging the tree.
ga: Rɔba tsei heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛtso lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtswa rɔba shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my rubber trees too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu rɔba tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin trunks that produce very little latex.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ latɛs fioo ko pɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young rubber trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi rɔba tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years while the rubber trees are still small, you can intercrop food crops between the rows to make food and money while the trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Will tapping latex from my rubber tree every single day harm or kill the tree?
ga: Ani latex ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli daa gbi lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: Tapping every day can weaken the tree and dry out the bark. Giving the tree rest days allows the bark to recover and continue producing latex for many years.
ga: Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha eshishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hejɔɔmɔ gbi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ejie nu afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is the bark on my rubber tree turning dark and rotting where I tap it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ he ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ he ni mitaa he lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal infections from tapping during wet weather or using dirty tools. Cleaning your tapping blade and avoiding tapping during heavy rain protects the wood from rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nibii ni he tseee ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ otsumɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtswaa tsei lɛ ahe ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river to irrigate my farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, river water is great for crops, but you must ensure the water is free from chemicals or pollution from activities like local mining, which can spoil the soil and kill plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, faa mli nu hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi ehe miihia ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai loo mujiwoo ni jɛɔ nifeemɔi tamɔ maŋ lɛ mli shika tsuru taomɔ mli baa lɛ bɛ nu lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ akpɔ̃ ni ekpata tsei ahiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ?

english: Plants lacking water usually have wilting, dry, or curling leaves during the afternoon, while plants standing in too much water get soft, yellow leaves and rotting roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni bɛ nu lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni damɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ji ŋmɔŋ, kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ.

english: What simple step can I take to stop the sun from drying out the soil around my crop roots?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo mafee koni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt around your plant roots with dry grass, leaves, or palm leaves (mulching) shades the soil and traps moisture so plants survive longer without rain.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmei baai (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do tree crops like rubber grow so much better in the Western Region compared to drier areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Anaigbɛ kɛ akɛto hei ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: The Western Region gets long rainy seasons, high humidity, and deep soils that retain moisture, which tree crops need to continuously build trunk size and foliage.
ga: Anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. high humidity Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni toɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aya nɔ amɛtswa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out quickly even after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ waa po lɛ?

english: If soil lacks organic matter like decayed leaves, heavy rain simply runs off the surface instead of soaking in. Adding organic compost helps soil hold onto rainwater like a sponge.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbo lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajo foi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni eeeŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli tamɔ sponji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives them back their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes when the afternoon sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural trick to save water when it gets too hot. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun, which stops moisture from evaporating too quickly out of the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ ŋaa ni akɛtoɔ nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ, hulu la ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ baashɛ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa oya tsɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they are stressed by too much sunshine, dry weather, or poor nutrients in the soil. Maintaining good shade trees and keeping the soil healthy helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they become pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hulu la babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shade kpakpa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain plant, they steal water and food from it. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem grows strong and gives you large bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, dumɔwu titri lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nakai dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ada waa ni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: How do I make sure I am putting cassava stem cuttings into the ground the right way?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ miiwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the stem cutting and make sure they point upward toward the sky before pushing the stem into the ground. If you plant them upside down, the cassava struggles to grow buds and produces fewer tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ. yɛ tsei ni afolɔ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ Ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Cassava baaná naagba yɛ shweremɔ mli ni ebaawo ŋmeii fioo.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are naturally climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make plant food. Staking helps the leaves get full sunshine, which directly feeds the big yam tuber growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ wain tsei anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This black rotting at the bottom is caused by erratic watering, which stops the plant from taking up calcium from the soil. Keeping your watering consistent helps calcium flow steadily into the growing fruit and stops the rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa lɛ baaye abua ni calcium lɛ aya nɔ atsɔ aduawai lɛ amli ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and destroys the pollen inside the flowers, causing the unfertilized flowers to drop off. Adding mulch around the soil keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi ni afeee amɛ pollin lɛ shwieɔ shi. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Is it true that growing cowpeas or groundnuts on my field makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground for crops you plant afterwards like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nibii bibii ni feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leafy tops but refusing to form a tight round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ hiɛ baai wuji shi eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni yitso ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo ahi teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather stays too warm, if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, or if watering is uneven. Balanced plant food and moist, cool soil encourage the center leaves to wrap tightly.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ baafee ekome kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo. Kɛji onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Aloo kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa Tse niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an essential food crops need to grow. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding organic compost helps the leaves turn green and regain their strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo organic compost tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of big green leaves but leaves me with tiny tubers during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ehaa mi ŋmeii bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, it wastes all its energy growing leaves on top instead of building food underground. Cassava produces better, larger tubers when grown in moderate soil without heavy chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Efiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Cassava woɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni dara waa kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to shield them from high heat and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akatsɔ la ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ, ni koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, exposes them to light, and prevents soil diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. tsɔɔ la mli Ni otsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes them to fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with tiny yields. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to feed well and produce a much bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why should I trim off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many small shoots (suckers) grow around a plantain tree, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) dara yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with little caterpillar dirt in the leaf center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats the growing points of maize. Spraying approved crop protection treatments or natural neem solutions early in the morning or late evening controls them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe loo adebɔɔ mli neem tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before they turn into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden changes in water supply. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing mulch around the plants helps them hold onto flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo nu jɛɛhe tsakemɔ trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ sũ wo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows specialized pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts naturally recharges soil nitrogen and cleans the land.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and dry out during hot weeks even when I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli moŋ?

english: Tomato plants lose water very quickly through their leaves in high temperatures, so occasional watering is not enough to keep up with the heat. Watering regularly at the roots and covering the surrounding soil with dried grass mulch helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which helps them make green food. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's growth restores their healthy green color and helps them produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK, tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ toi wuji.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plants experience extreme heat stress or lack consistent water and nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil moist and adding compost helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛnáaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni amɛnáa be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: What is eating up the central funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji mi bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa baai lɛ yeli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive caterpillars that hide inside the central growing point of maize plants. Spraying an approved biological control or insecticide into the leaf funnel early in the morning helps save your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same piece of land with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow very well together because cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves your total harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already in the soil and are adapted to sprout instantly with the first rain to steal light and nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks gives your crops a strong head start so they can outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba pɛ koni amɛju la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛye jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients meant for the fruit. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii dara kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛha aduawai lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no haa otso titri lɛ feɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why is it important to use tall sticks to stake my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei kakadaji atsu nii kɛwo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward the sun to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the hot soil, reduces leaf rot, and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he koni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baa lɛ mli fitemɔ he okadii lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa

english: How does adding dried animal manure to my farm help my crops grow better during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture longer when rain is scarce while slowly releasing steady nutrients that chemical fertilizers alone cannot provide.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa ni tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ aha lɛ kpo.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant sweet potatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Sweet potatoes grow best in loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil. If your soil is heavy clay or stays flooded with water, the potatoes will rot or stay very small instead of developing big, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Atomɔ baagbo loo ebaafee bibioo kwraa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving them proper spacing ensures every plant grows strong and yields well.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ daa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, or the soil may just need compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: How does cassava manage to survive long periods without rainfall during the dry season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during drought to conserve water and stores energy deep down in its thick underground roots, allowing it to rest until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ha ejɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans inside my maize farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps the soil because beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt, which helps the maize grow better without competing heavily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Yam rot in the ground is caused by tiny worms called nematodes or fungal infections that enter the tuber through waterlogged, poorly drained soil. Using clean seed yams and well-drained soil prevents it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully ready to be pulled out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready by pulling up one test plant; if the leaves have started turning yellow and the inside of the pod shells have dark brown markings, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛtsɔ kaa tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do tiny beetles start eating my harvested maize after I put it in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɔi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yeli beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Those beetles are weevils, which lay eggs in grain that still holds moisture. Sun-drying your harvested maize until it is completely dry and hard before storing stops weevils from surviving in it.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lolo lɛ amli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ kɛyashi ebaagbi kwraa dani okɛto koni ŋmeii akahi shi.

english: When is the right time for me to start applying fertilizer to my young papaya plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi mipapaya tso bibioo lɛ mli fɔmɔ nii?

english: You should apply fertilizer to your papaya crop at about 4 months after planting to help the stem and base build up and grow strong.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa awo opapaya tso lɛ mli aaafee nyɔji 4 yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ shishi kɛ eshishi ni amɛma shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Where exactly around my papaya plant should I put the fertilizer?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mipapaya tso lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer should be applied directly to the base of the papaya plant so it can easily feed the stem and encourage base growth.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo papaya tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni eha shishigbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What special care should I give my papaya plants around four months after planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mipapaya tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ sɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: At around four months, you need to apply fertilizer to the base of your papaya plants to boost their trunk development and prepare them for fruiting.
ga: Yɛ nyɔji ejwɛ mli lɛ Ebaabi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata opapaya tso lɛ shishi koni eha shishifã lɛ aya hiɛ ni esaa ehe kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: How can I help my papaya plants grow a thick stem and a wide base?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mipapaya tso lɛ ni ehiɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ?

english: Applying fertilizer to the base of the papaya plant around 4 months after planting encourages both the base and the stem to build up and grow large.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo papaya lɛ shishi aaafee nyɔji 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shishi kɛ eshishifã lɛ fɛɛ adara ni amɛfee agbo.

english: Why is my papaya stem so thin, and how does fertilizer help fix that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ mli etse nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa enɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A thin stem means the plant lacks essential nutrients for structural growth; applying fertilizer to the base gives the papaya the boost it needs to thicken its stem.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tseee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishi lɛ, ebaaha papaya lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔi ni he hiaa koni eha tso lɛ shishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to the structure of a papaya plant when fertilizer is applied to its base?
ga: Mɛni baa bɔ ni papaya tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo eshishigbɛ?

english: When fertilizer is applied to the base, it feeds the lower stem, causing the base and trunk to build up and grow significantly larger.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata shishitoo lɛ he Ebaaha shishigbɛ tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishitoo lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ feɔ ekome ni efeɔ agbo waa.

english: How can I prevent my papaya trees from falling over when wind blows or when heavy rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mipapaya tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa loo nugbɔ miinɛ waa?

english: Applying fertilizer at 4 months builds a large, sturdy base that anchors the papaya tree firmly to the ground so it won't easily topple.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni eye nyɔji 4 lɛ, ebaaha shishitoo agbo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha papaya tso lɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ koni ekagbee shi oya.

english: Will making the base of my papaya tree larger help it bear more fruit?
ga: Ani mi papaya tso lɛ shishitoo ni mifee lɛ agbo lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, a large and well-developed base gives the papaya tree the strength and stability it needs to hold and support a bigger load of fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishitoo agbo ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa papaya tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ shifimɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ yibii ni tsii fe lɛ ni ekɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why do some papaya trees fall under the weight of their own fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyibii ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Papaya trees collapse when their base is too weak; building up a thick, large base through proper fertilizing enables the tree to stand firm while bearing heavy fruit.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ baafite kɛji amɛshishi lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ afee shishitoo ni mli tse ni da ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: What simple step can I take to ensure my papaya farm gives me a high yield?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni mafee koni mipapaya ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Applying fertilizer to the base of your plants at around 4 months thickens the stem and base, which directly enables the tree to bear more fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa wo tso lɛ mli aaafee nyɔji 4 lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ eshishi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How long does it take for a pineapple crop to grow and produce fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ko kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pineapples are slow-growing crops. Depending on the variety and soil care, it usually takes between 12 to 18 months for a planted pineapple to produce a mature, harvestable fruit.
ga: Pineapple ji tso ko ni daa blɛoo. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani ŋmei ni akwɛɔ lɛ shwereɔ ni esaa kɛha kpamɔ. Enɛ damɔ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Can I grow a new crop of pineapples using the leafy tops cut off from harvested fruits?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni afo kɛjɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ makwɛ ŋmei hee ko?

english: Yes, the leafy top (crown) of a pineapple can be planted directly in well-drained soil, where it will sprout roots and grow into a completely new fruiting plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, abaanyɛ adu pineapple yitsei ni yɔɔ baai (akɔɔblei) lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaawo shishifãi ni eda ni etsɔ tso hee kwraa ni woɔ yibii.

english: Do pineapple plants need a lot of water and shade to produce good yields?
ga: Ani nu babaoo kɛ hulutsoo he miihia pineapple tso koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Pineapple plants actually thrive in bright full sunlight and are tough against dry weather. Too much standing water can rot their roots, so they prefer well-drained soil rather than heavy flooding.
ga: Anana tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛsumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nu afua ni naa wa.

english: What causes the leaves on my pineapple plants to turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pineapple tso nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the plant is starving for nutrients—especially nitrogen—or that the soil is holding too much water and suffocating the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my pineapple fruits are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pineapple lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Pineapples are ready to pick when the base of the fruit begins turning from dark green to golden-yellow and starts giving off a sweet, pleasant aroma.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakpa pineapple kɛji shishigbɛ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do Western-style chemical fertilizers actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ Anaigbɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers deliver high concentrations of essential plant foods—like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—directly to the roots, giving crops a quick boost to grow stronger leaves and larger fruits.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hia tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. ni shwereɔ babaoo kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛyibii lɛ hu adara.

english: Will applying store-bought chemical fertilizers damage my soil over time if I am not careful?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shwapo mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji mikwɛɛɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ?

english: If you overuse chemical fertilizers without adding organic matter like animal manure or compost, the soil can become overly acidic and lose its natural fertility over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee acidic tsɔ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall. Applying it near the base of the plant early in the morning allows roots to absorb it before rain washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ dani nugbɔ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops producing low yields even though I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone isn't enough for maximum production. Crops also require balanced soil nutrients, proper spacing so leaves get enough light, and weed control so plants don't compete for nutrients.
ga: Nu pɛ faaa kɛha nitsumɔ babaoo. Niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he miihia tsei. He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ sa bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ koni tsei akatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Can I use the wastewater from my tilapia and catfish ponds to water my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛ tilapia kɛ catfish ŋshɔi amli lɛ atsu nii kɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu?

english: Yes, wastewater from fish ponds is packed with fish waste, which acts as a rich, natural organic fertilizer that helps crops grow greener and produce plentiful fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔi amli lɛ eyi kɛ loo fɔji. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee nɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help your crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did my young tomato plants wither and die right after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer too close to young stems burns the roots by stripping them of moisture. Always apply fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in damp soil so the plant can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata tsei bibii lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashã ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my field after harvesting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Planting beans or cowpeas afterwards fixes nitrogen back into the soil naturally, refreshing your land so your next crop grows better.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans loo cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee ehee bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sun exposure. Big trees act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and drop off during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl and drop when temperatures get too high to stop the plant from losing water. Adding dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and preserves soil water.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akaje nu mli. Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rains keep coming late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ fiofio lɛ?

english: Instead of planting after the first light rain, wait until the soil is thoroughly wet up to the depth of your palm. This ensures there is enough groundwater to keep seeds germinating even if the rain pauses for a few days.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo po.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like powder inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of maize to eat the tender growth, leaving behind digestive waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Eshiɔ niyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli muji ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisting and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and mottled leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can manage this by planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest yield much smaller cobs than new seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibioo kwraa fe dumɔwui hee ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercially produced seeds are specialized hybrids bred for high yields in their first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, they lose their strength, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming extra branches removes leaves that waste energy. It allows the plant to send its nutrients straight into producing larger, healthier tomato fruits instead of just growing more leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baajie tsei ahe tsei ni fiteɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ baai babaoo afata he kɛkɛ lɛ

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so fast before I can sell them at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops rot quickly when they lose moisture or get infected by decay-causing organisms after harvest. Planting improved crop varieties with naturally firmer flesh or stronger skins helps them stay fresh much longer during storage and transport.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ fite loo nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ye amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni atsɔse amɛ kɛ loo ni mli wa loo hewolo ni wa ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi ehee be babaoo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ.

english: Extension officer, is there a crop variety I can plant that doesn't rot easily after harvest?
ga: Promotion officer Ani tsei srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ni fiteee oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, agricultural experts have developed improved crop varieties designed with tougher outer flesh and skins. These varieties resist soft spots and spoilage far better than traditional local varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli he nilelɔi efee tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee koni amɛná kponɔgbɛ loo kɛ hewolo ni mli wa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ fe blema ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How does the toughness of a crop's flesh help prevent it from going bad?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni tso ko wa ha lɛ haaa efite?

english: Tougher flesh acts as a physical barrier against bruising, insects, and decay germs. When the inner tissue is firm, rot-causing organisms cannot easily enter and spread through the crop.
ga: Heloo ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa. Kɛji mligbɛ fã lɛ mli wa lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why are the new seeds recommended by experts better than the traditional ones I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni nilelɔi jieɔ yi lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Expert-recommended seeds are bred specifically to overcome common problems like quick spoilage. They produce crops that have a longer shelf life and firmer texture compared to older, traditional farmer seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ŋaalɔi jieɔ yi lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛtsu naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ fitemɔ oya lɛ ahe nii. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ akɛto okwaafoi akusum dumɔwui ni etsɛ waa lɛ ahe.

english: I live far from the main town market, so how can I stop my produce from rotting during transport?
ga: Mikɛ jarayelihe wulu ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi aduawai kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ be mli ni mikɛmajeɔ lɛ?

english: Choosing crop varieties bred for longer shelf life and tough flesh ensures the produce can survive long journeys over rough roads without bruising or rotting before you reach buyers.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe afee mlɛo lɛ ni ahala lɛ haa nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ nɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni efiteee loo egbooo dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: What actually causes harvested fruits and vegetables to soften and rot?
ga: Mɛni diɛŋtsɛ haa aduawai kɛ aduawai ni akpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ?

english: Rotting happens when microscopic fungi and bacteria break down soft plant tissues. Crop varieties with firm, tough flesh slow down this breakdown process, keeping the harvest good for a longer time.
ga: Gbomɔ baa kɛji ŋmeii bibii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kpata tso bibii lɛ amli fãji lɛ ahiɛ. Tse henɔi ni wa, ni wa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ baa shi. Ehaa nifeemɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do some of my harvested crops last for weeks while others rot in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi otsii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shelf life varies based on the crop's variety and physical structure. Crops with denser, tougher flesh naturally hold onto water better and resist bacterial decay longer than softer varieties.
ga: Shihilɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahenɔi kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Tsei ni mli wa, ni wa lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do agricultural experts create crops that can stay fresh for a long time?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nilelɔi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfeɔ tsei ni baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: Experts select and breed plants that naturally develop stronger cell walls and firmer flesh. This plant breeding makes the harvested produce naturally resistant to rapid rotting.
ga: Nileelɔi halaa tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa wala yibii gbogboi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei afɔmɔ nɛɛ eha ŋmaa lɛ enyɛ eshi fitemɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Does rough handling of my crops during harvest make them spoil faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ yiwalɛ tsu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya?

english: Yes, rough handling creates tiny tears and bruises where rot organisms enter. While planting varieties with tough flesh offers better protection, gentle handling still helps maximize their shelf life.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. Enɛ baaha yaafo bibii kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba. Yɛ hei ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni wa ni aduɔ lɛ haa hebuu kpakpa moŋ. Shi kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lolo ni ekɛ eshihilɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: How will choosing crops with a longer shelf life help my farming business?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni mihalaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Crops that last longer cut down post-harvest losses, giving you more time to transport goods to market and negotiate better market prices without fear of your harvest rotting immediately.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa nɔ ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa onáa be babaoo ni okɛ onibii lɛ yaa jara nɔ ni okɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ baasusu he yɛ jara nɔ ni osheee gbeyei akɛ ŋmaa lɛ baafite amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I find small holes in my mangoes with tiny worms eating them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii hu yɛ. Ye lɛ kɛjɛ emli?

english: Fruit flies lay their eggs under the skin of young fruit. When the eggs hatch, the larvae feed on the flesh inside, making the fruit rot from within before it fully matures.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai bibii ahewolo shishi. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaye loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why does the inside of my fruit turn black and rotten even when the outside skin looks clean and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ amli miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Fungal infections or tiny insects can attack the fruit when it is very young and tiny. The damage stays hidden inside and grows as the fruit expands, ruining the core while leaving the skin intact.
ga: Fungal hela loo kooloi bibii ahe hela Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtutua aduawai beni amɛji bibii waa ni amɛji bibii waa. Nɔ ni efite lɛ teeɔ emli ni edaa be mli ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ mli yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ekpãtãa shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛ ni ehaa hewolo lɛ nɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: How can I protect my growing fruits from insects without damaging the harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miyibii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You can hang protein bait traps to catch adult fruit flies, bag young fruits with protective covers, and maintain good field sanitation by burying fallen, infected fruits.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ protein bait tsɔnei awo tso yibii amli ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe. Aduawai kotokui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni akɛ tsɔi ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ he nii ni amɛkwɛɔ hetsemɔ kpakpa nɔ kɛtsɔ aduawai ni egbee shi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the mangoes on my trees remaining very small instead of swelling big this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii moŋ fe ni eeefu yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fruits stay small when the tree lacks enough water or soil nutrients during its growth stage, or when the tree is holding too many fruits at once and cannot feed them all.
ga: Yibii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. aloo beni tso ko buaa aduawai babaoo naa yɛ be kome mli ni enyɛɛɛ eye fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young fruits drop off the tree when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ani eji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Trees naturally shed young fruit when stressed by severe dry spells, nutrient deficiency, or heavy pest infestation as a way to survive and conserve energy.
ga: Tsei woɔ yibii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ. niyenii ni esaaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi ni akɛ hewalɛ toɔ he

english: What makes the hard seed inside a mango grow healthy and strong?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni wa ni yɔɔ mango mli lɛ daa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ?

english: The inner seed or stone develops properly when the tree receives balanced nutrients, adequate moisture, and stays free from stem-borer pests during early fruit formation.
ga: Dumɔwu loo mesoderm lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. ni ebɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛɔ stem borers lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli

english: How can I tell if my fruit is mature and ready for harvest so it doesn't spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi yibii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ efiteee oya loo efiteee?

english: A mature fruit changes shape from flat to full, develops a lighter skin tone or color shift near the top, and emits a sweet fragrance near the stem.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yibii lɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni mli tse loo nɔ ni etsake yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ he

english: What practical work do I need to do on my fruit trees to get high quality yields every year?
ga: Mɛni ehe hiaa ni mafee mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ daa afi?

english: Prune dead branches to let sunlight in, apply compost or fertilizer around the tree canopy before flowering, and clear weeds to prevent them from stealing food.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ koni hulu la aba mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tso lɛ nɔ tsɔi dani ewo fɔfɔi ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni akaju niyenii.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Flowers fail to set fruit if heavy rains wash away pollen, if dry heat causes blossoms to drop, or if there are not enough bees and insects around to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli egbi lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Does pruning small branches really help my crop produce bigger fruit?
ga: small pruning Ani eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji?

english: Yes, removing weak or extra branches directs the tree's water and food nutrients straight to the remaining fruits, allowing them to grow larger and healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni he waaa loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ kɛyaa yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the young cocoa trees with essential shade and moisture during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.
