english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, humid, and overly shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in light and removing infected pods helps keep the crop healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni ekɛ la aba ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize foliage. Inspecting your field early, removing them by hand, or applying approved treatments during the cool morning or evening will protect your maize.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ. Oŋmɔji lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra manual removal Loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I store my harvested maize while the grains still feel slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ toɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he lolo akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Storing damp maize creates an environment for mold and dangerous toxins to grow, while also attracting storage pests like weevils that destroy your saved grain.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo muji kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbalaa ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the water in my field dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Rice plants rely on constant moisture to draw food and nitrogen from the soil. When the soil becomes too dry, the plant starves, causing its leaves to turn yellow and halting growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni amɛgbala niyenii kɛ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this virus from destroying your farm.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the wet ground to capture more sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to swell and produce large tubers below the soil.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfuu ni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I plant beans together with my maize, will it help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa Ani ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots holding up a very heavy stem. Weak soil, underground root pests, or lack of support cause them to topple, so propping stems with strong poles helps keep them standing.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ni tsii waa ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Aloo yelikɛbuamɔ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa amɛkuɔ shi? No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots prevents the blossoms from drying up and falling off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ daa koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I clear all the large trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their delicate leaves lose moisture too quickly and get scorched. Keeping bigger shade trees nearby protects young cocoa from harsh sun and heat, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa plants can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa. Ehaa tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo Ebaabu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: When too many seeds are planted closely in one spot, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food to build strong stems or big cobs, spacing seeds properly gives each maize plant the room it needs to yield full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa loo ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa tsu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of bushy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant direct its energy down into swelling the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ faaa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does my maize yield better when I plant groundnuts on the plot before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the groundnut harvest is done, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop of maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ agbe ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and preventing new fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi aduawai heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, aphids, or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves or spreading a plant virus. As these pests drink the plant's sap, the leaves distort, which stops the plant from making energy to form healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi loo helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight, which is necessary for the plant to manufacture food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases while maximizing sunlight capture to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la babaoo aba tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fungal leaf helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa hulu la nine shɛɔ bulbs wuji anɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky and dry, preventing the flowers from getting pollinated. Because unpollinated flowers cannot produce seeds or fruit, the plant sheds them to save its resources.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollen Enɛ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ ajieɔ tsei koni akɛbu nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily when strong rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that lie close to the soil surface, making them prone to tipping over when heavy. If root-feeding pests like nematodes or banana weevils damage those roots underground, the plant loses its anchor and easily falls in strong wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ebaagbee shi kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi, tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii kpata nakai shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ewaaa akɛ tsei laajeɔ amɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Lowland rice plants have special internal air channels that allow their roots to breathe underwater, while most weeds cannot survive being submerged. Keeping water in the paddy drowns competing weeds and maintains a stable soil temperature for the rice roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli lɛ, Nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow long leafy vines but refuse to produce flowers during certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji shi ewooo fɔfɔi yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Many cowpea varieties are sensitive to daylight duration, meaning they only trigger flowering when the days reach a specific length during the year. If planted in the wrong month, the plant continues growing leaves and stems while waiting for the daylight cue to start flowering.
ga: Cowpea henɔi babaoo nuɔ he waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, bei komɛi pɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tsina ŋmei fɔɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nyɔŋ ni ejaaa mli Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii be mli ni emɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ ni ebɔi fɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the soil has too much water which is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli eyi nu babaoo tsɔ ni eetsi shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: When planted too close, crops fight each other for sunlight and soil food, forcing them to stretch thin to reach light instead of using energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe bibii koni amɛbote la lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if the plant suffers from sudden water shortage while flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na nu ni faaa trukaa beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and weak roots that burn under full sun; they need shade trees to protect them from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look droopy in the afternoon but stand firm again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi koni enyɛ edamɔ shi ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun to stop losing water, but they recover overnight by soaking up moisture from the cool soil.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni shwieɔ lɛ akpa. Mohu ɔ, e náa he wami nyɔ mi kake kɛ gu nu nɛ e ngɔɔ kɛ jeɔ zugba nɛ mi jɔ ɔ mi ɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ.

english: Why is it taking so long for my planted yam setts to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-sweet potato lɛ shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rest naturally inside dry soil and will only wake up to sprout when the soil receives enough moisture and heat from early rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes jɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ebaate shi ni ekwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow so slow and weak when weeds grow close around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni jwɛi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves; they steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your main crops have a chance to drink or eat.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ loo amɛyeɔ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, so when the heavy bunch pulls the tree top down and rains soften the soil, strong wind easily pushes the plant over unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei akui ni tsii gbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛtee shishi ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa tsei ashwie shi mlɛo. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How often should I walk through my field to check on my crops for pests and diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ kɛji ŋmeii kɛ helai yɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: Walking through your field at least once a week allows you to spot early signs of insect attacks or leaf diseases before they spread and destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii loo tsei ahe hela miiba bo lɛ mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a crop disease is starting on my farm before it becomes a major problem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko miije shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ebatsɔ naagba wulu?

english: You can spot early disease signs during weekly checks by looking for unusual spots on leaves, wilting stems, or unexpected yellowing on young leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona hela lɛ he okadii mra yɛ otsi fɛɛ otsi mlikwɛmɔi amli kɛtsɔ hei ni yɔɔ srɔto ni oookwɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. tso ni egbo loo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat stress, which is a normal survival behavior in hot weather.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ ji subaŋ ni sa kɛha wala yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water, but early leaf drop can also mean the soil is low in essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi baai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni ato.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods turning black without a dusty fungus is often a natural process called 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot nourish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ ni sũ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ kookoo ŋmeii. ‘Cherelle wilt’, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but fail to produce tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miida ni ekɛ baai ebɔle ehe shi ewooo tomato lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants put all their energy into leafy branches rather than producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tsei lɛ aniji kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my crops are yellowing because of pests or because of poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: Pest damage leaves physical signs like holes or chewed edges, while poor soil nutrients usually cause a smooth, uniform yellowing across whole leaves or entire rows of crops.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ bu loo ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over easily when stem borer insects weaken the stalks from the inside, or when shallow roots lack soil support and potassium.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii bote tso lɛ mli, ni no haa tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emli. aloo be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɛ sũ kɛ potassium

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing wide leaves but failing to form a solid round head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly when temperatures are too warm, when plants are spaced too closely together, or when water supply is inconsistent during the head-forming stage.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ agbala yitsei amli jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo be mli ni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni tuber lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of essential plant food like nitrogen, or when the soil holds too much water around the roots. Feeding the soil with poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋtayaa fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to plant my cassava stick at a slant instead of standing it straight up in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting a cassava cutting at a slanted angle encourages roots to grow spread out evenly at a comfortable depth, which leads to more and larger cassava tubers underground when harvest time comes.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava ŋmeii yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛfata he yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ayi afa babaoo. Be ni kpamɔ be shɛɔ

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct midday sun. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to them acts like an umbrella to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ loo dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look dead in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up. Drooping is their natural way of resting to save moisture, and they usually bounce back once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot, when there is a sudden lack of water, or when insect pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protected helps flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni faaa trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up tight and turning sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny insects like aphids hide under the leaves to suck out the plant's sweet juices. The sticky liquid is left behind by these pests, and controlling them early stops the plant from getting stunted.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids, kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baashi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni amɛye nɔ mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without making strong stems when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛwooo ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete aggressively with their neighbors for sunlight. They waste all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa Amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ duɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which is then stored underground to make big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛ amɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my groundnut seeds rot in the dirt if I plant them right after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds need air in the soil to breathe as they sprout. If the dirt is completely soaked and flooded with water, oxygen cannot reach the seeds, causing them to drown and rot before they can germinate.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji muji lɛ mli ewo nu aahu akɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some of the plantain shoots I cut from an old farm yield small bunches while others yield big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni mifo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain shoots carry the traits and health of the mother plant. Shoots cut from healthy, thick mother trees that show no sign of stem-borer pests grow faster and yield much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ hiɛ su kɛ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni bɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ko lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaawo plantain ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like pencils when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during extreme heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural way of saving water so it does not dry out and die.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ ni egbooo.

english: Why do my vegetable plants look wilted in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Once the heat cools down in the evening, the plant usually recovers.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow into full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is often caused by water stress or heat when rains stop unexpectedly. The tree drops some of its young pods—a condition called cherelle wilt—to conserve water and keep the main tree alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ enɛ baa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa. Tso lɛ baashwie ŋmɔtɔ bibii komɛi. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Koni akɛbu nu he ni akɛbu tsei titrii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off when the soil gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, the plant cannot pull nutrients like nitrogen from the dry soil, so it sheds its older lower leaves to send what little water and food it has to the young top leaves.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛ nu fioo kɛ niyenii amaje ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why does the ground on my farm crack into hard pieces when the water dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli gbálaa kɛfeɔ bibii ni wa kɛ́ nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Soils with high clay content expand when wet and shrink as water evaporates in the sun. These cracks can break crop roots and expose them to hot dry air, making crops dry out faster.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji edɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ be mli ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tsei shishifãi ni eha amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii gĩɔ oya

english: What can I put on top of my soil to keep the water from drying up too quickly under the sun?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, leaves, or crop remnants—called mulching—acts as a blanket. It shades the soil from direct sunlight and slows down how fast water evaporates.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the air is cool and the soil can absorb water before the hot afternoon sun causes most of it to evaporate into the air.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa emli babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do cowpeas survive dry weather much better than maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep taproots that dig far down into the ground to find deep soil moisture, whereas maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly when surface water disappears.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli kwɔ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ laaje.

english: How does a sudden lack of water affect my cassava tubers underground?
ga: Te nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When water dries up during the growing stage, cassava plants focus on keeping their leaves alive instead of expanding roots, resulting in thin, woody tubers with very little starch.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ gĩ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ Kɛha ŋmei tsei lɛ, nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji baai lɛ akwɛmɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ amli tsei ni amɛji tsei, ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do insect pests seem to increase on my farm when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dry and warm weather speeds up the breeding cycle of many insects like whiteflies and mites, while water stress weakens your crop's natural ability to fight off insect damage.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa kooloi bibii babaoo, tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mites lɛ feɔ amɛhe oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu mli haomɔ haa nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni ekɛwuɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of the tiny cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up before growing full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease or natural self-thinning, where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot support with its current water and nutrient levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni nyɛŋ akwɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, drain food and water away from the main trunk. Cutting them off helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii kɛ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from dying due to heat stress and lack of moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ he.

english: How long will it take for my new oil palm seedlings to start bearing fruit bunches?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-palm dumɔwui heei lɛ awo aduawai akui?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually begin producing their first fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after planting in the field if they receive good soil nutrients and rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji onine shɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa.

english: Why should I not plant my oil palm seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ oil palm dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms need a lot of sunlight and space to spread their leaves. Planting them too close together makes them grow tall quickly without producing large or heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo kɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara oya ni amɛwooo yibii akui wuji loo ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my oil palm tree turning yellow and dropping down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower fronds usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or potassium in the soil. Pruning off the dead lower leaves helps keep the palm clean and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo potassium yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai ni egboi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ he tseɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds from research centers grow better than the seeds I pick from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mihalaa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Research center seeds are specially selected hybrid varieties bred to resist common local diseases, grow faster, and yield much more fruit than seeds saved from old farm trees.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔhe lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji dumɔwui ni ahala krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. edaa oya ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei momo amli lɛ

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava between my young oil palm trees in the first year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mu tsei ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can plant cassava or food crops between young oil palms during the first year or two, but keep them at a distance so they do not steal water and nutrients from the palm roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mu tso dumɔwui ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Shi tsi amɛ kɛjɛ he ko koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli.

english: Why do my crops look wilted in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can take it up from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to save moisture and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some types of rice produce long grains while others grow short and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi woɔ ŋmãa kakadaji lɛ? Shi henɔi komɛi yɛ dumɔwui kukuji kɛ kokroo?

english: Different crop varieties have different genetic traits passed down from their seed parents. Long-grain varieties naturally grow slender kernels that stay separate when cooked, while short-grain varieties contain more starch, making them sticky.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ nii ni jɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi amli fɔlɔi amli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni baagbala mli kɛji ahoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kukuji lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo

english: Are imported foreign crop seeds always better to plant than our local Ghanaian seeds?
ga: Ani be fɛɛ be lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe wɔ Ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Not always. Foreign seeds are often bred for high yields or specific grain shapes, but local seeds are usually tougher against local pests, poor soils, and hot weather. Your choice depends on your soil, access to water, and market demand.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui koni amɛná yibii babaoo loo dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. nu ni anáa kɛ jarayeli he hiamɔ nii

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because the soil lacks food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plants show hunger through their foliage. If older bottom leaves turn yellow first, the crop usually lacks nitrogen. If the leaves show unusual purple or pale patterns, it means other key soil nutrients are missing.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii krokomɛi ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What does it mean when extension officers talk about testing the nutrient level of my farmland soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ wie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kaa he lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Soil testing is like taking your land to a health clinic. It measures the hidden food content in your soil so you know the exact type and amount of fertilizer to apply instead of wasting money on the wrong inputs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tamɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛyaa helatsamɔhe lɛ. Esusuɔ niyenii ni akɛtee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ falɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ ole ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii kɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do chemical fertilizers feed crops much faster than animal manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya fe kooloi aŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain mineral nutrients that are already dissolved and ready for plant roots to drink immediately. Animal manure releases its plant food slowly over months as soil organisms break it down.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral nutrients ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Manure jieɔ tsei aniyenii fiofio. Ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with neighboring plants for sunlight, air, and soil food. They stretch upwards to reach light instead of using their energy to develop strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛshɛ la he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛfee tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my plant leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water vapor faster than the roots can drink from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to close their pores and save water, usually recovering once the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu lasu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni eye ebua ni nu lɛ akafite. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi pɛ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crops more this season than last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be nɛɛ mli fe afi ni eho lɛ?

english: Pest populations increase rapidly when weather conditions like temperature and rainfall change, or when fields are planted with the same single crop year after year without rotation.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ tsake. aloo kɛ́ adu ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni atsakeee.

english: Why do buyers in the local market pay higher prices for long-grain rice varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ woɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ jara babaoo lɛ?

english: Market buyers prefer long-grain rice because consumers view it as premium quality; it looks attractive, expands well when boiled, and does not turn mushy during cooking.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ omɔ ni mli edɔ ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ buɔ lɛ akɛ omɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ehiɛ yɔɔ fɛo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ahoo lɛ. Ni efeee basabasa yɛ be mli ni ahoɔ nii lɛ.

english: How does drying my harvested grains properly prevent them from getting destroyed before sale?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛhiɛ koni amɛkafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Drying removes internal moisture that mold and insects need to survive. Well-dried grains stay hard, store longer without rotting, and maintain the clean appearance buyers look for.
ga: Gbimɔ jieɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmei kɛ kooloi anyɛ ahi shi lɛ. Nibii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ shiŋŋ. Abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee. ni amɛhiɛ hetsemɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds and prepare my land long before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Clearing land early is like servicing machinery before a long journey; it removes weed competition and allows the soil to capture the early rain so your seeds get the best possible start without struggling for food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ mra Etamɔ tsɔne ko ni asaa dani aya gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ. Ejieɔ jwɛi akaŋshii kɛyaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ mɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ niyenii kɛ nu abɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: Is it worth buying new certified seeds every season instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Buying fresh certified seed is an upfront investment, but saved seeds lose their strength over time and produce much lower yields, while certified seeds are bred to resist local pests and produce uniform, healthy crops.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ hiɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants keep turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen—the main plant food needed for growth—or that excess water in the soil is suffocating the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to sow my seeds once the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: You should wait until the ground has received a few steady rains and stays moist for several days; planting after just one light shower will cause your seeds to dry out and burn in the hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehi shi gbii babaoo. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛshã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to leave so much space between my cassava cuttings when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei niji ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava roots need ample space under the ground to expand into large tubers; planting them too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot or when they do not get steady water, causing the plant to save its energy rather than feed growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus carried into the field by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions; pruning excess tree branches allows light and air to flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but almost no beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni ŋmeii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer or are grown in extremely rich soil, they focus all their energy on making leaves instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai afeemɔ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui akutsei ni amɛbaafee.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when heavy rainfall causes water to collect around the roots without proper drainage, creating ideal conditions for soil bacteria and fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua amɛhe naa. shishifãi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi.

english: Why do my crops still get sick even after I spray chemical medicine on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miiye lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai eshwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Chemical sprays usually kill surface insects or fungi, but many plant diseases are caused by microscopic living organisms like viruses or bacteria living inside the plant tissue where chemical sprays cannot reach or heal immediately.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi nibii bibii ni anaaa, tamɔ muawai loo muawai, ni hiɔ tsei amli lɛ kɛ tsei helai babaoo baa. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he loo elaaje amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and curl up when there are tiny white insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The tiny white insects carry invisible living organisms called viruses from infected plants and inject them into healthy cassava leaves while feeding, spreading disease across the field.
ga: Kplukai bibii yɛŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nibii ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ virus kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to burn diseased cocoa pods instead of leaving them on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛshã kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaashɛrɛ amɛ amɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Diseased pods contain millions of microscopic living fungi spores that stay alive on the ground and get blown or splashed by rain onto healthy pods, causing the sickness to spread.
ga: Nibii bibii akpekpei abɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ wala mli ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ loo eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. kɛ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Can crop diseases spread underground from one plant root to another?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi kɛjɛ tso shishifã kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, harmful soil-dwelling organisms like parasitic fungi and nematodes can move through damp soil from the roots of a sick plant directly into the healthy roots of neighboring crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ parasitic fungi kɛ nematodes baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is compost just dead plant leaves, or is there something living inside it that helps my crops grow?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji tsei ahe baai ni egboi kɛkɛ loo nɔ ko yɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Compost is full of millions of tiny, invisible beneficial organisms that actively break down plant waste and convert it into rich nutrients that crop roots can easily digest.
ga: Nibii bibii akpekpei abɔ ni anaaa, ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ eyi ŋmɔ mli obɔ. Enɛ gbalaa tsei amli jwɛi ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii kpakpai ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer work much faster when the soil is wet rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kwraa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe nɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are solid chemical compounds that need water to dissolve so tiny soil microbes can activate and help plant roots drink the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji tsofai ni mli wa ni biɔ nu dani etsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anyɛ akanya tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛye amɛbua amɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some insect sprays kill pests instantly while natural sprays take days to work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani etsuɔ ​​nii lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays act like strong poisons that kill pests immediately on contact, whereas natural or biological sprays introduce tiny living microbes or natural deterrents that pests must consume and slowly digest before dying.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai fɔji ni naa wa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ nii anaa ni esa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aye ni amɛye amɛhe fiofio dani amɛgboi lɛ baa.

english: How does changing the crop I plant every season prevent pests from destroying my harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ni mitsakeɔ daa afi lɛ aaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Many crop pests and soil organisms can only feed on specific plants; when you plant a different crop, those specialized pests cannot find their food and die off naturally.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii babaoo baanyɛ aye tsei srɔtoi komɛi pɛ. Beni oduɔ tsei krokomɛi Nakai kooloi bibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does a dry, hard seed suddenly wake up and sprout only when it touches water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni wa lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli pɛ lɛ?

english: A dry seed contains living cells that remain inactive until water enters the shell, triggering chemical signals that tell the seed embryo to start growing roots and shoots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli wala yibii ni tsuuu nii kɛyashi nu boteɔ amɛmli. Enɛ haa tsofa okadii ni kɛɔ dumɔwu fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii je shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young maize plants always lean in the direction of the morning sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi kɛyaa leebi hulu lɛ he be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops are living organisms that naturally produce growth hormones which push their stems to stretch toward sunlight so their leaves can capture energy and manufacture plant food.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ dalɛ mli tsofai. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee tsei niyenii.

english: Why do plantains and cocoa grow so much better in the Ashanti Region than in drier parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui kɛ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fe Ghana hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa and plantains require heavy, consistent rainfall, high humidity, and rich forest soils that are naturally present in regions like Ashanti. In drier areas, lower rainfall and sandy soils cause these water-loving crops to dry out and produce low yields.
ga: Cocoa kɛ plantains biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa. hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ koo mli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ fɛo ni yɔɔ kpokpai tamɔ Ashanti yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni sumɔɔ nu nɛɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is yam farming more successful in Northern Ghana than cocoa farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato okwaayeli yeɔ omanye yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ fe kookoo okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Yams thrive in abundant sunshine, distinct wet-and-dry seasons, and deep, loose soil where tubers can freely expand. Cocoa trees require continuous shade and rich forest humidity, which the drier climate of Northern Ghana cannot support.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ mli. nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bulb lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwa yɛ mli lɛ. Cocoa tsei biɔ hɔɔŋ be fɛɛ be kɛ koo mli nu babaoo. ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: Why do crop seeds brought from another region sometimes fail to grow well in my local district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crop varieties naturally adapt over time to the specific rainfall, temperature, and soil conditions of their local district. Moving a seed variety to a region with different weather or soil can stress the plant, resulting in poor growth and low harvest.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛyaa nugbɔshiimɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ amɛkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ajieɔ kɛyaa hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo shikpɔji srɔtoi yɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu faaa.

english: Why does cassava produce large roots on my neighbor's land but small roots on my land in the same district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil to allow its tubers to swell easily. If your land has hard, compact clay soil, the roots struggle to expand underground even if the leaves above ground look healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia cassava bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa po.

english: How do I know which crop will give me the best yield on my specific plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baawo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Every crop performs best when matched to the natural soil type, moisture level, and weather of your district. Observing which traditional crops thrive naturally in your immediate area helps you choose crops that yield maximum harvest with lower costs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ fata he. Fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ blema tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni shika fioo pɛ heɔ.

english: Why do some crops thrive near riverbanks but rot when planted on hillsides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ faai ahe shi amɛgboiɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Riverbanks hold rich, wet soil suitable for water-loving crops like rice. Hillsides drain water quickly, making them better suited for crops that prefer drier root conditions and rot easily in standing water, such as groundnuts.
ga: Faa lɛ naa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni edɔ. Ehi kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa. Gɔji lɛ hoɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ shishifãi ni mli egbi ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli, tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep underground water during dry periods. Without water, the plant cannot absorb essential nitrogen from the soil, causing its leaves to yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa.

english: If I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every season, why do my yields drop over time?
ga: Kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ eba shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating tomatoes with leguminous plants like beans replenishes nutrients and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akpa.

english: Why should I grow different types of crops on my farm instead of planting just one crop everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu tso henɔ kome yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ

english: Growing multiple crop types protects your overall income if bad weather or pests damage one specific crop. It also keeps your soil healthy, as different plants draw and return different nutrients to the land.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite nibii ni oduɔ lɛ eko. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei srɔtoi kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii srɔtoi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants seem to grow better when planted together with maize than when grown alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du fe bɔ ni amɛkome amɛdu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, while tall maize plants provide light shade that keeps the soil cool. Together, they share nutrients and protect the soil from drying out too quickly.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ. Amɛjaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or plantains because direct hot sunlight burns their leaves and dries up the soil moisture before their roots can grow deep.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil, often because the soil nutrients are low or heavy rains have washed them away.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo amɛ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant does not get enough water, or when tiny pests feed on the flower stems.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize and leaving brown waste inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant to eat the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific food nutrients that crop needs from the soil, leaving the earth weak unless you rotate crops or add plant food.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji je lɛ ni egbɔjɔ Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ tsei niyenii fata he.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass stop them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket (mulch) that shades the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the water that the crop roots need to drink.
ga: Hay lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. (Mulch) Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni ehe hiaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young cassava slow down its growth?
ga: Mɛni Hewɔ ni Jwɛi ni Ashiɔ Abɔleɔ Mibi lɛ ŋmei lɛ miiha edalɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your crop gets a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground if heavy rains hit right when they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be mli ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water, oxygen cannot reach the cassava tubers, causing them to drown and decay under fungal attack.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing shoots even when I have not buried them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii babaoo shweremɔ lɛ? Ni mikɛfuuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal clock; after resting for a few months, warmth and humidity tell the yam it is time to use its stored energy to sprout new stems.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Beni ejɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo sɛɛ lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ kɛɛ lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce very thin stems and tiny bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close together makes their leaves overlap, forcing them to fight each other for sun light and soil nutrients, which reduces the energy needed for big bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tsei wuji lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if a crop medicine will actually cure my sick plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso tsofa baanyɛ atsa mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A good plant medicine will stop leaf yellowing, kill harmful insects, or prevent spots from spreading within a few days of application. You can test a small section of your farm first to see if the plants recover and grow greener before applying it everywhere.
ga: Tsofa kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekpa baai lɛ ŋmɔŋ. gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ Obaanyɛ oka he bibioo ko okwɛ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona kɛji tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔji. dani akɛtsu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he

english: Why are worms eating holes inside the leaves of my maize plants at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms hide inside the cool center of the plant during the hot day and come out at night to eat leaves. Spraying an effective plant medicine early in the morning or late evening targets them when they are active.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni mli ejɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ebaje kpo koni ebaye baai gbɛkɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tso tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa tsofa lɛ ehiɛ beni etsuɔ ​​nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much trapped water. Adding fertilizer or animal manure feeds the plant so the leaves can turn green and make food again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen he miihia onibii, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛbatsɔmɔ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does adding dried animal dung to my land make my crops grow better than plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Animal dung acts like slow-release food for the soil. It improves the soil's structure so roots can spread easily and helps the ground hold water longer during hot days.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of root tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store food underground where you harvest.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shishifãi ni etse lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ he ni okpaa nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in strong sunshine. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create shade and keep the air humid, acting as natural umbrellas for the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa kookoo lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛɔ.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, resulting in a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do weeds on my land grow much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and efficient at stealing food, water, and sunlight from your land. Clearing them early stops them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jumɔ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect damage. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers stay on and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtoɔ tomatoi lɛ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense action where the plant rolls its leaves to hide from the harsh sun and trap moisture inside. If the plant recovers in the evening, it is managing heat, but if leaves stay curled, it may need water or pest control.
ga: Leaf curling ji hebuu gbɛ ko ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akawo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ eekwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lolo lɛ Ekolɛ Nu loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe baahia.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when plants lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when excessive rain floods the soil and prevents roots from feeding properly.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my field before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer away from your plants, leaving your crops hungry despite the application.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli. Hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ po.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve the ground for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha he ni miyɔɔ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas to provide necessary shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebua amɛhe naa lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun to make food for the tuber below. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot and pests.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Why do I need to cut off small shoots and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ni niji krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted water shoots (chupons) forces the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy pods rather than wasting food on extra leaves.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ, ni no haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and causing underground fungal infections.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually a defense sign against heat stress, or a symptom of a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Aloo eji hela ko ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ nu mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when they are not pollinated. They rely on tiny insects called midges to carry pollen from flower to flower; if these insects are absent or destroyed by strong chemicals, the flowers cannot turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ laaje loo tsofai ni mli wa kpata amɛhiɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What is cocoa hand pollination, and will it help my trees grow more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaaye ebua mitso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo?
