english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using tweezers or a small brush. It ensures that almost every flower gets pollinated, which can double or triple the number of pods your tree produces.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ tweezers loo brɔsh bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi nɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ afee enyɔ loo etɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods stay small and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree naturally drops young pods because it does not have enough water, soil nutrients, or energy to support all of them to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ‘Cherel wilt’, ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ejaakɛ nu mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he lɛ bɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to cut cocoa pods off the tree and put them in my harvest basket?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛwo ŋmaakpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange. Harvesting them at this color guarantees the highest quality cocoa beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɛkɛ su nɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa anáa kookoo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long without harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: If ripe pods stay on the tree too long, the seeds inside will start to sprout, and the pod becomes more likely to catch black pod disease or get eaten by animals, ruining your yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aná black pod hela loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afitemɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather when there is too much shade and heavy air moisture around your trees.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Be mli ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Are all tiny insects on my cocoa farm bad for my crops?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, not all insects are bad. Tiny midges are crucial because they pollinate cocoa flowers so pods can grow, while other insects like certain ants help kill pests that attack your crop.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Akpɔlɔi bibii ahe hiaa ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ ada. Yɛ be mli ni kooloi krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii komɛi yeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni tutuaa onibii lɛ.

english: Planting trees too close makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, weak trees that produce very few flowers and pods.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight reach the inner branches and improves air movement, which keeps the tree dry from diseases and encourages the tree to produce more flowers.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ hela mli, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn yellow during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan season, dry winds and hot weather suck moisture out of the leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil, causing the tree to shed leaves to conserve water.
ga: Yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsei ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on my farm before planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are like human babies—they burn easily under harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or cause water to sit around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo eha nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, helping it trap moisture inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe without air. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry enough to remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight provides the energy the plant needs to feed itself and grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ ehe ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or lacks enough water while flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing dry grass around the base of the plant to keep the ground cool helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I avoid burning dry grass and bushes on my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei bibii ni mikɛshãa yɛ midumɔi lɛ anɔ dani midu lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys the rich topsoil and kills good organisms that feed your plants. Leaving dry grass to rot naturally or plowing it into the soil creates free organic fertilizer and keeps moisture trapped in the ground for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests that like maize to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, hide in the central funnel because it is soft, moist, and contains the youngest leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended control methods directly into the funnels stops them from destroying the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ baai bibii fe fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tsɔne lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with one another for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows its stem to grow thick and leaves to spread out, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the sap underneath the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong leaves and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them without draining. The excess water suffocates the roots, allowing fungus and bacteria to cause underground decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu shwieee Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or irregular watering. Without consistent soil moisture during hot periods, the plant cannot support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which travels down to make the underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and cannot compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early gives young plants the head start they need to establish.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shishijee he ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: What is eating deep holes into the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso bibioo lɛ mli lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeli?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the central shoot of the maize to feed on the tender leaf tissues before the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli fãji dani tsei lɛ daraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do saved seeds from my last harvest produce smaller yields than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over multiple seasons lose vigor and disease resistance over time, whereas certified seeds are specially bred for high yields, uniform growth, and protection against common diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ be babaoo lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. uniform dalɛ kɛ helai fɛɛ atsimɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients the plant needs to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Instead of using energy to grow big cobs, the maize stretches upward to reach the light, making the stems thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu ŋmeii wuji. Abɛi lɛ baagbala ehe koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Why do people say planting cowpea on my farm helps the soil become better for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a special plant that traps natural nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil through its roots. When the cowpea leaves and roots decay, they leave behind rich plant food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji cowpea baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, hot sunlight because their leaves lose moisture too fast. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains provides a shelter that keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa is young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ haa anáa he ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, the soil becomes waterlogged, suffocating the tubers and causing fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they feel stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions get better.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing big leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa baai wuji lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or by a sickness passed to the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and quickly drink up the water and food in the soil. Even with good rain, your crops stay hungry because the weeds are taking most of the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to produce food that grows the big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp dirt, catching maximum sunlight and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii beni akwɛɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ muji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. Egbalaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa helai anaa

english: Why did the maize seeds I stored in a bag after last harvest refuse to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku mli yɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Seeds die if they are stored in damp places or if tiny bugs like weevils damage the inside of the seed. To stay alive for planting, seeds must be dried completely and kept in cool, tightly sealed containers.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fite dumɔwui lɛ amli. Koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛha dumɔwui. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa ni akɛto tsinsii ni mli ejɔ ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green leafy growth. It often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when water stays trapped around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmãa baa eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. aloo kɛ́ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: How come my cowpea crop has plenty of big green leaves but produces very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea is given too much fertilizer or planted in soil rich in nitrogen, it puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of flowering. Cowpea natural fixes its own nitrogen, so extra nutrients hinder pod formation.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas saa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsiɔ pod feemɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the harmattan starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ harmattan je shishi lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull water out of cocoa leaves faster than young roots can drink from the dry ground. Young cocoa trees lack deep roots, so they need shade trees like plantains to protect them from scorching sun and dry air.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or severe dry spells. High temperatures stress the plant, causing it to shed flowers to conserve water and survive rather than producing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa he. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tomato.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves and suck out the sap. As they feed, they cause the new leaves to twist, shrink, and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛhaa baai heei shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over because tiny worms in the soil, called nematodes, or stem borers have destroyed the roots and inner stem. Without strong, healthy roots anchored in the ground, the plant cannot hold up the heavy weight of a maturing bunch.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ahewɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tsɔne ni tsii ni ji tso ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater creates waterlogged soil, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, allowing soil fungi and rot bacteria to attack and spoil the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam tubers become twisted and deformed when planted in hard, stony, or compact soil. The growing tip of the yam cannot push through hard earth or rocks, so it bends and branches off in search of softer soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Sweet potato lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ekotoɔ ni ekɛ niji shwieɔ shi koni etao shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for light, water, and soil food. The crop stretches upward to reach sunlight instead of growing thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottom branches of my oil palm tree turn brown and dry out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: The lowest leaves of an oil palm naturally turn brown and dry as the tree gets taller and older. However, if many leaves dry up quickly at once, it means the palm tree is stressed from a lack of water or needs potassium fertilizer.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo gĩ oya shikome lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ loo potassium ŋmei ni he hiaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: What does potassium fertilizer actually do for my cocoa crops?
ga: Te potassium ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts like a health booster for crops. It strengthens the stems, helps the plant transport water and food internally, and makes the cocoa pods grow bigger, heavier, and healthier.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ mli hewalɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa mli. ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ agboi, amɛhe tsiimɔ, ni amɛhe wa.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is right at the start of the rainy season when the soil is damp. The rain helps dissolve the fertilizer so the tree roots can easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should plant cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. This gives each tree enough room for its roots and leaves to spread without fighting neighboring trees for light and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ odu okoo tsei lɛ aaafee ninetalɔi 10 (mitai etɛ) kɛjɛ he. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ebɔi akaŋ kɛha la kɛ niyenii.

english: Is it better for me to work on my large farm all at once or divide it into smaller blocks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli shikome loo yɛ tsũi bibii amli?

english: Dividing a large farm into smaller sections makes management much easier. It allows one person or small team to weed, fertilize, and harvest one block at a time without getting overwhelmed.
ga: Okwaafoi agbo mlijaa awoɔ fãi bibii amli Ehaa nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Ye obua mɔ kome loo kuu bibioo Ebaanyɛ ejie jwɛi, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni ekpa blɔki kome yɛ be kome mli ni ekɛ jatsu ko akawo enɔ fe nine.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them from excessive heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava kɛ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops like plantain and cassava with young cocoa is very beneficial. Plantains provide needed shade, while the food crops give you income and food while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii tamɔ plantain kɛ cassava ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantains haa hulutsoo ni ataoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii tsei haa onáa shika kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa trees if I want them to bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight to reach the middle of the tree. This reduces diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai aba shi ni ekwɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni pod lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should weed your farm 3 to 4 times a year, especially during rainy periods. Weeds steal water, soil nutrients, and light from your cocoa trees, which slows down crop growth.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ la ni jɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark brown and drying up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal attack like black pod disease or a lack of proper nutrients. Dampness and excess shade encourage the fungus, causing young pods to rot early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal tutuamɔ, tamɔ black pod hela, loo niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo woɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm is getting too damp and prone to diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba?

english: If your farm stays dark and wet with moss growing on tree trunks and leaves staying wet all day, it is too damp. Trimming shade trees and pruning cocoa branches will let sunlight in to dry the farm.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei anɔ ni baai lɛ edɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni afoɔ ni afoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the young top leaves and growing corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ kɛ abɛi toi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to grow properly, resulting in weak plants and smaller tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil to prevent rot and helps the leaves capture sun energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking haa baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛkafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs wuji.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that works with natural soil organisms to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the flower instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii

english: Why does my oil palm tree stop producing fresh fruit bunches during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekpa yibii heei ni amɛwoɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees require large amounts of water to produce healthy fruit bunches. During prolonged dry weather, the tree conserves its energy and moisture to survive, causing flowers to drop or fail to develop into fruits.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia oil palm tsei koni amɛwo aduawai akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems push themselves down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants bloom above ground, but after pollination, the stems grow downwards into the soil where the actual nuts form. The soil protects the developing nuts from hot sun and pests.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ daraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ buɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in standing water while my other crops rot and die in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Minɔ lɛ fite ni egbo yɛ nu lɛ mli?

english: Swamp rice has natural hollow air passages inside its stems and roots that work like tiny snorkels. These passages carry oxygen from above the water surface down to the submerged roots so they do not drown.
ga: Bung ŋmãa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni mli ewo muji yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔne bibioo ko Shɛɛ saji nɛɛ woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ kɛyaa shishifãi ni ebote nu lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. koni nu akabote mli

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the undersides of the leaves, or by plant viruses spread by insects, which stops proper leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Enɛ haa baa lɛ dalɛ kpakpa kpaa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to make food, or that excessive water is preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Aloo akɛ nu babaoo tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting beans in the same field as my maize improve my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa mi-ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Beans belong to a family of plants that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which feeds the nitrogen-hungry maize crops.
ga: Beans ji tsei akuu ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with many big leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji shi pods fioo?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes okra to focus all its energy on growing tall stems and leaves rather than producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa okra kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they turn into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme sun heat or sudden dry spells stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blooms to save energy and water for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When heavy rain saturates the soil completely, it deprives cassava roots of air, creating wet conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kwraa. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy leaves and fruit clusters at the top, making them easy to uproot unless supported by props or protected by windbreaks.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsii kɛ aduawai yɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishijee lɛ feɔ mlɛo Ja nibii ni akɛfiɔ he loo kɔɔyɔɔŋ glase ko yɛ ni haa nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that feed on sap and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa.

english: Weeds grow quickly and compete directly with young crops by stealing sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni amɛjuɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—when they lack enough water, soil nutrients, or shade to support all the growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel wilt, be mli ni nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pods fɛɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to push downward easily; hard or compacted soil blocks tuber development and forces the roots to bend or stay small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni enyɛ eshɛ shishi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ tuber lɛ shweremɔ naa ni enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfee bibii.

english: Why should I collect and store rainwater in poly tanks for my farm instead of just waiting for the next rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua nugbɔ nu lɛ naa ni mikɛto poly tanki amli kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Storing rainwater in poly tanks gives you a reliable water backup during dry spells. When rain stops unexpectedly, you can keep watering your crops regularly so they do not suffer heat stress or dry up.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni okɛtoɔ poly tanki mli lɛ haa onáa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo onibii amli daa koni hulutsoo loo tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Can I keep my crops alive through the harmattan season if I store rainwater in barrels?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji mikɛ nugbɔ nu to tanki mli?

english: Yes, collecting extra rainwater in barrels during the wet season allows you to keep soil moist during dry periods like the harmattan, letting you grow and harvest crops year-round.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu kroko ni ooobua naa yɛ tanki lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli tamɔ Harmattan, ni ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How does using pipes to channel stored water across my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Te paipii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ nu ni ato kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Piping water allows you to direct moisture straight to crop rows evenly and easily. This ensures every plant gets an equal drink of water without wasting your time or energy carrying heavy buckets.
ga: Nu paipii haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa tsei akui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, ni be loo hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ baagi ni tsii lɛ bɛ mli.

english: If I store rainwater in open barrels on my farm, will that water stay good for my crops after a few weeks?
ga: Kɛji mibua nugbɔ nu naa yɛ tanki ko ni agbele mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani nakai nu lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Stored rainwater remains safe for crops, but covering your barrels prevents mosquitoes from breeding, keeps dirt out, and stops green algae from growing and clogging your irrigation pipes.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni ato lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛ́ oŋa tsɔne lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafɔ. Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ muji he ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛtsiɔ o-irrigation paipii lɛ anaa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water through their leaf surfaces during intense heat. It is your plant's natural signal telling you that the soil is dry and needs irrigation.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akatsɔ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ bo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ehe miihia ni afɔ nɔ nu.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too little water or from too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu fioo loo nu babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miigboi?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, turn crisp, and brown at the edges. When crops get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and look weak because their roots are drowning and rotting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Crispy kɛ brown yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is watering my crops early in the morning better than watering them during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets plant roots absorb moisture before the day gets hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots ever get a chance to drink it.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard just a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries quickly when it lacks organic matter like manure or compost, which act like natural sponges to trap water in the dirt so crop roots can drink over many days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji ni ekɛmɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu gbii babaoo.

english: Why is it better to pour water directly around the stems of my crops instead of wetting all the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu kɛbɔle he lɛ? direct crop stem Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha baai lɛ fɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Plants drink water through their roots, not their leaves. Pouring water directly at the base delivers moisture right to the roots while keeping leaves dry, which prevents leaf spot diseases and fungi from spreading.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsofa ni ji leaf spot hela kɛ ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How does keeping my farm soil constantly moist change how fast my vegetables produce fruits?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛhaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha mi-aduawai lɛ awo yibii oya aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Consistent soil moisture prevents plant stress, allowing your vegetables to absorb soil nutrients continuously. This helps them grow faster, flower earlier, and produce larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe haomɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-vegetables lɛ yaa nɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua amɛ ni amɛ daraa oya, amɛ woɔ fɔfɔi oya, ni amɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or shade crops like plantains, excessive sunlight burns the young leaves and stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni fa babaoo baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why is it helpful to plant plantains on the same land where I plant new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade to shield young cocoa trees from the sun, while also providing food and extra income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily, but most of the flowers drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without forming pods if there are not enough tiny pollinating insects (midges) around, or if the tree is under stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ pollinators (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions with poor air movement. Removing infected pods and clearing overgrown weeds helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the branches on some of my young cocoa trees swelling and looking swollen like a balloon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi anɔ lɛ efu ni etamɔ nɔ ni efu tamɔ bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a classic sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD), which is spread from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs and requires careful removal of affected trees.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (CSSVD) he okadi ni ale waa, ni kooloi bibii ni jɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ni ehe miihia ni ajie tsei ni ena naagbai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry periods happen because the plant lacks sufficient soil moisture to draw up nutrients, causing it to shed leaves to conserve water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off extra branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo kookoo niji babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. This reduces humidity that causes disease and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if weeds on my farm are actively harming my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Weeds harm crops when they grow close to the crop's base, stealing fertilizer, water, and sunlight, while also creating humid hiding spots for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ hu kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ.

english: How does leaving dead leaves on the ground around my crop stem help the plants grow?
ga: Baai gbohii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te mi ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dead leaves creates mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the soil, keeps roots cool during hot days, and breaks down over time into rich plant fertilizer.
ga: Mulch ni bɔle tso lɛ he kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ feɔ mulch. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do some trees on my farm produce very small cocoa pods while neighboring trees produce large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ kookoo bibii waa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pod size depends on the variety of the cocoa tree, how much fertilizer or nutrients the soil has, and whether the tree gets enough light without being overcrowded by other plants.
ga: Pod lɛ dalɛ damɔ cacao tso lɛ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo Ni ani tso lɛ miiná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsei krokomɛi ehiɛɛɛ mli fe nine?

english: What is the best crop I can grow on my farm to make my own feed for my chickens?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Maize and soybeans are the best crops to grow for chicken feed. Maize provides energy for growth, while soybeans give the necessary protein for strong muscles and egg laying.
ga: Abɛi kɛ soybeans ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ adu kɛha tsina niyenii. Abɛi haa hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, soybeans haa protein ni he hiaa waa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli faji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why do soybean plants turn yellow and lose their leaves right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaaji lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is a natural process for soybeans. As the seed pods fully mature and dry out, the plant stops sending energy to its leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop off automatically.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ kɛha soybeans. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my newly cleared land is fully ready for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Your land is ready when tree stumps are removed, weeds are cleared, and the soil is plowed to loosen hard earth so young roots can easily spread and absorb nutrients.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, ajie jwɛi lɛ, ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Will driving heavy tractors and machinery on my crop field damage the soil?
ga: Ani traktɔi wuji kɛ tsɔnei ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Using heavy machinery on wet soil packs the ground too tightly, making it hard for crop roots to breathe and absorb water. It is best to operate heavy machinery when the ground is dry enough.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ nu. Esa akɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii atsu nii pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I decide how much land to clear for my crops to get a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mafo koni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai lɛ he?

english: It is better to clear a smaller piece of land properly with correct seed spacing and weed control than to clear a huge space that you cannot manage, as overcrowded or weed-filled crops produce less yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi he bibioo ko. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi fe he ko ni da ni onyɛɛɛ otsu he nii lɛ ni oootsi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi babaoo lɛ baawo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I use fresh droppings from my chicken coop directly as fertilizer on my food crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ tsina shĩa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmeii kɛha mi niyenii tsei lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken droppings are too strong and can burn plant roots. You need to let the manure dry and decompose in a cool pile for a few weeks before applying it to your soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Esa akɛ oha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni egbo yɛ ŋmeii ni mli ejɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and encourages pests to settle in. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii momo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, ni ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi jɛmɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can wastewater from a fish pond help my farm crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔi amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi okwaayeli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fish pond water contains natural waste from fish that acts as a rich liquid fertilizer, giving your crops natural nutrients and moisture to grow greener and stronger.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ loo nubu lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni jɛ loo mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa otsei lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout and the rain stops suddenly, young crop seedlings will dry up and die from heat before deep roots develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ latsaa lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba.

english: Why do wild weeds grow faster than my planted crops after I clean the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to sprout quickly even in poor conditions, whereas food crop seeds need carefully prepared soil and constant sunlight to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii po amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, niyenii dumɔwui lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ he miihia koni amɛya nɔ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their root systems are not yet deep enough to replace water lost through their leaves. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain or shade trees to keep them cool until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsake nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small holes chewed in the leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani oooye baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to escape the sun and feed on the soft leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli koni ejo hulu lɛ naa foi ni eye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in soil that is too rich, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing food in the tubers under the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme high temperatures can cause tomato pollen to become sticky or inactive, preventing pollination. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant naturally drops the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ekɛtsuuu nii. Bɔni afee ni akafee pollination Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baajie fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my pepper plants help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass creates a protective layer called mulch. It blocks direct sunlight from heating up the earth, which slows down water evaporation and keeps the soil cool and moist for the plant's roots.
ga: Kɛ́ agbɛ jwɛi lɛ ashwã lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shibɔlemɔ ŋulami lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over once the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. As the heavy bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily uproot itself unless you prop it up using a strong wooden pole fork.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛji tso lɛ kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shishi oya. Ja okɛ tso ni mli wa miifi sɛɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the maize I plant next season grow much stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce large yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛwo sweet potato agboi lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight without overlapping or getting infected by soil diseases, allowing the leaves to make more food to send down into the growing tuber.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ko loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ emɔɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and droop during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to prevent losing too much water through evaporation during the hottest hours.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and weak even when I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that grow faster than your crops. They absorb the water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil first, leaving your main crops starved of food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha otsei titrii lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: How can learning proper oil palm farming techniques help my farm succeed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei fɔ ni aduɔ lɛ he ŋaai ni sa ni akaseɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni eye omanye?

english: Getting proper training on how to work with oil palm teaches you the right field practices, which makes your farming work successful and helps your trees produce a high yield.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ ni sa ni oooná yɛ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmei fɔ tsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he lɛ baatsɔɔ bo nifeemɔi ni ja. Enɛ baaha okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aye omanye, ni ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I seek guidance on how to manage my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matao ŋaawoo yɛ mu tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he lɛ?

english: Learning proper management techniques ensures that your oil palm trees grow well, leading to a successful farm and a harvest with plenty of palm fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okase gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni o-oil palm tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ ŋmɔji ni yeɔ omanye kɛ ŋmei yibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ aba.

english: What can I do to ensure my oil palm trees produce plenty of fruit?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-oil palm tsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: By learning and applying correct oil palm farming methods, you improve the health of your crop, which results in a bountiful yield of palm fruit.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ mu tso lɛ kasemɔ kɛ nitsumɔ nɔ. Obaahã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa anáa tsei babaoo.

english: Will applying proper oil palm practices really increase my crop yield?
ga: Ani mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, when you learn and practice proper oil palm management, your farm work becomes successful and yields plenty of palm fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okase ni okɛ mu tso lɛ he nitsumɔ kpakpa tsu nii pɛ. Oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ baaye omanye ni ebaawo ŋmei yibii babaoo.

english: How do agricultural training projects assist oil palm farmers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi baanyɛ aye abua mu tsei okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Training projects teach farmers effective ways to cultivate oil palm, helping them achieve successful farm operations and abundant palm fruit harvests.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsɔɔ okwaafoi bɔ ni amɛbaafee amɛdu ŋmei fɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛye omanye yɛ okwaayeli kɛ ŋmei yibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ mli.

english: Is there a good market available if I decide to grow oil palm?
ga: Kɛ mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu mu tso lɛ, ani jara kpakpa baaba?

english: Yes, there is a huge market demand for oil palm produce once your harvest is ready for sale.
ga: Hɛɛ, jarayeli nibii babaoo yɛ ni ataoɔ yɛ mu tso mli nibii ahe beni onibii lɛ yɛ ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If my oil palm farm yields a lot of fruit, will I be able to sell everything?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-oil palm ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii waa lɛ, ani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, palm fruit has a large buyer market, ensuring that your heavy produce can be sold after harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei yibii lɛ yɛ jarayelɔi babaoo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ onibii ni tsii lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How is harvested oil palm produce typically taken to the buyers?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ akɛ mu ni akpaa lɛ yaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ adɛŋ bei pii?

english: Once your palm fruit is harvested for the market, it is loaded into cars or vehicles to be transported directly to buyers.
ga: Beni akpaa o-palm aduawai lɛ koni akɛya jara lɛ Akɛwoɔ tsɔnei loo tsɔnei amli koni akɛya mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What usually happens after a successful oil palm harvest is completed?
ga: Mɛni fɔɔ baa yɛ mu tso ni akpa ni eye omanye lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After completing a successful harvest, a huge market opens up for your produce, and vehicles are loaded to take the farm produce away for sale.
ga: Beni agbe ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni ye omanye naa lɛ Jarayeli wulu ko baagbele kɛha onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ. Ni tsɔnei hu yɛ ni akɛwoɔ nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii baa koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why is oil palm considered a reliable crop to sell in our region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ oil palm akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm is reliable because proper cultivation produces plenty of fruit, and there is a huge market ready to buy and transport your farm produce.
ga: Anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ oil palm nɔ ejaakɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Ni jarayelihe wulu ko yɛ ni obaanyɛ ohé okwaayeli nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni okɛya.

english: Why are there so many ants climbing up my crop trees, and are they actually harming my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛmiiye mi tsei lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Ants are often attracted to sweet sap or honeydew produced by smaller insects like mealybugs or aphids. While ants themselves might not eat your plants, their presence usually means other sap-sucking pests are hiding on your trees and damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wuo loo wuo ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids lɛ feɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeŋ otsei lɛ moŋ, Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni nuɔ nu yɛ ni amɛtee amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do ants seem to gather near the top leaves and branches of my trees instead of staying on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ tsei aniji anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Ants climb to the top of trees because that is where tender new leaves, shoots, and young fruits grow. These soft parts produce rich sap and attract other insects that ants feed on or protect.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kwɔɔ tsei anɔ ejaakɛ biɛ ji he ni baai heei, ŋmeii, kɛ aduawai bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Nɛkɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ jieɔ nu ni fa babaoo ni gbalaa kooloi krokomɛi. ni ŋmeii yeɔ loo amɛbuɔ he lɛ

english: Is it worth spending my time clearing ant nests from my farm trees, or will they just go away on their own?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ oooŋɔ be ni okɛjie ŋmeii atsuji kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ anɔ? Aloo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaalaaje?

english: It is definitely worth clearing ant nests because ants protect harmful pests from natural predators like birds and beneficial insects. Clearing their nests breaks this protection and helps keep your crop yield safe.
ga: Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa diɛŋtsɛ akɛ, ŋmeii atsuji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii buɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ tamɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe. Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni ooojie lɛ fiteɔ hebuu nɛɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I safely deal with biting ants on my crop trees so I can work and harvest without getting bitten?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe nii shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ matsu nii ni makpa nii ni mɔ ko akamɔ mi?

english: You can manage biting ants by keeping tree branches trimmed so they do not touch other trees, applying recommended pest control sprays directly along the trunks, or spreading wood ash around the base of the trees to deter them.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ koni amɛkɛ tsei krokomɛi akakpe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo okɛ tso sũ ashwã tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni ŋmeii akamɔ bo.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check my crop trees for pests like ants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ tsei lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once a week by walking along your plant rows and looking up into the tree canopy. Regular checks help you catch pest invasions early before they spread across your entire farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli kɛtsɔ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ nyiɛmɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ni oookwɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: What is the best way to check if insects on my trees are actually causing damage or just resting there?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ale kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite nii diɛŋtsɛ loo amɛmiijɔɔ amɛhe kɛkɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Look closely at the leaves, flowers, and young fruits. If you notice yellowing, curled leaves, sticky wet spots, or stunted growth where the insects gather, they are actively damaging your plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ona baai ŋmɔŋ, baai ni ebɔle, ŋmɔtɔ, hei ni ŋmɔɔ. loo dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ he ni kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiifite otsei lɛ.

english: Should I clear the weeds between my crop rows, or does grass help keep pests off my trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ mitsei lɛ ateŋ? Aloo jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa?

english: You should keep the pathways and spaces between your rows clear. Tall weeds act as natural bridges that allow crawling pests like ants and bugs to easily climb onto your crop trees.
ga: Esa akɛ oha gbɛjegbɛi kɛ gbɛ ni kã sɛɛkuu lɛ teŋ lɛ mli atse. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli blɔji ni haa kooloi ni shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛkwɔɔ otsei lɛ anɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do pests attack some trees on my farm while leaving neighboring trees completely untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛtaaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ eko he lɛ?

english: Pests usually attack trees that are stressed, weakened by poor soil nutrients, or getting too much shade first. Healthy, strong trees have better natural resistance against insect infestations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ. Egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. aloo enine shɛ hulutsoo babaoo nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my crops develop sticky black leaves even when I water and weed regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa diji ni shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi daa moŋ?

english: Sticky black leaves are caused by black soot fungus, which grows on the sweet waste left behind by insects like ants, mealybugs, and aphids. Treating the insects stops the black spots from forming.
ga: Sooty fungus ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ediŋŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, mealybugs kɛ aphids eshi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ atsa kooloi bibii lɛ, ebaaha amɛkafee ŋmeii diji.

english: How do I know if an insect on my farm is good for my crops or bad for them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii loo ehiii kɛha amɛ?

english: Bad insects usually leave signs of damage like chewed leaves, holes in fruits, or sticky liquid on branches. Good insects, like spiders and ladybugs, actively hunt down and eat those harmful pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔji lɛ shiɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfite, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu yɛ aduawai amli, loo nu ni mli tse, yɛ tsei aniji anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kpakpai, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii, shĩɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfite. Bei pii lɛ, amɛgbeɔ nakai kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or forest trees to shield them from intense heat and retain soil moisture while they establish strong root systems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why does my yam yield smaller tubers when I let the vines trail on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ naa bulbs bibii beni mihaa wain tso lɛ nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ staking lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture energy for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines into the air so leaves receive full light and stay safe from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ aná la ni fa babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: This is a key sign of nitrogen deficiency. When the soil lacks enough nitrogen, the maize plant pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work together with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shades the soil, slows down water evaporation, keeps root temperatures cooler, and stops the ground from baking hard in intense heat.
