ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ baa shi. ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ais yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season stays longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays soaked with standing water for extended periods, roots drown and fungal rot quickly destroys the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni ekã shi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when severe heat or extreme swings between dry and wet soil shock the plant, preventing proper pollination and stopping fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tsakemɔ ni naa wa ni ba shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni efɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ ha tso lɛ he fee lɛ yaa. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa ni ekpaa aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why are my maize cobs missing half of their grains even though the cobs themselves grew big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ fã bɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: If maize plants lack water right when they are producing silks and pollen, the pollen dries up before fertilizing all the seed spots, leading to cobs with missing grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ siliki kɛ ŋmãa lɛ, Agbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ dani akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amli ŋmãa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ dumɔwui baa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees keep falling over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Microscopic worms called nematodes or banana stem weevils attack and eat the underground roots and base of the plantain, destroying the anchor system until the heavy stalk collapses under its own weight.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana stem weevils lɛ tutuaa plantains shishifãi kɛ amɛshishi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ hiɛ kɛyashi ŋtayaa ni tsii lɛ baagbee shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests such as thrips, mites, or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves or spreading a leaf-curl virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ loo ŋmeii ni baa ŋmeii amli lɛ mli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant plantain or shade trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain loo shade tso yɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting plantain or fast-growing trees provides temporary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees build strong root systems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa.

english: Will plowing my farm with a tractor every season spoil my soil over time?
ga: Ani trakta ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Repeated heavy plowing breaks down the soil's natural structure, making it easier for heavy rains to wash away topsoil and nutrients. Alternating tractor plowing with minimal tilling or using cover crops helps protect and maintain soil health over the long term.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rain right after I put fertilizer on my farm affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall right after fertilizer application washes the nutrients off the topsoil or pushes them deep underground where crop roots cannot reach them. This leaves your crops without food and wastes the fertilizer you bought.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ tsiɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ohé lɛ hu laajeɔ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves, or that water is sitting around the roots and choking them. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee baai ni mli wa Aloo nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves above ground instead of sending food down to grow large root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air dry out tomato flower pollen, preventing proper fertilization. When fertilization fails, the plant drops the flowers to save its water and energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi fɔmɔ ni sa lɛ naa Kɛji fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tight during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to survive hot weather. By rolling up their leaves, they expose less leaf surface to the sun, which reduces the amount of water escaping from the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la fioo pɛ amɛnáa. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in cold, damp, and overly shaded environments. Pruning excess farm shade and clearing weeds lets sunlight and fresh air dry out the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Jwɛi ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize when it is still young and tender?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms miitutua mi ŋmãa lɛ? Ni eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ blɛoo lolo?

english: Fall armyworm moths prefer laying eggs on young maize leaves because soft, tender leaves are easy for newly hatched caterpillars to chew and are rich in nutrients needed for their growth.
ga: Autumn caterpillar ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ baa bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ yeɔ mlɛo. ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ eyi mli obɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing when water stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe and pull nutrients up to the leaves. When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots, causing them to rot and starving the plant of oxygen and food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tso lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. When there isn't enough plant food in the soil, the maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my field will make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen gas directly from the air and stores it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the crop is harvested and the roots decay, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbo. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and food. This competition results in thin, weak plants with tiny ears of maize, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough food and light to yield full ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of just growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight, prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, and leads to larger yam yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young vegetables with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai bibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, works like an umbrella for the earth. It keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and suppresses weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ekpaa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny green droppings left inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ani eshwɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ragged holes accompanied by tiny green droppings are clear signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing center of the plant. These caterpillars eat the tender leaves before they unfold, which can stunt or kill the crop if left untreated.
ga: Bu ko ni mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee mlɛo loo efite kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating your crops breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does sorghum stay green and survive during dry spells when my maize wilts and turns brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deep root system that reaches water far below the surface, and its leaves can roll up tight to lock in moisture during hot weather. This built-in protection makes sorghum much more tolerant to dry weather than maize.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu he kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Hebuu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa nyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi fe ŋmãa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any tomatoes can actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ afee diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of key soil minerals like calcium. When the plant feels under threat from harsh conditions, it drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ shihilɛi gbohii miiwo ehe gbeyei lɛ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can test maturity by digging up just one or two plants and opening a few pods. If the inside wall of the shell has turned dark brown or black and the seeds fit tightly inside, your groundnut crop is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ehewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome loo enyɔ ni oootsi ni ogbele ŋmeii fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ bafee ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need support to lift their leaves toward the sun. Exposing the leaves to maximum sunlight allows the plant to produce more energy, which leads to larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo hulu la babaoo mli bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants a steady, regular supply of water helps them retain their blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu haa otsei lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, protects the soil from direct heat. It holds moisture in the ground longer, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed inside the central leaves of the plant, and applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛ yeɔ tso lɛ teŋ baai lɛ. Ni tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisted and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow or light-green patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitswa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when they receive too much direct, harsh sunlight without enough shade or moisture. Planting shade crops nearby keeps the young cocoa plants safe until they are mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings about one meter apart gives each plant enough space to spread its roots and form big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot uses up specific nutrients in the soil and allows maize pests to build up. Rotating your field with beans or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer in two steps: apply a starter fertilizer shortly after planting to help roots grow, and apply a second dose when the maize reaches knee-height to help it form strong ears.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛjeɔ shishi lɛ awo mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he shii enyɔ nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua ni ewaje toi lɛ.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough water for me to start planting my seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can start planting when the rain has soaked the ground deep enough that squeezing a handful of soil forms a soft ball that holds together without leaking water, ensuring seeds won't dry out after sprouting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje dumɔ shishi beni nugbɔ enɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko shwie shi ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why does it seem like the rainy season keeps changing months compared to 10 or 15 years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nyɔji babaoo yɔɔ srɔto yɛ bɔ ni eji afii 10 loo 15 ni eho nɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Climate patterns are shifting over time, which causes rainy seasons in Ghana to start earlier or later than they used to. This means traditional planting months like March or December can change, so farmers need to monitor current weather updates rather than relying only on past calendar dates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi mra loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ kusum naa tamɔ March loo December baanyɛ atsake. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ ahiɛ ahi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda gbii ni eho lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can shifts in rainfall timing affect how long my crops take to yield?
ga: Ani be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aná be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ koni amɛwo yibii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, crops depend on consistent moisture and sunlight to grow. Delayed or erratic rainfall slows down plant growth because crops conserve water during dry spells, which extends the time it takes for them to mature and yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hulu la ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ebaaa daa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii hiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha be ni heɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right month to plant my seeds when the rainfall timing is no longer predictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Be mli ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Instead of planting strictly by calendar dates, wait until the soil receives consistent, deep rainfall that moistens the root layer. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a dry period follows.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kalanda gbi lɛ naa lɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baa daa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be eho.

english: Is it better to clear my land in December or wait until right before the rains start in March?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ December mli loo abaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba yɛ March mli?

english: Clearing your land early in December helps you prepare ahead of time, but leaving bare soil exposed to intense sun for too long can dry it out. It is usually best to complete final soil preparation right before the early rains begin.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni oootsi yɛ December shishijee gbɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ osaa ohe kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Shi kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha egbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee naagbee shikpɔŋ he saamɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Why does planting immediately after the very first rain sometimes cause my seeds to fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often only wet the surface without soaking deep into the soil. If hot, dry weather returns right after, the tender young roots will scorch and die before they can establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee.

english: Why do my crops stop growing or look weak when the early rains start and then suddenly stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ loo etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi trukaa ni ekpaa lɛ?

english: Young crops need continuous moisture to build strong roots. When early rains stop abruptly, the topsoil dries out rapidly, causing crop stress, stunted growth, or wilting because the young roots cannot reach moisture deep down.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ekɛ haomɔ aba tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraa loo amɛgboi ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when an unexpected dry spell occurs right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden dry weather after planting prevents plants from absorbing vital nutrients from the soil. When plants cannot draw up food and water, they experience stress, which shows up as yellowing leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu Haomɔ baaba ni baaje kpo tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I buy my seeds and inputs early instead of waiting for the rains to arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛ niyenii mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Getting your seeds, fertilizers, and cash ready early ensures you can plant immediately when the soil moisture is right. If rains come earlier than expected and you are not ready, you miss the vital early window of the growing season.
ga: Dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa yɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ mra fe bɔ ni okpaa gbɛ ni ofeee klalo Obaakpa shishijee fã ni he hiaa ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ.

english: What kind of crop varieties should I plant if I am worried the rainy season will be short this year?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji mihao akɛ afi nɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee kuku?

english: You should plant early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties. These varieties grow faster and produce yield in a shorter time frame, reducing the risk of crop failure if the rains cut off early.
ga: Esa akɛ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra.

english: How can I protect my farm from losing money if rainy seasons keep getting delayed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni shika akafite kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: You can protect your farm by planting different types of crops, using practices like mulching to keep moisture in the soil, and staggering your planting dates so all your crops do not rely on a single wet spell.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Nifeemɔi tamɔ mulching ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ atsake bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ akafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi kome pɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct hot sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving bigger trees or planting shade crops like plantain keeps the seedlings cool and moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food in the soil. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if weeds are stealing the plant's food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo jwɛi ju tso lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest underground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground right around the base of the stem will start to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my young maize leaves and tiny worms hiding inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. Mi nɔ ni akɛtee yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the worms hatch, they eat the soft parts of the plant, which requires early checking and pest control to protect your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli ni akudɔ amɛ mra. koni akɛbu onibii ahe

english: Why should I leave space between my crop rows instead of planting seeds very close together to get more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui akutsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, making them grow thin and weak. Proper spacing allows good airflow to prevent diseases and helps each plant produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli koni helai akamɔ tso fɛɛ tso ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rains start. If you plant too early, the hot sun during that dry gap can scorch the new seeds before they develop strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ ŋshɔkei ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. When the plant gets stressed by harsh weather or irregular watering, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass on the dirt around their crop roots during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It prevents the hot sun from evaporating the water in the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up off the hot ground into the sunlight so they can make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves healthy, reduces disease from the soil, and helps you get larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. koni akɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ jogbaŋŋ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leafy green growth. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure near the roots will help the crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant during hot weather helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows its stem to grow thick enough to support big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tseɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully matured and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the main stem will start to crack as the roots expand beneath the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ he lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaf sap and spread viruses. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or natural neem oil helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Ni ooofɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa bulbs wuji lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of lush leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when planted under heavy shade. Cowpeas need full, open sunlight and less leafy fertilizer so the plant directs its strength into making pods.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Cowpeas he miihia hulu ni fa kɛ baa mli ŋmɔshi nibii fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ pods feemɔ mli.

english: Young crops have short roots and cannot outgrow fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients go directly to your young crops instead of being stolen by weeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara fe jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ baa odumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni jwɛi baaju lɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the afternoon sun even though I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant temporarily wilts to save moisture, but it will stand back up in the cooler evening as long as the soil has water.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi ebaaŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ mli, be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baahi shi akɛ nu.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni kookoo tsei bibii jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure helps restore green growth and supports ear formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua toi lɛ afeemɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ he hewalɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps feed the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing tiny worms to eat holes in the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Niyeli bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center of maize. Applying approved treatments or neem extracts early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo yɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa ni ekaho oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same farm patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the same nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases specific to maize to build up in the earth.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be mli ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best part of the stem when planting cassava cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: The best cuttings come from the hard, mature middle section of healthy cassava plants, cut into lengths with about four to six visible nodes or buds.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ jɛɔ yucca tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni eda lɛ mli. Afoɔ lɛ mli bibii kakadaji ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni anaa aaafee 4-6 yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji

english: Should I apply my dry fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum aje shishi?

english: It is better to apply fertilizer when the ground is damp after a gentle rain; heavy rain can wash the fertilizer away before the roots have time to absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛŋɔ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom up, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the growing season helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the plants helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tsei baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying treatment directly into the leaf funnel helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ tso lɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight and away from the damp ground. Maximum sunlight exposure helps the plant generate energy to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Hulu la ni anáa babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing temporary shade like plantains shields young cocoa seedlings from harsh heat until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli oya tamɔ cocoa plantain lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: How do I pick the best plantain suckers from my field for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni madu?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have broad bases and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves early on, as they grow slowly and produce weak fruit bunches.
ga: Halamɔ 'sword shoot' ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ lance. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘sucker shoot’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ he mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ kui bibii amli.

english: Can I plant any part of a cassava stem to grow a new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã ko koni mikɛkwɛ tso hee?

english: Not all parts yield well. Cuttings should come from the mature, healthy middle section of the stem, avoiding the soft green top and the very woody base.
ga: Ekɛ yibii kpakpai baaa yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ ajɛ tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ashishi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my soil for next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil, enriching it for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool, reduces water evaporation, suppresses weed growth, and gradually adds organic matter as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ fiofio be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied during active growth stages—such as a few weeks after germination and just before flowering—when the soil is moist enough for roots to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ miida waa, tamɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ kɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to buy my crop fertilizers and protection sprays long before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Ordering your farm inputs early ensures you get quality products at fair prices before market shortages hit, and guarantees you have treatment ready to protect your crops at the exact right week without delay.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ooobi mra Enɛ baaha onine ashɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ jara ni sa nɔ dani jarayeli mli nibii ni faaa lɛ aba. Ni ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ obaaná tsofa ni asaa he koni ebu onibii ahe lɛ yɛ otsi ni sa lɛ mli ni okɛ be sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why should I treat my maize seeds with protective chemicals before putting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu ŋmãa dumɔwui ahe nii dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Treating seeds before planting acts like an early vaccine that protects them from being destroyed by soil pests, ants, and fungi, ensuring nearly every seed sprouts healthily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he mra, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to move my pepper seedlings out of the nursery and into the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie pepper dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready after 4 to 6 weeks of careful maintenance in the nursery, once they have developed strong roots and at least 4 to 6 sturdy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ, be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, amɛbaai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens if I keep my tomato plants in the nursery bed past their transplanting time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ wo tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli kɛho be ni akɛbaawo mli lɛ he?

english: If seedlings stay in a crowded seedbed too long, they fight for sunlight and become tall, thin, and weak, which makes them frail and unproductive once planted in the field.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ hi dumɔwui ashihilɛhe ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛbaawuu amɛha hulu la ni amɛbaadara, amɛhe afee shwilafo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why should I expose my nursery plants to full sunlight and reduce their water a week before moving them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha midumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu lɛ aba shi otsi kome dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This transition period hardens the young plants so they don't experience shock, wilting, or death from the sudden harsh sun and drier soil of the main farm.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsakemɔ be nɛɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ mli waa. Enɛ ji koni akafee shoofeemɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo gbele ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa trukaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fe ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to spray my young crops on a regular schedule even when I do not see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be naa, kɛji akɛ anaaa kooloi bibii komɛi po lɛ?

english: Routine preventive sprays protect delicate young plants from invisible disease spores and pest attacks early on, which is much cheaper and easier than trying to save damaged mature crops later.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ helai anɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni anaaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mra lɛ ahe. Enɛ jara waaa ni eyɛ mlɛo fe bɔ ni aaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ mli sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is weed control so urgent during the first few weeks after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ jwɛi anɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate during their early growth stage, and if weeds are allowed to compete with them during these first weeks, they steal moisture and nutrients, permanently stunting the crop.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. Ni kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii nɛɛ amli lɛ, amɛbaaju ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need fast-growing plantain trees next to them during their early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwu lɛ aná dumɔwu ko ni daa oya yɛ emasɛi lɛ? yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense tropical sun, so fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and cool moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato vines need wooden stakes or cages to support them as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato wain tsei lɛ ahe hiaa tsei loo ŋtayaai ni baaye abua amɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Stakes lift the plant and heavy fruits off the damp ground, keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases and stopping rot from destroying mature fruits.
ga: Fimɔ tsei lɛ woɔ tsei ni tsii kɛ aduawai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ ni ekpa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I apply starter fertilizer during the early planting phase rather than waiting until the crops start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Crops need concentrated nutrients during their first weeks to build a strong root system and sturdy stems, which later power heavy fruit and seed development.
ga: Niyenii ni mli wa he hiaa tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii lɛ amli koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ baaye abua ni sɛɛ mli lɛ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my land before planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and produce broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil cool and moist while young cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa ehe shi lɛ.

english: What will happen to my young cocoa plants if I put them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Without shade, strong sunlight burns the delicate leaves of young cocoa trees, stunts their growth, and causes many seedlings to wither and die from high heat and dry soil.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. ni ha dalɛ kpa ni eha dumɔwui babaoo gboi ni amɛgboi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Should I plant my plantains several months before my cocoa, or can I plant them both at the exact same time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu plantains nyɔji babaoo dani madu kookoo? Aloo obaanyɛ odu tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: It is best to plant plantains first so they can grow tall and develop big leaves. This ensures that when you put your young cocoa seedlings in the ground, shelter from the sun is already waiting for them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantains klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekwɛ ni eyɛ baai wuji. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kɛ́ okɛ kookoo tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ, He ko ni hulu lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ni miimɛ bo.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are over-aged and need to be cut down for replanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afo lɛ koni ekɛ ehee aba?

english: When cocoa trees get too old, their yield drops drastically even with good care, they become weak, and they are more vulnerable to pests and diseases. Replanting replaces them with fresh, high-yielding trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po. Kookoo tso lɛ baafee mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni amɛhe yɔɔ oya kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Abaawo tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must old cocoa trees be cut down completely instead of just planting new seedlings beneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei momoi lɛ kwraa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Old trees block needed sunlight and steal water and nutrients from the soil. Completely cutting them down removes competition and clears out pests or diseases hiding in the old trees, giving new seedlings a healthy start.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa kwraa, ni egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso momo lɛ mli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ

english: How does clearing my old farm and starting fresh benefit my income in the long run?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii ni mije ehee shishi lɛ baaha mishika ni mináa lɛ aná he sɛɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Although cutting old trees takes time to rebuild yield, starting fresh with modern seedling varieties and proper field setup results in much bigger harvests and higher profits than keeping low-producing old trees.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei momoi ni afoɔ lɛ heɔ be dani anyɛɔ anáa tsei heei moŋ, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ajeɔ shishi ekoŋŋ kɛ hei ni sa ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo ni sɛɛnamɔi babaoo hu baa fe tsei ni egbɔ ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why is a chemical treatment applied to the stumps of old cocoa trees after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo tso momo lɛ shishifãi anɔ beni afolɔ amɛ sɛɛ?

english: When an old tree is cut down, the stump can sprout fresh shoots or carry disease in its root system. Applying chemical treatment directly to the cut surface prevents the stump from regrowing and stops diseases from spreading in the soil.
ga: Kɛji afo tsei momoi lɛ Ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ tsei heei loo amɛkɛ hela aya shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai wo shikpɔŋ ni afo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will the chemical put on cut tree stumps harm the new crops I plant nearby?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei akutsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ baaye tsei heei ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ awui?

english: No, when applied properly directly onto the freshly cut stump, the treatment stays within the old tree tissue to kill it off and does not spread to harm nearby soil or young plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛwo tso ni afo ehee lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsofa lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli fãji momo lɛ amli koni ejie lɛ. ni egbɛ eshwaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is lining and row planting important before placing plantains and cocoa into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato ŋmeii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni adu amɛ dani akɛ plantains kɛ cocoa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, evenly spaced rows gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and airflow. It also makes walking through the farm, spraying crops, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ akɛ fɛɛ to he lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso baaná he ko, hulu la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ, tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Can I harvest and sell the plantains planted for shade, or will that hurt my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantains ni midu koni maná hulutsoo lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ? Aloo ebaaye mikoo tso bibioo lɛ awui?

english: You can safely harvest and sell the plantains. They provide extra food and cash while your cocoa is growing, and as long as you do not damage the cocoa roots during harvest, the plantains will continue to shade your trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa plantains ni ohɔ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe. Amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni o-cocoa lɛ miida lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ ofiteee kookoo shishifãi lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ aha otsei lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a cry for nitrogen, which is the food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Rain often washes away nutrients from the topsoil, leaving the young roots hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ biɔ nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ

english: Why does my soil become hard like concrete after rain, making my crops struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni mafee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves, grass, or manure. Adding compost keeps the soil loose and spongy, allowing plant roots to spread and breathe easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai, jwɛi, loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛmuɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plant before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dryness. When the weather gets too hot, the plant sheds flowers to save its strength until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo egbi waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know my oranges are ripe to harvest if the skin is still green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-orange lɛ eshɛ shi kɛha kpamɔ? Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo?

english: In tropical climates, citrus fruits like oranges often stay green on the outside even when they are fully sweet and mature inside because the weather never gets cold enough to turn them orange.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Citrus yibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, fɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kponɔgbɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ emli lɛ mli ŋɔɔ kwraa ni eshɛre kwraa moŋ. Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leafy stems look very big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tamɔ agbo ni eyɛ baai babaoo moŋ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rain, it puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo nugbɔ babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat as a defense trick to protect themselves from losing water. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, it might be a disease.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee hela.

english: Why are dark, rotting spots appearing on the bottom of my watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni egboi ni tsuɔ waa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ watermelon lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dark soft spots at the bottom of watermelons are caused by a lack of calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly, which usually happens when watering is uneven or dry spells occur.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ watermelon shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi.

english: Why am I supposed to prune off the extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called water suckers, steal energy, water, and food from the main tree trunk. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its energy into growing healthy flowers and large cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ nu mli tsei lɛ, juɔ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaabi ni tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why is it recommended to trim the leaves of plantain suckers before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɔ akɛ afolɔ dumɔwui ahe baai dani adu?

english: Trimming the leaves reduces water loss while the sucker has no active roots. It helps the stem stay alive and focus its energy on growing fresh, strong roots into the new soil.
ga: Baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi heei ni wa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my hybrid maize seeds give a better harvest than seeds I saved from last year's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed in a lab to give uniform high yields and resist local diseases. The seeds saved from a harvest lose this special power in the next generation, producing weaker plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ laboratori ko mli koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo aha be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land where I am starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni maje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ama shi lɛ.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during intense heat to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which conserves water inside the plant and prevents it from drying out.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When crops lack nitrogen in the soil, they move whatever nutrients they have left from their older, bottom leaves up to nourish new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daa koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do cowpea crops help make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina tsei yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen feeds the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpea kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, akɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms feed inside the center funnel of my maize plant instead of on the outside leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ naa niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaana niyenii yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the dark central funnel (whorl) of the maize plant because it stays moist, protects them from hot sunlight, and keeps them hidden from natural predators like birds.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ amli (rings) ejaakɛ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛkɛ amɛ ato adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly in cold, wet, and humid weather, especially when dense branches block sunlight and airflow inside the tree canopy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli, titri lɛ kɛji tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key plant nutrients needed to nourish fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ kpe. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni haa aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling up into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand if the soil is too hard and compacted for the tubers to push through, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the main nutrient plants use to build tuber energy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei shishifãi amli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my food crops immediately after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and sit dormant in the topsoil waiting for water. Once rain falls, they germinate faster than planted seeds to quickly grab sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni esa akɛ amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmɛ nu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ koni amɛŋɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why do stored seed yams start sprouting on their own in the barn even before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ po baa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal clock called dormancy that keeps them sleeping through the dry season. Once that internal clock expires, the yam naturally uses its stored energy to sprout, signaling it is time to plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, Sweet potatoes kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom leaves upward, it is a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-decomposed manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year if I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients from the earth and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dried grass help them stay healthy during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—blocks the harsh hot sun from drying out the soil. It keeps moisture in the ground longer, reduces weed growth, and cools the roots of your plants.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the earth when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in flat, packed soil because the roots cannot breathe in soggy ground. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I buried them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply run out of stored energy trying to push through all that dirt before reaching sunlight. Maize seeds should only be planted about two finger-joints deep so the shoot can easily emerge above the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ. Kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni ashwie sũ lɛ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee nineshi 2 pɛ. koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds come during fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil, making heavy bunches pull the tree down in high winds. Supporting the fruiting stems with bamboo or wooden props gives them the strength to stand until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni ŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Enɛ haa tso lɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ kɛyaa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to protect young cocoa from sunburn and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants with tall poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo mi-sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?
