english: Yam vines need to climb high toward the sun so their leaves can soak up sunlight and turn it into food, which makes the tubers underground grow big and heavy. Keeping leaves off the ground also prevents soil-borne diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛtsɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the undersides of the leaves. Spraying plants with diluted neem oil or soapy water controls these insects before they damage the whole farm.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla ewo mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when daytime weather becomes extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden stress from drying out completely. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ trukaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni egbo kwraa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Cocoa trees often drop their flowers when the soil lacks water or proper nutrients, or when small insects like mirids damage the blossoms. Ensuring proper shade, moisture, and pest control helps the tree hold its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids fite fɔfɔi lɛ, hulutsoo ni sa, hulutsoo, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii baa.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne kroko ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes weak or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach the main trunk and branches. This keeps the tree healthy, prevents fungal diseases, and directs energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewaa. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni okɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji

english: Is it bad if my cocoa trees receive full, direct sunlight all day long?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ ná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, direct intense sunlight can burn young cocoa leaves and stress mature trees. Cocoa trees need light shade from bigger trees to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai bibii ni eha tso lɛ adara. Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my cashew trees to produce very few nuts even when they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Low cashew yields are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or dieback insects damaging the flowers, or branches growing too closely together and blocking sunlight from reaching the inner flowering stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni egboi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cashew yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa. aloo tsei niji ni shwereɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cashew trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Cashew trees grow very wide branches and deep roots. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ niji ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees flower mostly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally flower during bright, dry weather because hot sunlight triggers flower production and allows insects like bees to easily pollinate the flowers without rain washing them away.
ga: Cashew tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi feɔ. Ni ehaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii oya ni nugbɔ lɛ shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, very wet, or overly shady farms. Clearing thick weeds and removing infected pods regularly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ waa loo ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why is clearing weeds around the base of my trees so important for my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from your tree's roots. They also hide harmful insects and plant diseases that can jump onto your cocoa or cashew trees and ruin your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli. Amɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ o-cocoa loo cashew tso lɛ nɔ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm needs fertilizer for my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi-kookoo lɛ?

english: If your cocoa tree leaves turn pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the tree grows very slowly and produces small pods, the soil is missing key nutrients and needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni efee ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do tree seedlings bought from a nursery yield fruit faster than seeds I plant straight from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are often prepared using high-quality parent trees or grafting methods that speed up maturity and guarantee the new tree produces heavy fruit much sooner than ordinary seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ nyɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni haa amɛdaraa oya ni ehaa nɔmimaa akɛ tsei heei lɛ baawo yibii ni tsii oya kwraa fe dumɔwui folo lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛsaa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I buy improved crop seeds instead of just using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred by researchers to resist local diseases, tolerate dry weather better, and produce higher yields than older seeds that lose their strength over time.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi baadu dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo fe dumɔwui momo ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties cook soft for boiling while others remain hard and are only good for processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ahoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni wa ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ pɛ lɛ.

english: Different cassava varieties have different starch and water contents; sweet varieties with low cyanide levels are best for direct boiling, while high-starch varieties are developed specifically for making gari or flour.
ga: Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ashikiŋsha kɛ nu falɛi srɔtoi yɛ. Nibii ni ŋɔɔ ni cyanide faaa yɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dãafeemɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ be mli ni afee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ kɛha kari loo ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food for plants that often gets washed away by heavy rains or blocked when the soil becomes waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titri kɛha tsei ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu.

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced smaller yields than expected, your soil is low on essential nutrients and needs manure or commercial fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo fe bɔ ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to preserve moisture and survive heat. The plant is not dead; it goes into resting mode until the rains return to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebabote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baatsɔ baai heei.

english: Why did half of the maize seeds I planted in the soil fail to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they were buried too deep for the shoots to reach the light, or if soil insects like ants ate them before they could germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ la lɛ he Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do crops yield more when planted in straight rows instead of scattering seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps your farm because beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: What causes fall armyworms to suddenly appear and destroy my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa cutworms lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa ni ekpãtãa mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths fly in during warm weather and lay hundreds of eggs under crop leaves overnight, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars that feed on tender plant leaves.
ga: Autumn mli ŋmeii baa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmeii ohai abɔ woɔ tsei ahe baai ashishi nyɔɔŋ kome. ni shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up my yams from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the soil dry out and turn yellow or brown, showing the plant has finished feeding the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii naa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water and survive the heat. Planting permanent shade trees and mulching around the roots helps keep the soil moist and protects young cocoa from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, why do the stalks grow tall and thin without big cobs?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmãa agbo ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete intensely for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into producing large cobs, the plants stretch upward to search for light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, tso lɛ tsɔ ehe ni etao la.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a defensive reaction to heat stress or water shortage, but it can also be caused by viral infections spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ ejɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies mli kɛbaa lɛ hu kɛba.

english: Why do my planted seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil pushes out oxygen, which seeds need to breathe and sprout. Drowned seeds rot quickly because soil fungi and bacteria thrive in overly wet conditions.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui lɛ amu ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo nu shishi lɛ fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants have thick green leaves but fail to produce any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to focus all their growth on foliage rather than fruits. Using balanced nutrients rich in phosphorus encourages blooming and fruit formation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama edalɛ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Niyenii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baawo fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their blossom flowers before any small fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani aduawai bibii baa lɛ?

english: Fruit trees shed excess flowers due to dry winds, heavy rains, or a lack of insect pollinators like bees. The tree naturally discards blossoms it cannot support with its available water and energy.
ga: Yibii tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to keep clear space around my yam mounds during the early growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi he ko yɛ he lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ fã lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight and free root space to grow thick tubers underground. Weeds steal sunlight, water, and nutrients, which prevents the yams from swelling properly.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ yaka koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ afuu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove the low branches that touch the ground on my tomato crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ yɛ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves that touch wet soil easily pick up fungal and bacterial diseases that spread to the rest of the plant. Trimming lower branches improves airflow and redirects energy into fruit growth.
ga: Baai ni taa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei krokomɛi lɛ eshwaa. of plants easily Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ yaa yibii lɛ adalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava reaches maturity, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall, while the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting beans alongside my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that absorb nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans ji ŋmãa ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: I keep hearing other cocoa farmers talk about 'akate', but what does this pest actually do to my cocoa trees?
ga: Miyaa nɔ minuɔ kookoo okwaafoi krokomɛi ni wieɔ ‘Agate’ he, shi mɛni ji nɔ ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ feɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Akate (capsids or mirids) are small insects that suck sap from young cocoa shoots and pods. They inject toxic saliva that leaves dark spots, causing young shoots to die back and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Akate (capsids loo mirids) ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: What is 'apotre' and how do I know if it is present on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘apotre’ ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apotre is a type of pest or pod borer that attacks cocoa pods and stems. You will know it is present if you see small entry holes, dark patches, or decaying areas on your cocoa pods and branches.
ga: Apotre ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo pod borer ko ni tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ eshishifãi. Obaale akɛ eyɛ jɛmɛ kɛji ona buji bibii, hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo hei ni egboi yɛ kookoo tsei kɛ tsei aniji anɔ.

english: How can I tell the difference between different pests like 'ate' and 'akate' on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ‘ate’ kɛ ‘akate’ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: While both 'ate' and 'akate' are harmful insects that feed on cocoa plants, they differ slightly in size, color, and the specific stage or part of the tree (such as new leaves versus mature pods) that they prefer to attack.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ‘ate’ kɛ ‘akate’ fɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yeɔ cacao tsei moŋ, shi amɛsoro amɛhe fioo yɛ amɛdalɛ, amɛhe su, kɛ tso lɛ fã pɔtɛɛ loo efã ko (tamɔ baai heei kɛ ŋmeii ni eda) ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛtutua lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa branches suddenly turning brown and dying back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: This dieback is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like akate feeding on the tender bark of new shoots, which blocks water and nutrients from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ academe ni yeɔ tsei heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe tsɔi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ gbele nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use local medicinal plants and strong vines to protect my cocoa trees from insects instead of chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofafeemɔ tsei kɛ wain tsei ni wa atsu nii kɛbu cacao tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, many traditional remedies made from mixtures of medicinal herbs and vines contain natural chemicals that repel or destroy insects like akate without harming the crop or soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, blema tsofai babaoo ni akɛ tsofai kɛ wain tsei afutu mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni shwieɔ loo efiteɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ akate, ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ awui.

english: Why do some farmers mix different medicinal plants together when preparing a treatment for cocoa pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsofai srɔtoi futuɔ amɛhe beni amɛsaa tsofai ni akɛtsaa kookoo mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ?

english: Combining different plants merges several active natural properties into one mixture, making the remedy stronger and able to fight off multiple types of farm pests at once.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsei srɔtoi fata he lɛ, amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni tsuɔ nii feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ mli waa ni enyɛɔ ewuɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi srɔtoi babaoo shikome.

english: Is it safe to make my own herbal pest spray with local plants, or will it burn my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii? Aloo ebaashã mikoo tso lɛ?

english: Herbal preparations are generally safe for crops because they are organic, but you must dilute them correctly with water and filter out debris so they do not damage leaves or clog your spraying equipment.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛsaa he lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ amɛji tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛjie jwɛi lɛ koni ekafite baai lɛ loo ekatsi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Should I filter or clear out dead insects and plant debris from my natural spray mixture before applying it to my crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo loo majie kooloi bibii ni egboi kɛ tsei amli nibii ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ mi adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, straining the mixture removes solid particles and dead creatures so that your spray flows smoothly and applies evenly across all the cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ nibii bibii ni wa kɛ nibii ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ baaha o-spray lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eha cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of year to treat my cocoa farm for destructive pests?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matsa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ?

english: The critical period for pest control is during the main growth and fruiting seasons (typically August through December), when new shoots and young pods attract high numbers of insects.
ga: Be ni he hiaa waa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii. (Be pii lɛ, August kɛyashi December) be mli ni ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii gbalaa kooloi babaoo kɛbaa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop insects from damaging my young cocoa pods before they mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni ŋmeii akafite kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara?

english: You can protect young pods by removing diseased pods early, keeping farm weeds under control, managing tree shade to lower humidity, and applying natural or recommended treatments at the first sign of pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie mra lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shade nɔ koni hulutsoo be lɛ akafee bibioo. ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ mli.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for making leaves green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or waterlogs the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct heat because their tender leaves burn quickly and lose water. They rely on temporary shade plants like plantains to protect them from the sun and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains anɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do many small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Amɛteŋ babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by cherelle wilt, which is the cocoa tree's natural way of discarding extra pods it cannot support with water and nutrients, though it can also be caused by fungal diseases during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherelle lɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ ashwieɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa moŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and short instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams struggle to expand in hard or clay-heavy soil. When the soil is too compact, the growing tuber meets physical resistance underground and becomes short, branched, or distorted.
ga: Sweet potatoes bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Bulbs ni miida lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shitee-kɛ-woo kpeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfeɔ kukuji, amɛfeɔ niji, loo amɛfeɔ srɔtoi.

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and tough if I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni amɛhe wa kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age past maturity, they start using the starch stored in their roots to keep the stems and leaves growing, which leaves behind fibrous, woody roots that are difficult to cook and eat.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ shɛɔ afii pɔtɛɛ ko he lɛ Amɛbɔi ŋmeii ni ato yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛdara. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ fiber ni ahoomɔ kɛ yeli wa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers drop their leaves right after I move them to a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: This happens due to transplant shock because the main roots were cut during separation from the mother plant. The seedling sheds old leaves to conserve water while it focuses on growing new roots in the soil.
ga: Enɛ baa yɛ transplant shock hewɔ akɛni afoɔ shishifã titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui shwieɔ baai momoi koni amɛkɛbu nu he, ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi heei ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when day temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly. Severe heat stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination and forcing the flower to fall off.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa ni onyɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbee shi

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a defense mechanism caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaf, or by viral infections spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji gbɛ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to lie dormant in dry soil for months and wake up instantly at the first drop of rain, giving them a head start over newly planted crop seeds that take longer to germinate.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkã shi ni amɛwɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni ete shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee, ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops look green and bushy but fail to produce many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to spend all their energy growing stems and leafy branches instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and strong so the plant can make healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil naturally. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that rich soil food to grow tall without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft and good enough for cassava tubers to grow big?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehi bɔ ni sa ni ŋmei shishifãi baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Cassava needs loose soil to expand its root tubers. If your soil is hard clay, mixing in organic compost and breaking up big mounds allows the tubers room to swell underneath.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa ni abua naa babaoo lɛ baaha bulbs lɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛshishi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shady weather. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods right away stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ hela lɛ naa oya koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, which eat the leaf tissue. Spraying early with approved treatments or putting neem leaf mixture in the plant funnel helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall flukes, ni yeɔ baai amli fãji lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ mra Aloo, kɛ akɛ neem baai ni akɛfutu tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants look curled, wrinkled, and yellow-spotted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural office keeps your crop safe from this leaf damage.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ lɛ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe koni baai lɛ akafite.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each corn stalk enough room to get sunlight and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la baa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, dried-out soil, or lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the ground moist and feeding the soil keeps flowers on the branches.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the vine leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally, showing that the plant has stored all its energy inside the mature tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɔ bo akɛ efee klalo kɛji wain tso lɛ baai lɛ kpa dalɛ. etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni eda kwraa lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect their soft leaves from high heat and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni oduɔ nii lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my yam vines growing huge green leaves, but the yams under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yams ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the yam plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛba shi koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellow patches instead of spreading out broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, which reduces your crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the growing funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu komɛi. Akɛtee niche ko ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars feed on the tender central leaves of the maize plant, which can destroy the plant before it produces corn ears if not managed early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso lɛ hiɛ dani ená ŋmãa toi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress makes the plant shed its blossoms to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Heat haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Rolling leaves is a protective response to heat. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa lɛ hetoohamɔ mli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and die after heavy rains leave water standing in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water fills all the soil air pockets, drowning the roots and causing root rot, which makes the plant wilt and die.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbiɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin and fall over when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward rapidly. This creates weak, thin stems that easily break or fall over in strong winds.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly even after I applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If weeds are not cleared first, their roots will steal the fertilizer and soil moisture faster than your crops can reach them, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food that helps crops grow strong. It can also happen when too much rain stays around the roots, preventing them from taking in air and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest every season when I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ kpaŋ nii fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains beside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can grow safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but only yield tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight and nutrients. They end up using all their food energy to grow leaves upward instead of building big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ shi moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up when I dig deep holes to bury them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mifoɔ bu ni mli kwɔ koni mikɛfu amɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of energy to sprout. If buried too deep in the ground, the young shoot uses up all its strength before reaching the top of the soil and rots underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some of my seeds rot in the dirt after planting without growing at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is flooded with excess water that blocks air, or when planted in dry soil where they sit too long and get attacked by soil insects and fungus before rain comes.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni dumɔwui lɛ taraa shi be kakadaŋŋ ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the center of my maize plants instead of eating the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: The central funnel of the maize plant is soft, wet, and shielded from direct sun and hungry birds, giving caterpillars a cozy, protected environment to hide and feed on young leaves.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ he ko ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ okpoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa he ko ni mli edɔ ni abuɔ he koni amɛtee amɛtee ni amɛye baai bibii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves and suck out plant juices, or by viruses carried by these insects that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when plants don't get consistent water. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, making it impossible for fruit to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haaa yibii aba.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting vines onto stakes helps leaves catch sunlight while keeping them off wet soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant ginger together with pineapple on the same land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ginger kɛ pineapple baafata he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping ginger with pineapple can be beneficial. Tall pineapple plants can provide partial shade that ginger appreciates, and growing both allows you to maximize space and earn income from two distinct harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmei ni akɛfataa ŋmei he lɛ hu he. Anana tsei kakadaji baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be fioo, taakɛ ŋmei hiɛ sɔɔ lɛ. Ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa onáa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ babaoo ni onáa shika kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi srɔtoi enyɔ mli.

english: Why do some crops grow better when planted alongside other crops instead of on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe fe bɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdu amɛ lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together helps protect the soil, reduces weed growth, and maximizes farmland use. Certain companion plants can also provide necessary shade or help reduce pests for neighboring crops.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ha jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi ni oha okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ aya hiɛ koni aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo Hefatalɔi tsei komɛi baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni he hiaa loo eye ebua ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi.

english: If I plant both pineapple and ginger, will one take away all the plant nutrients from the other?
ga: Kɛ midu pineapple kɛ ginger fɛɛ Ani tso mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli?

english: Not necessarily, because pineapple and ginger have different root depths and nutrient needs. As long as you apply adequate compost or fertilizer and space them correctly, both crops can thrive together.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ srɔtoi. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa baafata he ni okɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ ŋmɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome.

english: How can I know if my local district has the right conditions for growing ginger successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miyɔɔ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ ni yeɔ omanye?

english: Ginger needs rich, well-draining soil and adequate rain or irrigation. You can ask your local agricultural extension office to test your soil texture and review rainfall patterns to confirm if your district is suitable.
ga: Ginger biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni nugbɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ Obaanyɛ obi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe lɛ ni eka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii akwɛ ni ekwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ mli koni ema nɔ mi kɛji okpokpaa lɛ sa.

english: Do pineapples and ginger require the exact same amount of sunlight to grow well?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa ŋmei kɛ ŋmei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, pineapples thrive in full, direct sunlight, whereas ginger prefers light shade or filtered sunlight to prevent its leaves from scorching.
ga: Dabi, ananas shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei sumɔɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo hulu la ni mli tse koni ebaa lɛ akashã.

english: Why are buyers in the market willing to pay more when ginger is added to pineapple products?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Adding ginger to pineapple products like juice improves the flavor profile and adds health benefits. Creating blended or processed goods creates 'added value,' which allows farmers to sell at higher price points.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ginger fata pineapple nibii, tamɔ juice he lɛ, ehaa ŋɔɔ ni ehaa hewalɛnamɔ he sɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛfutu loo nibii ni atsu he nii lɛ feemɔ baaha 'sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfata he' aba ni baaha okwaafoi ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ

english: What happens if I harvest my pineapples but don't process or sell them quickly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmei shi mikɛtsuuu nii loo mihɔ̃ɔɔ oya?

english: Fresh pineapples spoil quickly in tropical heat after harvest. If you cannot sell them immediately, processing them into drinks, jams, or dried snacks helps preserve them and avoids losing money to waste.
ga: Ananas ŋmɔŋ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji onyɛɛɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tsakemɔ ni okɛfee nibii ni anuɔ, jam, loo niyenii ni egbi lɛ haa ehiɔ shi ni efiteee shika.

english: How can processing raw crops into finished goods help my farming business grow?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni akɛfeɔ nibii ni agbe naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Processing raw crops turns low-priced commodities into high-value products with longer shelf lives. This allows you to sell to wider markets, such as supermarkets, and earn steady income throughout the year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni ahoko lɛ ahe nitsumɔ haa nibii ni jara waaa feɔ nibii ni jara wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni akɛtoɔ shĩa mli. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nii ohaa jarayeli he ko ni da, tamɔ jarayeli hei wuji. ni amɛná shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: How long does a pineapple crop take from planting until it produces mature fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ananas woɔ yibii?

english: Pineapples generally take between 12 to 18 months to yield mature fruit, depending on whether you plant using crowns, suckers, or slips, as well as local weather conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani eshɛɔ. Edamɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo baai miikwɛ̃, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ.

english: What should I do with my pineapple farm after harvesting the main fruit?
ga: Beni akpa aduawai titrii lɛ agbe naa lɛ Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mi-anana abɔɔ lɛ?

english: After harvesting, the parent pineapple plant produces suckers (new shoots). You can remove and replant these suckers for a new crop cycle, ensuring your land remains productive instead of being left unused.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, pineapple tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ baawo suckers (tso lɛ mli tsei heei). Obaanyɛ ojie nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni odu ekoŋŋ kɛha dumɔ be hee. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential food found in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant cannot make green leaf material, but adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee nibii ni ji baai eŋɔli. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall but only produce small or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aloo pods ni bɛ nɔ ko pɛ?

english: Maize plants produce empty cobs when seeds are planted too close together, forcing them to fight for sunlight and nutrients, or when there is dry weather right when the plant is flowering and pollinating.
ga: Abɛi tsei woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ tsei lɛ afɔfɔii kɛ amɛhewolonɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct hot sun. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees turn brown and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the air and soil quickly. Cocoa trees drop their leaves on purpose to conserve water and protect the trunk and roots from drying out until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the main stem starts to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rainwater pools around the roots without draining away properly, creating a wet environment where soil fungi thrive and attack the tubers. Planting yams on raised mounds helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni afeɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot and dry or when the plant receives irregular watering. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy to stay alive during hot spells.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck leaf juices and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in a white powdery dust during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly when nights are humid and days are dry. Spacing your plants further apart lets air flow through and stops the moisture that fuels the fungus.
ga: Muji yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu tsoɔ waa kɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli. Shi gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops early instead of waiting until harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong yields before the weeds can choke them.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its strength and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot or when they do not get enough water. The plant does this to protect itself from dying of heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei feɔ enɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni haa mɔ gboɔ lɛ he.

english: Is water taken from a catfish or tilapia pond good for watering my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ catfish loo tilapia nubu mli lɛ hi kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, water from fish ponds contains natural fish waste, which acts as a rich liquid fertilizer that nourishes leafy vegetables and helps them grow faster without extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo nubu mli nu lɛ mli loo mli nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my tomato plants keep them alive during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) shields the soil from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly, allowing plant roots to stay hydrated longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up quickly when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that lose moisture fast in direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a green umbrella, protecting the seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak instead of putting energy into forming large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma ŋmei agbo ko ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains last for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots. Without air in the soil, the tubers cannot breathe and quickly rot underwater.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni egbo oya yɛ nu shishi.

english: Hard or stony soil blocks yam roots from pushing straight down. Loosening the soil deeply into high mounds gives the roots space to expand smoothly into large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi kɛya shi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtee gɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants look like holes were shot through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ bu etsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in young leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar that hide inside the central leaves of the plant and chew through them as they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant garden eggs in the exact same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-egg lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Plants in the same crop family attract the same soil pests and diseases. Rotating your garden egg plot with crops like beans or maize starves those pests out of the soil.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ tsei aweku kome mli lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Obɔɔ lɛ mli ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi loo ŋshɔŋlooi baatsake. Ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow green and strong. It can also happen if the ground has too much water around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛmu ni amɛhe niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special microbes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that leftover nitrogen naturally fertilizes the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ eshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaye abua yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. However, if too many fall off, it is usually a sign that the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks nutrients in the soil, or is being attacked by insects like capsids.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔji babaoo shwie shi lɛ, Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids tutuaa amɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil diseases and allows the plant to send more energy down to make big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants that produce fewer, smaller peppers and catch diseases easily because air cannot flow between them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni helai baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender leaves inside the plant. Catching them early with approved organic treatments or sprays prevents them from destroying the main growth tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite shweremɔ he tsɔji titrii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaaku?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the stem begins to crack open from the swelling roots beneath. You can also dig up one test plant to check root size before harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Obaanyɛ otsa tso kome hu ni okɛka lɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha dani okpa.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the vine right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa trukaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ beni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split open when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to crack.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji amɛná nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the head start they need to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ feɔ klalo ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: It is best to wait until the soil has been soaked through by two or three heavy rains rather than planting after the very first rain. Planting too early can cause seeds to burn and die if a short dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ kuku ko ba.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to build strong leaves and stalks, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet during heavy rains or when fungal diseases infect the stem cuttings used for planting. Raising plant beds helps water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ye tsei niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Dumɔhe lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, trap moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and stops weed seeds from receiving sunlight to grow.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: What is eating small holes in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Small holes in young maize plants are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the growing leaf funnel. Detecting them early allows you to apply recommended sprays or local remedies like neem extract.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. mra ni anaa Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ŋaa loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and crisp during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can drink from the dry soil. Providing shade trees helps reduce sun stress and wind damage during dry months.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Shade ni akɛhaa lɛ haa hulu haomɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when heat gets too extreme, water supply is irregular, or the plant lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering during dry heat helps plants hold onto their flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. loo tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, serving as a natural food source for nearby maize plants while giving you an extra crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting off surplus branches from mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning surplus branches opens up the cocoa tree canopy to sunshine and air flow, which reduces moisture where black pod disease thrives and directs plant energy into developing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha kookoo tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ hei ni black pod hela lɛ daa yɛ lɛ, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa pods ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even if there seems to be plenty of space between plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight directly from your crops, starving the crops even if space looks open above ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jɛmɛ egbele yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: How does crop research conducted by government officers actually help my daily farm output?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe niiamlitaomɔ ni nɔyeli mli onukpai feɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi daa gbi ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ?

english: Agricultural research tests and selects seed varieties that better withstand local heat, resist common Ghanaian pests, and produce higher yields in local soil conditions.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ kaa kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ halamɔ. Enyɛɔ Ghana tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anaa. ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo aba yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi amli

english: Why do my crops start rotting on the farm if I wait just a few days too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mimɛ gbii fioo pɛ, ni etsɛ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Once a crop reaches full maturity, its natural defenses weaken and it begins to attract pests, fungi, and moisture. Harvesting promptly prevents rotting and keeps the produce fresh for the market.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa shi. ni ebɔi ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii agbalamɔ. Nikpamɔ oya lɛ tsiɔ fitemɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ehee kɛha jara.

english: How can I know the exact time my crop is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as changes in color, drying of the leaves, or changes in firm texture. Learning these specific signs prevents harvesting too early or too late.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔ, baai ni egbi, loo bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha lɛ tsakemɔi. Okadii pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ akasemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmaakpamɔ naa mra tsɔ loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ.

english: Why does my produce go soft and spoil so quickly right after it matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: As crops mature, natural enzymes cause them to soften and produce ripening gases. Without harvest and proper storage, these natural processes quickly turn mature crops into rotten produce.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara lɛ Adebɔɔ mli enzymes haa tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ bɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite oya.

english: What happens to my crop quality if I leave ripe produce in the field for extra time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field exposes them to excessive heat, insects, and rainfall, which damages their quality, reduces their selling price, and increases post-harvest losses.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa dɔlɛ ni fe nine, kooloi bibii, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. Enɛ saa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ, ehaa jarayeli jara baa shi ni ehaa nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than other varieties of the very same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ mra fe ekrokomɛi ni ji tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Different varieties have unique genetic characteristics. Early-maturing varieties complete their life cycle faster, helping farmers harvest early in the season or avoid dry spells.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe sui srɔtoi. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nii mra yɛ be lɛ mli loo amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant two different varieties of the same crop together in one field?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi akɛ madu tso kome mli henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?
