english: Planting different varieties together can cause management challenges because they may mature at different times, making it difficult to harvest one variety without leaving the other to spoil.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ Kɛ amɛfee ekome lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he naagbai aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaakpa tso lɛ eko ni ashiŋ ekroko lɛ ni egbo.

english: Why do white yam varieties seem more delicate to handle and store than other types?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he waaa fe ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: White yam varieties often have thinner skin and higher moisture content, which makes them more sensitive to bruises, rotting, and damage during harvest and transport.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛŋ lɛ fɔɔ hewolo ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo. ni haa enyɛɔ efiteɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ gbɛfaa be mli lɛ he waa.

english: Why do my tubers break so easily when I am digging them up during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bulbs lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mifo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Tubers break easily when the soil is dry and hard or when the variety has naturally brittle skin. Wetting hard soil slightly before harvest and digging carefully helps avoid breakage.
ga: Tubers lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ hewolo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ fioo dani akpa ni akumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekakumɔ.

english: Why do some tubers crack open in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bulb komɛi fãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Tubers often crack when heavy rainfall occurs suddenly after a dry period, causing the inner root to swell faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ.

english: Why do my crops lose their freshness and market value so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛ jara ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops lose water rapidly when exposed to sun and heat. Keeping produce in cool, shaded areas immediately after picking preserves moisture and maintains market freshness.
ga: Tsei ni akpa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni adu lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa jarayeli lɛ feɔ ehee.

english: Why should I not plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs instead of large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmãa tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ ŋmãa toi agbo najiaŋ

english: Why are caterpillars eating the tender leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the young growing tip of the maize plant. If they destroy the center leaves, the plant struggles to grow properly and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpãtã teŋgbɛ baa lɛ hiɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba akɛ ebaada ni ewo ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure will correct this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is wet rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe nɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop's roots and will stay unused until moisture is available.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni tsuuu nii kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaba.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting maize afterward allows the maize to feed on that natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aye adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from hot weather. The plant rests underground until rain returns, after which it quickly sprouts new leaves and resumes growing tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Tsei lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba. No sɛɛ lɛ, ebaakwɛ baai heei oya ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant build large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem has enough energy to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil lacks water. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, causing the plant to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong heat. Planting them alongside shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees provides the canopy cover and moisture they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni etswaa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔ yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can reach maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la babaoo aba yɛ be mli ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ hu naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plants regain their green color and produce full cob heads.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not soaking wet. Fertilizer applied right after a light rain allows roots to absorb it quickly, whereas applying it during heavy downpours will cause the rain to wash the nutrients away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi edɔɔɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each plant enough soil nutrients and room for tubers to expand underground without fighting neighboring plants for water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni he ko yɛ ni bulb lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ awuu kɛha nu.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my tomato leaves and making the fruits rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ tomato baai amli ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa

english: This damage is usually caused by small caterpillars like fruit borers. Spraying your plants early with organic mixtures like neem leaf water or recommended safe insecticides keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ aduawai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the earth through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected and tested to produce higher yields and resist local diseases, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength and lead to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafee fiofio Amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are getting too much water during the heavy rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nu babaoo miihe o-vegetables lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: If your plant leaves turn yellow and droop even though the ground is very wet, or if the stem base feels soft and slimy, the roots are drowning. Digging drainage channels around your bed allows excess water to run off so roots can breathe.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa moŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu mli. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ saatso lɛ he lɛ ni oootsi lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from drought. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout fresh leaves and resume normal growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark black spots at the bottom before they can even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant move calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up right on the tree during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, overly humid conditions. Pruning shade trees and cutting away congested branches allows sunlight and air flow into the farm, which dries out the moisture that the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa baa loo aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips carrying a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early with biological sprays or insect traps prevents them from spreading the disease to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips, ni hiɛ hela ko ni ebote tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ wala yibii loo bug zapper nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ hela amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my cowpea blossoms falling off the plant before producing any beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Flower drop in cowpeas is commonly caused by flower thrips feeding on the delicate buds or severe heat stress. Spraying safe control measures right when flower buds appear protects the blooms so they can turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cowpea mli lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afɔ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je kpo pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil each season and allows maize-specific pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating your plot with crops like beans or groundnuts restores vital nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baatsake lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the hybrid maize seed from the agro-dealer mature faster than the traditional seed I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ shwere oya fe daa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to grow rapidly, resist common local diseases, and produce uniform ears within a shorter timeframe, whereas saved traditional seeds gradually lose vigor and take longer to mature.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ toi ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni shishijee dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ baa shi ni eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact time when my underground yams are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams are mature for harvesting when the vines and leaves naturally dry up and turn brown. This sign shows that the foliage has stopped making food and the underground tuber has reached its maximum size.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda kɛha nikpamɔ beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ ekpa niyenii feemɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored onions rot so quickly after I bring them in from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eba lɛ?

english: Onions rot quickly if they are stored with wet outer skins or kept in closed containers without air movement. Drying them under shade for a few days to cure their outer neck skin and storing them in open mesh bags keeps them dry and firm.
ga: Sabolai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ loo yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni aŋã mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Ha amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi koni amɛkuɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ akafite. Ni kɛ́ okɛwo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni agbele mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops, will it make them yield twice as much?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ani ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ?

english: No, giving plants too much fertilizer can burn their roots, stunt their growth, and reduce yield. Just like overfeeding can make a person sick, crops need only the correct amount of nutrients at the right time.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo otsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshishifãi lɛ ashã. tsiɔ dalɛ naa ni ebaanyɛ eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi Taakɛ bɔ ni niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine baanyɛ aha mɔ he ajɔ lɛ lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa pɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I use the exact same type of fertilizer for all the crops on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Different crops have different dietary needs. Applying the wrong fertilizer can cause poor fruiting or abnormal leaves because the crop is receiving inputs it cannot use for healthy growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii loo ebaa ni ehiii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even after I gave them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves after fertilizing often mean the plants were given the wrong nutrient mix or too much fertilizer at once, causing root stress that prevents the crop from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná niyenii ni esaaa loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo mli yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anɔ haoɔ ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I wait until I see diseases or pests on my crops before applying any treatment?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi mana hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani mikɛ tsofa ko atsu nii?

english: Preventive action is far better than waiting for symptoms. Once a disease sets in and damages the plant, simply feeding or spraying the crop may not heal the damage already done.
ga: Hela lɛ naatsii hi kwraa fe hela lɛ he okadii ni ooomɛ. Kɛ hela ba ni efite tsei lɛ Ekolɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa nɔ ni efite momo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to treat my seeds before planting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seeds acts like giving a child protective medicine. It shields the young seedling from soil-borne diseases and pests during its most vulnerable early stage of life.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsaa lɛ tamɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa ni akɛhaa gbekɛbii. Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee bei ni egbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can I spray the same insect medicine on my vegetables that I use on my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ?

english: Vegetables and trees have different tolerances. Using strong chemicals meant for cocoa on delicate crop leaves can cause severe damage and reduce your harvest.
ga: Aduawai kɛ tsei yɛ tsuishitoo srɔtoi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ tsei ahe baai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite nii waa ni eha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Will watering my crops continuously every day make them grow faster?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa gbi lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Too much water suffocates crop roots and encourages root rot. Over-watering is a common way farmers accidentally kill plants while trying to care for them.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ ji gbɛ ni okwaafoi fɔɔ nɔ amɛgbeɔ tsei yɛ oshara mli beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I let every single branch and flower grow on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa niji kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Allowing too many branches forces the plant to spread its energy too thin, resulting in small fruit. Removing extra growth focuses energy into producing bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɛ ehewalɛ lɛ eshwa fioo tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yibii lɛ faaa. Dalɛ ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Can any crop grow successfully on my land as long as I give it water and manure?
ga: Ani dumɔ nii ko baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Shii abɔ ni mikɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaha lɛ?

english: Every crop requires specific soil conditions and climates to thrive. Feeding a crop that is unsuited to your soil type will not guarantee a good harvest.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi koni ekwɛ̃. Niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni esaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa aná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens if I apply pest treatment directly to very young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and need mild, careful treatment. Full-strength chemicals meant for mature plants can scorch young leaves and kill the plant entirely.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii blɛoo ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii ni egbe tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just use my normal footsteps to measure the spacing between my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mihe ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛsusuɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he?

english: Everyone's stride length is different, which leads to uneven spacing across the farm. Using standard measuring tools like ropes or measuring tapes ensures every crop gets the exact same amount of sunlight, soil nutrients, and water.
ga: Esoro mɔ fɛɛ mɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yeee egbɔ. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe tamɔ kpãa loo tɛip ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ekwɛɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná hulu la. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why is it important to clear and level my land properly before planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing removes weeds that steal nutrients from young crops, while leveling the land keeps water from pooling in one area or washing away seeds during heavy rains.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haaa nu akabua ehe naa yɛ he kome loo ekɛ ŋmaa akafɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I mark out straight edges and lines on my farm before making planting holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makadi ŋwɛigbɛi kɛ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani mafee dumɔ bui lɛ?

english: Straight lines help you maximize space so no land is wasted. They also make it much easier to walk through the farm later to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Linei ni ja lɛ haa gbɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee he ko. Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ mli kɛya jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I determine the correct amount of fertilizer or seeds I need to buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You need to know the exact measurement of your land area first. Seed and fertilizer recommendations are given per acre or hectare, so measuring correctly prevents you from wasting money on extra supplies.
ga: Esa akɛ ole he pɔtɛɛ ni asusuɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Akɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawoi haa yɛ acre loo hectare fɛɛ hectare mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ osusu nii ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaafata he lɛ ahe.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops closer together so more fit on my land?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak plants with smaller yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: How does the distance between planting rows affect my crops?
ga: Te sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper row distance ensures adequate airflow and sunlight between plants, which reduces humidity and helps prevent crop diseases from spreading quickly.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa baa tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaaa tsei ahe helai agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do different crops require different planting distances?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ he ni amɛduɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Crops grow to different sizes both above and below the ground. Plants with large leaf canopy or wide root systems need wider spacing to mature fully without crowding.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ dalɛi srɔtoi amli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishi fɛɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ baai wuji loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ he miihia ni amɛná he ko ni mli kwɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: Why is planting in neat rows better than scattering seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting makes farm management easier, ensures every plant gets equal room to grow, and allows you to quickly spot and fix pest or weed problems.
ga: Row dumɔ haa ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jwɛi ahe naagbai oya ni osaa.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after preparing the soil or wait for the rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ?

english: It is best to plant when the soil has received good rain moisture. Planting in completely dry soil can delay seed germination or attract pests that eat the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo loo egbala kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some crops need to be grown in a small nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects tiny, fragile seeds from harsh heat, heavy rains, and pests. Once the seedlings grow strong enough, transplanting them to the main field gives them a higher chance of survival.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. Eyɛ oshara kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ dara waa bɔ ni sa lɛ Kɛ́ oya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hegbɛ kpakpa ni ekɛhi shi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tassels and silks, but some of the cobs end up completely empty without any grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii kɛ siliki lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii komɛi yɛ efolo ni dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli?

english: Maize needs pollen from the top tassels to fall onto the cob silks to make grains. Severe heat or dry weather during flowering kills the pollen before it can fertilize the silks, leaving the cob bare.
ga: Abɛi he miihia pollen kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli koni egbee ŋmeii lɛ anɔ siliki lɛ nɔ koni efee dumɔwui. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baagbe fɔfɔi lɛ dani ekɛ siliki lɛ abɔi fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ. Shi cob lɛ ni efee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my bean plants grow plenty of bright flowers, but the flowers just drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni kpɛɔ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: When bean plants get stressed by high heat, irregular rainfall, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, they drop their flowers to save energy rather than using strength to make pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ bean tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ekɛfee pods.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves, but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen fertilizer or heavy rain occurs, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking plant food before I even start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii dani mabɔi tsei dumɔ po?

english: You can spot poor soil if previous crops had stunted growth or if weeds growing on the land look pale, yellow, or very thin. A simple soil test by an extension agent is the best way to be sure.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ana nɔmimaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning pale yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged and packed tightly for the roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's harvest yield weaker plants and smaller fruits compared to buying new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahemɔ he lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties bred for a single high-yielding generation. Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their uniform vigor and produce inconsistent, weaker crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni aná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ni ebaawo tsei ni bɛ shiŋŋ, ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Do my tomato and pepper plants need bees and insects to visit their flowers to produce fruits?
ga: Ani mi tomato kɛ pepper tsei lɛ he miihia ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ayasara fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: While pepper and tomato flowers can self-pollinate through wind, visiting insects vibrate the flowers, releasing much more pollen, which creates bigger, healthier, and better-shaped fruits.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato fɔfɔi baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ moŋ. Shi kooloi bibii ni baasara lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpokpo. ni ejie pollen babaoo kpo Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adara, amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhiɛ afee fɛo.

english: Why are my young plantain suckers turning yellow and wilting when I cannot see any caterpillars or insects on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? Akɛni minaaa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ hewɔ lɛ.

english: This usually happens because microscopic pests like soil nematodes or fungal diseases are attacking the root system under the ground, preventing water and nutrients from reaching the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii waa tamɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ. Etutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn dark brown and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, shady conditions when raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do maize plants grown very close together end up with thin, weak stems and tiny ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves all the plants starving instead of thriving.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaashwere.

english: Why haven't my maize seeds sprouted even though I planted them a week ago in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds can enter a resting state called dormancy when soil is too dry. They are not dead; they are sleeping underground and waiting for rain to make conditions right for them to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ abote shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Amɛ gboko lolo. Amɛkãa shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ koni ekɛ shihilɛ ni sa aha amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Will my cowpea seeds spoil if I plant them in dry soil before the rain season starts?
ga: Ani mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ baafite kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi?

english: Good seeds have a natural ability to stay asleep underground without spoiling. They will simply rest in the dry dirt and sprout the moment the rains come to moisten the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛwɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfiteee. Amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to soak some hard seeds in water before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ dumɔwui ni wa woɔ nu mli dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Hard seeds go into a deep sleep to protect themselves. Soaking them softens their outer skin and lets them know that moisture is present, which encourages them to wake up and germinate faster.
ga: Dumɔwui ni wa lɛ gbeeɔ wɔɔ ni mli wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa amɛleɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How do dried seeds stay alive inside a bag in my room for months without growing or dying?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ahi shi yɛ kotoku ko mli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo ni amɛdaraaa loo amɛgbooo?

english: Healthy seeds go into a dormant or resting state when kept dry and cool. They remain inactive until you plant them in moist soil with the right warmth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ boteɔ shihilɛ mli, loo shihilɛ mli, kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Amɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi obaadu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually triggers a seed to start sprouting once it is in the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: A seed wakes up from its resting state when environment conditions become favorable around it—mainly getting enough moisture from rain, warmth from the sun, and air in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛ́ shihilɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hi. Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ, enine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli. hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Can the hot sun during the dry season stop my seeds from coming up?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, if the soil is too hot and dry, the conditions are unfavorable. The seed protects itself by remaining dormant underground until cooler, moist conditions return.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Dumɔwui lɛ buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛhiɔ kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some seeds in my field sprout immediately while others take weeks to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Moisture levels vary across your field, and seeds do not all wake up at the exact same speed. Each seed waits until its local soil conditions become moist enough to support growth.
ga: Humidity lɛ baasoro lɛ yɛ he ni okwɛɔ yɛ lɛ naa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ teee shi yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to sprout when I bury them very deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burying seeds too deeply deprives them of the air and light signals they need. Without those good conditions, the seeds either stay asleep or rot underground before reaching the surface.
ga: Kɛ́ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kane okadii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Kɛji shihilɛi kpakpai bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ loo amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds suddenly pop up all over my farm right after the first major rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi je kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds from last season lie dormant in dry soil for months without growing. As soon as heavy rain makes the soil wet, conditions become favorable and trigger thousands of weed seeds to sprout at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ kã shi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni shweremɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni shihilɛi lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ ni jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do weed seeds survive underground even after I clear and burn my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi dumɔwui ahi shikpɔŋ shishi beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mishã lɛ po sɛɛ?

english: Buried weed seeds enter a tough protective sleep state called dormancy. They can survive heat and dry spells deep underground until water touches them again, triggering them to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ boteɔ wɔɔhe shihilɛ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyashi nu baashɛ amɛhe ekoŋŋ. Wo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara

english: How exactly do my crops use water from the rain to feed themselves?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ nugbɔ nu tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ amɛyeɔ amɛhe?

english: Plants use their roots to draw up water from the soil, which carries dissolved nutrients up into the stem and leaves. Combined with sunlight, water provides the power plants need to create their own food and grow.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛ shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji baa kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ Kɛ akɛ hulu la fata he lɛ Nu baaha hewalɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops need water in order to benefit from the fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot absorb dry or solid fertilizer. Water must dissolve the fertilizer nutrients first so the roots can drink up that liquid mixture and send food to the rest of the plant.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ni wa. Esa akɛ nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu ni akɛfutu lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I still water my crops if it only rained a small amount today?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo pɛ ŋmɛnɛ?

english: Yes, because a light rain often only wets the top surface of the soil without reaching deep down where the crop roots are located. You should dig an inch into the soil to check if it is still dry underneath.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ efɔ shi eshɛɛɛ he ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi yɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ aaafee inchi kome koni ona kɛji egbi lolo yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster and greener during the rainy season compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rainfall provides a constant supply of moisture that keeps plant roots active and nutrients dissolved in the soil, allowing the plants to produce food continuously and build green foliage quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa be fɛɛ be ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛtsuɔ nii ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii daa ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops droop and look weak during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun gets very hot, crops lose water quickly through their leaves. They droop or curl up as a defensive behavior to reduce their surface area in the sun and conserve internal moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Amɛkotoɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe akɛ hebuu subaŋ koni amɛkɛba amɛhegbɛ lɛ shi yɛ hulu la mli ni amɛha amɛmli hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ shi gbɛkɛ.

english: How does daylight help my crops produce their food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii?

english: Green crop leaves act like little factories that use sunlight energy to turn water and air into plant food. Once daylight fades in the evening around six o'clock, this food production process stops for the night.
ga: Tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nitsumɔhei bibii. ni kɛ hulu hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsakeɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei Beni hulu lɛ laajeɔ gbɛkɛ aaafee 6 p.m. Niyenii feemɔ gbɛ lɛ hu kpaɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Can strong sunlight burn my crop leaves if there is not enough water in the soil?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã mitso lɛ baai lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Yes, water cools the plant down in hot sun much like sweating cools a person. Without enough soil water, the leaves overheat and burn, turning leaf edges brown and dry.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu haa tsei jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli hu. Kɛ latsaa ni haa gbɔmɛi feɔ fɛo. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baadɔ fe nine ni amɛbaashã. Enɛ haa baa lɛ naa tsɔɔ asarasu ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when my farm stays flooded with rain water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Does heavy rainfall wash away the food and nutrients my crops rely on?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mitsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, intense rain can wash away topsoil and dissolve nutrients, carrying them too deep into the ground or off the field before plant roots can catch them, a process known as leaching.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Ewoɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo ejɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching.

english: Why do some of my crops suddenly start flowering right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain acts as a natural wake-up signal for crops after a dry spell. The sudden intake of water triggers biological changes inside the plant that tell it it is time to reproduce by forming flowers and seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii teɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ tsakemɔi baa wala yibii amli yɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ amɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it wrong if I plant my pepper seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ pepper dumɔwui lɛ duɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients just like too many people sharing one small bowl of food. Spacing them out allows each plant to grow strong stems and yield big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Taakɛ mɛi babaoo tsɔ jaa niyenii yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa tso lɛ shishi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will feed the plant and restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha efee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rains don't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. It is best to dig a small hole near the plant stem, bury the fertilizer, and cover it with soil so rainwater doesn't carry it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni atsa bu bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afu mli, ni akɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ nu akaŋɔ lɛ kɛya.

english: What are these tiny worms eating holes inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides in the tender center leaves of corn. Inspecting your farm early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or approved pesticides early prevents major crop damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni mli tse lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long or when fungal diseases in wet soil attack the tubers. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for peak performance in their first generation only. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation crop will grow unevenly and produce much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves fold up and look tired during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ amɛ ni amɛfolɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop during hot hours as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss. As long as the soil has adequate moisture, the leaves will stand back up in the cool evening.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo egbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai lɛ teɔ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do ordinary weeds harm my crop if they are just growing nearby in the same soil?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. They also act as hiding places for harmful insects and plant diseases that can spread to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Etsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ amɛhe yɛ.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Removing extra side shoots stops the plant from wasting energy on growing excess leaves. This directs all the plant's food into producing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efiteee hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ awo tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants shed their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants often drop flowers due to extreme heat, insufficient moisture during flowering, or insect pests like thrips feeding on the young buds. Keeping the soil moist and managing early pests allows the plant to set pods successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ toɔ pods omanye.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their stalks down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called 'pegging.' Once the groundnut flower is pollinated, the stem bends and grows downward into the soil so the pod can safely develop underground away from heat and light.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fixation’ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi ŋmeii. Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni edaa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ la bɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize stretches upward to reach light instead of using its energy to develop large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni eha la abote mli.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies transmitting plant viruses, or by physical stress from extreme heat and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why does striga weed appear mostly around my maize and sorghum crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, is a parasitic plant. Its seeds lie hidden in the soil and only sprout when they detect chemical signals released by the roots of cereal crops like maize and sorghum, which they then attach to for nutrients.
ga: Striga, loo Witchweed ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Edumɔwui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛna tsofa okadii ni ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi jieɔ lɛ. ni amɛkɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why are my yam leaves turning yellow and dying early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Premature yellowing of yam leaves is usually triggered by fungal leaf spot diseases, root rot, or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Healthy yam leaves should remain green until the tubers mature near the end of the rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ji fungal leaf spot, shishifãi ni egbo loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ sweet potato baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ beni nugbɔ be lɛ baagbe naa lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or a long dry patch before the true rainy season starts. Seeds planted early may sprout and then wither away due to lack of follow-up moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ loo hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon even if it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a protective behavior. When the sun is hot, the plant rolls its leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji subaŋ ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni ebaajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does applying a lot of fertilizer cause my crop to produce thick green leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaa baa eŋɔli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in fertilizer forces the plant to focus all its energy on vegetative growth like stems and leaves, which delays or reduces flowering and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ tamɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe nii, ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo loo eba shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready for harvest without digging up all the roots?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava typically signals maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack, and the main stalk becomes thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. ni tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tso.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up when there is no drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Nitrogen helps crops stay green and grow big, so applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK early in the plant's life or spraying early against armyworms helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK atsu nii yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli. loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛjie shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ mra Ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the husks around the cob turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard when you press them with your thumbnail. You can also pull off a cob and look at the tip of the kernel where it attaches to the cob—a tiny black dot appears when the grain is completely mature.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle ehe. Kooloi lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ okɛ o-thumbnail lɛ nyɛ amɛnɔ. Obaanyɛ ojie ŋmei lɛ hu ni okwɛ ŋmei lɛ naagbee he ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ. Ayɛ ŋmeii diji bibii. Ejeɔ kpo beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my rice stalks falling over flat on the ground before the grains are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over—a problem called lodging—when you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer or plant the seeds too close together. Excess nitrogen makes the stalks grow very tall, thin, and weak, making them easy for wind or heavy rain to knock over.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi - naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lodging - kɛji okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli loo odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa waa, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shi oya.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of a widespread fungal leaf disease like Black Sigatoka or a lack of water and nutrients like potassium. Plantains need a lot of water and healthy leaves to make energy for big fruits, so cutting off diseased leaves and adding organic manure gives them the food they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ni gbɛ eshwa, tamɔ Black Sigatoka, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he miihia plantains koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha aduawai wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ tsei eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi etsu nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is too hard and compact or if the ground lacks potassium. Cassava needs loose, well-tilled soil so the roots can push outward easily and store food into thick, starchy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium lɛ, Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ oya ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the soil lacks phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps keep the flowers on the plant long enough to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing. Irregular watering is the main cause, so watering your crop on a steady schedule helps calcium move smoothly from roots to fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be ji nɔ titri ni kɛbaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni calcium lɛ aya kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves get wrinkled and curl up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that suck the nutrients out of young leaves. Spraying your peppers early with neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides controls these insects and keeps new leaves growing flat.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli Pepper ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ehaa baa heei ni daa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my farmland for other crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it directly into the soil. When you plant maize or vegetables after harvesting legumes, those crops feed on the free nitrogen left behind in the ground.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai beni okpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ Nakai tsei lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow fast at first but then completely stop growing halfway through the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkpaa dalɛ kwraa yɛ be lɛ fã mli lɛ?

english: Crops stall when they exhaust the initial nutrients in the seed or soil and run out of plant food mid-way through their life. Top-dressing your crops with extra fertilizer or compost four to six weeks after planting provides the secondary push they need to complete their growth cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shishijee niyenii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. ni tsei aniyenii baaho yɛ ewala beaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni odu lɛ, ebaaha oná hewalɛ ni ji enyɔ ni he hiaa koni ekɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Officer, how do I know if the piece of land I bought is good enough for planting cocoa?
ga: Te amralofoi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni amɛhé lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdu kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, fertile, and well-drained so water does not sit on top. It needs plenty of organic matter and should not be overly sandy or packed with hard clay, allowing roots to grow deep.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni nu akakã ŋwɛigbɛ. Ehe miihia nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli ni esaaa akɛ efeɔ ŋã tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa eyiɔ mli obɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn yellow when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees during their first two to three years to protect them while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to make extra food while the cocoa grows?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni mafee niyenii krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miida lɛ?

english: It is best to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava root systems are aggressive and steal too much water and nutrients from the soil. Plantain or cocoyam are safer shade partners for young cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tapioka ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Plantain loo cocoa haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa shweshweeshwe shihilɛ.

english: Does cocoa really need an artificial irrigation system, or can I just rely on regular rain?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛfee lɛ he miihia kookoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aloo manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: While cocoa can survive on natural rain in good seasons, dry spells and heat can kill young seedlings or cause adult trees to drop pods. Irrigation keeps soil moisture steady, protecting your harvest during dry months.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli moŋ, shi hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii loo eha tsei ni eda lɛ agbo. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ. Buu okpamɔ lɛ he yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How often should I water my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During the hot, dry Harmattan season, young cocoa seedlings should be watered at least twice a week. Keeping the topsoil moist prevents the leaves from wilting and stops the young roots from drying out.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa ni shishifãi bibii lɛ hu akagbi.

english: Why do many small flowers on my cocoa tree trunk fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbee shi ni etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks water, suffers from poor soil nutrients, or when tiny pollinating insects like midges are missing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why are you advising me to cut off the extra shoots growing near the bottom of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those bottom shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's energy and food. Cutting them off directs nutrients to the main tree stem, improving pod yield and allowing air to flow through the farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii afite. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baawo niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni pod feemɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: How many years must I wait after planting cocoa before I can expect my first harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Improved cocoa varieties in Ghana can start producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years under good management, whereas older traditional varieties typically take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ fɔɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 heɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná he ko ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ babaoo?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also creates a dark, damp farm environment that allows fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread rapidly.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ hu baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji, gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in cold, damp conditions. You can manage it by pruning overcrowded branches to let light in, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods promptly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni la abote mli, jwɛi ni ooojie, kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantain or cassava plants to protect their leaves from sunburn and to keep the soil moist while their root system develops.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo yucca mli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for dark green leaves and strong stalk growth, so applying fertilizer or organic manure helps restore leaf health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to plant on my farm for a strong yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free of pests or leaf diseases. Cut stems from the middle portion of the main stalk rather than the soft top growth or old woody base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsei ahe helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ tso wulu lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ tsei bibii loo tso momo shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade trees nearby can lower temperature stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo be mli haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to put bamboo stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso ama ŋmei tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi?

english: Yams are climbing vines that need stakes to lift their leaves into sunlight for energy. Staking also lifts foliage off the wet ground, which prevents leaves from rotting and catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ waa koni amɛha hulu la ashɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell early if armyworms are attacking my maize farm before my crops are destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male enɛ mra? Nakai cutworms lɛ tutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpata?

english: Look for small pinholes in the young leaves and a dark, sawdust-like powder inside the central tube (whorl) of the plant. Spotting this early allows you to treat the crop before caterpillars eat the growing point.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ (ring) lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni wɔkadi enɛ mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ hei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, stops water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the soil cool, prevents weed seeds from growing, and decays into nutrients over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ latsaa be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed nitrogen into the soil to support the main crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛye ebua ŋmãa titri lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for starting a new crop?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei heei ashishijee?

english: Use 'sword suckers', which have broad bases and thin, narrow spear-like leaves. They carry more plant energy and grow faster, produce larger plantain bunches, and resist pests better than 'water suckers' with wide leaves.
