ga: Kɛ 'sword shoot' ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ lɛ atsu nii. Amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni amɛdaraa oya. Woɔ plantains akui agboi ni eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ‘tso ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛ

english: What is the best time of day to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nu?

english: Water your vegetables early in the morning so plants can drink before the hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation. Watering late at night leaves foliage wet overnight, which encourages fungal leaf rot.
ga: Ha o-vegetables lɛ nu leebi koni tsei lɛ anu nu dani shwane hulu lɛ afee amɛ oya. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my crop is getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ he?

english: If leaves curl up and feel dry, your crop is thirsty. If the bottom leaves turn yellow and the soil stays muddy and smelly, the plant is drowning in too much water.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enu he akɛ egbi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji lolo ni eŋɔɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli tsɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They temporarily wilt to save water, but will recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi ebaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: What makes my crop leaves turn yellow, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving because the soil lacks food like nitrogen, or the roots are too wet to eat. Adding manure or compost helps feed the plant and make it green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ejaakɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ efɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Crops cannot eat dry food. They can only drink fertilizer once it dissolves in water, so putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni egbi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã ni efite shika.

english: Why should I prepare my land and soil food before the rains start instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ moŋ fe ni ooomɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing early allows your soil to trap the very first rains, so when you plant your seeds, they get food and water immediately and grow faster than weeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aná klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ odu dumɔwui Dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya fe jwɛi.

english: Why should I protect my crops against insects before I see big damage on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe dani amɛna nɔ ko ni efite waa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Stopping pests early prevents them from multiplying into thousands. Once insects eat most of the leaves, the crop becomes too weak to recover even if you spray medicine later.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni oookpa Mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee akpei abɔ. Beni kooloi yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehi shi kɛji okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po.

english: How do small insects cause my crop leaves to wrinkle and dry up?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi?

english: Insects suck the liquid juice out of crop leaves and can transfer sicknesses from infected plants to healthy ones, causing the leaves to twist up and die.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ hela ajɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds and dead plants away from my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei ni egboi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water and food meant for your crop, while old dead plants act as hiding spots for pests and sicknesses that will jump onto your fresh crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛtu kɛba oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my lower fruits rot when they touch the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: The ground contains tiny sicknesses that love wet soil. When plant leaves or fruits rest directly on damp soil, those sicknesses crawl inside and make them rot.
ga: Helai fioo komɛi ni sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ baai loo aduawai fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Nakai helai lɛ baakplekeshi mli ni amɛkɛ fitemɔ aba.

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for underground food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, resulting in thin plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋshii mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ tɛi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left from its oldest bottom leaves and sends it to the young top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa baai bibii amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cowpeas on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpea yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily and leaves the soil tired. Cowpeas belong to the bean family, which has a special ability to pull fresh nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil, naturalizing and restoring your land's fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi tsii yɛ niyenii he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ. Cowpeas yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Amɛyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen hee kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee adebɔɔ nɔ ni okɛba ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still small on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small organism that spreads during heavy rains and high humidity. Water droplets splash the disease from the soil or infected leaves onto the young pods, causing them to rot before they can mature.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ Black pod hela lɛ baa. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ hela kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii bibii anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Curling and pale leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease acts like a fever, weakening the plant so it cannot produce large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Hela nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atridii. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms instead of growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ tomato ni amɛduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive heat or a lack of water. The plant protects itself by dropping the blossoms because it senses it doesn't have enough water or cool conditions to support growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei buɔ amɛhe he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ nu loo shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ bɛ ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce plenty of flowers but very few actual nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Cashew flowers need friendly insects like bees to carry pollen between them before a nut can form. If there are few insects around, or if rain washes the pollen away during flowering, the flowers die without making fruit.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia ni kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo, tamɔ ŋmeii, atere pollen yɛ amɛteŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ loo nugbɔ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbo ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and break during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks and leaves store large amounts of water to stay firm and upright. When the soil becomes very dry, the plant loses water pressure inside its stem, making the heavy leaves sag and split under their own weight.
ga: Plantain tsei kɛ baai lɛ toɔ nu babaoo koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa baai ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi.

english: Is it harmful if I water my pepper garden in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-pepper abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering under hot sunshine can shock the plant roots with cold water on hot soil. Water droplets left on the leaves can also magnify the heat from the sun, scorching the foliage and losing most of the water to rapid evaporation.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛnu lɛ fa babaoo fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why must I build high soil mounds before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow down into the earth and need soft, uncompacted soil to expand. Mounds loosen the earth, improve water drainage so the tubers don't rot in soggy soil, and give the yams room to grow large and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi koni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. improve drainage Enɛ ji koni akafite ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. ni oha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot quickly if I put it directly into bags after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize still holds moisture deep inside the cobs. If sealed in bags immediately, that trapped moisture creates a warm, damp environment where mold and grain-boring insects multiply very fast.
ga: Abele ni ajie ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fung kɛ ŋmãa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests a permanent home. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha kooloi bibii lɛ ahi shi daa Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ kooloi bibii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does leaving more space between my maize plants give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ babaoo ni oooshi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and resources to develop large, full cobs instead of small, weak ones.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shi lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ tso bibioo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: Why does the savannah soil turn so hard and dry on my farm, and how does that hurt my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Savannah lɛ mli wa ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te enáa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Savannah soil loses moisture quickly under strong heat, forming a hard top crust that chokes roots and blocks water from soaking in. Covering the soil with organic mulch keeps it soft, cool, and moist for root expansion.
ga: Savanna shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Efeɔ ŋmei ko ni wa yɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaaa nu abote mli. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ organic mulch woɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Climbing supports allow the leaves to generate maximum energy, which is then sent underground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛkwɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ

english: When plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or leaf-boosting nutrients, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai muu fɛɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to heat, preventing moisture loss. If leaves uncurl when the sun sets, the plant is managing the heat stress well.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is needed to make green leaf food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure feeds the plant so leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni baa eŋɔli yɔɔ mli Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or tiny insect pests like thrips attacking the buds. Protecting the crop from pests and maintaining soil moisture keeps the flowers attached so pods can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni pods lɛ afee.

english: Is it better for me to plant my groundnuts immediately after the very first rain or wait a bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo mamɛ fioo?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady and consistent. The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can bake seeds in the soil or kill young sprouts before they establish deep roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fiofio ni ebaa shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbe tsei bibii dani amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my sorghum crop is suffering from dry weather and needs moisture?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sorghum lɛ miiye kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ aba mli?

english: Sorghum shows drought stress by rolling its leaves into tight tubes during the day to hold onto water. If the leaves stay rolled up into the cooler evening or start turning brown, the crop is dangerously short on water.
ga: Sorghum jieɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni nu lɛ ahi mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli loo amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ oshara nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no other plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni kookoo tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi lɛ Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my farmland before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this trapped nitrogen as free food to grow stronger leaves and bigger ears.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekɛwo baai ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant many seeds very close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to produce a big harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that can scorch new sprouts. Waiting until the rainy season is fully established ensures your seeds get steady water to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves high up in the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from spreading on wet leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem with a lush top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ashiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ efolo ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which part of a cassava stem is best for me to cut and plant for a new crop?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: The middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem works best because it has well-developed buds and enough stored energy to sprout strong roots quickly, unlike the soft top or woody bottom.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni edara jogbaŋŋ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ oya. Ejeee tamɔ tso bibioo loo tso shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main element responsible for leaf color and growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji nɔ titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when temperatures are too hot, water is irregular, or there are no insects visiting to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: How long does it usually take for a new plantain shoot to produce fruits that I can harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui heei baawo mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: A plantain plant typically takes between 12 to 15 months to produce a mature bunch from the day you plant a healthy sucker, depending on soil water and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ dumɔwui lɛ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛfeɔ kuu ni eda kɛjɛ gbi ni oduɔ suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Edamɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How many years can I harvest plantains from the same farm before the plants stop producing well?
ga: Plantains enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli dani tsei lɛ akpa yibii kpakpai?

english: A plantain farm usually gives good yields for about 3 to 5 years. After this time, the soil loses nutrients and the roots become crowded, so harvest sizes drop unless you replant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii baafite ni shishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ baa shi ja odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that lose water quickly in hot weather. During dry spells like the harmattan, the roots cannot find enough water in the soil, causing lower leaves to turn yellow and die to protect the main stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ Harmatta lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ koni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Can I share or give the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees to another farmer to plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ aha okwaafoi krokomɛi koni amɛdu?

english: Yes, those young shoots are called suckers. You can carefully dig up healthy shoots from the base of mature plants and transplant them to start a new farm or share them with others.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tsei ni eda lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okɛwo ŋmɔ hee mli loo okɛ mɛi krokomɛi agba he sane.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches even after growing for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigba kɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ adu lɛ be kakadaŋŋ moŋ

english: Small bunches happen when too many shoots grow around one main plantain tree and fight for nutrients, or when the soil lacks food. Cutting away excess suckers helps the main tree grow larger fruit.
ga: Kuu bibii baa kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he ni amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. aloo be mli ni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: How many young shoots should I leave around one plantain tree for the best harvest?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu kome he koni maná kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: It is best to leave only 2 or 3 shoots around the main mother plant: one medium sucker for the next harvest and one tiny one for the future. This ensures the main plant gets enough energy for a heavy bunch.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ yɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he: ŋmeii kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ ekroko hu kɛha wɔsɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to cut my plantain bunch so it doesn't spoil before I sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ plantains lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ekafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ

english: Harvest the bunch when the fruits are full and round, but still dark green. If you wait until they start turning yellow on the stem, they will ripen too quickly and rot before reaching the market.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmeii beni aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ kokroo shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Kɛ omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant plantains on the same land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very beneficial. The wide plantain leaves provide shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, keeping them cool and alive during their early stage.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: What can I do to keep my plantain crops alive when there is a long dry spell without rain?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-plantains lɛ ahi shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of the plantains with dry leaves and crop waste (mulching). This keeps the soil cool and traps moisture so the roots do not dry out quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantains lɛ shishi lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbi oya.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy weight at the top. Pests like stem borers or underground worms can also weaken the roots, making the heavy trees topple easily during rains and high winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ ashwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: How can I tell if land that has been farmed continuously for years is still good for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be afii babaoo lɛ hi lolo kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil that has been farmed continuously often gets depleted of essential nutrients. You can tell it needs rest or organic fertilizer if your crops grow thin, turn light green or yellow, or produce smaller harvests than in previous years.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa. Obaanyɛ ole kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli he miihia kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ. Tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ nɔ loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ

english: What happens to my soil if I leave a plot of land to rest for a year instead of planting on it consecutively?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ afi kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Leaving land to rest (fallowing) allows wild plants and deep roots to rebuild organic matter and replenish nitrogen, natural minerals, and moisture in the soil, restoring its fertility for future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (tillage) lɛ haa koo mli tsei kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ saa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ nitrogen mli ekoŋŋ. adebɔɔ mli shika tsuru kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu Ekɛ fɔmɔ kuɔ sɛɛ ehaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close to one another, the plants are forced to compete intensely for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of growing strong roots and fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ yibii.

english: It is safest to wait until the soil is thoroughly soaked by two or three consistent heavy rains, rather than planting immediately after the very first rain shower, which can quickly dry up and scorch your young seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi oya.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes after clearing my land or leave the cleared vegetation on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ loo mashi tsei ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving cleared leaves and weeds to decompose on the soil acts as natural mulch, keeping the ground cool, trapping moisture, and adding organic matter. Burning destroys these valuable nutrients and damages beneficial soil life.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shãa fiteɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni jara wa nɛɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop chemical fertilizer into the same hole with my seed when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ adu?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer in direct contact with a seed can burn or kill the tender young sprout before it emerges. Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away or applied after the plant has sprouted roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi loo akɛwo mli beni tso lɛ eshishifãi ebɔi shishifãi.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid crop harvest to plant again in the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield high crops only in their first generation. Replanting saved seeds from a hybrid harvest usually produces weaker plants with much smaller, uneven yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods as a survival mechanism to conserve internal water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and resume root growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaje shishifãi lɛ adalɛ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen gas from the air into the soil. This enriches the ground and acts as a natural food supply that helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii saa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and retain soil moisture, giving young cocoa the protection it needs during its first two years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hebuu ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and improves soil fertility without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which it needs to make green leaves and grow properly. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia koni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight, which encourages the underground tubers to grow large.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Weeds grow quickly and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young crops. Clearing them early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli

english: Removing small side shoots allows the plant to send its energy and nutrients directly into growing big, healthy fruits instead of producing unnecessary leaves and branches.
ga: Afã tsei bibii ni afoɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni mli wa ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee baai kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crop plants with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so you water less, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by hot dry days. If you plant too early, seeds sprout but then wither and die due to a lack of deep, continuous moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbi ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem begins to crack open as the swelling tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: How many years does it usually take for a newly planted cocoa seedling to start producing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Most modern cocoa varieties begin producing pods about 3 years after planting, provided they receive good rainfall, weed control, and basic field care.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi babaoo jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii etɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shishijee he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ

english: How do I know that a cocoa pod on my tree is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn deep orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmɔtɔi ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: How can I tell if the young cocoa seedlings I am given are healthy enough to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tsei bibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy cocoa seedlings have deep green, firm leaves, a strong single main stem, and clear roots without spots, wilting, or insect damage.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Trunk wulu kome ni mli wa. kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni egbo, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily in full sun; they require shade plants like temporary plantains to survive their early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ ephemeral plantains koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the main trunk of my cocoa tree instead of the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower and fruit on the thick wood of the main stem and major branches so the tree can physically support the weight of heavy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tso ni mli tse ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ tsei niji wuji lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects (midges); the tree naturally sheds the unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ŋmeii bibii (teŋgbɛbii) lɛ kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cocoa too close creates competition for sunlight and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak trees that produce fewer pods and spread diseases quickly.
ga: Cocoa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ feɔ tsei.

english: Why is it important for me to remove small extra shoots growing near the base of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: These extra shoots, called chupons, steal water and nutrients from the main trunk, which reduces the overall growth and pod production of the main tree.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ dalɛ kɛ pod ni ejieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some of the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Pods turn black mainly due to Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, overly damp conditions with high shade and poor air circulation.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ babaoo yɛ blackpod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Eyɛ shade ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good for growing successful cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo tsei ni yeɔ omanye lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, rich in decomposed leaves, deep enough for roots to spread, and holds moisture without staying flooded or soggy.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su ji ediŋŋ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo Emli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ shwieee nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong and stay green. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or leave the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. They need shade trees or plantain plants to shield them from the hot sun and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: How do small weeds harm my crops even when the weeds look tiny and harmless?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi bibii yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ tamɔ bibioo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he po lɛ,.

english: Underneath the soil, even small weeds have roots that quickly drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops. They steal these vital resources before your main crop can use them, which stunts plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi, jwɛi bibii po Eyɛ shishifãi ni nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛhaa onibii. Amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Enɛ baaha tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground remains soaked with standing water for too long, the roots drown, soft rot sets in, and the tubers decompose underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel or whorl of the maize plant during the day. They eat the softest inner leaves from the inside out, causing heavy damage before you see them crawling on the outer leaves.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ loo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Efiteɔ nii waa dani onaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehe miiwo kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I sow the seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in very small fruits and lower overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fɛɛ ni baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce a poorer yield than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first generation. If you plant the seeds harvested from that crop, the next generation loses its vigor, producing uneven plant sizes and fewer, smaller ears.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ dalɛi feɔ ekome, ni amɛtoi lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Extreme heat and moisture stress prevent proper pollination, causing the flowers to fall off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. ha fɔfɔii agbo

english: Why do my crops scorch and dry up when I place chemical fertilizer directly against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong mineral salts that pull water out of the plant's stem and roots if placed too close. Fertilizer should always be buried a short distance away from the stem in moist soil so the roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, fumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does swollen shoot disease move from one tree to infect other trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te bud swollen hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa swollen shoot disease is caused by a virus that is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. These insects crawl along intertwined tree branches or get carried by ants, spreading the sickness across your farm.
ga: Cocoa bud fuumɔ jɛɔ muawai ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ shwieɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ loo ŋmeii woɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Gbalamɔ hela lɛ mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I just save and plant the seeds from the fruits I buy at the market?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ aduawai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ amli ni makwɛ nɔ?

english: Market fruits are often hybrids or treated, meaning their seeds might not grow well or produce the same quality fruit. It is better to buy certified seeds from reliable agricultural suppliers to ensure a good harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji aduawai ni akɛfutu loo afee nɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ edumɔwui lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛwoŋ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe nitsulɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ koni aná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds sprout quickly while others in the same bed do not grow at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ kwraa?

english: Seeds sprout at different rates depending on their age, depth in the soil, and moisture levels. Damaged or weak seeds may fail to sprout entirely, which is why sorting seeds before planting is important.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ afii, shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni efite loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kwraa. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ahala dumɔwui lɛ dani adu lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my fruit trees during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje aduawai tsei adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Fruit trees should be planted right at the start of the major rainy season so their young roots can establish deeply with natural rainwater before the dry season begins.
ga: Esa akɛ adu aduawai tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ abote mli shɔŋŋ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nu dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even when rain fell a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: If your soil lacks organic matter like compost, it cannot hold water for long. Adding organic matter helps the soil act like a sponge, keeping moisture around plant roots between rains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, enyɛŋ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso shishifãi ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Which crops can I easily grow on my farm to feed my local chickens?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo koni mikɛha maŋ lɛ mli kooloi niyenii?

english: You can grow crops like maize, sorghum, and sunflowers, which provide rich energy and protein for chickens and help lower your cost of buying commercial feed.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ hulutsoo fɔfɔi, ni haa wuɔi lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo. ni eye ebua ni eba shika ni akɛheɔ kooloi aniyenii ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ shi

english: Is it safe to feed my pigs raw cassava harvested directly from my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã ŋmei ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ niyenii?

english: Raw cassava contains natural toxins that can upset a pig's stomach. Peeling, washing, and cooking or drying the cassava first removes these toxins and makes it safe feed.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji ni baanyɛ aha kpootoo musu afee shoo yɛ cassava ni ahoko lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei, afɔ he, ni ahoo loo agbi lɛ, ejieɔ nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ ni ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: How does putting animal manure in my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as food for both the soil and the plants. It releases slow nutrients, improves soil structure, and helps roots spread easily to absorb water.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo blɛoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛmɔ nu oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are getting too much water and cannot breathe.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ náa nu babaoo ni amɛmuɔ.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers need insects like bees to pollinate them to become fruit. High heat, lack of water, or missing soil nutrients can also cause flowers to drop off before setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwo amɛmli bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Why is it bad for my yield if I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all of them to grow tall, thin, and yield smaller harvests.
ga: adu ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and yield very little food when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete like crowded children for the same limited food, sunlight, and soil moisture. Giving each plant proper space allows its roots to spread wide and its leaves to catch sunlight, resulting in stronger plants and bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ tamɔ gbekɛbii. Amɛyiɔ amɛhe obɔ koni amɛye niyenii, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni falɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ebaa lɛ hu naa hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb toward the sun. Supporting them with stakes lifts their leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily, allowing maximum sunlight reach to feed the growing tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó amɛtso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya Enɛ haa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the cool morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã mitsei lɛ nu yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too strong. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate quickly into the air, and hot droplets on leaves can scorch the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli waa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Covering the soil—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, prevents rain from washing away soil, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the right food to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Weak soil leaves clear signs on your plants, such as pale yellow leaves, stunted growth, or thin stems. If crops take much longer than usual to mature or fail to produce good flowers, the soil is missing essential plant nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa otso lɛ nɔ, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛji tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni sa dani ekwɛ̃ɔ loo ewooo fɔfɔi kpakpai. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants suddenly showing small chewed holes and sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? Akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide deep inside the center whorl of young maize leaves. Catching them early with suitable organic or recommended treatments prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or a virus they transmit. These insects drain the plant's juices, causing leaves to warp, yellow, and stop fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, whiteflies, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛkpaa aduawai lɛ shweremɔ.

english: How can I protect my stored dry maize from being destroyed by tiny dark beetles?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ he koni ŋmeii bibii akafite lɛ?

english: These beetles (weevils) lay eggs inside dry grains. Thoroughly drying your maize to a low moisture level before storage and keeping it in airtight bags or clean, treated storage containers suffocates the pests and prevents damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ (ŋmeii) woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi mli. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi atsu nii ni okɛgbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋmãa ni he tse ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Excessive foliage growth with poor tuber formation usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, encouraging leaf growth instead of root development. Balanced soil nutrients ensure energy goes down into making big roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni tuber feemɔ ehiii lɛ baa kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa baa lɛ daa moŋ fe shishifãi ni baa lɛ. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa hewalɛ haa shishifãi wuji daa.

english: Why should I plant plantains or shade trees together with my newly transplanted cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ adu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like infants and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living umbrellas that shelter young cocoa from heat while keeping the surrounding soil cool and humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baa koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plant the nourishment it needs to stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land yield less maize when I plant it on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete against each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes them grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in much smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides essential canopy shade and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and will drink the moisture and eat up the applied fertilizer long before your crops get a chance to absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nourishment goes straight to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes are often caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep leaves of young corn plants and chews on them, especially in warm weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ

ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie niji bibii lɛ? Ni okɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tso nɔ koni amɛkwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes exposes their leaves to full sunlight, which the plant uses to generate food for growing big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ ehe baai lɛ ahe. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why should I trim off some of the tiny side shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Trimming tiny side branches directs the plant's water and nutrients directly into developing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on growing extra leaves.
ga: niji bibii ni afoɔ lɛ Afãi lɛ baaha nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ

english: Why does my cassava manage to stay green during dry spells when other crops wilt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that store water and food deep underground, allowing the plant to remain green and survive long periods without rain.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest yield less food than certified seeds from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlijalɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their genetic strength over generations and can easily carry hidden diseases. Certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist common pests and produce higher, healthier yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ fɔmɔ nii ahewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba oya. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛwo yibii ni fa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight. Direct sun burns their delicate leaves and causes them to lose water faster than their small root systems can absorb it from the ground, which is why they need shade from crops like plantains during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha nu lɛ afite oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie emli nibii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways near the topsoil rather than deep into the earth. Because the stem and leaf canopy are heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth and green color. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ adalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ehiɛ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle or horizontally instead of upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ moŋ fe ni abaatsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings have tiny buds pointing in a specific upward direction. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface while the roots fail to develop properly, leading to very low crop yield.
ga: Cassava nine lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Okadii ni yɔɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni akɛha yɛ ŋwɛi nɛɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsobii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Yam tubers usually rot in the soil due to waterlogging when rainwater cannot drain properly, or because tiny soil pests like nematodes wound the tuber, allowing destructive fungi and bacteria to enter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni amɛhiɛɔ mli lɛ hewɔ beni nugbɔ nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without producing any tomato fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely hot temperatures cause heat stress to tomato plants, which damages pollen so flowers cannot fertilize. Unfertilized flowers dry up and fall off before any fruit can start forming.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni fiteɔ pollen lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking pests such as whiteflies or aphids that transmit plant viruses. These pests feed on sap, damaging leaves and stopping healthy plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ mliki. efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ekpaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and thin when I plant seeds close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo nɛkɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly gives each stem enough room to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why do tiny beetles attack and turn my stored maize grains into dust a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji ladybugs lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ ni amɛfeɔ sũ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stored maize gets damaged by grain weevils if the corn is stored before it is completely dried. Moisture allows insects to multiply quickly and eat through the insides of the stored grains.
ga: Abele ni ato lɛ baafite kɛtsɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji akɛ ato abele lɛ dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them provides living umbrellas that protect the cocoa from excess heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaafee ŋwɛi ŋta ni baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in soil. This often happens when soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash away nutrients, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo muji loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ efo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield smaller maize harvests every year when I plant it on the same plot without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the ground, and planting the same crop continuously drains those nutrients completely. Rotating crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaakwɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I put four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɛɔ etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni akɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds properly ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains stay on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits continuously in poor-draining soil, it drowns the root system, causing bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids feeding on the sap under the leaves. Control methods, like neem oil sprays, keep these insects from damaging the growing leaves.
