ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii, thrips, loo aphids ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Tsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up pollen, preventing the flower from forming seeds. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui Kɛji pollination lɛ yeee omanye Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so the rain does not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, or split the application into smaller doses during growth. Avoid applying right before a heavy downpour, which washes the fertilizer away before roots can soak it up.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Aloo jajemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii bibii. yɛ dalɛ be mli Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground to catch maximum sunlight and improve air movement, which results in larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land during the off-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer that improves the ground for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more corn on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs instead of full, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmãa toi ni yeɔ emuu ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why are the powdery tassels at the top of my maize plants so important for my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ashikiŋsha ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: The tassels produce pollen that drops onto the silks of the developing corn ears below. Every single strand of silk must receive pollen to form a full kernel of corn on the cob.
ga: Tassels lɛ jieɔ pollen ni shwieɔ ŋmãa toi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã aná pollen koni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii toi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and prevents them from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plant finishes growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe ekwɛmɔ naa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my plants enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mitsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight away from your main crops, causing your crops to grow slow, weak, and produce low yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ daa blɛoo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Wait until the rainfall has soaked into the soil to about the depth of your finger. Planting seeds in soil that is too dry will cause the seeds to dry out and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ aaafee inchi kome. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or don't get enough water. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amɛnáaa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast before I can sell them at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and ripen after picking. Packing them tightly in hot containers or bruising them during transport damages their skin, allowing rot and fungi to destroy the fruit quickly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tsɛnsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ́ akɛmiitswa beni akɛmajeɔ lɛ, ebaafite hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii fiteɔ aduawai lɛ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time of the year to start planting cocoa on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa seedlings need steady rainfall to establish roots, so planting is best done at the onset of the major rainy season—usually around April to June in Ghana—so the young plants do not dry out.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛyashi June mli yɛ Ghana. koni tsei bibii lɛ akagbi

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers at certain months and pods at other times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees react to seasonal changes in rain and sunshine. Warm dry periods encourage the tree to produce flowers, while the following rains provide the water needed for those flowers to turn into mature pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsakeɔ yɛ be mli lɛ he nii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi. Nugbɔ ni nɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ nu ni he hiaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ ba.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange-yellow. When you tap a ripe pod, it makes a hollow sound because the beans inside have detached slightly from the outer shell.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli. Kɛ́ ota ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he lɛ Gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji baaje kpo ejaakɛ kɔfi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli fã lɛ efo fioo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does cocoa farming become so demanding around the middle of the year, like in July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi biɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ tamɔ yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Mid-year in Ghana coincides with heavy rains and peak growth. Farmers must weed, control pests, harvest early pods, and care for young plants all at the same time to prevent disease outbreaks.
ga: Afi teŋgbɛ yɛ Ghana ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Esa akɛ okwaafoi ajie jwɛi lɛ. pest control Kpamɔ tsei bibii lɛ mra ni okwɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli koni helai akaba.

english: How many years does a new cocoa seedling take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas traditional older varieties can take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune the branches of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overgrown branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree freely. This reduces humidity inside the tree canopy, stopping fungal diseases like black pod from developing.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the long dry season, and how do they behave?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli? Ni te amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During dry spells or the Harmattan season, cocoa trees try to save water by dropping some of their leaves. Without adequate shade or soil moisture, tree growth slows down and young pods may dry up.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be loo harmattan be mli lɛ, Cocoa tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi ni amɛshiɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ agbi.

english: Why do pests and pod diseases spread faster on my cocoa farm during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pod mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and cool conditions allow fungal diseases like black pod to multiply quickly, while wet weather also encourages pests to breed, making continuous farm maintenance essential during wet months.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu woɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he hiaa waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: Can I grow food crops together with cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii kɛ kookoo tsei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops like plantain or cassava with young cocoa provides necessary shade for the young plants while giving you food and income before the cocoa trees begin to yield fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava kɛ kookoo bibii ni akɛduɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: What will happen if I pick my cocoa pods before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifolɔ kookoo ŋmeii dani amɛdara kwraa?

english: Unripe pods have undeveloped beans with low sugar content. This prevents proper fermentation after harvest, resulting in poor-quality beans that fetch lower prices from buyers.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ pods ni edako lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni edako ni sugar faaa yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ehiii kwraa, ni no haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ jara baa shi.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eshwere.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing trees like plantains nearby provides protective shade that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I keep planting on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and attracts persistent pests. Rotating your maize with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore nutrients to the land naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How do weeds harm my crops even after I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from crowding your plants and spreading hidden pests or diseases across the field.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛhaa onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ anaa ni amɛkagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do insects suddenly appear and destroy my maize leaves right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest eggs hidden in the soil or surrounding weeds hatch as soon as the rains return. Checking under leaves early in the season allows you to catch and remove pests before they multiply and ruin the crop.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni ojieɔ amɛ dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce large tubers in one section of my farm but tiny ones in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ? Shi yitso lɛ ji bibioo yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to swell and expand into big tubers. Hard or packed soil squeezes the roots, preventing them from growing thick even if the plant looks healthy above ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛfuu ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without damaging either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the cassava with plenty of space and light to grow big later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Ha o-cassava lɛ gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda agbo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water to sow my seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one short shower can burn seeds if heat returns. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days to ensure seeds germinate safely.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kuku pɛ sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii fioo komɛi koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen from the soil. The plant moves food from its older bottom leaves to support the growth of fresh leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems from my tomato plants when they are growing so big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ beni amɛdara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches focuses the plant's energy into producing large, juicy fruits instead of spending power to grow unnecessary green leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni mli ewo nu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai ni wa Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can drink them in. If applied to dry soil during hot weather, the fertilizer stays concentrated in one place and can burn the roots, damaging your crop and wasting your money.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ he kome ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ oshika.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and scorch easily under direct sunshine. Taller shade trees protect the young cocoa from intense heat, reduce wind damage, and keep moisture in the soil so the seedling can survive its early years.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air circulate through your farm, drying out excess moisture and preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Extra pruning haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni etsĩ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging around one stem to check if the roots are thick and firm.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo baahi shi aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to tie yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Keeping the foliage lifted off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔi wuji baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving the plants consistent moisture around the roots and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni akɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves. Spraying early with natural neem oil or an approved pesticide stops the pests and allows fresh leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the ground quickly. It retains water, prevents weed growth, and eventually rots into rich compost that feeds your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Which type of plantain shoot is best for me to pick when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain esa akɛ mahala kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: It is best to pick 'sword suckers', which have broad bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. They grow faster, possess strong roots, and produce bigger bunches than shoots that already have wide, open leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala ‘klante ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Amɛ daa oya. eyɛ shishifãi ni wa Ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ dara fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost or NPK fertilizer early in the growing season gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why is it bad for me to burn my land before clearing it for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani ajieɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms that keep the soil fertile. Clearing weeds manually or allowing them to decay naturally adds organic food back into your soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ bo diɛŋtsɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ loo oha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli aba ekoŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my fertilizer not seem to work when I sprinkle it on top of dry soil in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ tsuuu nii kɛ́ mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can drink it, and high heat causes nitrogen to evaporate into the air. You should apply fertilizer into damp soil near the plant roots and cover it lightly with soil.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afata sũ ni mli efɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks so they grow large tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ odu ŋmei kɛjɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni onine ashɛ bulbs wuji anɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems about one meter apart gives the underground roots enough space to expand without competing with neighboring plants for soil moisture and nutrients.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and fragile. A nursery bed protects young seedlings from harsh sunlight and heavy rains so that only strong, healthy plants are transplanted to your main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛya oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dirty powder inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda muji yɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the central leaves of the plant. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays into the leaf whorl early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani efite he ni edara yɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree faces heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Planting shade trees and managing pests helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ atutua lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem varieties from agriculture officers prevents this disease and keeps your harvest high.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Fɔlɔi srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ helai ni jɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ ni okɛtsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hela nɛɛ naa ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. Placing dry grass or mulch around the plant base keeps the soil cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ wo otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and lets specific pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and stops pest buildup.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni oha kooloi komɛi abua amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ekpa kooloi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or taller forest trees, the young leaves burn, dry out, and the crop struggles to grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei kakadaji bɛ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ shãa, amɛgbiɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my garden crops wilt during the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can absorb it from the ground. Wilting is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and plants typically recover when temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash these nutrients away, or continuous farming without added organic matter can wear out the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ kɛya. Aloo okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite.

english: Why do experienced farmers say that planting beans or groundnuts improves the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that extract nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen remains behind, enriching the soil for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ ekome lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers growing from the same plantain stem compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers directs all the food energy into the main tree, resulting in much larger bunches.
ga: Tsei bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa kuu ko ni da kwraa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden sticks instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa he ni agbele lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight and good airflow to feed the tuber underground. Raising the leaves on stakes prevents them from rotting on wet soil and ensures maximum sunlight reaches the leaves to build larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. ni ehaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before any small tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, prolonged drought, or sudden changes in water supply. When stressed, the plant sheds blossoms to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa Kɛ haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is prolonged heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air within the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot under the surface.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing smaller than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects that stunts normal foliage growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa baa lɛ daaaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small ragged holes in the leaves and dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni muji yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Ragged leaf holes paired with sawdust-like waste inside the center whorl indicate Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip of young maize and chew through leaves before they unfold.
ga: Baai amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ sũ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ ebɔ he lɛ tsɔɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do insects suddenly appear in huge numbers on my farm even when I didn't see them last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo eba trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni minaaa amɛ otsi kome ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Pests can lay hundreds of eggs that hatch all at once when the weather becomes warm and humid. A small population can multiply rapidly in just a few days if conditions are right.
ga: Kpluka nɛɛ baanyɛ awo wɔji ohai abɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Gbii bibii baanyɛ afɔ́ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli kɛji shihilɛi lɛ ja.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different pest sprays together in my knapsack to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baafutu yɛ misɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing different chemicals without expert guidance can be dangerous. Certain chemicals react negatively when combined, which can destroy their effectiveness, damage your crops, or create harmful fumes.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛji ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe wo mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. ni baanyɛ afite nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ afite onibii loo ekɛ lasu ni yɔɔ oshara aba.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical spray to put in my water so I don't ruin my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mi nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ ni sa? koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Every chemical has a specific measurement ratio. Using too much spray can burn leaf tissues and poison the soil, while using too little will fail to kill the pests.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baa lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛ tsofa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I get overwhelmed by work and pause my weeding for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ mihe wo nitsumɔ mli ni mikɛ otsii fioo komɛi he hejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ migbalashihilɛ lɛ mli?

english: Pausing work gives weeds room to grow tall quickly. Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and water from your crops, which weakens the plants and reduces your final harvest.
ga: Hejɔɔmɔ be kukuoo ko haa he ko ni nɔ kwɔ baa oya kɛha jwɛi. Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What should I do if I notice different kinds of pests attacking my farm at the same time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi? Ba ni obatutua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Different pests require different solutions; a chemical meant for caterpillars might not work on sap-sucking insects. You need to identify each pest type first so you can apply the correct targeted treatment.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ tsabaa sɔrɔto. Ekolɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ oyɔse tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eko fɛɛ eko dani okɛ tsofa ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply pest spray on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening. Strong afternoon sunshine can cause the spray to evaporate too quickly or burn wet crop leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eshã tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Should I spray my crops before I see any insects, or wait until they start damaging the leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani mana kooloi bibii lɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛbɔi baai lɛ afitemɔ?

english: It is usually best to inspect your farm regularly and spray at the first sign of pests. Waiting too long allows pests to multiply, while spraying unnecessarily wastes money and can harm good insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ kɛji ona tsɛŋemɔ helai klɛŋklɛŋ okadi. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ shika ni he ehiaaa, ni ebaanyɛ eye kooloi kpakpai awui.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops starting to curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are common signs that tiny pests are sucking the juices from under the leaves, or that the crop is lacking essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe. Nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it risky to plant the same type of crop on the exact same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the land.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do my skin and eyes feel irritated after I finish spraying my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihewolo kɛ mihiŋmɛii nuɔ he akɛ mihe ejɔ mi beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Pesticide mist can easily blow back onto your body or absorb through your clothes. Always wear protective gear like long sleeves and a mask, and wash thoroughly with soap immediately after spraying.
ga: Abaanyɛ atswa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ amli nu lɛ aku sɛɛ awo gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli loo atsɔ atadei amli atsɔ mli oya. Wo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ nine kakadaŋŋ agboi kɛ mask be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛ samla afɔ he jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ efɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there is no shade above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shields them from extreme sun, keeps the soil cool, and helps them retain moisture.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage causing waterlogged roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or organic manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs plenty of sunlight on its leaves to produce big tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the wet ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni eshɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛfee bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni etsiɔ baa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Removing excess shoots, called suckers, leaves only 2 or 3 strong stems per plant. This prevents the shoots from stealing water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso kome mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain lɛ da ni etsii.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo beni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating the tender leaves inside the middle whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel and chew on young leaves, which can stunt or kill the maize plant if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ afee shoo loo egbe amɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests helps keep new leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu mi-veggies lɛ kɛ jwɛi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Spreading dry grass on top of the soil, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds very close to each other in the same farm bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows strong and produces a full yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: What does pollination actually do for my cocoa trees, and why is it important?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ pollination yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Pollination is how cocoa flowers turn into actual cocoa pods. When pollen is moved from one flower to another, it fertilizes the flower so it can grow into a healthy pod filled with cocoa beans instead of just falling off.
ga: Pollination ji he ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi. Kɛji akɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli lɛ, Akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni kookoo ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbee shi

english: Why are my cocoa trees flowering very well but not producing many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ shi amɛfɔfɔi babaoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers need to be pollinated by tiny insects or by hand to set pods. If there are not enough pollinators on your farm, the flowers dry up and fall off without forming cocoa pods, leading to a low harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen. aloo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ ni okɛto ŋmeii lɛ ahe Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: How does hand pollination work on a cocoa farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Hand pollination involves using simple tools like tweezers to manually transfer pollen from a male part of a flower to a female part, ensuring that specific flowers successfully fertilize and grow into pods.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he ji ni akɛ dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tweezers atsu nii ni akɛ niji ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli kɛya yoo lɛ fã lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi komɛi aye omanye yɛ fɔmɔ mli ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Can pollinating too many flowers on my cocoa tree hurt or weaken the tree?
ga: Ani pollination babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye tso lɛ awui loo ebaagbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, if a cocoa tree carries more pods than its roots and soil nutrients can support, it becomes exhausted and weak. You must preserve the health of the tree by only pollinating what the tree can safely carry.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe shishifãi ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ. Kookoo tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Esa akɛ okwɛ otso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nɔ pɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ atere shweshweeshwe lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ.

english: Where do natural pollinators come from, and how can I keep them on my cocoa farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã amɛhi kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Natural pollinators for cocoa are tiny midges that live in moist, shady places with damp organic matter like decomposing cocoa husks or plantain stumps. Keeping shade and mulch on your farm helps them live and multiply.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni hiɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo loo plantain tsei. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ha amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: What steps should I take if my cocoa farm consistently yields a very poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni ehiii kwraa be fɛɛ be?

english: A poor harvest often comes from poor pollination, lack of nutrients, or pests. You can improve your yield by introducing artificial hand pollination, maintaining tree health, and getting advice from an extension officer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ehiii baa ji pollination ni ehiii, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai. Obaanyɛ okɛ fɔfɔi ni okɛ oniji aaawo mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ ni onine ashɛ ŋaawoo nɔ kɛjɛ hiɛyaa he nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ

english: How do I choose which cocoa trees on my farm are best suited for hand pollination?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Select strong, healthy cocoa trees that show good resistance to diseases like Black Pod and have sturdy stems. Pollinating healthy trees ensures they can carry the heavy load of pods without breaking or dying.
ga: Halamɔ kookoo tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɛɛ amɛye, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛbui lɛ amli muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni amɛkuuu loo amɛgbooo.

english: Who can I reach out to if I don't know how to find or carry out pollination on my farm?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mileee bɔ ni mafee mana loo mafee pollination yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: You can contact your local Agricultural Extension Officer or local trained pollination services in your community. They can teach you the technique directly or connect you with trained pollinators.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaafoi akuu lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo pollinator nitsumɔ ko ni atsɔse lɛ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔɔ bo ŋaa gbɛi tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛkɛ bo kɛ pollinators ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ abɔ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off the tree within a few days of blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers only stay open for a short time. If they are not pollinated by insects or by human hands within 24 to 48 hours, the plant drops them because they cannot develop into fruit.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ be kukuoo pɛ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo gbɔmɛi kɛ amɛhe wooo mli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli lɛ, tso lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ enyɛŋ etsɔ aduawai.

english: Is hand pollination something young men and women in our community can learn to do as a job?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni oblahii kɛ oblayei ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akase ni amɛtsu akɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, hand pollination requires careful handling and good eye contact with tiny flowers. Young men and women can easily be trained in this skill to assist farmers and increase community cocoa production.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ kɛ hiŋmɛii ni akɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. Oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ aná tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋaa nɛɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛha kookoo ni amɛfeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ amɛ akutsei lɛ amli.

english: How long do I usually have to wait after planting cassava before it is ready to harvest and sell?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ?

english: Cassava typically takes between 9 and 12 months to reach full maturity. If you harvest too early, the tubers will be small and watery, but waiting until the full year gives you bulky, high-quality tubers that attract good market prices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Kɛji okpa mra tsɔ Yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni nu yɔɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha oná tsɔnei wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jara kpakpa yɔɔ jara nɔ.

english: How does a single seed maize grain manage to produce so many new grains on a cob?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa kome pɛ aaawo ŋmãa heei babaoo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: A planted seed uses water, soil nutrients, and sunlight to grow a tall stalk that forms cobs. Each cob contains hundreds of new seeds, allowing a single planted grain to multiply your initial investment many times over by harvest time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni haa tsei kakadaji ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Dumɔwui heei ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwu kome ni adu lɛ haa shika ni okɛwo mli shishijee lɛ feɔ shii abɔ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my yield if I harvest my crops at six months instead of waiting a full year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ afi muu fɛɛ?

english: Harvesting at six months often yields immature crop tubers or small fruits because the plant is still building its structure. Waiting the full growth period allows the plant to complete its storage cycle, giving you full weight and maximum yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 6 mli lɛ haa anáa ŋmeii loo aduawai ni edako kwraa lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei miitswa tsũi lolo. Be ni tso lɛ daa lɛ fɛɛ ni aaamɛ lɛ haa egbeɔ enitoohe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa onáa muji fɛɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my six-month-old crops not producing fruits yet like my neighbor's one-year-old plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ ni eye nyɔji enumɔ lɛ wooo yibii tamɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni eye afi kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops go through distinct age stages; during the first six months, plants focus all their energy on building strong roots and stems. Fruits and harvestable parts only develop after the plant reaches its full physiological maturity, usually around a year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shihilɛ mli shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa amamɔ nɔ. Beni tso lɛ egbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni anáa yibii kɛ fãi ni akpa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee afi.

english: If I plant 10 healthy suckers this year, how many new plants can I expect to get from them for next season?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui 10 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afi nɛɛ, tsei heei enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: As crops like plantain or banana grow over a year, each parent plant naturally produces multiple stems or offspring. Ten healthy plants can easily generate 30 to 40 new suckers by the end of the year, expanding your farm size automatically.
ga: Beni tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afi mli. Tso fɛɛ fɔlɔ tso baawo ŋmeii loo seshii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei nyɔŋma ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii heei 30 kɛyashi 40 kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee. Ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli alɛɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my tubers so buyers won't reject them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? koni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ akakpoo.

english: Crops indicate market readiness through visible signs such as yellowing leaves and firm, full-sized underground tubers, which usually happens near the end of their full growth cycle. Selling prematurely results in soft tubers that spoil quickly in the market.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esaa ehe kɛha jarayeli kɛtsɔ okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni dalɛ fa babaoo lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni ebɛŋkɛɔ shweremɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ mra lɛ haa tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How does planting one piece of yam turn into a bigger tuber over the season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: The planted yam seed provides initial energy for vines and leaves to grow above ground. Throughout the growing season, these leaves catch sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to swell and form a larger tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui ni adu lɛ haa wain tsei kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishijee hewalɛ. Yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, baa nɛɛ naa hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efuɔ ni efeɔ ŋmei agbo ko yɛ shishi.

english: Why must I plan my farm budget around a full year cycle instead of expecting quick money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato miŋmɔ mli shika he gbɛjianɔ daa afi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makpa shika oya gbɛ lɛ?

english: Most food crops require several months of field growth and care before generating any financial return. Planning your budget for a full year ensures you can cover farm upkeep during the long growing months before harvest income comes in.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ nyɔji babaoo ni akɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛná shika. Shika he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he nii yɛ nyɔji kakadaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Is it possible to increase my harvest volume without buying double the land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni miheɔ lɛ ebɔko he shii enyɔ?

english: Yes, by allowing your current crops to reach full age maturity and using good management practices, each plant will naturally yield its maximum weight and produce seeds or multiplication stems you can replant progressively.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ni oooha amɛdara kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Tso fɛɛ tso baawo muji ni fe fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaawo dumɔwui loo ŋmeii kɛha shweremɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I plant some crops early in the season and others later in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei komɛi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli, ni madu ekrokomɛi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting dates creates crops of different ages across your field, meaning you won't have to wait a full year for everything at once and can harvest produce continuously at different times.
ga: Gbii ni akɛduɔ nii ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani odu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa nibii ni anáa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ bei srɔtoi amli

english: Can I plant my cocoa trees on land that has a lot of rocks and stones?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, land that is stony or rocky should not be used for cocoa farming. The rocks prevent cocoa roots from growing deep, and the soil cannot provide the nutrients the crop needs to yield well.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ kookoo. Tɛ lɛ tsiɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ shɔŋŋ. ni sũ lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ aha.

english: Why is stony ground bad for growing cocoa compared to regular soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Stony ground holds very little moisture and nutrition for plants. Additionally, rocks absorb and radiate heat from the sun, which creates a harsh environment for cocoa roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei yeɔ nii fioo pɛ yɔɔ tɛi ashishi. Kɛfata he lɛ, tɛi lɛ gbalaa dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli wa baa kookoo shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know what kind of land to avoid when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ni esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he kɛji mije kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should completely avoid plots with heavy gravel, stones, or exposed rock formations. Cocoa needs deep, soft soil where its taproot can easily reach groundwater and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa shikpɔji ni ŋmeii, tɛi loo tɛi wuji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ kwraa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he ni taproot lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia Cocoa.

english: Can I clear the surface rocks off a stony piece of land to make it good for cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tɛsaa lɛ hiɛ koni mafee kookoo kpakpa?

english: It is still not recommended. Even if you clear the top rocks, stony ground beneath the surface continues to retain extreme heat and lacks the deep, fertile soil required for cocoa to thrive.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa lolo Kɛji ojie tɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ po. Shi shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. ni ebɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni he hiaa koni kookoo akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How does hot sun affect cocoa trees growing on rocky soil?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛsaa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When strong sunlight beats down on rocky ground, the rocks heat up like hot coals. This excessive heat stresses the cocoa trees, causing them to struggle, wilt, or fail to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tswa tɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tɛ lɛ baadɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine nɛɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, loo amɛdaraaa kwraa.

english: Does direct sunlight harm cocoa plants differently depending on the soil type?
ga: Ani bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ kookoo tsei anɔ awui lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, direct sun causes far more damage on stony land because the rocks heat up quickly and stay hot, whereas soft, deep soils stay cooler and protect the roots from heat stress.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ nii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ tɛi lɛ mli dɔɔ oya ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa crops seem to struggle more during the dry and sunny season on certain parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cocoa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Areas of your farm with stony or rocky soil overheat quickly under intense sun, making it very difficult for the roots to absorb water and keep the crop healthy.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni shikpɔŋ loo tɛi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ waa oya yɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there any safe treatments I can apply to my farm that will definitely not harm my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ekã shi faŋŋ akɛ eyeŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, gentle soil enrichers like well-rotted organic compost or mild soil conditioners can be applied safely without any danger of damaging or burning your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo blɛoo, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe ni oshara ko bɛ he akɛ ebaafite loo ebaashã otsei lɛ.

english: How can I be sure that a soil application won't burn or destroy my cocoa plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ sũ ni mikɛfataa he lɛ shãŋ mi-cacao tsei lɛ loo ekpataaa amɛhiɛ?

english: Using completely safe, non-toxic organic inputs or recommended natural soil amendments ensures your crops get nurtured without any risk of chemical damage.
ga: Akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni bɛ awui loo shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ ni tsofai ni baafite lɛ akafite.

english: Is it possible to improve my soil's condition without risking the safety of my existing crops?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ashweshweeshwefeemɔ wooo oshara mli?

english: Yes, using harmless soil applications allows you to improve soil quality and plant health without exposing your crops to harsh side effects.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ awui ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni oha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni okɛ naagbai ni mli wawai ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds during the first month after planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni adu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Adding extra chemical nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant grow excessive leaves instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa kroko ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to plant without using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without turning into stagnant mud, and contains beneficial earthworms and insect life.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efeee klon Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by a leaf-curl virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii yɛji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my yam seed setts to rot in the soil before sprouting?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in poorly drained soil that retains too much water, or when fungal pests enter fresh cuts on the seed piece that were not properly dried or treated with wood ash.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ bote dumɔwui bibii ni agbiko jogbaŋŋ loo akɛ tso sũ tsu nii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing stem and leaves rather than fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and watery instead of growing big and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛfee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small and watery if harvested too early, grown in waterlogged soil, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient needed to convert sunlight into thick root starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ mra tsɔ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛtsake hulu la ni etsɔ shishifãi ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold or droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop or fold during hot afternoons to reduce sunlight exposure and conserve internal water. It is a natural protection mechanism against drought and extreme sun.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is even ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in an upside-down 'V' pattern, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize every year if I keep planting it in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly and look weak whenever weeds are growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink up the water and eat the soil food before your crop roots can reach them, while also blocking sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ hu naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and wither when the dry Harmattan wind begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly under dry winds and full sun, which is why they need shade crops like plantain to protect them during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni cocoa tsei he hiaa ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers and young fruit when they experience heat stress or sudden dry spells as a natural way to save water and keep the main plant alive.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ ni ahaa tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young green tomatoes turning soft and black on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the crop cannot move enough calcium from the soil to the fruit, usually caused by irregular soil watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above the ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen without enough potassium in the soil, it spends all its energy growing leafy branches instead of swelling its roots underground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together so I have more plants on my farm, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ, tsei babaoo baahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo fe nakai?

english: When crops are crowded together, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and poor individual yields rather than a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ yibiiwoo ehiii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakpa babaoo lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea flowers bloom nicely but fail to form full pods of beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ̃ fɛfɛo shi amɛmiikwɛɛɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like thrips or pod borers often attack cowpea flowers and young pods, causing the blossoms to fall off before healthy seeds can grow inside.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo pod borers Bei pii lɛ, amɛtutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ pods bibii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots in the barn before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up from their resting period after a few months, using their own stored energy to grow new shoots when exposed to warm air.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii heei kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer can restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small and twisted when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards easily. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to push through the ground, resulting in stunted and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Ewa akɛ aaatsi yitso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the centers of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?
