english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the leaf whorl of young maize. Treating the crop early with recommended biological or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baai amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ wala yibii loo tsofai ni akɛba lɛ nɔ lɛ atsĩɔ naa koni ekafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look crumpled, twisted, and covered in yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf distortion is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this infection.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli tsakemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide the living shade and moisture shade young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves them with thin, weak stems and small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat or water stress. The plant aborts the blooms to conserve water and energy so it can survive the hot or dry spell.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Tsei baafo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli.

english: How does leaving dried leaves on top of my soil help my vegetables grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, and blocks weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for my land if I plant cowpeas after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmãa beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the soil, refreshing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my dry maize grains turn into white powder after staying in the storehouse for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow inside the dry corn to feed and reproduce, leaving behind powdery waste. Storing thoroughly dried grain in airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates the insects and protects the harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛfɔ. kɛtsɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ nɔ Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli lɛ baaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce so many tall branches and thick leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ waa kɛ baai ni mli wa shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in heavy shade, it uses all its energy to grow top leaves and stems instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and bunching tightly at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbua amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted and bunched leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the sap, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rain when the farm is too shaded, wet, and lacking good air movement.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Okwaafoi lɛ amli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl inward during the hot part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up in strong afternoon heat as a natural defense to conserve water and reduce exposure to the hot sun; they usually relax when temperatures cool down.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ni akɛbuɔ nu he ni akɛbaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain suckers dry up and turn brown rapidly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miigbi oya ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: While older bottom leaves naturally dry up over time, rapid drying on young suckers indicates the plant is suffering from dry soil, heat stress, or a lack of potassium.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ baai bibii ni edara lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ. Shi ŋmeii bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina shikpɔŋ ni egbi. hulutsoo he haomɔ loo potassium ni faaa

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers dropping off without developing into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not receive enough water, lack key soil nutrients, or when sucking pests like mirids damage the delicate flower stems.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni aŋɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ awo mli koni efite fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of flowers but very few actual bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of pollinators like bees, or insect pests feeding on flower blossoms can cause the flowers to fall off before forming pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nibii ni haa fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi Ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall over easily when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak and fall over (lodge) when plants are sown too close together, lack strong root support, or are damaged internally by stem borer insects.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi (ejeɔ kpo) kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Shishifãi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni wa ni bɛ loo enine eshɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ nɔ kɛjɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ

english: Why are my newly sprouted yam vines growing very slowly and failing to climb the stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ miida blɛoo waa ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Slow yam vine growth happens when the seed yam piece planted was small or diseased, or when the mound soil is too dry and hard for roots to spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso lɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ji bibii loo hela emɔ amɛ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni ewa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves roots sitting in too much water.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo ehaa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and turn hard during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from severe sun and prevent water loss. However, if the curling stays constantly dry and crusty, it is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Shi, kɛji akɛ tsitsii lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Yams grow deep under the ground and need loose, soft earth to expand into large tubers. High mounds give the roots room to stretch easily and keep heavy rains from surrounding the seed and rotting it.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ shwereɔ oya. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baabɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ naa ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akagbo

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which takes invisible plant food from the air and stores it in the soil. When grown with or after maize, groundnuts naturally fertilize the dirt for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ tsei aniyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa loo yɛ esɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells or extreme heat, saving their energy to survive. Tiny sap-sucking insects can also damage flower stems and cause them to fall off early.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. ni haa hewalɛ baa koni ekɛhi wala mli yɛ kooloo bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ efite fɔfɔii ashishifãi hu ni eha amɛgbee shi oya.

english: Why is my oil palm tree growing very tall but only bearing a few small fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms need plenty of direct sunlight, water, and soil nutrients like potassium to form heavy fruit bunches. If planted too close together or facing drought, the tree spends its energy growing tall instead of making fruit.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii tamɔ potassium koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛ hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits as soon as they start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Young pepper fruits drop when soil water fluctuates too sharply between very wet and very dry, or when high temperatures prevent proper pollination of the blossoms.
ga: Chili yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni egbi waa teŋ. aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the dirt before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when rainwater pools around the base of the plant without draining away properly. Damp, heavy soil allows microscopic soil fungus to enter and soften the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli efɔ lɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni anaa lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn dry and brown from the bottom up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baa lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants drop their lower leaves naturally during dry spells to cut down on water loss through the foliage, concentrating moisture in the center stem so the plant can survive the heat.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baajɛ amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ ashwie shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi Ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stay small and weak even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive competitors that drink up fertilizer and groundwater much faster than young crops can, effectively starving your plants of light and nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ la kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my crops are not growing well, how do I know if the problem is my soil or something else I am doing wrong?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ hu? Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ naagba lɛ ji shikpɔŋ lɛ loo nɔ kroko ni mifeɔ ni ejaaa?

english: Poor crop growth is not always caused by bad land. It often comes from planting at the wrong time, improper spacing, or lack of shade. Checking for pests and observing soil texture can help you figure out if the land needs fertilizer or if your farm management needs to change.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ehiii baa. Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ mli baa. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni esaaa loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ehe miihia ni atsake bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa.

english: Can poor land be fixed, or do I need to abandon my farm and find a new piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔ lɛ ni mayatao shikpɔŋ hee?

english: You rarely need to abandon land. Degraded soil can be improved by applying organic manure, planting cover crops like mucuna, and practicing crop rotation to restore essential nutrients.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Abaanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mucilage kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ koni akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I plant fast-growing crops like plantains before putting my primary seedlings into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains dani mikɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting plantains first is very helpful. They grow quickly and provide essential shade and moisture, creating a safe canopy for delicate young seedlings like cocoa or coffee before they face harsh sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa waa. Bɔɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aha dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo loo kɔfe. Dani ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baakpe

english: Why do some farmers plant food crops alongside young trees instead of planting only the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ niyenii yɛ tsei bibii ahe moŋ fe tsei lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting food crops alongside young tree crops maximizes land use, provides food and income while you wait for the trees to mature, and keeps the soil covered to reduce weeds.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo. Ha niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ. ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I stop stray goats from entering my field and eating my young plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi ni elaaje lɛ anaa koni amɛkaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛye mitsei bibii lɛ?

english: Goats love tender young leaves. You can protect your farm by building living fences with fast-growing shrubs, fencing with local materials like bamboo, or keeping free-roaming animals tethered during the growing season.
ga: Tooi sumɔɔ baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni ooofee ni tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ fĩɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Is it safe to let my household livestock roam freely on my farm after planting?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha mishia kooloi lɛ ayashara shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛye amɛhe beni amɛdu nii sɛɛ?

english: No, domestic animals like goats and sheep will quickly destroy young sprouts and compact the soil with their hooves, which harms root growth and lowers crop yields.
ga: Dabi, shia kooloi tamɔ tooi kɛ tooi fiteɔ tsei bibii oya ni amɛkɛ amɛnaji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ awui ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to inspect my crops for early problems?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛji naagbai komɛi yɛ mli mra?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week. Inspecting crops early helps you catch animal damage, pests, and leaf yellowing before the damage spreads across the entire farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kooloi ni efite, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani nibii ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How long does it usually take after trying a new planting method to know if it is working?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛji aka gbɛ hee ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ akwɛ kɛji etsuɔ ​​nii?

english: Most crops show signs of improvement within 3 to 4 months through greener leaves, faster growth, and sturdy stems, though full harvest benefits are best measured over a full season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jieɔ hiɛyaa he okadii akpo yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hewɔ. oya kɛ tso ni mli wa Eyɛ mli akɛ asusuɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli baa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend new techniques instead of the traditional ways we learned at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kɛ ŋaai heei baa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookase kusum gbɛ lɛ yɛ shia lɛ?

english: Traditional methods work well, but improved techniques are designed to help crops withstand modern challenges like unpredictable weather, reduced soil fertility, and new agricultural pests.
ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi afee ŋaai ni atsake lɛ koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛdamɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ naagbai tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ anaa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛ okwaayeli mli tsɛŋemɔ helai heei

english: If I have been farming the same way for over ten years, why should I change my planting methods now?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma etsu okwaayeli he nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ matsake gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mitsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ bianɛ?

english: Over a decade, rainfall patterns change and land loses natural nutrients. Updating your methods allows you to harvest more food from the same size of land with less effort.
ga: Yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ tsake ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ fo. Gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ nii lɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become tough and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long to grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ koni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil past its maturity age causes useful starch to turn into hard fiber. Just like over-aged animals lose meat quality, over-matured crops spoil in quality and taste even if they look bigger.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa. Agbɛnɛ hu, kooloi ni edara lɛ loo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda moŋ

english: How do I know the exact time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Maize is ready when the leaves turn dry brown and a dark spot appears at the grain base. Leaving ripe maize in the field exposes it to mold, insects, and decay, reducing your harvest quality.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi ni ŋmɔtɔ diji je kpo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛko yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmei aba. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, bɔ ni okpaa nii lɛ hi ha lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it true that leaving my ripe tomatoes on the stem longer makes them better for the market?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ ashi tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli?

english: No, over-ripe tomatoes become soft, crack open, and attract pests quickly. Harvesting at the right stage ensures firm fruits that survive transport and sell for a better price.
ga: Dabi, tomato ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya, egbɛɔ ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ aduawai ni wa lɛ yaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: What happens if I put too much chemical fertilizer on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo fata mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Excess fertilizer, especially nitrogen, causes plants to produce lots of leaves but drop their flowers and fruits. Over-feeding damages crop health just like improper feeding affects livestock.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine, titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Niyenii ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii ni esaaa ni akɛhaa lɛ saa kooloi ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and cracked even when the vines look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni egbɛ eshwa eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Big leaves only mean the plant got leaf-building nutrients. Tubers need balanced soil nutrients like potassium to develop full weight and smooth skin without cracking.
ga: Baai wuji tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naa niyenii pɛ ni ekɛfeɔ baai. Tubers he miihia sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ potassium, koni enyɛ eshɛ etsitsinɔnii fɛɛ kɛ ehewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etseee.

english: How does feeding my soil with compost make my vegetables look better to buyers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ mi-aduawai lɛ afee fɛo?

english: Compost feeds crops slowly with balanced nutrients, producing vibrant leaves and firm fruits that look healthy and stay fresh longer in the market.
ga: Kompost haa tsei niyenii fiofio. kɛ niyenii ni ja Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ kɛ aduawai ni wa ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves show that the plant lacks basic soil nutrients or proper water balance. Good soil feeding restores leaf strength so the plant can produce strong fruits.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni sa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebaa lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pod disease spreads when cocoa trees lack proper care, shade control, and field cleanliness. Regular upkeep keeps the pods healthy, glossy, and disease-free.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ akwɛɛɛ kookoo tsei jogbaŋŋ. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hetsemɔ Hekwɛmɔ daa haa ŋmeii lɛ anáa hewalɛ, amɛkpɛɔ ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Blossoms drop when crops face stress from poor soil feeding or heat. Proper feeding and soil moisture keep plants healthy so flowers turn into good produce.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo dɔlɛ mli. Niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi bafeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches instead of full heavy fingers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ niji ni eyi obɔ ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Thin bunches happen when the plant does not get enough soil nutrients during its early growth stage. Giving the plant good nutrition early gives it energy to bear heavy, well-formed bunches.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli. Niyenii kpakpai ni akɛaaha tsei lɛ mra Enɛ baaha oná hewalɛ ni okɛná jwɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ shihilɛ kpakpa mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers keep coming out small even when I plant a very big seed yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ sweet potato ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli waa lɛ?

english: When you plant a very large yam whole, the plant often spends energy sustaining the old seed tuber rather than forming new, large tubers. Using proper seed cutting techniques or improved setts ensures energy goes directly into producing a bigger and heavier harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okwɛ sweet potato tso muu ko ni da waa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Tsei yeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui ayitsei momo lɛ anɔ. Yɛ yitso hee agbo ko ni ooofee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Dumɔwui afolɔ gbɛi ni sa loo gbɛjianɔtoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha hewalɛ lɛ aya ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I multiply my seed yams so that one single yam gives me many new tubers for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei kome baanyɛ awo ŋmeii heei babaoo ni adu?

english: By cutting a healthy seed yam into smaller pieces called minisetts and treating them properly, each piece will sprout into a new plant. This technique allows a single parent yam to yield up to ten new seed tubers for the next season.
ga: Kɛtsɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooofo mli bibii bibii lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ minisɛt. ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Efã fɛɛ fã baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso hee. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmei kome feɔ dumɔwui heei yitsei ni shɛɔ nyɔŋma kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: No, seed size alone does not guarantee a big harvest. Soil fertility, proper planting depth, and adequate moisture have a much bigger impact on whether your final harvest turns out small or large.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ pɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ abaakpa nii babaoo. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo yɛ kɛji onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ ji bibioo loo agbo.

english: How can I prevent my planted yams from producing small, low-value harvests season after season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekawo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni jara waaa yɛ be mli lɛ?

english: To avoid small harvests, refresh your soil through crop rotation, use healthy seed setts from improved crop varieties, and ensure proper field spacing so each plant gets enough nutrients to grow large tubers.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akpa ŋmaa bibioo lɛ Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ jɛmɛ bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are improved crop varieties able to yield so much more than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are bred to absorb soil nutrients more efficiently and resist common local diseases, allowing a single planted sett or seed to multiply and produce a much higher total yield.
ga: Abaaha ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwu kome ni adu lɛ baanyɛ ashwere ni ekɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why do new crop varieties introduced in our area sometimes grow differently than local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛbaa wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: New varieties are developed with specific growth habits, such as stronger root systems or different tuber formation patterns, which cause them to feed and develop differently in the soil compared to older local crops.
ga: Afeɔ tso henɔi heei ni yɔɔ dalɛ sui pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ shishifãi ni mli wa loo tuber feemɔ gbɛi srɔtoi. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ niyenii ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety will perform well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii heei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: New crop varieties recommended by extension officers are tested for local climate and soil conditions, but following proper planting spaces and land preparation ensures they reach their high-yield potential.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha. Shi dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ nifeemɔi ni sa baaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do some high-yielding crops take longer to mature before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ lɛ?

english: High-yielding varieties often spend extra time building strong foliage and root systems underground to feed the tubers, which slightly delays harvest time but results in a much larger overall harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ heɔ be kroko ni amɛkɛmaa baai ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni baaye abua bulb lɛ. Enɛ baaha kpamɔ be lɛ asɛɛ afo fioo. Shi nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo kwraa.

english: Why haven't my crops matured for harvesting at the exact same time as my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ be kome mli kɛ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Growth speed varies based on soil moisture, land preparation, shade, and whether traditional or improved planting materials were used, causing crops planted at the same time to mature at different rates.
ga: Esoroɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa oya lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ blema loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my tubers past the usual time I normally harvest them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tubers lɛ akpamɔ be sɛɛ fe mikpamɔ be ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: If the leaves are still green, delaying harvest can allow tubers to keep growing larger; however, if left too long after the plant dies back, the tubers risk pest damage or rotting in the wet soil.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii wuji aba. Shi, kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ gbele sɛɛ lɛ, Tubers lɛ hu baanyɛ afite loo amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need from the soil. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje tso lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that traps nitrogen from the air and puts it naturally into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that stored nitrogen and grows much stronger.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni ato lɛ ni eda waa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but the roots under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava puts all its power into growing tall leaves and stems on top instead of storing energy underground. Reducing heavy fertilizers and giving the plant time allows it to send its energy down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ shi ni ahaa tso lɛ be lɛ haa ekɛ hewalɛ woɔ shi koni ekɛ bulbs akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off before any fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant feels stressed by extreme hot weather, lack of water, or a lack of insects to move pollen around inside the flower. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants enough space helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baatsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some crops like cassava survive dry weather while my maize dries up quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava has long, deep roots that dig far into the ground to reach hidden water, and its leaves can drop to save water during drought. Maize has shallow roots near the top of the soil, so it feels the heat and dry soil much faster.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Ni ebaai lɛ baanyɛ agbee shi koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛna dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi oya kwraa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from underneath the young leaves and spreading diseases. Spraying with neem water or safe crop medicines early stops these pests from damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tso tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ mra.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the tiny air holes in the soil, causing the tubers to suffocate from lack of air. This standing water creates a perfect environment for harmful rot germs to multiply and destroy the yam underground.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni damɔ shi nɛɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ babaoo ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantain trees grow broad leaves quickly that act like big umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the ground cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela agboi oya. Ha kookoo lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crop seeds after the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain wets the soil down deep enough—about the length of your hand—so that when seeds sprout, their tender roots find continuous moisture underground even if the rain pauses for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ—aaafee onine lɛ kɛlɛ—koni kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the soil for years waiting for sunlight and water. Once you clear the farm and rain falls, weeds jump to grow immediately, while farm crops take more time to wake up and establish.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛji ojie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baatu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or lack of water cause tomato plants stress, which makes them drop their blossoms to preserve water and energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo aduawai.

english: Why do my young crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to shrink its surface area and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛha ehiɛ afee bibioo ni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my vegetable plants turn yellow as the plant grows taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or overwatered, forcing the plant to move available nutrients from older lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which usually happens when watering is irregular rather than from an insect attack or disease.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Jeee kɛjɛ kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ loo hela mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruit off wet soil where fungal diseases live, while also allowing air and sunlight to move freely through the crop.
ga: Staking baaye abua ni abu baai kɛ aduawai ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi nɔ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my tomato crops spoil faster and get leaves with dark spots during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and constant wetness create the perfect environment for soil fungi to multiply and spread onto leaves and fruit, causing rapid rotting.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshwere ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baai kɛ aduawai amli. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa oya.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Crops planted too close together compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks and very small harvests.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does planting tomatoes in the exact same plot every season make them get sick more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa hela mɔɔ amɛ waa lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in one spot allows specific soil pests and diseases to multiply in the ground, waiting to attack the roots of the next planting immediately.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛtutua dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply different fertilizers when my crop starts flowering compared to when it was young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi atsu nii beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi fe be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young crops need nitrogen to grow leaves and roots, but flowering crops need extra phosphorus and potassium to produce strong blossoms and healthy, heavy fruit.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛba kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium krokomɛi koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi ni wa ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I harvest my tomatoes while they are still green and mature, or must I wait until they turn red on the stem?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa tomato be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lolo lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi tomato lɛ baatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ?

english: Full-sized green tomatoes naturally release a ripening gas as they mature, so picking them just as they begin changing color allows them to ripen safely on their way to the market without getting damaged on the plant.
ga: Tomato eŋɔli ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu lɛ baajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ootse tomato beni ebɔi su tsakemɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ ni efiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops die when floodwater sits on my field for too many days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gboiɔ beni nu afua lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air from the soil to stay alive. When heavy rainwater sits on top of the field without draining, it blocks oxygen from reaching the root zone, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow during two weeks of heat and no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii enyɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much moisture into the hot air, and they turn yellow when the underground soil becomes too dry for roots to take up essential plant nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme dry soil or excessive heat, because the stress forces the plant to conserve water and energy instead of growing new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo la ni mli edɔ waa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔnyɛɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkwɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo aduawai heei.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stems and leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich animal manure, the cassava plant directs all its food and energy into growing big leaves above ground rather than storing energy in underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ heɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa wuji lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create an ideal environment for plant fungi to grow and spread spores from leaf to leaf, leading to fungal leaf spot diseases.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei amli ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ baa kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. ni kɛ fungal leaf spot hela baa

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot before harvest time when the weather stays damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ? Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a soil-dwelling fungus that multiplies in heavy damp shade and splashes onto low-hanging pods during rainstorms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ Black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni fɔɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli waa, ni eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with poor yields when planted close together in the same bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo faaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he kome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together compete underground for water and soil nutrients while blocking sunlight from each other above ground, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my field soil stay moist longer when I plant low-growing cowpeas between my taller crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii ni shwereɔ fioo yɛ mitsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Low-lying cover crops form a living shade over the ground, reducing soil exposure to direct sunlight and keeping underground water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why do crops generally grow better in low valley land near water bodies than on dry hilltops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ fe gɔji ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland soil benefits from a naturally high underground water table and deep topsoil that holds moisture and washed-down plant nutrients longer than exposed hilltops.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ he sɛɛ, ni no haa nu ni hoɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe gɔji lɛ ayitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when I pour large amounts of water on them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo wo amɛnɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, which starves root systems of oxygen and washes mobile soil nutrients far below where roots can reach.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nyiɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he lɛ shishi.

english: Is it better for me to plant seeds saved from my previous corn harvest or buy certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Saved seeds often carry hidden diseases and lose their vigor over time, which can reduce your harvest by half before the crop even starts growing. Certified seeds are specially treated to resist early pests, germinate evenly, and give you a stronger, higher yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ afee enyɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsuɔ nii krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa onáa yibiiwoo ni mli wa ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do many of my maize seeds fail to sprout even after I work hard to clear and weed my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ beni mitsu nii waa koni mikɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛjie jwɛi lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If the soil is plowed too hard, planted when too dry, or seeds are buried too deep, they cannot sprout properly. Testing soil moisture and planting seeds at the right depth—about two inches—ensures most of your seeds germinate successfully.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii waa Dumɔ be mli ni egbi tsɔ. loo ofu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akwɛ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa, aaafee inchi 2 lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of corn every year even though I work just as hard every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ? Be fɛɛ be?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving it time to replenish. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and restores its natural strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young corn plants turn yellow and stop growing shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is holding too much water around the roots. Applying a small amount of starter fertilizer or well-rotted manure early gives seedlings the nutrients needed to build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo mli mra. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana niyenii ni he hia amɛ koni amɛ wo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and tall but give me very small cobs at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwiili shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your plants properly gives each corn stalk enough room and food to produce big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa abɛi tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my seedlings die off quickly if the rains stop for just a few days after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots that dry out easily in hot weather. Planting immediately after steady rains begin and spreading dried leaves or straw around young plants helps trap moisture in the ground so seedlings survive short dry spells.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in my young corn leaves before the plants even mature?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa kwraa?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms lay eggs on crop leaves very early in the season. Checking under leaves weekly and applying recommended biological or chemical treatments early stops pests before they ruin your crop's growth.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa otsi ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko awo mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do the stems and roots of my crop rot in the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water staying trapped around plant roots causes fungi to grow and rot the stem. Planting on raised soil ridges or digging drainage furrows allows extra water to run off, keeping roots dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni kpɛtɛɔ tso shishifãi ahe lɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ mli ŋshɔi ni atsa lɛ baaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Applying fertilizer at two key stages—once when planting or shortly after germination, and again when the corn reaches knee height—gives crops nutrients right when they need them to form strong leaves and large cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ ni he hiaa nɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ yɛ dumɔ mli loo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ enaji ahe Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa lɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs end up half-empty with missing grains at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi efo fã ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when hot, dry weather or poor nutrients affect the plant during its flowering stage when silks appear. Ensuring the crop has good water and fertilizer before flowering helps fill every cob completely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni esaaa lɛ saa tso lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔi be mli beni siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná nu kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ayi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants become heat-stressed and cannot pollinate properly. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ bafeɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense against drought. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and preserves water in its underground roots until the rain comes back.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ŋmei he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nu ato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: When planted too close, maize stalks compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into growing big cobs, the plants stretch upwards just to reach light.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ moŋ. Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni emɔ kane lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms eat my young maize leaves mostly at night while hiding during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide in the central leaves or soil during the heat of the day to avoid drying out and to escape birds. They come out at night when it is cool and dark to feed safely.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkagbi ni okpoi lɛ akajo foi. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ koni amɛbaye nii shweshweeshwe.

english: What time of day should I harvest my leafy vegetables so they stay fresh until I get to the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be esa akɛ akpa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi jara nɔ?

english: Harvest vegetables early in the morning before the sun gets hot or late in the evening. During these times, plants are full of moisture from the cool night, which keeps them crisp and prevents early wilting.
ga: Kpaa aduawai lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli baayi tsei lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa egbo oya.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have very wild, fast-growing roots that absorb fertilizer quicker than crop plants. If you do not clear weeds before fertilizing, you are feed the weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya, ni ji adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Obaafee jwɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or garden eggs in the exact same soil where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and insects. Planting them in the same spot continuously lets pests build up in the soil and attack the new crops immediately.
ga: Tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi jɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaatutua tsei heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off unnecessary branches from my cocoa trees before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and wind can pass through easily. This dries out wet leaves quickly after rain and prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to sprout when I plant them into dry soil before the rain arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to soften their tough outer coat and signal the plant inside to start growing. Without moisture, the seed stays asleep in the soil or can get scorched and ruined by hot dirt.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli awa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akɛ ebɔi dalɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo muji ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Officer, why is it important for me to just walk around my farm and look at my crops without doing any heavy work?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ manyiɛ kɛbɔle he lɛ? Okwaa ni okwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni nitsumɔ ni wa ko bɛ mli?

english: Regularly walking through your farm just to inspect your crops allows you to spot early signs of insect attacks, diseases, or water stress before they spread and cause major damage to your harvest.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni oootsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛyakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tutua bo, hela loo nu mli haomɔ. dani egbɛ eshwa ni efite onikpamɔ lɛ waa.

english: How often should I set aside time just to inspect my fields for potential crop problems?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mato be he gbɛjianɔ koni makwɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli koni mana naagbai ni baanyɛ aba yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to dedicatedly inspect your fields every two weeks so you can closely track how your crops are developing and catch any health issues while they are still easy to manage.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ daa otsii enyɔ bɔni afee ni okwɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ena helatsamɔ mli naagbai yɛ be mli ni ehiɛ kã shi lolo lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my trees or crops actually need to be pruned?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehe baahia ni afo mitso loo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You need to prune when you observe dead wood, diseased leaves, or overlapping branches that block sunlight and prevent fresh air from flowing through the inner parts of the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tsei lɛ ahe kɛji ona tsei ni egboi. baai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa akatsɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Will trimming off branches from my farm crops hurt their growth or lower my yield?
ga: Ani tsei niji ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite amɛdalɛ loo ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: No, removing weak or unnecessary branches actually helps the plant redirect its energy and food toward producing bigger, healthier fruits and pods.
ga: Dabi, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops droop or curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop to reduce their surface area and save moisture when heat is intense, which is a clear sign that the crop is experiencing heat stress and may need shade or water.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo egbee shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni ená hulutsoo loo nu.

english: Why are some of my crops turning yellow while others nearby remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Akutso lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔji lolo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that a plant is struggling to get enough nitrogen from the soil, suffering from root rot, or being attacked by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa amɛ

english: What signs should I look for on my crop leaves to know if a disease is starting?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ koni mana kɛji hela miije shishi?

english: Look out for small dark spots, powdery white patches, brown edges, or unusual yellow rings on the leaves, as these are early warnings of fungal or bacterial infections.
ga: Taomɔ hei bibii ni yɔɔ duŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko mli baa, ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if insects are harming my crops if I cannot see the bugs with my eyes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ mihiŋmɛii ana kooloi bibii hu?

english: Insects leave indirect signs such as tiny holes eaten into leaves, sticky fluid on stems, rolled-up leaves, or damaged crop buds where pests hide.
ga: Kplukai shĩɔ okadii ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ buji bibii ni ayeɔ awoɔ baai amli. Nu ko ni kpɛtɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. baai ni shwieɔ shi loo tsei ashishifãi ni efite yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my crops before they turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop early when the crop experiences sudden heat stress, lack of soil nutrients, or when there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my plants look weak and fall over easily after a small rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bibioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops fall easily if their roots are shallow, damaged by soil pests, or planted in compacted soil where roots cannot anchor deeply to support the weight of the plant.
ga: Tso lɛ baagbee shi oya kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Aloo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛfi tso lɛ muji lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides essential shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cob forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen moves to the newest leaves at the top to keep the plant growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ yaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eha tso lɛ ada. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and falling over easily when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition creates tall, weak stems that easily break or fall over during heavy wind or rain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fãa loo amɛkuɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience temperature heat stress or sudden dry spells, like during the Harmattan. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and maintaining regular watering helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa, tamɔ yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to invest all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its root tubers. Cassava needs balanced soil rich in potassium to grow thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni Cassava shishifã lɛ baagbɛ eshwa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting in the barn shortly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when wounded during digging or stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing undamaged yams off the ground in a cool, shady, and well-aired barn prevents rot-causing fungi from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji epila yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto hei ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my watermelon plant produce many yellow flowers but fails to produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce separate male and female flowers, and bees must carry pollen from the male flower to the female flower. If there are few insects around or if conditions are too dry, the female flowers will drop without forming watermelons.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ni esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli. Kɛji kooloi fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Fɔfɔi yei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee melon.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on the leaves of my garden eggs during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads fast in damp, humid weather. Pruning dense leaves improves air movement around the plant, keeping the leaves dry and reducing fungal growth.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I burn all the cleared weeds on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni mishãa jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter, beneficial insects, and soil microbes that naturally feed crops. Leaving cleared foliage to rot on the ground as mulch protects the soil from drying out and adds natural nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Ha baai ni he tse lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baa lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is frequently spread by small whitefly insects carrying a plant virus. Watering helps with moisture, but controlling whiteflies and removing infected plants is necessary to stop the spread of the leaf curl virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ tso hela lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi. Shi ŋmeii yɛji lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ he miihia koni akɛkpa leaf curl virus lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How can I check if the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest will actually sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani adu?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing ten seeds on a wet cloth and keeping it damp for five days. If eight or more seeds sprout roots, your seeds are strong and good to plant; if fewer sprout, it is better to buy fresh certified seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛwoɔ mama ni mli efɔ nɔ ni ahaa ewoɔ mli gbii enumɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ Odumɔwui lɛ baawa ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantains on the same land with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cocoa tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct heat from the sun. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the ground cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off when the dry weather begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves naturally during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will grow new green leaves and continue swelling its roots under the ground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai heei ni eshishifãi lɛ baafu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: My pepper plants have many flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mi pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by too much heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding compost gives the plant enough strength to turn flowers into peppers.
