ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow much taller and greener on the part of my farm where I planted groundnuts last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu mi ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ fã lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which pulls good nitrogen food from the air and fixes it into the soil. When you plant maize after groundnuts, the maize eats that leftover nutrient and grows faster and stronger.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa niyenii kpakpai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: If I bury my seeds very deep in the soil, will they grow stronger roots?
ga: Kɛ mifu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa?

english: No, burying seeds too deep buries them away from warmth and air, causing them to rot or waste all their stored food before reaching the surface. Planting seeds shallowly—about two finger-joints deep—helps them sprout quickly and healthy.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ooofu tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfiteɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ (aaafee inchi 2) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are those small worms eating the rolled-up leaves inside my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are fall armyworms, which feed on the soft, growing heart of the young maize plant. Catching them early when the leaves look ragged and applying targeted ash or recommended pest control stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Amɛji fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ atsuii lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Beni baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni akɛ sũ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ lɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look droopy during the hot afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomato plants curl and droop in the hot sun to slow down water loss through their leaves. As long as the soil has moisture, the plant will bounce back up and look fresh again in the cooler evening.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds come up out of the soil much faster than the crop seeds I planted after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ je kpo oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping inside the soil from previous seasons and are wild, tough plants built to survive. They wake up instantly with the first drop of rain, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni amɛji koo mli tsei ni wa ni ama koni amɛhi shi. Amɛte shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know under the ground that my yams are fully grown and ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the vines above the ground start turning yellow and drying up. This shows that the plant has stopped growing top leaves and has finished storing all its food energy down inside the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa eŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ eto bulb lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from dry conditions, or being attacked by pests like fall armyworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni amɛyɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms tutuaa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans inside my maize farm, and will it help my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for your maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves you with tall, thin plants that produce small tubers instead of big, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the heat is too strong or when the soil lacks enough steady water. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly when damp air and heavy shade keep the farm too wet. Pruning excess branches helps air move through and reduces the dampness.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa ni eyɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if my farmland has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ miifite ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, look pale or yellowish, or produce much smaller yields than in previous years, your soil has run out of nutrients and needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai awo mli.

english: Why should I buy packaged seed from the extension office instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli kɛjɛ Extension Office lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Packaged certified seeds are specially bred to yield more crops, resist common diseases, and tolerate dry spells better than seeds saved from old harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ anaa ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ blema ŋmaakpamɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and full of insects so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ŋmeii eyi mi ŋmãa lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is stored before drying completely. Excess moisture inside the grain attracts mold growth and creates a perfect place for weevils to multiply.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. ni efee he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ afɔ yɛ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can soak up water before the sun gets strong. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate too quickly and can scorch hot plant leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli awa tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei ahe baai ashã.

english: Young cocoa plants get leaf scorch when they receive too much direct sunlight without shade crops like plantains, or when the soil lacks adequate moisture during dry spells.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii baanyɛ aná baai ni shãa amɛ kɛji amɛná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ amɛhe, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, overly humid conditions when cocoa trees are not properly pruned or cleared of surrounding weeds.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ loo ajieee jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their flowers before tiny pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from severe heat stress, prolonged dry weather, or when there are not enough pollinating insects in the field to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do cocoa trees take several years before they start producing full bags of pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees spend their early years establishing deep roots and strong trunks to support heavy yields, though modern hybrid varieties are bred to start bearing fruit much faster.
ga: Kusum tso ni ji cacao lɛ yeɔ eshishijee afii lɛ amli ni edaa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni baaye abua nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii mra kwraa moŋ.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the field dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties depend on consistent soil moisture to absorb nutrients; when the field dries out completely, the roots cannot feed properly, leading to yellowing leaves and stunted growth.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my rice stalks are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the stalks turn a hard, golden-yellow color and the lower leaves of the plant begin to dry out naturally.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ni mli wa. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the stalks of my rice plants bending and falling over before the grains are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This issue, known as lodging, happens when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, are planted too close together, or are blown over by heavy wind while top-heavy with grain.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ shihilɛhe. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. adu ni ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ tsii yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce small fruit bunches with very little oil in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Kɛ mu fioo ko pɛ?

english: Oil palms require consistent rainfall, full sunlight, and high soil nutrients like potassium; without adequate fertilizer and regular weed clearing around the base, fruit bunches remain small and yield low oil.
ga: Mu tso lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. hulu la ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo tamɔ potassium. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, aduawai akui lɛ baakã he afee bibii ni amɛbaafee mu fioo.

english: Why do I need to ferment my harvested cocoa beans under banana leaves before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ woɔ banana baa shishi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the seed embryo, remove bitter tastes, and unlock the rich chocolate color and flavor that cocoa buyers inspect for before paying.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeleɔ tsokolate su ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kwɛɔ mli dani amɛwoɔ nyɔmɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested grains turn moldy even after I spread them out to dry on mats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ beni migbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛgbi yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Mold forms when crops are not dried down to a low enough moisture level, or when they absorb moisture from the humid air or damp ground during storage.
ga: Fungus baa kɛji akɛ agbiko tsei lɛ kɛyashɛɛɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant plantains on the same land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by hot, direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and develop wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Does planting plantains alongside my cocoa steal water and nutrients away from the cocoa roots?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo lɛ masɛi lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: When planted with correct spacing, plantains actually help the soil retain moisture by blocking hot sunlight. Plantain trunks also store water, which keeps the surrounding microclimate cool for young cocoa seedlings.
ga: When planted with the appropriate distance Plantains actually help the soil retain moisture by blocking the hot sun. Plantain tsei lɛ hu hiɛɔ nu. This keeps the surrounding microclimate cool for young cocoa seedlings.

english: Can I plant any food crop together with my young cocoa, or are plantains special?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo bibii adu niyenii? Aloo ani plantain henɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ?

english: Some crops compete aggressively for root space, but plantains are ideal because they grow tall fast to offer overhead shade without choking the young cocoa trees below, making them perfect companion plants.
ga: Tsei komɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi amli he ko he akaŋshii mli waa. But plantains are ideal because they quickly grow tall to provide shade overhead without interfering with the young cocoa trees beneath. Ni afee lɛ nanemɛi tso ni yeɔ emuu.

english: How am I supposed to feed my family while waiting several years for new cocoa trees to bear fruit?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo koni cacao tsei heei awo yibii lɛ?

english: By intercropping with fast-yielding crops like plantains, you can harvest and sell food within the first year. This provides food and quick income to keep your home running while your cocoa matures.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya tamɔ plantains Obaanyɛ okpa niyenii ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika ni onáa oya koni oha oshia lɛ aya nɔ yɛ be mli ni o-cocoa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How long does a plantain plant take to yield food compared to a young cocoa tree?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛ akɛto cacao tsei bibii ahe?

english: Plantain plants produce heavy bunches of fruit in about 12 to 15 months, whereas cocoa trees usually take about 3 to 5 years before giving significant harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting crops neatly in straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil space. It also makes weeding, spraying, and walking through your farm much easier without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What will happen to the plantain trees when my cocoa trees finally grow big and tall?
ga: Mɛni baaba dumɔwui lɛ anɔ beni naagbee lɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛbakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Once cocoa mature and form a full leafy top, they need more sunlight and no longer require intense shade. At that point, you gradually harvest and remove the plantain plants so the cocoa can produce maximum pods.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ, hulu la babaoo he miihia Cocoa, ni hulutsoo be ni mli wa he ehiaaa lɛ dɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, obaakpa dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie amɛ koni kookoo lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ.

english: Does having large plantain leaves overhead make weeding my farm easier or harder?
ga: Ani plantain baai agboi ni yɔɔ miyitso nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo ewaa?

english: Plantain leaves create heavy shade on the farm ground, which prevents weeds from getting sunlight to grow rapidly. This reduces the amount of labor and time you spend weeding.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa jwɛi lɛ ashɛ hulu la he koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ kɛ be ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Where do I get new plantain plants from after harvesting the main stem?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana tsei heei beni akpa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally produce small shoots at their base called suckers. You can carefully dig up these young suckers and replant them to expand your field or replace old stems.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ eshishigbɛ akɛ ŋmei. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nɛkɛ tsei bibii nɛɛ ahe nii ni odu eheei koni okɛha he lɛ mli alɛɛ loo okɛto tsei momo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can agricultural extension officers assist me when I am starting a new farm layout?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ beni mijeɔ okwaayeli he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Extension officers can teach you proper row spacing, supply healthy, high-yield plant suckers or seedlings, and guide you on the best crop combinations for your land.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ line lɛ ato. Ha hewalɛ, tsei ashishifãi loo dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo. ni ewo bo ŋaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaafata he kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or if the ground stays flooded for too long.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get too stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer. If the air is too dry or hot, the plant sheds flowers to save its strength.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hao amɛ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo yɛ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the Harmattan to save water. By shedding leaves, the tree loses less moisture to the dry wind and heat, helping the main trunk and roots stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ harmattan be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli nu fioo pɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a few steady rains to stay moist deep down. Planting after just one light rain can trap seeds in dry ground if the sun comes back strong, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa koni ekɛha hei ni mli kwɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown and rot because wet, soggy soil attracts destructive water molds.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛgboi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nu lɛ.

english: Yam tubers twist and stay small when the soil is too hard, stony, or clayey for them to push through easily. Loosening the soil into soft mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛhi shi bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sũ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tuber he lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops even when my plants are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ dara momo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to fill out their fruits or grains. Even big crop plants produce smaller yields if weeds are constantly competing with their roots underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ aduawai loo ŋmaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuji po baawo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ jwɛi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ miitswa akaŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of pods. They need full sunlight and balanced nutrients to switch from growing leaves to growing beans.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmeii nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Amɛmiitao hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni ja koni amɛtsake kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why do insects attack my vegetables more during the warm, rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warm and moist weather creates the perfect conditions for insects to hatch, feed, and multiply rapidly. Tender new leaves and shoots growing during the rains also attract hungry pests.
ga: Dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i shihilɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha koolooi ni amɛ fɔ, amɛ tao niyenii ni amɛ fɔ oya. Baai kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers dry up and fall over even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ po lɛ?

english: This usually happens because pests like stem borers or nematodes are tunneling inside the root base and stem, weakening the plant from within so it can no longer take up water or support its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes tsɔɔ shishitoo kɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ emligbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nu awo mli loo enyɛŋ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the certified seeds I buy give a better harvest than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred in laboratories to resist diseases and produce high yields. Saved seeds lose their strength over time and often carry over pests and diseases from the previous season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni bei pii lɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is my land producing fewer bags of maize each year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season. Without adding manure, fertilizer, or rotating with crops like beans to restore the soil, the ground gets tired and weak over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fataaa he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can happen when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash the food away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ biɔ nitrogen. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii laajeɔ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen can stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and thin even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving the main plants starving.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn plant roots and stems if placed directly on them. Placing it a few centimeters away allows roots to safely absorb it.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, will I harvest more cassava roots?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani manyɛ maná ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil food. Giving them space allows the roots room to expand and grow big.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does cassava survive long dry seasons while my maize dies after a few weeks of no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava has deep taproots that reach water stored deep underground and drops its leaves to conserve water, whereas maize has shallow roots and needs steady moisture.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he, ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli daa.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, tender inner leaves of young corn. They hide in the central shoot during the hot day and feed when it cools down.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni oye kɛji fɛ̃i ba

english: Why do some crop varieties take only four months to grow while others take much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ pɛ dani amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo fe nakai lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different rainfall conditions. Fast-maturing varieties, like those taking about four months, are designed so farmers in dry areas can harvest their food quickly before the rains stop.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli lɛ naa. Henɔi ni daa oya, tamɔ nɔ ni heɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ Afee lɛ koni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ anyɛ akpa niyenii oya dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: What type of seed variety should I plant if my farm is in an area that doesn't get much rain?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ madu?

english: In low-rainfall areas, you should choose quick-maturing crop varieties—such as those taking around four months to mature—so the crop finishes growing and can be harvested before drought sets in.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ tsei ni heɔ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he, ni akpa amɛ dani hɔmɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why should I pay attention to the maturity period of a crop before buying seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama be ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ nɔ dani mahe dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Matching the crop's growth time to your local weather ensures your plants get enough rain to mature fully, preventing total crop failure if the rain stops early.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ adalɛ bei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra.

english: How do I know if a crop variety is suitable for quick harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko sa kɛha nikpamɔ oya?

english: You check its maturity time; varieties bred for dry or short-rain regions usually mature in a short window, like four months, allowing you to harvest and bring your produce home early.
ga: Okwɛɔ be ni sa lɛ mli. Varieties bred for dry areas or short periods of rain. They usually ripen in a short period of time, such as four months, so you can harvest and take the produce home quickly.

english: Why do crops that grow well in Kumasi often fail when planted in drier parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Kumasi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Kumasi is in a forest area with heavy rainfall, so its crop varieties are adapted to high moisture and longer growing times, whereas drier areas need quick-maturing varieties that survive on less water.
ga: Kumasi yɛ kooi babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Shi hei ni nu bɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kooloi srɔtoi ni daa oya ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi.

english: What kind of crop varieties perform best in heavy rainfall areas like the forest zone?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ, tamɔ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Forest zones need strong crop varieties that hold up well against heavy, continuous rain without rotting or dying from excess water.
ga: Kooi amli kpokpai lɛ ahe miihia tsei srɔtoi ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ naa ni amɛgbooo loo amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant a crop variety meant for wet forest areas in a place with low rainfall?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo yɛ?

english: The crop will likely dry out or fail to produce a good harvest because it expects continuous heavy rain and a longer rainy season to reach full maturity.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baagbi loo amɛwooo yibii kpakpai ejaakɛ akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baaya nɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: How does my farm's location in Ghana affect the type of crop seed I should buy?
ga: Te he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ saa dumɔwui srɔtoi ni esa akɛ mahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Your location determines your rainfall pattern; forest areas with heavy rain need hardy, wet-tolerant varieties, while dry areas require fast-maturing varieties to beat short rain cycles.
ga: Your location determines your rainfall pattern. Kooi amli hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ biɔ tsei srɔtoi ni wa, ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hei ni nu bɛ lɛ he miihia tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛye nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Can heavy rain damage crop varieties that are not meant for forest areas?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei srɔtoi ni afeee kɛha kooi amli hei lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, varieties not suited for wet forest regions can easily get damaged or diseased by heavy rain, which is why farmers in places like Kumasi use varieties specifically bred to hold up well in heavy water.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite kooloi srɔtoi ni esaaa kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ oya loo amɔ amɛ hela. Nɔ ni haa okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Kumasi lɛ kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: How does choosing a four-month crop variety help me beat the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nyɔji ejwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni mihala lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maye hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kunim?

english: A four-month variety completes its growth cycle fast, allowing you to harvest and safely store your crop at home before the dry weather harms the plants.
ga: Nyɔji ejwɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ gbeɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii ni okɛtoɔ shia lɛ shweshweeshwe dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing fewer fruits at 15 years old, and should I cut them down already?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni eye afii 15 lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees can live and yield well for 25 to 30 years. At 15 years old, the tree is still in its prime; a sudden drop in fruit is usually caused by lack of nutrients, poor rainfall, or poor pruning rather than old age.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ afii 25 kɛyashi 30. Beni tsei lɛ eye afii 15 lɛ, no mli lɛ amɛyɛ amɛfɔmɔ afii lɛ amli lolo. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ trukaa lɛ baa. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ fe afii.

english: How do I know when an oil palm tree is genuinely too old and needs to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mu tso ko egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake lɛ?

english: A palm tree should only be cleared when it grows too tall for harvest tools to reach safely or when its fruit production stays very low for several years despite proper feeding and care, which typically happens after 25 to 30 years.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie ŋmei tsei lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛkwɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe. aloo be mli ni ŋmei tsei lɛ ayibii lɛ faaa kwraa afii babaoo yɛ niyenii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to prune dead leaves from my oil palm trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mu tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Removing dead leaves allows more sunlight to reach the tree, makes it easier for you to see and harvest fresh fruit bunches, and stops pests and diseases from hiding under the dry branches.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie baai ni egboi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ ooona aduawai heei ni abua naa lɛ ni obaakpa. ni ehaaa ŋmeii kɛ helai akatee tsei niji ni egbi lɛ ashishi.

english: Is it safe to use any crop chemical that my local agro-input dealer recommends?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mimaŋ okwaayeli he nibii ahe jarayelɔ lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ baatsu nii?

english: While agro-dealers sell useful inputs, their advice might focus on selling products rather than understanding your specific farm soil. It is best to verify chemical choices with an extension officer to avoid buying unnecessary or damaging treatments.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ moŋ, Shi amɛ ŋaawoo lɛ baanyɛ akɔ nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ ahe fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ shishinumɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ o-extension agent lɛ baakwɛ tsofai ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ amli koni okahe tsofai ni he ehiaaa loo ni fiteɔ mɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray strong chemical weedkillers continuously on my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni he wa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Overusing chemical weedkillers destroys the healthy organisms in the topsoil, hardens the ground, and can weaken your crop roots over time, leading to lower yields in future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa Ni ebaanyɛ eha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young crops turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the crop is starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the roots are struggling to find water during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium lɛ miiye sũ lɛ hɔmɔ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛna nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer without expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni aka lɛ akwɛ ni jara wa?

english: If your plants have pale or light green leaves, grow very slowly, or produce unusually small fruits despite getting enough rainfall, your soil lacks the nutrients that fertilizer provides.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo eŋɔli ni mli tse, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do my palm trees drop their tiny young fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young fruit drop happens when the tree experiences stress from severe dry spells, nutrient shortages in the soil, or inadequate insect pollination during the flowering stage.
ga: Yibii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpe. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does my tree farm produce a huge harvest one year and very little the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli ni afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like palm trees often go through natural resting cycles; after spending energy on a massive harvest, the tree needs time and extra soil nutrients to rebuild its energy for the next big cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. Beni akɛ hewalɛ etsu nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko mli sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ he miihia be kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ hee kɛha sɛɛkuu agbo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani abaanyɛ afee yɛ mu tsei bibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when young palms are small, intercropping with food crops works well, as long as you keep enough distance so the crops do not fight for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo. Nibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsei lɛ akashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ,

english: How can I tell if a fertilizer or pesticide I want to buy at the store is genuine and not fake?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni misumɔɔ ni mahe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni jeee amale?

english: Genuine agrochemicals usually have clear registration numbers from regulatory bodies like the EPA, intact security seals, clear manufacture/expiry dates, and are sold by licensed agro-dealers. Fake products often have misspelled words on the label, broken seals, or unusually low prices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, agrochemicals diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ nɔmba ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni jɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ EPA lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni amɛyɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he okadi ni yeɔ emuu. Tsɔɔmɔ gbi ni afee/egbe naa ni okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ Bei pii lɛ, amale nibii lɛ yɛ wiemɔi ni ejaaa ni aŋmala yɛ nɔ, naatsii ni ekumɔ, loo jara ni baa shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ.

english: Is it bad if I mix two different crop chemicals together in the same sprayer tank to save time?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ futu mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Yes, mixing incompatible chemicals can cause them to react negatively, forming clumps that block your sprayer, making the chemicals useless, or creating a harsh mixture that can burn your crop leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ afee nɔ ko ni ehiii. Efeɔ kui ni tsiɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa tsofai feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa Aloo efeɔ tsofa ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops so it works properly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best times are early morning (6 AM to 9 AM) or late evening (4 PM to 6 PM). During hot midday hours, sunlight and heat make the chemical evaporate too quickly before the plant or pest can absorb it, and it can also burn the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi (6:00 AM kɛyashi 9:00 AM) loo gbɛkɛ (4:00 PM kɛyashi 6:00 PM) yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ hu ashã.

english: How should I store my farm chemicals after opening them so they don't lose their power before the next season?
ga: Kɛ́ agbele naa lɛ, te esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ato tɛŋŋ koni amɛkafite dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Store them in a cool, dry, dark place off the floor, tightly closed in their original containers. Heat, direct sunlight, and moisture degrade the chemical ingredients and make them ineffective over time.
ga: Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni duŋ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha ehi shishijee tsɛnsi lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ hulutsoo baafite tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ebaaha amɛkatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my cocoa pods even after I sprayed pesticide on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ.

english: Pesticides may fail if they are expired, diluted with bad water, applied at the wrong dosage, or if insects are hiding under dense foliage. Spraying repeatedly with the wrong chemical can also make the insects resistant to it.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛbe eho. Akɛ nu ewo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ falɛ ni ejaaa atsu nii Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ Baanyɛ aha kooloi anyɛ atsu nii

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient, or that excessive rain has flooded the root zone and prevented the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ nii Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ shi ni ehaaa eŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow in heavy shade, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo amɛdara yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific soil minerals like calcium and boron during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is still wet from rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Ani nugbɔ lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that attack the roots and stems, blocking water from moving up inside the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil actually needs fertilizer before I spend money to buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Dani mafite shika kɛhe?

english: You can check soil health by observing previous crop growth; small, weak plants with pale leaves mean low soil fertility. A simple soil test conducted through an extension officer will tell you exactly what nutrients your land is missing.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ha kɛtsɔ tsei ni etsɔ hiɛ amɛdara lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni extension officers lɛ feɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep getting sick even after I cut off the infected leaves with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dade tswa baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ po?

english: Plant diseases spread easily through contaminated farm tools like cutlasses and shears. If you cut a sick plant and then use the exact same blade on a healthy plant without cleaning it with soap or disinfectant, you transfer the sickness directly into the healthy plant's stem.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mli ewo muji tamɔ dade kɛ sɛkɛs nɔ. Kɛji oofo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ, okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii ni okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai etsuuu he. Obaajie hela lɛ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under full sun. Shade trees or plantain plants act as natural sunshades, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa leaves until the trees are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo tsɔnei. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or chicken manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground. Balanced nutrients like potassium are needed to swell the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii ni ja, tamɔ potassium he miihia koni ŋmeii lɛ aya nɔ afuu.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year, why does my harvest keep decreasing?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, while allowing crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants dry up and drop off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by insects or wind, or when the plant is stressed by extreme heat and drought. Without pollen moving from one part of the flower to another, the plant abandons the unpollinated flower to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollen ko bɛ ni nyiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ, Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and covered in small dirt that looks like sawdust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni muji bibii ehà nɔ lɛ? No tamɔ ŋmei?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows deep into the growing funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft inner leaves and leaving behind its sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the ground. Curling and drooping leaves is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface exposed to the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi akɛ tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni baa lɛ nɔ hulu la ni baa lɛ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do the crops I grow from the seeds of last season's high-yielding hybrid tomatoes give me smaller, weaker fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli tomato dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wo yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops do not retain all the strong traits of their parent plants. The second generation breaks down genetically, leading to uneven growth, smaller fruits, and lower resistance to diseases compared to the original packaged hybrid seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hiɛɛɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ sui ni mli wa lɛ amli. Ajara yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɔmɔ su mli. Ekɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa Yibii lɛ ji bibioo. ni helai ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ shishijee tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce food efficiently. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil-borne fungi from causing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ koni hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ aná babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ akakɛ baa helai aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and thin even when there is plenty of rain for all of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that suck up fertilizers, mineral nutrients, and soil space before your crops can reach them. Even with abundant rainfall, crops turn pale because weeds are stealing the essential nitrogen needed for healthy green leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. mineral nutrients kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiju nitrogen ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested rice turn out dirty and broken if I take it to a local corn mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite kɛji mikɛtee maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Corn mills use heavy friction designed for hard maize kernels. Because rice grains are delicate, putting them through a corn mill crushes the grain into broken pieces and mixes husk dust into the final product instead of cleanly separating it.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ friction ni tsii ni afee aha abɛi ŋmeii ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ejaakɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli wa Kɛ́ akɛwo ŋmãa ŋmãa mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli bibii bibii. ni okɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afutu naagbee nɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ooogbala mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the main difference between polished rice and the fresh brown rice I harvest from my field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ ehee ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Freshly harvested rice still has its outer bran layer, which gives it a brownish color and extra nutrients. Polishing uses machines to rub off this outer layer, leaving behind smooth, clean white grains that many market buyers prefer.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ bran layer ko ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lolo ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Sanding kɛ tsɔne ko jieɔ nɛkɛ kponɔgbɛ fã nɛɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he tse ni jarayelɔi babaoo sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested grains shatter into small pieces during milling while others stay long and whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi fãa bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni miikpaa lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛyiɔ obɔ lɛ?

english: Grains shatter during milling if they were harvested too late, dried unevenly under harsh heat, or if the grain variety naturally has weak internal structures. Proper drying and choosing sturdy seed varieties keep grains intact.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa lɛ baafite yɛ be mli ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Egbiɔ yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmaa henɔ lɛ yɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ halamɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: How do I choose which seed variety to plant if buyers in my market specifically want long-grain rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni mikɛbaadu lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ mijarayelihe lɛ miitao ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ afata he

english: Look for certified long-grain seed varieties from your agricultural officer that are adapted to local soil. Planting unverified seeds leads to mixed grain sizes that do not meet the uniform standards buyers look for.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni dumɔwui kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ mli ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Dumɔwui ni akwɛko mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni akɛfutu lɛ akashɛ dalɛ he mlai ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ he.

english: Do long-grain crop varieties take longer to mature in the field compared to short-grain ones?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kukuji lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Maturity time depends on the specific plant genetics rather than grain length. Some long-grain varieties mature quickly within 90 days, while others take longer depending on rainfall and soil nutrients.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Be ni tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ damɔ tso lɛ mli wala yibii pɔtɛɛ nɔ fe dumɔwu lɛ kɛlɛ. Dumɔwui kakadaji komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ gbii 90, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu baanyɛ ahe be babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water or wet soil, while my maize crop roots rot in the same wet spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mi-abele shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni efɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their roots that allow them to breathe even when flooded. Maize roots lack these air tubes, so standing water smothers the roots and causes them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ kɛji nu shwie amɛnɔ po. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tall rice plants bend over and lay flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ dani amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: This is called lodging. It happens when heavy grains make the top of the plant heavy, or when weak stems caused by too much nitrogen fertilizer collapse under rain and wind.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa kɛji dumɔwui ni tsii ha tso lɛ yiteŋ tsii. Aloo beni tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛbaa lɛ gbee shi yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains crack open if I leave them drying directly under the intense afternoon sun for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli fãa kɛji miha amɛgbi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Harsh afternoon heat dries the outside of the grain much faster than the inside. This uneven drying creates stress cracks inside the grain, causing it to break easily during milling.
ga: La ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa fe emligbɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ejaaa nɛɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli fãa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I harvest the grains early while they are still moist and soft?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa dumɔwui lɛ mra be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Harvesting moist grains makes them easy to crush during handling, and the remaining dampness encourages mold and insects to destroy the crop during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akpaa lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpãtã amɛmli yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii hewalɛ koni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do grains harvested from the same field end up with different colors and sizes after processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akpa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ yɛ su kɛ dalɛi srɔtoi yɛ be mli ni atsu he nii agbe naa lɛ?

english: Uneven field conditions—such as shaded spots, mixed seed stock, or patchy water distribution—cause plants to ripen at different speeds, resulting in mixed grain sizes and colors at harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi ni ejaaa tamɔ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, dumɔwui ni efutu loo nu mlijaa yɛ hei srɔtoi Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa oya yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ adalɛi kɛ amɛhe sui futuɔ kɛji akpa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build strong leaves and stalks, and when the soil doesn't have enough, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil with air to survive. When heavy rain fills up all the space in the soil with water, the roots cannot breathe, causing underground fungal infections and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on my plot after harvesting my yam crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam plants pull a lot of nutrients out of the ground, leaving the soil tired. Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, restoring your farm's fertility naturally for the next season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ Cowpea ji ŋmei tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛsaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees curling up and dropping off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and drop to conserve water when the air gets dry and dusty. Young trees do not have deep root systems yet, so they shed leaves to prevent losing too much moisture through evaporation.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni sũ ebɔle he. Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, eshwieɔ ebaa lɛ koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni baa shi lɛ naa kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fresh leaves after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ baai heei beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you plant a new sucker, its initial energy goes into growing fresh underground roots before it can support new top growth. Once the roots establish themselves in the soil, leaf growth will resume quickly.
ga: Kɛji odu sucker tso hee lɛ Eshishijee hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi heei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua ŋwɛi dalɛ hee. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my mature oil palms produce many small fruit bunches instead of large, heavy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ni eda lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii babaoo yɛ aduawai wuji ni tsii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Small bunches are often a sign of water stress or insufficient potassium and boron in the soil. Oil palms need consistent moisture and balanced fertilizers to fill out big, nutrient-dense fruit heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ji nu mli haomɔ loo potassium kɛ boron ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Mu tsei lɛ biɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa koni amɛwo amɛ aduawai ayitsei wuji ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as temperatures that are too high, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. The plant sheds the flowers to conserve its own life when conditions are difficult.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa tsɔ kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled instead of spreading out flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled, curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. As these pests feed on the juice beneath the leaves, they deform leaf growth and can transfer viral diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa, ejaakɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ adalɛ efite ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves full of small holes shortly after growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars, like the Diamondback moth larvae, feeding on the greenery. These pests target tender cabbage leaves to feed themselves before maturing.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kwɛɔ kaabii bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe niyenii dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my rice crop bend and fall over flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This behavior is called lodging. It happens when the grain heads become very heavy and the stems are too weak to support them, often caused by applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or heavy rainfall and winds.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa kɛji dumɔwu lɛ yitso lɛ tsii waa ni eshishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa

english: Why should I plant my maize in different groups weeks apart instead of planting all my seeds on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ kui amli ni otsii babaoo kɛ amɛhe aaawo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ.

english: Staggering your planting spreads out your harvest time, protecting you against total crop loss if a sudden dry spell hits during flowering and ensuring a continuous supply of fresh harvest to sell over a longer period.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi nɔ lɛ baagbɛ okpamɔ be lɛ eshwã. Ebuɔ ohe koni onibii fɛɛ akafite kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. ni ehaa nɔmimaa akɛ abaaya nɔ aná ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and small if I leave them in the ground for too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach their best size and starch quality between 9 and 12 months. If left unharvested too long, the plant begins to consume its own stored food reserves to grow top leaves, making the tubers tough, fibrous, and less valuable.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ amɛ starch kpakpa he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni akpaaa amɛ. Tso lɛ baabɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ niyenii ni ekɛto lɛ yeli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Ehaa tubers lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, fibrous ni sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn yellow when planted in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full tropical sun. Planting them alongside companion crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid while the young trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer yields when I plant cassava on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas returns vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the seeds I saved from last season's harvest sprouting much weaker than the new seeds from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ miikwɛ̃ bibii kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their vigor in the next generation, and stored farm seeds often weaken if exposed to heat and moisture. Certified seeds are bred specifically for strong germination and high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Ni ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui ni ato lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off old or crowded branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egbɔ loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This reduces humidity inside the canopy, which prevents fungal diseases like Black Pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even during periods of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your main crop, effectively starving your plants even when there is plenty of water.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni jɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as intense heat waves or irregular watering. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he amanehulu. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ leebi?

english: Small ragged holes in young leaves are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm feeding. Catching these signs early allows you to treat the central whorl of the plant before the pest destroys the main growing tip.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm miiye niyenii. Kɛ́ omɔ okadii nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋta titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomato plants temporarily curl their leaves during peak afternoon heat to slow down water evaporation from their leaves. If they perk back up by evening, it is a normal self-defense mechanism against heat.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ akafee mlɛo. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba jogbaŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and dry up, and the inside of the pod shells shows dark brown or black markings when you pull up a sample plant.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni pod tso lɛ mli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛji ogbala nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi.

english: What happens if I leave my groundnuts in the soil too long past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: If left too long in the ground, groundnuts will start to sprout in the soil, the stems holding the pods will weaken and break off during digging, and the nuts become easily infected by rot and mold.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Peanuts baaje shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni hiɛɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ejaraa yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aŋɔ hela oya.

english: Why do groundnuts flower above the ground but form their pods underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After pollination, groundnut flowers produce long stalks called 'pegs' that bend downward and push into the soil, where the pods safely grow and mature away from light and surface heat.
ga: yɛ pollination sɛɛ Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Pods lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni la kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: What is the best way to handle my groundnuts right after digging them up so they do not spoil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu mi-peanuts lɛ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mifo amɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: After digging, dry the groundnuts on clean mats in the sun with the pods exposed to air until the seeds shake loosely inside, which prevents dangerous molds like aflatoxin from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbe naa lɛ, gĩ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni he tse nɔ. Gbimɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baahoso yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Does growing groundnuts help improve the soil quality for my other crops?
