ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛhaa mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops you plant in the next season, like maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nibii ni oduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some banana plants produce very large yields while others give tiny bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Fruit yield depends on the banana variety, adequate water and soil nutrients, and whether you prune excess shoots (suckers) so the mother plant gets enough energy to build big fruits.
ga: Yibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ banana henɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji obaafolɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eha tso nyɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: If I find a high-yielding banana plant growing wild, can I plant its shoots on my farm?
ga: Kɛ mina banana tso ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni miida yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can dig up healthy young shoots (called sword suckers) from a strong plant and replant them on your farm to grow new plants that share the exact same high-yielding traits.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii. Okɛ dumɔwui (ni atsɛɔ amɛ klante ŋmeii) kɛjɛ tsei ni wa amli ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei heei akwɛ̃. ni yɔɔ sui ni haa yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ

english: How do I know green bananas are mature enough to harvest for selling at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Bananas are mature when the fruits lose their sharp angular edges and become plump and rounded, even while the skin remains completely green.
ga: Banana shɛɔ dalɛ he beni aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: How can I keep my harvested green bananas from ripening too quickly before I get them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa koni akakpa mra tsɔ dani aya jara nɔ?

english: Keep harvested banana bunches in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight, avoid bruising the fruit, and do not store them near already ripe fruits like papayas or mangoes.
ga: Kɛ akwadu tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ aduawai lɛ ni ooofite lɛ he. Ni kaakɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ tamɔ papaya loo mango.

english: Why does my banana plant sprout so many young shoots around its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii babaoo ebɔle eshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Banana plants multiply by producing side shoots; you should prune most of them and leave only 2 to 3 shoots per mat so they don't steal water and nutrients from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Banana tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi tsei lɛ ashishifãi 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ yɛ mat kome nɔ bɔni afee ni okaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves in maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is under attack by pests like fall armyworms. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or using appropriate pest control early helps the crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua lɛ. Kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ loo okɛ mra be mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during heavy rains are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, cool weather. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ he koni hulu la babaoo aba nɔ, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: If crops from your previous harvest grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced small fruits, your soil is likely low on nutrients. Observing poor weed growth or getting a quick soil test from an extension officer can confirm if fertilizer is needed.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni okpa tsutsu lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ akwɛ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa oya ni mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kwɛɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ema nɔ mi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why do some farmers plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for maize. In return, the tall maize stalks give the bean vines something to climb on as they grow.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa wain tso lɛ naa nɔ ko ni ekwɔɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small tuber yield under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants bending and leaning towards one side of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ efo ehe kɛmiiya ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean toward sunlight to make their food. If large trees or structures shade one side of your field, the pepper plants will bend toward the open, sunny areas to get the light they need.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji tsei loo tsũi wuji tsi ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome naa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe kɛya he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa koni amɛná la ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashi amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots built to absorb rainwater and nutrients instantly. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing moisture and fertilizer meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ama koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest or buy certified seeds from a dealer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds from official dealers are specifically bred to yield more and resist local diseases and droughts. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and are more likely to carry diseases into your fresh farm.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai kɛ hɔmɔ ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba oŋmɔ ni akɛ sũ fee lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop insects and rot when I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli kooloi yɔɔ mli ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Grains rot and attract insects if they are not dried completely before being bagged, or if stored in a damp place. Residual moisture inside the grain allows mold to grow and creates ideal conditions for insect eggs to hatch.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa dani amɛwoɔ kotoku mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their flowers and turn black before forming good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛfee ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers and young pods turn black due to fungal black pod disease or insect attacks. Protecting the trees with proper spraying helps these delicate parts survive so they can develop into healthy, mature pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii amli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa nɛkɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni eda kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot so fast when the weather turns wet and cool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Cool, rainy weather creates high humidity, which is the perfect environment for the black pod fungus to multiply and spread quickly from pod to pod across your farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungus lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ pod mli kɛya pod mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa crop if I delay spraying during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Delaying spraying during the rainy season gives fungal diseases a chance to spread unchecked, which can quickly destroy most of your developing pods before harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo oya dani akpa.

english: Why do the fresh green shoots on my cocoa trees dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Young, juicy shoots are targeted by pests like mirids (capsids). They bite the stems to feed on sap, causing the shoots to dry out, turn brown, and die.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ kwɛɔ tsei bibii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ, ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ koni amɛye tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. gĩ ŋmeii lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ blɔfo ni egbo

english: Why do cocoa trees growing in full sunlight get attacked by bugs more than trees under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Insects like capsids thrive in warm, sunny environments. Cocoa trees exposed to full sun attract more pests, making regular crop protection even more important for open farms.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ. Cocoa tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baagbala tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe buu daa lɛ he hiaa fe tsutsu lɛ po kɛha ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: How do I know if insects are attacking my cocoa crop before the leaves start falling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi cacao tsei lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛgbee shi?

english: Early signs of bug attack include small dark spots on young stems, gummy liquid oozing from the bark, or twisted new leaves long before the tree leaves drop.
ga: Nɔ ni fata mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tutuaa amɛ lɛ ahe ji ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ, ni ji nu ko ni shwieɔ shi. ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi loo baai heei ni etsake dani amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing plenty of flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Tiny insects often attack cocoa flowers and flower cushions, causing the blossoms to fall off before they can be pollinated and turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tutuaa kookoo fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi akushɛi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pollin ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: How does spraying my cocoa trees help make the cocoa beans inside the pods bigger and heavier?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cacao tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa cocoa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛhe wa?

english: Spraying keeps pests from sucking nutrients out of the growing pods, allowing the tree to direct all its energy toward filling the beans inside.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Will spraying chemicals on my cocoa trees damage the very young pods?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii ni edako lɛ?

english: When applied properly in correct doses, recommended crop protection sprays shield young pods from diseases without causing any harm to the plant.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ falɛ ni sa mli Tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe ni ekɛ awui baaa tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe to spray my cocoa trees when the soil is very dry and there has been no rain?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafɔ kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: Spraying trees when they are stressed by extreme dry weather can burn leaves. It is best to spray when the crop has adequate moisture so it absorbs treatment safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie tsei anɔ kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ miihao amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water in its roots. The plant is not dead, and it will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu akahi eshishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots turn hard and woody inside when I cook them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become tough and woody if they are left unharvested in the ground for too long past maturity, or if the soil suffered from severe lack of water.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni akpaaa amɛ. aloo kɛji nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over easily before the bunches are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by pests or heavy rain. Heap soil around the base of the plant and support the main stem with a strong wooden prop to keep it standing.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ afite amɛ. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots to plant so they grow fast and bear good fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base—because they grow stronger and yield fruit faster than shoots with wide, leafy tops.
ga: Halamɔ ‘tsobii bibii’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse, tamɔ akpɔlɔ, ni amɛshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young orange trees drop all their tiny green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Citrus trees drop small fruits when they are stressed by uneven watering, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests. Regular feeding and mulching help the tree hold onto its fruit.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baaná aduawai bibii. Drops kɛji akɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni ejaaa mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Niyenii ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ aduawai amli.

english: What causes wavy shiny lines on my orange tree leaves, making them curl up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Those lines are made by tiny pests called leafminers feeding inside the leaf. Spraying young leaves with neem oil or targeted pest control protects the new foliage.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ nɛkɛ line nɛɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ baai shwielɔi ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashwie baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai heei ahe.

english: How do I know when a palm nut bunch is fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A palm bunch is ready when the fruits turn a bright reddish-orange and at least five to ten ripe fruits naturally loosen and drop to the ground at the base of the tree.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ 5-10 baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Should I cut off the lower fronds of my oil palm trees that turn brown and hang down?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efolɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, pruning dead and yellowing lower leaves helps the palm tree direct its food and water toward producing larger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egboi ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ kroko nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain together in the same field without them spoiling each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantain and cassava by giving them proper spacing. Plantain grows taller to get sunlight, while cassava uses lower space, allowing both to share the field well.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmei kɛ gbɛ ni sa. Plantains baakwɛ̃ ni amɛná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ he ko fioo. Enɛ haa amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛjaraa he ko jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds in a circle around the roots of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from your plants. Clearing a ring around each crop ensures all the soil nutrients go directly to growing your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Ring ni ebɔle he lɛ mlijiemɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii fɛɛ aya onibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What does potassium actually do to help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni potassium yeɔ ebuaa yɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts like a booster for plants—it strengthens their stems, helps them retain water during dry weather, and allows them to produce larger, healthier fruits and grains.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni kanyaa tsei. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishi ni eeefee ni ewa lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmaa ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are lacking potassium in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack potassium, the edges of their leaves usually turn yellow or brown as if they were burned, and the stems become weak and easily fall over in the wind.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ potassium lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, tamɔ nɔ ni ashã. Ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbee shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even when there is a little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Plants use potassium to open and close tiny pores on their leaves. Without enough potassium, crops lose water too fast and wither easily during dry spells.
ga: Tsei kɛ potassium tsuɔ nii kɛgbeleɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛŋaa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya tsɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What is the difference between the main nutrients in crop fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɔɔ srɔto?

english: Nitrogen builds green leafy growth, Phosphorus builds strong roots early on, and Potassium improves the size, taste, and disease resistance of the harvested crop.
ga: Nitrogen haa baa eŋɔli daa. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa mra. Ni potassium haa tsei ni akpa lɛ dalɛ, amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize cobs and cassava roots getting smaller every harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ miifee bibii be fɛɛ be lɛ? Nikpamɔ be?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every year. If key nutrients like potassium are not replaced, the soil becomes tired and cannot feed the plants enough to form large cobs or tubers.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa afi. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium lɛ eyaaa mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛŋ eha tsei lɛ niyenii bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my crops getting attacked by diseases more easily this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Just like ill-fed humans get sick easily, crops growing in nutrient-poor soil have weak cell walls, making it easy for diseases and pests to invade them.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ni ayeee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná hela oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ wala yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my root crops like yams and cassava need extra care with soil nutrients?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava he hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Root crops need extra potassium to move food made in the leaves down into the roots, which is what causes the tubers to swell and grow heavy.
ga: Shishifãi ahe miihia potassium kroko koni ekɛ niyenii ni afee kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ aya shi kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fũuɔ ni efeɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow while the plants remain short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: This usually means the soil is hungry for basic nutrients. When plants do not get enough balance of nutrients early in life, their growth stalls and leaf color fades.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni sa ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra lɛ, Baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhe su baaho aya.

english: When is the best stage in a plant's life to give it potassium fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ tso shihilɛ mli ni esa akɛ akɛ potassium awo mli?

english: It is best applied early in the plant's growth so roots can absorb it, and just before the crop starts flowering or forming fruit so it has energy for a full yield.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛwo mli mra beni tso lɛ miida lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. kɛ dani tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ loo amɛwo yibii koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aha nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and draw water out of the crop, causing leaves to scorch and plants to die.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã ni tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and getting scorched by the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted alongside them to act as natural umbrellas, keeping them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛnáa nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tip and moving down the middle in a V-shape is a clear sign that your crop lacks nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores green leaf growth and boosts crop yield.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves squeezed together with dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai kɛ corn baai ni ashɛre lɛ mli lɛ, muji yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing point of the plant. Checking fields early and applying recommended biological or chemical sprays directly into the leaf whorls will protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from my farm to plant a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a large, strong underground base. These produce healthier plants and heavier fruit bunches than 'water suckers,' which have broad leaves and weak stems.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo agbo ni wa. Enɛɛmɛi haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa fe ‘ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy, soggy soil for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, winds dry out the air, or watering is inconsistent. Providing light shade and keeping the soil damp during hot spells prevents heat shock.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli tse baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to train my yam vines to climb upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛtsɔse mi sweet potato tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make more food and grow larger, heavier underground tubers.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: How do weeds growing near my young crops actually affect my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives crops the space and food they need to grow strong yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for next season's crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, this nitrogen stays in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil for my crops when rainfall becomes irregular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry leaves, cut grass, or crop stalks—known as mulching—prevents water from evaporating, keeps the soil cool, and protects roots during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni bɛ nɔ ko ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi ni afolɔ, loo tsei ahe ŋmeii ni akɛhaa he lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why do my seeds need to stay buried in the dark soil before they can sprout into young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds need dark, moist conditions underground to absorb moisture and trigger germination. If left exposed on top of the soil, the harsh sun will dry them out and kill them before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ewo fɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛŋɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛwo amɛkwɛ̃mɔ he hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha amɛgbi ni egbe amɛ dani amɛdara.

english: How deep under the soil should I plant my maize seeds so they sprout strong shoot paths above ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni miyɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná ŋmeii ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plant maize about two to three centimeters deep. If planted too shallow, heat or birds will destroy them; if planted too deep in the darkness, the young sprout wastes all its energy trying to reach the surface.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Heat loo okpoi baafite amɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ duŋ mli tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to nurse my pepper seeds under a shaded nursery bed before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursing delicate seeds in a protected nursery guards the fragile young sprouts from direct hot sun and heavy rain, ensuring only strong, healthy plants are moved to your farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the cassava stem cuttings I collected from a neighbor will grow healthy tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni mijie kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaha amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Choose stem cuttings from mature plants that are free from disease signs like yellow leaves or twisted stems. Good cuttings should have visible, healthy buds or 'eyes' where the new shoots and roots will sprout.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he, tamɔ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ aná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni anaa loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi heei baajɛ mli aba.

english: Why do I need to clear heavy stones and heap loose soil high before planting my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tɛi ni tsii ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ama shi dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui akutsei lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow down into the dark earth. Mounding soft, stone-free soil gives the root tubers plenty of room to stretch outward and expand smoothly without hitting hard barriers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa gbɛtsii nii ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the tall trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting delicate young cocoa plants from heat burn and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes neighboring plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients underground, resulting in skinny stems and small plantain bunches.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa.

english: How do groundnut plants push their seed pods into the dark soil after flowering?
ga: Te ŋmeii tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛtsiɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, small stems called 'pegs' bend down and push themselves deep into the dark soil, where the nut pods safely swell and mature away from sunlight.
ga: Beni ŋmeii fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa yɛ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or pests are damaging the roots underground. Adding compost or poultry manure supplies the nutrients needed for dark green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kompost loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during dry afternoons even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni nu egbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly from leaves faster than roots can pull moisture from the dirt. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass retains moisture underground longer.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmeii ni afo lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Spacing cassava about one meter apart gives the roots enough room under the soil to grow big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ ŋmei wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ

english: Is it better to clear my farmland by burning the bush or by clearing it manually without fire?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ashãa nɔ loo akɛ niji aaatsumɔ ni akɛ la tsuuu nii?

english: Clearing without burning is much better because fire destroys natural nutrients and useful organisms in the soil. Clearing manually and letting weeds rot enriches your soil with free organic matter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ hi kwraa ejaakɛ la fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni akɛ niji jieɔ jwɛi lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow short and bent instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams become short or deformed when the soil underneath is packed too hard or contains rocks. Building high, soft mounds with loose soil gives the tuber space to expand downward easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes feɔ kuku loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni sũ ni mli tse yɔɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ haa tuber he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress makes the plant drop flowers to save its strength to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Heat haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during the rainy season. Trimming extra tree branches lets sunlight in and helps prevent the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni akafite.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily loosen in wet soil during strong winds, especially if tiny worms (nematodes) have weakened the roots. Supporting fruiting trees with bamboo poles keeps them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii. (Nematodes) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii fiɔ aduawai tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why is it important for me to rotate my crops instead of planting maize in the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting different crops like beans or groundnuts after maize breaks pest cycles and naturally restores nutrients to the soil, keeping your land rich without buying as much fertilizer.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How can I protect my stored maize from weevils without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can store thoroughly dried maize in airtight hermetic bags or sealed drums. Without oxygen inside the container, insects cannot survive or reproduce, keeping your grain safe.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni atsĩ naa mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ, kooloi nyɛŋ ahi shi loo amɛfɔ bii. Ha odumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is too waterlogged for their roots to breathe. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any pepper grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and shaded during the hottest part of the day helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Plantain leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and reduce water loss. Providing organic mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and prevents severe wilting.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa egbo waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes water to sit in the soil without draining, the roots drown and soil microbes cause them to rot, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges is recommended.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves and grass around my crop plants help them grow better?
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my crop plants grow very tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space allows them to receive enough light and nutrients to grow thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year if I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows pests to build up. Swapping maize with beans or cowpeas refreshes the soil by naturally adding nitrogen back into it.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tiny holes are caused by insects or caterpillars eating the leaves to grow. Checking under the leaves early in the morning allows you to catch pests before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Kplukai loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are weeds growing so much faster than my newly planted seeds after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui heei ni adu yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions and quickly consume moisture and nutrients faster than farm seeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to establish.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cocoa trees flowering heavily, but I am not seeing many cocoa pods growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi waa lɛ? Shi minaaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko ni miida?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated—either by beneficial tiny insects or manually by hand—to turn into pods. If flowers are not properly pollinated, they wither and drop off the tree without forming any fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ afee cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ koni ebatsɔ pod Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbo ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: What is hand pollination in cocoa farming, and how does it increase my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã minitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Hand pollination is the process of manually transferring pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools like tweezers. Doing this carefully ensures that a much higher percentage of flowers successfully turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nibii bibii tamɔ tweezers tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ ni afeɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli oha mlijaa 100 ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ omanye ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if I am doing hand pollination correctly on my cocoa flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ miniji miiwo mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If hand pollination is done correctly, the flower will not drop off after a few days. Instead, you will see a small green pod (called a cherelle) beginning to swell at the base of the flower stem within one to two weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee nine nɔ pollination jogbaŋŋ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeŋ shi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Obaana ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Fɔfɔi ahe tsei (ni atsɛɔ amɛ cherelles) lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfuɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishi yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli.

english: How do small insect pests affect whether my cocoa flowers turn into pods?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ náa bɔ ni mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pests like mirids or capsids feed on delicate young shoots and flower buds, destroying them before pollination can take place. Controlling these pests protects the flowers so they can successfully develop into cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids loo capsids yeɔ tsei bibii kɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni ekpãtã amɛhiɛ dani amɛfee pollin. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛye omanye ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my cocoa trees to give me a full harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ baakpa yibii babaoo?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing their first pods around 2 to 3 years after planting, reaching stable and high production levels by their 5th year of harvest if properly cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, ni ebaashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni nɔ kwɔ he yɛ kpamɔɔ afi ni ji enumɔ lɛ mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before reaching full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ gbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛ elɛɛmɔ he.

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of shedding extra pods it cannot support, or by fungal diseases like black pod. Proper feeding, good air movement, and hand pollination help reduce pod loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods, niyenii ni sa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni nyiɛɔ Kɛ nine mli pollination haa pods ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does trimming or pruning extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches, allowing sunlight and air to circulate through the tree canopy. This encourages the tree to put its energy into producing strong flowers and pods along the main trunk and branches.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔii ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: How often should I harvest ripe cocoa pods from my farm during the main harvest season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest ripe pods every 2 to 3 weeks during the peak season. Leaving mature pods on the tree for too long leads to over-ripening and disease, while harvesting them promptly encourages the tree to remain healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni eda yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine ni helai aba amɛnɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nikpamɔ woɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Does shade affect how well my mature cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be lɛ saa bɔ ni mi cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he?

english: While young cocoa seedlings need heavy shade to survive, mature cocoa trees need balanced shade and adequate sunlight. Too much shade reduces flower production, whereas good sunlight combined with adequate soil nutrients boosts pod yields.
ga: Nakai beaŋ lɛ, hɔɔŋ ni mli kwɔ he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ taoɔ hɔɔŋ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la kpakpa ni akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ baaye abua ni pod yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm so my trees yield maximum pods?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni mitsei lɛ aná pod yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer is best applied at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist. This provides the tree with essential nutrients right when it is developing new leaves, flowering, and forming pods.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛji baai heei, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ ba pɛ.

english: How do I know which crops will grow best in my area before I acquire land for farming in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Dani ebaahe shikpɔŋ kɛha okwaayeli yɛ Ghana

english: Different crops thrive in specific climatic zones across Ghana. Regions with heavy year-round rainfall are ideal for moisture-loving crops like oil palm, rubber, and cocoa, while crops like mangoes and cashews prefer drier regions with a clear dry season to flower and produce well.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Kpokpai ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ mu, rɔbɔt kɛ kookoo, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mango kɛ cashews sumɔɔ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be ni mli tse lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can I plant any crop I want anywhere in Ghana as long as the soil is fertile and there is water?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tso fɛɛ tso. Miisumɔ he fɛɛ he yɛ Ghana. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii ni nu hu yɛ mli lɛ

english: No, fertility and water are not the only factors. Crops also depend on local weather patterns, humidity, and rainfall amounts; planting a crop in an environment with too much humidity or rain can prevent fruiting and cause diseases.
ga: Dabi, jeee fɔmɔ kɛ nu pɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu damɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ekɛ helai aba.

english: What are the best crops for me to farm if my land is in a very rainy area like the Western Region?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: In high-rainfall areas like the Western Region, tree crops such as rubber, oil palm, coconut, and cocoa perform best because their roots and growth patterns are suited to constant moisture.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ, tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei tamɔ rɔba, mu, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ sa kɛha hulutsoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the roots of my crops rotting when there is heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain leaves the soil waterlogged, which starves the roots of oxygen. Without air, roots begin to die and rot, making it easier for soil-borne fungal diseases to attack the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi gboimɔ ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baatutua tsei.

english: Can too much rain actually harm my crops even if they need water to grow?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Yes, while plants need water, excess rain washes away important soil nutrients, promotes leaf and root fungal diseases, and can prevent fruit trees from setting fruit properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei he hiaa nu lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get more leaves with fungal spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in warm, wet, and humid conditions. High rainfall leaves moisture on plant leaves for long periods, creating an ideal environment for fungal spores to sprout and spread.
ga: Kwao lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni edɔɔ, nu, kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are my mango trees not producing good fruit even though my farm gets plenty of rain in the Western Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ anaigbɛ lɛ?

english: Mango trees require a distinct dry period to trigger healthy flowering. Constant heavy rain causes mango flowers to rot or drop off, and encourages the tree to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia be pɔtɛɛ ko kɛha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa mango fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi. ni awo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛshi baai moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii

english: Why do the flowers on my fruit trees keep falling off whenever heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops can physically knock delicate blossoms off the tree. Additionally, high rain and humidity cause flower blight, a fungal disease that rots flowers before they can form into fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa fɔfɔi fiteɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why is my fruit tree growing lots of healthy green leaves but giving me very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When a plant gets continuous water and nutrients without a dry stress period, it focuses its energy on vegetative growth (growing leaves and branches) rather than reproductive growth (producing flowers and fruits).
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni bei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛ hewalɛ maa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ. (baai kɛ tsei niji adalɛ) moŋ fe fɔmɔ dalɛ. (Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai afeemɔ)

english: Why do mango trees yield so much better in drier parts of Ghana than in high-rainfall zones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ fe hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Drier zones provide the clear dry spell that mangoes need to initiate flower buds, while also keeping humidity low enough to prevent fungal diseases from destroying the blossoms.
ga: He ni egbi lɛ haa be ni mli egbi ni mango biɔ koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi bɔ ni sa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akafee fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the upper leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient, or that the soil is waterlogged. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls the nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa tsei loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: This often happens when soil-borne fungi damage the plant's root system, causing root rot. Even though there is water in the soil, the damaged roots cannot absorb it fast enough to replace what the sun dries out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ fite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ lɛ oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nɔ ni hulu lɛ egbi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many dark leaves, but the tubers underground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium. The cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green foliage above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nitrogen fa babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he. Yucca tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil experiences sudden dry spells. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the useless bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hɔmɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehe ehiaaa.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them away from damp soil where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant produces a much larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily burn and dry out under direct, intense sunlight. Larger shade trees create a cool microclimate that protects young seedlings until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots. When the plants decompose, they leave this free nitrogen behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛye tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm crawls deep inside the leaf funnel during the hot part of the day to feed on soft new leaves while staying hidden from heat and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ

english: Why do weeds always sprout and grow much faster than my crop seeds after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and extremely resilient, resting in the soil for long periods waiting for moisture. They are adapted to germinate instantly and shoot up quickly to capture sunlight before cultivated seeds can establish.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui ni amɛhe wa waa. Ebaajɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ebaamɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Officer, I see some farmers building covered plastic house structures over their crops; how does growing vegetables inside them actually help my harvest?
ga: Amralofoi Mina okwaafoi komɛi ni miima plastic tsũi ni amɛkɛha amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Te aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikpamɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Growing crops inside a protected structure shields your plants from heavy rain, extreme sun heat, and destructive insects. This controlled environment allows crops to grow faster, suffer less disease, and produce much higher, better-quality yields than open fields.
ga: Tsei ni oookwɛ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ baabu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ Shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya. hela bɛ emli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ

english: If I spend money to improve my farming methods, what guarantee do I have that my crops won't fail?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ shika lɛ tsu nii koni mikɛha okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ aya hiɛ Mɛɛ nɔmimaa mafee akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efiteee?

english: While no farm has a 100% guarantee due to weather, following proper practices—like using good seeds, protecting crops from pests, watering correctly, and feeding the soil—drastically reduces risks and makes a successful, profitable harvest almost certain.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ ko bɛ ni 100% yɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ moŋ. But following proper practices, such as using good seeds Protecting crops from pests Proper watering and feeding in the soil This greatly reduces risk and ensures a successful and profitable harvest.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss and shield themselves from intense heat. However, if the yellowing stays, it usually means the crop is stressed from dry soil, lack of nutrients, or a early disease.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu naa ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo hela ko ni baa mra lɛ egba tso lɛ naa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences sudden stress, mostly caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like calcium and phosphorus needed to form the fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe trukaa. ni nɔ ni kɛbaa babaoo ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus, ni he hiaa koni aduawai aba lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach light instead of using that energy to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ eedara yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ ená la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tso nguanguahi nɛ a wa.

english: Why do seeds sprout nicely in my nursery bed but die soon after I move them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-nursery saatso lɛ nɔ shi amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings suffer from 'transplant shock' when moved abruptly into full sun and dry field soil. You need to water them well before moving them and transplant during cool late afternoons so they adapt gently.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa ‘Transplant shock’ he amanehulu kɛji akɛ adu amɛ trukaa kɛtee hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Obaasumɔ ni okɛ nu aha amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ amɛ adu ni okɛ amɛ awo shwane mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛhe ajɔ amɛ blɛoo.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning pale green because of poor soil or because of too much rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo hewɔ?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a main plant food that heavy rains often wash deep into the ground away from roots. Adding manure or fertilizer restores the deep green color and plant vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii titri ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant cassava or tomatoes on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply, leading to lower yields each season.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: What causes my watermelons to crack open on the field before they are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelons lɛ fãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛdaraa?

english: Watermelons crack open when they take up a sudden, large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer rind to split.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ atse

english: Officer, why do you advise me to cover the dry soil around my crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi abɔle he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around their roots, which stops them from taking up essential nutrients to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no miitsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi akɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, lack proper insect pollination, or do not have enough soil nutrients to support food production for pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Kplukai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Aloo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Yams are climbing plants, and staking spreads their leaves out to catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight helps the leaves make food, which travels down to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes miikwɔ tsei ni amɛmiifo amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems so the tubers can grow very big?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana ŋmeii wuji?

english: Planting cassava stems about 1 meter apart gives each plant enough space under the ground for tubers to expand without competing with neighboring plants for soil nutrients and moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How can I test if the crop seeds I bought will sprout well before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a quick germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days; if 8 or 9 sprout, your seed batch is strong and ready for field planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before heat sets in and reduces water evaporation, whereas afternoon watering can cause root stress and fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulutsoo lɛ baa, ni ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ aná haomɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Why is it good for my farmland if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing your land for the next crop season after maize has exhausted soil nutrients.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Beni ŋmãa lɛ eye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often brought on by uneven soil moisture when watering is inconsistent.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny brown powder behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ powda bibioo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Sɛɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding in the center whorl of the maize plant; they chew the young leaves and leave behind their waste product, requiring early pest control action.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ nibii ni fiteɔ nii. Enɛ biɔ ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai mra.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow strong stems and produce larger, healthier cobs.
