ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná shishifã ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil, taking away nutrients. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take natural plant food from the air and put it back into the soil, making it fertile again for your next crops.
ga: Abele haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii babaoo ni ejieɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha tsei nɛɛ afee yibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This yellowing in a 'V' shape usually means the soil is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ‘V’ ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and off the damp ground, which also prevents rot and disease.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai hu anaa.

english: Why is my maize plant producing flowers at the top before I see any corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii yɛ amɛyiteŋ dani minaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: The flowers at the top make fine dust called pollen. The wind carries this dust down to the silk of the young cob below, which is what actually causes the maize seeds to form.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ sũ bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ sũ nɛɛ kɛyaa ŋshɔŋloo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli tsɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmãa ŋmeii feɔ.

english: This is usually caused by a virus carried by tiny white insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this problem and keeps your yields high.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ hiɛɔ enɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa ni ebaaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Regular watering during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ he ko ni latsaa waa, nu bɛ, loo pollination lɛ ehiii. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why am I advised to cut off extra young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many extra shoots steal water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the plant food and water from the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early lets your crops get all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and healthy, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: What makes my farm soil become hard and dry so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or dead leaves, which normally act like a sponge to hold moisture and keep the ground soft for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crops when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three good, heavy rains so the soil is wet deep down, rather than planting right after the very first light shower.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni naa wa waa, ni naa wa waa enyɔ loo etɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the ground at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to grow if they were buried too deep in the dirt, if the ground was too dry, or if insects and birds ate them before they could sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ye lɛ dani ekwɛ̃.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, making all the plants weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ha tsei fɛɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, which is usually caused by sudden high heat, lack of regular water, or a shortage of plant food in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu ni hoɔ daa loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ bɛ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black spots on the bottom while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is irregular.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants naturally adapted to your soil and climate, so they can absorb water and plant food much faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nu ni amɛdu niyenii oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn in full sunlight, so taller plants provide gentle shade and cool moisture while the cocoa plants are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kookoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start to rot or sprout so quickly in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya waa yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when they feel warmth and humidity because they think it is time to grow, and they rot when small cuts on the skin allow moisture and mold to enter.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe edɔ ni amɛhe edɔ ejaakɛ amɛsusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. ni ebaafite kɛ́ pilamɔ bibioo ko yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables wilt and spoil so quickly when left in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, crops continue to breathe and lose water rapidly, especially in high heat. Keeping them cool slows down their breathing and water loss, extending their freshness.
ga: Kɛji akpa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ amu ni nu lɛ baaje mli oya. Titri lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ amɛha amɛhe jɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛmumɔ kɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ehee ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops at the bottom of heavy storage bags rot faster than the ones on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni tsii amli lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Excessive pressure crushes crop tissues and restricts airflow, creating warm, airless conditions at the bottom that accelerate spoilage and rot.
ga: Nɔnyɛɛ ni fe nine fiteɔ tso fãji ni etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ baa shishigbɛ ni haa nɔ ni fiteɔ kɛ fitemɔ yaa oya.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots develop dark streaks within two days of harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid internal chemical deterioration when exposed to heat and oxygen right after harvest. Keeping them cool immediately after harvest prevents this breakdown.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ aha amɛfee fɛ̃i amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen all at once inside my warm storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ fɛɛ miikwɛ̃ shikome yɛ mi nitoohe ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops release a natural ripening gas called ethylene, and warm temperatures speed up this process. Cooling the storage area slows down ripening so you can sell your plantains over a longer period.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. Kɛ́ afee he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ plantains be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does keeping my harvested tomatoes cold protect them from going bad?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tomato ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ friji mli lɛ baanyɛ abu ehe koni ekafite?

english: Cold storage lowers the crop's temperature, which puts the fruit's natural decay process on hold and prevents mold and bacteria from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why does my stored grain get hot and sweaty inside closed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ latsaa yɛ kotoku ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Stored grain contains moisture and continues to breathe, releasing heat into small spaces. Proper cooling and airflow remove this trapped heat to keep the grain dry and safe.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛmuɔ. Ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛyaa he bibioo ko Dɔlɛ ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ ni emɔ mli lɛ koni ŋmaa lɛ agbi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How does controlling the air pressure and ventilation inside a storage shed help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Regulating air flow and pressure distributes cool air evenly around all the produce, removing hot spots and stale ripening gases so crops stay fresh longer.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akudɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ jaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa Kɛtsɔ hei ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔi ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: How can I keep my harvested produce cool if high electricity costs make fridge storage too expensive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mikpamɔ lɛ mli ajɔ? Kɛji akɛ sarawa hewalɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ haa friji mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ jara wa tsɔ

english: Solar-powered cooling systems use energy directly from the sun to run cold storage units, eliminating monthly electricity bills while keeping your crops fresh.
ga: Hulu friji gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkudɔɔ fɛ̃i nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa srawa hewalɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni afeɔ daa nyɔɔŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ehee.

english: Can solar power really generate enough energy to keep a large crop storage room cold continuously?
ga: Ani hulu hewalɛ baanyɛ aha hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii atoohei wuji lɛ amli adɔ be fɛɛ be lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Yes, solar power systems store daytime energy in batteries or thermal cooling units to maintain a cold storage environment day and night without relying on the power grid.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu hewalɛ gbɛjianɔtoi toɔ gbi hewalɛ yɛ batrei loo thermal cooling units amli. Koni akwɛ koni shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ahi mli shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ ni akɛ he afɔ̃ɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛtswaa la lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to store my harvested fruits in a regular room or a solar-powered cold room?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ baato tsu ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ mli loo tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulu hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: A regular room stays warm and speeds up spoilage, whereas a solar cold room keeps temperatures low and constant for free, allowing you to hold produce longer until market prices rise.
ga: Tsu ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli baadɔ ni ebaafite oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be mli fɛ̃i tsu lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehiɔ shi daa ni aheee nɔ ko. Ehaa okɛ onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ jara nɔ jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do I have to cut down my whole cocoa tree when only a few leaves show sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ? Be mli ni baai fioo komɛi pɛ jieɔ hela he okadii akpo lɛ?

english: Diseases like swollen shoot spread under the bark and into the roots long before the whole tree looks yellow. Cutting down the infected tree quickly stops the sickness from travelling through the roots and air to ruin the rest of your farm.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofolɔ oya lɛ haaa hela lɛ akatsɔ shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛfite oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji krokomɛi?

english: Pruning removes excess branches that block sunlight and trap damp air, which cause black pod disease. Cutting them off directs the tree's energy and nutrients directly into producing bigger, healthier pods instead of just leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ. ni ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwo tso lɛ mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. yɛ baai kɛkɛ najiaŋ

english: How long should I wait before replanting new cocoa seedlings on land where diseased trees were cleared?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Waiting several months allows the old diseased roots in the soil to completely decay and die out. It gives the soil time to rest so your new seedlings will not catch the old sickness from the ground.
ga: Nyɔji babaoo ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agboi ni amɛgboi kwraa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei akaŋɔ helai momo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow if I plant them during August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji midu yɛ August mli lɛ?

english: In Ghana, August often sees a short dry spell where rainfall drops before resuming later. Planting right before or during this dry break leaves tender young roots without enough water to establish themselves.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ August yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku. Nugbɔ lɛ nɛ dani eku esɛɛ eba sɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii dani hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ loo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi aba.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers drop their leaves right after I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ baai amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes shock to the plant because its roots are disturbed and cannot absorb enough water immediately. The plant naturally drops leaves to conserve water until new roots grow to support it.
ga: Tso lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ haa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ haoɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto nu kɛyashi shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃ koni amɛye amɛbua lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn when I plant them in an open field without big plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa kɛ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting tall, fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade that protects the seedlings while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stems to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛlaaajeɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from heat stress, a lack of shade, or prolonged dry spells. Very heavy rains can also wash away the tiny insects needed to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo kooloi bibii kɛya. ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during severe dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its growing tubers underground. Once the rains return, the plant uses its stored energy to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni abu bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young trees before the main rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Tsei bibii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop trees once rain falls and will steal all the moisture and soil nutrients. Clearing them early guarantees your young trees get full access to food and water to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. ni ebaaju ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni okwɛ koni odumɔwui lɛ ana niyenii kɛ nu babaoo koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my tomatoes spoil so quickly if I wait until they are completely red on the vine before picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mimɛ ni wain tsei lɛ afee tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa dani mikɛ amɛ shwie shi lɛ?

english: When tomatoes reach full red ripeness on the vine, their skins become thin and soft, making them easily damaged during harvest and transport. Harvesting at the 'breaker stage'—when the green fruit shows its first blush of pink or red—allows the fruit to finish ripening safely off the plant while keeping its skin firm enough to survive transport to the market.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato lɛ fee tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ. Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Efiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ gbɛfaa mli. harvest at ‘Breaker stage’ lɛ ji be mli ni aduawai eŋɔlii jieɔ su ni ji pinki loo tsuru kpo klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso yibii lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni akɛya jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact right stage to harvest my tomatoes so buyers will pay a good price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛɛ bo he ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa tomato koni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ ni sa?

english: The best time to harvest tomatoes for market is when the bottom of the fruit starts turning from light green to a pale pink or orange color. Harvesting at this stage ensures the fruit stays firm, resists bruising, and has a longer shelf life, which market traders prefer over soft, overripe fruits.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa tomato ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ ji be mli ni aduawai lɛ ashishi jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enyɛɔ efiteɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni jarayelɔi sumɔɔ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ.

english: Why are my orange tree flowers falling off the branches before they can turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiiwo yibii lɛ?

english: Citrus flowers drop early mostly because of water stress during dry spells or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Providing reliable water during flowering and feeding the tree with organic manure or balanced fertilizer helps the tree hold onto its flowers and turn them into fruits.
ga: Orange fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi mra titri lɛ yɛ nu mli haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli kɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ amɛ yibii.

english: Why do my sweet orange fruits stay small, dry, and thick-skinned instead of getting big and juicy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet oranges lɛ ji bibii, ni egbi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Oranges need plenty of water and nutrients while the fruit is filling out. If the soil lacks moisture or nutrients during this period, the fruit stops expanding, resulting in a thick rind with very little juice inside.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ eyi lolo lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo niyenii bɛ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Yibii lɛ baakpa shweremɔ. Enɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo ko ni mli tse ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant seeds directly from an orange I bought at the market to grow a high-yielding tree on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ amli koni mikɛdu tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Growing oranges directly from market seeds usually produces wild, slow-growing trees that take up to 7 years to fruit and may produce sour fruit. It is better to buy grafted nursery seedlings, which grow faster, produce sweet fruit within 2 to 3 years, and resist common soil diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, citrus ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ haa koo mli tsei ni daa blɛoo ni heɔ afii kpawo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ baa, ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ citrus. Ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ, ni baakwɛ̃ oya. Ewoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why does tying my harvested vegetables tightly together in bundles make them rot faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ, ehaa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Tying fresh produce too tightly traps heat and airless moisture inside the bundle. This creates a warm, wet environment that allows bacteria and fungi to multiply rapidly, leading to soft spots, discoloration, and quick decay.
ga: Nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ baaŋɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni haa muawai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa oya. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, ehiɛ su tsakeɔ, ni efiteɔ oya.

english: How can I pack my fresh produce so it doesn't get crushed on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo nibii heei ni atswa lɛ amli koni ekakumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Avoid stacking heavy amounts of crop directly on top of each other in deep baskets. Use rigid, shallow wooden or ventilated plastic crates lined with dry grass or leaves to absorb shocks and protect the fruits from pressure damage during transport.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ tso ni wa loo plastic adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo mli koni ekɛjie shoofeemɔ. ni ebuɔ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: What causes my harvested tomatoes to turn soft and leak water a day after picking?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato ni mikpa lɛ mli nu lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nu hoɔ gbi ko beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes turn soft and leak water when they are harvested under strong, hot afternoon sun or handled roughly. Heat builds up inside the picked fruit, speeding up internal decay, so harvesting early in the morning when the weather is cool helps keep them firm.
ga: Tomato baatsɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ebaatsɔ nu kɛji akpa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ mli. Ehaa mligbɛ fitemɔ yaa oya No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa yibii lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha yibii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to collect seeds from my neighbor's high-yielding tomato crop to plant on my own land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahere mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tomato dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ayiwala ni madu yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Saving seeds from high-yielding hybrid varieties often leads to weak plants with low yields in the next generation. It is safer to purchase certified seeds from registered seed dealers to guarantee strong growth and uniform fruit quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo baa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe jarayelɔ ko ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Koni eha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aba nɔmimaa.

english: Why do orange prices go so high during certain times of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jara wa waa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Citrus trees have natural fruiting seasons, leading to shortages and high market prices during the off-season. Farmers can take advantage of high off-season prices by planting early-maturing or late-maturing citrus varieties and establishing basic irrigation.
ga: Orange tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo be. Enɛ haa nibii faaa kɛ jarayeli jara ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Okwaafoi baanyɛ aná jara ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ lɛ he sɛɛ kɛtsɔ citrus tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra loo ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛfee shishijee nu shwiemɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rains stay away for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ enɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells because dry soil prevents the plant from absorbing nitrogen, forcing it to draw nutrients from its lower leaves to keep the top growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná nitrogen. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: When is the right time for me to plant yam so that the tubers do not rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmeii koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam is best planted early in the dry season on well-drained mounds so the seed tubers can establish roots before heavy rains cause waterlogging and rot.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ sweet potatoes yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ shikpɔŋ gɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aha amɛtsɔ nu ni amɛgboi.

english: Why should I give space between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Giving cassava enough space ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients to develop large tuberous roots rather than competing and producing thin roots.
ga: Kɛ́ oha o-cassava lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni tamɔ tuber lɛ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe baabɔ akaŋ ni amɛha shishifãi komɛi

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same piece of land, and how will it help?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua?

english: Yes, cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on leaves and crawl into the central funnel of young maize to feed on the tender emerging leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni miiba lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck plant sap and spread viruses, which stunts leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ baatsi baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when rain splashes spores onto the pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less harvest every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting crops on the same land continuously depletes essential soil nutrients; without adding manure or fertilizer, the soil loses its fertility over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for fertilizer or if they are suffering from hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ fe nine?

english: Nutrient deficiency shows as specific color patterns like yellow leaf veins or purple stems on leaves, while heat stress causes whole leaves to wilt or dry at the tips.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: When cassava stays in the ground long past maturity, the roots turn their soft starch into tough fibers and wood to help the plant survive, making them hard to cook.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaada kwraa. Shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛ starch ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ fibers ni wa kɛ tsei ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi, ni no haa ewaa akɛ eeehoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when I plant them under certain big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Some big trees have very deep and heavy root systems that suck up all the nutrients and water from the ground, leaving nothing for young cocoa plants. Additionally, overly thick shade prevents the sunlight cocoa needs to make food and survive.
ga: Tsei wuji komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni amɛtsii. Enɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ eshiuuu nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛhaaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛfata he lɛ, hulutsoo babaoo tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa kookoo lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni ehi shi lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant my cocoa crops under any type of large tree on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashishi?

english: No, not all shade trees are good for cocoa. Some trees drop leaves or release chemicals into the ground that make the soil poor and suppress crop growth, so only specific shade trees recommended for cocoa farms should be kept.
ga: Jeee tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hi kɛha kookoo. Tsei komɛi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi loo amɛjieɔ tsofai kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ sũ lɛ ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ato tsei ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee shade kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ pɛ.

english: How much sunlight do my young cocoa seedlings need to grow well without dying?
ga: Hulu la enyiɛ he hiaa mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni egbooo?

english: Young cocoa needs a balance of light shade and indirect sunlight. Too much direct sun burns their young leaves, while too much shade causes them to become weak, stunted, and eventually die.
ga: Cocoa ni mli tse lɛ he miihia ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baashã baai bibii. Yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe afee shoo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaagboi lɛ.

english: How do thick weeds on the ground prevent my cocoa plants from thriving?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwere?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal vital groundwater and soil nutrients away from your cocoa roots. When they spread heavily, they physically choke the cocoa plants and trap too much moisture, creating conditions that rot crop roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Kɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã waa lɛ Etsiɔ cacao lɛ naa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni haa tsei shishifãi fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does the soil in some parts of my farm seem to become poor after weeds spread over it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite beni jwɛi egbɛ eshwa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When fast-growing weeds take over an area, they drain the soil's essential plant food very quickly. If they are left unchecked, they leave the ground depleted, making it hard for newly planted crops to establish roots.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ye jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei ni adu ehee lɛ akɛ amɛaafee shishifãi.

english: Is it bad to leave cleared weeds sitting on the soil right around my cocoa stems?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? mi kookoo tso lɛ

english: Yes, leaving heaps of green or rotting weeds directly against the base of your cocoa plant can create a damp hideout for destructive pests and fungal diseases that attack the trunk and cause the plant to die.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi eŋɔli loo jwɛi ni egboi ni abua naa yɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ afee hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii ni tutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: How often should I clear the ground around my young cocoa trees to keep them healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafo he ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should clear the ground around young trees every 2 to 3 months, especially during the rainy season when weeds grow fastest, to ensure the crop roots don't have to fight for nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie he ni tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya lɛ. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look weak even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough; crops need healthy soil rich in nutrients and room for their roots to breathe. If there is heavy root competition from nearby trees or dense weeds, the crop will remain weak and stunted.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ahe akaŋshii ni naa wa jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if the spot where I want to plant my cocoa has good or poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni misumɔɔ ni madu kookoo yɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo shikpɔŋ gbonyo?

english: Good soil is usually dark, moist, and crumbles easily in your hand. If the soil is very hard, pale, or surrounded by thick, woody wild weeds that choke out other plants, it is likely depleted and needs land preparation or fertilizer before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ediŋŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nine mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo koo mli jwɛi ni mli ewo wu ni ha tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ ebɔle he. Etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe baahia ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii.

english: Why do leaves on my cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up from the bottom moving upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant's roots are starving for nitrogen because neighboring weeds are taking all the nutrients, or that the soil around the roots is too waterlogged and poor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ejaakɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ miiná niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I know if the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest will sprout well before I plant them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can do a simple float test in water—discard seeds that float because they are dry or damaged inside—or place ten seeds in a damp cloth for five days. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni nu lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ egbi loo efite yɛ mli lɛ ni oooshɛrɛ ashwie lɛ nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛha gbii enumɔ Kɛji tsei kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to come up out of the soil even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to come up if they were planted too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if insects or birds ate them underground, or if the soil became too waterlogged and rotted the seeds before they could grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo okpoi ye amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them out allows each plant to get enough food and light to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eshishifãi ni mli tse kɛ eshishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the air moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is the plant's natural way of protecting itself. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to slow down water loss until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baa amɛhiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small, short, and woody when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii, kukuji kɛ tsei kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers are modified roots that need loose, well-tilled soil to expand. In hard or rocky soil, the roots struggle to push through the earth, which stunts their growth and makes them tough.
ga: Cassava tubers ji shishifãi ni atsake ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni egbɛ eshwa. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen acts like natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, drink water and food away from the main mother tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Baa nu nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni ekɛ plantains babaoo aba.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Tiny holes in the center leaves of maize are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the soft, growing parts of the plant. Catching this early allows you to spray or clear the pests before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tso lɛ fãi bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa afɔ loo ogbe tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I collect runoff rainwater on my farm and reuse it to water my crops later?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni mikɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, collecting rainwater runoff in simple farm ponds or dugouts allows you to store water during heavy rains and reuse it during dry spells, ensuring your crops get water when rain is scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni ooobua naa yɛ nubu bibioo ko mli loo ŋmɔ mli nubu mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni okɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil is cool and plants can absorb the water before the hot sun evaporates it away, helping you save water and keep the soil moist longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nu toɔ ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are receiving too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu bɔ ni sa?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl, or dry up. When they get too much water, the soil stays soggy and the leaves turn soft and yellow because the roots are drowning and rotting.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpã, loo amɛbaagbi kɛji amɛná nu babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why does water sit on top of my soil for a long time after rain instead of sinking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni ebaagbee shi lɛ?

english: Water pools on top when the soil is hard and tightly packed, especially heavy clay soil. Loosening the soil and adding manure or organic material helps rainwater sink deep into the root zone instead of wasting away.
ga: Nu ŋshɔ ko yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. titri lɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeeshi lɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass or straw around the base of my crops help keep water in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tsei ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass (mulch) acts like a blanket that shades the earth from the hot sun, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly and keeping the roots cool.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni okɛ jwɛi (Mulch) shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and droop so fast during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya yɛ Harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During hot and dry periods, plants lose water very quickly through their leaves into the dry air. If the roots cannot pull up enough soil water to replace what was lost, the leaves droop to protect the plant.
ga: yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛto nɔ ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Baai lɛ baagbi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do the roots of my crops stay shallow instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ shi moŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: If crops receive light surface watering too often or if the ground below is very hard, roots stay near the top where water is easy to get. Watering deeply encourages roots to grow downward searching for trapped underground moisture.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni mli tse nɔ shii abɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa waa. Shishifãi lɛ baabɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna nu yɛ mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ woɔ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ waa koni amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyatao nu ni mli ewo shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my vegetable flowers fall off before turning into fruit when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat combined with irregular soil water causes severe stress to the plant, making it shed its blossoms to save energy and water for survival instead of growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my crops develop rotten leaves when water stays on them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni nu eshwɛɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: When water stays on leaves for many hours, especially during cool nights, it creates the perfect environment for small fungal spores to hatch and infect the leaves, causing spots and rot.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo Titri lɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Nu lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛye baai lɛ anɔ hela. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do crops growing in low areas of my farm where water collects always look weak and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: When water collects and stands in low spots, it drives air out of the soil. Roots need air to breathe and absorb nutrients; without air, the plant starves and turns yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni edamɔ he ko ni baa shi lɛ Ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains provides natural protection and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hebuu haa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the plantain fruits start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbee shi kɛ́ plantain lɛ miitsii waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be weakened by soil pests or soft earth. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting it with wooden stakes prevents the stem from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli kooloi loo sũ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baanyɛ aha egbɔjɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ shishifã lɛ naa koni ekafo loo eshishifã.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower part of the plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow, so adding manure or recommended fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small holes and powdery dirt inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso bibioo lɛ teŋ lɛ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft tender leaves inside the funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early with recommended pest controls prevents them from destroying the growing heart of the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant suffers from heat stress or lack of water, it drops flowers to preserve its survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil with poor drainage. Excessive soil moisture cuts off air supply to the roots, allowing fungal rots to set in under the soil surface.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kpaɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Yam leaves generate energy for root tuber growth by catching sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into maximum light while keeping them clean from wet soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ haa hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya la ni fe fɛɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa ehe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil without soaking deep enough. If hot dry days follow, seed sprouts wither in the hot ground. It is safer to wait for steady, continuous seasonal rains before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa. Kɛji gbi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gĩ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ ni yaa nɔ dani oduɔ nii.

english: Why is it wasteful to put fertilizer on my farm while heavy rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away over the soil surface or deep underground past the crop roots before plants can absorb it. Fertilizer should be applied when soil is moist but not flooded.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants lose their leaves and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baa lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside them creates a protective canopy that reduces sun heat and retains moisture in the air and soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa tsũ lɛ yiteŋ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf surface to sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, allowing the leaves to capture sunlight efficiently to produce energy that grows larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie baa lɛ nɔ kɛha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii wuji shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizers helps restore green leaf growth and improves crop yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize make my farm soil richer?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, reducing the need for costly chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How does spreading dry palm leaves or grass around my crop roots help during the dry season?
ga: Palm tso lɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ Teɔ tɛŋŋ mitso lɛ shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from reaching the soil. This prevents soil water from evaporating quickly and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy soil and cuts off oxygen to the root system. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni efo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil stress. Consistent watering at the root level keeps the plant stable so the flowers can form tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ awo tomato yibii.

english: What causes holes in the leaves and small caterpillars inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Applying organic neem oil or recommended sprays early into the central funnel protects the plant from major destruction.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. kɛya gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ wulu ko he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from leaves. Spraying plants early with soap solution or botanical neem spray controls these pests before leaves deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ samla loo neem tso mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra. Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my previous maize harvest give me smaller yields when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved hybrid maize seeds lose their vigor and disease resistance in the second generation. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong growth and maximum grain harvest.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahere lɛ lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛkpaa dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why do rubber trees yield more liquid latex when they are tapped very early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni rɔbɔt tsei feɔ latɛs ni mli edɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Rubber trees build up natural water pressure inside their bark overnight. Early in the morning, when temperatures are cool and the tree hasn't started losing water through its leaves, this high pressure forces the latex to flow freely and abundantly when the bark is cut.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ buaa nu mli hewalɛ naa yɛ amɛhewolo lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛkɛ kome, leebi, beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni tso lɛ ejeko nu shishi kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa nɛɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ebɔi babaoo kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. Planting taller crops like plantains nearby provides shaded cover and traps soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do oil palm trees produce smaller fruit bunches if we don't prune the old lower leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji wɔfolɔɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ?

english: Old, dying fronds (leaves) continue to draw water and food from the tree without contributing to its growth. Pruning away these lower fronds allows the oil palm to direct all its nutrients and energy into growing bigger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Baai (baai) ni egbɔ ni miigboi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛhaaa tso lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛtsɔ nɛkɛ shishigbɛ baai nɛɛ ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ, mu tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfee aduawai akuu ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to save water. Shedding leaves stops moisture from evaporating into the hot air, allowing the plant to stay alive while its roots remain safe underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava gbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛbaahere nu. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaa. Ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to convert energy into plant food. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where they might rot, spreading the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight, which directly results in larger tubers growing under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsake hewalɛ ewo tso niyenii mli. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ saa ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the center vein of lower maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce food, so this yellow pattern means the crop is starving for soil nutrients.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eye niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni adu lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume plants like groundnuts and beans work with beneficial bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done, these roots decay and leave naturally rich plant food behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni emɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ naa lɛ Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii babaoo ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and shrink into tight balls instead of growing flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from new leaves, or by a virus spread by insects. The damaged tissue cannot grow properly, causing the leaves to twist and roll up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ Fãji ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada jogbaŋŋ, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, water supply is uneven, or bees are not available to move pollen inside the flower. Without successful pollination or under extreme heat stress, the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. Aloo ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye loo eyɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off the extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers growing together compete with the main mother plant for food, sunlight, and soil water. Removing excess shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main tree gets full nourishment to bear a heavy bunch.
ga: Tsei bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tso ni tsii.

english: I want to expand my farm and plant more maize this season, but how do I know if my soil is rich enough to yield a good harvest?
ga: Miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu ŋmãa babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: You can check soil fertility by its color, texture, and the types of wild plants growing on it. Dark, loose soil that holds moisture well and has earthworms is rich, whereas very sandy or hard clay soil will need compost, manure, or fertilizer to support a high yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii ehaa lɛ kɛtsɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ ahe su, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha, kɛ amɛhenɔi anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ shikpɔŋ ni tsii baabi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii koni ená yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops produce a huge harvest in the first year after clearing bush land, but produce very little when I plant on the same plot the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Crops feed heavily on natural nutrients in fresh soil during the first season. By the second year, those nutrients are exhausted, so without adding compost, animal manure, chemical fertilizer, or rotating with legumes like groundnuts, the soil becomes too tired to feed new plants.
ga: Tsei yeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ hee mli lɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but giving me very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi beni mikpa lɛ lɛ, ehaa bulbs bibii waa beni eyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from over-applying certain fertilizers or raw manure—the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots. Balanced nutrients ensure energy goes down into building large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ haa bulbs wuji daa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly gives each maize stalk enough room and food to grow strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ni he wa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly damp with mulch and proper feeding helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he amanehulu. aloo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, keeping them cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I tell the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps starting late?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to avoid planting after the very first rain, as it might be a false start. Wait until you get two or three steady rains within a week that soak deep into the dirt, ensuring the soil stays moist long enough for seeds to germinate and root.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afee shishijee ni ejaaa. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ otsi kome mli ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up, and why are they stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi? Ni mɛni hewɔ dalɛ hee lɛ kpaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or safe insecticides keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the tender center leaves of my young maize, and will the plant survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ? Ni te tsei baafee tɛŋŋ amɛhi shi?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the soft center leaves where new growth happens. If caught early, applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel of the plant stops the pest and allows the maize to recover and produce cobs.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ he ni dalɛ heei miiba lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ mra Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akpa ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ni ewo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting in the barn even though they looked healthy when I dug them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ moŋ?

english: Yams rot quickly after harvest if they suffer small cuts or bruises during digging, or if they are stored in a hot, poorly ventilated area. Handling tubers gently and storing them off the ground on well-ventilated wooden racks prevents moisture build-up and rot.
