ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ eyɛ fãji bibii loo etsɔ fãji bibii yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ okɛ bulb lɛ tsu nii blɛoo ni okɛto shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tso shĩa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabɔle ehe ni efite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh heat. They need shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, protecting them from full sun and keeping the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are many of the small flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed. Flowers drop when there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate them, or when the tree is short on water and nutrients to nourish every flower into a pod.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo beni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ aná hewalɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called water suckers, steal valuable water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing them leaves all the soil food for the main tree to produce bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii. Ejuɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, eshiɔ shikpɔŋ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ dɛŋ lɛ koni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by a wet-weather disease called Black Pod. High humidity and rainwater allow microscopic fungal spores to grow on the pods, rotting the shell and destroying the beans inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Akpɔlɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is running out of food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When the soil lacks food, leaves will turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, the trees will grow very slowly, and they will produce far fewer pods or fruits during harvest.
ga: Kɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo waa. ni ebaawo pods loo aduawai fioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do the leaves and young pods on my trees look dry and burnt like fire touched them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eshã tamɔ la etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called mirids or akate. As they feed on the stems and young pods, they inject a toxic liquid that causes the plant tissues to dry up and look burned.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ Mirid loo Akate. Beni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Amɛbaawo nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei amɛwo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me more yield at harvest time?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, skinny trees that produce small fruits and spread diseases quickly among themselves.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni woɔ yibii bibii ni helai gbɛɔ eshwãa oya.

english: Why does my crop yield a big harvest this year but very little in the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ shi afi ni baa lɛ wo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Trees use up vast amounts of energy to produce a large harvest. If they do not receive enough rainfall, fertilizer, or rest afterwards, they take the next season to recover energy rather than making new pods.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo nibii babaoo. Kɛji amɛnáaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ. Amɛbaaye be ni baa lɛ ni amɛkɛbaahe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee pods heei.

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their skin changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Picking them early leaves beans undeveloped, while picking late causes beans to sprout inside.
ga: Efee klalo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ ookpa mra lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink up soil water and take fertilizer away from your crops. They also block sunlight, depriving young crops of the energy they need to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi tsei ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when there is no shade on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and lose water quickly under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and humid so the young cocoa roots can keep up with the water needs of the leaves.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni edɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ atsu nu ni he hiaa baai lɛ ahe nii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food in the soil. When the plant cannot find enough food, it takes the nitrogen stored in its older bottom leaves and moves it up to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Eheɔ nitrogen ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop all its leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmatha be lɛ mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during the dry season as a natural trick to save water. Since leaves release moisture into the dry air, shedding them allows the cassava plant to survive safely underground in a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ ŋmei lɛ gbɛ ni egbee shi lɛ, ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stem without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or unequal watering. When conditions get too dry or hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for staying alive rather than spending energy to make fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food to build large underground tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground where fungal diseases like to grow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii koni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Staking hu haa baai lɛ eyaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii helai sumɔɔ ni amɛshwere yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors that suck up fertilizer nutrients and soil moisture much faster than your crops can. Even with rain, your crops remain weak because weeds are stealing the plant food hidden in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa, ni amɛmuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiju tsei aniyenii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When maize is crowded, each plant stretches straight up to fight its neighbors for sunlight. Because all their strength is spent growing tall to reach light, the plants have no energy left to grow thick stalks or fill out large cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso ja koni ekɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ enaanyo lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ awuu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse loo ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little rolls during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the hot afternoon is the plant's defense to protect itself from water loss. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the scorching sun, which prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ haa ebaa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plant wrinkling and twisting instead of opening flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips feeding on the soft tender leaves before they open fully. Their sucking damages the leaf tissue, causing it to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni efite lɛ baa. Amɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. ha efee nɔ ni efite

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before putting dry fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi abɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink it in. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil under hot weather prevents the crop from absorbing it and can burn the roots with concentrated mineral salts.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to keep the young top leaves alive and growing.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas in the field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores the soil nutrients that maize took away during the previous season.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni ŋmãa kɛtee yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains to put fertilizer on my crops instead of putting it on dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn and damage root tips and waste your money.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite. kɛ shika ni afiteɔ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more cobs on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ he koni maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very tiny maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves all the soil nourishment for the main tree so it can produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Removing them leaves all the soil nutrients for the main tree so that it can grow large, heavy branches.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni makwɔ ŋmei tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and prevents damp soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking keeps the leaves in high light and prevents disease in moist soil from rotting the leaves.

english: Why do my cassava leaves shed and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to stop water from escaping into the air. The plant is not dead; it goes to sleep to preserve water while the tubers remain safe underground.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ koni nu akajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni tuber lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without making pepper fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat damages pepper pollen and stresses the plant. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save energy until cool weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pepper pollen ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my tomato plants with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Black pod is caused by tiny water molds that multiply and spread in wet, cool conditions. Raindrops bounce off the wet soil and splash these mold spores directly onto your cocoa pods.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii bibii ni faa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my crops grow better than in my open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or glass house that protects crops from extreme sun, heavy rain, and destructive pests. It creates a controlled environment where plants like tomatoes and peppers can grow faster, stay healthy, and produce food all year round.
ga: Greenhouses ji plastic greenhouses loo greenhouses ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni tsei tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. baanyɛ adara oya Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why do greenhouse tomatoes produce so much more fruit than the ones I grow on my open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni akɛwoɔ greenhouse mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tomato ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: In a greenhouse, plants receive constant water, balanced nutrients, and total protection from insect attacks and intense weather. Because the crops are not stressed by heat or heavy rain, all their energy goes into producing plenty of fruit.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ, tsei naa nu daa. niyenii ni ja ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni baatutua lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ fɛɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the market prices for my vegetables fall so low every time my whole village harvests together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ jara baa shi nɛkɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa akrowa muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: When many farmers bring the exact same crop to market at the same time, the market gets flooded. Because there is more produce than buyers need, buyers offer lower prices knowing farmers must sell before the vegetables spoil.
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ba jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, nu shwieɔ jara lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fa fe bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa, ejaakɛ amɛle akɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ dani aduawai lɛ afite.

english: How does growing my crops during the off-season help me get better prices at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ jara kpakpa nɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: During the off-season, vegetables are hard to find in the market, but buyers still want them. Because supply is low, buyers are willing to pay much higher prices for whatever fresh produce you can harvest.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ewa akɛ aaana aduawai yɛ jara nɔ, shi mɛi ni heɔ lɛ miitao amɛ lolo. Akɛni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa kɛha nibii heei fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural survival trick to protect itself from extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture inside the leaf from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekafo oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean the plant is under water stress. To save whatever water is left in its system, the crop purposely sheds its older leaves so it can keep its stem and growing points alive until rain returns.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu haomɔ shishi. Bɔni afee ni ajie nu ni eshwɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anyɛ ato tso lɛ shishi kɛ hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my crops to grow lots of healthy flowers but fail to form any fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruits when plants are stressed by high heat, lack of water, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Excess nitrogen fertilizer can also make crops grow big leaves while dropping their flowers before fruiting.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai wuji yɛ be mli ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my vegetable plants growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops stretch upward rapidly to fight each other for sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and light to grow sturdy stems and broad leaves.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ.

english: Our elders always say to plant immediately after the first rain, so why are my young seedlings drying up shortly after?
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain does not always mean the rainy season has fully started. Early false rains are often followed by long hot spells, which dry out young roots before the true, continuous rains begin.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni eyaa nɔ.

english: Why does planting the same crop on my farm year after year lead to smaller harvests over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haaa yibiiwoo aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: The same crop drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that attack that crop to build up in the soil. Changing crops each season helps the soil recover and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains together with cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains ni kookoo tsei yɔɔ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and provide essential shade to protect young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight, while their heavy stems hold moisture in the soil to help the cocoa survive its early stage.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni tsii lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua kookoo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Can young cocoa trees grow well on my farm without plantains next to them?
ga: Ani cacao tsei bibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni plantains bɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and dry out easily under full sun. Planting plantains alongside them provides needed shade and acts as a natural water reservoir for the young cocoa roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni akɛtoɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do plantain trees help my cocoa plants get enough water?
ga: Te dumɔwui baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantain stems store a large amount of water inside them. When the plantain matures or is cut, this stored water releases into the ground for neighboring cocoa roots to drink.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ kɛ nu babaoo toɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa loo afo lɛ Ajieɔ nu ni ato nɛɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni kookoo shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anu.

english: What happens to the water inside a plantain stem when I cut it down?
ga: Mɛni baa nu ni yɔɔ plantain tso mli lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifo mli?

english: The water trapped inside the cut plantain stem slowly leaks out into the surrounding soil, giving nearby cocoa plants a steady supply of moisture.
ga: Nu ni emɔ plantain tso ni afo lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya fiofio. shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli Enɛ haa kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be.

english: How does leaving chopped plantain stems on the ground help cocoa trees during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ ashi banana tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Chopped plantain stems act like wet sponges on the ground, slowly releasing moisture directly into the soil where the cocoa roots can absorb it during dry spells.
ga: Plantain tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ, ni ejieɔ nu ni mli edɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ blɛoo. ni kookoo shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ.

english: What should I do with my old plantain stems after harvesting the plantain fruit?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee plantain tsei momoi lɛ beni akpa plantain lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Instead of throwing old stems away, you should cut or uproot them and leave them near your cocoa trees so the moisture left in the stems can feed your cocoa.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ tso lɛ tso momo lɛ oshwie Esa akɛ ofo loo ojie shishifãi lɛ ni okɛma cacao tso lɛ masɛi koni ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ aha cacao lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers cut down plantain stems after a couple of years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: After a couple of years, the plantain stem has stored plenty of water. Cutting it down releases all that trapped water directly into the soil for the cocoa tree to absorb.
ga: Yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ hu toɔ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, nu fɛɛ ni emɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo tɛ̃ɛ koni cacao tso lɛ aŋɔ.

english: Will big plantain trees steal too much water away from my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji lɛ baaju nu babaoo kɛjɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: While a plantain tree grows, it draws water, but once it reaches full size and is cut down, it returns all that stored water back to the soil for the cocoa tree to use.
ga: Beni dumɔwu lɛ daa lɛ, egbalaa nu, shi beni tso lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he lɛ, afoɔ lɛ. Ekɛ nu fɛɛ ni ato lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni cacao tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How long should I keep plantain trees growing alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi? Be enyiɛ kookoo tso hiɔ shi?

english: Plantains are usually kept for the first couple of years until their stems grow big. After that, they are cut so that the cocoa gets full access to the space and stored water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ plantains toɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ daraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, afoɔ amɛ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ aya he ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni ato yɛ mli lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Does uprooting an old plantain stem harm the nearby cocoa trees?
ga: Ani plantain tsei momo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ awui?

english: No, uprooting or cutting an old plantain stem actually benefits the cocoa because the water left in the roots and stem is absorbed by the cocoa plant.
ga: Dabi, plantain tsei momo ni ajieɔ loo afoɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha kookoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni eshwɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baaŋɔ.

english: Yellowing in young maize leaves usually means the plants are starving for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the dirt, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It is not caused by an insect or a spreading disease, but by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Jeee kooloi bibii loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa. Shi nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants and leaving black dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni ashiɔ muji diŋŋ yɛ mli?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant, so any control spray must be directed straight down into the funnel early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awo faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the air moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto wooden sticks or poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei loo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground with poles allows the plant to absorb more sun and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hulu la babaoo. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slower and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. If you leave weeds in the field, they steal the food your crops need to produce food.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛná niyenii.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ yitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why don't seeds saved from my last maize harvest grow as well as new seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ hu?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum yield in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that vigor and will produce smaller stalks and fewer grains.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui fioo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which plants need to grow leaves and make food, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni amɛfee niyenii Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I clear my land for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani mafo mli kɛha dumɔ?

english: If your previous harvests were much smaller than before, or if weeds on the field look stunted and pale, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni baa shi kwraa loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops immediately after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and lie dormant in the soil, allowing them to absorb water quickly and outrun farmed crops to capture early sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu oya ni amɛjoɔ foi fe ŋmɔ mli nibii ni adu lɛ koni amɛná leebi hulu la lɛ.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava stems instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Spacing allows each cassava plant to get enough sunlight, air, and soil moisture without competing with nearby plants, which results in larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa baa.

english: Will planting cowpeas on the same plot as my cassava hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, cowpeas actually support cassava because their roots capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, providing natural plant food for your cassava.
ga: Dabi, cowpea fiɔ ŋmei sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha o-cassava.

english: Why should I spend money on certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ lɛ ahe? Mohu ɔ, i du wuhi nɛ i he kɛ je nyagbe kpami be ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases and yield more food, whereas saved seeds weaken over generations and can carry hidden diseases into your field.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu ni ewo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to full sunlight during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong direct heat, which is why they require temporary shade plants like plantains to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni cacao tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers during the hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heat is too high and water is scarce, tomato plants drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent themselves from dying.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ gbele he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, common pests in Ghana that target the tender growth centers of maize plants to feed on moisture and young plant tissue.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ koni eye ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe fãji.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when I leave them exposed under the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight heats up the skin of harvested yams, causing them to lose moisture rapidly and creating ideal warm conditions for mold and rot bacteria to enter the tuber.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli adɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. ni ehaa hulutsoo shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ abote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward like tiny cups during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing too much water under the strong afternoon sun, though it can also mean tiny insect pests are feeding under the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛyeɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi po.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the maize plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or lacks enough moisture to feed its lower leaves properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii loo ebɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce good nuts even when I do not apply nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nitrogen wooo mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a special plant family that works with beneficial soil bacteria in their roots to produce their own nitrogen straight from the air.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei aweku krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛfee nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but have tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much rich nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days or nights are too hot, or when there is too much rain, which stops the flower from getting proper pollination to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo gbɛkɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines turn yellow and die off right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: The dying back of yam vines is natural; it shows the plant has finished growing leaves and has pushed all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber, showing it is ripe for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni miigboi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tsei. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe baai lɛ akwɛmɔ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi. ni tsɔɔ akɛ etsu kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do my cassava stems produce white milky water when I break them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ mliki kɛ́ mikumɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: The milky sap inside cassava stems carries water and stored food throughout the plant, helping it stay alive even during dry weather periods.
ga: Nu ni tamɔ mliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ woɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛyaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po.

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a microscopic fungus that spreads easily in dark, wet conditions. Trimming extra branch shade lets sunlight and air dry out the pods to keep them healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have strange yellow and green spot patterns on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow and green mosaic patterns are caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies; using healthy, disease-free stems for planting is the best way to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mosaic ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ eŋɔli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii beni aduɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, a vital plant nutrient. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves what little it has from older, lower leaves up to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli. Okɛ baai lɛ aba shi kɛya ŋwɛi koni shweremɔ hee akafite.

english: Why do my cassava stems keep growing tall and bushy, but the underground tubers stay very small?
ga: Why are the cassava trees still tall and bushy? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive moisture, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing top leaves and tall stems instead of storing energy in big roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai kɛ eshishifãi kakadaji lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi wuji amli lɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain shoots alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight and dry wind. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I rotate my maize with groundnuts or beans next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Maize consumes heavy amounts of nutrients from the dirt, while groundnuts and beans have roots that actually trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing it for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread easily, allowing the plant to generate more food to build larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. ni etsĩ enaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ he ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay small and soft when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete heavily for moisture, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leaving no single plant with enough food to form a firm, big head.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli waa. Akɛni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branch before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark foliage during heavy rains. Clearing excess farm weeds and pruning cocoa branches allows air and sunlight in to dry out and stop the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ ni mli efɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly inward and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe waa kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects that steals nutrients from the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ

english: In intense afternoon sun, water leaves the plant through its foliage faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to shrink its surface area and conserve internal water.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nu shĩɔ tso lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato flowers become stressed and the pollen dries up, causing the flowers to fall off instead of developing into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tomato.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is performing well early in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Healthy maize plants will have thick stems, broad dark-green leaves, and steady growth, which shows that the soil has enough nutrients and moisture to support a strong harvest.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Baai ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow so quickly during good rainfall but stall during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai amli shi amɛfeɔ ais yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Corn relies heavily on water to carry soil nutrients up through its roots and stems, so adequate rain triggers rapid growth while dry weather causes the plant to conserve energy and slow down.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ waa koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya kɛtsɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo.

english: What causes my corn cobs to stay small or missing grains even when the plant looks tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibii loo ŋmãa ni bɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Poor pollination during the flowering stage, often caused by extreme heat or drought when tassels appear, stops the grains from filling out evenly on the cob.
ga: pollination ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa beni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baatsi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni eyi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why does the selling price of maize in town change so suddenly from month to month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jara tsakeɔ trukaa daa nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize prices in town shift based on overall crop supply, seasonal availability, and changing transport costs like fuel or vehicle fares needed to move produce from farms to markets.
ga: Abele jara ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ naa. Be mli hesaamɔ kɛ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo ni tsakeɔ, tamɔ gas loo tsɔnei ni he hiaa koni akɛjie nibii ni adu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya jara nɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo.

english: How does high transport fare to the market affect the profit I make on my harvested corn?
ga: Te shika ni fa ni mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ saa sɛɛnamɔ ni mináa kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Higher transport charges increase the total cost of getting crops to buyers, which reduces your net profit unless market prices rise enough to cover the extra fare.
ga: Nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baaha shika fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ ni oyɔɔ lɛ aba shi. ja jara lɛ nɔ jara lɛ tee hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu tsɔne he nyɔmɔwoo ni fata he lɛ he nii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks sufficient nitrogen, causing the plant to pull remaining nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my corn crop need extra fertilizer right before it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering and cob formation require massive energy, so feeding the plant extra nutrients right before this stage ensures maximum cob size and full grain development.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo waa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ dani nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ baashɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo ni amɛshwere jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my corn at the start of the rainy season give a better yield than planting later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo kpakpa fe nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early planting allows the crop to maximize the full duration of rain and moderate temperatures, building strong root systems before harsh dry spells set in.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa. Too shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa aba.

english: Why do some maize varieties survive dry spells better than others in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Certain improved maize varieties develop deeper root systems and retain leaf moisture better, allowing them to withstand brief droughts that wilt traditional varieties.
ga: Abɛi henɔi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ yɛ baa lɛ mli nu ni amɛhiɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo ni haa blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to dry my corn thoroughly before storing or selling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmãa dani akɛto loo ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Drying corn prevents moisture build-up that causes mold, rot, and insect attacks, preserving grain quality so it can fetch a higher price at the market.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ naa. shwiemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that acts like food for growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant cannot produce enough green chlorophyll to catch sunlight, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow first.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha dalɛ Beni nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hulu la. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani nibii babaoo baaba?

english: No, planting crops too closely causes them to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough room to spread its roots and produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ekɛ ŋmei wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt even when the soil has plenty of water after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: When soil remains flooded with too much water, plant roots drown because they cannot get air. Drowned roots begin to rot and stop absorbing water, which makes the plant leaves droop as if the soil were completely dry.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lolo lɛ Tse shishifãi lɛ baagbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ. Shishifãi ni ebote nu shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni ekpaa nu ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tamɔ nɔ ni sũ lɛ egbi kwraa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant nutrients. Under high heat, the plant saves energy by dropping flowers it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant maize under the shade of big trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Maize needs direct, unshaded sunlight all day to make food and grow full ears of corn. Growing maize under big shade trees prevents sunlight from reaching the leaves, resulting in thin, weak stems with few or no grains.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni enyɛ ehoo ni ekwɛ̃ abele toi ni eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same soil every season drains the specific nutrients that crop uses and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and reduces disease.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: How exactly do weeds make my crops grow weak and small?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow strong. When weeds grow close to your crops, they consume the soil nutrients before your plants can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe Nakai jwɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages their small root tips, leading to root shock. If you transplant them under a hot sun, the seedlings dry out before their damaged roots can take in water; transplanting in the cool late afternoon helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashishifãi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji okɛdu yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ shishi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi dani shishifãi ni efite lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli Ye obua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava tubers taste bitter while others from a different season taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi ni jɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally produce bitter chemicals as a defence mechanism when exposed to drought stress or harsh soil conditions. Adequate soil moisture and timely harvesting prevent the roots from becoming bitter.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa baa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa kpe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ be naa lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better for my vegetable crops if I water them in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the air is cool, allowing the soil to absorb the water down to the roots before the hot sun evaporates it off the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli dani hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them provides living shade that cools the soil and protects the young plants until they are mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaabu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, and holds moisture without staying flooded. If water sits on top of your soil for days after rain, the land holds too much water, which can rot the roots of your cocoa trees.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni nu shwieee nɔ. Kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: It is not ideal because cassava grows dense leaves that block light and aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients from young cocoa. Plantains or legumes are better companions because they provide gentle shade and enrich the soil.
ga: Enɛ ejaaa ejaakɛ ŋmei yɛ baai ni mli tse ni tsiɔ la naa kɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei bibii amli lɛ. Plantains loo legumes ji nanemɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Many flowers fall off because they were not pollinated by tiny insects like midge flies, or because the tree does not have enough nutrients and water to feed all the growing pods at once.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ midge flies lɛ shwieee amɛ nɔ, loo ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi ni miida lɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why is an extension officer telling me to cut off some good branches from my healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji kpakpai lɛ? Kɛjɛ mi koko tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cutting selected branches, or pruning, lets sunlight and fresh air reach the middle of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing big cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni ahalaa ni afoɔ loo afoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cocoa before I get my first harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onine ashɛ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take between 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my trees to turn black and rotten before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Weeding regularly, pruning extra branches, and plucking off infected pods quickly will help keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning yellow and dropping during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water. Spreading dried grass or leaves around the tree base as mulch helps keep moisture in the soil during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ shi. Tsei ashishi tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why should I not plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can get more trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting trees too close makes them compete for water and nutrients, resulting in weak trees. Close spacing also stops airflow, creating damp conditions where diseases like Black Pod quickly spread.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Spacing hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni no haa helai tamɔ black pods gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color completely changes from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting pods when they are green means the beans inside will not be fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru kwraa nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen naturally from the air and feed it into the soil, leaving free natural fertilizer behind for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, cassava plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, spending all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of expanding their roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ená la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small seeds like tomatoes only have a little stored energy; if buried too deep, they run out of energy before the shoot can reach the surface and get air.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii tamɔ tomato lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtoɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ dani tu lɛ shɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ ni enáa kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some extra branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak branches so the tree does not waste energy on extra leaves, directing all its water and nutrients into growing bigger and healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get stressed when weather gets too hot or dry, causing them to drop flowers to save water rather than trying to feed growing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: On hot days, plants lose moisture into the air faster than their roots can suck water up from the soil, so they temporarily collapse their leaves to prevent drying out.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekagbi.

english: Why does ginger prefer growing under tree shade while maize needs full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei sumɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Crops have different natural habitats; ginger evolved on dark forest floors where direct sun burns its leaves, while maize needs strong, direct sunlight to build its stalks and grains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhei srɔtoi. Ginger ba yɛ koo ni mli ewo duŋ mli he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa ebaai lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia hulu la ni naa wa, ni tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do insect pests attack my weak plants more than my strong, healthy plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mitsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy plants produce natural defensive chemicals that turn pests away, whereas weak or thirsty plants give off scents that attract insects looking for easy food.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ko ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast when I pick them in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpaa nii lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested in the hot afternoon carry high internal heat, which makes them breathe faster and rot quickly compared to crops picked in the cool morning.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ waa lɛ yɛ mligbɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛmuɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ oya. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni abua naa yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe

english: Why do extension officers always tell me to build soil ridges instead of planting directly on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi be fɛɛ be akɛ amɛma shikpɔŋ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni amɛaadu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Making ridges loosens the soil so roots can grow deep easily, prevents heavy rains from washing your topsoil away, and keeps crop roots from rotting in standing water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shɔŋŋ oya. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu ŋmei tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbote he lɛ mli babaoo?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants with very small roots or tubers instead of a large harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii loo bulbs yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Can using net covers on my nursery beds really protect young crop seedlings?
ga: Ani saatso nɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi akwɛmɔhe lɛ baanyɛ abu dumɔwui bibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, fine net covers act as a physical shield that keeps destructive insects away from tender seedlings while still allowing sunlight, air, and water to reach them safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔŋloo kpakpa ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akaje dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu shɛɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do seeds planted in a nursery bed sprout so much better than seeds I sow directly into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ saatso wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery beds provide loose, rich soil, gentle shade, and regular moisture, protecting delicate seeds from hot sun, heavy rain, and soil pests during their weakest stage.
ga: Nursery saatso lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ. kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa Ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the crops planted at the very edge of my field dry out faster than the ones in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Plants on the outer edge receive direct wind and full sunlight from all sides, which makes them lose moisture much faster than plants sheltered inside the main field.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛhe shwieɔ nu oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up the flower pollen. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and water so it can survive the heat wave.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions, so their strong root systems absorb rainwater and soil nutrients instantly, faster than domestic crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi ni he wa lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. oya fe shia tsei ahe dumɔwui

english: Why is it important to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruit off the damp soil where soil-borne diseases live, while also allowing air and sunlight to pass through the plant to prevent rot.
