ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai kɛ aduawai akahiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekafite.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rain pattern keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi? Beni nugbɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Maize needs steady moisture right after planting to sprout. Instead of planting after the very first light rain, wait until the soil stays consistently moist after two or three strong rains so the seed doesn't dry up and die underground.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually point to cassava mosaic disease, spread by tiny whiteflies, or a lack of plant nutrients. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and keeping the farm weed-free helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ nɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu ni oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant cowpeas and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good for your land. Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a free fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni aheee nɔ ko

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, insufficient watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during dry hot days helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I store my harvested yams so they do not rot before I can sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yams rot quickly when kept in hot, damp, enclosed spaces. Storing them in a raised, shade-covered, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them cool, dry, and safe from ground pests.
ga: Atomo fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, ni edɔ ni atsĩ naa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛ̃i, egbiɔ, ni ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from market tomatoes and plant them on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ tomatoi amli lɛ ato ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: While you can plant them, market tomatoes are often hybrid seeds whose offspring produce lower yields or get sick easily. Buying certified seeds from an accredited dealer ensures strong growth and better yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu tomato yɛ jara nɔ moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome, ni amɛshwiei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo loo hela mɔɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What causes Fall Armyworms to attack my crops, and how do I catch them early?
ga: Mɛni haa Fall Armyworms lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ amɛ mra?

english: Fall Armyworms are caterpillars hatched from eggs laid by moths on green crop leaves, especially maize. Inspect your young crops weekly for small holes in the center leaves so you can treat them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworms ji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai eŋɔli anɔ lɛ amli. titri lɛ ŋmãa Kwɛmɔ otsei bibii lɛ daa otsi kɛji bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ koni onyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Water your vegetables early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering during the hot middle of the day causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni oooha yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: I am starting a farm for the first time; what simple crop can I grow that matures quickly?
ga: Mijeɔ ŋmɔ shishi klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni makwɛ oya?

english: Vegetables like okra, cucumber, or leafy greens are great choices for beginners because they mature in 60 to 90 days, require simple land management, and provide quick returns to support your farm setup.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ okra, kukumba, loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ. Akɛni nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ nyɔmɔwoo aha oya koni eye ebua oŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my crops grow better than relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ pɛ nɔ ni mikɛaafɔ̃?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly, but animal manure improves the soil itself. Manure helps sandy soil hold water longer, keeps the earth loose for root growth, and releases nutrients slowly over time.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ fɛo. Manure yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. ni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo fiofio Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if excess water stays around the roots for too long.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without tall shade trees or fast-growing crops like plantains to block the harsh sun, the delicate cocoa leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink, causing the plant to burn.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Delicate cocoa baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ashãa

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high temperatures, a sudden dry spell during flowering, or too much fertilizer that forces the plant to grow green leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Gbimɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to yield heavily in the first generation. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the offspring lose that special vigor, leading to uneven growth, small cobs, and low yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Seshi lɛ baafite hewalɛ kroko. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa, ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots grow thin and crooked instead of thick and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of unbroken clay, the roots struggle to push outward, forcing them to stay small, thin, and twisted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo shikpɔŋ eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ yɛ bibioo, eyɛ mlɛo, ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the plant right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani amɛtsɔ tsuru lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when heavy water or sudden rain follows a long dry period. The inside of the tomato rapidly swells with water, but the outer skin cannot stretch fast enough to hold it, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nugbɔ nɛ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli baafu oya kɛ nu. Shi kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo mli. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: If I plant my maize very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting too closely makes crops compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of many healthy cobs, you will get weak, tall stalks with very small or empty cobs, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Obaaná ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛlɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my young maize crop so quickly right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest moths hide in surrounding wild grass during the dry season. As soon as rains trigger fresh, green maize leaves to sprout, adult moths lay hundreds of eggs on the young plants, causing sudden outbreaks.
ga: Akpɔlɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ koo mli jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Kplukai ni eda lɛ woɔ wuji ohai abɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ. ni kɛ hela ko ni baa trukaa lɛ baa

english: Why does my harvested yam rot so fast when stored in a closed barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni agbe mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. Storing them in hot, enclosed spaces with poor airflow causes moisture to build up on their skin, creating ideal conditions for fungi and rot to destroy them.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba ohewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take so many weeks to sprout new leaves after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo dani ewoɔ baai heei beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A transplanted plantain sucker must focus its energy on growing new roots underground before it can push out new leaves above ground. Soil that is too dry or unmulched slows root development and delays green growth.
ga: Esa akɛ suckers ni atsake amɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ ama shishifãi heei ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi baai heei kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo ni awoko nɔ ko lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ oya, ni ehaa tsei lɛ hu daaa oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield their leaves and keep the soil moist while their root systems are still small.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground around my young crops with dry grass help them survive the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha he ni mi dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating under the hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crop.
ga: Hay lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: I want to start growing coffee, but how does a coffee bush produce its fruit compared to cocoa?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi kɔfe dumɔ. Shi te kɔfi tso lɛ woɔ yibii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto kookoo he?

english: Unlike cocoa where pods grow directly on the main trunk, coffee bushes produce clusters of small berries along their branches. These berries start green and turn bright red when they are fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Esoro kɔfe tsei yɛ kookoo he yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɔfi tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ yibii nɛɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ tsuru ni mli tse kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How do I know when my coffee berries are mature enough to pick from the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kɔfi yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Coffee berries are ready for harvest when they turn from green to a deep cherry red. Harvesting only the bright red berries ensures that the coffee seeds inside are fully developed.
ga: Kɔfi yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛtsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee cherry tsuru ni mli kwɔ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tsei ayibii tsuji ni kpɛɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni akɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when rain falls continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ otsii babaoo ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains cause waterlogging and poor drainage, the roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly cause the tubers to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu shwieɔ shi ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why does my plantain plant give smaller bunches when I allow all the small shoots around it to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main mother plant to direct all its energy into producing a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects or if the tree experiences water stress and extreme heat. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot support to save its energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ he ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ehe koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do I get bigger yams when I support the yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii wuji anɔ beni mikɛ tso ni kɛlɛ fiɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture the food that builds the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines high into the air so the leaves receive maximum sunlight to feed the growing yam.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ he koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Do my plants really need fertilizer, or can they just feed on the regular soil on their own?
ga: Mi tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii waa. Aloo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛna niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Just like people need good food to stay strong, crops exhaust the nutrients in the soil over time. Fertilizer acts as extra food for the plants so they can grow big leaves and produce healthy pods.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛfataa tsei ahe koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Can I use kitchen waste or food scraps to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shĩa mli jwɛi loo niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, but food scraps must first decompose into compost. When organic matter rots naturally in the soil, it converts into nutrients that plant roots can easily drink and use.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ afee niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Atsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu ni amɛkɛtsu nii mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry and lacking soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn yellowish, their stems remain thin, and they grow much slower than healthy crops nearby.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni edaa blɛoo kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Is it good to leave dry fallen leaves around the bases of my crops?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ mabɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ?

english: Yes, leaving dry leaves on the ground creates mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the dirt so the roots stay cool, and as the leaves rot, they feed the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Mulch lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni kɛ́ baai lɛ gbo lɛ Ebaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some new cocoa varieties produce pods much faster than the old trees my grandfather planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi heei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii oya kwraa fe tsei momo ni minaa du lɛ?

english: Improved varieties like 'Cocoa Nkrumah' or hybrid cocoa are bred specifically to mature early and produce pods in two to three years instead of waiting five or six years.
ga: Akwɛ kooloi srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ‘Cocoa Nkrumah’ loo cocoa hybrids lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ afii enumɔ loo enumɔ

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wilt and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and small roots that cannot hold much water. High heat burns them quickly if they are exposed to direct, strong sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ ato nu babaoo. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ ehe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many green leaves but very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi cocoa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: If a cocoa tree receives too much nitrogen or grows too thick with branches, it uses all its energy making leaves instead of flowers and pods. Trimming excess branches helps the tree make pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo eniji lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Should I clear away all the big trees in the bush before planting my new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: No, you should keep some tall forest trees. Young cocoa needs shade from bigger trees to protect it from harsh sunlight and maintain humidity in the air.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji lɛ ekomɛi ahi shi. Kookoo bibioo lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions. They quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your main crop needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ oya.

english: Is pouring traditional offerings on the soil the same as feeding the crops?
ga: Ani kusum afɔlei ni afɔseɔ ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: While traditional customs show respect for the land, crops cannot feed on whole foods directly. They can only absorb broken-down minerals and decomposed organic matter through their roots.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema kusumii tsɔɔ bulɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ aye niyenii muu lɛ fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjie shika tsuru ni ekumɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them correctly allows each plant to grow strong stems, develop healthy roots, and yield bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifã ni wa. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni okɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aha

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ Aloo sũ lɛ mli nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply liquid fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is mild. Hot midday heat causes the solution to evaporate quickly and can burn the plant's leaves.
ga: Okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ. Gbi teŋ dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni eshãa tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and reduces leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni ebaa baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ shi

english: Plantains have broad leaves that catch strong winds and shallow root systems that hold weakly in soft, wet soil. Staking the tree with a strong wooden prop supports the weight of the fruit bunch and keeps the tree standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he nii, kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my pepper plant shed its flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought stress, or very wet soil. Maintaining regular watering and providing light shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping, the main stem turns woody, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant where the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Yitso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. Removing affected pods quickly and pruning excess branches helps airflow and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya ni afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ hela lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that burrows into the leaf whorl of young maize. Early spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and removing infected plants prevents the virus from damaging your whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Early Whitefly Control Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves. When the soil runs out of nitrogen or gets too waterlogged, the plant cannot make food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do we plant cassava by burying stem cuttings instead of using seeds like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔduɔ ŋmãa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni wɔduɔ yɛ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa najiaŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava stems store food and active growth nodes that sprout roots quickly. Planting stem cuttings produces stronger roots and larger tubers much faster than growing cassava from small, slow-growing seeds.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ dalɛ he nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ toɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba oya fe ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing heavy underground tubers. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents ground moisture from rotting the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden lack of water. When it gets too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save water and protect itself from dying.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, which is a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid weather. When heavy rain drops stay on the pods for too long, the fungus spreads and destroys the pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite pod lɛ.

english: How do dry seeds in the soil know that the rainy season has started so they can start growing?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni egbi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ leɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seeds stay dormant when dry, but once rainwater soaks through their outer shell, it triggers chemical signals inside the seed that wake it up and tell it to push roots into the wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ kɛji amɛgbi, shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu tsɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ, amɛwɔɔ. Ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ feɔ okadii ni teɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛɔ lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon but stand back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli shi amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl and droop in peak afternoon heat to reduce the leaf space exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too fast. Once the sun goes down, the plant recovers its water balance.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nu ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow while standing in flooded water when water kills my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ be mli ni edamɔ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Beni nu lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Swamp rice has special hollow spaces inside its stems that act like tiny air pipes. These pipes carry oxygen from the air down to the roots, allowing the roots to breathe even underwater.
ga: Khao Bueng yɛ hei krɛdɛɛi yɛ etso lɛ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei bibii. Nɛkɛ paipii nɛɛ woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi po.

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground to get pollinated, but the actual nuts grow underground. After pollination, the flower stem grows downward to bury the seed pod where it is safe from sun and heat.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha pollination, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi koni amɛfu dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he abuɔ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees drop leaves when they get too much direct heat and lack soil moisture. Providing shade trees and mulching around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and conserves water during dry spells.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Shading kɛ mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only tiny insects called midges pollinate them. If the farm is too dry or lacks rotting plant material where midges live, pollination fails and the unpollinated flowers simply fall off.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo tsei ni fiteɔ ni midge lɛ hiɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and helps air move freely, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, hɔɔŋ, kɛ nu ni efɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and develop yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava right inside my main cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots grow deep and consume a massive amount of water and soil nutrients, which starves young cocoa trees. It is better to plant cassava on the borders of your farm rather than right next to cocoa.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei bibii. Kasava ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ko naa lɛ hi fe ni aaadu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard after growing maize on the same land for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa beni mikɛ afii babaoo edu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy nutrients from the ground without giving much back. Repeating this without resting the land or adding manure breaks down the soil structure, making it hard and poor for future crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ nɔ ko kwraa haaa. Kɛ́ afee nakai ekoŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of year for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied early in the rainy season when the soil is damp. Applying it in heavy rain washes it away, while putting it on dry ground can burn plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaho lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow. Tapping a ripe pod also makes a hollow sound because the seeds inside have loosened from the inner shell.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru mli kɛtee yellow-orange Kɛ́ atswa ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu, ehaa gbee ni mli ewo muji baa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my maize produce small ears with many missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ toi bibii ni ŋmeii babaoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when maize plants lack water or nutrients during the flowering stage, preventing proper pollination. Giving plants enough water and compost when silks appear ensures full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ha tso lɛ beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or urea around the base of the plant helps restore their green color and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tso lɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: How should I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should plant cassava stem cuttings at a slight angle or straight into the soil with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down will prevent the roots and shoots from growing properly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo loo okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ehaaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree experiences extreme dry weather, pest attacks, or does not get properly pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Keeping shade trees and maintaining proper soil moisture helps pods form successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mɔ. loo ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli tse jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and rot at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Watering your tomato plants consistently and avoiding letting the soil dry out completely prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛtsi naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb tall stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow large, healthy tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the ground, helping your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early with organic sprays like neem oil or recommended insecticides helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I select plantain suckers with narrow leaves instead of broad leaves when setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala plantain tsei ni baai lɛ mli tseee lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves have stronger roots and more energy stored in their underground corm, which leads to faster establishment and bigger plantain bunches than suckers that produce broad leaves early.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shishitoo oya kɛ plantain tsei wuji fe ŋmeii ni woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why is it so important for me to clear weeds from my farm during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crop a head start so it can grow strong enough to cover the ground and shade out future weeds.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ aje shishi oya. Enɛ baaha eda waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ shwie shi ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does lowland rice grow better when there is standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa folo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally adapted to thrive in waterlogged soil, while shallow standing water prevents most weeds from sprouting and competing with the rice for plant food.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi babaoo naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa akaŋ koni amɛye tsei niyenii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older leaves at the bottom to feed the growing young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Kɛ́ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy with large leaves but produce small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ jwɛi agbo ko ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry grass and leaves on the surface of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass and leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during hot dry spells, and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ejara mli fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Large shade trees protect them from heat and help keep the air humid until the cocoa plants are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Without mild conditions and moisture, the plant aborts the flower before fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Kɛji shihilɛi ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be bɛ. Tso lɛ baaŋmɛɛ fɔfɔi ahe dani ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insect pests like flower thrips often attack and destroy the cowpea blossoms before they can transform into pods. Protecting the flowers during the blooming stage ensures those flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ flower thrips Bei pii lɛ, amɛtutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛfɔɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Vines left on the hot ground get shaded and diseased, resulting in much smaller yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai yeɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree stay on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Allowing too many side shoots, called suckers, creates heavy competition for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Sɛɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ amɛ fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo aba.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to plant my maize seeds after the early season rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli shishijee lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one light rain is risky because the seed may sprout and then dry up if rain stops. Waiting until rain soaks deep enough that a handful of soil stays in a soft ball when squeezed ensures seeds have enough steady moisture to survive.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ ji oshara ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ sũ lɛ fã ko afee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashɛre. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize turn yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or the plant is sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage keeps the plants green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii loo tso lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛaawo mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant's juice, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling insect pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ Early Pest Control Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain floods the ground for days, water replaces the air, causing underground rot fungi to multiply and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant gets irregular water. Without cool temperatures and steady water, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ lɛ Tsei hu baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight for energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil into the sun, which prevents diseases and helps the underground tuber grow much bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbele amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why does my maize produce small cob ears with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ toi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains on a maize cob happen when hot weather or drought damages the moist silks during flowering time, preventing wind pollen from fertilizing every grain.
ga: Kernels ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hɔmɔ kpata siliki ni mli efɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekawo dumɔwui fɛɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same farm plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests build up in the earth. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove weeds from my crop farm while the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing them early prevents weeds from starving your crops before their roots get established.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ anaa dani amɛshishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot dry days, stops weeds from growing, and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or the roots are suffocating from too much standing water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or clearing drains to remove excess water helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. tso niyenii ni he hiaa Aloo shishifãi lɛ amli nu efo kɛjɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ ni akɛjieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller harvests when I plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific soil diseases to build up. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba shikpɔŋ henɔi komɛi anɔ Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to heat and burn under direct sunlight. Retaining larger shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a protective canopy that provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more corn in the end?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Yɛ naagbee lɛ, ani wɔkpaŋ ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete aggressively with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stems with small or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing allows each plant to mature fully and yield large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ feɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rainwater sits in the soil without draining, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges encourages water to run off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo shwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ egbiɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year arrives?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start, followed by a dry spell that can scorch and kill newly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent so the young sprouts have reliable moisture to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture. Watering deeply in the late afternoon or early morning helps keep roots hydrated through the hottest hours.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before they turn into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of key nutrients. Covering the soil with mulch keeps moisture around the roots and helps the plant retain its blossoms until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. shishifãi lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii

english: How do tiny caterpillars manage to destroy my corn leaves so quickly in just a few days?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpãtã mi-abele baai lɛ ahiɛ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm reproduce rapidly and feed continuously on young leaf tissues inside the heart of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm regularly allows you to spot egg patches early and manage them before the caterpillars multiply and ruin the crop.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ daa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mra. Ni nyɛkwɛa amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ ayi afa ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to grow slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛfee bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves in your field, consuming the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your main crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your main crop gets all the resources necessary for a strong harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii julɔi yɛ oŋmɔji amli, ni amɛyeɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves dry out very quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler, moist environment that protects the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo baa. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing that starts at the bottom leaves and moves upward usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant regain its healthy green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni eyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are mature enough to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and shedding, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also dig up one plant at the edge of the farm to check if the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa tso kome hu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving broad chew marks?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni eshi ŋmɔlɔ he okadii wuji.

english: Ragged holes inside the leaf funnels of young maize are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended treatments or neem fruit extracts can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem aduawai amli nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa enɛɛmɛi dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus. Watering regularly at the roots and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi amli daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will grow unevenly, produce smaller cobs, and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji obua naa ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ edaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa cob yibii bibii ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or straw around your plants acts as mulch. It traps moisture in the soil during dry spells, keeps the roots cool under hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant garden eggs in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting crops from the same family in the same soil continuously allows pests and soil diseases to build up and multiply. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas breaks disease cycles and restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa ni amɛshwere. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Pruning them so that only the main tree and one strong sucker remain ensures your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso titri lɛ pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray liquid fertilizers or water on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu loo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to water or apply foliage liquids is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. During midday heat, water evaporates too fast before plants can absorb it, and liquid droplets on leaves can scorch under hot direct sunlight.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nu loo akɛ nu awo baai lɛ anɔ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ enɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I do not plant plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni miduuu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight when they are young. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides fast-growing broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ ni daa oya ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing that starts from the lower leaves of a maize plant usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green leaves, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and sunlight to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi kwɛŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings will not sprout if they are planted upside down, cut from weak or diseased stems, or planted during severe dry spells. Ensuring the stem buds face upward and planting in moist soil helps them sprout quickly.
ga: Kasava ni afo lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Afo kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. aloo adu yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ ni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do I need to build wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa tso kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant receives inconsistent water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during hot spells help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ ná nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying appropriate organic or chemical controls stops insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akpa.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives roots enough time to absorb water before the peak sun.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnu nu dani hulu lɛ shɛɔ he ni eshɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts on my farm help the maize crop I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. When the groundnut crop is harvested, the leftover roots add free plant food that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei tsei Shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ fataa he.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the root area cool, and prevents wild weeds from growing and taking nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: I hear some farmers hire machine operators to harvest their corn. How does hiring an operator work for a farm like mine?
ga: Minu akɛ okwaafoi komɛi heɔ tsɔnei ahe nitsulɔi ni amɛkpaa ŋmãa. Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ aaaŋɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi tamɔ mi?

english: Hiring combine harvester operators saves time and reduces crop losses during harvest. Operators usually charge per acre or take a small portion of the harvested grain as payment. To use them, your farm path needs to be cleared of big stumps and rocks so the machine can move freely.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ tsɔne kudɔlɔ ni kpaɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa be baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ biɔ shika yɛ acre kome mli loo amɛheɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ fã ko akɛ nyɔmɔwoo. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛtsu nii Esa akɛ Oŋmɔ gbɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ tɛi wuji bɛ mli koni otsɔnei lɛ anyɛ aya he fɛɛ he.

english: Does using a machine to harvest my corn damage the grain compared to picking it by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Machine harvesting does not damage corn if the crop is fully mature and dry. However, if the corn is harvested while still too wet or soft, the machine's sheller can crush the grains. Waiting until the crop reaches the right dryness prevents damage.
ga: Tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ efiteee ŋmãa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni egbi. Shi, kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Mashin lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ ŋmãa. Kɛ́ omɛ ni tso lɛ agbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Where can I find affordable machine operators to help harvest my crops when farm labor is hard to find?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana tsɔne ni jara waaa ni baaye abua mi ni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: You can locate affordable harvesting operators through local farmer groups, agricultural mechanization centers, or by contacting your district extension officer. Booking an operator early before the peak harvest season often gets you better rates.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona ŋmaakpamɔ nitsulɔi ni jara waaa kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akui anɔ. Agricultural Machinery Center loo okɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ agba sane Okɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo aba mra Dani ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛbaahã bo nyɔmɔwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: After I finish harvesting my corn, is it better to sell it immediately at the farm or dry and manage it myself?
ga: Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Aloo ehi akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ obaagbi ni okwɛ nɔ?

english: Selling immediately gives you quick cash and avoids storage risks, but prices are usually lowest right after harvest. Drying and storing the corn yourself allows you to wait and sell when prices rise, provided you have a dry space to protect it from mold and insects.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ haa onáa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekwaa nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe oshara. But prices are usually lowest after harvest. Kɛtsɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ o-ŋmã ni ooogbi ni okɛkpa lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ omɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ. Esa akɛ he ko ni egbi ahi koni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why does my harvested corn start rotting or growing mold even after I have gathered it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested corn still contains moisture from the field. If it is stored in sacks or piled up without proper sun-drying, heat builds up inside and creates mold. Spreading the corn out to dry in the sun until the grains are hard prevents rotting.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ yɛ nu ni jɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lolo. Kɛ akɛto kotokui amli loo ato he kome ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he. Heat builds up inside and causes mold. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa koni ekɛtsi ŋmãa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my stored corn grains lose weight and turn into powder after a few weeks?
