ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ fo ni etsɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weight loss and powder in stored corn are caused by insects like weevils eating the inside of the grains, combined with natural moisture loss. Storing your dry corn in hermetic (airtight) bags stops these pests from destroying your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli shwiili kɛ powda ni baa shi lɛ baa ji kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa mli ŋmeii lɛ. kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni laajeɔ lɛ fata he Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so it doesn't spoil on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn is ready for harvest when the leaves turn completely brown and dry, the husks turn tan, and the grains become hard. Leaving corn on the field too long after this stage exposes it to birds, rain, and fungal attack.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. The shell turns tan. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ oshara mli kɛha okpoi, nugbɔ, kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do corn prices drop so low right after the harvesting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara baa shi nɛkɛ beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Prices drop during harvest because almost all farmers in the area are harvesting at the same time, filling the market with plenty of corn. When supply is high, buyers offer lower prices, but prices gradually rise months after the harvest ends.
ga: Jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli ejaakɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaa ŋmaa yɛ be kome mli. ni haa jara lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kɛ ŋmãa Beni ŋmãa ni akɛhaa lɛ fa Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baaha jara ni baa shi. Shi jara lɛ baaya hiɛ fiofio Eyaa hiɛ nyɔji komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ naagbee sɛɛ.

english: Why is it sometimes difficult to buy harvested corn directly from local farmers even when the crop is available?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ewaa akɛ abaahe ŋmãa ni akpa kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɛ po lɛ?

english: Many farmers pre-sell their harvest to traders who gave them loans early in the season, while others hold onto their grain expecting higher prices later. Building direct agreements with farmers before harvest helps secure access to produce.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo hɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ amɛhaa jarayelɔi ni haa amɛ nyɔmɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi Mɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli kɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ akɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ejara baaya hiɛ. Kpãŋmɔi ni akɛ okwaafoi feɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani akpaa nii lɛ haa anyɛɔ anáa nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can small farmers like me group together to get better prices for our harvested corn?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi afee ekome koni amɛná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha amɛ ŋmãa ni amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: By combining your harvested corn into one large batch with other farmers, you can attract wholesale buyers who pay higher prices for bulk amounts and save on transportation costs.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni okpa lɛ ni okɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi baafee ŋmãa agbo kome lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala mɛi ni heɔ nibii babaoo ni woɔ jara babaoo kɛha nibii babaoo lɛ, ni okɛ shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ akato.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need regular water to form flowers and pods. During the dry season, the trees conserve water and energy by stopping pod production until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia nu daa koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ buɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ pod feemɔ ni amɛkpaa lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I keep my crops from drying out and dying when there is no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagbo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can place a layer of dry leaves or grass around the base of your plants. This is called mulching, and it traps water in the soil so the sun does not dry out the plant roots quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni hulu la akaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi oya.

english: What other crops can I plant on my cocoa farm to harvest food when cocoa is off-season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi manyɛ madu yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makpa niyenii kɛji kookoo be lɛ eshɛɛɛ?

english: Planting food crops like plantains, cassava, or cocoyam alongside young cocoa trees gives you food and money during the dry months when cocoa trees are not bearing fruits.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantain, cassava loo cocoa ni okɛ cacao tsei bibii duɔ lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ mli ni cacao tsei lɛ wooo yibii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi? Be ni miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Removing weak or crowded branches allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which encourages healthy flowering and prevents energy from being wasted on useless foliage.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni mli ewo wu lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa hewalɛ ni afiteɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees yield fewer pods every year even when I work hard on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their natural ability to produce pods drops. Replanting old sections of your farm with fresh seedlings will bring back high yields.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa kɛhoɔ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui heei tsake hei momo ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to leave big shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa leaves from harsh direct heat, keep the farm humid during hot months, and prevent soil from drying out too fast.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ

english: Heavy rain creates high dampness which causes Black Pod disease to spread quickly. Clearing excess shade and pruning trees lets sunshine dry the pods and prevents rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni ehaa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off the tree before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks enough water, shade, or nutrients, or when insects attack them before they can form into small pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, hɔɔŋ, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua amɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How do I know if my soil has become tired and needs extra plant food to produce cocoa well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii krokomɛi koni ekɛ kookoo kpakpa aba?

english: If your plant leaves look yellow instead of dark green and the trees stop growing well, the soil is missing key nutrients that can be restored with organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast when rain falls, and how does clearing them help my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oyayaayai kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Weeds love rainwater and rapidly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees. Clearing them leaves all the nourishment for your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi sumɔɔ nugbɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ofɔ amɛhe lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha onibii titri lɛ.

english: How long does a yam crop usually stay in the ground before it is fully mature for harvesting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most traditional yam varieties take about 8 to 12 months—roughly a full year—to grow underground from the day you plant the seed piece until they are completely ready for harvest.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 (aaafee afi muu fɛɛ) dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛjɛ gbi ni odu dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ klalo kwraa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Around which month of the year do farmers usually begin harvesting yams in Ghana?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi jeɔ ŋmeii akpamɔ shishi yɛ Ghana yɛ afi lɛ mli mɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ?

english: Yam harvesting typically begins around July or August when the early rains end, marking the start of the new yam season across many regions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato ŋmaa lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ July loo August mli, beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shishijee be lɛ mli lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji sweet potato be hee lɛ shishijee yɛ kpokpai babaoo anɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are ready to be harvested without digging up the whole mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ oookpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You will know the yam is mature when the leaves and vines naturally start to turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Obaale akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Is it possible to harvest a yam plant early and still get more tubers from it later?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa sweet potato tsei lɛ mra ni sɛɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmeii babaoo lolo?

english: Yes, through a practice called 'milking' or double harvesting, you can carefully cut out the mature tuber mid-season while keeping the roots intact so the plant grows smaller seed yams before the season ends.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘milking’ loo ŋmaakpamɔ shii enyɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ bulbs ni eda lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ dani be lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Can I grow healthy crops successfully without using any chemical fertilizers or sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can farm naturally by using organic compost, clearing weeds early, and rotating your crops, which keeps the soil fertile and reduces your reliance on expensive store-bought chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. ni amɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa tsofai ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ahe hiɛnɔkamɔ baa shi.

english: How can I protect my crops from farm pests if I choose not to spray chemical pesticides?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Ni kɛji mihala akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieee nɔ hu?

english: You can control pests naturally by spraying solutions made from crushed neem leaves or local soap, and by planting pest-repelling plants around your farm borders.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa loo maŋ lɛ mli samla fee lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsei ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it bad to just plant my crops and wait until harvest time without checking on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ ni mamɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli ni mikwɛɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need continuous care like regular weeding, soil mounding, and pest checks; simply leaving them alone allows weeds and diseases to steal nutrients and drastically reduce your harvest.
ga: Tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa, ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ lɛ, ebaawo jwɛi kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why do some harvested yams spoil and rot quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they are bruised during digging, exposed to hot sunshine right after harvest, or stored in warm rooms without proper airflow.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers use so many different local names for yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi srɔtoi babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Different local names represent specific yam varieties (like Pona, Labako, or Bayere), each having unique features such as how fast they mature, how they taste, and how long they last in storage.
ga: Gbɛi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi (tamɔ Pona, Labako loo Bayere), ni eko fɛɛ eko yɛ sui srɔtoi tamɔ bɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya, bɔ ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ. Ni be enyiɛ abaanyɛ akɛto?

english: Why do some yams grow very large while others in the same field stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi dara nɛkɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: Tuber size depends on soft soil structure for easy root growth, adequate water, balanced soil nutrients, and using healthy, disease-free seed yams at planting.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara oya ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii

english: Why do the leaves of my maize start turning yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach them, and waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing properly, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly due to extreme heat stress, poor watering habits, or lack of insect pollination, which prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa titri yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he su gbonyo loo kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ ni bɛ Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same farm with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for crops like cassava.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: Soil is likely tired if previous crop yields were poor, weeds look stunt or yellow, or the soil has turned very hard, pale, and dry, indicating a lack of organic matter and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛ tsɛmɔ kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ehiii kwraa. Jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ egbɔjɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat up the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing center (funnel) of young maize plants and feed on the leaves before the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why do small insects attack and spoil my maize seeds after I harvest and store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ beni mikpa ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils attack maize if the seeds were not dried completely before storage or if the storage container is not airtight to block pests out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli

english: Why do I need to cut off extra young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers prevents them from competing with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and light, allowing the main tree to grow bigger bunches.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ akaye shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ la he akaŋ. Ha tso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why is it necessary to lift yam vines off the ground using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to more direct sunlight for food production while keeping the leaves away from soil-borne diseases and pests on the ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛfee niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out watery and small instead of firm and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji nu kɛ bibii yɛ nɔ ni wa ni amɛdara lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become watery and thin if harvested too early, if harvested during heavy rainfall when the plant absorbs excess water, or if planted in nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee nu ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ mra tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because it allows plants to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot while letting leaves dry quickly to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi oya koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ bo.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure helps the plant stay green and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo kooloi aŋmei wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ŋmeii lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are shaded, the cassava puts all its strength into growing stem and leaves instead of roots. Balanced nutrients and full sunlight encourage the plant to swell its tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ ewo shade mli lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi kɛ baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds remove moisture from young cocoa leaves faster than small roots can suck water from the ground. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects seedlings from harsh winds and direct sun.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai bibii amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any small peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much water at the roots. Consistent watering and mulching the soil around the plant help keep the flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my tomato seeds too close together in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crowded seedlings compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, making them thin and weak. Proper spacing creates strong, sturdy stems that survive better when transplanted to the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa, ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do I get smaller cobs if I plant three maize seeds in one hole instead of one or two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei bibioo nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei dumɔwui etɛ yɛ bu kome mli moŋ fe ekome loo enyɔ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole causes intense competition among the roots for water and fertilizer. Spacing seeds out ensures each plant gets enough food to develop large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa akaŋshii ni naa wa baa shishifãi lɛ ateŋ kɛha nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves or spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting and protects your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is caused by water pooling around the roots or fungal infections in poor planting seeds. Making high mounds for good drainage and using clean seed yams keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa dumɔwui ni aduuu jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afee koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for maize when I plant maize on the same land later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my watermelon fruits staying small and not turning sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ ji bibii ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Watermelons need full sunlight and potassium in the soil to make sugar, along with good pollination from bees while flowering. Lack of sun, dry soil, or poor pollination leads to small, tasteless fruit.
ga: Hulu la ni fa kɛ potassium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia watermelon koni ekɛfee sugar. kɛfata ŋmeii ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe, hulu la ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni ehiii Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe bɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun gets very bright during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and thin leaves that lose water rapidly under direct sunlight. They need living shade plants, like plantains or fast-growing trees, to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist around their roots until they are mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni daa oya. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees stop producing flower buds when the branches grow very thick and dense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii feemɔ beni amɛniji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers directly on their main trunks and older branches, which require light breezes and dappled sunlight to attract pollinators like tiny midges. When tree canopies become too thick, darkness and high humidity suppress flowering and encourage fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eniji ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa koni ekɛgbala kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tamɔ bibii lɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli edɔ tsɔ. Duŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs large amounts of nitrogen to grow strong; when the soil lacks this nutrient, the plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks break at the base and fall over during normal rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over (a condition called lodging) when roots are too shallow, soil is too loose, or stem borer pests have hollowed out the inside of the stalk. Planting seeds at the correct depth and mounding soil around the base during weeding strengthens root support against wind and heavy rain.
ga: ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse tsɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛ stem borers lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa ni okɛ sũ lɛ ato amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hewalɛ kroko ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy green leaves but very small, thin tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi agboi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava puts its energy into growing thick leaves above ground instead of tubers below ground when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants receive too much shade. To get heavy tubers, cassava needs balanced soil nutrients and full sunlight.
ga: Yucca kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo beni tso lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni Cassava aná yitso ni tsii lɛ, ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la babaoo aba.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to sprout well when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good cassava stem cuttings should come from mature plants (8 to 12 months old) that are free from visible spots, mites, or stem damage. Cuttings should be taken from the middle, woody part of the stem with closely spaced nodes (buds) that contain fresh latex juice when cut.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii kpakpai ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ajɛ tsei ni eda (ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12) ni bɛ ŋmeii ni anaa, ŋmeii, loo nɔ ni efite ŋmeii lɛ amli. Esa akɛ afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni tso yɔɔ mli lɛ mli, ni ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa (ŋmeii). which contains fresh latex when cut

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tiny and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking plant sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Watering more will not fix this; the insects must be controlled early using natural or recommended sprays before they stunt the entire plant.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. More watering does not fix this problem. Insects must be controlled early. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii dani amɛha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee shoo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, dry, sunken spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular—going from very dry soil to flooded soil—which prevents roots from absorbing calcium consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa—kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ—ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my planted yam seeds rot in the soil before they can sprout green vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ wain tsei eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in poorly drained, waterlogged soil or when cut seed pieces are planted immediately without allowing the wet cut surface to dry and form a protective callus. Fungi and bacteria in wet soil enter open wounds and destroy the seed piece.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni afolɔ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ahaaa nɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi ni efee nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ ni agbele lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli fãi lɛ.

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients and organic strength when crops are planted continuously on the same land without returning nutrients through organic manure, fertilizer, or allowing the land to rest (fallow). Over time, the exhausted soil can no longer feed new crops properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ e-adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa ejɔɔ ehe (egbee shi) yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun gets too hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ amɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and thin bark that easily dry out under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides vital shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food plant uses to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains waterlog the soil for long periods, the roots suffocate and rot. Plant cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges to help water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni eye ebua nu lɛ ni eho mlɛo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes pepper plants to experience stress, leading them to drop their blossoms to conserve water and energy. Mulching the soil around the base keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land yield much less grain when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and encourages pests to multiply in the soil. Rotating your maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛfɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants actually help make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies or is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo loo akpa. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars eat holes right in the center heart of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides deep inside the growing tip of the corn plant where it is warm and soft. Checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments into the leaf funnel controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai amli lɛ baakudɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build thick stems and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up into small, tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by severe water stress. Controlling whiteflies early and maintaining consistent watering helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ tomato mli. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ni nu ni oooha bo daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and cause my crops to produce smaller leaves and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee baai bibii kɛ aduawai lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow full and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Can pests and diseases from a nearby farm spread to my healthy crops if the owner neglects their field?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ? Kɛji nuŋtsɔ lɛ ku ehiɛ eshwie egbɛhe lɛ nɔ

english: Yes, insects, fungal spores, and crop diseases can easily travel through wind, rain droplets, and flying insects from an unmanaged neighboring farm onto your healthy crops. Regular farm hygiene and boundary monitoring help prevent these infestations.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii, tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔshiimɔi, kɛ kooloi bibii ni foɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli kɛya onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli oya. Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ ni afeɔ daa kɛ husui amli kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool and winds are calm. Spraying during the hot sun can burn your leaves, and strong heat causes the chemicals to evaporate quickly before working.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee dioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya dani atsuɔ nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving water drainage usually helps green them up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and underdeveloped roots that cannot handle intense, direct heat. They require temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them from sun scorch and retain soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my cassava crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive easily, so they absorb groundwater and soil nutrients much faster than young crops. Clearing weeds early gives your cassava space and food to grow strong before the weeds overtake them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ waa dani jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ he.

english: Does trimming extra branches off my vegetable plants help them yield more fruit?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning unnecessary lower branches and side shoots allows the plant to send its energy and nutrients directly to developing fruits instead of wasting energy on useless foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: If maize seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants will compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks and very small or missing corn ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ Dense tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ mli wa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ni ŋmãa toi lɛ hu faaa kwraa loo ebɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is becoming weak and needs fertilizer for my next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include stunted crop growth, pale leaf colors, weak stems, and noticeably smaller harvest yields compared to previous years, even when rain is sufficient.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe ji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni tsuɔ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa fioo kwraa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high moisture and damp shade. Removing infected pods regularly and opening up tree leaves to air circulation helps keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa ni agbeleɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants full of holes and looking ragged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the throat of the maize plant and chew through young leaves, which can severely reduce your harvest if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsitsi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ amɔɔɔ bo mra.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks cause stress to the plant. When stressed, the tomato plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer to my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so that roots can absorb it safely. Placing fertilizer in dry soil concentrates the chemicals around the roots, which can burn them and destroy the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai babaoo abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. which can burn and destroy crops

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in my farm after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand into thick tubers. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot swell properly, resulting in thin, woody cassava.
ga: Kassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei bibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli tseee ni eyɛ tso.

english: Why do other farmers trim off some of the small side branches on tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi shwieɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Pruning extra side shoots forces the plant to send its food, water, and energy straight to the growing tomatoes, producing larger, healthier fruit instead of excess foliage.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ amaje niyenii, nu, kɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ. This results in larger, healthier fruit. Instead of too many leaves

english: Is it better for me to plant saved seeds from my last maize harvest or buy new certified seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to withstand local diseases, sprout evenly, and yield more crop. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and turn pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these resources first, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛbaaju nibii nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why can't I just save and plant seeds from my current maize harvest instead of buying new certified seeds every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahere ni madu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, a be nyɛe maa he dumɔwu ehe nɛ a wo he odase ɔ daa be.

english: Commercial seed varieties lose their strong yields after the first harvest. If you replant saved seeds, the second generation often grows unevenly, resists pests poorly, and gives you much smaller yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ du ekoŋŋ Bei pii lɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enyɛŋ eshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ fioo kwraa.

english: Why do some of the packaged crop seeds I buy sprout much faster than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni miheɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe mimaŋ dumɔwui ni miheɔ daa lɛ?

english: Packaged certified seeds are specifically treated and selected for uniform quality and high vitality, allowing them to absorb moisture and break dormancy quickly once planted in moist soil.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii krɛdɛɛ ni ahalaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛfoɔ wɔɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into developing big fruits or cobs, the plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii koni ekɛwo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ shi koni ená la.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow thick roots in soft soil but produce small, woody roots in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ lɛ? Shi tsei shishifãi bibii yɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil to expand and store starch easily. Hard or compacted soil restricts the roots from expanding, forcing the plant to store less food and producing small, tough roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ starch ato mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tooɔ niyenii fioo ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look limp during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in strong heat is a plant's natural way of saving water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and keeps moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ mli yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ

english: Why are my pepper plants shedding their flowers before any peppers begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper nutrients. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and burn after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer or spreading it too close to the plant stem burns the roots and prevents them from taking up water, causing the leaves to dry out and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli tsɔ loo okɛgbɛ eshwa tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does a selective weedkiller chemical destroy the grass on my farm without harming my cassava crops?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ agbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni egbeee mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Selective chemical weedkillers target specific biological traits that grasses have but broad-leaf plants like cassava do not, allowing the crop to remain healthy while the target weeds die off.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ kwɛɔ wala yibii pɔtɛɛ ni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ efeee nakai. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni akɛmamɔ ehiɛ lɛ gboiɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my farm soil over time if I only use chemical fertilizers without adding manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ tsu nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli?

english: Relying only on chemical fertilizers without organic matter like animal manure causes the soil to become acidic and hard, destroying beneficial soil microbes and making it harder for soil to hold moisture.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acidic ni efee shiŋŋ. Efiteɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli

english: Why do dark spots and white powder appear on my vegetable leaves right after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during the rainy season create perfect conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and spread across wet leaves, especially when plants are spaced too closely for air to flow.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii helai babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pawpaw trees turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pawpaw tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Pawpaw leaves usually turn yellow due to poor water drainage causing root damage, or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Ensuring water doesn't pool around the trunk and adding well-rotted manure helps keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pawpaw baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ koni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce many flowers but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo yibii ko kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants have male, female, and hermaphrodite trees. Male trees only produce pollen-bearing flowers on long stems to fertilize other trees, but they cannot produce fruits themselves.
ga: Paw paw tsei lɛ baa yɛ hii, yei kɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ fɛɛ mli. Tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen eyi mli obɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ pɛ koni amɛkɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli. shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe

english: Why do young pawpaw fruits fall off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Small fruits drop early when the tree suffers from sudden water stress, severe heat, or incomplete pollination. Regular watering during dry spells and keeping a mix of fruit-bearing trees nearby helps hold the fruit.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nu he haomɔ trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ na tso lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ aduawai tsei ni ahiɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ Amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaafee ekome lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it taking so long for my pineapple plants to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-anana tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pineapples are naturally slow growers and usually take between 14 to 24 months to fruit. The timeline depends heavily on soil fertility and whether you planted from suckers, slips, or fruit crowns.
ga: Pineapple ji tsei ni daa blɛoo ni bei pii lɛ eheɔ nyɔji 14 kɛyashi 24 dani ewoɔ yibii. Be ni ato lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ nɔ waa. Ni ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji ooda kɛjɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo aduawai anɔ.

english: Why are pineapples usually plentiful in some months but hard to find in other seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi efɔɔɔ kaa yɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pineapple plants naturally flower when days become cooler and shorter, leading to a major harvest season. Without forced flowering techniques using special regulators, there are months when very few fruits mature.
ga: Pineapple tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni gbii lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ kuku lɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ hiɛ kɛyaa kpamɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii ni anyɛɔ mɔ nɔ ni akɛ nɔkwɛlɔ krɛdɛɛ ko tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Nyɔji komɛi yɛ ni aduawai fioo ko pɛ shwereɔ.

english: Can I grow pawpaws and pineapples together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ paw paws kɛ pineapple yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant them together because pawpaw trees grow tall with slender roots, while pineapples stay close to the ground. This allows both crops to share sunlight and land space without heavily competing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ pawpaw tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ mli.

english: Which planting material should I use to get pineapples to grow faster?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔ nii esa akɛ akɛtsu nii koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya?

english: Using side shoots called suckers or slips from existing pineapple plants produces fruit faster—usually within 14 to 18 months—compared to planting the leafy top crown, which takes up to two years.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers loo ŋmeii ni jɛ pineapple tso ko ni yɔɔ momo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo yibii oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 14 kɛyashi 18, kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni heɔ afii enyɔ lɛ he.

english: What kind of soil is best for starting a pineapple farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ shishijee?

english: Pineapples grow best in loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water quickly. They do not tolerate muddy or waterlogged ground, so planting on raised mounds is recommended if the soil retains too much water.
ga: Ananas kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã, sũ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ oya. Amɛkpɛlɛɛɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: How can I prevent my pineapples from spoiling while transporting them to markets in Accra?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-pineapple lɛ naa koni ekafite beni mikɛyaa jara nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Harvest pineapples when they are mature but still slightly green, load them carefully without stacking too high to avoid crushing, and ensure good airflow in the vehicle to keep them cool during long trips.
ga: Kpaa pineapple kɛji edara kwraa shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ fioo lolo. Okɛ amɛ awo he jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ akato he ko ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ koni akakumɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ abɔle he jogbaŋŋ koni eha ŋmei lɛ mli ajɔ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I keep harvested pawpaws fresh so they do not rot too quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-pawpaw ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi ehee koni ekafite oya?

english: Store harvested pawpaws in a cool, shaded, and airy place away from direct sunlight. Keep them off the warm floor and separate from overripe fruits to slow down natural decay.
ga: Kɛ paw paws ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, shade, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ha amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ aba sɛɛ.

english: Why do some trees on my farm keep the soil moist while others seem to dry up the ground around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekrokomɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli gĩɔ lɛ?

english: Certain deep-rooted native shade trees drop leaves that form a protective mulch layer, trapping soil moisture and keeping the ground cool. In contrast, fast-growing trees like eucalyptus absorb vast amounts of water from the soil, leaving less moisture for surrounding crops.
ga: Maŋ tsei komɛi ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ shiɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ eucalyptus lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ fioo

english: How does watering my crops early in the morning help them more than watering at midday?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni oooha amɛ nu leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ fe nu ni oooha amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning allows plant roots to soak up moisture before the heat of the day causes rapid evaporation. Midday watering causes most water to evaporate instantly in the hot sun, wasting effort and potentially stressing hot plant leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa efoɔ oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji hewalɛ fitemɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ.

english: Can I collect and use the sweet juice inside cocoa pods instead of letting it drain away during fermentation?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mabua nu ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa ni mikɛtsu nii. Mohu ɔ, anɛ o ha nɛ e ho ngɛ flɔmi be mi?

english: Yes, you can collect fresh cocoa pulp juice right after opening the pods to produce sweet fruit drinks, jelly, or alcoholic beverages. Collecting this pulp juice creates an extra product to sell without harming the quality of your dried cocoa beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obua cocoa ŋmɔtɔ hee naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ogbele ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli ni okɛfee aduawai amli nu ni ŋɔɔ, jeli loo dãa ni wa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ni ooobua naa lɛ feɔ nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni okɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ kpakpa lɛ baaa shi.

english: Is it better for my income to tap my oil palm trees for palm wine or let them keep producing palm fruit?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shika ni mináa lɛ akɛ matswa tsei ni akɛ mu woɔ mli lɛ koni mikɛfee ŋmei wain loo maha amɛya nɔ amɛwo ŋmei yibii?

english: Tapping trees for palm wine gives quick, daily cash income, but it often kills or weakens the tree over time. Letting the trees grow and harvesting the palm fruit yields palm oil for many years, giving you a steady long-term income.
ga: Tsei ni atswaa koni akɛfee ŋmei wain lɛ haa anáa shika oya daa gbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, egbeɔ tso lɛ loo ehaa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akpaa ŋmei yibii lɛ, ehaa anáa ŋmei fɔ afii babaoo. Shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baaha bo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: What is the difference between using old natural compost and using modern bagged fertilizers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ blema adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a fast boost of specific nutrients but do not build soil structure. Natural compost releases nutrients more slowly while improving the soil's ability to hold water and nutrients over many future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi oya shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I trim branches off my fruit trees when traditional farmers used to let them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji? Be mli ni blema okwaafoi haa ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Trimming or pruning allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner branches, which prevents fungal diseases and pest buildup. It also forces the tree to direct its energy into producing larger, healthier fruit rather than excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ baai krokomɛi.

english: Should I burn the crop waste left on my field after harvest or leave it on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving crop waste on the soil creates a natural protective layer that retains moisture, prevents soil erosion from rain, and breaks down into natural soil nutrients. Burning destroys these nutrients and leaves the soil bare to heat and rain damage.
ga: Nibii ni adu mli lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ naa. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shãa fiteɔ niyenii nɛɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they do not have enough water, shade, or nutrients to feed all potential pods. It is the tree's natural way of saving energy so that remaining pods can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Will leaving large shade trees on my land prevent my crops from getting enough sunlight?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mashi lɛ baatsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Heavy shade can reduce sunlight too much, but moderate shade from selected trees shields sensitive crops like young cocoa from extreme sun heat and keeps humidity high enough for healthy growth.
ga: Hulu ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ aba shi. Shi hulutsoo ni sa ni jɛ tsei ni ahala lɛ amli lɛ baabu tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he. ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special root bacteria that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Maize roots absorb this nitrogen, which acts as a free, natural fertilizer to make the maize leaves green and strong.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Bacteria ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe Koni ekɛha ŋmãa baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehe wa

english: Why does letting tall weeds grow around my cocoa trees cause the pods to get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ obaashi jwɛi lɛ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? Ani mi cacao tsei lɛ miiha ŋmeii lɛ miihe hela?

english: Overgrown weeds trap damp air and shade around your cocoa trees. This creates a wet, dark environment where diseases like black pod fungus thrive and easily spread onto your cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ shade ni bɔleɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ baa, ni helai tamɔ black pod fungus baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã o-cocoa pods lɛ amli.

english: How often should I clear the bush inside my cocoa farm to keep the crop healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing bush regularly keeps air moving through the trees and allows sunlight to dry off wet leaves and pods, which stops diseases from growing and attacking your yield.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli daa. ni oha hulu la lɛ aha baai kɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai shwereɔ ni amɛtutuaa onibii lɛ.

english: What should I do with cocoa pods that show black spots or turn rotten on the branch?
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: You must pluck off diseased pods immediately and remove them completely from the farm. If left on the tree, rainfall and insects will carry the disease spores from the rotten pod to healthy ones.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Nugbɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni egboi amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Is it safe to leave diseased cocoa pods on the ground between my crop rows after plucking them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, leaving sick pods on the ground leaves the disease alive in your farm. Raindrops splashing on the ground can bounce fungal spores back up onto healthy lower cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ ahi shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛba kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does disease seem to spread faster across my farm during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases are caused by fungi that need moisture to reproduce. High rainfall and damp conditions help these germs multiply and move rapidly from tree to tree.
ga: Fungi ni biɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ efɔ bii lɛ kɛ tsei ahelai babaoo baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ babaoo ni amɛyaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: Why should I carefully observe my farm in my village before changing how I manage my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani matsake bɔ ni mikwɛɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ mihaa lɛ?

english: Every village has slightly different rainfall, shade, and soil conditions. Watching how your trees naturally react to your local weather helps you make smart decisions that won't accidentally harm your crop.
ga: Akrowa fɛɛ akrowa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ sɔrɔtoi fioo. Kɛ́ ona bɔ ni otsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okpɛ oyiŋ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do farming techniques that work in a different region sometimes fail on my own cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react differently based on local land biology, shade levels, and weather patterns. A technique must match the specific conditions of your local environment to work well.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli, hulutsoo, kɛ akutsoŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Esa akɛ ŋaa gbɛ ko kɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee bɔni afee ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does keeping my farm well-maintained prevent me from losing cocoa during harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ baanyɛ atsĩ minaa koni mikafite kookoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Proper maintenance ensures nutrients go to your cocoa trees instead of weeds, and it prevents disease from destroying pods before they mature, ensuring maximum harvestable pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa kookoo tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe jwɛi lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa pods babaoo.

english: What naturally causes cocoa trees to drop or spoil their pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Trees spoil or drop pods mainly due to fungal infections encouraged by excess shade, unmanaged bush, or competition for nutrients from uncleaned weed growth.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ tso fitemɔ loo fitemɔ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine mli baa. jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni he tseee ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I protect my cocoa pods from rotting before they are ripe enough to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dani amɛshwere bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie?

english: Keep the farm floor clear, prune excess branches to let light in, and remove any sick pods immediately so that healthy pods have room and clear air to ripen.
ga: Ha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa gbɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are becoming sick early before the disease spreads?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa?

english: Look closely at the leaves and stems for unusual yellowing, swollen shoots, or dark spots on young pods. Spotting these signs early allows you to treat or isolate infected trees before the entire farm gets affected.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmeii ni efuu, loo he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa loo otsiɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anaa dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baaná hela.

english: If I plant my cocoa farm right next to another cocoa farm or research station, will my trees easily catch diseases from them?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ŋmɔ kroko loo niiamlitaomɔ he. Ani mi tsei lɛ baaná hela oya?

english: Yes, diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or Black Pod can easily cross farm boundaries through wind, insects, or shared tools. Creating a barrier strip or planting shade trees along borders helps protect your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus loo Black Pod baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛjaraa lɛ nɔ afo ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli mlɛo. Gbɛtsii nii ni ooofee loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my cocoa trees starting to show signs of disease just one year after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi hela okadii jiemɔ yɛ afi kome ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young trees have tender leaves and weaker defenses, making them soft targets for insects like mealybugs and fungal spores. Infection often happens in the nursery or during the first year while the plant is adjusting to field conditions.
