ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ hebuu ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs kɛ fungal spores lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ baa yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ loo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miitsake amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli lɛ.

english: What should I do if a disease on my cocoa trees spreads faster than I can manage on my own?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji hela ko ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya fe bɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ matsu he nii?

english: When an outbreak goes out of control, stop applying random chemicals and contact your local extension officer immediately. For viral diseases, cutting down infected trees and their immediate neighbors is often the only way to save the rest of the farm.
ga: Beni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ hela lɛ Kpa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni afeee nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ni okɛ ohewalɛ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ abɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. kɛha helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ afolɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahereɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: Is it safe to leave a sick cocoa tree standing if I just cut off the bad branches?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛji mifo niji ni ehiii lɛ?

english: For fungal infections on branches, cutting off affected parts can work if caught early. However, for viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, the virus spreads through the whole sap system, so trimming branches will not save the tree—the whole tree must be uprooted.
ga: Kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei aniji anɔ lɛ, he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ mra. Shi, kɛha helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ, helatsɛmɛi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mliki gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ hereee tso lɛ yiwala. Esa akɛ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishi.

english: How do cocoa diseases move from one tree to another so quickly across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases spread mainly through sap-feeding insects like mealybugs, wind-blown fungal spores, and rain splashes. Farmers can also spread diseases accidentally by using the same pruning cutlass on sick and healthy trees without cleaning it.
ga: Hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa titri kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs, ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ. Okwaafoi hu baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã yɛ oshara mli kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛ nɔŋŋ ni amɛtsumɔko amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to report crop disease problems to an extension officer?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ abɔ tsei ahe helai ahe naagbai ahe amaniɛ aha mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: You should contact an extension officer as soon as you notice unfamiliar symptoms like leaf discoloration or swollen stems that do not clear up. Waiting until the disease covers the whole farm makes control much harder and more costly.
ga: Esa akɛ oyana o-extension nitsulɔi lɛ pɛ kɛji ona okadi ko ni oleee, tamɔ baai ni etsake su loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu ni bɛ faŋŋ. Ni aaamɛ kɛyashi hela lɛ eha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ejara hu wa.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact spot where I just removed sick cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ko ni mijie kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ kɛkɛ?

english: It is risky because disease spores and infected root debris remain in the soil. You should clear all old roots, treat or solarize the soil, and wait a few months or plant disease-resistant cocoa varieties in those spots.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Tsɔɔmɔ loo otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ hulu la. Ni mɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi loo odu kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ yɛ nakai hei lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in heavy shade, cool temperatures, and high humidity. Pruning excess shade branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the farm helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fungal hela ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, latsaa ni mli ejɔ, kɛ latsaa ni naa wa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Do ants and tiny insects on my cocoa stems cause leaf diseases or just feed on the plant?
ga: Ants kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, kɛ foliar hela baa loo amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Tiny insects like mealybugs feed on the sap and act as carriers (vectors) that transmit viruses like Cocoa Swollen Shoot between trees. Ants often protect these mealybugs, so controlling ant nests also helps stop the spread of disease.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ mealybugs yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ mɛi ni hiɛɔ (nibii ni hiɛɔ) ni gbɛɔ helai, tamɔ cacao tsei ni efuu ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii buɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii atsuji ni akudɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct heat and full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a living umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni baanyɛ ashã yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or heavy rain washing away topsoil nutrients. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the boost it needs to regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená eŋɔli su ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear in the central whorl of my corn plants right after the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii je kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warmth and moisture after early rains cause fall armyworm eggs hidden in the soil or nearby weeds to hatch rapidly. Applying targeted treatment into the central leaf whorl early on stops the pests before they destroy the plant's growing tip.
ga: He ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Koni akɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce much smaller roots when I plant it in the same field three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi bibii kwraa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws high amounts of specific nutrients, like potassium, out of the soil every season. Planting cassava continuously in the same spot exhausts the soil and builds up root pests; rotating the field with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo daa be mli. Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots spread over my cocoa pods during the cold, wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in humid, cool shade. Pruning dense cocoa branches to let sunlight and air circulate, along with clearing infected pods quickly, stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ni sumɔɔ nu ni shwereɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Folɔ kookoo tsei ni mli ewo muji koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛfata ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry up, preventing pollination and forcing the plant to drop flowers to save water. Mulching around the base of the plant and watering regularly keeps the soil cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa kɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he Mulching ni akɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do seeds harvested from my hybrid maize produce weaker crops than the seeds I originally bought in the bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mi-corn hybrids lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni mihe shishijee yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give maximum yield only in the first generation. Saving seeds from that crop results in mixed genetic traits in the next planting, leading to uneven growth and lower total harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ kɛ sui ni futuɔ baa yɛ dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing very bushy with dark green leaves but yielding almost no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi ewooo yibii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants put all their energy into leaf growth rather than flowering. Switching to fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop growing extra leaves and start setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekpa baai ni fa fe nine lɛ shweremɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil when rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need well-drained soil to breathe. Heavy rain on flat ground creates waterlogged conditions that drown the roots and invite fungal decay, which is why planting yams on raised mounds or ridges protects them from sitting in standing water.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ baa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkatara nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnuts start sprouting underground if I leave them in the farm past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni kpamɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Once groundnuts reach full maturity, their seed dormancy naturally ends. If moisture remains in the soil, the pods receive a signal to begin growing into new plants, so harvesting promptly when the foliage turns yellow prevents losing seed quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛdɔɔ lɛ baa naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Pods lɛ nine shɛɔ okadi nɔ koni amɛje shishi amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ pɛ kɛkɛ ni akpaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong cobs. Applying fertilizer like NPK or adding compost early in the season helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Look closely at the buds or 'eyes' on the stem cutting. The buds should point upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up easily without wasting energy.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ mlɛo ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the leaves of my young maize plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which thrive in warm weather and hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem water early in the morning when you first notice them helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem nu tsu nii leebi beni oyɔse amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye amɛnɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plants lack water, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving them steady water and partial shade during very hot weeks helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fã ko yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni baai loo jwɛi egbi yɛ amɛdumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Covering soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist under the hot sun, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as the leaves break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch more sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground, while keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ pensil yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a survival trick plants use to save water during hot hours. It reduces the leaf surface exposed to the burning sun, helping the plant hold onto its internal moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa hewolo ni hulu la shãa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Will removing some of the lower leaves of my pepper plants help me get bigger peppers?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔtɔ tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔtɔ wuji?

english: Yes, pruning off low-hanging leaves and extra shoots helps the plant direct its energy into producing bigger pepper fruits rather than extra foliage, while also improving airflow to stop fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ pepper yibii wuji aba moŋ fe ni eeená baai babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa fata he ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside cassava, cowpeas feed the soil naturally, reducing your need to buy expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmei Cowpeas lɛ, eyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is low or washed away by heavy rains, the plant cannot make enough green pigment to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen faaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge leafy stems above ground but only produce small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishifãi ni baai wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants receive too much shade, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of underground roots. Balanced sunlight and soil nutrients are needed for energy to store in large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ akɛ hewalɛ ato bulb agboi amli.

english: Cocoa flowers dry up and fall off if tiny insects called midges are not around to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by extreme drought or a lack of shade. Without proper pollination and shade, the tree rejects the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii ba amɛmli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji kɛha pollination. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ pollination kɛ shade ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baakpoo fɔfɔi.

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil. It is usually caused by irregular watering, such as letting the soil get extremely dry and then flooding it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ waa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot spell before the main rainy season fully arrives. If seeds sprout during that brief wet period, the intense dry heat afterward will scorch and kill the young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni efɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, la ni egbi lɛ baashã ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a strong windstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ahum ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deep into the ground. If the soil is waterlogged or damaged by tiny underground worms called nematodes, the roots lose their grip and the heavy plant topples.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ efite lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ shi ni tso ni tsii lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves. As they suck the plant juice, they cause the leaves to twist and stunt new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛnuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛbaatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛbaatsi dalɛ hee naa.

english: Why are small black insects covering the shoots of my cowpea beans during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji haa mi-cowpeas lɛ yiteŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These black insects are aphids, which multiply very quickly in warm, dry weather. They cluster on soft growing shoots to drink the plant's sap, causing the plant to weaken, wilt, and drop its leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii diji nɛɛ ji aphids, ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ tsei bibii anɔ koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Cassava heavy-feeds on soil nutrients to build its large tubers. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil's fertility completely and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the dirt.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmei pɔtɛɛ he lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear and plant my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years and are naturally adapted to sprout immediately once sunlight and rain hit the cleared ground, whereas crop seeds take longer to establish their root systems.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them creates a canopy that shields the cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow together, they steal water and food from each other. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo bua amɛhe naa lɛ Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers underground when their leaves get maximum sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes spreads the leaves out to catch light and prevents fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la fe fɛɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni la abote mli ni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are there tiny worms eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Niyeli bu yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli?

english: Those are fall armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize. They hide in the central funnel of the plant, so checking your farm early and using recommended treatments prevents them from destroying the crop before it tassels.
ga: Amɛji cutworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛfɔ̃ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into small tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by severe heat stress. Controlling insects early and keeping the soil evenly watered helps stop the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Haomɔ ni naa wa Mra ni akɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why is it better to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which naturally take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them enriches the soil with free plant food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows pests that feed on it to build up in the soil. Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist after rain before applying fertilizer to my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer on dry ground during hot weather can burn the crop's roots and cause the fertilizer to evaporate. Moist soil helps the fertilizer dissolve quickly so the roots can soak it up safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ la. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist when flowers appear helps the plant hold onto its blossoms to form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji fɔfɔii je kpo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Which crops are easiest to grow and sell quickly in Ghana right now?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ akɛ aaadu ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Fast-growing staples like maize and cassava have high local demand in Ghana. Cassava is especially hardy and grows well in various soil types with minimal effort, making it ideal for beginners.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ Ghana. Yucca lɛ wa waa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi babaoo nɔ ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. ni haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants survive during the dry season while my maize dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that reach water stored deep underground and can drop leaves to conserve moisture, whereas maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly without frequent rainfall.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ashwie shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ shii abɔ lɛ.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my land help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baajieɔ amɛ?

english: Tractors loosen packed soil deep down, allowing crop roots to spread easily, absorb more nutrients, and retain rainwater much longer than hand-weeded ground.
ga: Trakta lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Eheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛ niji shwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal sunlight, water, and nutrients, while making it much easier to use simple machines or hand tools for weeding and harvesting.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɔnei loo nitsumɔ dadei kɛ nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them provides a cool cover and protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛ hebuu aba kɛyashi be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my yam mounds washing away whenever heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains easily carry away loose soil on sloping land. Planting cover crops like beans or creating ridged rows across slopes holds the soil together and prevents yam mounds from eroding.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ oya. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food for plant leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes groundnuts good to plant on my land before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni sa akɛ adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii aba?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, leaving behind rich soil for the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize crop but leave my cassava field untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ shi amɛshiɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer sweet, soft cereal leaves like maize and sorghum. Cassava leaves contain natural defense compounds that deter these specific pests.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmaa baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ abele kɛ ŋmãa. Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsiɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa yɛ cassava baai amli.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too hot or when soil moisture changes too drastically. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to cover them, sunlight scorches the leaves and causes them to dry out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni egbi amɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main parent stem. Removing them leaves only the strongest shoots, allowing the main plant to produce large, healthy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small holes in them and look like someone poured powdery sawdust into the middle leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko shwie ŋmei ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed inside the young leaves at the center of the corn plant during the day and leave behind shredded leaves and powdery waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni eshiɔ baai ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ sũ ni efite

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry patch before the main rains begin. Seeds that germinate after the first rain can wither and die if there is no continuous rain to support their early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbo ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ nɛɔ ni baaye abua amɛdalɛ mra lɛ bɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I bury my cassava stem cuttings when I am planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds or leaf scars pointing upwards towards the sky. Planting stems upside down causes shoots to grow downwards into the soil first, leading to weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii loo baai okadii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be lifted up on sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight so the plant can make more energy for tuber growth. It also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ babaoo kɛha tuber dalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ, ni no haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or inconsistent watering. When water is scarce, the plant discards flowers to save moisture instead of spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck sap from young shoots, or viruses carried by whiteflies that cause leaves to deform and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ woɔ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ kpaa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fresh animal dung directly to my crops right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure produces high heat as it breaks down and contains strong salts that can burn crop roots. Letting the manure dry and decompose first makes the nutrients safe for the plants.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo baa kɛji efite, ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe aha tsei.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer for the crop that follows.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is naturally fertile enough to grow maize without adding a lot of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo fataaa he?

english: Naturally rich soil usually has a dark color, holds moisture well, and supports healthy wild plant growth. Even on fertile land, a simple soil test or observing past yields will tell you if the soil already has enough strength for maize so you do not waste money buying unnecessary fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa koo mli tsei ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii anɔ po Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Aloo, nibii ni eho ni eho lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa.

english: Can good, fertile land lose its strength if I keep planting maize on it season after season?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baa nii lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa shii abɔ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps your fertile land strong for years.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: I have a plot of land that has been left wild for years; how do I prepare it without damaging its natural strength?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni ashi yɛ koo mli afii babaoo nɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa lɛ ni mifiteee adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Clear the overgrown bush without burning it so you do not destroy the beneficial organic matter. Clear deep roots manually and till gently so the natural nutrients stored in the rested soil remain available for your crops.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oshãaa amɛ bɔni afee ni okafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Okɛ onine ajie shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ fiofio. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni eshwɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What will happen to my maize if I put too much fertilizer on land that is already good?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ momo lɛ he?

english: Adding excess fertilizer to already fertile land can burn the crop's roots, waste your money, and cause the plants to grow too tall and weak to support heavy corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse momo lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi, efite shika, ni eha tsei lɛ afee shwiili ni amɛhe waaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ.

english: How do I determine the right amount of chemical fertilizer to add to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ falɛ?

english: The right amount depends on your crop type and current soil fertility. Applying fertilizer based on a soil test or standard extension advice prevents over-fertilizing and ensures your plants get only what they need.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo ŋaawoi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ afee lɛ he lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine awo mli lɛ naa, ni ebaaha otsei lɛ ana nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why are my crops giving me a small harvest even though my land is known to be very good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ? Ale akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi waa?

english: Good soil alone does not guarantee a high yield. Poor land management—such as failing to control weeds, bad planting spacing, or poor water drainage—can prevent crops from using the natural strength of the land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa pɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba. Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni ehiii, tamɔ jwɛi ni akudɔɔɔ He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ehiii. loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ akatsu nii.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops on good land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds love rich soil just as much as crops do and will quickly consume the water and nutrients in the ground. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the full benefit of the soil's natural fertility.
ga: Jwɛi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii babaoo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ebaaye nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ ahe sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are the early warning signs that I am not managing my farm land properly?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mikwɛɛɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Key signs include rainwater washing away topsoil, soil forming hard crusts, persistent weed outbreaks, and crop yields dropping year after year despite good weather.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe ji nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Jwɛi yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the best crop to plant based on the type of soil I have?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Different crops thrive in different soils; for example, maize prefers well-drained, nutrient-rich soil, while crops like cassava tolerate poorer soils better. Matching your crop to your soil type maximizes yield and saves input costs.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ŋmãa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmei kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni ehaa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo baa shi.

english: How can a mobile farming app help me make better decisions about my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mobile farming app ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpɛ miyiŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Farming apps combine local weather forecasts, soil data, and crop guidelines to give tailored advice on what to plant, how much fertilizer to use, and how to properly care for your specific piece of land.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he app lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji, shikpɔŋ nɔ saji kɛ dumɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi feɔ ekome ni ekɛ ŋaawoi ni sa aha yɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ adu lɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and soft before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. When there is heavy rain and dense shade, water drops stay on the pods and spread the fungal spores from tree to tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni hulutsoo be babaoo ba lɛ Nu ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amɛshwãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly, starving the roots of air. It can also happen if you plant stems taken from older plants that were already infected with cassava disease.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ odu tsei ni egbɔ ni yucca hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli tsei ahe tsei.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often a sign of stress from high heat, lack of water, or tiny pests like whiteflies and mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, chili baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo miihao, nu faaa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce only tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from overusing chemical fertilizer or fresh animal manure—the maize plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of forming thick, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ ngma nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the soil. If the soil is too loose or wet, or if pests like nematodes weaken the roots, the heavy stem cannot support itself against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. If the soil is too loose or wet Or if pests such as nematodes cause the roots to become weak. Tso ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land is good enough to grow tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko hi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu tomato?

english: Good tomato soil should feel loose and dark, drain water quickly after rain so it doesn't stay muddy, receive full sunlight, and not have grown tomatoes, peppers, or eggplants in the last year.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nu oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni sũ akabote mli. Receive full sunlight and did not plant tomatoes, peppers, or eggplant last year.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years. Clearing the bush opens up sunlight and air, which triggers those hidden weed seeds to sprout and grow aggressively before your crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii lɛ, ebaagbele hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa nakai jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it continuously in the same place drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli kwraa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn pale yellow when there is heavy rainfall in August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ August mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away mobile nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them. Excessive water also suffocates roots, preventing them from feeding the plant properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu babaoo hu haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ aha tsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Wait until the rains become steady—usually after two or three good downpours that moisten the soil deeply—rather than planting after the very first scattered rain, which can dry out and kill young seeds.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ sɛɛ—shi moŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What is a foundation seed, and how is it different from the seeds I collect from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni ji shishijee dumɔwui? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Foundation seeds are pure, high-quality seeds produced under strict control by plant breeders to ensure high yields and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds from your farm naturally lose these strong qualities over time.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ yɛ kudɔmɔ ni mli wa shishi. Koni aná yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a company when I can just use my left-over grains from last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe ko dɛŋ be mli ni manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to give higher yields, grow uniformly, and resist pests, while old farm-saved seeds often lead to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui momo ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nibii babaoo.

english: How do seed companies manage to produce enough seeds to sell to farmers for several months of the year?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi lɛ nyɔji babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: Seed companies take pure foundation seeds, plant them in bulk under carefully monitored conditions to multiply them, and then properly process and store them to sell during the planting season.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ ŋɔɔ dumɔwui ni afɔko amɛ ni amɛduɔ amɛ babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli koni amɛyi fa babaoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ koni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers start planting seeds inside a room or sheltered nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi jeɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ tsu loo ŋmɔ ko mli dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a sheltered area protects vulnerable young sprouts from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and insects, giving them a strong, healthy start before they are transplanted into the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ahe, ni ehaa amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ dani amɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Which crops need to be started in a nursery first instead of putting them directly into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ aje shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛbaawo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Crops with small seeds like tomatoes, peppers, and cabbage do best in a nursery where they can be protected, while crops with larger seeds like maize, beans, and groundnuts do better planted directly in the field.
ga: Tsei ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kaabɛji, ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni abaanyɛ abu amɛhe yɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even when I put them in the soil and water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ nu awo nɔ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are dead from improper storage, planted too deep in the dirt, lack enough oxygen, or are destroyed by soil fungi before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛgboi yɛ bɔ ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Oxygen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How can I store my harvested seeds for many months without them spoiling or losing their power to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo ni mifiteee loo mihewalɛ ni haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo?

english: Seeds stay alive longest when kept completely dry, cool, and stored in airtight containers off the ground to protect them from moisture, heat, and insects like weevils.
ga: Dumɔwui hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛto he ko ni egbi, amɛhe jɔ, ni akɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: How can I check if seeds I saved from last season are still good to plant before putting them into my whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo akɛ adu dani adu amɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can test them by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days; if 8 or more germinate and sprout roots, your batch of seed is strong and good to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant too many seeds close together in a small space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he ko bibioo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak crops with low yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Can crop diseases from my previous harvest stay hidden inside the seeds I saved for this new season?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela ko ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ato dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛha be hee nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, many plant diseases survive inside or on the surface of saved seeds and will infect the new plant as soon as it sprouts, which is why using clean, treated seeds prevents disease outbreaks.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo hiɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ amli loo amɛhiɛ. ni ebaatswa tsei heei ahe hela kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni he tse ni atsa amɛ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai akaje kpo lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly onto my growing maize plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee awo mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very concentrated and produces heat as it breaks down, which can burn crop roots. You should dry and compost the manure for a few weeks before mixing it into the soil so your crops can absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii otsii 2-3 dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to nourish new top growth, showing you that it is time to feed your soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni eda babaoo Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmãa hee ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot withstand intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields young trees from heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl in hot weather as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, preventing water loss. Deep watering early in the morning helps the plant stay strong through afternoon heat.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni laajeɔ lɛ naa Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane latsaa be mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress causes plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the slow-growing cassava to take over the land and mature later without competing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ha ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eda sɛɛ mli ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why is it harmful to grow maize on the exact same patch of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the ground every year and allows pests and diseases that prefer maize to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores fertility and cleans the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crops. Even with adequate rain, your crops will struggle because weeds consume the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave mature cassava tubers in the ground for a long time after they are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashiɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni amɛfee klalo sɛɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil too long past maturity causes the tubers to turn woody, lose starch quality, and become vulnerable to rotting or termite attacks. Harvesting on time clears the ground and yields high-quality roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsei. Ashikishaŋ kpakpa ni elaaje ni amɛyɔɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite loo ŋmeii baafite amɛ Kpãa yɛ be naa lɛ baaha he lɛ afee faŋŋ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How do I check my farm early to see if fall armyworms are attacking my maize crop?
ga: Makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji fall armyworms miitutua mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Look closely into the central funnel of young maize plants for small ragged holes in the leaves and tiny green or brown droppings. Catching these early signs before leaves are completely eaten allows for effective control.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. koni ana bu bibioo ko Yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli Mra be mli okadii nɛɛ ni amɔmɔɔ dani ayeɔ baai lɛ kwraa lɛ haa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and thin bark that dry out easily under intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that traps moisture and shields the young cocoa until its roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my plantain stalk die after producing just one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk is naturally built to produce flowers and fruit only once. After harvesting, that stem dies back so all the soil nutrients and water can feed the small shoot stems growing at its base to form the next crop.
ga: Abɔ plantain tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai shikome pɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai tso lɛ baagbo. No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding and eating the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that prefer the soft, young inner leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved neem extracts or recommended insecticides into the central leaf whorl protects the growing tip from destruction.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baa lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced organic manure helps the blossoms stay attached and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to produce food, which is then sent underground to grow big yam tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, ensuring maximum sunlight exposure and keeping the foliage safe from soil-borne rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe babaoo ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ sũ ni kɛ sũ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them and allows underground fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off, keeping the roots well-aerated.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa

english: Why do people advise me to cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool during hot days, stops groundwater from evaporating quickly, and naturally turns into rich plant food as the dry grass decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii beni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot consumes the same soil nutrients year after year and causes maize-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Switching to crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the air is cool, allowing soil to absorb water deeply before the hot sun evaporates it. Watering in peak afternoon heat can burn tender leaves and wastes water.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee blɛoo ni efite nu lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen. The maize plant is pulling available nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves and growing ears on top.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Abɛi tsei miigbala niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei kɛ toi ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that live under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. These insects suck the sap, causing the leaf to deform as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do I know which way to face the buds when planting cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ akpee beni miduɔ yucca ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small leaf nodes or 'eyes' where shoots grow out. These nodes should always point upward toward the sky when buried; if you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upwards, resulting in weak plants and lower tuber yields.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ baai bibii loo ‘buds’ ni ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ mli baa. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ afu. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Shoots baaná naagba yɛ shweremɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why don't plantain plants grow from seeds like maize or tomatoes do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato mli lɛ?

english: Domesticated plantain varieties do not produce fertile seeds. Instead, they produce young shoots called 'suckers' at the base of the main stem, which you dig up and replant to grow new plantain trees.
ga: Shia plantain henɔi lɛ wooo dumɔwui babaoo. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tso bibihi nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ ke ‘tso’ ngɛ tso titli ɔ sisi. ni otsiɔ ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ koni okwɛ plantains heei.

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to yield heavily in the first generation. If you save and plant those second-generation seeds, the resulting crops lose that vigor, growing unevenly and producing much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu lɛ Tso ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafite hewalɛ. Edaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade trees or plantains nearby to protect their delicate leaves and keep the air and soil humid while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which is then sent down into the ground to build bigger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. This is sent underground to create larger, heavier tubers.

english: Tomato plants often shed their blossoms during extremely high temperatures or dry conditions because heat stress disrupts pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the unfertilized bloom to save water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo he ni nu bɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ha tomato tsei ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ ashwie koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in their roots to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that rapidly absorb fertilizers and water from the ground while their tall leaves block sunlight, effectively starving your crops of essential growth resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni baai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ jeɔ odɛŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut down my cocoa trees when they get sick instead of just treating them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso ko kɛji hela mɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofa baatsa lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certain serious plant diseases, like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, have no cure once they infect a tree. Cutting down and removing infected trees is the only effective way to stop the virus from spreading through the air or insects to your healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ahe helai komɛi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ, kɛji amɛbote tso lɛ mli pɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo ni ojie lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi amli kɛya o-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If my cocoa farm is destroyed by disease, can I plant fresh cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot right away?
ga: Kɛji hela kpata mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually risky to plant immediately. Disease pathogens and pests often remain alive in the soil or old roots. It is better to clear the old roots, let the land rest, or plant non-host cover crops for a period before putting new cocoa back into the ground.
ga: Oshara yɛ be fɛɛ mli akɛ abaadu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui hiɔ shikpɔŋ momo loo shishifãi amli. Ehi akɛ ooofɔ shishifãi momoi lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee gbɔi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ be ko dani okɛ kookoo hee aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a disease on my crops is dangerous enough to ruin my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ oshara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Dangerous diseases usually spread rapidly from plant to plant, causing leaves to turn yellow or drop early, stems to swell, or pods to rot quickly. If you notice symptoms spreading across multiple neighboring trees, it requires immediate action before it destroys the whole farm.
