ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ oshara gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛji ona okadii ni miigbɛ eshwa tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ Esa akɛ afee nɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani akpata ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: If cocoa is failing on my land, is rubber a good alternative crop for me to plant in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji kookoo nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani rɔba ji nɔ ni hi ni mahala akɛ makwɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Rubber can be a strong alternative because it is resilient and provides a steady income through latex collection for many years. However, rubber trees take about 6 to 7 years before you can start harvesting, so you need a plan for income while waiting for them to grow.
ga: Rɔba baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ mlɛo ni ehaa anáa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛjɛɔ nu ni akɛkpaa nu lɛ mli afii babaoo lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani obaanyɛ oje amɛkpamɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni oná shika he gbɛjianɔtoo be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Should I rely only on growing cocoa, or is it safer to plant other types of crops on my farm as well?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ nɔ loo ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: Planting different crops alongside or near cocoa, known as diversification, protects your income. If cocoa prices fall or a disease hits your cocoa trees, crops like plantain, cassava, or cashew can still provide food and money.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Kɛfataa loo ebɛŋkɛɔ kookoo Ale lɛ hu akɛ mlijaa. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shika ni onáa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ kookoo jara ba shi loo hela ba kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava loo cashew nuts. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika hu aha.

english: How do I choose the right new crop to plant if my land is no longer supporting cocoa well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso hee ni sa ni madu? Ni kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fioo kooloi akwɛmɔ sɛɛ dɔŋŋ hu?

english: You should consider your soil type, the amount of rainfall your region receives, and how easily you can sell the harvest at local markets. Crops like oil palm, rubber, or cashew thrive in different conditions than cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ he. Nugbɔ enyiɛ nɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ? kɛ bɔ ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei fɔ, rɔba loo cashew ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli fe kookoo.

english: What short-term crops can I grow to make money while waiting for newly planted cash crops like cocoa or rubber to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni adu, tamɔ kookoo loo rɔba lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You can plant quick-growing food crops like plantains, maize, cassava, or vegetables between the rows of young trees. These crops provide early harvests and income during the first few years before the main trees start producing.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ woɔ yibii oya kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli dani tsei titrii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How do I prepare my soil if I want to switch my field from cocoa to growing food crops like corn or cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni matsake miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo mli kɛya niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: After removing old cocoa stumps, you must clear remaining root debris and loosen the soil. Because cocoa trees draw specific nutrients over many years, adding organic manure or fertilizer helps restore the soil so food crops can grow strongly.
ga: Beni ojie kookoo tsei momo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ehe miihia ni ojie shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ afii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if an old cocoa tree has reached the end of its life and needs to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tso momo lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni ehe miihia ni atsake lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree yields very few pods despite proper weeding and fertilizing, has brittle decaying branches, or is over 25 to 30 years old, it is usually more profitable to cut it down and replant with improved, high-yielding seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Eyɛ niji ni shwieɔ shi. loo amɛye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he akɛ aaafolɔ amɛ ni akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops take many years to produce harvest while others produce in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi aheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛkpaa amɛnibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa and rubber spend their early years building deep root systems and thick trunks to support years of future production. Short-term crops like maize focus all their energy on quick growth and seed production, dying after one harvest.
ga: Tsei tamɔ kookoo kɛ rɔba yeɔ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni baaye abua wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni abaafee lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ oyaiyeli ni amɛdaraa kɛ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ lɛ he nii. ni baagbo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kome sɛɛ.

english: Why do the fruits on my farm keep falling to the ground when the sun becomes very scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: When midday heat becomes extreme, crops experience severe thermal and water stress. To protect their stems and roots from dying, the plants drop their fruits to conserve water and energy.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ. Koni abu tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛyibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Can intense afternoon sunlight damage my fruits while they are still on the plant?
ga: Ani shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite mi aduawai lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, direct scorching sunlight can burn the skin of your fruits, cause heat damage, and force the plant to shed them before they fully ripen.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã aduawai ahewolo. Eha dɔlɛ afite ni enyɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ eyitsɔi afɔ shi dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or wilt in extreme sun to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which helps the plant trap moisture and stop water loss.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle loo egbo yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mulching the soil with dry grass or leaves shades the ground from direct sun, keeps root zones cool, and retains soil moisture much longer during hot spells.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Does it mean my fruit tree is completely dead if all its unripe fruits fall off in the dry season?
ga: Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi aduawai tsei lɛ baagboi kɛji aduawai ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ gbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: No, dropping fruit is a survival response. The plant sacrifices its current fruit yield so it can keep its roots and branches alive through severe heat.
ga: Dabi, aduawai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji yiwalaheremɔ hetoo. Tsei kɛ nibii ni amɛfeɔ amrɔ nɛɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛnyɛ amɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: Should I leave some tall shade trees on my farm to protect my lower crops from heat?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: Yes, maintaining selective shade trees shields sensitive crops from direct midday rays, keeping the microclimate cooler and reducing heat-induced fruit drop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei pɔtɛɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ daaŋ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa aduawai ni dɔlɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi

english: Why does the ground under my crops get so hot during dry periods, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashishi lɛ mli dɔɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Uncovered soil absorbs direct heat from the sun, heating up the shallow roots and causing stress that leads to leaf burn and dropped fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ haomɔ ni haa baai lɛ shãa ni aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi baa.

english: What is the best time for me to water my farm when the weather is extremely hot?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Water your crops early in the morning or late in the evening so the roots can soak up moisture before the scorching sun evaporates it from the ground.
ga: Okɛ nu awo onibii amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do with fruits that have dropped onto the hot ground under my trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee aduawai ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Remove dropped fruits promptly to prevent pests and rot from spreading, and add organic mulch around the tree base to keep the soil shaded.
ga: Shĩ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã. Ni okɛ organic mulch abɔle tsei lɛ ashishi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop flowering when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause plants to pause flower and fruit formation, shifting their energy strictly toward surviving the dry and hot conditions.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. ni etsake hewalɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Rain can wash nitrogen away from the roots, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing extra shade branches, weeding around the trunks, and removing infected pods early helps air flow through the farm and protects healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kroko baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaf. Spraying the crop with natural neem oil solution or an appropriate pesticide gets rid of the insects so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme midday heat or erratic watering. Keeping the soil moist continuously and covering the ground with dry grass mulch keeps root temperatures cool so flowers can form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhao kɛjɛ gbi teŋ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing plenty of flowers but no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce mostly male flowers when they are young or going through a long dry spell. Once the tree matures and receives adequate rain and soil nutrients, it will start producing female flowers that grow into palm fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei babaoo woɔ fɔfɔi hii beni amɛji gbekɛbii loo amɛtsɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ. Beni tsei lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaabɔi fɔfɔi yei ni daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei yibii akui lɛ feemɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb up toward sunlight so their leaves can make food for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off damp ground, preventing leaf rot diseases and ensuring the leaves catch maximum sunlight to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni akɛ amɛbaa lɛ atsu nii akɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni okwɛ ni baa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ koni efee bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop and look wilted during hot afternoons even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoon hours, leaves lose water faster into the dry air than roots can suck it up from the soil. This temporary drooping is the plant's natural defense to save moisture, and the leaves will stand up straight again as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni baai lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing huge green leafy branches above ground but giving me tiny roots beneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ tsei niji agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overloaded with fresh chicken manure, cassava uses all its energy to make leaves on top instead of tubers below. Using balanced fertilizers high in potassium encourages the plant to store energy down in its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsina ŋmei hee fa tsɔ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha baai lɛ ahi ŋwɛi moŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛto hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize crop grow better afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that natural food remains in the earth, feeding the next crop of maize without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii baakã he ahi je lɛ mli. Eji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni akɛhaa kooloi ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: Why do my plantain stems fall over easily during heavy wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains fall easily if microscopic soil worms called nematodes have eaten their roots away underground. Planting clean suckers treated in hot water ensures strong roots grow deep into the soil to hold the heavy crop firmly against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ye amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsu nii ni akɛdu ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi ni wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to cover them, the intense sun burns their young leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Can I plant cassava together in the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa trees because cassava roots aggressively draw nutrients and water out of the soil, which starves the young cocoa plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi jieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close, their branches block sunlight from reaching lower leaves and they fight over soil nutrients, which reduces pod yield and makes it easy for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eniji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ni amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa pod yibii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves and branches from a healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baai kɛ eniji komɛi?

english: Pruning allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy, helping the tree send energy into producing pods rather than unnecessary leaves, while also stopping rot diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekpaa gangrene hu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when excess moisture gets trapped under heavy shade and wet leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Beni nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ emɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi ni baai lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when cocoa trees experience stress from lack of water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave dry fallen leaves on the ground under my cocoa trees instead of clearing them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni majie amɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a protective layer that traps moisture in the soil, and as they decay, they break down into natural plant food for your cocoa roots.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni kɛ́ efite lɛ Ebaakumɔ mli ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the right nutrients for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha kookoo dumɔ?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow during good rainy weather, or if the trees grow very slowly and produce tiny pods, your soil likely needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Aloo kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni efee ŋmɔtɔ bibii. Your soil may need fertilizer.

english: How do cocoa trees behave when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Te kookoo tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi?

english: During Harmattan, cocoa trees save water by dropping leaves and slowing down pod growth. Adding dead leaves around the roots helps keep the soil moist during this dry weather.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa fioo lɛ nɔ. Baai ni egboi ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi tamɔ nɛkɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my farm during rainy season and how does that affect my cocoa?
ga: Why do the weeds on my farm grow so fast during the rainy season? Ni te enáa mikoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast in warm, wet weather and steal water and nutrients from your cocoa trees. If left unchecked, high weeds also trap moisture and create habitats for crop pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. ni oju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ jwɛi kakadaji lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ shĩa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my farm, and how does that affect my crop yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The top layer of soil contains the essential nutrients and organic matter that crops need to grow. When heavy rain washes it away, it leaves behind poor soil, causing crops to stunt and yield far less.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ gbonyo yɛ esɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I stop big gullies and deep gutters from forming across my farmland after it rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi faai wuji kɛ ŋshɔkei ni mli kwɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Deep gullies form when rainwater rushes freely across bare or sloped ground. You can slow the water down and protect your land by planting vetiver grass along the slopes or digging small contour ridges.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hei ni agbele loo hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ amli oya. Obaanyɛ oha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ vetiver jwɛi ni ooodu yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe loo ŋshɔkei bibii ni ooofo lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it worth spending money to repair damaged soil on my farm, or will the land heal itself over time?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mafite shika kɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Aloo ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsa ehe yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Eroded land rarely heals on its own because each rainy season washes away more soil. Investing in soil protection keeps your land productive and prevents you from losing usable farmland completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsaaa ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fɛɛ be hoɔ shikpɔŋ babaoo kɛyaa. Shikpɔŋ hebuu mli nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii, ni ehaa okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baaje odɛŋ kwraa.

english: Yellow, curling leaves are typically a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps prevent this sickness from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela nɛɛ efiteɔ onibii.

english: Can diseases on my neighbor's crops spread into my farm and ruin my plants?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ akutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efite mitsei lɛ?

english: Yes, crop diseases can easily travel between farms through the wind, flowing rainwater, flying insects, or shared farm tools. Removing sick plants quickly and cleaning your tools helps protect your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ anɔ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. loo okɛ okwaayeli he nibii aha Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe saamɔ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every season even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground as they grow. If you plant year after year without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and drained of nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ odu nii afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, sũ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil fertile again for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer enriches the soil for the next crop you plant on that same piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa trees from burning while they establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la he yɛ be mli ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen to breathe. When water sits on the field with nowhere to drain, it drowns the roots, preventing the plant from taking up food and causing the maize to turn yellow and decay.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ta ŋmɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye niyenii. ni eha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni egbo.

english: How can I keep my vegetable crops from drying up so fast during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-vegetables lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi oya yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of plants and soil quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or palm leaves (mulching) retains soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ mli oya. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baa (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my maize plants curl up their leaves during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baa ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture and protect itself from drying out during high heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni oha ohe akagbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: As cassava matures past its main harvest period, the plant converts starchy energy into tough fiber and wood-like material to support its structure, making the roots hard and unpalatable.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ da kɛho ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ he lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ ŋmei hewalɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ nibii ni tamɔ tsei ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ŋɔɔɔɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop blossoms to conserve its remaining energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with thick stems but producing very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ tso ni mli tse shi ewoɔ pepper fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into leafy growth and stems instead of setting flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ato

english: What is the best way for me to get water to my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Farmers can use simple groundwater wells, bucket drip irrigation systems, or rainwater collection ponds to keep crops watered efficiently during dry periods without heavy evaporation.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nubui atsu nii. Tank type drip irrigation system loo nugbɔ nu ni abua naa nubu Koni eha tsei lɛ aná nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni mli wa waa bɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the early morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb water before the heat arrives, minimizing evaporation loss and protecting leaves from scald caused by hot water droplets.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Ha lasu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu baa lɛ he kɛjɛ shãa ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he

english: How does adding dried cow manure help my soil hold water longer for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Dried cow manure adds rich organic matter that acts like a sponge in the soil, improving its ability to retain moisture and nutrients after rainfall or watering.
ga: Tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni ekɛhaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without tall shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because intense sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out root moisture quickly before the plant gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ agbi oya dani tso lɛ baanyɛ adara.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting maize when the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plant when rainfall is strong enough to wet the soil to a depth of about 10 to 15 centimeters for a few consecutive days, ensuring seeds have steady moisture to germinate.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 mli gbii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall in poorly drained soil can cause root rot or fungal leaf diseases, which reduce the root system's ability to take up nutrients, causing older bottom leaves to yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo loo fungal leaf hela aba. Enɛ baaha nyɛmɔ ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛaana niyenii mli hewalɛ lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What does it mean when people say cocoa is an economic tree in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kookoo ji shika helɛtemɔ tso yɛ Ghana lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: An economic tree is a crop protected by law because it brings essential income and foreign exchange to the country. Cocoa is specially designated under Ghanaian law so people cannot legally destroy healthy farms for non-agricultural activities.
ga: Shikayeli tsei ji tsei ni mla buɔ he ejaakɛ amɛkɛ shika ni he hiaa kɛ maŋsɛɛ shika baa maŋ lɛ mli. Ahala cocoa krɛdɛɛ yɛ Ghana mla shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɛi nyɛŋ afite ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ mla naa kɛha nitsumɔi ni jeee okwaayeli nitsumɔi.

english: Is it illegal for me to cut down my own healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eji mlakwamɔ akɛ ooofo bo diɛŋtsɛ o-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, under Ghanaian law, healthy cocoa trees are protected economic assets. Even as the farmer, you are not allowed to uproot or clear healthy cocoa trees, especially for activities like illegal mining.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ Ghana mla shishi. Kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji shika helɛtemɔ nibii ni abuɔ he. Ákɛ okwaafonyo po lɛ, Aŋmɛɛɛ bo gbɛ ni ojie loo ojie kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ nifeemɔi tamɔ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he.

english: Can someone force me to destroy my cocoa farm so they can mine for gold?
ga: Ani mɔ ko baanyɛ anyɛ minɔ koni makpãtã mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛjie shika tsuru?

english: No, clearing cocoa farms for illegal mining (galamsey) is strictly against the law. Cocoa trees are protected, and destroying them for mining carries serious legal penalties.
ga: Dabi, kookoo ŋmɔji amli ni ajieɔ kɛha shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) lɛ ji nɔ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ mla kwraa. Abuɔ kookoo tsei ahe. Ni kookoo tsei ni akpataa koni akɛtsa shika lɛ ji mla naa toigbalamɔ ni naa wa waa.

english: Why does the law treat cocoa differently from other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mla lɛ kɛ kookoo yeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a vital cash crop that supports Ghana's national economy and rural livelihoods. Because of its economic importance, specific laws were written to protect cocoa trees from being casually destroyed.
ga: Kookoo ji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa Ghana shika kɛ akrowa shihilɛ. Akɛni ehe hiaa yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ hewɔ lɛ, aŋmala mlai pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni akɛbu cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ oshara mli.

english: What should I do if someone damages or uproots my cocoa trees without my permission?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mɔ ko kpata mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahiɛ loo ejie amɛshishifãi ni miŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ?

english: You should report the incident immediately to your local COCOBOD extension officer, police, and traditional authorities, because destroying cocoa trees without legal cause is a criminal offense.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ he amaniɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ otsɔɔ COCOBOD extension officer ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, polisifoi kɛ kusum nifeemɔi ahe nitsulɔi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko kpata cacao tsei ahiɛ ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ, eji efɔŋfeemɔ.

english: Am I allowed to cut down a cocoa tree if it gets sick?
ga: Ani aŋmɛ mi gbɛ ni mafo kookoo tso kɛji hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, the law allows you to remove or uproot cocoa trees if they are diseased or severely damaged, as this prevents infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus from spreading to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, mla lɛ ŋmɛɔ bo gbɛ ni ojie cacao tsei loo ojie kɛji hela mɔ cacao tsei lɛ loo efite waa. Enɛ ji akɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa tree is sick enough that it needs to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ kookoo tso ko aahu akɛ ehe miihia ni afo lɛ?

english: Look for signs like swollen branches, yellow patterns on leaves, or pods dying prematurely. When a tree is infected with viruses that cannot be cured, cutting it down is necessary to save the rest of your farm.
ga: Taomɔ okadii tamɔ tsei niji ni efuu kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. loo pod lɛ gboɔ oya Kɛji hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ emɔ tso ko No hewɔ lɛ tso ni afoɔ lɛ he miihia koni akɛbu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Can I uproot very old cocoa trees that no longer produce good pods?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie kookoo tsei ni egbɔ waa ni wooo ŋmeii kpakpai dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, uprooting old, unproductive, or damaged trees for farm rehabilitation and replanting fresh cocoa seedlings is permitted and encouraged by agricultural officers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni egbɔ, ni wooo yibii loo ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ kɛha ŋmɔ mli saamɔ kɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei adumɔ ji nɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Since I planted the cocoa trees myself, why can't I clear them to build houses?
ga: Kɛjɛ be mli ni mi diɛŋtsɛ miduɔ kookoo Mɛni hewɔ ojieee mli ni oma shia?

english: While the land is yours, the law protects cocoa trees as national economic assets to safeguard national cocoa production. Changing the land use requires proper guidance and authorization.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji onɔ̃ moŋ Mla lɛ hu buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he akɛ maŋ shika helɛtemɔ nibii. Bɔni afee ni abu maŋ lɛ mli kookoo feemɔ he Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ biɔ ŋaawoo kɛ hegbɛ ni sa.

english: How does illegal mining affect cocoa trees growing nearby?
ga: Te shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ saa kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Illegal mining destroys the topsoil, pollutes groundwater, and washes toxic chemicals into nearby farms, which stunts cocoa growth, turns leaves yellow, and can eventually kill the trees.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni afiteɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni ashwieɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ dalɛ kpaa. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ekolɛ ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains grown above them during their first two years to trap moisture and protect their leaves until they develop a strong root system.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛyiteŋ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaaná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress, which destroys pollen before fertilization can happen. The plant naturally sheds its flowers to save energy when it senses it cannot support fruit under extreme heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ dani fɔmɔ baanyɛ aba. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa aduawai yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ.

english: Yams are climbing plants that rely on upright foliage to capture sunlight for photosynthesis. Staking lifts the leaves into full sunlight, improves air circulation around the plant, and keeps leaves away from damp soil pathogens that cause leaf spot diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ nɔ koni amɛmɔ hulu la kɛha fotosintɛsis. Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ kpaaa gbee lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Multiple shoots competing around one mother plantain stem fight over soil nutrients, water, and space. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one or two strong successors ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi babaoo kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli yɛ he. Plantain tso kome shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ ŋwɛi. Ni aaafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni eshi nɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko kɛha he odase lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are produced through specific breeding techniques that maximize plant vigor, disease resistance, and yield. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose these traits in the next generation, leading to weaker growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ fɔmɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ. Helai ahe hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the soil when planted during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need well-aerated soil to breathe and push out roots. Heavy rains in poorly drained soil cause waterlogging, which starves the cutting of oxygen and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the stem.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ afolɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni anyɛ amu ni ashɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and V-shaped at the tips while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee V-shape yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, causing the lower foliage to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial soil bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil fertilizer. This natural process enriches the soil and improves the growth of companion crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa tsei ni fata he tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves scorch and die if I place dry fertilizer directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are composed of concentrated mineral salts. When placed right against a dry plant stem without being dissolved in moist soil, the salts pull water out of the plant tissues through osmotic pressure, causing severe burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo tsei ahe tsei ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ, amɛshwieee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Nu gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ osmotic pressure nɔ. Ekɛ shãa ni naa wa baa

english: Upward curling on pepper leaves is typically caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids, or viruses carried by whiteflies. As these tiny insects feed on the undersides of young leaves, they damage leaf cells and distort their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni whiteflies kɛyaa lɛ Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. Amɛfiteɔ baa mli wala yibii ni amɛfiteɔ amɛdalɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn warm and spoil so quickly when I keep it in ordinary plastic bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotoku mli daa lɛ?

english: Harvested maize is still living tissue that releases moisture and heat. Ordinary airtight plastic bags trap this moisture inside, creating a warm, damp environment that causes mold to grow and ruin your grain quickly.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kpo. Plastic kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ naa lɛ mɔɔ nu yɛ mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ adara ni efite ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Where do the small weevils in my stored corn come from even when I keep the bag tightly tied?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni mitoɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ? Ni mikɛ baagi lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the corn grains while the crop is still standing in the field. When you store the corn in a warm place, those hidden eggs hatch into insects that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Beni okɛ ŋmãa toɔ he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ Nakai ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: How do I know if my corn on the field is dry enough to harvest and store without it rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa ni mikɛto ni egbooo?

english: Maize is dry enough when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that your thumbnail cannot easily dent them. High moisture in wet grains leads to heat and fungal growth inside storage bags.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akumɔ onaneshi ni etsɔ mli lɛ mlɛo. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to mix my maize seeds with protective chemical powder before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afutu ŋmãa dumɔwui dani adu lɛ?

english: Mixing seeds with protective treatments coats them with a protective shield against soil insects, birds, and fungal diseases, ensuring the seeds survive underground long enough to sprout into healthy seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he futuɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi bibii, okpoi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds fail to sprout after I plant them and rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged by insects during storage, planted too deep in heavy soil, or if the soil became flooded and starved the seeds of the air they need to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just take maize grains from my harvest bag to plant as seeds next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli ni mikɛduɔ akɛ dumɔwui yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains saved from hybrid maize crops lose their vigor in the second generation. Planting saved grain instead of fresh, certified seed results in weak growth and a much lower harvest.
ga: Ŋmaa ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ najiaŋ lɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up and turn brown during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ blɔfo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water when the sun gets too hot. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce surface area and stop moisture from evaporating, though prolonged heat will cause the leaf tips to dry out permanently.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, dɔlɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha baa lɛ naa agbi daa.

english: Why are some of my maize plants tall while others on the very same land stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Maize plants need balanced nutrients and moisture from the soil. Because soil fertility and water holding capacity are uneven across a field, plants in poorer or harder patches of soil struggle to grow tall.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa tsei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ nu mli lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant too many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks that produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing grains and empty gaps instead of full rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty spaces on a cob happen when dry weather or high heat damages the silks at the top of the cob during flowering. If the silks do not catch pollen from the tassels, those specific grain spots will stay completely empty.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha siliki ba tso lɛ yiteŋ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ emɔɔɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Nakai mfoniri pɔtɛɛ hei lɛ baafee efolo kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa from hot sun while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my maize and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. Night-flying moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the tightly wrapped center of the maize plant where it is soft and moist to feed on the young leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni foɔ gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ lɛ mli. Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize farm produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those specific food sources and lets soil pests that target maize build up in large numbers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hoɔ. kɛ gbɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest underground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava matures, the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem. You will also notice the soil around the base of the plant cracking open as the expanding tubers push outward.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. Obaana shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mligbalamɔ be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on before the tubers under the ground can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni ekwɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. The wooden stakes lift the leaves off the damp ground away from rot and pests, allowing the plant to catch enough light to send energy down into the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Tso tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ heɔ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. Without enough moisture, the plant cannot feed the flowers, so it drops them to save its energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha fɔfɔi lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: What causes the leaves on my green pepper plants to curl upward like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects that distorts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Why do my crop stems turn black and dry up when I place granular fertilizer right next to the plant base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem draws water out of the plant tissue like a sponge, burning the stem and roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli tamɔ sponji. Shãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni oooha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and weak even after I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weed roots usually grow faster and spread wider than crop roots. They quickly absorb the fertilizer and water you apply before your crops can reach it, while also blocking sunlight from reaching the crop leaves.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa fe tsei shishifãi. Amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Do not plant after just one short shower because the subsoil remains dry. Dig into the soil with a cutlass; if the damp earth reaches as deep as your hand's length (about 15 cm), there is enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kaadu yɛ be mli ni okɛ nu fioo ko pɛ efɔ sɛɛ. shikome pɛ Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsɔne kuku tsuɔ nii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tamɔ onine lɛ kɛlɛ (aafee 15 cm) lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects with recommended sprays or neem oil keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up so they get maximum sunlight and stay off the damp ground, which prevents disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe, ni no baaye abua ni helai akamɔ bo.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoot stems growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main tree. Pruning them away and leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ni ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree is stressed by intense sunlight, dry weather, or pests like mirids. Keeping proper shade trees in your farm and protecting the trees from pests helps the flowers develop into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ hulu la. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots feed calcium to the tomatoes and stops the rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa loo calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhaa tomato lɛ calcium, ni ekpaa fitemɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the sun from drying out the ground, protects roots from extreme heat, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Buu shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why does lowland rice grow well in standing water while my other crops die when flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Mine died when it flooded?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems that carry oxygen down from the leaves straight to the roots underwater, allowing them to breathe where other crops would rot and drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛtso lɛ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Ehaa amɛmuɔ yɛ he ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛŋ amu yɛ lɛ. baagbo ni ebaagbo yɛ nu mli

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help make the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When the plants die after harvest, this extra nitrogen stays in the soil to fertilize whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do coconut trees seem to grow so much better near the ocean here in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ masɛi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Coconut trees naturally thrive in coastal regions because they love salty sea air and high chlorine levels in the soil, which helps them absorb water efficiently and produce bigger nuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ ŋshɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ chlorine ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Does the breeze near the sea actually help my crops, or is it bad for them?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: For crops like coconuts, coastal air is very beneficial because it carries moist, mineral-rich sea spray containing chlorine and salt, creating the ideal atmosphere for healthy tree growth.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ŋshɔnaa kɔɔyɔɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋshɔ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ mineral ni chlorine kɛ ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell what hidden nutrients my farm soil is missing before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ dani madu nii?

english: You need to perform a soil test through an agricultural extension officer, which chemically checks your land to show exactly what elements—like chlorine, nitrogen, or acidity—your soil lacks.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ. Enɛ baatsɔ tsofa nɔ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ koni etsɔɔ nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ chlorine, nitrogen, loo acidity.

english: Why should I spend money to test my soil when I can already tell my land is good just by looking at it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa he? Be mli ni obaanyɛ ona akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛtsɔ ekwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Looking at soil only tells you its color and moisture, but soil testing reveals invisible minerals and salt levels that determine whether a specific crop like coconut will yield well or fail.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaana bɔ ni eyɔɔ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ha lɛ pɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ nɔ kaai jieɔ shika tsuru ni anaaa kɛ ŋmei ni falɛ ni tsɔɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko tamɔ ŋmei baawo yibii jogbaŋŋ loo ebaawo yibii kpakpai lɛ kpo.

english: What is the first step I need to take with my land before planting coconut seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu ŋmei dumɔwui?

english: Before planting, you should test the soil to check its chlorine and mineral levels so you can add the correct nutrients to the land before the young trees go into the ground.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ okwɛ bɔ ni chlorine kɛ mineral yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ okɛ niyenii ni sa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is salt or chlorine actually useful for any crops, or will it kill my plants?
ga: Ani ŋmei loo chlorine he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaafite mitsei lɛ?

english: While salt damages most food crops, tree crops like coconuts actually require chlorine to stay healthy, grow strong fronds, and survive dry seasons.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei gbeɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo moŋ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmeii he miihia chlorine koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ, amɛná baai ni wa, ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: My coconut trees are yielding small fruits and growing slowly—what could be missing in the soil?
ga: Mikokoo tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii. kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ fiofio—mɛɛ nɔ elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Slow growth and low yield in coconuts often mean the soil is low in chlorine and key minerals, which are frequently lacking when farming far away from coastal areas.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ klorin kɛ nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, ebɛ kɛ́ atsu okwaayeli he nii ni kɛ ŋshɔnaa hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Can I add salt to my land to help my coconut trees if my farm is far away from the sea?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni eye ebua mi ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, coconut farms inland often need added chloride or agricultural salt, but you must test your soil first so you put the exact right amount without damaging the roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni akɛ chloride loo ŋoo awo ŋmei ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛha okwaayeli. Shi ehe miihia ni oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ falɛ ni sa awo mli ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do plants behave when they don't get the exact soil minerals they prefer?
ga: Te tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛnáaa shika tsuru ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops miss their specific preferred nutrients, their leaves turn pale, growth slows down, and they produce very few or poor-quality fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdalɛ baa shi. ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do two farmers planting coconuts on neighboring land often get totally different yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ okwaafoi enyɔ ni duɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa lɛ?

english: Crop success depends heavily on good management skills, such as knowing how to test soil, correcting missing soil nutrients like chlorine, and caring for the trees properly over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ omanyeyeli damɔ nibii akwɛmɔ he ŋaa kpakpa nɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni aleɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ chlorine lɛ asaamɔ, kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to turn dark green and grow fast again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara oya ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my farm right before heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface or washes it too deep into the ground before the crop's roots can drink it, which wastes your money and leaves the plants hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is exhausted and needs plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo mi ni tsei niyenii he miihia mi?

english: Exhausted soil shows signs like slow crop growth, pale or yellowish leaves, and small yields even when there is enough rain, indicating that the natural nutrients in the ground have been used up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛ yibii fioo pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil, which results in tall, thin stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves on top of my soil help my crops during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves creates a protective blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating and keeping the ground moist for your crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Taller trees or plantain plants give them the shade and cool air they need to survive until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ loo plantain lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it helpful to trim the small extra branches at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Trimming lower branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the plant to stop diseases, and it forces the plant to send its energy into making larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afolɔ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni helai akpa. Ni ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the farm office grow better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ Farm Bureau lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Specially prepared certified seeds are bred to resist local pests and diseases and are selected so that almost every seed germinates evenly to give a bigger harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo jɛmɛ kooloi kɛ helai. Ni ahalaa lɛ bɔni afee ni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ená yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stems stops this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ŋmɔŋ baa. ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Tsoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa enɛ kpaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of specific soil nutrients needed to hold and develop the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛhiɛ aduawai ni amɛwo lɛ mli ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Officer, why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from heat. The plant is not dying; once the rains return, it will grow fresh green leaves and continue swelling its roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ gbooo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfuɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold up when the heat is high to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun. This smart behavior stops the plant from losing too much water through sweating.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa koni ebaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieee nu babaoo yɛ latsaa hewɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or dry, or when insects fail to visit and move pollen. Keeping soil moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni kooloi nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛkɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi amli lɛ aya Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ mulch haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Stretching for light makes them tall and weak, leaving little energy to form big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ kane lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee shwiili ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and bent instead of straight down into the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, stony, or unplowed soil. Making deep, soft mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to push downward smoothly and grow straight.
