ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ shi kɛya shi mlɛo ni amɛdara ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Kookoo tsei bibii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal the water and plant food from the soil. Clearing them before the rains ensures your young trees get all the nutrients to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii. kɛ nu ni ajuɔ kɛ niyenii ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ojie amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Officer, is it safe for me to mix leftover wood ash into the soil before planting my pepper seedlings?
ga: Ofisa Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ tso sũ ni eshwɛ lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu pepper dumɔwui?

english: Yes, mixing small amounts of wood ash adds useful nutrients like potassium and reduces soil sourness. However, do not use too much, as heavy ash can burn young pepper roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ fioo ko futu mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ potassium afata he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ aba shi. Shi kɛlɛ, kaakɛ babaoo atsu nii. Ejaakɛ sũ ni tsii baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juice from under the leaves. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can feed itself.
ga: Nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛhe niyenii.

english: Why do the stems of my vegetable seedlings rot right at the ground level after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when soil fungi attack soft stems in overly wet ground. Creating good drainage channels so water does not sit around the stem protects young seedlings from rotting.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutua tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛi kpakpai ni afee koni nu akabɔle tso lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil quickly when I put it inside bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains hidden moisture inside the grains. Bagging wet grain traps moisture, creating a warm environment where mold and rot grow rapidly. The cobs must be sun-dried thoroughly before storage.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmaa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ oya Esa akɛ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Sick cocoa trees often show yellowing leaves, swollen shoots, or dark patches on the pods. Checking your trees regularly for these unusual signs helps you spot disease early before it spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmeii ni efuu, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli daa koni ona okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona helai mra. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down cocoa trees that have the swollen shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ?

english: Cocoa swollen shoot disease has no cure once a tree is infected. Cutting down the infected tree removes the virus from your farm, stopping mealybugs from spreading it to your healthy cocoa trees nearby.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsa cocoa tso lɛ mli fũu lɛ kɛji hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ pɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hela lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpaa mealybugs lɛ gbɛ koni ekagbɛ eshwa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does crop disease spread from one farm in a village to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ akrowa ko mli kɛyaa ekroko mli?

english: Crop diseases can spread through infected seeds, wind, rain, insects, or even farm tools like cutlasses carrying infected sap from an unhealthy field to a healthy one.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dade ni hiɛɔ nu ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ po nɔ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings right where I just cut down old, diseased trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛji mifo tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ?

english: It is best to clear the area properly and wait a few months, as disease-carrying insects or pathogens might still live in the remaining roots or soil of the old trees for a period after cutting them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi, ejaakɛ kooloi loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso momo lɛ shishifãi loo shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli be fioo yɛ be mli ni afo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Does planting crops near streams or rivers affect how easily my cocoa gets sick?
ga: Ani dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ faa loo faa ko masɛi lɛ saa bɔ ni hela mɔɔ mi-kokoo lɛ oya lɛ he?

english: Streams create high humidity and damp conditions, which can encourage fungal diseases like black pod disease to grow faster on cocoa trees if there is not enough air circulating through the farm.
ga: Faji lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi baa. Enɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct, harsh sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and roots before they can establish deep root systems to absorb enough water from the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Should I clean my cutlass and farm tools after cutting a sick tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-daggers kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe beni mifo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, always clean your cutlasses and pruning shears with soap or disinfectant after cutting infected plants, so you do not accidentally transfer disease sap to healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai atsumɔ o-dagger kɛ o-pruning shears lɛ he beni ofo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni okɛ tsofa ni hela emɔ lɛ akawo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oshara mli.

english: What small insects should I look out for that bring disease to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloi bibii esa akɛ male ni baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mealybugs are tiny, white, cotton-like insects that carry the virus causing cocoa swollen shoot disease, so controlling them with safe practices helps keep your trees healthy.
ga: Mealybugs ji kooloi bibii. Nibii yɛŋ, ni tamɔ kotoku ni hiɛ hela ni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fũuɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kudɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my crop leaves turn yellow, does it always mean the plant has a disease?
ga: Kɛji mi tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ani etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hela be fɛɛ be?

english: Not always; yellow leaves can be a sign of disease, but they can also mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is receiving too much water or sunlight.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be; Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee hela he okadi. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu loo hulu la babaoo tsɔ.

english: What should I do if my neighbor's cocoa farm has a disease but mine does not?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɛ hu?

english: You should inform your neighbor and an extension officer so the infected trees can be safely cut down or managed together, because insects and air carrying diseases do not stop at farm boundaries.
ga: Esa akɛ oha akutsoŋbii lɛ ale ni owo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ hewalɛ koni afo loo akɛtsu nii ekomekomei shweshweeshwe. Ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ ekpaaa ŋmɔji amli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade during their early years because full, direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil faster than their tiny roots can absorb water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbi. Ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu.

english: Yellowing leaves from the tips usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential food plants need to build strong leaves and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I make sure I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miidu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds or nodes on the stem where old leaves grew; these buds should always point upward toward the sky so the roots grow down and the shoots grow up properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni baai momo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni ŋmeii lɛ hu aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer over the farm right before a big downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ dani nugbɔ anɔ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes the fertilizer off the top of the field and away from your crops before their roots can drink it in, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ kɛyaa he kroko kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani amɛshishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Efiteɔ oshika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with tiny fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close to one another, they fight for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough strength to produce big harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛaawo yibii babaoo.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark green dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of young corn stalks during the day to feed on the tender leaf growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil to plant maize on the exact same farm patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ abele yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas work with microscopic life in the dirt to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil when the plants die.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi ni ji adebɔɔ niyenii kɛji tsei gboi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Extra suckers drink water and steal nutrients from the main mother tree, which causes the main plantain bunch to grow smaller and take longer to ripen.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains akuu titri lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛɔ.

english: Why should I place dry bush leaves and grass around the roots of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei bibii ni egbi kɛ jwɛi abɔle he lɛ? Tomato tso shishifãi

english: Covering the dirt with dry plant material acts like an umbrella that keeps the soil cool, holds water in the ground longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die if I plant them in an open field without any shade crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides shelter, keeps the air cool, and retains soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo ashiɔ kookoo tsei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up long wooden stakes to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni ekɛ bulb agbo aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy. Staking lifts the vines off the muddy ground, allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and feed that energy back down into building larger roots.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ekɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen runs low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating crops helps the soil rest and stay fertile naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehiɛɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts or beans makes my soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special microbes on their roots that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants finish growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small, weak ears when I drop three or four seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up fighting each other for the limited water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each seed enough resources to produce full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look pale and thin even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that absorb soil water and suck up fertilizers much faster than your main crops can. Even with good rain, the weeds rob your crops of the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ sũ mli nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otso titri lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi jwɛi hu juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of flowers but then drop them without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛshiɔ amɛ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of insect pollinators causes stress to tomato plants. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy instead of trying to nurture fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo pollinators ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if heavy rain floods my farm close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When water covers the field for several days, it starves the roots of air, causing them to drown and decay under the wet earth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ. ni ehaa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does spreading dry grass over the bare soil around my pepper plants help them survive heat spikes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiye amɛmiibua amɛ ni amɛmiiye hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from baking the ground. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly so the roots stay moist.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main parent stem. Removing most suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough energy to yield a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why is my maize field turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like NPK, Urea, or well-rotted animal manure restores the green color and helps the plant grow strong ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK, urea, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal nutrients, space, and fertilizer from your soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is causing tiny green caterpillars to eat holes inside the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ feɔ? Ye bu ko yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center of maize plants. Applying targeted treatments or placing a pinch of clean sand or neem powder into the plant funnel helps suppress them early.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ he ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii loo akɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo loo neem powda fata dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa okadii nɛɛ mra.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early with soapy water solutions or neem oil prevents the leaves from shrinking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni kɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long, causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. Watering the plants regularly at the root level and applying dry grass mulch keeps the soil cool and helps flowers develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi awo mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and keeps the leaves away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ amɛ

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings fall over and die at the base right after sprouting in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛshishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This issue, called damping-off, is caused by soil fungi thriving in overly wet conditions. Watering nursery beds lightly in the morning rather than late evening prevents standing moisture and keeps seedling stems firm.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu shwie ŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ fioo Leebi maŋkpa moŋ fe gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaabu tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni eha dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily burnt by direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide crucial shade and keep the soil moist, acting like living umbrellas while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ,.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant will help it grow green and form healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbɔle Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni otoi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing small caterpillar holes in the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding deep inside the central leaves of the corn plant. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract in the late afternoon will protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and space to grow big and yield high-quality produce.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas make my farmland better for my next crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant, like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or uneven watering. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the soil cool and moist, allowing the flowers to stay on and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my rich topsoil and seeds on sloped land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ midumɔwui ni baa nii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting across the slope in raised ridges (contour farming) creates barriers that slow down running water. This keeps the rain from washing away your nutrient-rich topsoil and seeds during heavy downpours.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli (Contour farming) lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo. Enɛ baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm early when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ehe miihia beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks gives your crops a strong start without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Can I save corn seeds from my harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔ be mli koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted traditional seeds, you can save them if dried properly. However, if you planted high-yielding hybrid seeds, replanting saved seeds will result in a much smaller yield. It is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season for hybrid varieties.
ga: Kɛji odu blema dumɔwui Obaanyɛ okɛto kɛji ogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni ooodu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa. Esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi kɛha dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome.

english: How long does a pepper crop take from planting before I can harvest and make money?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa pepper tso ko ni enáa sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Pepper usually takes about 2.5 to 3 months to start fruiting after transplanting seedlings into the main field. Once harvesting begins, you can pick fresh peppers every few days for several months, providing a regular income stream.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 2.5 kɛyashi 3 dani ŋmeii jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni adu dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Beni kpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi Obaanyɛ okɛ chili hee ato be fɛɛ be. Gbii fioo kɛyashi nyɔji babaoo Enɛ baaha shika aba daa.

english: How do I decide whether to plant pepper or rice on my farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu pepper loo ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pepper gives high returns on smaller plots of land with continuous harvests, but requires closer attention, quick sales, and regular labor. Rice requires more land and steady water, yields a single bulk harvest, and can be stored easily if you want to wait for better market prices.
ga: Pepper woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔji bibii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ nɔ daa lɛ anɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya, ni akɛ be fɛɛ atsu nii. Omɔ he miihia he babaoo kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. yibiiwoo shikome Ni abaanyɛ akɛto he mlɛo kɛji oosumɔ ni omɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I join with other farmers to farm on one large land instead of farming alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi afee ekome kɛtsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu kome nɔ moŋ fe ni mikome too matsu okwaayeli he nii?

english: Grouping land and working together allows farmers to buy seeds and fertilizers in bulk at lower prices, share labor and equipment costs, and attract bigger buyers who are looking for large volumes of produce.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni abua naa kɛ ekomefeemɔ haa okwaafoi heɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Jaa nitsumɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni ogbala jarayelɔi wuji ni miitao nibii babaoo ni amɛbaahe lɛ.

english: Why do market prices for local rice change from one season to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa jara tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Rice prices fluctuate based on supply and demand. Immediately after the main harvest, the market has plenty of rice so prices are lower. During the lean season when rice is scarce, prices go up.
ga: Omɔ jara tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa kɛ nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ naa. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jara lɛ nɔ ŋmãa babaoo yɛ, no hewɔ lɛ jara baa shi. Yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baashɛ ni jara baaya ŋwɛi.

english: Pepper flowers usually fall off because of extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil properly watered and nourished helps flowers stay on the plant to form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I calculate my expected profit before I even buy my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu sɛɛnamɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ akɛ maná lɛ he akɔntaa dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: First, add up all expenses like land preparation, seeds, fertilizer, labor, and transport. Next, estimate your yield and multiply it by the current market selling price. Subtracting your total expenses from expected sales shows your estimated profit.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, okɛ shika fɛɛ ni he hiaa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ, dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, nitsulɔi, kɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ afata he. No sɛɛ lɛ, bu nɔ ni obaaku sɛɛ aba lɛ he akɔntaa ni okɛ jara ni ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɛɛ abɔ he. Kɛ́ ojie shika fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ obaahɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni osusuɔ akɛ obaaná lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant a large area like 12 acres with only one type of crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko tamɔ acre 12 kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ?

english: Planting a single crop on a large scale can give big profits if market prices are good, but it carries higher risk if pests attack or market prices crash. Splitting large land between two different crops helps spread and reduce your financial risk.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he waa kɛji jara nɔ jara hi. Shi oshara ni fa babaoo yɛ kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua amɛ loo jara nɔ jara ba shi. Shikpɔŋ wulu ko ni oooja yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ateŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa shika he oshara ni oyɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How many times can I pick pepper from the same plant once it starts fruiting?
ga: Peppers enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: With proper watering, good fertilizer, and pest management, a healthy pepper plant can be harvested repeatedly every 5 to 7 days for a period of 3 to 6 months.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nu ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shii abɔ daa gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 kɛyashi nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6.

english: What kind of soil is best for growing healthy peppers?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Peppers grow best in well-drained, rich sandy-loam soil that allows water to pass through easily. Heavy clay soils that trap standing water cause pepper roots to rot quickly.
ga: Peppers kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni haa nu hoɔ yɛ mli mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Is it better to sell my harvested crop immediately or hold onto it for a few months?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi?

english: Selling immediately gives you quick cash to cover expenses, but selling right at harvest time often brings lower prices due to high market supply. Perishable crops like pepper should be sold quickly, while dry grains like rice can be stored to sell later when prices rise.
ga: Kɛ́ ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaawo shika ni ofiteɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, jarayeli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ haa jara baa shi yɛ jarayeli nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmaa ni egbi tamɔ ŋmãa ato koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the rest of the plant is green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps it build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plant will help restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji feɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the cocoa seedlings from scorching sun and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ kookoo tsei lɛ, ebaabu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing the tubers of my cassava to rot and turn watery inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛwoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays too soggy for too long, allowing water-loving fungi to attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs; giving each seed proper space leads to bigger cobs and a heavier overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛaaha amɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl tightly upward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during extreme heat as a survival trick to reduce surface area and slow down water loss. Mulching the base of the plants with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and moist so the leaves relax.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ fiteɔ lɛ shi blɛoo. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards easily without pushing against hard clay or rocks. High mounds provide soft soil for deep tuber growth and ensure good drainage so tubers don't rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni wa ahe. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha tuber shweremɔ, ni ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ eshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping the soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why can't I save the seeds from this season's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their special strength in the second generation, leading to mixed, weak plants and much smaller harvests. Buying fresh certified hybrid seed each season guarantees high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni efutu lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibii kwraa. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa.

english: Why does fast-growing grass in my groundnut farm reduce the amount of nuts I harvest under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers must bend down and push themselves into the soil to grow nuts. Dense weeds block these flower pegs from reaching the ground and steal the fertilizer meant for your crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ akoto shi koni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛdu ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ nɛkɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks when clearing a new plot of land?
ga: Te esa akɛ odu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni kɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ oosaa shikpɔŋ hee?

english: Planting cassava about one meter (3 feet) apart in straight rows leaves enough space for the roots to expand into large tubers and ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ aaafee mita kome (naji etɛ) yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Should I plant my crops on raised soil ridges or plant directly on flat ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting on raised soil ridges loosens the earth so root crops like cassava and sweet potatoes can grow bigger tubers, while also protecting roots from waterlogging during heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni nu akabote mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and use stakes for my yam vines to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii ni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce energy that travels down into the soil to feed and expand the yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaye niyenii ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food in the soil or the ground is soaked with stagnant water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage helps leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni damɔ shi ewo sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from drought, insect damage, or a lack of shade. Maintaining good shade and controlling pests like mirid bugs helps flowers develop into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, kooloi fitemɔ, loo hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ myrids lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping up fruiting stalks with wooden poles and planting suckers deep enough in rich soil prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. cause a lot weight Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso yibii lɛ amli lɛ du ni adu ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight and dry out quickly. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides the protective shade young cocoa needs.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps prevent this fruit rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai nɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can I plant legumes like cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize naturally enriches your soil. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the ground, feeding the nearby maize plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap, or viral diseases carried by these pests. Spraying recommended organic treatments helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa Organic ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ŋaawoo baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and skinny without making big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are placed too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and nutrients to build strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni magbee shi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni mitsakeee mi-cacao ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree lacks water, gets too much heat, suffers from pest attacks, or is too young to support pods. Proper shade and soil moisture help the flowers stay on and grow into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Get too hot Piŋmɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui amli loo amɛdarako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni wa.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain tree steal food and water from the main stem. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe Dumɔwui komekomei babaoo tsɔ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why are tiny green worms eating the leaves inside the tops of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ayiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Catching them early and treating the plants prevents them from destroying the center of the crop where new leaves and cobs form.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Amɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ he ni baai kɛ ŋmeii heei baa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids, or a virus they spread. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and allows the plant to flower and fruit normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the sides just as they start to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly receiving a lot of water. The inside of the fruit grows faster than its skin can stretch, causing it to crack. Keeping watering steady prevents this.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu babaoo ni enine shɛɔ nɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause rupture Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: If your crops from the last harvest grew slowly, had pale green or yellowish leaves, or produced smaller yields than before, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer, manure, or compost.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe tsutsu lɛ Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Planting the same crop in the same place every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps restore the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to remove weeds early when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your plants. Clearing them early ensures your young crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do coconut trees grow so well near beaches and rivers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa kɛ faai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Coconut trees thrive near water bodies because they need a continuous water supply to grow well. Their roots spread wide to constantly draw underground water, allowing them to flourish in places where water is always accessible.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo koni amɛya nɔ amɛjie shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Kwɛmɔ ni amɛshwere yɛ hei ni amɛnáa nu be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: How does a coconut nut get filled with water even when there has been no rain for months?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ nu awo ŋmeii amli ekoŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo moŋ?

english: Coconut trees have deep and extensive root systems that reach far underground to drink water continuously. The tree acts like a natural pump, storing this drawn-up water inside the nut so it never runs dry.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛná nu be fɛɛ be. Tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli pɔmpii. Kɛtsɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. koni ekagbi

english: Can I plant coconut trees on dry farmland far away from any river or water source?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni kɛ faai loo nu jɛɛhei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can plant them on higher or dryer ground, but they will not produce as many nuts. Coconuts yield the best fruits when planted where underground water is easy for their roots to reach at all times.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shi amɛbaafee ŋmeii babaoo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɔɔ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he oya be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does my farmland dry out so fast just a few hours after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Sandy soil or soil with low organic matter allows water to drain away very quickly. The hot sun also pulls water out of the surface soil rapidly unless the ground is covered or shielded.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ mli oya waa. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. ja shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo duŋ loo eyɛ teemɔŋ

english: How can I keep soil moist for longer so my crops do not suffer during short dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii akapiŋ yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from reaching the dirt, trapping moisture in the ground for your plants to use later.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ha onibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni otsei lɛ kɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops wither quickly in hot weather while trees like coconut stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmeii hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Crops with shallow roots only get water from the top surface of the soil, which dries out fast under the sun. Large trees like coconuts have deep roots that pull water from far below ground where it stays wet.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ naa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei wuji tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are struggling from lack of water before they start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miipiŋ dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi?

english: When crops run low on water, their leaves will curl up, droop, or turn a dull grayish-green during the hottest part of the afternoon to prevent moisture from escaping into the air.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ nu fioo lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbeeɔ shi, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings need water every day while older trees don't?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei momo lɛ ahe ehiaaa nu lɛ?

english: Seedlings have tiny, short roots that can only reach the top layer of soil, which loses water quickly. Older trees have long roots that spread deep into the earth where moisture is constantly available.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii, kukuji. ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋwɛi fã ni nu fiteɔ oya lɛ pɛ he Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Will my crops spoil if I plant them in low areas where water collects during rainy season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite kɛji midu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Most crops like cassava and maize will rot if their roots sit in standing water for too long because roots need air to breathe. Only special crops like rice or coconuts can tolerate having wet roots continuously.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ babaoo baafite kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Tsei pɔtɛɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa pɛ baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shishifãi ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is water so important for my crops right when they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Flowering is the hardest work a plant does. It needs maximum water during this stage to form healthy seeds and fruits; without enough water, the plant will drop its flowers to save itself.
ga: Fɔfɔii afeemɔ ji nitsumɔ ni wa fe fɛɛ ni tso tsuɔ. Be nɛɛ biɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛfee dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ nu bɛ Tso lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛkwɛ ehe.

english: I noticed tiny white eggs stuck under my maize leaves, what are they and will they destroy my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ. ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmãa baai ashishi Mɛni ji amɛ? Ni ani ebaakpãtã midumɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Those are usually insect eggs, such as from the Fall Armyworm. When they hatch, the caterpillars eat the maize leaves and young ears rapidly, so you need to check your field regularly and treat them early before they destroy your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi awui, tamɔ nɔ ni jɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ toi bibii oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mra. Dani amɛbaakpãtã onibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Is it safe for me to spray my crops with pest chemicals when they are close to harvest time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, every chemical pesticide has a required waiting period before harvest called a Pre-Harvest Interval. Harvesting too soon leaves dangerous chemical residues on the crops that can make people sick when consumed.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni amɛkɛmɛɔ dani akpaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ pre-harvest period. Nikpamɔ oya tsɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi aná hela kɛji amɛye.

english: Why does my harvested dry maize get full of small holes and powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: That damage is caused by small insects called grain weevils that lay eggs inside the corn. To stop them, make sure your maize is completely dry before storing it in airtight bags or properly treated storage bins.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ seed weevil ni woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa mli. Koni okpa ŋmãa lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too full of water for the roots to feed properly. Adding fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This acts as a natural food source that helps your maize grow stronger without exhausting the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni edaraa waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: How does adding dried chicken droppings or cow manure help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil by slowly feeding the crops with essential nutrients, while also helping sandy soil hold onto rainwater longer during dry days.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ekɛhaa tsei lɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are drooping because of heat or because of a plant sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso baai miiho yɛ latsaa loo tso hela hewɔ?

english: If crops lack water, their leaves wilting during the hot afternoon sun will bounce back fresh in the cool evening. If it is a sickness, the leaves will remain spotty, yellow, or withered even after it cools down or rains.
ga: Kɛji nu efo tso ko mli lɛ, baai ni gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baakã he ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni edɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops die when heavy rain water stands on my farm field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to stay alive. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to rot so the plant can no longer take up food and water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leading to thin stalks and tiny yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy fruits or ears.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai loo toii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and crowd out my crops even during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that extract food and water from the soil much faster than farm crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the water and nutrients they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ wa waa ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up when I irrigate them with salty water from a borehole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ mikɛ ŋmei nu ni jɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Salty water pulls moisture out of plant roots instead of feeding them. High salt content in irrigation water prevents crops from absorbing water properly, causing them to dry up and die even when the soil looks wet.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ po.

english: Can putting regular table salt on my pepper farm help control weeds without harming my soil?
ga: Ani okpɔlɔ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi ni eyeee mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Adding regular salt to your soil destroys crop land. Salt builds up in the root zone, damages the soil structure, and prevents future crops from taking up water and essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei folo ko wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nuŋ buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifã lɛ he. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea to soak my crop seeds in water before planting them in the ground?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ aduawai dumɔwui awo nu mli dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: Soaking seeds in clean water for a few hours softens their outer shell, helping them absorb moisture to germinate faster. However, soaking them in salt water or for too long can destroy the seed inside.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu ni mli tse mli ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛheɔ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Shi, kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni mli edɔ mli loo akɛwo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes burst open on the vine right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive a sudden flood of water, the roots pump excessive moisture into the fruit faster than the skin can stretch. This internal water pressure causes the skin to crack open.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ ná nu trukaa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa hewolo lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Why are my garden eggs soft and bloated with water instead of being firm and solid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfuɔ kɛ nu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Vegetables become soft and watery when they take up too much water without enough balanced soil nutrients like calcium. Calcium builds strong cell walls that give crops a firm, solid structure.
ga: Aduawai feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ nu babaoo wo amɛmli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ calcium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Calcium feɔ wala yibii gbogboi ni mli wa ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How do crop roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Crop roots act like tiny sponges that naturally draw up water and dissolved minerals from the soil. If the soil has too much salt or unwanted chemicals, it blocks the roots from drinking normally.
ga: Tse shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji bibii. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji sũ lɛ mli ŋmei loo tsofai ni ataooo babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot so quickly after I soak them in water to make them heavier for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛwo nu mli koni efee nɔ ni tsii kɛha jara lɛ?

english: Cassava readily absorbs excess water, which temporarily increases its weight, but trapped moisture creates a breeding ground for bacteria and mold, causing the tubers to spoil rapidly.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ baaha mɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ ji he ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do market women sprinkle water continuously on green vegetables like cabbage and gboma?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei shwieɔ nu amɛshwieɔ aduawai eŋɔli tamɔ kaaba kɛ burdock nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Harvested leafy greens lose moisture through their leaves and shrink. Sprinkling clean water allows the leaves to absorb moisture through their surface, keeping them plump, fresh, and attractive to buyers.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efeɔ ehee ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ nyaa he.

english: Why do my watermelons taste bland and watery when I give the farm lots of water right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni eyɛ nu beni mihaa ŋmɔ lɛ nu babaoo dani mikpaa lɛ?

english: Excessive watering right before harvest forces the fruit to absorb too much water. This extra liquid dilutes the natural sugars and healthy nutrients, making the melon taste watery instead of sweet.
ga: Nu ni oooha aduawai lɛ fe nine dani akpa lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Nɛkɛ nu krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa melon lɛ feɔ nu moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does soaking harvested grains in water before sale affect the health of people who buy them?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛwo nu mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ saa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he?

english: Soaking harvested grain creates trapped moisture inside the seeds, leading to the growth of dangerous fungal toxins like aflatoxins. These invisible toxins are harmful to human health when eaten.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛfeɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ aflatoxin. Nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji ni anaaa nɛɛ yeɔ adesa hewalɛnamɔ awui kɛ́ aye.

english: How does light drizzling rain affect my corn compared to a heavy downpour?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ saa mi-ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Light drizzling rain soaks gently into the soil without washing away topsoil or fertilizers, giving plant roots a steady supply of moisture to help crops grow smoothly.
ga: Drizzles lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli blɛoo ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efɔɔɔ. Ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is gentle, continuous rain better for my crops than waiting for big storms?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni yaa nɔ Ani ehi fe ahum wulu ko ni ooomɛ?

english: Yes, gentle rain allows the ground to absorb almost all the water slowly, whereas heavy storms often cause surface runoff where water sweeps across the field without sinking in.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ babaoo fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ahum ni naa wa waa kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. he ni nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni efooo lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants look so healthy during weather with frequent light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Frequent light rain keeps the air humid and the soil consistently moist, which reduces heat stress on the plant and allows leaves to stay green and food-productive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii.

english: Can rainy or drizzling weather cause fungal diseases on my maize crops?
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be Ani ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba mi ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, prolonged dampness and drizzle keep crop leaves wet for long periods, which creates ideal conditions for fungal spores to hatch and cause leaf spots or rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ baaha tsei ahe baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni fungal spores lɛ afã ni ekɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: How do I know when my corn is fully ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is ripe when the outer husks dry out and turn brown, the silk threads at the top turn dark brown, and the kernels inside feel firm when pressed.
ga: Ahooɔ ŋmãa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ anyɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why does my maize seem to ripen faster when the weather is warm with slight rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-abele lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the plant's natural maturation process, while light rain provides just enough water to fill the grains without causing waterlogging.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ yaa oya. Be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ lɛ Ebaaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ nu baaa.

english: Is it safe to leave ripe corn on the stalk in the field when it drizzles constantly?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: It can be risky because damp weather can cause moisture to get trapped inside the cob husk, leading to grain mold or causing seeds to sprout early.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɛ̃i ahi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Eha tsɛŋemɔ hela aba loo eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: My elders say a light drizzle is a good weather sign, but how can I be sure my crops are getting enough water?
ga: Mi onukpa lɛ kɛɛ nugbɔ miinɛ. Fioo ko ji kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa he okadi. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: You can check by digging a few inches into the soil around your crops; if the dirt easily forms a ball in your hand, your crops have enough moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ he ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ inchii fioo komɛi. Kɛji muji tsɔ bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli Oŋmɔshi nibii hu yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I help my soil retain moisture during dry weeks when there is only light rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ amli?
