english: Covering the soil around your plants with organic mulch, like dried grass or crop leaves, traps moisture from light rains and stops the hot sun from drying out the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai baawo mli. Ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi

english: Why does my corn crop fail to produce grains if heavy rain falls during the flowering period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ wooo yibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away or clump the pollen from the tassels before it reaches the silk, preventing proper fertilization needed to form complete cobs.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ loo emɔmɔ pollen ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ dani eshɛ siliki lɛ he. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ nii ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋtayaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tips, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is a vital food crop plants need to build strong leaves and stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs missing seeds at the very top tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ?

english: Missing seeds at the tip happen when the corn plant lacks enough water or food during the flowering stage, or when hot winds dry out the silks before every seed can form.
ga: Kernels ni elaaje yɛ naagbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa siliki lɛ gĩɔ dani dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu baanyɛ afee lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet, which shocks the plant and stops it from holding onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ekpaa fɔfɔi.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing thick green leaves but almost no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse shi pepper ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft, dark spots at the bottom while still on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the crop cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty leaves, but giving me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its strength into growing tall stems and foliage instead of tubers when the soil has too much leaf-building fertilizer or when the plants are shaded by trees.
ga: Yucca wajeɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bulbs najiaŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai baa lɛ fa babaoo loo beni tsei ewo tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yams start rotting inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot under the ground when rainwater settles around the roots without draining away, creating soggy conditions where soil fungi easily destroy the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. shishifãi ni nu hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, which is the cocoa tree's natural way of dropping extra young pods it cannot feed due to lack of water, nutrients, or light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji cherel ŋmei. Enɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ tsɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ nu, niyenii, loo la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during wind, even before the bunch is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Dani ŋmɔ lɛ po baakwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests in the soil attack their roots, weakening the plant's hold on the earth so it cannot support the weight of the heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bote mli. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa eshishifãi lɛ Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔ ni tsii ko nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get hot and start molding when I heap it in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn is still living and sweating out moisture; if piled together while still wet, trapped heat and water cause mold to grow rapidly.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ekɛ latsaa miiho. Kɛji akɛ ato he kome be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to follow a fixed planting schedule instead of just planting my seeds right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ ko atsu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: The very first rain of the season can be a false start followed by long dry spells. Following a recommended schedule ensures your seeds are planted when the rains are reliable, giving young roots continuous moisture so they do not dry up and die.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ onyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha adu odumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ba. Ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ.

english: How do I know the best time of the season to plant my maize so it receives enough rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa koni nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Maize needs moisture most when it is flowering and forming cobs. Planting according to an extension calendar aligns these critical growth stages with the heaviest rainy weeks of the season.
ga: Abele he miihia ŋmɔtɔ fe fɛɛ kɛ́ eyɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ kalanda ni alɛɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ haa nɛkɛ dalɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛ be lɛ mli otsii ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after my crop sprouts before applying fertilizer instead of putting it down on planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli moŋ fe ni mafee yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Newly planted seeds do not have strong root systems yet to drink up nutrients. Waiting until young plants develop roots ensures they actually absorb the fertilizer instead of the rain washing it away.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ lolo. Mɛɛ ni tsei bibii lɛ aná shishifãi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha nugbɔ lɛ ahoo amɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply fertilizer when the weather is very hot and the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve safely into the soil. Applying it during hot, dry weather can concentrate salts around the roots and burn your crop leaves, doing more harm than good.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmei abɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ. ni kɛ awuiyeli babaoo baa fe kpakpa

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants still turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ ewo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plants are receiving the wrong type of nutrients, or that heavy rains flooded the soil and washed the fertilizer away before the roots could reach it.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná niyenii ni esaaa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: How do modern crop protection sprays work to protect my farm from insect damage?
ga: Te ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii eha tɛŋŋ koni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe?

english: Modern crop medicines act like a protective layer; some stay on the leaves to stop insects from chewing them, while others are absorbed by the plant so pests die when they try to feed on it.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Henɔi komɛi hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni kooloi akaye amɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei shwieɔ ekomɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye lɛ.

english: Why am I advised to spray crop medicines early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes liquid sprays to evaporate into the air before the plant can absorb them, and strong midday winds can blow the medicine away from your target crop.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ni shwane mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa tsofa kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛmamɔ ohiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed has only a small amount of stored energy to sprout and reach the surface. Burying seeds too deep wastes that energy before the leaf shoot can reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ni ato koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni afuɔ lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without forming any fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin Akɛ nu woɔ tsei amli koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool umbrella that keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water. As long as the main stems stay healthy, the tubers under the ground remain alive and will produce new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava baagbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli wa lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛbaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plant will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baabɔle Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ eŋɔli su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil afterwards, the maize uses that natural plant food to produce bigger yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do we need to make high soil mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani wɔdu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and wide under the ground, so they need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Building high mounds also prevents rain from pooling around the roots and causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on dry ground just before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer across the surface of dry soil before the roots can absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied to soil that is already moist so it dissolves right into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni edɔ momo lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying natural solutions like neem oil water helps control these insects before they stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ nu kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Providing steady watering at the base and light shade during scorching days helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ kɛ hulutsoo gbii amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my stored maize get destroyed by tiny insects even when kept inside sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui amli po lɛ?

english: Weevils lay hidden eggs inside grain while it dries, or enter unsealed woven sacks. Storing thoroughly dried maize in airtight (PICS) bags cuts off oxygen and smothers insects before they can multiply.
ga: Kplukai lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛteeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. loo awo kotokui ni akpɛ́ ni atsĩ naa mli Abele ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kotokui ni akɛ tsɔne ni mli ewo muji mli (PICS) mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii dani amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes rot quickly if I store them immediately after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mifo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly dug tubers have tender skin and small cuts from harvesting. Leaving them in a warm, shaded area for a few days allows the skins to harden and heal, preventing decay fungi from entering during long storage.
ga: Bulbs ni atsa ehee lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ fioo kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji oshi yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ gbii fioo lɛ ebaaha hewolo lɛ mli awa ni etsa. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni ekabote mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides in the funnel of the plant. Early detection allows you to apply recommended treatments into the leaf funnels before the caterpillars destroy the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo baai lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is infected by cassava mosaic disease. Nutrient-poor soil prevents the plant from feeding itself, which ultimately leads to smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo tso lɛ emɔ cassava mosaic hela. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni naagbee lɛ ekɛ yitso bibioo baa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping soil moisture consistent and avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant hold onto flowers and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be fɛɛ be, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to naturally fertilize heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ eshwɛɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ awo ŋmãa mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How can I tell if the soil is moist enough to plant my seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting in soil that is too dry can cause seeds to rot or sprout and die. Squeeze a handful of soil from root depth: if it forms a soft ball without crumbling or leaking excess water, the moisture is right for seed germination.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akpɔ̃ loo amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi. Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli: kɛji efee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efooo loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning dark brown and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering. Regular, even watering allows the roots to absorb and carry calcium from the soil into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa tomato ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds steal vital plant nutrients and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach them. Even with rain, dense weeds choke the crop root systems and block sunlight, causing your crops to starve.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Hɔmɔ ye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings in the nursery grow tall, thin, and fall over easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni egbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch and grow weak when they do not receive enough direct sunlight, often because the nursery shade canopy is too thick. Slowly reducing the shade gives seedlings light to build strong, thick stems before transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ni aaaha hulutsoo lɛ aba shi fiofio Ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná la koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa ni mli wa dani adu amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get damaged easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa tree is young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Why should I not plant my maize seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are packed too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi feɔ bibioo, ni ŋmei lɛ hu feɔ bibioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which crops need to grow strong. Adding manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ waa yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the green leaves on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai eŋɔli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: If the soil is hard and packed tight, the roots cannot expand underground. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges before planting gives the cassava tubers room to swell.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii dani adu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they experience stress from heat or sudden dryness in the soil. Regular watering and placing mulch around the base helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to develop dark rotten spots at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomatoi lɛ amli ewo ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant absorb the calcium it needs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small green worms eating big holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those worms are moth larvae that feed on leafy crops. Removing them by hand early or using safe insect sprays protects the cabbage leaves from being destroyed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai. Nine ni akɛjieɔ mra Aloo okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu kaabeji baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho oya dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when the soil gets too hot and dry or when beetles attack the roots underground. Covering the soil with grass mulch protects the roots and keeps moisture in.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. aloo beni ŋmeii tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the ground, but groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which refreshes the farmland for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my oil palm fruit bunch is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: An oil palm bunch is ready when its color turns deep orange-red and a few loose ripe fruits begin falling to the ground naturally.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Ni aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ekomɛi bɔi shikpɔŋ shwiemɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I know if an improved seed variety is better than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to give higher yields, resist local pests and diseases, and grow uniformly, whereas saved seeds often lose their vigor and produce smaller, unpredictable harvests over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive dry weather better than traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Certain improved crop varieties are developed with deeper root systems or leaf structures that conserve water, allowing the plant to stay green and healthy even when rainfall is low.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni haa nu hiɔ shi lɛ yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: How can I find out which crops are in high demand before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni ataoɔ waa lɛ dani mabɔi amɛdumɔ?

english: You can talk to local market women, traders, and agriculture extension officers, or visit nearby markets to see which produce buyers are constantly looking for and willing to pay good money for.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei, jarayelɔi kɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsulɔi awie. Aloo yaa jarayelihe ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni ona nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nibii lɛ taoɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwo he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low in Ghana right after the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi yɛ Ghana yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest and bring the same crop to market at the same time, the supply becomes greater than what buyers need, which forces the price down.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛbaaha lɛ baafee babaoo fe nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. ni haa jara lɛ baa shi lɛ

english: Is there a way for me to secure a fixed selling price for my crops before I plant them?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ jara lɛ ahi shi daa dani madu?

english: Yes, through contract farming or off-taker agreements, where a company or buyer agrees in advance to purchase your harvest at a guaranteed, stable price.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ kpaŋmɔ okwaayeli loo gbekɛ ni aŋɔɔ lɛ he kpaŋmɔi anɔ. He ni nitsumɔhe lɛ loo hɔlɔ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ akɛ ebaahe onibii lɛ yɛ jara ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ.

english: What happens to market prices if all the farmers in my community grow the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni baa jarayeli jara lɛ nɔ kɛji okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ du ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop causes a flood in the local market at harvest time, giving buyers the power to lower prices because they have too many options to choose from.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa nu afua baa maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaa jara shi ejaakɛ nibii babaoo yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhala mli.

english: What makes certain crops easier to farm for a single farmer working alone?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa okwaafonyo kome pɛ akɛ ebaatsu he nii?

english: Some crops require less frequent weeding, lower fertilizer demands, and fewer chemical sprays, making them less labor-intensive and easier for one person to manage successfully.
ga: Tsei komɛi biɔ ni ajie jwɛi shii abɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ baa shi ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu faaa Enɛ haaa etsu nii waa ni efee mlɛo kɛha gbɔmɛi. Gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ omanyeyeli nɔ

english: How do I pick a crop that gives good profits without being too difficult to care for?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he ni amɛkwɛmɔ waaa tsɔ?

english: Look for crops that naturally suit your local soil type and rainfall, have reliable seed sources, and have strong local market demand without needing expensive daily maintenance.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kpãa gbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dumɔwui jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ. ni eyɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi.

english: How does the quality of my crop affect the price a buyer will offer me?
ga: Te bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi ha lɛ saa jara ni mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baaha mi lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for crops that are uniform in size, free from pest damage or spots, and properly dried, because high-quality produce lasts longer and sells faster to consumers.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ. Ebɛ nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii amli. ni ogbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni abaahɔɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why does my harvested produce spoil so quickly, and how can I keep it fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miifite oya nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Harvested crops spoil fast when exposed to heat and direct sunlight; harvesting early in the morning and keeping produce in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas slows down spoilage.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protection, strong heat bakes the leaves, causing them to dry up, burn, and drop off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji hebuu ko bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi, amɛshã, ni amɛgbee shi.

english: What can I plant on my farm to protect my new cocoa trees from harsh sunlight?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu kookoo tsei heei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: You can plant plantains, bananas, or temporary shade trees alongside your cocoa. These companion plants grow tall quickly and act as natural umbrellas to block direct sun rays.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu plantains, banana, loo tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yɛ kookoo lɛ masɛi. Nɛkɛ nanemɛi tsei nɛɛ daraa oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Can young cocoa seedlings grow properly if I clear all the large trees off my farmland?
ga: Ani kookoo dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, completely clearing all trees exposes young cocoa to too much direct sun. Keeping some tall forest trees or shade crops is essential to create filtered light that cocoa needs to thrive.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo aba kookoo bibioo lɛ nɔ. Koo mli tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Aloo, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ he miihia koni akɛfee la ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to my farm soil if intense sunlight beats down on it for several months?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji hulu lɛ tso yɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo?

english: Excessive sunlight dries out soil moisture, hardens the ground, and kills beneficial soil organisms. This makes the land poor and difficult for roots to draw nutrients.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ ohiafo ni ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Is it good practice to clear my land right before the peak of the hot dry season?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ majie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ aba?

english: It is better to wait. Clearing land right before intense heat leaves bare soil fully exposed to the sun, causing severe drying and loss of rich organic topsoil.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli dani latsaa lɛ baa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ waa, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ hu laajeɔ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist and cool when there is no rain and the sun is hot?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: You can practice mulching by spreading dry grass, crop leaves, or plant stalks over the soil surface around your crops to shield the ground from direct heat and trap moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi, tsei ahe baai loo tsei ashishifãi ni ooogbɛ oshwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from excessive sun heat rather than a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe dɔlɛ babaoo kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli? Mohu ɔ, anɛ e ji tso he hiɔ lo?

english: Heat stress usually causes leaves to wilt, curl, or burn at the edges across many plants at once during the hottest hours, whereas disease often starts as spots or rot on individual plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ haa tsei babaoo ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛshãa amɛnaa. tsei shikome yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ.

english: If my cocoa trees get scorched by the sun, will they die completely or can they recover?
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ shã kookoo tso lɛ, ani ebaagbo loo ebaatsa?

english: If the damage is not severe, trees can recover and sprout new leaves once shade is provided and rains return, though severe sunburn can kill very young seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ waaa Tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai heei kɛji hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aná dumɔwui bibii hu anɔ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, crops conserve water by closing small pores in their leaves, which temporarily slows down their growth process until cooler conditions return.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛŋaa lɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛdalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does leaving my land unworked for a few months affect the survival of my crops during hot weather?
ga: Te nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mishiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni minyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If land is left unworked without proper cover or shade, harsh sun can bake the soil and weeds can choke young crops, making it much harder to restore productivity later.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni bɛ he ko ni sa loo hulutsoo be, Hulu la ni fa babaoo baanyɛ ashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni jwɛi baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa akɛ abaaku sɛɛ afee nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the bottom up before the crop even produces corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani tso lɛ po woɔ abele lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and tall. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the plant's life solves this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts between my main crop rows helps my other crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When the plant grows and breaks down, that extra nitrogen feeds neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsei daraa ni amɛfiteɔ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why does my garden crop produce plenty of thick green leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli waa shi amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Switching to a fertilizer richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set heavy fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by insects like mirids. Maintaining partial shade trees and controlling pests early allows flowers to mature into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Tso ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli wa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viral diseases. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap early keeps these insects away so leaves stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ mli tsofa loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does that small purple-flowered weed keep weakening my maize even after I weed my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? No haa mi-ŋma lɛ gbɔjɔɔ beni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ?

english: That weed is Striga (witchweed), a parasite whose roots attach directly to maize roots underground to steal water and food. Rotating your field with crops like cowpeas starves Striga seeds out of the soil over time.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji Striga (witchweed), ni ji shishifã mli hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ebaaha Striga dumɔwui lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them in flat, heavy soils without proper drainage. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie amɛhe. Amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my healthy-looking plantain trees suddenly fall over during mild winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ko tswa lɛ?

english: This happens when microscopic worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects destroy the root system underground. Treating fresh plantain suckers with clean hot water before planting protects the new roots so the tree stays firmly anchored.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kpata shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse ni mli edɔ tsu plantain tsei heei ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi heei ahe. koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom as they start to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebote shishi beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, which occurs when plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots transport calcium to developing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots even when I want to keep them to sell later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛto koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli po?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to heat, light, and humidity because the tuber senses it is time to grow in the ground. Storing tubers in a cool, well-shaded, and elevated yam barn slows down sprouting so they stay fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛwo hulutsoo, la, kɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo ŋmeii atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni awó nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it becoming harder for me to get a large piece of land near the city to farm vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi fe tsutsu lɛ akɛ mana shikpɔŋ agbo ko ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ ni madu aduawai yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As towns and cities expand, houses and roads take over farmland, pushing traditional open-field agriculture further into rural areas and leaving only small plots available near urban centers.
ga: Beni maji lɛ amli lɛɛɔ lɛ, tsũi kɛ gbɛjegbɛi baye okwaayeli shikpɔji anɔ. Tsi kusum okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa akrowai amli. Ni shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ eshwɛ. Ebɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ pɛ

english: Can I still make a good income from growing tomatoes if I only have a tiny piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika kpakpa lolo kɛtsɔ tomato dumɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ?

english: Yes, by using intensive growing methods like greenhouses, crops are supported to grow upwards, producing far more harvest per square meter than traditional open-field planting on small plots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops suffer when I plant them close together on my small plot to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ naa amanehulu kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: In open fields, crowding crops forces them to compete for sunlight, ground space, and soil nutrients; structural farming methods like greenhouses solve this by training crops to grow vertically using ropes or stakes.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai ahe akaŋ. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii, tamɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shi shiŋŋ kɛtsɔ kpãai loo tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables spoil so fast when I bring them from my distant rural farm to sell in town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ akrowa ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli kɛba koni mikɛbaahɔɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables lose water quickly after harvest, so long travel times from far rural areas cause wilting; growing vegetables closer to urban areas using small-space setups ensures produce reaches buyers fresh.
ga: Nu ni baa yɛ aduawai amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛfaa kɛjɛɔ akrowai ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli kɛyaa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ maŋtiasei lɛ yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ haa nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ shɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help me grow vegetables without a big farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni madu aduawai ni mibɛ ŋmɔ agbo?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made with special netting or plastic that protects plants, allowing you to control their environment and get high yields from a very small piece of land.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni akɛ ŋshɔŋ loo plastic krɛdɛɛ ko fee ni buɔ tsei ahe. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni onine shɛɔ shika babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ.

english: Why do vegetables grown inside covered structures seem to grow faster than those in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni aduawai ni adu yɛ he ko ni aha nɔ lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inside a covered structure, crops are shielded from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and harmful insects, creating a low-stress environment where the plant can focus all its energy on fast growth and fruit production.
ga: yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ni haomɔ bɛ mli baa Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ oyaiyeli ni amɛdaraa kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why should I consider building a structure for my crops instead of just planting directly in open soil as usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he akɛ matswa tsũ ko kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: As farmland near towns gets smaller, open-soil farming yields less; growing inside a structure protects your crops year-round from weather damage and produces much more food from the exact same small footprint.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ bafee bibioo lɛ, ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ wooo yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ okwɛ̃ yɛ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baafite lɛ ahe. ni amɛfee niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry out so quickly on my small land near the expanding town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ ko ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Town areas often lack natural tree cover and have hotter surrounding air, causing soil moisture to evaporate quickly; enclosed farming structures help hold in humidity and shade crops from extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ maŋtiasei amli lɛ bɛ, ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli edɔ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi ni aŋã lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli.

english: Will growing vegetables under a greenhouse cover protect my seeds from being washed away during heavy rain?
ga: Ani aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ ŋtayaa shishi lɛ baabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, the roof of a greenhouse blocks direct heavy rainfall, preventing topsoil erosion and protecting young seed roots while allowing you to give the plants the exact amount of water they need.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yiteŋ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ.

english: Why do pests attack my vegetable crops more easily when I farm on a small plot near urban areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua mi aduawai lɛ kɛ́ mitsu ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ maŋtiase ko lɛ?

english: Small urban plots often lack natural bush barriers that keep pests away, but growing crops inside a net-covered greenhouse creates a physical barrier that keeps destructive insects out.
ga: maŋtiase bibioo mli Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋtayaai ni akɛtsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa lɛ bɛ. Shi tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ehà nɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from direct sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does my main plantain tree stop producing big bunches if I let all the small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain titri lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main mother stem. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough energy to grow large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow from the tips down the center of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and strength, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava plants are mature enough to harvest so the tubers do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa? Koni yitso lɛ akafite?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, usually indicated when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off. Leaving mature tubers in waterlogged soil for too long causes root rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the wet ground, maximizing sunlight exposure while protecting leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking ŋmɛɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to fully set in before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one isolated rain is risky because a sudden dry spell right after will dry out the topsoil, killing tender germinating seeds before their roots reach deeper moisture.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ ji oshara. Ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni baaba yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants to eat the growing tip, requiring early treatment to protect crop yields.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps prevent flowers from dropping.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do tomato plants that lie on the damp ground rot faster than those tied to sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe nɔ ni akɛfi tsei aniji ahe lɛ?

english: Damp soil contains fungi and bacteria that easily infect tomato leaves and fruits. Staking keeps the plant dry, improves air circulation around the leaves, and lifts the fruit off the wet ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ tomato baai kɛ aduawai oya. Staking yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: If I harvest seeds from a very tall and healthy maize plant, will the new crops also grow tall and healthy?
ga: Kɛji mikpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa tso ni kɛlɛ ni mli wa mli lɛ Ani tso hee lɛ hu baakwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa?

english: Crops inherit major physical traits like height, strength, and yield potential from their parent plants. Selecting seeds from healthy parent plants gives your next crop the best foundation to grow strong.
ga: Tsei yeɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui ni he hiaa tamɔ amɛlɛɛmɔ kɛ amɛhewalɛ gboshinii. kɛ bɔ ni abaanyɛ aná yibii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli Dumɔwui ni ohalaa kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee shishitoo ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do the crops I grow from my saved seeds sometimes yield less than the original certified seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry genetic traits from their parent plants. Over generations, saved seeds can lose the special combined traits of the original parents, leading to lower yields compared to freshly bred certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ fɔmɔ nii ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ shishijee fɔlɔi lɛ asui yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui srɔtoi heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant seeds from a big, sweet pepper fruit, will the new pepper bushes produce the same big peppers?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ agbo ko mli Ani ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔ hee lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ agbo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fruit traits such as size, taste, and shape are passed down from the parent plant to its seeds. Planting seeds from high-quality fruits increases your chance of getting similar quality in the harvest.
ga: Akɛ aduawai ahe sui tamɔ amɛdalɛ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyaa edumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ akɛ obaaná ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my neighbour's maize stalks much taller than mine, even though we planted on the same day with the same rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ fe mi nɔ lɛ kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ moŋ?

english: Different seed varieties inherit different growth traits from their parent plants. Your neighbour is likely using a variety bred specifically for tall growth and strong vigor.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Ekolɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ kɛ srɔtoi miitsu nii. Titri lɛ kɛha shweremɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Where do the natural nutrients in my farm soil actually come from before I add any fertilizer?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli?

english: Soil nutrients naturally come from the parent rocks and organic matter beneath the ground. As these original rocks break down over long periods, they release minerals directly into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii lɛ jɛɔ tɛi ni ji fɔlɔi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni nɛkɛ shishijee tɛi nɛɛ gbee shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Amɛjieɔ shika tsuru kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is the soil on my farm dark black, while the soil in the neighbouring village is red clay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji ediŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ akrowa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ tsuru?

english: Soil color and texture depend on the parent rock material it developed from. Red clay comes from rocks rich in iron, while darker soil comes from parent matter high in organic materials.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ tɛ ni ji fɔlɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ tsuru jɛɔ tɛi ni dade babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shi shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do some lands naturally support crops better than others even without chemical inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hei komɛi yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe hei krokomɛi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai po wooo mli lɛ?

english: The natural richness of soil depends on the minerals present in the parent rock material beneath it. Some lands have parent soils naturally packed with essential crop nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋkukuji komɛi yɛ maŋ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If my farm has rich soil and good fertilizer, can I just plant any cheap or weak seed and still get a big harvest?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni jara waaa loo ni edako ni maná ŋmaa babaoo lolo?

english: Rich soil provides food for the plant, but it cannot fix poor genetics. If a seed comes from weak parent stock, it lacks the biological potential to produce a heavy yield, regardless of soil quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ haa tsei niyenii. Shi anyɛɛɛ asaa fɔmɔ su ni ehiii lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ jɛ fɔlɔ ko ni bɛ hewalɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ wala yibii babaoo. ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha

english: Does applying fertilizer to my cassava make it naturally resistant to diseases, or does that depend on the type I planted?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ haa helai nyɛŋ emɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa? Aloo edamɔ tso ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Disease resistance is a trait inherited from the parent plant variety, not created by fertilizer. Soil nutrients help a plant grow well, but the natural ability to resist disease comes from the seed variety itself.
ga: Helai ahewalɛ ji su ko ni anáa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Jeee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Shi adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ helai lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ amli.

english: What is more important for getting a huge harvest: buying high-quality seeds or having fertile soil?
ga: Mɛni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmaa babaoo: dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aheɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni anáa?

english: Both are equally vital. High-quality seeds carry the genetic blueprint for high yield inherited from good parent plants, while fertile soil provides the actual food needed for the crop to reach that full potential.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he miihia pɛpɛɛpɛ. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso kpakpa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa.

english: Why does my harvested maize lose weight after I dry it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain a lot of internal water weight. Sun drying evaporates this excess moisture, which reduces the total scale weight but preserves the grain, preventing mold and rot during storage.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu mli tsiimɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa slag muu lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi shi ehaa ŋmaa lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How does weighing a small sample of my grains help me know the quality of my whole harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui bibii ni mikɛsusuɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni male bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ hi ha?

english: Taking a standard sample, such as 100 grams, allows officers to count healthy grains versus damaged ones. This small measurement accurately reflects the overall quality and moisture level of your entire harvest.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ, tamɔ gram 100 ni ajieɔ lɛ haa onukpai lɛ kaneɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni efite lɛ. Nɛkɛ susumɔ bibioo nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni okpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli fɛ̃i yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaajie amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning excess tree branches improves air circulation and helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Treating the plants early with organic neem oil or recommended sprays helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves available nitrogen to its newest top leaves to keep growing, showing that it needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mli.

english: What makes my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa?

english: Tomato plants drop blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Under severe environmental stress, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for basic survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ ni naa wa shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during heavy rains even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that microscopic pests called nematodes can damage. Weakened roots combined with top-heavy bunches make the plant collapse easily; supporting stems with bamboo props prevents this loss.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛ panicles ni tsii fataa he lɛ haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too close creates intense competition among crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground moisture. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures roots and leaves get enough resources to produce large, heavy yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa tsei ni hulu la he hiaa amɛ lɛ ateŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot occurs when fungal spores enter small cuts created during harvest, worsened by high heat and poor ventilation. Handling tubers gently to avoid wounds and storing them in a cool, airy barn prevents early decay.
ga: Sweet potato fitemɔ baa kɛji ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ bote ŋmeii bibii amli. ni baa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii blɛoo koni akapila amɛ, ni okɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite mra.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to yield the best weight?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmei lɛ muji ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the bottom leaves yellow and drop off, around 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting at this stage ensures the roots have accumulated maximum starch content and weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ shweremɔ he kɛji baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmei kɛ muji ni akɛtoɔ lɛ babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect its underground tubers. It enters a resting state and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ebabote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli ni ebaakwɛ tsei heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when the soil dries out, as the plant prioritizes its own survival over producing fruit under severe stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ nɔ fe yibii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During peak heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more moisture and recovers when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he, ni amɛbaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop needs more nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ he miihia niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy maize leaves are deep green. If the lower leaves turn pale green or yellow in a V-shape starting from the leaf tip, the crop is lacking nitrogen and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Abele baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, kɛjɛ baa lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my field for days instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Heavy clay soil or hard, compacted ground prevents water from draining properly. Standing water cuts off air supply to the crop's roots, which can rot the roots and stunt plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni etsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves mostly during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the cool center of the maize plant during the hot day to stay moist, coming out to feed on leaves at night when temperatures drop.
ga: Fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni mli ejɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees look burned and curled at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by mirid insects (capsids) that suck sap from young stems and leaves, releasing toxins that leave scorched brown marks on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirid kooloi bibii (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ejieɔ tsofai fɔji ni shĩɔ shãa he okadii ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Yam vines need stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make enough food energy to swell the tuber underneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do plantains planted too close together produce smaller bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When planted too close, plantains compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving less energy for individual plants to develop large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli wa Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from under the earth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves begin to yellow and drop, and the inside of the pods turns dark brown with visible seed vein patterns when you crack them open.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni dumɔwui ahe mfoniri ko ni anaa kɛji ogbele mli.

english: What is the main difference between hybrid seeds and the traditional seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ shishijee dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are produced by cross-breeding two carefully selected plant parents to combine their best traits. This produces a stronger crop that yields significantly more food, resists diseases better, and grows more uniformly than seeds saved from past harvests.
ga: Akɛ tso fɔlɔi enyɔ ni ahala amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ foɔ mli koni akɛ amɛsui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome kɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni woɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ baa. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni edaa be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni akpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to plant seeds harvested from hybrid crops. The second generation loses its special vigor and uniformity, which leads to much lower yields and weaker plants compared to buying fresh hybrid seeds each season.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni fa kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ahemɔ daa afi.

english: Why do hybrid crop varieties usually cost more than regular seeds sold in the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds require years of scientific research, careful hand-pollination, and strict quality control to produce. Although they cost more upfront, their higher yields typically generate far more income at harvest than the extra cost of the seed.
