ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ afii babaoo. Nine ni akɛwoɔ pollination mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ quality nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa yɛ nifeemɔ mli Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛheɔ shika babaoo kɛtsɔɔ hiɛ moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa anáa shika babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli fe dumɔwui ahe nyɔmɔwoo kroko.

english: How does the government's Planting for Food initiative help me afford high-quality seeds for my farm?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ Planting for Food nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mahe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Through programs like Planting for Food and Jobs, the government absorbs a significant portion of the cost of improved seeds and fertilizers. This subsidy allows input dealers to sell certified hybrid seeds to farmers at up to half the normal market price.
ga: Kɛ nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi. Nɔyeli lɛ woɔ shika ni akɛtsuɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ fã ko ni he hiaa waa. Yelikɛbuamɔ nɛɛ haa mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni awo he odase lɛ amɛhaa okwaafoi yɛ jara ni shɛɔ jara ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ fã nɔ.

english: Why do hybrid seeds sprout almost all at the same time, unlike my traditional seeds that come up unevenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ani enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ midumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he?

english: Hybrid seeds have uniform genetic strength and undergo strict quality processing. Because every seed has the same vigor, they all absorb moisture and germinate at the exact same pace, giving you an even crop stand across your field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa ni amɛtsɔɔ nitsumɔ ni mli wa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui fɛɛ ahe wa tamɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui fɛɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli. Enɛ haa onáa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Do hybrid crop varieties require more fertilizer and water to grow well compared to local seeds?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe?

english: Because hybrid crops grow faster and produce larger yields, they need adequate nutrients and water to reach their full potential. Applying the right amount of fertilizer ensures the crop can support its heavier cobs or fruits.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ŋmeii loo aduawai ni tsii fe no lɛ.

english: Why do hybrid crops usually mature faster than local crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Hybrids are bred to convert sunlight, water, and soil nutrients into growth much more efficiently. This allows them to finish their growing cycle earlier, helping you harvest before late-season droughts or pests set in.
ga: Afɔ hybrids koni amɛtsake hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbeɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa naagbee lɛ baa.

english: How do drought-tolerant hybrid seeds help my farm survive when the rains stop early in Ghana?
ga: Bɔ ni dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ kpa mra yɛ Ghana

english: Drought-tolerant hybrids are bred with deeper root systems and leaves that reduce water loss. This enables the crop to pull moisture from deep in the soil and remain healthy during unexpected dry spells.
ga: Afɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant hybrid seeds with strict spacing instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu hybrid dumɔwui ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Hybrid crops grow vigorously and need sufficient sunlight, air, and soil room. Proper line planting prevents plants from crowding each other out and makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Hybrid tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbiɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni sa koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi, ni ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do some hybrid crop varieties stay green while surrounding traditional farms are damaged by pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni amɛbɔleɔ blema ŋmɔji ahe lɛ? ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite

english: Many hybrid varieties are bred with natural resistance to common pests and diseases like armyworms or leaf rust. Their strong natural defenses allow them to withstand attacks that would normally ruin traditional crops.
ga: Afɔ tsofai sɔrɔtoi babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai amli ŋmeii. Amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni mli wa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tutuamɔi ni baafite blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize crops failing even though I planted them during the same month I always do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns in Ghana have shifted over recent years due to climate changes. Planting strictly by traditional calendar months no longer guarantees rain, so it is better to wait for steady soil moisture or check updated seasonal forecasts before planting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ etsake yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kusum kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ haaa nugbɔ anɛ dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ loo okwɛ be mli nibii ni awieɔ he lɛ ahe saji heei dani odu.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and survive drought better than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have deep, natural root systems adapted to local conditions that allow them to search for deep soil water, whereas cultivated crop plants need steady moisture and nutrients to establish themselves.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛtaoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛma shi.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and stay small even when I clear and weed the field properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil is out of essential nutrients like nitrogen. Farming the same land continuously without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer exhausts the soil, making plants weak.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ otsu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why does burning the bush on my land before planting make my soil poorer after a couple of years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, the intense heat kills beneficial soil organisms, burns off natural organic matter, and leaves the soil exposed to severe heat, causing it to lose fertility over time.
ga: Beni shãa lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ waa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big leaves, but yielding small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing tall stalks and leaves instead of expanding their root tubers. Balanced nutrients and proper plant spacing help form larger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli. Niyenii ni ja kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulbs lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks cause stress to pepper plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: What is causing small holes in my young corn leaves and making the tops look chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing center of maize plants. Identifying them early and applying natural or recommended controls protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii loo nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani fitemɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn dark and rot at the bottom before they can even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ miifee diŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛba po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium and keeps the fruits healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce much smaller yields than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yielding seeds are hybrids designed to perform best only in their first planting season. Saving and replanting seeds from hybrid harvests leads to weaker plants and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shweremɔ be lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to make healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ afee hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help feed the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can pull nitrogen food out of the air and trap it in their roots. When those roots break down in the ground, they leave behind natural plant food that helps the maize grow.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ amɛ awo amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ hu yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to support my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to manufacture food for the crop. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get sunlight and stays safe from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Esa akɛ hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ená niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni eha ehi shi shweshweeshwe koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses. Spraying the crop early with recommended control measures stops the insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu Ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted over a long time to grab water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and light away from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot and dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and moisture, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa ni egbi lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when rain flooded the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to drown and decay under fungal rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds very close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants with small harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to be moist before applying granular fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji granular fertilizer awo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to melt and travel into the soil so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it on hot, dry soil can burn plant roots or cause the fertilizer to evaporate into the air.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli ni efã gbɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or cassava around them to block direct sunlight and keep the surrounding soil moist while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni ebɔle amɛhe. koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock. Moving seedlings damages their delicate roots, and putting them into hot soil under direct sun dries them out faster than their weak roots can take in water. It is best to transplant late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day and water them immediately.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baafite amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the farm stays full of water after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Ani nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the farm for too long without draining, it smothers the roots, causing them to drown, decay, and turn watery and soft.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli, amɛgboi, amɛtsɔ nu ni amɛfee blɛoo.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers as the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow and staying short instead of growing tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee kuku lolo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from forming fruit, so the plant simply sheds the unfertilized flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ yibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni sũ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the young maize leaves where new growth forms, chewing through the tender leaves before they unfold and leaving behind saw-dust-like waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli yɛ he ni ŋmãa hee miida lɛ. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo ni amɛshi jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny pests in the soil called nematodes or stalk borers often attack and weaken the root base. Without strong roots anchoring it into the ground, the tree cannot support the extra weight of the fruit bunch without wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi bibii Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ tutuaa shishitoo nibii ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni fata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing your plants properly ensures every stalk gets enough food and light to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ shishifã naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp but not during or right before a heavy downpour. Burying or covering the fertilizer with a thin layer of soil near the plant base keeps rain from washing it across the field.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo dani ebaa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ fu loo aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akafɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Just like young children need regular water, shade, and rest to grow, young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves. Without shade trees and sufficient soil moisture, the direct sun scorches them before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii bibii ji lɛ, nu, hulutsoo, kɛ hejɔɔmɔ he miihia amɛ daa. Cacao tsei bibii hu yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã tso lɛ dani enyɛ ewo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Is rainwater enough for my cocoa trees, or do I really need to add fertilizer?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu lɛ fa kɛha mi cacao tsei lɛ loo ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mawo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rainwater only provides the crop with water to drink, but fertilizer provides the essential food and nutrients it needs to grow strong. Just as a growing child needs both food and drink to stay healthy, crops need soil nutrients alongside water to produce good yields.
ga: Nugbɔ nu pɛ haa tsei lɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa lɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni miida lɛ he hiaa niyenii kɛ nii fɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu he miihia ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛfata nu he koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops suddenly start flowering or producing seeds when the weather becomes very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui ashishi trukaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When a plant feels that severe drought or heat might kill it, it instinctively tries to produce seeds or fruit to leave behind a successor. This sudden flowering is a stress reaction to ensure its offspring survive even if the main tree dies.
ga: Kɛ tso ko nu hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ. Tsei baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni amɛbaashi yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Nɛkɛ fɔfɔi ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli koni ekwɛ koni ebii lɛ ahi shi kɛji tso titri lɛ gbo po.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is dying or under severe stress before it is too late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigboi loo amɛmiiye haomɔ ni naa wa shishi dani eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: A tree shows warning signs long before it dies, such as yellowing leaves, premature leaf shedding, or sudden out-of-season flowering. Recognizing these distress signs early allows you to provide water, shade, or fertilizer to save the tree.
ga: Tsei jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii akpo dani amɛgboiɔ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai ni laajeɔ mra, loo fɔfɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Haomɔ he okadii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ehaa okɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo ŋmɔshi nibii haa koni okɛkwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crops require natural periods of rest to conserve energy, much like humans do after heavy work. During cooler or drier periods, cocoa trees reduce pod production to store strength for the next major harvest season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Taakɛ adesai feɔ yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa sɛɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ loo hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baa pod ni amɛfeɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha kpamɔɔ be ni he hiaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Whenever I cut down an old cocoa tree, why do new shoots immediately sprout from the stump?
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni mafolɔ kookoo tsei momo lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When a tree is cut, its root system is still alive and senses that the main stem is gone. To survive, the roots push stored energy into dormant buds on the stump, rapidly growing new shoots to replace the lost tree.
ga: Beni afo tso lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni enu he akɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ etee. koni ehi shi Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ kɛyaa tsei ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli. ni ehaa tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛkɛye tsei ni elaaje lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce so many leaves instead of pods after I prune heavy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ beni mifo tsei niji ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy pruning shocks the tree into thinking it is damaged. It focuses all its food energy on growing new leaves and stems to rebuild its canopy for survival rather than spending energy on growing pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afolɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ he ajɔ lɛ ni esusu akɛ efite. Ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ pods

english: How do I stop unwanted water shoots from growing back after I trim my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu mli ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ? Beni afo kokoo tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: When you prune a branch, the tree naturally tries to regrow shoots at that spot. You must prune these vertical shoots (chupons) while they are still soft and young so the tree directs its energy into flower and pod formation instead.
ga: Kɛji ofo tso nine lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda ekoŋŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ (chupons) lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdara lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ afee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii moŋ.

english: If a tree is stressed by drought, lack of food, or lack of shade, it drops its flowers to protect itself. It avoids spending energy on heavy pods so it can use its limited resources to stay alive.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni bɛ, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei anaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Etsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsu nii yɛ pods ni tsii lɛ ahe lɛ he bɔni afee ni ekɛ nibii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do weeds and wild shoots grow back so much faster right after I clear my farm floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing opens up the ground to direct sunlight and rainfall. Seeds and hidden root systems lying in the soil sense this light and warm temperature, triggering rapid growth as a natural survival response.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ la kɛ latsaa he. Ehaa mɔ daa oya ni ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in harsh sunlight. Plantains or shade trees planted next to them act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and humid so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops before applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weeds aggressively absorb water and nutrients from the soil. If you apply fertilizer without clearing weeds first, the weeds will consume most of the food, leaving your main crop weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni ogbeee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii lɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth, or that excess water is suffocating the roots. Adding composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nu ni fa fe nine ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, preventing the fungus from taking over.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves instead of expanding its roots. Soft, well-drained soil encourages cassava to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy wooden prop pole prevents strong winds from uprooting the tree while the fruit matures.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayitsei feɔ tsiimɔ. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie tso lɛ shishi be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Flowers drop off due to extreme heat stress or tiny pests attacking the blossoms. Providing light shade, regular watering, or spraying organic neem water helps the plant hold onto its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahewɔ. Ha hulutsoo be ni mli tse. Nu daa Aloo organic neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stems and big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse kɛ tsei wuji ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground for longer periods, and gradually breaks down into rich food for the plants.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ, ejaraa mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha tsei.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my harvested maize grains after keeping them in the room for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛwo tsu lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: These holes are caused by grain weevils, insects that lay eggs inside the seeds. Properly drying the maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags stops insects from feeding on your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kplukai ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui amli Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye onibii lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated, which often happens due to high heat, lack of wind or insects to shake the pollen, or extreme wet or dry soil conditions.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni baatsirɛ pollen lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. loo shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ loo egbi waa

english: What helps my cocoa trees produce more pods from their small flowers?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi bibii amli?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects called midges for pollination. Keeping moist leaf litter around the base of cocoa trees gives these insects a good environment to live and pollinate flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Baai ni mli efɔ ni ahiɔ he fɛɛ he Kokoo tso lɛ shishi haa shihilɛ kpakpa ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my watermelon vines have many flowers but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon wain tsei yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants produce both male and female flowers. Bees must visit the male flowers first to pick up pollen and then visit female flowers to fertilize them so fruit can grow.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii aya fɔfɔi hii aŋɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛyabua pollen naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, yaasara fɔfɔi yei lɛ koni oyawo amɛ fɔ koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen, an essential plant food that helps crops stay green and grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa baai ni wa.

english: Will planting groundnuts together with my cassava take away food from the cassava?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baaje mli?

english: No, groundnuts actually capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed the cassava and improves soil health without harming cassava growth.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeee ŋmei lɛ dalɛ awui.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller cob yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni cob yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: How do I know if my farm size is too big for the labor I have?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ da tsɔ kɛha nitsulɔi ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: If you are unable to weed, apply fertilizer, or harvest on time across the whole area, your farm is too big for your available labor, which reduces overall crop yield.
ga: Kɛji onyɛɛɛ okɛ jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, loo okpa okpɔŋɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be naa lɛ, Oŋmɔ lɛ da tsɔ kɛha nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by intense heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop during dry weather as a natural defense to limit water loss through their broad leaves when the soil dries out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi.

english: Removing side shoots forces the plant to send its food and water straight to forming bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu koni amɛwo yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen. Rain can wash soil nutrients away, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn dark green and make energy to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baaha amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the temporary shade and moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and overly shaded farms. Clearing thick bush around the trees and pruning excess branches improves airflow and prevents the moisture fungal spores need to attack pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the crop, the soil gets waterlogged, suffocating the cassava tubers and allowing rot fungi to attack them. Planting on raised mounds or ridges prevents this.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua ehe naa ebɔle tsei ahe lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows targeted soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, drought, or irregular watering. Without uniform soil moisture, the plant panics and drops its flowers to preserve its own survival instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa lɛ he. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashe gbeyei ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans between my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have friendly bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil fertilizer, which feeds both the cowpeas and neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni woɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ tamɔ ŋmãa fɛɛ.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by pests like the Diamondback Moth caterpillar feeding on the crop. Inspecting under leaves early in the morning allows you to catch the caterpillars early before they destroy the whole harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Diamondback Moth ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii lɛ mra. dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl inward during the sunniest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to expose less surface area to direct sun, keeping water from evaporating too quickly during extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my stored yams start producing green shoots even when kept inside a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and have a natural biological clock. After a few months of rest, changes in air humidity signal to the tuber that it is time to grow a new plant using the starch stored inside itself.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Yɛ hejɔɔmɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ ŋmeii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu tsei heei.

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient the crop needs to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my yam plants produce plenty of leafy vines but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ?

english: When yam plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing lush green leaves above ground rather than feeding and swelling the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baama baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ niye ní nɛ e haa nɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ fuɔ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops leaves to save water and protect itself during severe dry spells. The roots underground stay alive, and new leaves will grow back as soon as the rains start again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains nearby to filter the sun, the heat scorches their leaves and slows down their growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba, ni baatsi hulu la naa lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How does sorghum survive dry weather much better than my maize crop?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deeper roots that pull water from deep underground, and it can temporarily pause its growth and roll up its leaves to conserve moisture until rain falls.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko ni amɛfolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up tightly like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on leaf juices, or by a virus carried from plant to plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees snap and fall over at the root when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ fãa yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny underground pests like nematodes or stem borers, leaving the heavy tree without a firm grip on the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when air temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii.

english: Why do I see tiny round bumps on the roots of my groundnut plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: Those bumps are root nodules containing beneficial bacteria that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer for the groundnut plant and the soil.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛhaa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why does lowland rice need standing water in the field while my other crops rot in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ he hiaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ eŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu he hiaa lɛ lɛ? Mi nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ nu mli?

english: Lowland rice has special internal air channels that allow roots to breathe underwater, while the standing water prevents weeds from growing and competing for nutrients.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ emli ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the ground is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves become healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. tso niyenii ni he hiaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes often shed their flowers when temperatures get extremely high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during scorching heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔmɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips, or viruses passed on by them. Spraying the plants with neem oil, mild soapy water, or approved insecticidal sprays stops these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips, loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ, nu ni mli ejɔ, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ. Ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ kpaa, ni ehaaa baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small holes in the central leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing whorl of maize. Applying recommended control products or neem leaf extracts directly into the leaf funnels early in the morning helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛyeɔ hela nɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ wo tso lɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays continuously flooded or lacks air movement, causing root diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. kɛ shishifãi hela baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, intense sunlight in their early stages. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture so the young cocoa can establish safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing seed maize after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant immediately after the very first isolated rain, as the soil underneath may still be too dry. Wait until you receive two or three good, heavy rains so the soil has enough deep moisture to support root growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai fioo komɛi ni naa wa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, reducing foliage diseases and significantly increasing your yield.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai helai baa shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily blow over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stem with strong bamboo forks or wooden stakes helps hold the plant upright until the fruit is mature.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ kɛyashi yibii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on top of the soil help my vegetables grow better in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—shades the ground from the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents weed seeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture, helping young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes increases sunlight exposure and prevents diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant naturally grows fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which prevents proper pollination and fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa pollination kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the leaves inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central growing leaf of maize plants to feed on tender tissue, which can ruin the crop if left untreated.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my big cocoa trees when they already look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso agbo lɛ he lɛ, be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ momo lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through, which dries out excess moisture and stops fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why should I leave space between my maize seeds instead of planting many together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu babaoo? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Placing seeds too close together forces the maize plants to compete for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, resulting in thin stems and small, poor yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even if I cleared the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ dani miduɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots, starving your plants even if the field was initially cleared.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on my field when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so crop roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch or burn the crop roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo ashã tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, leaving free fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen or water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea at the right time helps the plant build strong, green leaves to produce food for healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo nu. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my field next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize pulls a lot of nutrients out of the soil, while groundnuts naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating with groundnuts heals the soil and makes it rich for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii lɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni etsa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha efee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh growing tip of maize plants. Spraying recommended treatments like neem leaf extracts or approved insecticides early stops them from killing the plant before it matures.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ ehee lɛ najiaŋ. Akɛ tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔse mra. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbo dani eshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without proper drainage, it suffocates them and allows soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha mumɔ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sun, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo cob babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground, keeps the root area moist longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant feed calcium to the growing fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium aha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that swells the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and exposing them to full sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ aba enɔ kwraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by long dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or damage from pests like mirids. Protecting the trees with shade and proper feeding helps flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni sa bu tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa plants mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves, or the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: If I plant groundnuts together with my cassava, will the groundnuts steal food from the cassava?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei he Ani ŋmei baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmei mli?

english: Groundnuts actually enrich the soil rather than steal from it. They belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil, which naturally feeds neighboring crops like cassava.
ga: Peanuts haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ. yɛ juu najiaŋ Amɛfata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each seed adequate space ensures every plant gets enough food to grow large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli: Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso agbo ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps flowers turn into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does it matter which part of the cassava stem I cut to plant for my next harvest?
ga: Ani mifoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ fãi komɛi koni mikɛdu kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cuttings from the middle section of a mature cassava stem works best. Top cuttings dry out too fast, while bottom cuttings are too woody and take much longer to sprout.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ yucca tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to build big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my main crops when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from choking your crops of sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baa kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? Ekɛ ehe ewo gɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, which feed on the growing heart of the maize plant. Catching them early by inspecting your farm allows you to control them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni otsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the surface of my farm soil form a hard crust after rain, making it hard for seeds to break through?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli.

english: Heavy raindrops crush exposed soil particles into fine mud that hardens like concrete under the hot sun. Adding organic manure or spreading dry grass over the soil acts as a protective cover that keeps the soil soft.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie sũ mli nibii bibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ anɔ ni etsɔ muji bibii ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash this key nutrient away, leaving the plant unable to feed itself properly to maintain healthy green leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye ehe niyenii jogbaŋŋ koni ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and shade moisture, protecting the delicate cocoa plants during their early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshweremɔ shishijee mli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much standing water and lacks good drainage. The waterlogged conditions suffocate the roots and create a friendly environment for fungal diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli wa baa kɛha ŋmeii ahe helai ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather conditions get too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to preserve its own energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baatsi efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs instead of strong plants with full yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii. Mohu ɔ, e maa pee tso nɛ he wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii kɛ pi si.

english: Why should I wait for continuous rains before planting instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔmɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani wɔduɔ nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: The first rain of the season can be misleading; if a hot dry spell follows, sprouted seeds will dry up and die in the ground. Waiting for steady rains ensures there is enough lasting soil moisture for seedlings to establish.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔ lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the growing center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of young corn plants, eating tender leaves before they unfold, which weakens the plant's growth.
