ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni ayeɔ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a shield that reduces water evaporation from the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking root.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa nu ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akawo shishifãi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viral infections spread to the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli lɛ mli

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in the same field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, leaving behind free plant food that makes the soil richer for your next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi tsei niyenii yɛ kpo nɔ yaka. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my vegetable crops and drowning their roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli?

english: By building raised soil beds and creating shallow drainage channels around your field, excess rainwater will safely flow away without destroying the roots or washing away topsoil.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsũi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afee kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee shishifãi loo efɔɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the late afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can take up water before the intense sun hits, which reduces water evaporation and stops fungal diseases from spreading on wet evening leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku waa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the field has too much standing water, which prevents roots from feeding on soil nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ niyenii kpakpai aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and preventing the fruits from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crop seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop seedlings and will steal all the sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer before your crops have a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe dumɔwui bibii. Ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvesting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ tso ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the air becomes too hot and dry, when there is insufficient water in the soil, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce big lush leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes sweet potato plants to direct all their energy into producing green leaves above ground instead of growing large tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, du bulb nguahi ngɛ sisi.

english: How do I know if there is enough water in the soil for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: You can test soil moisture by squeezing a handful of soil from a few inches deep; if it forms a soft ball without crumbling or dripping wet, the soil has enough water to help your seeds germinate.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋwɛi shɔŋŋ ni ji inchi fioo ko lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efoŋ loo efeee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa zugba a ngɛ nyu bɔ nɛ sa nɛ e maa ye bua wu ɔmɛ nɛ a puɛ.

english: Should I continue planting my seeds if the rains suddenly become irregular?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ madu dumɔwui kɛji amɛgboi trukaa? Ani nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: It is best to pause planting when rains become irregular because newly planted seeds require continuous moisture to establish roots; without steady rain, the young seeds will dry up in the soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa dumɔ be kukuoo ko beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa lɛ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is rainfall considered the main factor that determines when I should plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni tsɔɔ be ni esa akɛ adu nii lɛ?

english: Rainfall provides the moisture needed to soften seed coats so they can sprout, and it dissolves soil nutrients so young plant roots can feed and grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa nu ni he hiaa koni ekɛha dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ afee blɛoo koni amɛkwɛ̃. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: How do I decide whether to pause planting or keep going during a short dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ makpa dumɔ loo maya nɔ madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli?

english: Check the moisture of your topsoil; if the top two inches are completely dry and no rain is expected within a few days, you should hold off on planting until steady rains return.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi inchi enyɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa ni akpaaa nugbɔ gbɛ gbii fioo komɛi. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are some of my planted tree seeds sprouting while others in the same field are not showing any growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, dalɛ ko bɛ kwraa?

english: Seeds sprout at different rates depending on how much soil moisture surrounds them, how deep they were planted, and whether individual seeds received enough water to trigger germination.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ Ni ani dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃?

english: Why do seeds fail to sprout even after I have properly cleared and tilled my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛtsu nii po lɛ?

english: Good land preparation creates a soft seedbed, but seeds strictly require water to activate their growth engines; without sufficient soil moisture, they remain dormant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa haa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ɔ he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Shi nu he miihia dumɔwui waa koni ekanya amɛdalɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahi shi ni amɛhiɛ ejɔ.

english: Why do my young tree crops suddenly sprout lots of new leaves right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔwu lɛ shwereɔ baai heei babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rainwater triggers a sudden uptake of nutrients from the soil, giving the young trees the quick surge of energy they need to push out new growth and leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa. feemɔ tsei bibii Oya ni oná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ hee kɛ baai.

english: What will happen to my newly sprouted seedlings if a dry period starts right after they come up?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ? Kɛji akɛ fã ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni eje kpo lɛ,.

english: Young seedlings have very shallow root systems, so if the topsoil dries out quickly, they cannot reach deeper water and will wilt and dry up.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩ oya Amɛnyɛŋ amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he ni amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Can my young tree seedlings survive on limited water during their early stage of growth?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli?

english: Young seedlings need consistent moisture to build strong roots and stems; prolonged water shortages during early growth will stunt their development or kill them.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Nu ni faaa be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ baatsi amɛdalɛ naa loo ebaagbe amɛ.

english: Why do my crops look healthy during the rainy days but quickly start wilting when the sun shines for three straight days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbii amli, shi amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When crops lose water through their leaves faster than their young roots can take it up from drying soil, they lose their internal pressure and begin to wilt.
ga: Kɛ tsei shwie nu kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔi shwiemɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure exact distances between my trees when planting instead of just putting them anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu he ni mi tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji lɛ he beni miduɔ nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo he fɛɛ he lɛ

english: Giving your trees set room allows their roots to spread properly and prevents them from fighting for nutrients, water, and sunlight, which helps every single plant produce more yield.
ga: He ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers always advise me to plant my crop trees in straight lines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ adu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it much easier to walk through your farm, clear weeds, apply fertilizer evenly, and count your total crop yield without missing any trees.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli daa. Ni okane nibii fɛɛ ni ofee lɛ ni tsei komɛi akafo mli.

english: What will happen to my crop trees if I plant them too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When trees are overcrowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for soil food, causing them to stay thin, tall, and give very little harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni kɛlɛ, kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: If I plant fewer trees far apart, won't I get less harvest than planting many trees close together?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ fioo yɛ he kroko lɛ Yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ. Ani tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, because trees with enough space grow much larger, produce stronger branches, and yield far more fruit per tree than many overcrowded trees combined.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baadara babaoo. Niji lɛ daraa waa. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ tso kome nɔ fe tsei babaoo ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ akɛto he.

english: How can I easily measure equal distances between planting holes if I do not have a measuring tape on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni yɔɔ dumɔ bui lɛ ateŋ lɛ he mlɛo? Kɛji akɛ tɛp ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can cut a straight wooden stick or rope to your desired distance, like 10 feet, and use it to measure from one hole to the next across your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo tso loo kpãa tɛ̃ɛ. taakɛ bɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ, tamɔ ninetalɔi 10 lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ susumɔ kɛjɛ bu kome mli kɛya ekroko mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Will planting my trees in evenly spaced rows make controlling weeds on my farm easier?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ani enɛ baaha efee mlɛo akɛ abaakwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, standard spacing leaves clear paths between rows so you can walk freely with a cutlass or equipment to clear weeds without accidentally damaging your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ ni kã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne loo dɛŋdade anyiɛ oya ni okɛjie jwɛi ni okɛfiteee onibii yɛ oshara mli.

english: Can I plant crop trees on swampy or marshy areas of my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ?

english: Most tree roots will rot if they sit in water constantly, but you can plant them successfully if you choose water-tolerant crops or drain the excess water away.
ga: Tso shishifãi babaoo baagbo kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo nu mli be fɛɛ be. Shi obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ohala tsei ni nu nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi loo okɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie shi.

english: How can I tell if a spot on my farm is too waterlogged for regular crops to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he ko mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃?

english: If water collects on top of the soil for days after heavy rains, or if the soil stays soft and muddy all year round, it is too wet for crops that need dry ground.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee bɔdɔɔ kɛ muji afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi.

english: How should I prepare planting holes if my farm ground naturally holds too much water?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa dumɔwu lɛ bu lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he ko yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nu babaoo yɛ mli hu?

english: You should heap the topsoil into raised earth mounds or ridges and plant on top of them so the young plant roots stay above standing water while still getting moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ato gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ lolo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow and wilting even though the ground is wet and muddy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ muji lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely flooded, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the plant to choke and drown because its roots cannot take up air or nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu kwraa lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I start my seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them straight into my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery gives delicate crops a safe, controlled environment where you can easily water, shade, and protect them from pests until they grow strong enough to survive the harsher conditions of the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni akudɔɔ. He ni obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo mli, okɛ hulutsoo aha, ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ mlɛo. Kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli.

english: How can I test if the crop seeds I bought are good quality before I plant them on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can perform a quick germination test by placing 10 seeds wrapped in a wet paper or cloth for a few days; if 8 or more sprout, your seeds are high quality and ready for nursery or field planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛwo wolo loo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ loo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: How do I know when my seedlings in the nursery are ready to be moved to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 4 true leaves and developed a firm, strong stem, which typically takes 3 to 4 weeks depending on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and look weak right after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock, caused by root disturbance and sudden environmental changes. Moving seedlings during late afternoon or on cloudy days, and watering them immediately, helps prevent wilting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni gbaa mɔ naa kɛ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkagbo.

english: Why do my tender young crops wither and die when there is hot direct sunlight during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are too shallow to pull up enough moisture to replace what the leaves lose in intense heat, so providing light shade or planting alongside shade crops helps keep them alive.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto nɔ ni baai lɛ laajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha loo odu yɛ hulutsoo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How can a small quantity of seeds cover a very large plot of farmland?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui fioo ko aha okwaayeli shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ hu?

english: When seeds are nursed first and planted at precise, recommended distances rather than scattered randomly, every single seed counts, allowing a small quantity to cover many acres efficiently.
ga: Beni atsuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii dani aduɔ yɛ he ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛdu lɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ajaa trukaa Akaneɔ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui fioo komɛi ni haa acre babaoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Will I harvest more crops if I plant my seeds closer together on my plot?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight over light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests compared to crops grown with proper spacing.
ga: Dabi, tso ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How should I prepare my farm soil before transferring my seedlings out of the nursery?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Clear all weeds, loosen the soil deeply to encourage root growth, and mix in organic manure or compost so the young plant roots immediately find food when transplanted.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ewo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why is it critical to remove weeds around my young crops during their first month in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mana mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛtswa amɛhe amɛma shi lɛ oya.

english: Why do two farmers using the exact same quantity of seeds end up with totally different harvest amounts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi enyɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui abɔ kome tsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi kwraa lɛ?

english: Harvest size depends heavily on field practices like proper nursery handling, good field spacing, weed management, and soil watering, rather than just the initial seed quantity.
ga: Nikpamɔ dalɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii akwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ. ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kpakpai ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛhaa Jeee shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen fertilizer or that excess water in the soil is choking the roots and preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water during the rainy season cuts off oxygen supply to the cassava tubers in heavy soil, allowing rot fungi to attack and destroy the roots quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ yaa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant my yam setts too close to each other on the mounds?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ?

english: Planting yams too close forces the plants to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, which results in many small tubers instead of big, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Mɛi babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji ni he wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when stressed by hot, dry weather, nutrient shortages in the soil, or damage from insects like mirids that feed on delicate flower stems.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ iris ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good to keep some big trees on my farm to shade my cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tsei wuji ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛha kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect cocoa leaves from severe sun burn, keep the soil cool and moist, and protect the crop from drying out during the hot harmattan season.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ harmattan be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees keep falling over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, and pests like root nematodes or stem borers weaken them further, causing the heavy plant to tip over easily in wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers. Ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ fe tsutsu lɛ po. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven during dry weather.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that feed on leaf juices and spread stunt-causing plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwaa.

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the soil surface and carries it away from the plant roots before the crop has a chance to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally fertilizing the soil when the plant stems and leaves decay.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is hungry and lacks nitrogen. When you apply fertilizer, it gives the corn the nutrients it needs to turn green, grow tall, and build big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nitrogen bɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Abɛi baaná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli, ekwɛ̃, ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: Why does fertilizer make my crops give a bigger harvest than planting without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii haa miŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for the soil, providing essential minerals like nitrogen and phosphorus that crops need to build strong roots, tall stems, and full grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shika tsuru nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. akɛ ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ ama shishifãi ni wa, ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, kɛ ŋmaa ni eye emuu

english: Can fertilizer harm my maize seed if I put too much in the planting hole?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo dumɔ bu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, placing too much chemical fertilizer directly against a seed can burn the tender sprouting roots, which kills the plant before it comes out of the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo wo dumɔwu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ tso lɛ dani enyɛɔ edaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to grow out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the ground is too dry, if they are buried too deep away from sunlight, or if soil insects destroy the seed before it germinates.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ kɛjɛ hulu la mli Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do new hybrid maize seeds from agriculture offices give more harvest than seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hee ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni jɛ Bureau of Agriculture lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and produce larger, uniform ears, while saved seeds lose their strength over generations and yield less.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo toi wuji ni tamɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in neat rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows makes sure each crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil space, while also making weeding and applying fertilizer much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do some crops mature quickly while others take many months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yeɔ nyɔji babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different growth cycles; fast-growing grains like maize produce food in a few months, whereas perennial tree crops invest time building strong trunks first.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels inside become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmei lɛ akatsɔ ŋmei.

english: Why does my harvested maize grain go bad or turn moldy in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ fite loo ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage if it is not dried completely under the sun before storing, because remaining moisture allows mold, fungi, and insects to grow inside the granary.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni efite lɛ ato kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How much extra yield can I expect if I give my crop proper fertilizer and clean water?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ nu ni mli tse ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, yibiiwoo kroko ni fa enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ?

english: Proper feeding and moisture can double or even triple your normal harvest because the plants do not waste energy struggling for basic nutrients in depleted soil.
ga: Niyenii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ ni okpaa daa lɛ afee shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei efiteee hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by severe heat, lack of rain, or poor soil nutrients. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil moist during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ha fɔfɔi lɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that heavy rains washed nutrients away. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and fuels rapid growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laajeɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ oya.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem to plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always select healthy, hard stems from the middle section of a mature plant with clear, raised buds. Avoid the tender green tops and old bottom roots, as the middle section sprouts fastest and produces the strongest roots.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, halamɔ tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛjɛ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo, ni ewó nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ, ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ tsei kakadaji awo shikpɔŋ kɛha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which feeds the growing tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni baaha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa Ni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leafy funnel of the maize plant. Applying organic neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments early in the morning kills the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Leaf curl happens when tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies suck the plant's juice and pass on a virus. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water mixture or neem oil helps clear these insects and protects new growth.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, nu tsei amli nu ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ mɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my ripe tomatoes getting soft black spots at the bottom before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ shishigbɛ dani akpa?

english: This soft black bottom is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plant prevents this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishigbɛ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are soil builders that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil, so your future crops grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele ni adu sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients right out from under your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: How many times can I plant maize on my farm in a single year?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi mli?

english: Without irrigation, you can typically plant maize twice a year in southern and central Ghana—once during the major rainy season and once during the minor rainy season.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ. Shikome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli, kɛ shikome hu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo mli.

english: What is the difference between the major season and the minor season for growing crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli be ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: The major season brings the primary, longer period of rainfall which gives crops plenty of water for high yields. The minor season has shorter, less reliable rainfall, which requires faster-maturing crop varieties.
ga: Be titri lɛ kɛ nugbɔ baa shishijee mli ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya.

english: When is the best time to start clearing and tilling my land for the main planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ shishi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ?

english: Land preparation should begin a few weeks before the major rains are expected, so your soil is loose, weed-free, and ready to absorb seeds as soon as the rains settle.
ga: Esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ shishi otsii fioo komɛi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse. jwɛi bɛ mli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi pɛ

english: What happens to my maize yield if I depend only on rainfall instead of using irrigation?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Relying strictly on rainfall limits you to planting only during the rainy months, and an unexpected drought period can dry out your crops before they produce good cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaha odu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli pɛ. Ni hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi dani amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Can an irrigation system help me harvest maize three times in one year?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa ŋmãa shii 3 yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, if you have artificial irrigation, you do not need to wait for the rainy seasons, allowing you to plant and harvest crops year-round up to three times.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oyɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo. Ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ aba. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nibii ni okpaa shii etɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do to protect my crops if the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: Applying dry grass or leaves around the bases of your plants (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil longer so the crops can survive dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi bɔle tsei lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: How can I tell if my plot of land is suitable for growing corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good corn land should have dark, fertile soil that drains excess water well so that roots do not drown during heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why does water collect and stay on some parts of my farmland after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil with high clay content or poor drainage holds standing water, which can choke crop roots and prevent them from breathing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli babaoo loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha enyɛŋ emu.

english: Why does my maize crop grow bigger during the major rainy season than in the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The major season provides consistent water and sunlight needed for full stem and cob growth, whereas the minor season's unpredictable rain can stunt plant growth.
ga: Be titri lɛ haa nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants curling up during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl inward during dry weather as a natural defensive reaction to reduce surface area and minimize water loss through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack the necessary nutrients or energy to support them. Spraying crop boosters or special liquid fertilizers provides the tree with essential nutrients that help retain flowers and turn them into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa loo hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe loo tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite ni etsɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: This is often caused by a condition called cherelle wilt or a lack of plant food. Using nutritional sprays helps feed the young pods directly so they can grow into full, mature cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilting loo tso niyenii ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eda kwraa.

english: Is there a way to encourage my cocoa trees to produce more flowers during the farming season?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, applying flower-stimulating products or specialized sprays encourages the tree to produce more blossoms, which leads to a higher potential yield of cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo otso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ baaha bɔ ni abaanyɛ afee cocoa pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do small cocoa pods get enough strength to grow into large pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo tso bibioo ko náa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsɔ tso agbo?

english: Small pods rely on the nutrients the tree absorbs from the soil and through its leaves. Spraying targeted crop enhancers gives young pods the extra nutrition they need to develop fully without stunted growth.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ damɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ baaa shi.

english: What does spraying liquid products on my cocoa trees actually do for the crop?
ga: Te nu ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spraying delivers vitamins, minerals, and growth boosters directly to the leaves, flowers, and pods. This quick absorption helps the tree produce more flowers and protects small pods from failing.
ga: Spray lɛ kɛ vitamini, mineral kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ daa lɛ yaa baai, fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi oya nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe. Kaaha egbee shi.

english: Do I need to spray a large amount of chemical on my cocoa trees for it to work?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo afɔ cacao lɛ nɔ koni etsu nii?

english: No, many effective yield-boosting products only require a small, properly measured amount sprayed evenly over the tree to help it flower and produce pods.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ pɛ ni akɛshwie tso lɛ nɔ fioo ni asusu he jogbaŋŋ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: What kind of product should I buy if I want my cocoa trees to produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mahe kɛji miisumɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Look for biostimulants or flower-and-pod boosters, such as Kankani, which are specially formulated to help trees produce abundant blossoms and assist small pods in growing safely.
ga: Taomɔ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli loo nɔ ko ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, tamɔ Kankani, ni afee lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔii babaoo ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ afee bibioo. eda shweshweeshwe

english: Why are my cocoa trees looking green and healthy but still not giving me many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: A tree can have healthy leaves but still lack the specific nutrients needed for fruiting. Adding a yield-enhancing spray gives the tree the extra boost it needs to translate leafy growth into pods.
ga: Tso baanyɛ aná baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ shi loloolo lɛ, ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ yibiiwoo nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛtsake baai lɛ adalɛ ewo ŋmeii amli.

english: When is the best time to apply a flower and pod booster to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse fɔfɔii kɛ booster pods yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to apply these boosters is just before or during the main flowering period, so the tree has enough nutrients right when it starts forming flowers and young pods.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli nɛɛ baatsu nii ji dani fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ be titri lɛ loo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii fɔmɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield a lot of pods in one season but very few in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Trees can get exhausted after a heavy harvest season. Using special plant boosters helps replenish their strength so they can continue to flower and produce pods consistently every season.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afee shoo yɛ kpamɔ be ni mli wa sɛɛ. Tsoi ahe nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the insects still destroying my crops even after I sprayed them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects can survive chemical spraying if the chemical is mixed with too much water, applied at the wrong time of day, or if the pests have built resistance to that specific chemical from over-use.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ babaoo futu nu mli, akɛwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ eshi nakai tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛ nitsumɔ fe nine mli.

english: Is it bad if I spray my crops with weed killer right before it rains?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Yes, rain will wash the chemical off the weed leaves before it has time to soak in, wasting your money and leaving the weeds alive to compete with your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ jwɛi baai amli lɛ ahe dani amɛnáa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ amɛ. Eji oshika ni ofiteɔ ni ehaa jwɛi hiɔ shi koni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ akaŋ.

english: Will using a tractor to clear and turn my soil make my crops yield more than using a hoe?
ga: Ani traktɔ ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsake lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo fe tsɔne ni mikɛbaatsu nii?

english: A tractor loosens hard soil deep down so roots can spread easily and capture water, but over-using heavy machinery can dry out the soil and pack it down too hard over time.
ga: Trakta lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni wa lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Shi tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up faster in fields that were ploughed very deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni atsuɔ nii yɛ mli waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Deep ploughing exposes lower damp soil to the hot sun, causing moisture to evaporate quickly if rain does not fall soon after planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are logged with water and cannot breathe or collect food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛto niyenii

english: Crops drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium needed to hold the flower.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii anɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ calcium ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why do I get smaller yields if I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots get smaller every year if I keep planting on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same food out of the soil every season while allowing pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to build up in the dirt.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my fertilizer burn and kill my young crop shoots when I applied it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are rich in salts; if placed directly against young stems or roots without enough soil water, they suck moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Fertilizer ni ŋmei eyi mli obɔ Kɛ akɛwo tsei bibii loo shishifãi bibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground, but the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the stems bend down and push themselves deep into the soil. The groundnut pods then develop underground where it is moist and safe from pests.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollination sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Peanut pods lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my groundnut plants turning yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the plant has a fungal disease like leaf spot. Crop rotation and using healthy seeds help keep the leaves green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Pull up a few sample plants and open the pods. If the inside of the shell has dark brown or black veins instead of being white, and the leaves are turning brownish-yellow, your crop is mature.
ga: Gbalamɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ ni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light rain. Wait until the rain falls steadily for two to three days so the soil is moist enough to keep seeds alive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster when I clear the weeds around them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie amɛhe daa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing weeds lets your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowded plants fight each other for water and light, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce a full crop.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ nu kɛ la miitswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsu fɛɛ tsu mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ.

english: Why does my cassava rot in the soil if I leave it too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living organs. Once they reach full maturity, keeping them in wet soil causes bacteria and fungi to enter and decay the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli. Kɛ amɛdara kwraa Kɛ́ okɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii abote mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing on the leaves of my young crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Tiny holes are caused by small insect pests feeding on the leaves, which weakens the plant and reduces its ability to make food from sunlight.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why must I dry my harvested groundnuts and grains thoroughly in the sun before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-ŋmeii kɛ ŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Moisture in stored crops creates dark, damp conditions where mold and grain-eating insects grow quickly, destroying your harvest within weeks.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli lɛ haa duŋ, fɛ̃i shihilɛi baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ daa oya yɛ. Efiteɔ onibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow at the tips and down the midrib, it usually means the plant is suffering from nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the essential food plants use to stay green and grow, and heavy rains often wash it away beyond the reach of the plant roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ kɛtee shishigbɛ kɛtee ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara. Ni bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nitrogen yaa hiɛ fe tsei ashishifãi.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves on top, but the roots underneath stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Cassava plants put all their energy into leafy growth above ground when the soil has too much nitrogen or when the soil is too hard and compacted, preventing the plant from storing starches and expanding its tubers underground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ato ŋmeii ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when daytime heat gets too high or when soil moisture drops suddenly. Extreme heat dries out the pollen, causing the plant to shed the blossoms to conserve its moisture and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwie shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green pepper fruits turning black and soft while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili aduawai eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which occurs when plants cannot absorb enough calcium while the fruit is developing. It is usually caused by irregular watering, where the soil switches between being too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Why do vegetables grown inside a greenhouse produce higher yields than those I grow in my open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses shield crops from harsh weather, destructive pests, and heavy rains while providing steady warmth and moisture. Because the plants do not spend energy fighting off pests or extreme weather, they put all their energy into producing leaves and fruit.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuuu nii kɛwuuu kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted next to them during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn and dry out easily under direct Ghanaian sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and broad, providing essential living shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha wala ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and making the plant stop growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to distort and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants close or fold up in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves during the hot afternoon hours to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to direct sunlight. This natural defense mechanism prevents water from evaporating too quickly from the plant during intense heat.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ nɛɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ tsei amli oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before they are ready for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages split when sudden heavy rains or over-watering occur right after a dry period. The inner core of the cabbage absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the tight outer leaves can stretch, forcing the head to burst open.
ga: Kaabaji baafite kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kaaba lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. ha yitso lɛ mli agbala

english: Why do weeds always grow back much faster than my farm crops after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to local conditions over thousands of years, allowing their root systems to take up water and nutrients much faster than domesticated farm crops, which need more care and cultivation to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shĩa, ni biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce pods at different times of the year instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? afi lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛ pods lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Cocoa trees respond to rainy and dry seasons in Ghana. The heavy rains trigger main flowering, creating the primary harvest season, while minor rains later in the year produce a smaller secondary harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe nii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi shishijee baa. ni kɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ baa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ kpamɔ bibioo ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor's farm give three harvests in a year while my farm only gives two?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ daa afi yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Harvest frequency depends heavily on soil nutrients, rainfall, shade control, and regular pest management. Farms with better soil moisture and protection against pests can sustain flowers and pods longer into the dry periods.
ga: Nikpamɔ shii abɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ shade nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ daa Okwaafoi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my cocoa trees produce more fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil by replacing depleted nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. This strengthens the roots, helps the tree grow healthy leaves, and provides the energy needed to form large, full cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni efite tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai ni wa. ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is damp. The moisture helps dissolve the fertilizer so the tree's roots can easily drink in the nutrients as flowering starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mlɛo kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray chemicals on my cocoa trees even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Spraying protects your farm before invisible threats take over. Insect pests like capsids and fungal spores that cause black pod disease can infect healthy trees quickly, so spraying early keeps your crop safe.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he dani gbeyeishemɔi ni anaaa lɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baanyɛ atswa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaha onibii ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in high humidity and shade. Removing infected pods right away and applying approved fungicides helps protect the remaining healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use the exact same chemical spray to treat both insects and diseases on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi tsei anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛtsa kooloi bibii kɛ helai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: No, insecticides are specially made to kill insect pests like capsids, while fungicides fight fungal infections like black pod. Using the wrong chemical will not solve the problem and wastes money.
ga: Dabi. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ naagba lɛ aba naagbee, ni eji shika fitemɔ.

english: What is the best way to care for young cocoa seedlings right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains, clear ground free of weeds around their bases, and adequate soil moisture so their delicate roots can settle.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains, shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ ni bɔle amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and unnecessary shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak branches and unwanted shoots so the tree doesn't waste vital nutrients on them. It also lets in sunlight and airflow, which reduces diseases and helps the main stem produce more pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni ataooo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is suitable for planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei adumɔ?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, fertile soil that retains moisture but drains well so water doesn't pool around the roots. It should also have some shade trees available to shelter young seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli shi etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ahi shi koni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize early in the season rather than waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa mra yɛ be lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: Planting maize early allows the crop to make full use of the initial rains and cool weather, helping young roots establish strongly before hot dry spells or pests affect their growth.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishijee nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanáa amɛdalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting my maize seeds properly in straight lines and right depth help them grow better?
ga: Te ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing prevents seedlings from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, while correct depth protects seeds from birds and helps roots anchor firmly in the soil.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛto dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, yɛ be mli ni mlibotemɔ ni sa lɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe ni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Why should an extension officer test my soil before I buy and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ dani amɛhe ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Soil testing shows what nutrients your land already has and what it lacks, so you only spend money on the specific plant foods your crop needs to produce a good yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteɔ shika yɛ tsei niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ pɛ he.

english: Is it true that every part of my farmland needs fertilizer for crops to grow well?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, not all land lacks nutrients. Some soil is naturally fertile, and adding unnecessary fertilizer can burn crop roots or waste money without increasing your harvest.
ga: Jeee shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ henɔi komɛi yɛ ni amɛwoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo efite shika ni ehaaa yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale or yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. A soil test helps identify missing nutrients so you can apply the right plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baanyɛ aye abua ni ana niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsei niyenii ni sa atsu nii.

english: Should I clear weeds and old plants from my land before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei momo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Clearing land early removes aggressive weeds that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young seedlings, giving your maize a strong head start.
ga: He lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Egbeɔ jwɛi ni baa shi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ha o-corn lɛ afee shishijee kpakpa.

english: Why does loosening and preparing my soil properly help maize roots grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows crop roots to easily push deep into the earth to find underground water and nutrients, making the plant stronger against high winds and drought.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii. Ehaa tsei nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds provided by the government are good for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Government-provided seeds are high-yield, disease-resistant varieties specially tested to grow well in Ghana's weather conditions when planted according to official guidance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ji dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Be ni esa akɛ adu yɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ agbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me if my crops are not performing well?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ?
