english: Extension officers inspect your field to diagnose plant diseases, soil problems, or poor growth, providing step-by-step advice on how to save your crop and improve your yield.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baakwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛna tsei ahe helai, shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai, loo amɛdalɛ ni ehiii. Ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi haa yɛ bɔ ni ooofee obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni oha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ he.

english: How can government farm grants help me get better results from my crop harvest?
ga: Te nɔyeli ŋmɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Grants provide financial assistance to help you afford essential farm inputs like quality seeds, soil testing, and fertilizers at the right time in the planting season.
ga: Shika ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shika ni yeɔ ebuaa bo ni okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni hi, shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahaa yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing so many leaves but yielding very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure makes sweet potatoes focus all their energy on growing lush green leaves instead of root tubers. Reducing nitrogen and adding potassium helps the plant store energy in the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifã lɛ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ potassium ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Do I need to buy seeds to plant sweet potatoes, or can I use the stems from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe dumɔwui koni mikɛdu ŋmeii? Aloo manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ atsu nii?

english: You do not need seeds for sweet potatoes. You can cut fresh, healthy vine stems about 30 centimeters long and plant them directly into mounds or ridges of loose soil.
ga: Dumɔwui he ehiaaa bo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ wain tso hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 30 ni okɛwo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ ejɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on tomatoes are usually a sign of sap-sucking pests like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or a lack of water and nutrients in the soil during hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. aloo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and woody before I can harvest them for cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ tsei dani manyɛ makpa amɛ koni mikɛhoo lɛ?

english: Okra pods turn hard and tough if left on the stalk too long. You should harvest okra while the pods are young, tender, and snap easily, usually three to four days after the flower opens.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Esa akɛ okpa okra be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya, bei pii lɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my okra plants falling off without forming any okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Okra flowers drop off mainly due to stress from irregular watering, sudden heat spikes, or small insect pests eating the base of the blossoms before pollination happens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ Roselle fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli baa. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ Ye fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi dani pollination aba.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs missing seeds at the top when I peel open the husk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Incomplete corn cobs happen when dry weather or hot winds dry out the corn silk before pollen can fertilize every grain, preventing seeds from forming all the way to the tip.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii ni edako lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha abɛi siliki lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbi dani pollen lɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ amli. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkafee kɛyashiɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cucumbers taste bitter when I pick them from the garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kukumbai lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cucumbers develop a bitter taste when the plant experiences stress, especially from hot sun combined with uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents bitterness.
ga: Kukumba bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my cucumber vine have plenty of flowers, but no cucumbers are growing on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani kukumba ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ?

english: Cucumber plants produce male flowers first, which only produce pollen and cannot grow into cucumbers. Fruit will only form on female flowers once bees visit to pollinate them.
ga: Kukumba tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ. ni baajie pollen pɛ kpo ni enyɛŋ eda ni etsɔ kukumba. Yibii baa yɛ fɔfɔi yei anɔ pɛ kɛji ŋmeii shwie amɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant tall crops like okra together with tomatoes in the same vegetable garden?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ okra kɛ tomato yɛ aduawai abɔɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, you can plant them together, but space them properly so the tall okra plants do not cast too much shade over the tomato plants and starve them of sunshine.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome. Shi too he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okra tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akaha tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛkaha hulu la lɛ akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: How can I estimate the total amount of crop yield I will harvest from my farm before I start picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔmɔ?

english: You can estimate your total yield by counting the average number of good cobs or fruits on a few sample plants, multiplying that by your total number of plants, and dividing by the weight of a standard bag.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai kpakpai ni yɔɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni afee amɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ abɔ he. ni akɛ kotoku ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli tsiimɔ jaa mli

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and scorch when the hot season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves scorch because direct sunlight burns them and dries out the moisture in the plant. Cocoa naturally grows best under partial shade, so planting shade trees or plantains nearby shields them from harsh heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni fe nine akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to build strong stalks and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants and feed on the growing shoot, which weakens the plant unless caught and treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ja amɔ lɛ ni atsa lɛ mra.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field help my maize grow better the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the crop leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adumɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot under the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil and suffocates the roots, which allows rot fungal diseases to attack. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa fungal rot hela lɛ tutuaa mɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch sunlight. When the leaves spread out in full sun, they make the energy needed to push nutrients down into the ground to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji baai lɛ gbɛ eshwa hulu lɛ mli Ehaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛtsi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee bulbs agboi.

english: Why is my maize stunted and yellow even though I cleared all the visible weeds around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni anaa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ moŋ? Miŋmɔshi nibii

english: Your soil may contain a parasitic weed called Striga, or witchweed. Striga seeds attach directly to the roots of maize underground, stealing water and food before the weed even pops up above the soil.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga loo witchweed lɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Striga dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii dani jwɛi lɛ po ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the air is too dry, or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents the flower from pollinating to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi ni awo mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ awo yibii.

english: When is the best time to apply NPK fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded, ideally a day after a moderate rain. Burying the fertilizer in small holes a few centimeters away from the plant stem and covering it with soil protects it from heavy rainwater runoff.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli gbi kome yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni aaafu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bu bibii amli Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi ni okɛ sũ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ waa lɛ akaho.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the bunches are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots, and when too many suckers grow around the main trunk, they weigh the plant down and steal support. Pruning extra suckers to leave only three stems per mat and propping up heavy trees with wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, amɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛjuɔ nɔ ni ekɛfiɔ esɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ tsei etɛ pɛ yɛ mat kome nɔ, ni akɛ tsei ni tsii fiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do some of my short crops stop growing well when I plant them under tall tree crops like coconut palms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kukuji lɛ ekomɛi kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmei tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Tall trees block direct sunlight with their large leaves. Shorter crops underneath need adequate sunlight to make food through photosynthesis, so heavy shade slows down their growth.
ga: Tsei kakadaji kɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni tsii haa shweremɔ baa shi.

english: What can I do if my large coconut trees are casting too much shadow on my lower crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso agbo ko ha shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ?

english: You can prune the lower, older fronds of the tall trees to allow more light to filter down to the ground crops, ensuring both the trees and ground crops receive enough sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ koni la babaoo atsɔ tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ mash lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables underneath my tall trees to save space on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can intercrop under tall trees, but you must choose crops that tolerate shade or plant your tall trees far enough apart so light and rain can reach the ground level.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei awo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashishi. Shi ehe miihia ni ohala tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi. Aloo dumɔ tsei kakadaji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni la kɛ nugbɔ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant tall trees if I intend to grow other crops beneath them?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ tɛŋŋ kɛji mikɛ mihe wo mli akɛ makwɛ tsei krokomɛi yɛ amɛshishi?

english: Plant tall trees at least 8 to 10 meters apart so their top leaves do not completely overlap, allowing sunlight and rainfall to reach the soil for your smaller crops.
ga: Dumɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 koni ŋwɛi baai lɛ akafee ekome. Koni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha onibii bibii lɛ.

english: Will tall trees in my field steal water and fertilizer from the smaller crops growing underneath them?
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ. Ani eedara yɛ eshishi?

english: Yes, tall trees have large root systems that absorb nutrients and water quickly. You need to apply extra manure or fertilizer and maintain proper spacing so all plants get enough nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu oya. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he. ni amɛkwɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it good practice to leave fallen tree fronds and leaves on the ground around my lower crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaashi baai kɛ tsei ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? Mishishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, leaving fallen leaves on the ground creates a natural mulch layer that conserves soil moisture, keeps the soil cool, and releases organic nutrients as the leaves rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛji baai lɛ fite

english: Why does heavy rain wash away topsoil in open land but not under a dense tree cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ shi efɔɔɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The leaf canopy of tall trees breaks the impact of falling raindrops so they hit the ground softly, preventing soil erosion and allowing water to soak deep into the earth.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he hewalɛ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛtswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ blɛoo. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ehaa nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How do big canopy trees help protect my young crops during the scorching dry season?
ga: Te tsei wuji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa be mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Big trees act as natural sunshades, reducing the surrounding temperature and protecting delicate young crops beneath them from burning under excessive heat.
ga: Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine shishi.

english: Why do tall trees like coconut palms survive heavy winds while my smaller crops get destroyed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmei tsei yeɔ wala yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yeɔ wala lɛ? Ani akpata minɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english: Tall tree palms have strong, fibrous root networks and flexible trunks built to withstand strong winds, which can also act as windbreaks to protect smaller crops nearby.
ga: Palm tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ amɛhe ni afee amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa. Abaanyɛ akɛ enɛ atsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do plants growing under thick tree shade get mold and leaf spots more often than plants in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ náa ŋmeii kɛ baai ahe ŋmɔlɔ shii abɔ fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy shade keeps moisture trapped on leaves for longer periods after rain or dew, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Shade ni tsii yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: When maize plants do not get enough food (nitrogen) from the soil, they move whatever nutrients they have to the new upper leaves to keep growing. This starves the older leaves at the bottom, making them turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii (nitrogen) ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water. Without leaves, the plant loses less moisture to the air and goes into a resting state until the rains return to grow new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ baa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ eba ni baa heei jeɔ kpo.

english: Why are small white, powdery spots covering the leaves of my cucumber plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ lɛ? Mihaa mi kukumba tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: That white substance is a common plant illness called powdery mildew, caused by microscopic fungi. It spreads in humid weather and blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves, which slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ ji tso hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops its flowers because it does not have enough energy to support growing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaye amɛbua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the sides just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden, heavy amount of water after a dry stretch. The inside of the tomato absorbs water and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu babaoo mli trukaa beni ajie amɛ ni amɛgbi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrink on the tree before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which thrives in wet and shady conditions. The fungus attacks the pod skin and spreads inside, killing the beans and causing the pod to dry up.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Fɛ̃i lɛ tutuaa pod hewolo lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa emli. Gbemɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ogbi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rains when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? No je shishi etere kuu agbo ko?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that spread sideways rather than deep into the earth. When the heavy fruit bunch weighs the plant down and rain softens the soil, weak roots easily pull out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa amɛsɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers rotting from the inside while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ mli beni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rot in stored yams often starts in the field from tiny soil insects, nematodes, or small cuts made during harvesting. Fungi enter these small wounds and slowly eat away at the inside of the tuber over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi bibii, nematodes, loo ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli. ni baa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli Fungus boteɔ pilamɔi bibii amli Enɛɛmɛi ni eyeɔ yitso lɛ mli fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are there tiny holes all over the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ eggplant lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small insects called flea beetles chew those tiny holes into the leaves to feed. Loss of leaf surface makes it hard for the plant to catch sunlight and make food, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flea beetles lɛ shwieɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ baa lɛ hiɛ fite lɛ, ewaa ahaa amɛ akɛ amɛaana hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why are my rice heads light and standing straight up with empty husks instead of full grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa yitsei lɛ kpɛɔ ni amɛdamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty rice husks occur when pests like stem borers cut off water and food inside the stem, or when high heat hits during the flowering stage, preventing the grain from filling up properly.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem-boring worms lɛ ba. Kpɔ̃ɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. aloo kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli Enɛ haaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ayi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose moisture quickly under direct sunlight. Without shade from companion plants like plantains, the harsh sun scorches their leaves and dries out the surrounding soil before the roots can take in water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ he kome lɛ bɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do farmers usually plant plantains on the same land with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting delicate cocoa seedlings from direct heat. They also help keep the soil moist while giving you food and extra income while waiting for your cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni emɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and stay healthy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow huge stems and leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves around the base of my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating into the air, helping your crops stay hydrated during hot, dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes them grow thin and weak, resulting in a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees when they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ be mli ni eda jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Pruning extra or dead branches opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can pass through freely. This prevents moisture buildup that causes fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli oya. Enɛ haaa nu ni buaa ehe naa ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal nutrients and water directly from the soil before your main crops can drink them, effectively starving your crops of food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions with bad airflow. The fungus spreads quickly from pod to pod through water droplets during heavy rains.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu eyaaa jogbaŋŋ. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by sudden dry spells, continuous heavy rains, or attacks by small insects like capsids that damage the delicate stems of the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji ahum ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds just when the fruit bunch appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akutsei lɛ jeɔ kpo pɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface, and a heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy. Propping up the stem with a strong bamboo pole gives the plant the extra support it needs against strong wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii tsiiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa damɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kroko yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their bright green color and boosts grain size.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam tubers twist when the soil underneath is packed too hard or contains hidden rocks that stop the root from pushing downward. Creating high, soft soil mounds helps the yams grow smooth and long.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli ewo wu tsɔ. Aloo tɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛba shi lɛ yɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry weather to save water. The plant goes to sleep above ground while keeping its roots safe under the soil until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni akɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaahã amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my corn produce empty cobs with missing kernels when rainfall stops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli shi ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra lɛ?

english: Maize needs plenty of water when producing silks and tassels. If a dry spell hits during flowering, pollen dies before it can fertilize the cob, leaving empty gaps on the cob.
ga: Abɛi biɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛfee siliki kɛ tsɔji. Kɛji fɛ̃i be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollen lɛ gboɔ dani ekɛ cob lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baa ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft before they get mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads during cool, wet weather. Trimming overgrown shade branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the pods and keep the fungus away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ mli kɛbaa. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and feeling sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny whiteflies that suck plant juices and pass on viruses. Spraying neem water or using insect nets protects tomato plants from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu ni ekɛ helai baa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu shwie nɔ loo okɛ kooloi bibii atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni pepper ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when afternoon heat becomes extreme or when the soil gets too dry, as a way to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my sweet orange tree produce many flowers but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop extra flowers if they lack soil nutrients or if heavy rain washes away pollen. Adding well-rotted manure before flowering helps the tree carry full fruits to maturity.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi titri kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary shade like plantains acts as an umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has left from the older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help fix my soil for next season's crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Does it really matter which direction I stick cassava stems into the dirt when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ atsɔɔ akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the buds to grow downward into the ground before turning back up toward the sun. This wastes the plant's energy, resulting in weaker growth and much smaller tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ odu o-yucca tso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ekɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ baa shi ni tuber yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Yams need their leaves lifted high into the air to catch maximum sunlight and stay off the damp dirt where diseases spread. Climbing high allows the leaves to make more food, which is sent down into the ground to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes miisumɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. kɛ muji ni mli efɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ, ebaa lɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why are there small holes raggedly chewed into the leaves of my young corn plants with brown dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔɔ ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ koni lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep inside the central growing tip of the corn plant to eat the softest leaves where it is safe from rain and birds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ kɛ okpoi nyɛŋ aba lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering or prolonged dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant exposes less leaf area to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly and keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hulu la fioo. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, insufficient water, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni kɛ fɔfɔii baabɔ koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai lɛ faaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and pale even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal nutrients and sunlight directly from your plants' roots and leaves, starving your crop of the essential food it needs to grow thick and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Lifting yam leaves onto stakes spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn ears are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa toi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to stay green and build big stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni niyenii tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei wuji.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon heat is too strong, when the soil is too dry, or when there are no insects visiting the flowers to pollinate them.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni baasara fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves to suck out the juice, which damages leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When excess rainwater stays trapped in soggy soil, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing water mold diseases to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ batsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tuber rot aba.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil over and over, while giving maize-loving pests a permanent home to multiply in your land.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii momo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that can trap nitrogen food from the air through their roots and leave it behind in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and yield very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your land; they steal water, soil food, and sunlight away from your main crops, leaving your plants weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots supporting a heavy stem, so if tiny worms or pests damage their roots, or if the soil is too soft, strong winds can easily push them down.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni fiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii kpata eshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa amɛ shi oya.

english: Why do some seed varieties yield so much more food than the traditional seeds I've always planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are bred specifically to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and convert soil nutrients into harvestable crops more efficiently than traditional seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo bei amli ni etsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ akpa jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-focused pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants and smaller overall yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli baa.

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade from larger trees or companion plants like plantain to protect their sensitive leaves from harsh direct sunlight and retain moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient, or that excessive water in the soil is preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo akɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I pour fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant to make it grow faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni eha tso lɛ adara oya?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and damage roots; fertilizer should always be applied a few finger-lengths away from the stem where feeding roots can safely reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi. ni niyenii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates sharply, or when the plant lacks sufficient balanced nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a protective blanket over the soil, keeping ground temperature cool and preventing water from evaporating into the air so the roots stay moist.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli Koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and produce tiny harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, water, and soil food that your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Baai ni eyi obɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The moisture from fresh rains causes insect eggs hidden on the leaves to hatch into caterpillars, which feed heavily on the young leaves to grow.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ hee mli Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ afɔ̃ɔ amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ kɛyashiɔ amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green, or produce small yields despite getting rain, your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ moŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the following season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants have tiny holes in the leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which feed on young maize leaves and stems. Catching them early with appropriate organic or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall worms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning brown and drying up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm, wet weather encourages fungal diseases like blight to spread quickly on tomato leaves. Spacing plants out and trimming lower leaves helps air circulate and keeps the foliage dry.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tomato baai lɛ anɔ oya. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct heat. They require shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot while they are still under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for water and nutrients. Leaving only one strong sucker allows the main plant to produce large, healthy bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Sucker ni mli wa kome ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to grow downward smoothly. Hard, compacted, or stony soil stops the roots from expanding easily, causing tubers to bend or split.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. ha yitso lɛ abɔle loo efo

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my harvested hybrid maize for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred to give high yields only in their first planting generation. Saving seeds from that harvest leads to weak plants and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or compost around the base of the plants will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland get so hard and dry like stone after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter, like old leaves and compost, to keep it soft and spongy. Adding manure, compost, or leaving crop residues on the soil helps retain moisture and keeps the earth soft for roots to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai momoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in wet, dark, and damp conditions. Pruning excess branches on your cocoa trees allows sunlight and fresh air to dry up moisture, which prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the leaves and heart of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibi lɛ baai kɛ tsuii amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves feeding on fresh maize foliage. Inspecting your field early and spraying recommended treatments directly into the center funnel of the plant can stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa baai heei. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpa enɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and cool moisture while the cocoa plants establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Beni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi miida lɛ

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots and mulching the base helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ kpe. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Roots lɛ he lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ mulching lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my garden bean plants start creeping on the ground and need wooden sticks to stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miibɔi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei koni amɛdamɔ shi lɛ?

english: Certain bean varieties are climbing plants that naturally seek sunlight by climbing upward. Using wooden sticks or stakes keeps the vines off the wet soil, preventing rot and allowing the plant to produce more pods.
ga: Beans henɔi komɛi ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛtaoɔ hulu la kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkwɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsoi loo tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tsei lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ.

english: Why do heavy rainstorms knock down the buds and flowers on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miiha ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers have delicate stems, so strong winds and heavy falling raindrops easily detach them before fruit can form. Mulching around the plants and planting tall crops nearby as windbreaks can protect fragile pepper plants.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaagbala mli dani yibiiwoo aba. Mulching ni abɔleɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiimɔ he lɛ baanyɛ abu pepper tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves dry out and fall off, and cracks begin to appear on the soil surface directly around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baa lɛ egbi ni egbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil underneath is too hard or rocky for the tuber to expand downward easily. Building high, loose soil mounds or ridges allows the roots to grow straight and big without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa ja ni amɛdaraa ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-composted manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei niji ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava tubers need room underground to expand. Planting cuttings too close together forces them to compete for soil nutrients and light, resulting in very thin tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during dry periods and keeping the soil moist helps fruits form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I burn dry weeds on my farm before planting?
ga: Ani ebaana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji mishã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu?

english: Yes, burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms like earthworms. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally or using them as mulch improves soil moisture and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo akɛtsu nii akɛ mulch lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases to build up over time. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or maize starves those pests and restores soil nutrients.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa Ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing concentrated chemical fertilizer directly against plant stems can burn the tender plant tissue and roots. It is best to apply fertilizer in a ring a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni mli edɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ahe fãji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms boring holes into my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miitswa bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are caused by caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect the leaves.
ga: Buji nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔ̃ɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Groundnuts are generally ready when the plant leaves turn yellow and drop off. Pull up one plant to test: if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings, it is time to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii feɔ klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Gbalamɔ tso kome nɔ ni okɛka: Kɛji akɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native, hardy plants adapted to steal water and nutrients very quickly. Weeding early prevents them from overshadowing and starving your young farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakumɔ okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkaye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do animals keep digging up my freshly planted cassava stems and tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi miyaa nɔ mifoɔ mi-cassava ni midu ehee lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Animals like rodents and bush pigs dig up young cassava because the loosened soil makes it easy to reach the sweet, moisture-rich roots and stems. Protecting the field perimeter or burying stems at the correct angle helps keep them safe.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ koo mli tsinabii shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ náa mlɛo. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ loo tsei lɛ ahe ni afuɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes my yams to get dark holes and rot while they are still growing underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Dark holes in underground yams are usually caused by tiny soil pests called nematodes or yam beetles. They feed on the growing tuber, creating wounds where water and fungal diseases enter and cause rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo sweet potato beetles lɛ kɛ buji diji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ, ni amɛfeɔ pilamɔi yɛ he ni nu kɛ ŋmeii helai boteɔ mli ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ.

english: How can I stop grasscutters from chewing the stems of my young oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-oil palm tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Grasscutters attack young oil palms because the center of the base is soft and sweet. Putting wire mesh collars around the base of each seedling creates a physical barrier that stops rodents from reaching the trunk.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii ejaakɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ waya fĩ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips downward when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil food, or when too much water around the roots prevents them from feeding properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo be mli ni nu ebɔle he Shishifãi babaoo haaa anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporarily droops to protect itself from drying out and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, ebaatsa kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few groundnuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need loose, soft soil so that the flower pegs can easily push down into the earth to form nuts. Hard soil or excess nitrogen in the soil makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of underground pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia ŋmeii. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anyɛ atswa fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya koni efee ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they can grow into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Consistent soil moisture helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains or shade trees provide temporary living umbrellas that reduce heat and hold moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa wɔnáa he ko ni amɛhiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni haa dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does planting beans in the same field with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and leguminous crops capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots feed the soil, nearby maize plants absorb that free nitrogen to grow taller and greener.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ nakai nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do the stems of my planted cassava cuttings rot in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain saturates the farm, water fills all the air pockets in the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe, allowing rotting fungi and bacteria in the wet soil to attack and destroy the cassava stems.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo nu. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Ha ŋmeii ni egboi kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmei tsei lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time to start planting my maize when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ?

english: Following reliable daily weather forecasts helps you time your planting right after the first sustained rains begin, ensuring your seeds get enough moisture to germinate without rotting in dry soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ daa gbi lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oto be ni okɛbaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Seeds may sprout from the initial moisture, but the young seedlings will quickly dry out and die under the hot sun if follow-up rains do not arrive to nourish their delicate roots.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shi tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaa koni eha eshishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ niyenii,

english: Why do my crops wilt even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Light surface rain only wets the top layer of soil, whereas deep crop roots need heavy or continuous rainfall to soak deep down so plants can draw enough water during hot afternoons.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ tse lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa loo ni yaa nɔ koni amɛbote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much heavy rain waterlogs the soil and suffocates the root system, preventing the roots from taking up air and essential nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why does heavy downpour during the flowering stage reduce my yield of crops like tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mi tomatoi lɛ ayibii baa shi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can physically knock delicate flowers off the branches before they are pollinated, preventing them from developing into full fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kwraa

english: Why should I check the weather forecast before spending money to apply fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji amli dani mafite shika koni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If a heavy downpour occurs immediately after fertilizer application, the runoff water will wash away the expensive nutrients before your crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ Runoff lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ mli dani onibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Is it better to clear and prepare my land before or after the forecasted early rains start?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ aba loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: You should finish clearing and preparing your land before the expected rains start so that the loose soil can immediately absorb the early moisture when planting begins.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni osaa lɛ naa dani nugbɔ anɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra kɛji akɛ dumɔ je shishi pɛ.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil for my vegetable crop if the weather report predicts a dry stretch ahead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha mi-vegetables lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he amaniɛbɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ baaba hu?

english: Placing dry leaves, grass, or straw around the base of your plants acts as a protective blanket that traps soil moisture and stops the sun from drying out the root zone.
ga: Baai, jwɛi, loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: What does it mean for my farm when the weather forecaster says we will get light rain instead of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nilelɔ lɛ kɛɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Light rain cools the air and refreshes surface leaves, but it is usually not enough water to moisten deep soil for planting new seeds or sustaining heavy feeding crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he jɔɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i waa ni akɛdu dumɔwui heei loo tsei ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if the rainy season ends much earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra kwraa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ?

english: When rains end too early, young cocoa pods stop growing properly, dry up, or drop off early because the tree lacks the constant groundwater needed to fill the pods.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni edako lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ, amɛgbiɔ, loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yaa nɔ daa ni he hiaa koni akɛwo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray powder or fungicide on my crops every few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ powda loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa nyɔji fioo lɛ?

english: Regular protective spraying acts like maintenance for your farm. It prevents microscopic fungi and insects from settling on the stems and leaves, keeping the plant healthy so it produces bright, high-quality yields at harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa daa lɛ tamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akamɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ yibii ni kpɛɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees every few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-kookoo tso lɛ he daa nyɔji fioo lɛ?
