english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches so the plant doesn't waste energy on them. It opens up the tree so air and sunlight can flow through, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ajieɔ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ. Egbeleɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ daraa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops regularly instead of waiting until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing them regularly ensures your main plants get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ofɔ amɛhe daa lɛ, ehaa otsei titrii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural shades, keeping the ground cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil isn't dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko moŋ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it during heavy heat. Wilting is the plant's natural defense to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun and preserve its internal moisture.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbaa baa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the plant is hungry, particularly for nitrogen. When nitrogen is lacking in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed new growth, turning the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it continuously in the same spot drains the soil completely, whereas rotating it with leguminous crops like cowpeas puts valuable nitrogen back into the land.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ mli kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil after a light rain while the crops are actively growing. Applying it during dry dry spells can burn the plant roots, while heavy downpours can wash it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do we make big mounds of loose soil before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔma shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji agbo ko dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth so the tubers can expand easily downward and outward. Hard soil stops the yam from swelling, resulting in small, stunted tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shikpɔŋ kɛ kponɔgbɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa baaha ŋmeii lɛ akafu. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni egbɔjɔ baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava shows maturity when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil surrounding the base of the main stem begins to crack as the enlarging roots push outward.
ga: Cassava shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni eda lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the earth on my farm get very hard and dry up so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture rapidly under direct sunlight and hardens into a crust. Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or fallen leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping the soil soft and trapping moisture for your crops to drink.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi, ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ Dumɔwui ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii anu.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to plant my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and soak the soil at least finger-deep, usually after two or three heavy rains. Planting after just one light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up if the rain stops for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni kɛ hoo lɛ, okɛ sũ lɛ awo mli inchi kome. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps (nodes) on the stem where old leaves used to grow; these bumps must point upward toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the buds struggle to grow upward and your harvest will be very small.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii (nodes) ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ he ni baai momoi lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baawa ni ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the dirt. This causes plants to grow thin, weak, and yellow, resulting in a smaller harvest than if you spaced them out properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up toward the sun to catch light and make food, which grows the big tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant make much larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛfee niyenii. Tuber agboi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ ehe?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, scorching sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a gentle umbrella that protects young cocoa trees from the harsh heat during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells or extreme afternoon heat. Giving your tomato plants regular water at their roots early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni akɛtee mli

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which eat young leaves from the inside out. Checking your farm early and applying recommended natural sprays like neem leaf extract or proper treatments while the worms are small can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni sa atsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild survival experts that are naturally stronger at stealing water, sunlight, and food from the dirt than food crops. Clearing weeds around your crops while they are still small ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji wala yibii ahe nilelɔi yɛ koo lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ko ni jɛ fɔmɔ mli ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe niyenii tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves usually means the maize is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and grow heavy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, which often happens when soil water goes up and down too quickly. Watering your tomatoes regularly and mulching the soil keeps water steady so the fruit stays healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ hela nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tee ŋwɛi ni eba shi oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai haa mɔ he waa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves, or by excessive heat. Spraying with organic neem oil or appropriate pest control protects the leaves so they can spread out flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look lifeless in the hot afternoon sun, but perk up again by evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ebaaku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ ni ekpɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from hot, dry soil during peak heat. The leaves wilt temporarily to save water, but covering the soil around the plant stem with dried grass keeps the roots cool and moist.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi mulching ni bɔleɔ Dry stems lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers to conserve energy for only a few strong pods. However, sudden heat, strong wind, or lack of shade trees can cause too many flowers to drop before insects can pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, latsaa ni baa trukaa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsei ni bɛ hulutsoo lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi babaoo ashwie shi dani kooloi bibii anyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my watermelon plants have plenty of yellow flowers, but no fruits are forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelons produce male flowers first to attract bees, followed later by female flowers that have tiny fruits behind them. If bees are not visiting your field to transfer pollen from male to female flowers, no fruit will grow.
ga: Watermelon hii fɔ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni egbala ŋmeii. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji fɔfɔi yei ni woɔ yibii bibii. sɛɛgbɛ Kɛji ŋmeii eyaaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli koni amɛyajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli lɛ, Yibii ko bɛ ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the tubers under the soil. Lifting the vines on stakes keeps leaves exposed to light and away from damp ground where dampness causes fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ naa la, ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ agbo lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy green leaves, but yielding small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its power on growing stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage energy to go down into making fat cassava tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hewalɛ aba koni ekɛfee ŋmei shishifãi ni mli ewo fɔ.

english: Why should I cut down the extra young suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many young suckers steal food, water, and sunlight from the mother plantain tree. Pruning extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong followers ensures the main tree bears a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsei bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ ni ashi sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over flat onto the mud just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over when their stems are too thin or tall to carry the weight of heavy grain heads. Planting seeds too closely together or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer weakens the stems, making them fall easily in wind or rain.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bafee mlɛo loo amɛkwɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ tswa lɛ

english: Why should I plant a special improved crop variety instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred to give higher yields, grow faster, and resist local pests and diseases better than traditional seeds, which helps secure a bigger harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. amɛdaraa oya ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nibii babaoo

english: Where can I get genuine, high-quality crop seeds to plant on my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can get certified seeds directly from government agricultural officers, recognized seed distributors, or registered agro-dealers to ensure they germinate well and produce healthy plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ajalɔ ni ale lɛ loo okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Do I need to nurse all crop seeds in a nursery bed before planting them directly on the main field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Not all seeds need a nursery, but delicate or small seeds benefit from a nursery bed where they can receive extra shade, water, and protection from pests until they are strong enough for the main field.
ga: Jeee dumɔwui fɛɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo bibii lɛ baaná dumɔwui atsu ni baanyɛ aha amɛná hulutsoo, nu, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ he sɛɛ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa kɛha saatso wulu lɛ.

english: How many days do I need to water my seedlings in the nursery before transplanting them?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ nu dani manyɛ mawo amɛ?

english: Most crop seedlings require about 21 to 30 days of regular watering in the nursery until they grow 4 to 6 strong true leaves and are ready to be moved to the main field.
ga: Tso dumɔwui babaoo biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu gbii 21 kɛyashi 30 be fɛɛ be yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaaná anɔkwa baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ kɛya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: How often should I water my nursery seedlings every day?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-nursery dumɔwui lɛ nu daa gbi?

english: Seedlings should usually be watered twice daily—once early in the morning and once late in the afternoon—so the soil stays moist without becoming waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ daa gbi—leebi maŋkpa kɛ shwane ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni eha nu akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better for me to transplant my crop seedlings in October or wait until November in Ghana?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo tsei ahe dumɔwui yɛ October mli loo mamɛ kɛyashi November yɛ Ghana?

english: Transplanting in October is usually better because soil moisture is still good from the late rains, whereas November brings dry Harmattan winds that can quickly dry out young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake yɛ October mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hi lolo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ naagbee. yɛ be mli ni November kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbi oya.

english: How does the starting month of the planting season change how I care for my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nyɔŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ daa lɛ shishijee nyɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni wɔkwɛɔ dumɔwui anɔ wɔhaa lɛ?

english: Planting early in the rainy season allows seedlings to rely on natural rainfall, while planting later in the season requires you to provide extra manual watering to keep them alive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ. Beni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ onine awo nu mli babaoo koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant my seedlings to the field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: It is best to transplant seedlings late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day so the heat of the sun does not dry out and kill the young plants before their roots settle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi ni efite tso bibioo lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ atswa.

english: How do I know when my nursery seedlings are strong enough to be moved to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have thick stems, at least 4 to 6 full leaves, a strong root bundle, and show no signs of leaf yellowing or disease.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa. ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo hela he okadi ko bɛ.

english: Why do my seedlings look weak right after I plant them in the main field, and how can I help them survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua amɛ ni amɛhi wala mli?

english: Seedlings suffer from 'transplant shock' when moved to new soil; watering them thoroughly right after planting and providing temporary shade helps them recover and take root.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaná ‘Transplant shock’ he amanehulu kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ Nu ni awoɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ ni ahaa amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up during the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains nearby to protect them, intense heat dries out the delicate leaves, causing them to burn and wither.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu amɛhe lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when they start bearing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Clearing away extra shoots around the base and supporting the main tree with a strong wooden prop keeps it standing upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ Base lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving tiny dark dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa. yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ

english: That is damage from Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide in the leaves of young maize to feed, which destroys the crop unless caught early and treated with proper sprays or clean soil/ash dropped into the plant center.
ga: No ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ja amɔmɔ oya ni afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo shɛrɛ shikpɔŋ/ashwishwɛ ni he tse awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and infected planting stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using clean stem cuttings prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛ tsei aniji ni he tse ni afolɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains turning into powdery white dust inside my barn after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils are eating the inside of your dried corn kernels. Drying the maize completely until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or treated storage containers keeps weevils out.
ga: Kpluka ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ grain moth lɛ miiye o-corn ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa ni akɛto vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more cobs on my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ he koni mafee ŋmãa babaoo yɛ mihe bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This makes every plant weak and thin, producing tiny cobs and a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Feemɔ cob bibioo ko ni nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ faaa

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, preventing soil-borne rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii helai kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my crops immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period called a false start. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but the tender seedlings will burn and die in dry soil before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ale lɛ akɛ amale shishijee nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Tired soil shows clear warning signs: your crops grow very slowly, the leaves stay light green or pale yellow instead of deep green, and your harvest gets smaller every year even when it rains well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ haa: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi akɛ eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni onikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo daa afi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells cause heat stress in tomatoes, making the flowers drop before fruits can form. Regular watering at the roots and mulching the soil around the plants helps prevent blossom drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ sũ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with big leaves but produce tiny roots when I crowd them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ dara shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mɛɛ be abua naa?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their leaves fight for sunlight and roots compete for soil nutrients. This causes the plant to waste its energy growing tall instead of storing starch underground in thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛdaraa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ starch baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for green growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes what little it has from older bottom leaves and sends it up to nourish new leaves and ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi baaŋɔ fã bibioo ko kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛmaje amɛ koni amɛyakwɛ baai kɛ toi heei.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn purple during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ purple yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl and turn purple when heat and dry soil make it difficult for root systems to absorb phosphorus. The leaf curling is the plant's way of reducing water loss through its leaves during harsh conditions.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ purple kɛji latsaa lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ fɔsfɔs. Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli.

english: How do I know if armyworms have invaded my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji cutworms eba mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Armyworms feed inside the central funnel of young maize plants. You will see ragged holes on fresh leaves and dark, sawdust-like droppings left behind inside the leaf folds.
ga: Cutworms yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Obaana bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai heei amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to survive in dry soil and sprout immediately with the first drop of rain, whereas farm seeds take longer to wake up and establish deep roots.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. To save water and stay alive, the plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy forming peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu aba shi ni ahi shi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baafee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops have lush green leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich animal manure, cowpea plants focus all their growth on leafy vines instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa amɛdalɛ nɔ yɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui akui.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the green vines and leaves naturally dry up and turn yellow toward the end of the rainy season, signaling that energy storage in the underground tuber is complete.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tu lɛ mli lɛ egbe naa.

english: Why do my groundnuts rot or sprout in the ground if I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: If groundnuts remain in hard, dry soil long after maturity, moisture changes cause pods to crack, allowing termites and fungi in the soil to enter and rot the seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii hi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ, Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akumɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I plant trees on the same land where I grow my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Trees improve the soil by dropping leaves that turn into natural fertilizer, and they protect crops like cocoa from getting scorched by the hot Ghanaian sun. Over time, they also act as windbreaks to protect your farm from storms.
ga: Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ahum he.

english: Will large trees steal water and nutrients away from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji baaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Deep-rooted trees take water and nutrients from far below the ground where small food crops cannot reach. They then bring those nutrients up into their leaves, which fall and enrich the topsoil for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni niyenii tsei bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa ŋwɛi kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baagbee shi ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain while waiting for my young tree seedlings to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei be mli ni mimɛɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, you can farm quick-yielding food crops between young tree seedlings during their first two to three years. This gives you food and income while the trees are still small and not yet casting full shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ niyenii tsei ni woɔ yibii oya yɛ dumɔwui bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo ni amɛnáaa hulutsoo kwraa lolo lɛ.

english: How long will it take before a newly established crop and tree farm starts yielding well?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tsei kɛ tsei ahe ŋmɔ hee ni ato shishi lɛ baaje ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afeemɔ shishi?

english: It usually takes about two to three years of dedicated effort to build up a productive multi-crop farm. During these early years, the plants focus on growing strong roots before producing steady yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani anyɛɔ amaa ŋmɔ ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ yibii. Yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do tree seedlings need so much care and protection during their first couple of years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ dumɔwui anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni abu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have small roots and soft stems, making them very vulnerable to weeds, hot weather, and animal damage. Once they survive their first two or three years, their roots go deep and they become strong enough to thrive on their own.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ kooloi fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛda.

english: Why are my plants growing very slowly above the ground during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the first year, plants spend most of their energy growing roots hidden deep in the soil to find water and anchor themselves. Once that strong root foundation is built, you will see fast growth above the ground.
ga: Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ena nu ni ekɛ ehe awo mli. Kɛji ama shishitoo ni wa pɛ Obaana dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do shade trees keep the soil on my farm from drying out quickly?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya?

english: Tree leaves form a green ceiling that blocks direct sunlight from hitting the ground. This keeps the soil cool and reduces the amount of water evaporating into the air, keeping the ground moist for nearby crops.
ga: Tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves falling from trees on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decompose on the ground and turn into rich organic manure. This natural fertilizer improves the soil structure and feeds your crops without costing you money.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni efiteee ŋshɔ lɛ naa.

english: How do tall trees help protect my crops during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Te tsei kakadaji baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall trees break the speed of heavy raindrops and strong winds, preventing rain from washing away your topsoil and stopping winds from bending or breaking your crop stems.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ gbalaa bɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ yaa oya lɛ mli. Ehaa nugbɔ shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu shwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ loo amɛkuɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young tree seedlings are getting enough sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If your seedlings have firm, dark green leaves and straight stems, they are getting enough light. If they look pale green or yellow and grow thin and tall very quickly, they are stretching to search for light and need more open space.
ga: Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifãi ni ja Tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ miiná la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji amɛfee tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkwɔ oya lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiigba amɛhe kɛmiitao la ni ehe miihia ni amɛná he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my young maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and wind, preventing excess water from evaporating until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekaho kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too extreme or when the soil suddenly shifts from very dry to very wet. Sudden stress stops the flower from pollinating and producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Haomɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb a lot of moisture from wet soil. When rain water stays in the ground too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing waterlogging fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hiɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, giving leaves maximum sunlight while keeping them away from wet soil that can cause leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni baanyɛ ekɛ baai helai aba.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain tree, they fight with the main tree for nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the remaining tree to produce large, healthy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ. Ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ niji wuji ni he wa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from lack of water or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, feel dry, and turn brown at the tips. When crops have too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, look limp, and the soil around them stays muddy and smells sour.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ, amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi, ni baa lɛ naagbeehei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baafee muji ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year lead to smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize pulls specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Repeatedly planting it in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or beans before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi woɔ cowpea dumɔ he hewalɛ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When you plant maize after harvesting beans, the maize feeds on that leftover natural soil food to grow strong.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Spraying early with natural neem oil helps protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ shwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shweremɔ hee he.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow when the surrounding shade trees are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ afo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not like intense direct sunlight. Without shade trees acting as natural umbrellas, the harsh sun burns the tender leaves, causes stress, and turns them yellow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo bɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ. kɛ haomɔ baa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my crops get soft and start rotting when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat scorches plant tissues and causes cells to break down. When coupled with moisture, this soft, heat-damaged plant tissue becomes an easy target for bacteria that cause rotting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa tso lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ akɛ hulutsoo fata tso nɛɛ mli fã ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni la ni mli edɔ lɛ efite lɛ he lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni helatsɛmɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Why do my cabbage heads look large on the outside but are mushy and rotten inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabii lɛ feɔ tamɔ agbo yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi emli lɛ efee basabasa ni efite?

english: When crops experience high heat alongside excess moisture, the inner layers grow too fast and break down into watery, soft tissue that easily rots before the crop fully matures.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine fata he lɛ. Mligbɛ fã lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ fã ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tamɔ nu ni fiteɔ oya dani tso lɛ daa.

english: Why do my leafy green vegetables turn yellow and stop growing during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many green crops are sensitive to strong heat. When it gets too hot, the plant slows down its growth to save water, causing the leaves to weaken, turn yellow, and lose their freshness.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛkɛbu nu he. tsɔne lɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Can harsh sunlight alone kill my vegetables even if I give them water every day?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ pɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa gbi po?

english: Yes, intense sun heat can bake crop tissues faster than roots can draw up groundwater. This sunburn damages the plant's skin, leading to soft patches and decay despite regular watering.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ mli fãji oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewolo. Ekɛ muji kɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ nu daa po.

english: Why do some crop varieties handle hot weather easily while others rot and fail completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kpɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties are bred for different weather conditions. Heat-sensitive varieties break down quickly in high temperatures, while heat-tolerant varieties have stronger cell structures that resist sun damage.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. Henɔi ni nuɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ yɛ wala yibii ni mli wa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ hulu la ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers mostly thick watery skin instead of good heavy starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nu ni mli edɔ fe starch kpakpa lɛ?

english: Excessive soil heat combined with nitrogen stress forces the plant to build thick, watery outer layers rather than storing dense, healthy starch inside the root.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nitrogen haomɔ haa tsei feɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni mli edɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa ɔ toɔ sisifã ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Why are my harvested tomatoes developing pale watery spots that quickly decay in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ yɛ nu mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ oya lɛ?

english: Direct exposure to strong sun causes sunscald on the skin of tomatoes. This cooks the tissue underneath into a watery patch that fungus and rot organisms quickly destroy.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa tomato nɔ. Enɛ baahoo fãji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni etsɔ nu ni ŋmeii kɛ nibii krokomɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ baafite oya.

english: Why are my yams rotting inside the mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: When soil gets extremely hot and soaked with rain, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, causing the fleshy tissue to suffocate, turn soft, and rot underground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Enɛ haa loo lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my harvested produce spoil so much faster during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heat accelerates the breathing rate of harvested crops, causing them to lose water quickly and enabling spoilage micro-organisms to multiply faster.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tsei ni akpa lɛ amumɔ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya. ni ehaa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya

english: Why is my crop failing even after I applied strong fertilizer to force it to grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa woɔ amɛmli koni mikɛnyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Fertilizers cannot overcome severe heat stress. Forcing a crop with heavy chemicals during hot, dry conditions burns the roots and weakens the plant further instead of helping it produce.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aye dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa nɔ kunim. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If I pick the biggest maize cobs from my harvest to use as seed, will they automatically produce big maize next season?
ga: Kɛ mihala ŋmãa ni da fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui lɛ, Ani amɛbaawo ŋmãa wuji amɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Selecting big, healthy cobs helps, but if the crop came from a hybrid seed packet, the seeds saved from that harvest will split traits and produce much lower yields in the second generation.
ga: Kɛ́ ohala ŋmei agbo ni mli wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli hu? Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná sui ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do older farmers in my village hang their saved maize cobs directly above the kitchen smoke and fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ eŋmãa ni ekɛto lɛ fĩɔ lasu kɛ la ni yɔɔ etsu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The gentle heat dries the seeds completely, while the smoke coats the maize cobs and keeps weevils, insects, and mold from attacking the grain during storage.
ga: mild heat Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, lasu lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii akatutua ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I spend money on certified seeds from an agrodealer when I can just use seeds from my own previous harvest for free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ? Akɛni manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yaka hewɔ lɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist diseases, endure drought, and yield far more grain than seeds saved year after year from older crops.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui babaoo fe dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen or are getting too much water. Nitrogen is the main plant food that makes leaves green and healthy, so adding manure or recommended fertilizer will help them turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods can even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaada po?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, high heat, or poor soil food. Providing shade trees and keeping mulch around the root area helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shishifãi lɛ wo shishifãi lɛ amli ni okɛ sũ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun instead of building strong stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he, ni moŋ amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for days without proper drainage, water fills all the soil spaces, drowning the roots and causing fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baayi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ obɔ. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the stems of my crops help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeps the root area cool, and holds moisture so your plants don't wilt quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni tsei lɛ akagbo oya

english: Why is it good for my soil when I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally catch nitrogen food from the air and put it deep into the ground. This feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize grow bigger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-ŋmã lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants look healthy in the morning but wilt completely under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa leebi shi amɛgboiɔ kwraa yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the roots cannot suck up ground water fast enough to replace what heat evaporates from the leaves, or because underground pests or fungal wilt diseases are damaging the stem and roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ miifite tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do simple weeds hurt my crops if they are all just plants growing in the same dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛkɛ ji amɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than your food crops and aggressively steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. They also attract insects and crop diseases to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe oniyenii ni oduɔ lɛ ni ejuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ amli lɛ waa. Egbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai hu kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil. If tiny worms called nematodes eat the root tips or if the soil is too soft, the heavy stem and fruit bunch will easily pull the roots out of the ground in wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji ŋmei bibioo ko Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Tso lɛ yibii ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small leaves and side branches from my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai bibii lɛ? Ni niji ni jɛ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary leaves forces the plant to send its water and soil food straight to the fruits and flowers, resulting in larger, higher-quality produce rather than just a bushy plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya aduawai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nibii ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tsei akuu ko kɛkɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees break easily when they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ mibɔi aduawai babaoo miwomɔ lɛ?

english: When a plantain tree produces a fruit bunch, the top becomes very heavy. Because the stem is made of soft layers rather than hard wood, this extra top weight puts severe pressure on the stem, making it easy to snap, especially in strong weather.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ wo aduawai akui lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tsii waa, ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fee ŋmeii lɛ moŋ fe tsei ni wa. Nɛkɛ tsɔne ni tsii fe nine nɛɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa baa tsɔne lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa efoɔ mlɛo, titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli.

english: Are young plantain plants also affected by strong winds, or is it only the mature ones with fruit?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa dumɔwui bibii ahe? Aloo tsei ni edara pɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Young plantains usually survive winds better because they are shorter and do not carry heavy loads. Mature plantains that have developed fruit bunches are at the highest risk of breaking because their center of gravity is shifted upward.
ga: Plantain bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ kuku ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi tsɔne ni tsii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ. Plantains ni eda ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui lɛ ji mɛi ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ akɛ amɛbaakumɔ beni hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants seem to break more easily during the dry season when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi plantains lɛ fãa oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: During long periods without rain, plantain stems lose water and their inner pressure drops. This makes the stem brittle and less flexible, so when strong dry winds blow, the tree cannot bend and snaps easily.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ ni mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi fãa ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa miitswa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛkumɔ mlɛo.

english: Does heavy rain directly destroy my plantain crops, or is it the wind that causes them to fall?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ kpata midumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni ha amɛgbee shi?

english: Rainwater itself does not destroy plantain plants because they need moisture to grow. The main danger is the strong gusting wind that comes before or after the rain, which pushes against the heavy wet leaves and fruit bunches, causing the plant to break.
ga: Nugbɔ nu gbeee plantains ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛdara. Oshara titri ni yɔɔ mli ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ loo no sɛɛ lɛ tswaa baai ni efɔ waa kɛ aduawai aniji, ni efoɔ tsei.

english: What makes a plantain tree snap right in the middle of the stem instead of coming out from the roots?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeejɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: A plantain stem is a pseudostem made of water-filled leaf sheaths rather than deep wood. If the plant is carrying heavy fruit and loses stem moisture, the middle section becomes the weakest point and snaps under the weight, even if the roots are still firm in the ground.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ji amale tsei ni akɛ baai ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu fee moŋ fe tso ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ wo yibii ni tsii ni eshishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, teŋgbɛ fã lɛ bafeɔ he ni egbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ ni efoɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ lolo moŋ.

english: How can I protect my fruiting plantain trees from snapping when strong winds come?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ba?

english: You can support your plantain trees by propping them up using strong wooden or bamboo poles placed firmly under the fruit bunch. This crutch supports the heavy weight of the fruit and keeps the stem from bending and snapping in strong winds.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua dumɔwui lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa ni okɛbaawo aduawai akui lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Tso nɛɛ fiɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do plantain stalks become so fragile after a long period without rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei lɛ waaa kwraa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains rely on water stored in their stem cells to stay upright and rigid. When a dry spell lasts a long time, the plant drains its stored water, causing the stem to weaken, soft-collapse inside, and become fragile.
ga: Plantains kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni ato yɛ amɛ stem cells lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ Tso lɛ baajie nu ni ato lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. gbee shi yɛ emli ni ebatsɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ

english: Does the stage of growth affect how my plantain crop reacts to bad weather?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mi-plantains lɛ daa lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli lɛ he?

english: Yes, growth stage matters a lot. Vegetative plantains without fruit bend more easily and recover from wind, but once a plantain matures and holds heavy fruit, its flexibility decreases, making it very sensitive to weather changes.
ga: Hɛɛ, dalɛ fã lɛ he miihia waa. Plantains ni bɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛhe jɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ plantains lɛ dara ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii lɛ, amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over even when there is no flooding on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? Nu afua ko bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Flooding or excess soil water is rarely the cause of plantains breaking. Stems break mainly from the combination of high top weight from fruit bunches and sudden strong wind pushes, even on dry soil.
ga: Nu afua loo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ atswa. Tso lɛ yibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwie shi kɛjɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswa trukaa lɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli. yɛ shikpɔŋ gbiŋ nɔ po

english: Is there a specific period in the life of a plantain plant when I should watch out for stem damage?
ga: Ani bei komɛi yɛ plantain shihilɛ mli ni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: The most critical period is right after the plant flowers and forms fruit bunches until harvest. During these weeks, the stem carries maximum weight and is most vulnerable to damage if a dry spell is followed by sudden strong winds.
ga: Be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji beni tso lɛ ewo fɔfɔi ni efee aduawai akui kɛyashi be mli ni akpaa lɛ. Yɛ otsi nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baatere muji ni fe fɛɛ ni ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ akɛ ebaafite kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa trukaa nyiɛ sɛɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi.

english: What is the difference between urea and other fertilizers I see in the market?
ga: Urea kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi ni minaa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Urea is a strong nitrogen fertilizer that helps your crops grow dark green, healthy leaves quickly, while mixed fertilizers like NPK supply nitrogen alongside other food that builds strong roots and good fruits.
ga: Urea ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK lɛ haa nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No haa shishifãi ni wa kɛ yibii kpakpai baa.

english: I hear farmers talk about giving ammonia to crops—what does ammonia actually do for my plants?
ga: Minu okwaafoi ni miiwie bɔ ni amɛhaa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ammonia lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ammonia yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Ammonia provides a fast supply of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need during their early stages to build strong stems and thick foliage.
ga: Ammonia haa nitrogen ni fa oya. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei yɛ shishijee mli koni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse.

english: Can I dissolve my solid fertilizer in water before giving it to my crops, or must I always put it directly into the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa awo nu mli dani mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii? Aloo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, dissolving fertilizer in water allows plant roots to take in the nutrients faster, but you must mix the right amount so the solution does not become too strong and damage the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ bɔ ni sa afutu mli bɔni afee ni tsofa lɛ akafee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to mix into a bucket of water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mikɛbaafutu yɛ tanki lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You must use recommended weight measurements from an extension officer, because mixing too much fertilizer into a small amount of water creates a thick solution that will burn crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni jɛ o-extension officer lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo futu nu fioo ko mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: If I add more water than required to my fertilizer mixture, will it ruin the fertilizer?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu babaoo fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ fata ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ he Ani ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Adding extra water dilutes the strength of the fertilizer, making it safer for young crops, but if it is watered down too much, your plants will not get enough food to grow well.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu kroko fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi. ni ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei bibii Shi kɛji okɛ nu wo mli babaoo Tso lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should my farm soil be dry or wet when I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo edɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Soil should always be moist when applying fertilizer, because moisture helps dissolve the nutrients so the crop roots can drink them without getting scorched.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ ni amɛshãaa.

english: What time of day is best for me to apply liquid fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Early morning or cool evening is best because the sun is gentle, allowing the soil to hold the moisture so the plant roots can feed without losing water to hot air.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei shishifãi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii ni nu lɛ fiteee yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How often in a season should I give liquid fertilizer to my maize or vegetable crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa loo mi-aduawai lɛ amli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Most crops only need feeding 2 or 3 times during their growing season—usually after planting, during fast growth, and just before flowering.
ga: Tsei babaoo biɔ niyenii 2 loo 3 pɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, beni adu lɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa oya kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi

english: Why did the leaves of my crops turn yellow and dry up after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: This happens when crops receive too much fertilizer or when strong fertilizer touches the roots or stems directly without enough water, causing 'fertilizer burn'.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ shishifãi loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli, ni ekɛ ‘ŋmɔshi nibii ni shãa’ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for fertilizer or if they just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo nu babaoo he miihia amɛ?

english: If the leaves look pale yellow and growth is stunted even when the soil is wet, your plants need fertilizer; if the leaves are wilting but still green, they just need water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji baai lɛ egbo shi amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ Nu kɛkɛ he miihia

english: Why do people recommend planting pear trees or other shade trees together with my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu pear tsei loo tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ? Kɛ mi kookoo lɛ fata he?

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa plants from strong sunlight and retain soil moisture, but they must be properly spaced so they do not compete with cocoa for water and nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Shi esa akɛ gbɛ ni sa ahi jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji koni akatswa kookoo he akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Can I plant any random big tree on my cocoa farm to provide shade?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli trukaa koni maná hulutsoo?

english: No, some trees harbor pests and diseases that attack cocoa, while recommended shade trees improve soil fertility and provide the right amount of filtered light.
ga: Dabi, tsei komɛi hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa kookoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ la ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ abɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If there is too much shade, cocoa trees produce fewer flowers and pods, and the high moisture under the canopy can encourage fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ Cacao tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ahe hewalɛ.

english: Will planting fruit trees mixed with cocoa reduce my final cocoa yield?
ga: Ani aduawai tsei ni akɛ kookoo efutu mli lɛ ni madu lɛ baaha minaagbee kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: If fruit trees are too crowded, they steal sunlight and fertilizer from cocoa, but a few well-managed shade trees actually help cocoa produce consistently over many years.
ga: Kɛji aduawai tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Nakai tsei lɛ baaju hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ kookoo lɛ mli. Shi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni aná kookoo be fɛɛ be yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: When I walk through my farm, why is it important to look down at the ground and not just up at the leaves?
ga: Kɛ miho miŋmɔ lɛ he Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi, shi jeee baai lɛ pɛ?

english: Looking at the ground helps you notice dropped leaves, fallen twigs, insect signs, and soil dryness early, which alerts you to hidden pests or diseases before they spread.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona baai ni egbee shi. niji ni egbee shi Okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kɛjɛ shishijee. ni bɔɔ bo kɔkɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ahe dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Is it helpful or harmful when fallen leaves and small branches cover the ground under my trees?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua loo ebaaye mɔ awui kɛ́ baai lɛ shwie shi ni niji bibii ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ?

english: It is usually helpful because rotting leaves act as natural fertilizer and keep the soil cool, provided the fallen materials are not caused by pests or disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ enɛ he ejaakɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. kɛji akɛ jeee tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai kɛ nibii ni egbee shi lɛ ba.

english: I notice many tiny dry twigs lying on the ground like matchsticks under my cocoa trees; what is happening?
ga: Miyɔse tso nine bibioo ko ni egbi. Mɛi babaoo ka shikpɔŋ tamɔ mats tsei yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi. meni ba?

english: Fallen dry twigs often mean pests like stem borers or mirids are attacking the young branches, causing them to die, snap off, and drop to the floor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni egbi ni egbee shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo branch borers miitutua niji bibii lɛ. ni haa amɛgboiɔ, amɛkuɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: What signs on the farm floor tell me that pests are active in my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ okadi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mi akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fallen chewed leaves, insect droppings, sawdust-like material, and broken dry branch tips on the ground show that insects are actively feeding on your trees.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi, kooloi amli ŋmeii, nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii Kɛ tsei niji ni egbi ni ekumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi miiye otso lɛ waa.

english: How should I use my cutlass around cocoa plants without damaging them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dade abɔle cacao tso he ni mifiteee lɛ?

english: Use your cutlass to clear weeds near the base of the tree carefully, taking care not to scrape the bark or cut shallow roots, which allows diseases to enter.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛjie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okafolɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ loo okafo shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha helai abote mli.

english: Why should I prune back heavy upper branches of shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shade mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming upper shade tree branches allows sunlight to reach the cocoa blossoms so pods can grow, while preventing heavy branches from falling and breaking your cocoa trees.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi ni amɛkumɔ o-cocoa tso lɛ.

english: Which food crops can I plant on my farm that will still survive and produce yield even if rain does not fall well this season?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baahi shi ni ebaawo yibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli po?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpea, sorghum, and millet are very heat and drought-tolerant. They either have deep roots to reach underground moisture or naturally use less water, making them reliable during dry years.
ga: Tsei tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa waa. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ loo amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu fioo pɛ tsu nii. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ afii amli.

english: How can I keep my soil from drying out too fast when there is a long break in rainfall?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?
