english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or crop remnants (mulching) shades the earth from direct hot sun, stopping soil water from evaporating so fast.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite (mulching) awo otsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya waa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die shortly after germinating, even though I planted right after the first rain fell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: The very first rain of the season can be misleading. If it is followed by hot dry days, the top layer of soil bakes and dries out, killing fragile tender roots before they grow deep enough to find moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Kɛji akɛ gbi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baashã ni ebaagbi. Kpata shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛda kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ nu kpe.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tightly to protect themselves from losing water. By exposing less leaf surface to the hot sun and wind, the plant conserves internal moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni nu akaje mli. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la fioo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose during drought to save water and energy. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant and keeps its energy safe in the underground tubers until rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaahi shi ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani amɛwoɔ aduawai?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, severe lack of water, or nutrient shortages. Shade nets or steady watering during heat spells help flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. nu ni faaa waa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ okɛ shade loo nu wo mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of lack of rain or because the soil is poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: When crops lack water, the leaves wilt and dry up from the tips inward across the entire field. If soil nutrients are low, leaves turn yellow in patterns (like between the leaf veins) even when the soil is wet.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ naagbeehei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ (tamɔ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ateŋ) kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together in order to fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and soil water. Overcrowded crops stay thin and weak, producing smaller yields than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with thick green leaves, but fail to produce big tubers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi enyɛŋ ewo ŋmeii wuji loo aduawai.

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen encourages fast leaf and stem growth, but crops need nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to build strong tubers and big fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa oya. Shi tsei he miihia niyenii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Can planting crops like beans together with my maize help my soil stay rich without buying extra fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil and improve maize growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha ŋmãa lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow under intense direct sunlight because young trees cannot handle full heat. Cocoa plants naturally prefer shade from taller plants, which keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli kwraa. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kookoo tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ ashã.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by very small insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and drinking the plant's juices, which distorts the leaves as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, dropping the blooms to save energy for their own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ. ni ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛwala

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the soil does not have enough nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow tall, especially after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Titri lɛ, beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts with maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This provides free natural food for crops like maize planted near them.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I spread dry grass on top of the dry soil around my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, blocks the sun from baking the soil dry, keeps water in the ground longer, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cuttings to plant for good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Good cassava cuttings should come from the middle section of healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, with thick stems and visible, undamaged buds ready to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse ni anaa jogbaŋŋ, ni efiteee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ teŋ.

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, and if left untended early on, they will starve the young crop seedlings before they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Ni kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ mra lɛ Amɛbaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha wɔkɛto he koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can spread out to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant send energy down to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha edumɔwui lɛ adara.

english: Why do pests attack my young cocoa trees more than the bigger, mature trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ fe mi-cacao tsei wuji ni eda lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and tender leaves that are very easy for insects to bite through and feed on. Because young plants are still establishing their roots, pest damage affects them much faster than strong, older trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛha kooloi bibii ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso bibioo lɛ miiwo shishifãi lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ saa tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ ahe oya.

english: Why do small cocoa seedlings wither and die quickly when insects touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ Aaagbi ni amɛgboi oya kɛji kooloi bibii ta he lɛ?

english: Small seedlings have delicate tissue and limited stored energy, so when insects suck their sap or destroy their foliage, the young plant loses its ability to feed itself and dries up quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu nu lɛ loo amɛfite baai lɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: How can I protect my newly planted cocoa trees from insect infestations?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Providing adequate shade, weeding regularly to remove pest hiding spots, and applying approved extension-recommended organic or chemical treatments early on will protect young trees while they establish.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be ni sa baaha Jwɛi lɛ daa koni ejie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ mra akɛ akɛbaatsa nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny insects to gather on my cocoa plants and destroy them?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ?

english: Insects gather on cocoa plants because the trees produce sweet sap, tender shoots, and pods that provide food and shelter. Warm and humid farm conditions also allow these pests to reproduce very fast.
ga: Kplukai kpɛtɛɔ kookoo tsei ahe ejaakɛ tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ni haa niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ hu haa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fɔɔ oya waa.

english: How do pests move from one infected tree to infest my entire cocoa farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko jɛ tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ mli kɛba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Pests can fly, crawl, or be carried by wind, farm animals, and even on a farmer's clothes or tools from an infected tree to healthy ones nearby.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afã, akɔlɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa amɛ kɛya. Kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo okwaafonyo lɛ atadei loo edɛŋdadei po anɔ, kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyashi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if the insects on my farm are actively damaging my crop or just resting on the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛhiɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Damaging insects leave visible signs such as chewed leaves, small puncture holes, sticky sap oozing from stems, or stunted growth, whereas harmless insects usually leave no visible marks.
ga: Kplukai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shĩɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni atsɔ mli, ŋmeii bibii ni afolɔ mli, nu ni shwieɔ shi ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ. loo dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeee mɔ awui lɛ shiii okadi ko ni anaa lɛ,.

english: What is the best way to prevent pests from damaging my cocoa crop before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite mi-cacao tsei lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Combining regular farm sanitation—like pruning dead branches and clearing weeds—with timely harvesting and targeted pest sprays creates an environment where insects cannot easily survive.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa tamɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ awo mli Ha ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be naa kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ afee ekome. Ehaa shihilɛ ko baa ni kooloi nyɛŋ ahi shi mlɛo.

english: Why are the cocoa beans inside my pods getting destroyed before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpãtãa cocoa yibii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Insects often pierce the outer shell of young pods to lay eggs or feed on the sweet pulp inside. This allows fungi and bacteria to enter, which rots and ruins the cocoa beans before harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ asɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛwo ŋmeii loo amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abote mli. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods look normal on the outside but have ruined beans on the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ daa kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi emli lɛ egbo?

english: Certain pests pierce very small holes into young pods that heal over on the surface as the pod grows, but the damage or disease introduced inside continues to destroy the developing beans secretly.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ekomɛi woɔ bu bibii. kɛboteɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ mli Enɛ laajeɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ. Shi mligbɛ nibii ni efite loo hela fiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ lolo.

english: Does pest damage on cocoa pods affect the final price I get when I sell my beans?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ saa naagbee jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛ́ mihɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, pest damage spoils the quality, color, and weight of the cocoa beans. Buyers pay less for poor-quality or insect-damaged beans because they produce bad chocolate.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ saa bɔ ni kookoo yibii lɛ hi ha, amɛhe su kɛ amɛtsiimɔ he. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kɛha ŋmeii ni ehiii loo ni kooloi efite ni haa tsokolate ni ehiii baa lɛ.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more heavily when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering and fruiting stages are sensitive because plants direct high amounts of energy and nutrients there, making them soft, sweet, and very attractive to pests. Protecting your crop during this sensitive period is critical to securing your final harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli wa waa ejaakɛ tso lɛ haa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ, ni ŋmeii sumɔɔ amɛ waa. Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ooobu yɛ nɛkɛ be ni mli wa nɛɛ mli lɛ he miihia waa kɛha onaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings die so quickly after bugs bite them compared to mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya beni ŋmeii emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young plants are at their most vulnerable stage because their stems and root systems are small. Just like a human baby, a little damage from pests can kill a seedling, whereas an older, stronger plant can survive and recover from minor pest damage.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa. Tamɔ gbekɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Nibii bibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ amli.

english: What makes pests suddenly show up on my farm when I am about to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa beni miitao makpa nii lɛ?

english: Pests are naturally drawn to crops that are ripening because of the high sugars and nutrients present. They often arrive right at this sensitive stage to feed before the crop is harvested.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai gbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ sugar kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛshɛɔ nɛkɛ be ni mli wa nɛɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii dani akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer asks me to do scouting on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛ́ extension nitsulɔ ko bi mi koni makwɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Scouting simply means regularly walking through your field to inspect plants, look under leaves, and check stems for early signs of bugs, eggs, or diseases before they cause major damage.
ga: Scouting tsɔɔ akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa koni oyakwɛ tsei lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi. ni okwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli kɛji kooloi, ŋmeii, loo hela ko yɛ mli mra dani amɛfite waa.

english: How often should I walk through my field to check for crop insects?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ kɛji kooloi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: You should walk through and inspect your field at least once or twice every week. Checking regularly helps you spot bugs or disease signs early while the crops are still healthy and easy to protect.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ mli ni okwɛ oyale lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ he daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona kooloi bibii loo hela he okadii mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni abuɔ he mlɛo.

english: What specific things should I look out for when inspecting my crops for pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Look for holes in leaves, changes in leaf color, sticky residues, tiny eggs on the underside of leaves, and insects hiding around plant stems or flowers.
ga: Taomɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli. Baai lɛ ahe su tsakemɔ, nibii ni kpɛtɛɔ he, wɔji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi, kɛ kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ shishi loo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe

english: Is spraying chemical medicine the only way to protect my farm from pests?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: No, chemical spray is not the only way. You can use Integrated Pest Management (IPM), which combines good weeding, crop rotation, hand-picking bugs, and using natural predators or traps alongside minimal chemicals to control pests safely.
ga: Dabi, jeee tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii. Obaanyɛ okɛ Integrated Pest Management (IPM) ni kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ kpakpa feɔ ekome lɛ atsu nii. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Nine ni akɛbuaa kooloi bibii anaa kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ loo tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛye kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to clear weeds around my farm to control insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie jwɛi ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ? Okwaafoi ni akɛbaakudɔ kooloi bibii?

english: Weeds act as hiding places and secondary food sources for pests. Removing weeds destroys the insects' shelter and forces them away from your farm, especially when your main crops are young.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ amɛhe kɛ niyenii ni ji enyɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ kooloi ashihilɛhei ni eshwieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ beni otso titri lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why are pests still destroying my crops even after I sprayed pest medicine a few weeks ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ otsii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ.

english: Chemicals wear off over time due to rain or heat, and new pest eggs can hatch after spraying. Regular field checks are necessary so you can apply control methods again if a new generation of pests arrives during a sensitive crop stage.
ga: Tsofai fiteɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ nugbɔ loo dɔlɛ hewɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmeii heei baanyɛ afɔ yɛ be mli ni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ ŋmɔ mli daa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yinɔ hee ko ba yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ be mli lɛ

english: Can planting different crops together help keep bad insects away from my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmeii gbohii akaje miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting certain crops together—known as intercropping—can help. For example, strong-smelling crops like onions or pepper can confuse or repel bad insects, keeping your main crops safer without relying solely on chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa, tamɔ sabolai loo shito, baanyɛ afutu loo ashwie kooloi fɔji. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ afee shweshweeshwe ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai pɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Nitrogen moves to the newer top leaves when there is not enough in the soil, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ yaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ha baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients that the crop relies on, and it allows soil pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in high numbers over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses carried by aphids, which stops normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni aphids kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop harvest to drop even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they steal the fertilizer nutrients, water, and sunlight before your main crops have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them from heat and conserve soil moisture until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe tsɔi, koni amɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aaawa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for root space, underground water, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi ahe he, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to expose their leaves to direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from heat and rot, allowing the plant to feed bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato vines need their leaves to be exposed to direct sunlight to feed the plant. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fitemɔ he. This allows the plant to grow larger tubers underground.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and causes rot-inducing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruits during heatwaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ shwie fɔfɔi ni yibii bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing pollination from happening so the unpollinated flowers simply drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen ni no hewɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crop stems help them during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli?

english: Covering the ground around crops, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct sun, preventing moisture from evaporating quickly and keeping root temperatures cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni eha shishifãi lɛ amli adɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Giving the plant nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps it green up and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen fertilizer loo compost ha otsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or poor nutrients. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil covered helps the tree retain its flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa ni enine shɛɔ nɔ Shading kɛ mulching yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and light to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ mli tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why does my harvested maize get hot and sweaty when I store it in a closed sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ latsaa kɛ́ akɛto kotokui ni aŋã mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grains are living seeds that release moisture. If you bag them before they are fully dry, water builds up inside the sack, generating heat that leads to mold and spoilage.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji okɛwo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Nu baabua ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: How do tiny insects get inside my tightly sealed bags of dried beans?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote mi-baagi ni mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ewo mli lɛ mli?

english: Most storage insects lay invisible eggs on the crop while it is still growing in the field. Once you put the beans in bags, the warm environment allows the eggs to hatch into bugs that feed on the stored grains.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ateŋ babaoo woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Beni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ kotoku lɛ mli Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to put into storage bags safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli shweshweeshwe?

english: Well-dried grain should be hard and make a sharp cracking sound when you bite it. If it feels soft or indents under your teeth, it still holds too much water and needs more sun drying.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni etswa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ. Kɛji enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo ŋmei ko yɛ onyanyɔŋ shishi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ lolo ni hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I do not harvest them after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects in wet soil without draining, air cannot reach the roots. This lack of air causes underground cassava tubers to rot rapidly.
ga: Beni nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why didn't some of the maize seeds I buried in the ground sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛko lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep for the shoot to reach the top, if the soil is too dry, or if soil pests eat the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables grow faster when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with essential nutrients and improves its ability to hold water, giving young plant roots a steady supply of food and moisture to grow quickly.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu daa koni amɛdara oya.

english: How can I get my maize field to produce double the amount of grain it usually yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmaa babaoo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: To double your harvest, you need to use quality improved seeds, space your plants properly so they don't fight for sunlight, apply fertilizer at the right stage of growth, and clear weeds early before they steal nutrients from your corn.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nɔ ni fa fe nakai lɛ shii enyɔ Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii. Too tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ lɛ akaye akaŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa ni edaa lɛ mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ o-corn lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small and woody even though the leaves on top look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ po.

english: When cassava plants get too much nitrogen in the soil or are planted too close together, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and big leaves instead of storing food down in the tubers.
ga: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen in the soil or are planted too close together. They devote all their energy to the tall stems and large, growing leaves. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ahi oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when plants suffer from irregular watering, or when small pests attack the delicate stem. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps fruits set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. When plants experience irregular watering problems or when small pests attack delicate stems. Keeping the soil evenly moist and shaded during periods of extreme heat helps the fruit to establish.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nutrient boost they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my farmland dry out and crack so quickly just a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter to act like a sponge. Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) and adding compost keeps moisture trapped in the soil for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha etsu nii tamɔ sponji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha kɛbɔle Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha onibii ahe, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no nuts inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods usually happen when the soil lacks calcium, a mineral the plant needs specifically to fill out its pods. Applying agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil during planting helps form solid, healthy nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji shika tsuru ni he hiaa tsei pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso ashwishwɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds close together if I want to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin and weak plants. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy as fruit bunches grow. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden Y-sticks (propping) and piling dirt high around the base of the plant (earthing up) keeps them firmly in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ (bracing) kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ (grounding) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my farm during the first month of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are small and weak, so fast-growing weeds can easily overpower them by stealing their water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks lets your young crops establish strong roots without competition.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aye jwɛi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are a sign of pest caterpillars, such as Fall Armyworm, eating the tender growing leaves. Inspecting your farm regularly and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract early will stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei ko, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ eba. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo mli mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for growing cocoa before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Good cocoa land should have deep, fertile soil that drains water easily so the roots do not rot. A trained extension officer checks soil depth, texture, and slope to ensure trees can grow strong roots and receive proper moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ oya koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. Nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, ehiɛ kɛ eshishigbɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná nu ni sa.

english: Is it better to raise cocoa seedlings on my own farm or get them from an outside nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookwɛ kookoo dumɔwui yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli loo oookwɛ amɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Raising seedlings on your farm saves money and ensures they are adapted to your soil, but getting certified hybrid seedlings from approved nurseries guarantees higher yields and stronger resistance to diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni oookwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa okɛ shika baa shi, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ana dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba ni helai hu nyɛŋ ashi amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I just plant seeds taken straight from cocoa pods I bought at the local market?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is not recommended because market pods may carry hidden diseases or come from low-yielding trees. Certified seeds from agricultural offices produce healthier trees that give much more cocoa.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baanyɛ ahi jarayeli pods lɛ amli loo ejɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa baa, ni amɛwoɔ kookoo babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that lose water quickly in direct sun. They behave like infant crops and require shade from taller plants like plantains during their first few years to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei bibii ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: How far apart should I plant cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees are usually planted about 3 meters apart (10 feet by 10 feet). Proper spacing prevents trees from fighting for sunlight and soil nutrients, while allowing good air movement to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kookoo tsei aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ akashiɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava together with my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava kɛ cacao tsei heei?

english: Yes, plantains and cassava provide essential shade for young cocoa and give you food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature. However, avoid planting too close to prevent food crops from choking the cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain kɛ cassava haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo bibii. and provide you with food and income while waiting for the cocoa to ripen. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ he koni niyenii tsei lɛ akamɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's natural way of saving water during dry periods. Reducing its leaves helps the tree conserve moisture in the trunk and roots until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni kookoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ eshishi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older, traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or lack of pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping soil moist with shade and mulch helps flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná he sɛɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young cocoa seedlings so much in the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cocoa seedlings and steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping the area around young cocoa clean allows the seedling to use all available food to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe kookoo dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la kɛ sũ mli niyenii. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Koo tso lɛ he tsemɔ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I treat my yam setts with a liquid mix before putting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ewo mli lɛ afutu dani mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Treating or conditioning yam setts before planting coats them in protective medicine that stops soil insects and fungi from rotting the seed yam before it can sprout strong roots.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa sweet potato loo afee lɛ fɛfɛo dani adu lɛ, ekɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my cassava cuttings when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted right after the soil receives enough steady rain to stay moist, allowing the stems to grow roots quickly without drying out under the hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa koni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Is it bad if I plant yams on the exact same piece of land where I harvested yams last year?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, growing yams on the same spot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows yam pests to build up; rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores the earth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa sweet potato mli ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes high-quality breeder seeds better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔlɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Breeder seeds are carefully bred by experts to grow uniformly, produce bigger yields, and resist local diseases, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and quality over generations.
ga: Nileelɔi kwɛɔ fɔlɔi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛdara daa. ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpakpa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli.

english: Does it really matter how deep I push my seeds into the soil when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ mihaa kɛ́ midu lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep prevents the young shoot from reaching sunlight before running out of energy, while planting too shallow leaves them exposed to hungry birds and drying heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mli tsɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ dani amɛhewalɛ lɛ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ aná amɛ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why does my farm soil dry up and turn hard like rock, and how can a soil conditioner help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ tɛ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Soil hardens when it loses moisture and organic content; a soil conditioner acts like a sponge, helping the earth hold onto water and nutrients so roots can easily expand.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I be sure that a new fertilizer treatment recommended for my soil is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfee mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can test the treatment on a small section of your farm first and compare it to an untreated patch; healthy dark green leaves and faster growth in the treated area prove the method works.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka tsofafeemɔ lɛ okwɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ No sɛɛ lɛ okɛto wolo ni atsuuu he nii lɛ he. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ oya yɛ he ni atsa lɛ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off without turning into full peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛtsɔko pepper ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they face stress from extreme dry heat, lack of water, or insufficient nutrients, causing the plant to save energy instead of forming fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the food crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally built to steal soil food, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is needed to give your crops room to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Which is why clearing it first is essential to allow your crops to thrive.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left from older leaves up to the new growth at the top.
ga: Yellow leaves on the underside usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. When the nitrogen in the soil runs out The plant transfers what little is left from the old leaves to the new growth on the shoot.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots decay, that natural food remains in the dirt to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshishifãi lɛ egbo. Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover fertilizer with soil after applying it near my crops instead of leaving it on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe beni mikɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, moŋ fe ni mashi yɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving fertilizer uncovered allows the hot sun to evaporate the nutrients into the air, or rain to wash it away. Covering it with a little dirt locks the food in place right where the roots can drink it.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Aloo ha nugbɔ anɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ okɛ muji ni mli tseee ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ ahi he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and cool moisture, acting like an umbrella until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants stay small and produce weak harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. If weeds are left to grow, they steal the food and water your crops need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Ebaaju niyenii ni ebaaha onibii lɛ nu koni amɛya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves are a sign that tiny insects like thrips or aphids are hiding underneath and sucking out the plant's sap. This damages the young leaves as they grow and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo aphids, kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baai bibii beni amɛdaraa lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground, making them top-heavy when carrying big bunches of fruit. Strong winds can easily pull up these shallow roots, especially if tiny soil worms have damaged them.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. This makes it heavy when carrying large bunches of fruit. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛɛmɛi baa mlɛo. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ. kpata nakai shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm and water cannot drain away, the roots suffocate in the water, allowing fungi and rot to destroy them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie kɛya lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo yɛ nu lɛ mli. Ha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects to move pollen inside the flower. Without successful pollination or steady water, the plant discards the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ ni bɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination loo nu ni yɔɔ daa bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves dry and healthy, allowing the plant to make maximum food and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants build strong leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the cassava roots under my plants very small even though the leaves above ground look huge and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ, shi.

english: When cassava gets too much water or rich leafy nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and green leaves instead of storing energy in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ baai babaoo lɛ amli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants curl up and turn brown during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water when it is very hot. If they turn brown quickly, small insects might also be sucking the juice out of the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya lɛ Kooloi bibii hu baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when water is un-even. Without regular moisture, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits rotting at the bottom while still growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper aduawai lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when watering is irregular—drying out completely and then getting soaked.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. No ji, ha egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo nu mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like human babies—their leaves burn easily in full sun. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains provides a canopy that protects young cocoa from severe heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow so much faster than the maize and vegetables I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions. They naturally sprout faster to steal light, water, and soil nutrients before your planted crops have a chance to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛju la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dani otso lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni ekwɛ shishifãi lɛ,

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply chemical medicine to my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai awo mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Midday heat makes liquid chemicals evaporate too fast or burn the soft leaves under direct sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo amɛshãa baai bibii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know if my crop needs chemical medicine for pests or if it just needs fertilizer for food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia tsofa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ kɛha niyenii?

english: If leaves are chewed, have holes, or show sticky webs, insects are eating them and need pest control. If leaves look whole but pale, small, or stunted, the plant needs fertilizer for food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashɛreɔ baai lɛ, eyɛ bu loo eyɛ tsɔji ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miiye nakai baai lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, bibii, loo egbɔjɔ lɛ, tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to sprout after I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if their base roots were damaged during digging or if they are planted in hard, unworked soil that prevents new roots from pushing out easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ shishitoo lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni atsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii ni haaa shishifãi heei aje kpo mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: It is best to grow cassava on separate land. Cassava grows bushy leaves and heavy roots that steal sunlight, moisture, and nutrients from young cocoa trees, causing the cocoa to struggle or die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto. Yucca kwɛ̃ɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni juɔ hulu la, fɛ̃i, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ha Cocoa abɔ mɔdɛŋ loo egbo.

english: Why do many farmers plant plantains next to new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade for young cocoa seedlings, protecting delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight while providing shade and moist soil.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa.

english: What kind of crops are safe to plant alongside my new cocoa trees in the first year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu yɛ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ masɛi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Temporary nurse crops like plantain and cocoyam are good choices because they provide soft shade and soil cover without choking the roots of the young cocoa plants.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa lɛ ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛtsiii kookoo tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: How do I decide whether two crops can be planted together or need separate fields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ yɛ he kome loo hei srɔtoi he miihia?

english: You can plant crops together if one helps the other, such as a tall plant shading a delicate seedling. If both crops greedily compete for the same sunlight, soil space, and water, they should be planted on separate fields.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei afee ekome kɛji mɔ kome ye ebua mɔ kroko lɛ, tamɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni haa tso bibioo ko ni waaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji tsei enyɔ kɛ hiɛjoomɔ miitswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ, kɛ nu kome lɛ, Esa akɛ adu tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli.

english: Why do some crops fail to grow well when planted close to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daraaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Crops need sunlight, water, and plant food from the soil to grow. When competing crops are planted too close together, the stronger or faster-growing plant steals these resources, leaving the weaker crop starved.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni he wa loo ni daa oya lɛ baaju nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: How does growing root crops like cassava affect the crops around them?
ga: Te tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ saa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava develops large underground tubers that spread widely in the topsoil, drinking up heavy amounts of water and nutrients while blocking the roots of nearby plants from expanding.
ga: Cassava feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo. Enuɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I plant heavy-feeding crops continuously without planning?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mitee nɔ midu niyenii ni tsii ni mitooo gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ?

english: Heavy-feeding crops rapidly drain the soil of vital nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, leaving the land depleted and incapable of supporting delicate cash crops like cocoa without expensive fertilizers.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ niyenii babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ kookoo nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Is it good practice to plant big timber trees like mahogany mixed into my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsei wuji tamɔ mahogany yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Big timber trees like mahogany grow huge branches and deep roots that can cast too much shade, drain underground water, and make managing or harvesting your cocoa crop very difficult later on.
ga: Tsei wuji tamɔ mahogany lɛ yɛ niji wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa tsɔ. underground drainage Ni enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ oookwɛ loo oookpa o-cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is cocoa considered a difficult crop to establish compared to other food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni aduɔ kɛ akɛtoɔ niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa requires very specific growth conditions, such as the right amount of light, stable moisture, and protection from harsh weather, especially during its young seedling stage.
ga: Cocoa biɔ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni haa edaa, tamɔ la ni sa. hulutsoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli Titri lɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee beaŋ.

english: Do cocoa trees need heavy shade or direct sunshine to thrive?
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Aloo ani hulu la yɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni baaha eda?

english: Young cocoa trees need gentle shade to prevent their delicate leaves from scorching, but as they grow mature and strong, they require more sunlight to flower and yield cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo blɛoo koni baai bibii lɛ akashã. Shi kɛ́ eda kwraa ni ehe wa lɛ Ehe miihia hulu la babaoo koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii aba.

english: Cocoa flowers drop naturally when the tree is stressed by intense heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients, or if tiny pollinating insects called midges are missing from the farm.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollination Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ laaje kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa roots are shallow and cannot reach deep water. Without shade trees and leaf mulch to protect the soil, the dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can take it up.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛyashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Akɛni tsei ni baaha hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ bɛ hewɔ lɛ, Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Trimming extra branches lets light and air flow through the tree. This keeps the farm dry enough to prevent fungal diseases and helps the tree direct its energy into growing large cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli, ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to remove black pods from my cocoa trees immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ojie ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black pods carry a fast-spreading fungal disease. Leaving infected pods on the tree allows rain drops and wind to carry the sickness to healthy pods across your entire farm.
ga: Black pods ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hela aya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are there so many ants crawling on the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ants are usually attracted to a sweet liquid produced by tiny pests like mealybugs or aphids, which hide under the leaves and suck the food out of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids lɛ feɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a plant usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I need to put animal manure on my farm if I am already buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ? Be ni miheɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ momo?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant directly for a short time, but animal manure improves the structure of the soil so it can hold water and nutrients longer during dry spells.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. But animal manure improves soil structure. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Planting cassava stems too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, soil water, and space, resulting in tall thin plants with very small roots underneath.
ga: Yucca tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ ŋwɛi he, ni no haa amɛfeɔ yam tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛlɛ ni shishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and cracks begin to form in the soil around the base of the stem from the tubers swelling below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii ebɔi feemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when there is heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very heavy tops. When heavy rains soften the soil, strong winds can easily pull the shallow root system out of the ground.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu tsii waa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Rain can wash nitrogen away, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks easily fall over when there is a small wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak and fall over if seeds are planted too close together or if the soil lacks potassium. Proper plant spacing and good soil nutrients give the stalks the strength to stand firm.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: How do I choose the best maize seeds so that my farm produces a big harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ koni miŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmãa babaoo?

english: The best seeds are clean, dry, free from insect holes, and bought from approved certified seed sellers. Using saved seeds from your previous harvest often yields less because those seeds lose their strength over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he tse, egbi, ni kooloi ahiɛ bɛ mli. kɛ nihɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa ejaakɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, you can plant both together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the land after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ afee ekome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs end up empty or missing grains at the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo amɛbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Missing grains at the tip happen when the corn plant suffers from lack of water or poor soil nutrients during the flowering stage, preventing all parts of the cob from receiving enough energy to form full grains.
ga: Kernels ni elaaje yɛ naagbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ nu ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ fã fɛɛ fã náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the husk covering the cob turns straw-colored, and the grains become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Hewolo ni ha tso lɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi su. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my maize farm before they spoil my crop?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You should clear weeds at least twice: first within the first two to three weeks after planting when the crops are small, and a second time before the plants start producing flowers and cobs.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2-3 lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ ajeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ shishi.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa.

english: What causes my stored corn to turn into white powder after a few months in the room?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi mitsu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils burrow inside stored corn and eat the grain from the inside out, leaving powder behind. Drying your corn thoroughly and storing it in airtight sacks keeps these insects out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ, ni amɛshiɔ powda yɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmãa lɛ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why does my maize turn moldy and black when I leave it in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize turns moldy if it stays damp or gets rained on while drying on the ground. Raising the corn off the bare ground on raised platforms allows air to flow underneath and dry it safely.
ga: Abɛi baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ awó ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee kpoku ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehaa egbiɔ shweshweeshwe.
