english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. This often happens when the soil lacks organic matter or when heavy rains wash away nutrients, so adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on your farm for too long without draining, the roots drown and rot, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, or shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Providing regular watering at the root level and shade during very hot days helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa kɛ hulutsoo gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rainy season starts late?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and soak the ground deeply rather than planting after the very first light shower, because early dry spells can easily burn young seeds before their roots establish.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa oya lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii lɛ oya dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and very heavy stems. As the fruit bunch grows larger, the plant becomes top-heavy, so propping the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboo stakes keeps it upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii waa. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil extract or recommended pest treatments stops these insects from damaging new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛtsiɔ amɛhe. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Aloo, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie sleeping in the soil for years and germinate instantly when sunlight and rain reach them. Because wild weeds grow faster than farm crops, clearing them while your crops are still young prevents them from stealing water and plant food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji hulu kɛ nugbɔ ba pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ otsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans, cowpeas, and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and trap it inside their roots. When the plants die and decay, that trapped food stays in the soil and feeds the maize crops you plant next.
ga: Beans, cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni okwɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and crooked instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push downward as they swell. If the soil is hard or full of hidden stones, the tuber bends to find an easier path, which is why building tall, soft mounds gives tubers space to grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli be mli ni amɛfuɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ena gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ hewɔ ni gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from older leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. which is essential food for plant growth When plants grow It pulls nitrogen from old leaves to feed growth on new shoots.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-ŋma lɛ mli?

english: The best time to apply early fertilizer is a few weeks after sprouting when plants are knee-high, because this is when roots are ready to take up heavy nutrients for fast growth.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ awo mli mra ji otsii 2-3 yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaná niyenii ni tsii koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and drying up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal attack that spreads quickly in damp, shady, and overly wet weather. Pruning heavy canopy branches helps air flow and reduces moisture buildup.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be, hulutsoo be mli, kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ fe nine mli. Niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young corn leaves with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a hungry caterpillar that feeds on the soft inner leaves of maize. Early spraying with appropriate crop protection chemicals stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Kpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips. Spraying recommended crop protection products removes these pests and stops leaf deformation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa baai lɛ ashishijee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in full sunlight without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Planting plantains alongside provides fast-growing living shade that cools the soil and holds moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui adumɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa wala ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ yaa nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight to capture energy, which helps the plant store food underground and produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil moist and using proper balanced fertilizers prevents blossom drop.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soils because suffocated roots cannot breathe without oxygen in wet ground. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: How do crop protection chemicals help my farm when weeds start competing with my crops?
ga: Te tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ beni jwɛi kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛyeɔ akaŋ lɛ?

english: Crop protection products target unwanted weeds without harming your main crop, ensuring your maize or vegetables do not have to fight with weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ awui. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ kɛ jwɛi awui koni amɛna hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and crisp during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them to shield their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds along the stalk. When planting, these buds must point upward toward the sky so the plant can sprout leaves above ground and build heavy roots below.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu lɛ, esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni tsii aba shishi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋtayaa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers insist that I plant my maize in neat rows with measured spacing instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni anyɛɔ asusuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Planting in straight lines also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ hu haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ jwɛi, awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpaa nii oya babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell before the real rainy season begins. If seeds sprout during this dry pause, the young seedlings will wither and die from lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: What is causing holes in the leaves and center whorls of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of maize. Applying recommended control treatments early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ tsu nii mra Ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering puts heavy stress on tomato plants, causing them to shed their flowers to save energy rather than spending resources on growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden poles to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei ahe tsɔi koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which helps the plant direct energy downward into growing larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato on the exact same piece of land where I harvested them last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops from the same family share the same diseases and soil pests. Planting them in the same spot continuously allows soil diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli lɛ yɛ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komekomei. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main mother plant. Removing excess shoots ensures all nutrients go into producing a larger, heavier cluster of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ plantain akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower part of the plant usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early helps the plant stay green and form full cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri ni haa eŋɔli lɛ daa. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra. Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ cob.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water so the root underground stays alive. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will grow fresh leaves and keep feeding the tubers.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi lolo. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei baaba ni abaaya nɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as shade umbrellas, protecting the delicate cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. The seedlings grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as shade. Buu kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni efee hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When the leaves and vines turn yellow and start to dry up on their own, it shows the plant has finished storing energy underground, meaning the yam tuber is mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi momo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa, ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get steady water, which stresses the plant. Watering consistently at the roots during flowering prevents this heat stress.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Nu ni oooha amɛshishifãi lɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo haomɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin instead of strong when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight for sunlight and stretch upward too fast to reach the light. Giving them proper spacing lets sunlight reach the stems, helping them grow strong and produce better yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe baawo ŋwɛi oya tsɔ ni enyɛ eshɛ la lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up into small wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil solution helps control these pests so the leaves can open up and grow healthily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry quickly even after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure, which works like a sponge to hold water. Adding organic manure improves soil texture so it retains moisture longer for plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo kooloi afɔfɔi ni fiteɔ. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa nu hiɔ shi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Maize consumes the same specific nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the land weak over time. Rotating maize with beans or cowpeas restores fertility because legumes add nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp, and bushy farms. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunshine and fresh air stops the fungus from destroying the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this stored nutrient, saving you money on artificial fertilizer and giving you better yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nɛkɛ niyenii ni ato nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the young shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that burrows into the center of the maize plant to eat soft leaves. Spraying early with neem leaf extract or recommended safe chemicals before the plant blossoms can stop them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ mli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akpa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtãmɔ.

english: Why does that purple-flowered witchweed (Striga) make my sorghum and maize stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni ji purple witchweed (striga) lɛ haa mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to the roots of your crop under the ground. It steals water and nutrients meant for your crop, effectively starving the plant from the inside out.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves as a survival trick to save water during long dry spells. The plant goes to sleep to protect the roots underground, and as soon as the rains return, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava baa shwiemɔ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Tso lɛ wɔɔ koni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and bright light, which scorch their young leaves and dry out their stems. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to act as leafy umbrellas during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la he waa. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my vegetable crops stop producing fruits and develop spots when there is too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo kɛ amɛshweremɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain keeps the soil soaked, which drowns crop roots by cutting off air and creates warm, damp conditions where fungal diseases easily spread on leaves and blossoms.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Fungal hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ oya.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of putting energy into making peppers, they stretch upward to fight for light, resulting in tall, weak plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee chili Moŋ lɛ, ekpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛwuu kɛha la lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Ensuring consistent watering and protecting flowers from sap-sucking pests keeps the blossoms on the plant so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua tso lɛ. Ehe miihia ni aha tsei lɛ nu daa ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ ahe. Ebaaha fɔfɔii akpɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot usually starts when tubers get bruised during digging or are exposed to hot direct sun right after harvest. Bacteria and fungi enter through the bruised skin, especially if stored in a warm room without fresh airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato fitemɔ jeɔ shishi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbo yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Muawai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai boteɔ hewolo ni etse lɛ mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yellow and curling leaves on cassava usually mean the plant has cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your crop healthy and ensure a good harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen inside the blossoms, causing them to fall off before fruit can form. Giving the plants light shade and watering near the roots early in the morning helps protect the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Hã amɛgbee shi dani amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ ni okɛ nu wo mli yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I leave wide space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food to grow strong and produce large ears of corn.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa toi agboi afeemɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die if I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa creates a safe cover that retains soil moisture and protects the young trees until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shi tsei wuji koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Ehaa nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its strength before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grew poorly in the previous season, or if their leaves look pale green or yellowish instead of dark green, your soil is likely low on nutrients. Weak weed growth and hard, dry soil are also signs that the land needs manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli loo kɛji ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni edaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but crops like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally put good nutrients back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating maize with these crops restores soil fertility naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ niyenii kpakpai kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abɛi ni akɛduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Ani mi-plantain shishifãi lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ aba?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots—called suckers—is important because too many stems attached to one root compete for food. Leaving only two or three strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to grow thick stems and heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifã kome he lɛ yɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse kɛ plantains babaoo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my food crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local conditions, so they absorb rainwater and soil food much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: While you can save seeds, seeds taken from high-yielding hybrid maize often produce weaker plants with much smaller harvests in the second year. Buying certified seeds each season gives you the strongest plants and the highest yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ ohere dumɔwui lɛ ayiwala moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii fioo kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha oná tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact time when my yam tubers are mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn brown. This shows that the plant has finished storing energy in the ground and the yam tuber has reached its full size.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ni sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ amɛhe momo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink, causing them to scorch.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. ni kɛ shãa henumɔ baa

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the leaf tip down the center in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is low on nitrogen. The plant moves its remaining nitrogen up to feed the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ, ni efee V su. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when it rains too heavily for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for days, oxygen gets blocked, creating conditions for fungal rot to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Abaatsi oxygen lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow better and give bigger tubers when I stake them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ tswa lɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need height to spread their leaves. Staking gets the leaves off the ground and exposes them to sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more energy to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when temperatures get too high or when water is low. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fertilization from happening.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ faaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ aba mli

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the topsoil every year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every extra sucker growing at the base competes with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing excess suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to develop a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ tso titri ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Sucker ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Curled and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf sap, or by viruses carried by these insects. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, making it shrink and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look very healthy with green leaves but fail to produce any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Insect pests such as flower thrips often attack cowpea plants right when flowers begin to form. They destroy the tiny flower buds before they can open and form pods, even while the rest of the plant looks healthy.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ flower thrips Bei pii lɛ, amɛtutuaa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi amɛfee pɛ. Amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Dani ebaagbele ni efee pod Eyɛ mli akɛ fãi krokomɛi Tsei lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Weeds have faster-growing root systems than most crops. When fertilizer is applied, weeds absorb the nutrients and water first, effectively starving your crops and blocking sunlight from reaching them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya fe tsei babaoo. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, amɛmɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts most of its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and if you allow too many suckers to grow around one stem, they compete for root space and anchor poorly in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees dry up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under intense sunlight without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to protect them and keep the surrounding air humid.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni tsei loo plantains ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ amɛhe. Koni ebu kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he ni eha edɔ

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts on the same plot before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil to feed nitrogen-hungry crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Nɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is getting too weak to support a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baawo?

english: Signs of weak soil include crops that turn pale green, thin stems, slow growth, and hard soil that crusts over easily after rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni feɔ eŋɔli, tsei bibii, amɛdalɛ blɛoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and white powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni powda yɛŋ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf whorl, which damages the plant's growing point if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular or the soil dries out completely.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haaa tsei akwɛ̃.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which can dry up the soil and kill young germinating seeds before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I water them in the early morning or late afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane mli?

english: Early morning watering is best because the soil absorbs moisture before the hot afternoon, and the leaves dry quickly, preventing fungal diseases from growing overnight.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni baai lɛ baagbi oya Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Why are the young cocoa trees on my farm turning brown and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without temporary shade plants like plantains to protect them, the strong sun scorches their delicate leaves and quickly dries out the soil moisture around their roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high off the ground instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves so they can capture maximum sunlight to produce food for the crop. Leaving vines on damp soil causes leaves to get shaded out, catch fungal diseases easily, and yield much smaller tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ fungal helai baa mɔ nɔ ni ehaa yitso bibioo kwraa

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, which is usually caused by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: What is causing the small holes in my maize leaves and the powdery dirt inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant where they eat the soft leaf tissues and leave behind droppings that look like coarse sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants look twisted, yellow, and much smaller than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni eyɛ bibioo kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stems for planting. The virus starves the plant of energy, leading to stunted leaves and very thin, weak tubers.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛduɔ nii anɔ. Virus haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni bulbs lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa.

english: This is Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, shaded, and humid conditions. Excess shade and unpruned branches trap moisture on the pods, allowing the fungus to infect them.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fungal hela.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips in a V-pattern is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant moves its limited nitrogen supply to feed the newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Abuɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V su mli lɛ akɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts around the root zone, which can burn and severely damage the plant roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever a moderate storm or wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots holding up heavy stems and fruit bunches. If planted too shallowly or in poor soil lacking potassium, the root system cannot anchor the weight of the tree against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni fiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso lɛ muji lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomato fruits turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is forming. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between very wet and very dry, preventing steady calcium uptake.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni egbi waa teŋ. Etsiɔ calcium ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ naa be fɛɛ be

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen transferred from one flower to another to form pods. In nature, tiny insects called midges do this work, but if there aren't enough insects around, many flowers dry up and fall off without producing any cocoa.
ga: Ehe miihia ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya fɔfɔi kroko nɔ koni efee pods. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔ nɛɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛjieee kookoo ko kwraa kpo.

english: Is hand pollination real, and how can it help my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani nine nɔ pollin lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools or hands. Doing this guarantees that flowers get pollinated, which can significantly increase the number of pods on your tree compared to relying only on wild insects.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko loo nine nɔ. Nakai feemɔ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baawo ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Kɛ akɛto kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemicals when my cocoa trees are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on beneficial tiny insects for natural pollination. Spraying harsh chemicals during flowering kills these helpful insects, leaving your flowers unpollinated and reducing your total pod harvest.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa pod ni akpaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better to clear weeds using a motorized weed cutter instead of my traditional cutlass?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baajie jwɛi lɛ moŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ?

english: Motorized weed cutters clear land much faster and require far less physical strength than cutlasses. They cut weeds evenly close to the ground without tiring you out, helping you maintain larger areas of land in much less time.
ga: Motor ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ajie he ko oya ni ehe ehiaaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo fe tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ. Amɛfolɔ jwɛi lɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. kɛfata he ni ehaaa otɔ lɛ Ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa hei wuji yɛ be fioo ko mli.

english: How can using modern farm machines help get young people interested in cocoa farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oblahii kɛ oblayei ni amɛná kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miishɛɛ?

english: Traditional farming with cutlasses and hoes requires intense physical labor that deters many youth. Modern machines speed up hard labor like weeding, spraying, and land preparation, making farming less exhausting and more attractive to younger generations.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔ ni akɛ dade kɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni tsii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ, ni no tsiɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei babaoo anaa. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei haa nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ yaa oya. Ehaa okwaayeli lɛ haaa mɔ he ajɔ lɛ, ni ehaa yinɔ hee lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: Will using motorized tools on my land damage the soil or my cocoa tree roots?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛshishifãi?

english: Handheld motorized tools like motorized weeders are lightweight and cut weeds above the ground surface without disturbing the protective topsoil or breaking the shallow feeding roots of cocoa trees.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ he waaa ni amɛfoɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛgbalaaa sũ ni buɔ he lɛ nɔ loo amɛfiteee kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees struggle and turn yellow when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally grow under the shade of taller trees and cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Sunburn damages their leaves, which is why they need shade plants like plantains during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ fiteɔ ebaa lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni amɛhe hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark, and crowded conditions. Cutting away unnecessary branches lets sunlight and air in, keeping the tree dry and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne kroko ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches that waste the tree's energy. By cutting them away, the cocoa tree sends all its food and water directly to developing pods and healthy flowers.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni haa tso lɛ he waaa lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Kɛtsɔ cacao tso lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ fɛɛ majeɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural way cocoa trees save water during dry spells. Having fewer leaves reduces water loss, allowing the tree to survive through the dry season until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger shade trees or intercropping with plantains provides essential shade and keeps moisture in the soil so the tender cocoa plants can grow without getting scorched.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo loo ni akɛ plantains adu amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ adara ni shãaa amɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves developing ragged holes and small green pellets inside the central stem funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ stem cone lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the growing shoots of maize plants. Early detection and applying recommended bio-pesticides or spraying early in the morning when caterpillars are active helps protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ mra ni akɛtsu nii. Aloo kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, ani gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds (nodes) pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down delays root growth, causes weak stem development, and drastically lowers your yield of tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. ni eha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi waa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the foliage so the leaves catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the crop. This encourages the underground tubers to grow much larger and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛdara babaoo, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up tightly and stop producing good fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibii kpakpai womɔ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is typically a viral disease spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves. Controlling whiteflies early, removing infected plants immediately, and planting disease-resistant seeds helps keep the crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi bibii amli kɛbaa. ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ Early Whitefly Control Jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei momo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal strain that thrives in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air flow through your farm, along with removing infected pods promptly, stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ duŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I plant suckers with broad leaves instead of the ones with narrow leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ panicles bibii beni miduɔ ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ nɔ ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Narrow-leaved 'sword suckers' have strong underground stems packed with energy, leading to vigorous growth and heavy bunches. Broad-leaved 'water suckers' lack strong reserves and grow slowly, yielding smaller fruit.
ga: Swordsucker’ ni baai lɛ mli etse lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Ekɛ dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii baa. ‘Nu mli tsei’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips down the center of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center rib of leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the root zone helps the crop regain its rich green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle sũ lɛ he. He ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yɔɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ toi ni mli wa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off primarily due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce only stems instead of fruit. Regular watering during dry spells helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii pɛ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready to dig up from underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can test by pulling a sample plant; if the insides of the pods have developed dark brown or black markings on the inner shell, the harvest is ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso ko ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ eshɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees or plants like plantain to protect them from intense direct sunlight and heat. Without shade, the young leaves burn and the plant dries out quickly before its roots can grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ baashã ni tso lɛ baagbi oya dani shishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a virus spread by tiny flies called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings is the best way to prevent this from ruining your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing whorl of the maize plant to eat tender leaves. Catching them early with proper spraying or natural remedies prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli tsamɔ nɔ lɛ, abaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make the maize crop grown after them produce better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ beni ewo yibii kpakpai sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth and acts as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants experience heat stress, which prevents the flowers from pollinating properly. Without pollination, the plant drops the dried flowers to conserve its energy and water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛ fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why is it necessary to cut extra branches and leaves off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he ni ashɛrɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ ashwie lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the cocoa tree canopy. This keeps the tree dry, preventing damp fungal diseases like black pod from spreading, while encouraging the tree to direct food to its pods.
ga: Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa. Kɛfata he lɛ, ekanyaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii amaje pod lɛ.

english: Why does that purple-flowered weed keep attaching to my maize roots and causing the maize to stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ purple flower weed lɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmã shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa mi ŋmã lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: That weed is called Striga (or witchweed), and it is a parasite that attaches directly to the roots of maize to steal water and food. Rotating your field with non-cereal crops like soybean helps break its life cycle.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Striga (loo abɛi jwɛi) ni eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee ŋmaa, tamɔ soybean tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, efiteɔ amɛshihilɛ gbɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper crops very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and small peppers. Crowded plants also trap moisture, which leads to fast-spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or turn moldy after putting it in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miifite loo miifite beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it is put away while still holding too much moisture. Grain must be completely dried in the sun until hard before storing so that mold fungi and bacteria cannot grow inside the barn.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted when I plant them in hard, unworked soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfiteɔ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft earth to expand easily under the ground. Mound building or deep tillage softens the soil so the tuber can expand downwards smoothly without meeting hard rocks or compacted dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi mlɛo. Gɔji ni aaafee loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ni amɛkɛ tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekpeee.

english: Why are the tiny cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shrinking before they grow into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, which is a fungal infection, or natural cherelle wilt where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot feed. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and spraying at the right time helps save your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela loo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tso lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fa fe nine ni nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees look scorched and brown like fire touched them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: That damage is usually caused by sap-sucking insects called capsids or akate. They attack young shoots and stems during warm weather, which makes the plant tissue die and turn brown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo akates lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa. Amɛtutuaa tsei bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso mli fãji gboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting new cocoa seedlings before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ midu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔmɔ?

english: If you plant the improved hybrid cocoa varieties, they usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties can take 4 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu cocoa hybrids ni atsake lɛ Bei pii lɛ Amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ he.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to produce plenty of flowers during some months but very few during others?
ga: Mɛni haa mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi amɛwoɔ fioo kwraa yɛ ekrokomɛi amli?

english: Flowering changes with the weather seasons. The start of the rainy season triggers heavy flowering because the tree gets enough water, while extreme dry heat forces the tree to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii baa be mli ni tsei lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, latsaa ni mli egbi waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and lose their leaves during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and need protection from hot sun. Without taller shade trees to block direct light and retain moisture in the soil, the dry wind and heat will scorch the leaves and stunt the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ afee shoo.

english: Will cutting off some branches from my cocoa tree hurt the tree or make it produce more fruit?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaaha ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning dead or overcrowded branches actually helps the tree produce more. It opens up the tree so sunlight reach all parts, allows fresh air to blow through to prevent fungal growth, and directs tree food into forming pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Abaagbele tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ naa. ni ekwɛɔ niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli kɛyaa ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm to harvest while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ teŋ koni makpa be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa. Cassava is a heavy feeder that takes away water and nutrients from the soil, which will compete with and weaken your young cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ. Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaye akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is weak and needs fertilizer to help my crops grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, leaves turn light green or yellow instead of deep green, stem growth becomes slow, and trees produce very few flowers or small pods even when rain falls regularly.
ga: Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio, ni tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii fioo komɛi, kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa po.

english: Why must I heap my freshly harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days instead of drying them in the sun right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo hulu lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermenting the beans under plantain leaves builds up natural heat. This process kills the seed inside, destroys bitterness, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color required for good quality beans.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kɔfi ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Does heavy rainfall always help cocoa trees give a big harvest, or can too much water cause problems?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo be fɛɛ be aloo nu babaoo baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai aba?

english: While cocoa needs good rain, continuous heavy rainfall and standing water can rot root systems and create high moisture levels that cause black pod disease to spread rapidly across your farm.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nugbɔ kpakpa he miihia Cocoa. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be ni haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: If a crop package says it matures in 120 days, do I have to harvest everything on day 120 exactly?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ yɛ gbii 120 mli lɛ, ani mikɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baakpa yɛ gbi ni ji 120 lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The 120 days is just a general guide, not a strict deadline. Weather and soil conditions can speed up or slow down maturity, so you should always look for physical signs like yellowing leaves or dry husks rather than relying only on counting days.
