ga: Gbii 120 ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko kɛkɛ ni kɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he. Jeee be ni ato ni mli wa ji no. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ baanyɛ aha ekwɛ̃ oya loo ebaa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otao gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookane gbii lɛ kɛkɛ

english: Can I harvest part of my crop field today and leave the rest to harvest next week?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fã ko ŋmɛnɛ ni mashi nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛha otsi ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, for crops like peppers or cassava, harvesting in batches works fine. However, for grain crops like maize or rice, leaving mature crops in the field too long exposes them to pests, birds, and mold.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili loo cassava. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ kui amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni amɛdara yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii, okpoi, kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my crop is ready for harvest if I lost track of the planting date?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mihiɛ kpa gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when they are ready. Grains usually turn golden-brown and dry out, root crops make the soil crack around the base, and fruits change color and feel firm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ amɛfee klalo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shika tsuru ni amɛgbiɔ. Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ su ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I leave my mature crops in the soil longer to harvest later, will they spoil?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni makpa yɛ sɛɛ mli hu? Ani ebaafite?

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field past their maturity increases the risk of damage from insects, farm animals, rain rot, and sunburn, which lowers the quality and price of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho be ni esa akɛ akwɛ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ kooloi baafite lɛ yaa hiɛ. Okwaafoi amli kooloi, nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo Enɛ baaha onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahilɛ kɛ amɛjara aba shi.

english: What is the difference between farming on upland and farming in lowland areas?
ga: okwaayeli yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa kɛ okwaayeli yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Te amɛsoro amɛhe amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Upland is higher ground that drains water quickly, making it good for crops like maize and cassava that hate waterlogged roots. Lowland stays wet longer and gathers runoff water, making it ideal for water-loving crops like rice.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ji he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa ehe baa sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni sumɔɔɔ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni efɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ebua nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ehi kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Can I plant maize on lowland soil that easily floods when it rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is risky to plant maize in flood-prone lowland because maize roots will rot if submerged in standing water for too long. Lowlands that hold standing water are much better suited for rice.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nu afua fɔɔ baa lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ abɛi shishifãi lɛ baafite kɛji amɛta nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu damɔ shi yɛ nɔ lɛ ji hei ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I choose whether to plant my farm on a slope or in a valley bottom?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kɛji madu ŋmɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ loo yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plant on the higher slope if you are growing crops like tomatoes, groundnuts, or maize that need good water drainage. Choose the valley bottom if you need naturally moist soil for rice or off-season vegetable farming.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ kɛji oodu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni biɔ nu kpakpa. Halamɔ jɔɔ lɛ shishi kɛji oosumɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I use an irrigation system if it already rains during the farming season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii kɛji nugbɔ enɛ momo yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Rainfall can be unpredictable or stop early before your crops finish growing. Irrigation gives you control over water supply, preventing crop loss from sudden dry spells and allowing you to farm year-round.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo ekpa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nu ni baa lɛ. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ naa. ni ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why can I only grow certain crops during one specific season of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops depend on specific patterns of sunlight, temperature, and rain. Some crops need the heavy rains of the main season to thrive, and planting them in the wrong season without irrigation causes them to fail.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ hulu la, dɔlɛ, kɛ nugbɔ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be titri lɛ mli koni amɛshwere. Ni kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni esaaa mli ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Will my crops grow differently if I use irrigation instead of depending only on rainfall?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, irrigated crops usually grow more evenly and mature on time because they receive steady water, whereas rainfed crops can stall or mature prematurely if drought occurs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afɔɔ amɛ nu lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ be ni sa mli ejaakɛ amɛnáa nu daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee mɛi ni bɛ wala loo amɛdara mra kɛji hɔmɔ ba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen or water. Maize needs nitrogen from compost or fertilizer to build healthy green leaves and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Abɛi he miihia nitrogen kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack soil nutrients, or are attacked by tiny pests like capsids. Providing shade and controlling pests helps the flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ capsids tutuaa lɛ. Shade kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and look dead during the afternoon heat even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, water evaporates from tomato leaves faster than the roots can suck it up, or soil-borne fungi may be blocking the stem's water channels.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai amli lɛ shwieɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmeii ni afɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide broad leaves that shade the cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough moisture to start planting maize after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it crumbles instantly when you open your hand, the ground is still too dry for seeds to germinate safely, and you should wait for more rain.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji efo trukaa beni ogbele onine lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lolo ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. Ni esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the stems and leaves look very big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Softening the soil helps roots grow thick.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ blɛoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing in twisted, strange shapes instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee srɔtoi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni etsake yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and twist when they hit hard, unplowed soil, rocks, or gravel underground. Building high, soft mounds gives the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaatsɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii tswa amɛ waa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil much faster than farm crops, which need extra care to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛye nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei, ni biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko koni amɛya nɔ amɛye akaŋ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to lose their leaves right after they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ebɔi yibii womɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Pepper plants drop leaves during fruiting if they lack water or soil minerals like calcium, or if tiny insects like whiteflies have spread a virus to the leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo minerals yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of tiny holes and white powder after two months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ beni akɛto nyɔji enyɔ sɛɛ.

english: Insects called weevils bore into stored maize to eat and lay eggs. Drying the grain completely before storage and keeping it in airtight bags starves the insects of air and stops them from damaging the crop.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo ŋmãa. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui dani akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the branches grow very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni eniji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree becomes too bushy, sunlight cannot reach the inner branches where flowers grow, and the tree wastes energy feeding leaves instead of pods. Pruning opens the tree up so light and air can boost pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ eyi tsɔ lɛ, Hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mligbɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ahe. Ni tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbeleɔ ehe kɛyaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni ehaa pod lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: How does clearing weeds and heavy brush around my cocoa trees help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse lɛ ajiemɔ Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-cacao tso ni ebɔle mihe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Heavy weeds and brush steal water and soil nutrients directly from your cocoa roots. Clearing them away ensures your cocoa trees get all the food they need to stay strong and bear heavy pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni tsii.

english: As cocoa trees age, older branches become less active in carrying nutrients. Pruning away old or dead wood encourages new branch growth, which helps the tree produce bigger, healthier pods again.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Babaoo ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ, nakai niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shi. Tso momo loo ni egbo lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha tsei niji heei akwɛ̃. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: Pods turn black mainly due to black pod disease, which thrives in high humidity and heavy shade. Trimming dense branches lets sunlight in to dry the dampness and keep your pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pods ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji black pod hela, ni daa yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Dense pruning haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa o-pods lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my cocoa pods more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Pests love cool, damp, and shaded conditions that rain creates. Keeping your cocoa farm pruned and weed-free allows wind and sun to dry the leaves quickly, making it harder for insects to thrive.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni nugbɔ haa. Kɛ́ okwɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaada.

english: How can I prevent my young cocoa pods from drying up and dying on the trunk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Young pods often wilt and dry up when the tree is stressed by lack of nutrients, poor shade balance, or disease. Ensuring clean farm conditions and proper pruning helps the tree carry pods to full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Shade ni ehiii loo hela. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree trunk fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects or if the tree lacks the strength to feed them. Balanced shade, rich soil, and good air circulation help flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli loo kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ amɛ nɔ. shade ni ja shikpɔŋ ni baa nii Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is mature enough to pick without damaging future harvests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni efiteee wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A pod is ready when its color changes fully from green to yellow, or red to orange. Always cut the stem cleanly with a blade so you do not harm the flower cushion on the trunk where next season's pods will grow.
ga: Pod lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ehiɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfo tso lɛ he. Enɛ yeŋ fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ he ni be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ awui.

english: Does my cocoa farm produce more crop in full sunlight or under shade trees?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ashishi?

english: Cocoa trees need a balanced combination of partial shade and sunlight. Full sun without shade stresses young trees and dries out the soil, while too much shade creates fungus that destroys your pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko afutu mli. Hulu ni fa tsɔ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aje kpo faŋŋ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo babaoo haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ o-pods lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my cocoa trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes their roots to fight for soil food and their leaves to block out sunlight. Proper spacing allows every tree to get enough light and nutrients to yield maximum pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ, ni ehaa hulu la ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that cools the plants, preserves soil moisture, and protects fragile leaves until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he waa. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni obu baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow in a V-shape while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen travels to the growing top parts of the plant first, leaving older lower leaves starved of nutrients unless compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer is added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa lɛ shishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ yaa tso ni miida lɛ yiteŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow healthy leaves and pods even when I do not add chemical fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii moŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria living in their roots to capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and convert it into natural plant food. This process nourishes the crop and improves the soil naturally without needing added nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain floods my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in heavy soil without proper drainage, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing root-rot fungi to thrive and destroy the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Hɔmɔ miiye shishifãi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why does spreading dry palm leaves or dry grass on top of my soil keep my vegetable beds moist during dry hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei ni egbi loo jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter, known as mulching, creates a blanket that blocks direct sunlight and wind from hitting the dirt. This slows down water evaporation, keeps the root zone cool, and helps the soil retain water longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Efeɔ blanket ko ni tsiɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress. Heat dries out the pollen inside the flower, preventing fertilization, so maintaining regular watering and light afternoon shade helps set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my maize crop produce tassels and flowers very early while the stalks are still short during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tassel kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ oya yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme water drought early in life, they panic and rush their reproductive stage to set seed before dying. This stress-induced flowering causes short stalks and smaller maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpe yɛ amɛwala beaŋ lɛ Amɛsheɔ gbeyei ni amɛyaa fɔmɔ be lɛ mli oya bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani amɛgboi. Fɔfɔi ni nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread flat across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ atswa mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air so they can capture maximum sunlight for food production. It also prevents leaves from rotting on damp ground and improves airflow, which lowers the risk of fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield small, light bunches when I allow all the young shoots to grow around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni miha tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso nyɛ lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers growing around a single plantain tree compete heavily for water, light, and soil nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the mother plant to direct all its food into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni efee tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or viruses spread by them. These pests drain the leaf sap, causing uneven tissue growth that twists and curls the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fãji lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni etsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does my maize crop grow so rapidly in the first few weeks compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ da oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli kɛ akɛto mi-tsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing grain that uses soil nutrients quickly to build strong roots and tall stalks early in its cycle. Giving it good sunlight, water, and early fertilizer helps it shoot up fast during its initial growth phase.
ga: Abele ji dumɔwu ni daa oya ni kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei kakadaji yɛ eshishijee mli. Hulu la kpakpa, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my corn so it doesn't dry up on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akagbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn should be planted right at the onset of the steady rainy season when the ground has stayed moist for a few consecutive days. Planting too early before rains are reliable can cause the seeds to dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my young corn plants, and how does it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. If left untreated, these insects slow down plant growth and reduce your harvest, but early sprays or traditional remedies can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni eye tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi. Shi kɛ́ akɛ tsofai shwie amɛnɔ mra loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: If I plant corn on the exact same plot of land every single year, why does my yield keep decreasing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Corn is a heavy feeder that pulls key nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same land exhausts the earth, so rotating it with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore natural fertility back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii titri kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my young cocoa seedlings to burn and wither when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni ha mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgbi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and need protection from direct sunlight, much like shade-loving forest plants. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa shelters the seedlings from harsh heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni ebiɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ koo mli tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui lɛ adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa pods start rotting and turning black before I can process them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani abaanyɛ atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods rot quickly due to fungal conditions like black pod disease, which thrive in excessive dampness and shade. Harvesting pods as soon as they ripen and keeping the farm weeded helps prevent fungal spores from destroying your crop.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi pɛ ni oha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fungal spores lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do so many small flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but only a small percentage turn into pods. Flower drop happens because of incomplete pollination by tiny insects, dry weather, or the tree shedding excess flowers it cannot support with its available water and nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ bafeɔ pod. Fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi. Aloo tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its outer skin changes color completely, usually from green to bright yellow or from red to orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside have proper sugar content for good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ lɛ etsake su kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei nɔ Akpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ koni ana akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ sugar ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kpakpa.

english: Can I plant corn inside my new cocoa farm while waiting for the cocoa trees to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, you can intercrop corn with young cocoa during the first year to earn income and food. However, maintain enough space between them so the fast-growing corn does not block light or steal water and nutrients from the young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa bibii awo ŋmãa mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli koni oná shika kɛ niyenii. Shi kɛlɛ, ha okɛ ohe akabɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ akatsĩ kane lɛ naa loo ekaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for my crops when the rains dry up unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crops with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks creates a protective layer called mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the soil, prevents weed growth, and shields the earth from heat during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ahe tsei ahe lɛ ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or humidity is extremely high, as heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination required to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ fa tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ naa kpɛɔ amɛhe, ni ehaaa amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa, ni he hiaa koni amɛwo aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants start falling over onto the dirt as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato vines naturally have soft stems that cannot support heavy fruit on their own. Tying them to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruit off the wet ground, protecting them from soil diseases and rotting.
ga: Tomato wain tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛfi tso ko he lɛ, ehaaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the sides before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden, heavy amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen or is receiving too much water at its roots, forcing it to move nutrients upward to protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu babaoo miiná tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni ebu tso hee ni eda lɛ he.

english: Why is it better to start tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaaje tomato dumɔwui ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate; starting them in a small nursery bed lets you easily shade, water, and protect the young sprouts from pests until they are strong enough to survive in the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Je shishi kɛ tsei bibii ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ koni akɛwo hulutsoo, nu ni akɛbu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy fresh seeds from the store instead of saving seeds from the tomatoes I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ato lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from market tomatoes often grow into weak plants that yield small, uneven fruits. Store-bought certified seeds are specially produced to resist common diseases and produce high yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: How do I properly measure my land so I know how many tomato seeds to buy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ? Koni ole tomato dumɔwui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ ohe

english: You can measure your farm size by pacing out the field borders using equal steps or using a measuring tape with an officer, which helps you calculate the precise quantity of seeds and fertilizer needed without wasting money.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ steps po asusu oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he. Aloo okɛ tɛp ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii kɛ nitsulɔi lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni obu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ofiteee shika babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant them close to large forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Big forest trees have long, aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients from the soil, while their dense leaves block the sunlight your crops need to make food and grow properly.
ga: Tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows soil-borne pests and diseases that attack tomatoes to multiply in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tomato lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves look limp and wilted during the middle of the day even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. If the plant recovers by evening, this afternoon wilting is a normal defense mechanism against heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɛnɛ shwane nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after I spray farm medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves turn yellow if chemical medicine is mixed incorrectly, applied at the wrong strength, or sprayed during the burning midday sun, which damages the plant tissues instead of protecting them.
ga: Tso lɛ baai baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛ tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ futuuu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ falɛ ni ejaaa atsu nii Loo okɛshwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei ahe fãji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or damaged by fake farm medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai amalei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii loo efite?

english: Diseases usually spread slowly from plant to plant over time, whereas damage from bad or incorrectly used chemicals appears suddenly across all sprayed crops at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio. Kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko nɔ beni be hoɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa loo ni akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to apply protective medicine on my crops every year at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa afi yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Insect pests and diseases multiply in seasonal cycles linked to the rains or dry spells, so crops require protection right before these annual outbreaks occur.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani helai ni baa daa afi lɛ aba.

english: What happens to my crops if heavy rain falls right after I apply medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa wo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the medicine off the leaves before the plant can absorb it or before it can stop pests, leaving the crop unprotected and causing the medicine to fail.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsofa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ loo dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ nyɛɔ ekpaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abuuu tsei lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji nyɛɛɛ atsu nii

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl and droop to save moisture and protect themselves from severe heat, but they usually recover in the evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crops more during the dry season than the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, plants suffer from water stress and become weak, making it easier for hungry insects to attack them in search of water and nutrients.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaná nu he haomɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ akɛ amɛbaatutua amɛ koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to poor conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, too little water, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu fioo tsɔ he. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy expanding leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to build large roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu amɛ kɛba shi koni amɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my crops produce less food every year even though I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every season, so without adding organic matter, rest, or fertilizer, the soil becomes starved and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, nibii ni eshwɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enyɛŋ eha tsei heei niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from scorching sunlight and to keep moisture in the soil while their roots are still developing.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but only produce tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes maize grow tall leaves, but if the plants lack phosphorus or are planted too close together, they won't have enough nutrients and sunlight to fill out large cobs.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná baai kakadaji. Shi kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tsei lɛ amli loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Niyenii nibii kɛ hulu la lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ agboi lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off before the tubers are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can mean the plant is shifting energy to tuber growth, but early leaf drop is often caused by drought stress, poor soil nutrients, or pests.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsake hewalɛ kɛmiiya bulbs ni miida lɛ amli. Shi bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area and prevent the plant from losing too much water during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Curling ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ shi ni atsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to use a motorized cutter or cut my rice manually by hand when harvesting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ ŋmãa loo akɛ nine baafo ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛ́ ookpa ŋmãa?

english: Motorized cutters save time and reduce grain loss from over-ripening on large fields, while manual cutting works best on small or flooded plots where machinery cannot easily move.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfoɔ nii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ be baa shi ni ehaa ŋmaa ni fiteɔ yɛ hei wuji ni shwereɔ fe nine lɛ baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni nine ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei bibii loo hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, he ni tsɔnei nyɛɛɛ aya mlɛo lɛ,.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy in storage even when I cut it at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifolɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested maize spoils if it is not properly dried to a safe moisture level before storage, as remaining dampness allows mold and insects to thrive.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii adara.

english: How can I increase the total amount of crop I harvest without buying more land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni miheee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can boost production by using improved seed varieties, planting in proper row lines, applying the right fertilizer at key growth stages, and keeping weeds under control early.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni sa Nuŋtsɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ mra

english: Why do my plantains take so long to produce fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, plantain plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which slows down their development and delays fruiting.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing near the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra side shoots directs the plant's energy and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruit instead of wasting energy on excess stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the grass and old crops on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter in the soil, kills beneficial insects and micro-organisms, and exposes the topsoil to rain erosion, lowering your farm's fertility over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni eha nugbɔ lɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When water sits around the roots for too long, oxygen cannot reach them, causing soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Yams need soft, deep soil and proper staking. Hard or stony soil blocks the tuber from expanding downward freely, while a lack of wooden stakes prevents the leaves from catching enough sunlight to feed the growing tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋtayaa ni sa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛha amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni bɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than the certified seeds I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred from distinct parent plants to produce a high yield in the first generation. Saving seeds from that harvest causes those special high-yielding traits to break down, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating out the soft growing center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmã tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the whorl (center leaves) of maize to feed on tender leaves. Catching them early with recommended treatments stops them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmei whorls (teŋgbɛ baai) amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and lose leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves faster than young cocoa roots can pull water from the soil. Young cocoa plants need temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them from hot winds until their root system grows deep.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni kookoo shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow surface roots rather than deep taproots. As the heavy fruit bunch develops at the top, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you support the trunk with bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen, so growing them together naturally improves soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen akɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under leaves, or by viruses they spread. They drain nutrients from the plant, causing leaves to twist and growth to stall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is exhausted and losing its fertility?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Exhausted soil shows signs like stunted plant growth, yellowish or purplish leaves on healthy crops, low yields despite good rain, and heavy infestation by tough weeds like spear grass.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo. Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo purple yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ Yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ jwɛi ni wa tamɔ spear jwɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer to my crops at specific intervals instead of giving it all at once during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops consume nutrients gradually as they grow. If you put all the fertilizer in the soil at planting, much of it gets washed away by heavy rains before the plants are big enough to use it. Giving fertilizer at spaced intervals ensures the crop gets fresh nutrients right when it is growing leaves, flowering, or forming fruit.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni oduɔ nii lɛ, Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛyaa dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii heei beni amɛwoɔ baai, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, loo amɛwoɔ yibii pɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not food for plants; it only helps them drink nutrients from the soil. Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, which must be added to the soil through compost or fertilizer at regular intervals.
ga: Nu pɛ jeee niyenii kɛha tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, ni baaha akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: How often should I feed my vegetable crops with fertilizer during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: In dry weather, crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer well. You should feed them small amounts of fertilizer dissolved in water at shorter intervals so the roots can continuously draw food without getting burned by concentrated chemicals.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni haa nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ aha amɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii be fɛɛ be ni tsofai ni mli ewo muji lɛ ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why do crops growing along riverbanks or in swamps stay green without me applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ faai ahe loo yɛ ŋshɔi amli lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Water flowing in rivers and swamps carries rich silt, organic matter, and dissolved minerals from upstream. Plants growing in or right next to water continuously absorb these free, naturally occurring nutrients without needing scheduled chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ faai kɛ ŋshɔi amli lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ mli nibii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ ni jɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nu mli loo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nɛɛ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Can crops like swamp cocoyam grow properly inside standing water without their roots rotting?
ga: Ani tsei tamɔ swamp cocoa baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbooo?

english: Yes, swamp cocoyam (taro) has special spongy roots designed to live in waterlogged soil. Unlike land crops, it absorbs nutrients directly from the surrounding water and mud while taking in air through its leaf stems.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, swamp cocoyam (taro) lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni tamɔ sponge ni afee koni ehi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nu kɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni enine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Is it necessary to fertilize my rice crop when it is already growing inside flooded water?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ mli?

english: Flooded rice naturally feeds on nutrients dissolved in the water and trapped in the mud. While it finds a lot of its own food in the water, adding small amounts of extra fertilizer at key growth stages will help produce heavier grains.
ga: Omɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni egbɛ eshwa nu mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛna niyenii babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Why do wild weeds and floating plants grow so fast in my fish pond without anyone feeding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi loo ŋshɔ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko haaa amɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Pond water accumulates waste from fish, decaying leaves, and nutrient-rich soil runoff. Aquatic plants absorb these dissolved wastes as direct food, allowing them to feed themselves and grow rapidly without human intervention.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ buaa loo mli jwɛi naa. baai ni egboi kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu mli tsei lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ muji ni egbɛ eshwa nɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe niyenii ni amɛdaraa oya ni adesa kɛ amɛhe wooo mli.

english: Why do my cassava and pepper plants die when heavy rain leaves standing water on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ pepper tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava and pepper are land crops whose roots need air to breathe. Standing water cuts off oxygen to their roots, causing them to drown and rot because they are not adapted to feeding or surviving in water.
ga: Cassava kɛ pepper ji ŋmɔ mli nibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe esaaa akɛ ayeɔ nii loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nu mli.

english: Why does sugarcane grow so tall and thick when planted close to water sources?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ?

english: Sugarcane requires huge amounts of water and continuous nutrients to build thick stems. Being near water allows its deep roots to drink constantly and pull up dissolved minerals buried deep in damp soil.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai he miihia shɛ̃ be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Nu ni ebɛŋkɛ lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu be fɛɛ be. ni egbalaa shika tsuru ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ

english: What is the difference between how land crops and water plants get their food?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei kɛ nu mli tsei naa amɛ niyenii lɛ teŋ?

english: Land crops depend on soil moisture and scheduled top-dressing of manure or fertilizer by the farmer. Water plants continuously draw dissolved food directly from the surrounding moisture without waiting for scheduled feedings.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni okwaafoi kɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nu mli tsei gbalaa niyenii ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ be fɛɛ be. ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow well the first year after I burn my land, but fail in the years after that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mikɛshã shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi eyeee omanye yɛ afi sɛɛ?

english: Burning plant bush gives a quick boost of ash fertilizer to the soil for the first season, but the fire destroys the living organisms and organic matter needed to keep the soil fertile for future years.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ni ashãa oya lɛ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Shi la fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to take over my farm much faster after I burn the bush to clear it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya waa beni mishã jwɛi lɛ koni mikɛjie amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fire clears the ground surface completely, which exposes hidden weed seeds to direct sunlight and rain, allowing tough weeds to sprout and grow faster than your crops.
ga: La tsuuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa jwɛi ni wa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to my crops if I leave cleared bush to rot on the farm instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji miha jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving cut plants to rot naturally creates compost that feeds the soil over a long time, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, and helps hold rainwater around crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni afolɔ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa sũ lɛ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ tsei shishifãi ahe

english: Why are my maize plants smaller and producing fewer ears than they used to on this same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ efee bibii ni amɛtoi fioo fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting crops on the same soil repeatedly without adding organic matter or resting the land drains all the natural plant food, causing crops to grow weak and yield less.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ Ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔ lɛ baaha tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ afite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: How can I keep getting good crop yields if I stop clearing fresh forest land every few years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ maná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mikpa koo mli shikpɔŋ heei ni mifoɔ daa afii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: You can keep your existing land productive by rotating different crops, adding animal manure or compost, and planting cover crops like beans to continuously rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ momo lɛ awo yibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni oootsake lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji afata he. ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ daa.

english: Can planting crops like cowpeas or groundnuts really help fix tired soil for my other crops?
ga: Nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Ani manyɛ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts capture natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, making the ground richer for the next crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm has become too weak to grow food crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu niyenii jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your soil becomes pale, forms a hard crust when dry, does not absorb rainwater easily, or causes crop leaves to turn yellow early, the soil has lost its fertility.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse Ebafeɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieee shi oya loo ehaaa tsei ahe baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ oya Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efo mli.

english: Will keeping some forest trees on my farm prevent my food crops from getting enough light to grow?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi mi niyenii tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara?

english: While dense shade can slow growth, leaving scattered high-canopy trees lets light filter through while protecting crops and soil from being scorched by the intense midday sun.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa baanyɛ aha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo moŋ, shi tsei ni ŋwɛi ŋtayaai kakadaji egbɛ eshwã lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa la tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ akashã amɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so much faster now during the hot season than it did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: When forest trees are completely removed, direct wind and sunlight hit the bare soil, causing water to evaporate rapidly out of the ground before crops can drink it.
ga: Beni ajie tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ.

english: How do trees on my farm protect my food crops during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tree roots act like nets underground that hold the topsoil together so heavy rains do not wash away crop nutrients, while tree branches break the force of strong winds and rain.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋloo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieee niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ. Beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbálaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I test if my stored maize seeds are still good to plant before I put them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hi kɛha dumɔ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: You can test seed strength by placing 10 seeds on a damp cloth for three days. If at least 8 seeds sprout strong roots, your seed batch is healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛbaawo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛha gbii etɛ Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ dumɔwui 8 kwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: How do I harvest my fresh tomatoes without causing them to rot quickly before reaching the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa tomato hee ni efiteee oya dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Fresh tomatoes have thin, delicate skins that bruise easily. Harvest them early in the morning when it is cool, keep the stems attached, and handle them gently to prevent tiny cracks that let in rot.
ga: Tomato ehee yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni egbɔjɔɔ oya. Kpaa leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso, ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmeii bibii akagbala. koni efite

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Improving soil drainage and adding well-composted animal manure will restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaafee jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi aŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stalks and produces very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced feeding will help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ niyenii ni sa baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow well together. Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while protecting the ground from weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abele lɛ daa waa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are suffering from severe heat and drought stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miina dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ?

english: During drought, cocoa leaves curl up, turn brown at the edges, and fall off prematurely. The tree drops leaves intentionally to save water in its trunk and roots.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eshishigbɛi lɛ yɛ blɔfo. ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking my young maize plants so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-babi corn tsei lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target young maize because the central funnel leaves are soft, tender, and easy for caterpillars to eat. Checking your fields weekly allows you to catch and treat them before major damage happens.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa otsi lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ omɔ amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani nɔ ko wulu aba.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die immediately after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer transplant shock if moved under bright afternoon sun or if their delicate root hairs are broken. Transplant late in the afternoon and water the soil right away to help them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa shishi loo kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fã. Okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwane mli ni okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know if my harvested yam tubers are safe to store for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yams are safe for storage when the outer skin is completely dry and cured, with no open cuts or soft spots. Storing damaged yams invites fungal decay that can spread to the rest of your harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakɛ sweet potato ato kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ egbi kwraa ni etsa. ni bɛ ŋwɛigbɛ loo he ni egbɔjɔ yɛ Atomɔ ni efite lɛ ni akpaa lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmaa lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect themselves from heat. They are not dying; they will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Amɛgbooo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ nɛ lɛ, etsɛ̃ɔ baai heei.

english: High heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination causes tomato plants to drop flowers to save energy. Ensuring steady watering and light mulch around the base helps fruit set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo pollination ni ehiii Ha tomato tsei lɛ afɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akã shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and looking eaten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the tender leaves. Early treatment with recommended organic leaf extracts or safe pesticides can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsamɔ ni afeɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akudɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses. Controlling these pests early prevents the spread of infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Supporting them with strong wooden props or stakes helps balance their weight against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli tse. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsei ni wa fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛtsiimɔ lɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sunlight so the plant can produce more food, which helps grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows each plant enough food and room to thrive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas helps make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping their young fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This issue is often caused by nutrient shortages in sandy soil or root stress. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizer strengthens the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli loo shishifãi ni haoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is most effective when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after germination, allowing roots to quickly absorb nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out their roots. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees around them during their first few years to protect them from heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This struggle makes them grow tall and thin, leading to weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
