ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ta nɛɛ ha amɛkwɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select stems from mature, healthy cassava plants that are about 8 to 12 months old. Use the hard middle portion of the stalk rather than the soft green top or the woody base, and make sure it has healthy buds.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eda ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12. Kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tso shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big green leaves but fail to bring out fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai ni dara waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes it spend all its strength growing foliage instead of flowers. Tomatoes need phosphorus and potassium to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tomato he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same spot continuously pulls the same nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the land weak. It also allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply and remain in that soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaya nɔ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil become hard and dry quickly just a few days after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter, like decayed leaves or manure, which acts like a sponge to trap water. Bare soil exposed directly to the hot sun also loses its moisture rapidly to heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni emɔɔ nu Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hu fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ edɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the soft center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that hides in the center funnel of young maize plants to feed on new leaves. Detecting them early allows you to treat the crop before they destroy the growth point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni eye baai heei. mra be mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani efiteɔ he ni edara yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from the plant and spreading plant viruses. Removing damaged plants and controlling these insects helps protect the healthy crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni efite lɛ ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 8 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do tiny insects leave holes and white powder in my stored maize grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shĩɔ bu kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils, which lay eggs inside dry corn kernels. As the young insects hatch, they eat the inside of the grain, leaving empty shells, small holes, and powdered corn behind.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ŋmei, ni woɔ ŋmei ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Eshiɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli, bu bibii, kɛ ŋmei sũ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: What does it mean to broadcast seeds when planting, and which crops can I plant this way?
ga: Mɛni dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ́ adu nii lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ?

english: Broadcasting means scattering seeds evenly over the surface of the soil by hand instead of placing them one by one in measured holes. Crops with small seeds or tubers, such as tiger nuts, rice, and grass pastures, are often broadcasted to save time and labor.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwu ɔmɛ kake kake kɛ wo buhi nɛ a susu ɔ mi. Bei pii lɛ, akwɛɔ tsei ni dumɔwui bibii loo bulbs yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tiger nuts, rice, kɛ heather koni akɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ akafite.

english: Why do I have to plant my maize seed by seed instead of just scattering the seeds on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and heavy, requiring deep roots, plenty of sunlight, and dedicated space to feed. Planting them individually in measured rows ensures each stalk gets enough nutrients and leaves room for easy weeding and harvesting.
ga: Abɛi daa ni eshɛɔ babaoo. Ebiɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. kɛ niyeli he ko ni ajɔɔ nɔ aha Amɛdumɔ srɔtoi yɛ ŋtayaai ni asusu mli lɛ haa ŋtayaa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni oshi gbɛ kɛha jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Are there crops I can grow in Ghana that take less daily physical effort to plant than maize?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni heɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo fe ŋmãa?

english: Yes, crops like tiger nuts and sweet potatoes are often easier to plant because they can be scattered or planted in simpler beds without the strict, seed-by-seed digging required for tall grains like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tiger nuts kɛ sweet potatoes fɔɔ kaa akɛ adumɔ waaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ adu amɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. ni dumɔwui ni mli wa lɛ fataaa he komekomei, ni he hiaa kɛha dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: If I scatter seeds across my field instead of planting in rows, will it save me money on farm labor?
ga: Kɛ migbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, Ani manyɛ makɛ shika ato ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he?

english: Yes, scattering or broadcasting seeds reduces the number of farm laborers you need during planting season because one worker can cover a large area very quickly compared to planting in drilled holes.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ooogbɛ oshwã loo ooogbɛ oshwã lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ayibɔ ni he hiaa bo yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitsulɔ kome baanyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ wulu ko he nii oya waa kɛ akɛto dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nubu mli lɛ he.

english: What are tiger nuts, and how do they grow on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji jata nut? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Tiger nuts are not true nuts from trees; they are small, sweet tubers that grow underneath the ground attached to the roots of a grass-like plant, similar to how peanuts or small potatoes mature in the soil.
ga: Tiger ŋmeii jeee tso ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ. Eji tso bibioo ko ni ŋɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ekpɛtɛɔ tso ko ni tamɔ jwɛi shishifãi ahe. Etamɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale and thin if I plant too many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that demands a lot of light, water, and soil nutrients. When planted too close together, the leaves shade each other out and the roots fight for the same soil food, leading to weak stalks and small cobs.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ la babaoo, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How should I prepare my land if I want to scatter crop seeds instead of digging individual holes?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã moŋ fe ni mafo bu?

english: The soil must be plowed fine, cleared of large weeds, and leveled smoothly so that scattered seeds make good contact with loose soil and germinate evenly without being washed away by heavy rain.
ga: Esa akɛ atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Jiemɔ jwɛi wuji lɛ ni oha he ni eyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for crops like tiger nuts that mature under the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei tamɔ tiger nuts ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Underground tuber crops prefer loose, well-draining sandy loam soil because it allows the roots to expand easily underwater without compaction and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Tubers sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nu shishi oya ni ekɛ amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How does the way I plant my crops affect how fast weeds grow on my farm?
ga: Te bɔ ni miduɔ nii mihaa lɛ saa bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops scattered densely cover the bare ground quickly and shade the soil, which blocks sunlight and prevents weeds from growing, whereas crops planted far apart in rows leave open soil where weeds can spread rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni egbɛ eshwã babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni adu amɛ srɔtoi yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ shiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni jwɛi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why are some farmers in Ghana choosing to grow tiger nuts alongside traditional crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miihala akɛ amɛbaadu tiger nuts yɛ blema nibii tamɔ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Growing tiger nuts allows farmers to diversify their income because tiger nuts have a high market demand for snacks and milk production, and they offer a different labor routine than traditional grain crops.
ga: Tiger nuts ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa amɛshika srɔtoi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tiger nuts lɛ yɛ jarayeli nibii babaoo ni ataoɔ yɛ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ mliki feemɔ mli. Ni tiger nuts lɛ yɛ nitsumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ srɔto fe blema ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when roots are sitting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ tara sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops, like beans or peanuts, helps restore soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why is my maize staying short and stunted even though I planted it at the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe ejɔ nɛkɛ lɛ? Adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when plants cannot absorb food from the ground. This occurs if the soil is exhausted, if the soil is too acidic, or if parasitic weeds like Striga are attached to the roots and stealing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli ewo wu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates living shade umbrellas that protect cocoa seedlings and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot, dry weather as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. If the leaves uncurl when the air cools down in the evening, the plant is simply adjusting to heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miitsake amɛhe amɛwo hulutsoo be mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience temperature shock, prolonged dry spells, or overwatering. Using too much nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to drop flowers because it focuses energy on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi amli. egbi be kakadaŋŋ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashwie shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when rain creates standing water around the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away quickly so the roots do not drown and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni no haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small fruit when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread its roots and leaves to produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbɛɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing black, rotten spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is forming. It is usually caused by inconsistent watering, where the soil switches between being too dry and too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: Why are my harvested yams starting to sprout early while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ oya beni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and sprout when they feel warmth and high moisture in the air, signaling that it is time to grow. Storing yams on raised racks in a shaded, cool, and well-ventilated barn delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ enu he akɛ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ oda Okɛ sweet potato toɔ shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Baaha kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow tall. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea gives the maize the food it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good to plant cowpea or beans on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize helps both crops. Beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time is when the soil is already moist and the young crops are growing quickly, usually 2 to 3 weeks after planting. Never apply fertilizer on dry soil or during heavy downpours, as the rain will wash the fertilizer away before roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tsei bibii lɛ miida oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ. Kaaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings grow better under shade trees than out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo shishi fe bɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight and lose water too quickly. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moisture in the ground until the seedlings are mature enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni kookoo lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛna hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start producing big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground, so when a heavy bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy. Propping the stem up with strong bamboo forks or poles keeps the heavy tree from breaking or falling in strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kuu agbo ko yɛ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ baaná muji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ akɛ fɔk loo ŋmei tso atsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ewa. Ebaaye ebua ni tsei wuji akakumɔ loo amɛkagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays around the roots for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to run off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers underneath the soil. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air away from wet dirt, which also prevents fungal diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akatutua baai lɛ hu.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot weather helps the plant stay relaxed so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ehe jɔɔ lɛ. Fɔfɔi baanyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a disease, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Keeping the plant watered and spraying organic neem oil protects the leaves from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu ni akɛ organic neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my farm crops from growing big?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds within the first month after planting gives your crops all the food and space they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my small pepper seedlings seem to need so much food and nutrients even though they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwu bibioo lɛ he hiaa niyenii kɛ niyenii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ eji bibioo lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Young crops are in a rapid stage of development, building their stem and root systems quickly, which requires a heavy intake of nutrients relative to their small size.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ miiya hiɛ oya. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifã kɛ shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ni afee oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛ akɛto bɔ ni eyɔɔ bibioo lɛ he.

english: Is it normal for young maize plants to consume more nutrients early on than when they are fully matured?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, young plants need high amounts of energy early in their life cycle to establish strong roots and leaves before they begin flowering and fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, hewalɛ babaoo he miihia tsei bibii yɛ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ shishijee mli koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa dani amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my small tomato plants take up so much liquid fertilizer every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ kɛ nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii daa otsi.

english: Small plants absorb liquid nutrients fast because their growing shoots and roots constantly draw in dissolved minerals to support active cell growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni ji nu lɛ oya ejaakɛ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ miigbala nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua wala yibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: If my plant fertilizer comes in a light powder form, should I mix it with water before applying it to my crop?
ga: Kɛji mi tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ba yɛ powda ni mli tse mli Ani Esa akɛ mikɛ nu afutu mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, light or powdered fertilizers should be dissolved in water so the plant's roots can easily drink them in without burning the tender root tissues.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse loo ni akɛfee powda awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãaa shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ.

english: Why does dry powdered chemical fertilizer burn the leaves of my young crops when I sprinkle it directly on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ kɛ́ mikɛshwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Dry powdered inputs are very concentrated; without adding water to dilute them, they draw moisture out of the plant stems and leaves, causing leaf burn.
ga: Powder ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa. ni akɛ nu fataaa he koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ebaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: How should I feed my small crop seedlings if the nutrient mix is dry and very light?
ga: Mahã ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli egbi waa ni eyɛ mlɛo

english: You should add water to light, dry nutrient mixes to turn them into a liquid solution, making it safe and easy for young crop roots to absorb.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu afata niyenii ni egbi ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ he koni etsɔ nu mli nu. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efee mlɛo.

english: Can I spray dry powdered booster directly on my vegetable crops, or do I need to add water first?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dry powder booster lɛ afɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ nu afata he klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: You must add water first to create a spray mixture; this ensures the powder spreads evenly over the plant leaves without clumping or blowing away in the wind.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu afata he dani obaanyɛ ofee tsɔne ni akɛfutuɔ nii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa powda lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to water the soil immediately after applying light organic powder manure around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ powder ni ji organic fertilizer fioo ko ebɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Adding water helps carry the light organic powder down into the root zone where small roots can access it, rather than letting it sit dry on the topsoil.
ga: Nu ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ organic powder ni tsiimɔ waaa aba shishifãi lɛ amli he ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ. accessible Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi.

english: Should I give small crop seedlings light, diluted liquid food or heavy concentrated dry food?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tso dumɔwui bibii lɛ niyenii ni mli ewo nu? aloo niyenii ni egbi ni mli edɔ waa kɛha tsei bibii adumɔwui?

english: Small seedlings absorb food best when it is light and diluted in water, as their delicate roots cannot handle concentrated dry inputs.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji la yɛ ni nu mli ewo mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ niyenii ni egbi ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa nursery plants look thirsty right after I give them powdered soil nutrients?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ sũ mli niyenii ni akɛ powda ewo mli lɛ ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Powdered nutrients draw moisture away from the soil as they react; adding water when feeding them ensures the young plant stays hydrated while absorbing the nutrients.
ga: Niyenii mli nibii ni akɛfee powda lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu fata he kɛ́ ooha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa from burning while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How does leaving proper distance between my crops help them produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each crop enough space ensures it gets all the food and light it needs to grow strong and yield larger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa ni ewo aduawai loo ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same soil nutrients and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil a break and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When the plants finish growing, that trapped nitrogen acts as free natural fertilizer for the next crop planted there.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe ekwɛmɔ naa Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my pepper plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and rot if heavy rains soak the field before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excessive water when left in waterlogged soil for too long, causing the starch inside to break down and rot. Planting on raised soil mounds or harvesting before the heavy flood season prevents this loss.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ nɔ loo nikpamɔ dani nu afua be lɛ baa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: What is eating the tender center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving small holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the whorl of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying approved bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high, when the soil experiences sudden wet and dry spells, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balanced fertilizer keep the blossoms attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni egbi trukaa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest grow weaker plants than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwere fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations and can carry seed-borne diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist local pests and produce uniform, high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ aba kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow strong. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant steals it from older leaves at the bottom to feed new growth, causing the lower leaf tips to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from too much heat, lack of shade, or dry weather. Without shade trees to cool the air and keep the soil moist, the cocoa tree gets stressed and drops its blossoms to save its own strength instead of producing pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ahe hulutsoo bɛ ni baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni cacao tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ, amɛhaoɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other, will I harvest more cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani wɔbaakpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close together actually reduces your yield because the plants fight under the ground for space, water, and food. When crowded, the cassava grows plenty of weak stems above ground, but the tubers beneath the soil stay small and thin.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu kɛ niyenii kɛ́ mɛi ebɔle amɛhe. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ. lots above ground Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm getting smaller every year even though the plants look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ? Ani nakai tso lɛ da?

english: When a main plantain stem sprouts too many young suckers around its base, they steal food and water from the parent plant. To get large plantain bunches, you must prune away extra suckers so all the plant's energy feeds the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain tso lɛ tsei wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni oná plantains akuu agbo ko Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ aya tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same field, or will they hurt each other's growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ cowpea kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome kɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaaye amɛhe dalɛ awui?

english: Cowpeas and maize work well together as good neighbors. Cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed the maize, while the maize stalks give support and shade to the soil surface.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ akɛ akutsoŋbii kpakpai. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baaye abua ni akwɛ ŋmãa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall stakes to climb on to produce big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛwo bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like solar panels that convert sunlight into food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so every leaf can catch maximum sunlight without rotting from ground dampness.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei, ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass keep them green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which acts like a blanket over the earth. Mulch stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil, keeping the roots cool and moist even when it does not rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ sũ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli. Mulch tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes on the exact same piece of land where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot year after year allows soil pests and diseases that attack tomatoes to multiply in the ground. Rotating to a different crop family starves out those pests and gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa tomato lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsei aweku kroko mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛsaa ehe niyenii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small green droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm infestation, a caterpillar that hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant during the day to feed on fresh inner leaves. Catching them early when the maize is young prevents them from destroying the crop's main leaf tip.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ji gbekɛ lɛ enɛ haaa amɛfite tso lɛ baai titrii lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: If I expand my farm to a larger size, how do weeds affect my crop yields if I cannot weed the whole farm at once?
ga: Kɛji migbɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ko ni da lɛ Te jwɛi baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mafo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shikome hu?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food. If you have a large farm, focus on weeding your crops during their first four to six weeks of growth, which is when crops are too small to defend themselves against weed competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛji oyɛ ŋmɔ agbo lɛ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4-6 ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ jwɛi akaŋshii he.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer to my crops just two weeks after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii yɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: At two weeks, young seedlings have used up the nutrient energy stored in their seeds and are developing their first real roots. Applying fertilizer at this time gives them the food they need to build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Otsii enyɔ eho. Dumɔwui bibii lɛ efite hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ. ni eefee shishifãi diɛŋtsɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma tsei kɛ baai ni wa.

english: What does urea do for my crops when I apply it at two months?
ga: Te urea yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ urea tsu nii nyɔji enyɔ?

english: Urea provides a large boost of nitrogen, which acts as growth fuel. At two months, crops enter a rapid growth phase and prepare to yield, so urea helps them grow dark green leaves and develop heavy produce.
ga: Urea haa nitrogen lɛ yaa hiɛ waa. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ fuel kɛha dalɛ Nyɔji enyɔ eho. Tso lɛ boteɔ dalɛ oya be mli ni esaa ehe kɛha nitsumɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, urea baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná baai ni tsuɔ waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply urea right at the time of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ urea tsuɔ nii beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Young seeds and tender roots can get burned by strong nitrogen fertilizers like urea. Early on, plants need balanced nutrients for root development, whereas urea is best used later when the plant is larger and hungry for leaf growth.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nitrogen ni mli eyi obɔ tamɔ urea ashã dumɔwui bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni urea ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ mli beni tsei lɛ dara ni ataoɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do crops need to be fed fertilizer at different specific stages instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni aaawo amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops have different nutritional needs as they mature. Early feeding supports root growth, while feeding later at two months supports foliage and fruit building. Spreading it out prevents fertilizer from washing away in the rain before the plant can use it.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi kɛ́ amɛmiida. Niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni akɛhaa sɛɛ mli yɛ nyɔji 2 sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua baa kɛ aduawai afeemɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How do I know if my growing crops are hungry for nitrogen like urea?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni miduɔ lɛ he miihia nitrogen tamɔ urea?

english: When crops lack nitrogen, their leaves start turning pale green or yellow, starting from the bottom leaves, and their growth slows down. Applying urea restores their dark green color and speeds up growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. Kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baa lɛ nɔ kɛ dalɛ baafee mlɛo Urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How much money should I expect to budget for fertilizer when farming one acre of land?
ga: Mɛɛ shika esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ acre kome miitsu nii?

english: For a standard one-acre farm, buying the necessary fertilizers and basic crop inputs can cost around 5,000 Ghana Cedi, depending on the specific crop and local market prices.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre kome lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahemɔ baanyɛ afite aaafee Ghana cedis 5,000, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli jara nɔ.

english: How many plots of land usually make up one acre when I am calculating input costs?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ enyiɛ yɔɔ acre kome mli kɛ́ mibu nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo he akɔntaa?

english: In general farm measurements across Ghana, about three to four standard plots make up one full acre, which helps you calculate how many bags of fertilizer or seed you need.
ga: Koni asusu ŋmɔji adalɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ he. Aaafee 3-4 standard lots feɔ acre kome ni eyi obɔ, ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui abɔ ni he baahia bo lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Can I just scatter fertilizer everywhere on my farm or should I put it near each plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã he fɛɛ he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mikɛma tso fɛɛ tso he?

english: It is best to place fertilizer directly near the root zone of each plant rather than scattering it everywhere. This ensures your crops get the food instead of feeding weeds in the open soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso fɛɛ tso shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náa niyenii yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How close to the plant stem should I put fertilizer for two-week-old crop seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ midumɔwui ni eye otsii enyɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ mli yɛ he ni mabɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Place the fertilizer in a small ring a few finger-widths away from the stem. Putting fertilizer directly against the delicate stem can burn and kill the young plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aaafee 2-3 inch kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso bibioo lɛ ashã ni egbo.

english: Do I need to clear weeds before putting fertilizer on my young crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Yes, always clear weeds around your crops before applying fertilizer. If you leave weeds present, they will steal the fertilizer away from your young crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Kɛji oshi jwɛi lɛ Amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the seedlings I buy will give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Good harvest starts with strong source material, often called 'mother plants' or certified seeds. Buying from accredited offices like the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) ensures you get disease-resistant varieties tested to produce high yields.
ga: Nikpamɔ kpakpa jeɔ shishi kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘tso lɛ nyɛ’ loo dumɔwu ni awo he odaseyeli. Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ tamɔ Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: What kind of assistance can I get from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) as a small farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ maná kɛjɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) akɛ okwaafonyo bibioo?

english: MoFA officers give free expert advice on selecting the right crop varieties for your soil, teach proper planting methods, and help farmers access reliable seeds and disease treatments provided by government programs.
ga: MoFA nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa haa yaka yɛ tso henɔi ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ halamɔ he. Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa okwaafoi ni amɛná dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ tsamɔi ni nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi kɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why should I buy improved seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time and produce smaller yields. Improved seeds from agricultural officers are specially bred to resist local pests, survive dry weather, and give higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ebaawo yibii babaoo. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why do my oil palm trees take a few years before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first three to four years building a strong root system and a thick trunk. They need this time to grow strong enough to support heavy bunches of fruit later.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Be nɛɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into producing fruit, they stretch upward trying to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii Moŋ lɛ, etsɔ ehe koni eka ni eshɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Yellow leaves across whole rows usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen. If only a few plants have yellow spots, rings, or curling leaves, it is usually caused by pests or a fungal disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, loo baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ji nɔ ni haa enɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops look droopy and weak right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. Moving a young plant disturbs its roots, making it temporarily lose water faster than it can take it up. Giving them light shade and water helps them recover within a few days.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso bibioo ko ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbala eshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ashɛre yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, crops lose water into the air through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Wilting is the plant's natural way of saving water during peak heat, and they usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ

english: Why is it bad to plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to multiply in the ground, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some trees produce big fruits while other trees of the same crop produce small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ yibii wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii?

english: Fruit size depends on the plant's parent genetics and how well it is cared for. Planting seeds that come from a high-producing 'mother tree' combined with proper spacing and fertilizer ensures larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Yibii lɛ dalɛ damɔ tso lɛ fɔmɔ su, he ni ejɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ‘nyɛ tso’ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli Enɛ, kɛ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, baaha yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant on the same field every single season without giving it a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Soil loses essential nutrients and beneficial micro-organisms when cropped continuously without rest. Giving the land a break or leaving it fallow allows the soil to naturally rebuild organic matter and replenish vital nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛkpaaa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni efite loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ehe nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my crops remain weak and stunted even though I apply fertilizer near the weeds growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that absorb water and nutrients much faster than crops can. Clearing weeds ensures your main crop receives the full benefit of soil moisture and applied fertilizers without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onibii titri lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he sɛɛ kwraa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into long tubes when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee tsɔnei kakadaji lɛ? Beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural protective response to drought. Reducing the leaf surface area exposed to direct sunlight helps the plant slow down water evaporation and survive hot dry spells until rain falls.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hɔmɔ hetoohamɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds often rot in the ground when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain usually warms up dry soil without providing deep, lasting moisture. If a dry spell follows, seeds get trapped in warm soil without enough water to germinate properly, causing them to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni hiɔ shi daa haaa. Kɛji hɔmɔ nifeemɔ ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers actually start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium and boron, which are needed to hold and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ boron. ni he hiaa kɛha sɛɛfimɔ kɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my crops grow dark green leaves very quickly but fail to produce big cassava tubers or large corn cobs after I put nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmei agboi loo ŋmei agbo beni mikɛ nitrogen ŋmei ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen forces plants to spend energy growing leaves and stems rather than developing roots, flowers, or fruit. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to build strong tubers and grain.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi, fɔfɔii, loo aduawai lɛ, niyenii ni ja he miihia amɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very few leaves when I plant them under tall corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei kakadaŋŋ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava requires full sunlight to manufacture food for root growth. When shaded by taller crops, cassava plants stretch upward searching for light instead of developing thick stems and large tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni ená niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ adara yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛtao la. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ yi mi wa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce smaller fruit bunches when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces plantains to compete for limited soil nutrients, underground water, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each sucker receives enough energy to produce thick trunks and heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni nuɔ nu lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow and dry up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate a nitrogen shortage, as plants shift available nutrients up to new growth, or it can be a sign of soil-borne fungal diseases spreading from the wet soil upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei tsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amɛwoɔ dalɛ hee mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ sũ ni mli efɔ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ he okadi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial root bacteria that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving behind natural nutrient fertilizer that nourishes subsequent crops like maize.
ga: Bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa mli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant need to grow. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions with poor airflow. Trimming excess branches from overhead shade trees and removing infected pods quickly will help keep the air moving and protect healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shade lɛ amli lɛ, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ aya ni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves, but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi ani oooha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of swollen roots. Adding wood ash or potassium-rich fertilizer to your field encourages the plant to direct its food down into the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ faaa lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai anɔ yɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata otsu lɛ he lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii amaje amɛbulb lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize yields when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil. Changing crops each season—such as following maize with groundnuts or cowpeas—restores essential nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ewo mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce tiny fruits when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every root has room to feed and every leaf gets enough light to make big fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã náa he ko ni ekɛyeɔ nii, ni ebaa hu naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and feature wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my maize and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli?

english: This is damage from the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the leaf whorl of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic neem seed extracts or recommended sprays directly into the center of the plant stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli lɛ fiteɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants curl up and feel sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji ota he lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies. They drink the plant's juices and leave behind a sweet liquid; spraying your leaves with a mix of mild soap and water helps wash them away and stops disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa. Amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛshiɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ amɛhe ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, usually caused by sudden heat waves, very dry soil, or waterlogged roots. Mulching around the plants with dry grass keeps the soil temperature cool and holds moisture steady so flowers can stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa kɛ enɛ baa. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo shishifãi ni mli efɔ Tsei ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i aba ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop a dark, soft, rotten spot right at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni egbo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the developing fruit, usually when watering is irregular. Watering your plants consistently helps roots draw up calcium smoothly and prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ gbo beni mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni ashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely fragile, like human babies, and their leaves burn easily under full sun. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the young plants cool and soil moist until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ waaa kwraa. Tamɔ abifao pɛpɛɛpɛ Ni ebaa lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ enɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed instead of planting them directly in the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Tomato seeds and newly sprouted plants are tiny and vulnerable to harsh weather, insects, and heavy rains. Nursing them in a small, protected area lets you hand-care for them easily until they are tough enough to survive on the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ji bibii ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Amɛtsɔsemɔ yɛ he ko bibioo Amɛhebuu lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ onine kwɛɔ amɛ mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die if I move them straight from the nursery shade into full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings grown under nursery shade get shocked if suddenly exposed to full sun and wind. You must gradually reduce their shade over a week—a process called hardening off—so they step-by-step get used to tough field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafee shoo kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa amɛnɔ trukaa. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba shi fiofio yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ hardening. Bɔni afee ni amɛle ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni wa lɛ jogbaŋŋ fitsofitso

english: How should I water my tiny vegetable seeds so they do not wash away?
ga: Mawo aduawai dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ nu. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha minɔ lɛ akaho?

english: Very young seeds need gentle, light watering using a fine sprinkle or watering can rose rather than heavy buckets. Heavy streams of water displace tiny seeds and snap fragile new shoots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ he miihia ni akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe baagi agbo. Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa bibii lɛ anajiaŋ. ni efoɔ tsei heei ni waaa lɛ amli

english: Can I apply all the fertilizer to my maize crop at once when I plant to save labor?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ shikome kɛ́ midu koni mikɛ nitsumɔ akafite?

english: Applying all fertilizer at once is like giving a baby a month’s worth of food in one sitting—it can burn the young roots and get washed away by rain. Applying fertilizer in small doses as the crop grows ensures the plant gets fed when it actually needs it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni heɔ nyɔŋ kome ha abifao yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã ni nugbɔ lɛ ahoo amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata he beni tso lɛ miida lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni ehe hiaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for growth. As the crop grows, it uses up soil nutrients fast, signaling that it needs additional fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ tsei dara Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do farmers place dry leaves and straw around the base of young plantain shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ plantain bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing dry organic matter around plants is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the soil, trapping moisture, keeping the roots cool during dry weather, and preventing weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do weeds harm my small cassava shoots so much more than my mature cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi yucca bibioo lɛ yiteŋ awui waa fe mi yucca tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young shoots have small roots and few leaves, so weeds easily steal their water, light, and nutrients. Mature cassava plants have deep roots and large canopy leaves that shade out competing weeds.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai agboi ni haa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants fall over once they start producing heavy peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbee shi beni ebɔi pepper ni tsii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Young pepper stems are often too thin to support the weight of heavy fruit loads. Tying the plants gently to wooden stakes provides support so the branches do not snap under the weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ahe tsei tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli. Fimɔ tso lɛ blɛoo kɛya tso ko he. Ebaaye ebua ni efi niji lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkafo kɛjɛ muji lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to inspect my young maize farm for fall armyworms so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikwɛɔ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ koni mana kɛji fall worms yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize plants are tender and easy for caterpillars to destroy quickly. Inspecting your farm regularly allows you to spot pests while the plants are small, preventing total crop destruction early on.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii baafite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ. Tsi ŋmɔshinii ni akafite mra lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch direct sunlight to make food. When yam leaves stay crowded flat on the ground, they rot easily in wet soil and cannot feed the plant enough to grow big yam tubers below.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ lɛ Ebaagbo oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and strong. When there is not enough food in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has left from its older bottom leaves up to feed the young top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil switches from very dry to suddenly flooded. This heat or water stress stops the flowers from forming seeds, so the plant sheds them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ loo nu mli haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why can my rice crop survive sitting in flooded water when my maize and cassava die if underwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ je nu afua lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛni mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa gboiɔ kɛji amɛ yɛ nu shishi hewɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems and roots that act like tiny breathing pipes. This allows oxygen to travel from the leaves down to the roots underwater, whereas maize and cassava roots suffocate and rot without air in the soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔnei bibii. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot make food, resulting in much smaller cassava tubers at harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ, amɛfeɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot while still hanging on the tree during heavy rains?
