ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, cool weather. Raindrops splash the fungus from damp soil onto the pods, causing them to rot rapidly if the farm canopy is too thick and dark.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ agbo oya kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ediŋ.

english: Why does my plantain stem die right after it produces one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its life. Once the main bunch matures, the main stem naturally dies off to pass all its remaining food and water to the young sucker shoots growing around its base.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei wulu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei wulu lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋmei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my maize plant growing extra thick roots out of its stem high above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ jɛɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are called brace roots. As maize grows tall and heavy with cobs, it shoots out these extra roots above the ground like wooden poles to anchor itself firmly so strong rainstorms do not blow it over.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ shishifãi. Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ da ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsii Ejieɔ shishifãi krokomɛi nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli koni ekɛmɔ ehe koni nugbɔ akatswa.

english: Why does my hot pepper plant stop growing straight up and start branching before it flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ebɔi niji ŋmɔmɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants naturally split into a 'Y' shape when they are mature because flowers and peppers only grow at the fork joints where new branches meet. This branching gives the plant a sturdy shape to hold the weight of heavy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajara amɛhe amɛwo 'Y' su mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni tsei niji heei kpeɔ yɛ lɛ pɛ. Nɛkɛ niji nɛɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ekɛfiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seedlings instead of just picking the free ones growing wild under my old trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ yɛ mitso momo lɛ shishi lɛ pɛ?

english: Seedlings growing wild under old trees often carry hidden diseases or inherit weak traits from the mother plant, whereas certified seedlings are bred to give you fast growth, high fruit yields, and strong disease resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi amli yɛ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛnáa sui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni eha oda oya, yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ bo jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does investing in high-quality seeds help me make more profit from my harvest?
ga: Te shika ni mikɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: High-quality seeds produce plants that yield larger, healthier fruits with fewer crop losses, allowing you to harvest more produce and sell it at higher market prices.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ faaa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise against buying crop seeds from unapproved local sellers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi ni akpɛlɛɛɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Unapproved vendors often sell low-quality grain meant for eating or seeds infected with pests, whereas certified suppliers sell tested seeds that are guaranteed to germinate and produce healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ ŋmaa loo dumɔwui ni ayeɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some young seedlings need shade from big trees to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii komɛi ahe hiaa ni amɛná hɔnɔ kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have delicate roots and leaves that easily dry out under full, hot sunshine. Shade protects them from extreme heat and keeps moisture in the soil while they are young.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do my seedlings look healthy under heavy shade but dry up when I plant them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shi amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plants kept in deep shade develop thin, soft leaves that are easily scorched by direct sunlight. They need to be exposed to sunlight gradually in a nursery before being moved to an open field.
ga: Tsei ni akɛtoɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Esa akɛ amɛfee fiofio Na hulu la fioo yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli.

english: What happens to seedlings if I let too many of them grow crowded together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni baaba dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji miha dumɔwui babaoo bua amɛhe naa yɛ he kome?

english: Crowded seedlings compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, and sunlight, causing them to grow thin, weak, and unhealthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baatswa he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How can I know if a new crop variety will grow well on my farm before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu lɛ?

english: You can visit local demonstration farms or consult extension officers to observe how the crop grows, how much fruit it produces, and how well it handles local soil conditions.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara ŋmɔ ko ni akɛtsɔɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo oyabi mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa, amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa.

english: Is it better to plant seeds directly into my main field or raise them as seedlings first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli loo aaadu amɛ akɛ dumɔwui klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising delicate seeds into seedlings in a protected area shields them from pests, heavy rainfall, and intense sun during their early stage, giving them a much stronger start before field planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni aduɔ awoɔ dumɔwui amli yɛ hei ni abuɔ he lɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa yɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa amɛjeɔ shishi waa dani amɛduɔ amɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ.

english: Can seedlings picked from under an old tree bring diseases to my new farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Yes, old trees often harbour fungal spores and pests in their canopy and soil, which easily infect the wild seedlings growing directly beneath them.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, tsei momo lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ amɛshishi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa koo mli dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ náa hela oya.

english: Why do improved seed varieties bear fruit much faster than the local wild seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa fe koo mli dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred by crop scientists to shorten the plant's growth cycle, allowing the crop to mature and start fruiting in a shorter time frame.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ afee kuku. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct heat. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide the young cocoa trees with essential shade and moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with small ears of corn or no yield at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo amɛwooo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and disease while maximizing leaf exposure to the sun for bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai anaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la babaoo he bɔ ni ooonyɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to preserve water and energy. Providing light shade or keeping the soil moist during hot spells helps the plants keep their flowers and form peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. ni haa hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack and split open on the vine right after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli fãa ni etswaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa trukaa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain follows a dry spell, tomato plants take up water very quickly. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit to split.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa yibii lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field before my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the soil, they naturally fertilize the field, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer needed for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and tough, resting in the soil ready to sprout immediately at the first drip of water. Crop seeds take longer because they need ideal soil moisture and seedbed preparation to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa. Ehe jɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji enine shɛ nu klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui asaamɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow and green mottled colors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the tender center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which prefer the hidden, soft inner leaves of young maize. Checking your field early and applying targeted treatments into the whorl of the plant protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ahe. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest grow slower than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa blɛoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jalɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and treated for high germination, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Saved seeds often lose vigor over generations and may carry invisible diseases or damage from storage pests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Ni ekolɛ helai ni anaaa loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii kɛjɛɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aba.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, which helps the plant stay green and grow strong, or it could mean the roots are sitting in too much water.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni edaa hewalɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and twisting during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water in extreme heat, but curling can also be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha curling aba.

english: Why are my maize plants staying very short and bushy instead of growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ji kukuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɔ lɛ?

english: Stunted maize growth is often caused by insect attacks like fall armyworms eating the growing central shoot early on, or poor soil nutrients that prevent the main stem from stretching.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ fall armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei bibioo lɛ daalɛ baa. Aloo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa bɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their small flowers without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, etsakeee efeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can feed, so the tree sheds the excess flowers to conserve its energy for a smaller number of strong pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni fa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛfee fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ fioo.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ daa?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the daytime heat is too intense or when the soil gets too dry, which stops the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollin ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look very bushy with big green leaves but produce very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea put all its energy into growing leaves rather than making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil and starve the roots of air, creating a wet environment where rot-causing fungi and bacteria easily attack the tubers underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ mlɛo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible; the leaves use sunlight to make food, which then travels down to build big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, eshiɔ shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, so the heavy weight of the fruit bunch combined with strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso yibii niji ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the field right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rain after a dry spell makes the inside of the watermelon absorb water very quickly, expanding faster than the outer rind can stretch and causing it to crack open.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ko sɛɛ lɛ haa watermelon mli loo lɛ shwieɔ nu oya waa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he kɛyashi abaanyɛ agbele.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots and chokes them.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle he. shishifãi ni okɛmiimɔ amɛ

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my farm when the soil is dry or after a heavy rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after rain. Plant roots need water to drink up the nutrients in the fertilizer, whereas putting fertilizer on very dry soil can burn the crop's roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛnu niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves to suck out the plant's juice, or by a sickness passed to the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat becomes too intense, when the soil dries out during the flowering stage, or when small insects attack the blossoms before the fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a open place with full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out and burn easily in direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantain to protect them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down to make the yam tuber underneath the ground grow big and heavy.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow strong and bear big bunches, while others stay weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi ahe wa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? while some are still weak

english: Plantain suckers with thin, sword-like leaves have stronger roots connected to the main bulb, making them grow faster and yield better than suckers that start out with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ, ni yɔɔ baai bibii, tamɔ klante, yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni kɛ bulb wulu lɛ tsaa. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai fe ŋmeii ni jeɔ shishi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant will begin to crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi gbee be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds growing near my young crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they quickly drink up the water, take the soil nutrients, and block sunlight from your young crops, leaving them weak and underfed.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛnuɔ nu oya. Na niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni otsi hulu la ni jɛɔ odumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black or get moldy when I put it in bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo baagi mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still contains hidden water inside the cob. If you bag it immediately, heat and trapped moisture cause mold and tiny fungi to grow and rot the grain.
ga: Abele ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni akɛtee ŋmei lɛ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ baagi wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. shweremɔ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmaa baanyɛ afite

english: Why should I cut or trim around the bottom of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafo plantains shishi lɛ?

english: Trimming the base of your plantain plant keeps it from becoming overly big and wild. It opens up space, controls excess shoots, and keeps your farm neat so nutrients go straight into making good fruit.
ga: Ni afoɔ plantains lɛ ashishi koni amɛkafee agbo tsɔ. Egbeleɔ gbɛ. Kudɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya yibii kpakpai afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to use my cutlass to trim the base of a plantain plant?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsɔne kuku baafo plantains shishi?

english: Yes, using a clean cutlass to carefully prune around the base of the plant is a good modern practice. It helps clear unwanted foliage and keeps the growing stem neat without damaging the main plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ dade ni he tse tsuɔ nii lɛ, afoɔ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ Abuɔ tso lɛ shishi akɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai ni ataooo lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi feɔ fɛo ni efiteee tso titri lɛ.

english: What happens if I just let my plantain plant grow as big as it wants without trimming it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha mi-plantain lɛ da bɔ ni esumɔɔ ni mifooo nɔ ko?

english: If a plantain grows unchecked without trimming, it wastes valuable soil energy on extra leaves and unwanted stems. Managing its size keeps the plant manageable and strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ dara ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ loo afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ, Enɛ baaha hewalɛ ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ni ataooo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: In the past, our parents didn't use cutlasses to trim plantains, so why should I do it now?
ga: Be ko ni eho lɛ, wɔfɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii kukuji tsuuu nii kɛfolɔ plantains. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofee lɛ bianɛ?

english: Older traditional methods often allowed plantains to grow wild, which caused overcrowded fields and smaller harvests. Modern trimming keeps the crops healthier, neater, and more productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ haa plantains lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔji lɛ ayiɔ obɔ kɛ nibii ni baa lɛ faaa. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. ni yɔɔ fɛo fe tsutsu lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ

english: How does trimming my plantain tree help me deal with weeds around it?
ga: Plantains lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ tsuɔ nii. Te plantain lɛ daa tɛŋŋ?

english: When you trim and manage the base properly, it changes how light reaches the ground and allows the plantain to outcompete surrounding weeds, causing weeds around the tree base to naturally die off.
ga: Kɛji ofo shishitoo lɛ ni okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ La ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa plantain lɛ ni eyeɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ kunim, ni ehaa jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ daa. Tso lɛ shishi gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the weeds around my plantain start dying off after I manage the base of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi plantains lɛ bɔi gbele beni mitsa shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Proper base management and broad leaf coverage cut off necessary sunlight and nutrients to the weeds underneath, suppressing their growth naturally without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Shishitoo nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ baai babaoo ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baafo hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. ni etsĩɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ naa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do some plantain sprouts look messy while others grow up neat and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains komɛi feɔ basabasa nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi daraa fɛfɛo ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Sprouts look neat when excess suckers and base leaves are trimmed regularly. If left unpruned, too many shoots fight for space and look chaotic.
ga: Sprouts lɛ baafee fɛo kɛji afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛ shishi baai lɛ daa. Kɛji akɛ ashi ni afolɔko tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, tsei babaoo baatswa he akaŋ ni amɛbaafee basabasa.

english: How does trimming the extra shoots help the new plantain sprouting up?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii heei ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing weak or extra shoots allows the main new sprout to get all the light, water, and soil food it needs, making it sprout up looking strong and neat.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri hee lɛ naa la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ. Ha eda ni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efee fɛo.

english: Does keeping my plantain field looking clean and neat really affect how the crops grow?
ga: Ani mi plantain saatso lɛ nɔ ni mihaa ehe tseɔ ni efeɔ fɛo lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, a neat plantain field reduces pests, improves airflow around the stem base, stops weeds from stealing food, and helps your crops sprout cleanly.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aju niyenii. ni oye obua ni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if I have pruned the base of my plantain plant correctly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mifo mi-plantain lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You will know it is done right when the base looks tidy, the new shoot sprouts up neatly, and the surrounding weeds start to clear out naturally.
ga: Obaale akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ fee fɛo ni eyɛ fɛo. Tsofɔi heei kwɛ̃ɔ fɛfɛo. kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Jeɔ shishi egbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally prefer partial shade because their young root systems cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what high heat evaporates from the leaves. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block harsh direct sunlight, the leaves overheat and burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ baanyɛ adɔ fe nine ni amɛshã.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits in waterlogged soil without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, which suffocates them and allows soil fungi to break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread out near the surface instead of deep taproots. As the heavy bunch of fruit grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to push over unless it is propped up with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa nu lɛ hiɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji aduawai lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli, ja tsei fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose maximum leaf area to direct sunlight, which energy powers tuber growth under the soil. Staking also lifts the leaves away from wet soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie baai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as intense heat waves, lack of water, or low nutrients in the soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's defense mechanism to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛtoɔ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni dalɛ shihilɛi lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken while growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the developing fruit during dry spells or irregular watering. Without steady water to move calcium through the plant, the tissue at the bottom of the fruit collapses.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ ni baaha calcium aya tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, Faji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafite.

english: Why does my young maize look pale yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to produce green chlorophyll and build foliage. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore dark green, fast-growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to absorb nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When these plants die, the stored nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the following crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and thin even when I rain-water the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ mikɛ nu haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that compete directly with your crops for light, root space, soil nutrients, and moisture. Even with enough water, crops stay small because weeds steal the plant food required for growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha la, shishifãi, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛji nu yɛ po. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ faaa lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ tsei lɛ aniyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm leaves roll up tightly during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry air and hot winds draw moisture out of leaves quickly. Oil palms roll or curl their foliage to reduce surface exposure to the wind, keeping internal moisture from evaporating until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieee shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Yam vines need to expose their leaves to direct sunlight to create energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and helping the plant build bigger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stems when planting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni otsɔɔ gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upwards. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downwards first before turning up, which wastes energy and leads to smaller roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu cassava tsei ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛ hiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛya shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: No, planting crops too closely makes them fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong stalks and larger, fully developed maize ears.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni he wa kɛ ŋmãa toi ni dara ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the earth cool and traps moisture so the soil stays wet longer. It also stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of older leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants move nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground. Planting them alongside maize feeds the soil without forcing you to rely entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Edumɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves drying up and dropping off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and high heat cause plants to lose water faster than roots can draw it from dry soil. Cocoa trees shed leaves to conserve water and prevent the trunk and branches from dying completely.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer on the same day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ woɔ mli yɛ gbi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young seeds and tiny seedlings only need a very small amount of food at first. Adding too much fertilizer at planting can burn tender roots, and heavy rains will wash the excess away before the plants grow big enough to use it.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii Niyenii fioo pɛ he hiaa yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and small brownish droppings inside the center fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli

english: This pattern is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot. They feed on the tender young leaves during the night or early morning, leaving holes and waste behind as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ loo leebi. Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often brought on by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rains or watering.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato ni shishi edɔ ni ebote mli lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ teŋ.

english: How can I tell if my coconut trees are struggling because of too little water in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ miiwuu kɛ nu fioo tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When coconut trees lack water, their lower leaves turn yellow and droop down around the trunk, and young nuts start dropping before they mature. Putting dried plant leaves around the base of the trunk helps keep moisture in the soil during hot dry spells.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he, ni ŋmeii lɛ baabɔi shwiemɔ dani amɛdara. Tso baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and not over-fertilizing helps the plant hold onto flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green so the plant can make food and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii koni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for roots to spread and leaves to catch sunlight.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni baai lɛ hu aná hulu la.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often tricks farmers because the ground underneath remains dry. You should dig down a few inches to confirm the soil is wet deep down before planting, so young roots do not dry out if the rain pauses for a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shishigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Esa akɛ ofo shi inchi fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii 2-3.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly when they are in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than farmed crops, so they drink the soil water and eat the nutrients before your crops can get to them, essentially starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by heat stress. Keeping insects away and ensuring regular watering helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Kooloi ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shades the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I prune or trim the bottom leaves of my crop plants as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Cutting off lower yellow or touching-the-ground leaves allows air to move freely around the base of the plant, preventing fungal diseases and forcing the plant to send energy up to building fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo baai ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle tso lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ heyeli mli Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni onyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛtsu hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii

english: What is Prekese, and is it a good tree crop for me to plant on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji Prekese ni ani eji jwɛi tso kpakpa ni esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Prekese (Aidan fruit) is a native tree that produces medicinal and aromatic spice pods. It has strong local market demand and can be integrated into traditional farming systems, though it takes several years to mature and produce heavy yields.
ga: Prekese (Aidan aduawai) ji maŋ tso ko ni woɔ tsofa kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ŋɔɔ. Kuu lɛ mli jarayeli he nibii ni ataoɔ waa yɛ. ni abaanyɛ akɛwo blema okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi amli Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ afii babaoo dani ekwɛɔ ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa moŋ.

english: Why would an agricultural officer advise me not to plant certain trees next to my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu tsei komɛi yɛ he ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ lɛ?

english: Some trees grow large roots and dense canopies that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from neighboring crops, while others might attract pests or diseases that harm nearby plants.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi baanyɛ agbala kooloi loo helai ni yeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ awui lɛ,.

english: How long does a tree crop like Prekese usually take before it starts producing fruits?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani Prekese tso ko kwɛɔ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Most native tree crops take between 3 to 5 years after planting to produce fruits. While waiting for them to mature, you can intercrop fast-growing food crops like corn or vegetables between the young trees.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei babaoo heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni amɛdara Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Abaanyɛ akɛwo tsei bibii ateŋ

english: Why should I process my harvested crops before selling them instead of selling them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ ahe nii dani mahɔ̃ɔ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Processing crops—such as drying, chopping, or grinding them—extends their shelf life and increases their market value, allowing you to sell to buyers who pay higher prices for ready-to-use products.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ, tamɔ ni amɛgbiɔ, amɛfoɔ, loo amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa amɛjara lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ohaa mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni afee klalo akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Can I process my harvested crops by hand if I do not have money to buy machines?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji kpa lɛ ahe nii? Kɛji obɛ shika ni okɛbaahe tsɔnei?

english: Yes, many traditional crops like Prekese can be sun-dried and processed manually using basic farm tools, though using machines becomes necessary when handling very large quantities quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ blema nibii babaoo ni aduɔ, tamɔ Prekese lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ niji atsu he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔnei ahe miihia beni esa akɛ atsu nibii babaoo ahe nii oya lɛ moŋ.

english: How can I stop my harvested crops from spoiling while waiting for a buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ be mli ni emɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Drying your crops thoroughly under the sun and storing them in dry, well-ventilated bags off the bare ground protects them from mold, rot, and insects until you find a buyer.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni okɛto kotokui ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ amli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe. fitemɔ kɛ ŋmeii kɛyashi obaana mɔ ni baahe

english: How can I produce a large quantity of crops to supply big buyers in town?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni mikɛha mɛi wuji ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: To yield large quantities, you need proper plant spacing, healthy soil management using fertilizers or compost, and effective pest control. Alternatively, you can partner with neighboring farmers to combine harvests.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ nibii babaoo aba Esa akɛ oná gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui jogbaŋŋ Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ afee ekome kɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ ekome.

english: Where can I get high-quality seedlings when I want to start growing a new crop?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni miisumɔ ni mabɔi tsei heei akwɛmɔ?

english: You can source certified seedlings from Ministry of Agriculture nurseries, trusted local extension officers, or registered commercial farm nurseries to ensure the plants are healthy and high-yielding.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ Ministry of Agriculture ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Kuu lɛ mli shweremɔ nitsulɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ loo jarayeli ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli nibii akwɛmɔhe ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I find buyers for my crops before harvest time arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana mɛi ni baahe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can connect with local processors, join a farmers' cooperative, or ask your extension officer to link you directly with traders and bulk buyers looking for reliable producers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi lɛ abɔ. Kɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko mli Aloo bi wɔ nibii ahe nitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛkɛ jarayelɔi kɛ jarayelɔi babaoo ni miitao nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ abɔ bo tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is proper spacing important when planting tree crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he hiaa beni aduɔ tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, air circulation, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong and yield well without crowding out other nearby plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai ni amɛkabote tsei krokomɛi amli. bɛŋkɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and leaf skin that scorch easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a natural canopy that shields the young cocoa from direct sunlight and keeps the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass (called mulching) keeps the soil cool, traps rainwater so it doesn't evaporate quickly, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli koni ekatsɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings so they yield big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana bulbs wuji?

english: Giving cassava plants about one meter of space between each other allows their underground roots enough room to expand into thick tubers without competing with neighboring plants for light, water, and food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up toward direct sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the vines off the damp ground onto stakes prevents leaf diseases and ensures the plant directs its energy down into making large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ he helai anaa, ni ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ awo shi ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my maize seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the ground at least palm-deep twice. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the dry weather returns for a few days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, onineshi shii enyɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii fioo krokomɛi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-decayed animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer returns the green color and strength to the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers drop off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plant is stressed by irregular watering or extreme heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root zone helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the juice from under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with a gentle mixture of soapy water or neem oil helps remove these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of the maize plant during the hot day and feed at night. Applying neem extract or recommended pest treatments directly into the plant's central funnel early in the morning destroys them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same spot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests multiply. Alternating maize with cowpeas or groundnuts returns good nitrogen food to the soil and starves out maize-loving pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen kpakpa. ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very soft leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava above them to act as umbrellas and retain moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize seeds take several days to sprout out of the dirt after I plant them, even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Seeds go through a waking-up process after planting. They must absorb water to soften their outer shell and grow roots underground first before you can see the green shoot push up through the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui atsɔ teemɔŋ gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛjie nu koni amɛha kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛkwɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani ana ŋmeii eŋɔli ni miitsi amɛhe kɛmiitsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I apply fertilizer to my crops today, why don't I see them grow bigger by the next morning?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɛnɛ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minaaa akɛ eda enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer takes time to dissolve in soil water before the roots can drink it up. Once absorbed, the plant uses that food gradually to build leaves and stem tissue over several days.
ga: Be he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii atsɔ shikpɔŋ nu mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ eŋɔ mli pɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ nakai niyenii lɛ baatsu nii fiofio. koni ekɛfee baai kɛ tso lɛ mli fãji gbii babaoo

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and look like they are dying right after I move them from the nursery bed into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants breaks tiny feeder roots that absorb water, causing transplant shock. The plant Wilts temporarily until it settles into its new home and grows new root tips to drink water again.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ baafo niyenii bibii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. ni kɛ transplant shock baa Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi ebaahi eshia hee lɛ mli. ni amɛkwɛ shishifãi heei koni amɛnu nu ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and light, leaving all the plants starved and unable to grow big fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baawuu kɛha nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la haa tsei fɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: When the soil has too much leaf-growing fertilizer (nitrogen) or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves on top instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ŋmɔshi nibii (nitrogen) babaoo lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or when there is too little water, because the plant gets stressed and loses the energy needed to turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my yam as soon as the very first rain falls in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli pɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period, which leaves the hot dirt dry enough to bake and destroy the soft young shoots before regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa ni ekɛshã ni egbe ŋmeii bibii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield if my crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo hu?

english: Even if crops are tall, weeds have fast-spreading roots under the soil that swallow up fertilizer and water before your crops can reach them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa moŋ Shi jwɛi hu yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava curling up and turning light yellow instead of staying broad and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Curled yellow leaves on cassava are a sign of mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck plant juices and pass a sickness to the crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji mosaic hela he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep dying when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and drying winds. Without shade trees or companion crops like plantains to shield them, the intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil, killing the tender seedlings.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei krokomɛi ni buɔ wɔhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gboiɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: If you plant maize too deep, the seeds will waste all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to reach daylight. This causes them to rot underground or sprout as very weak, uneven plants.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui fiteɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ waa koni amɛshɛ la he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛshwereɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ waa ni amɛfeee ekome lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot spell before the main rains actually start. If you plant right away, the soil will quickly dry out again and kill your young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ waa sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya ekoŋŋ ni enɛ baanyɛ agbe otso bibioo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a inverted 'V'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which is a key food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding fertilizer like NPK or compost will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your corn crop grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-corn tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Growing cassava continuously in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients it needs from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack cassava to multiply in the ground year after year.
ga: Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei be fɛɛ be yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops so much even if I give my plants fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than your crops and act like thieves. They steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your plants weak and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties when planting prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or the soil gets too dry, the tomato plant gets stressed. To protect itself from losing water, it drops its flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ hewalɛ baawo yibii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers spoil so quickly if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: When the soil gets soaked with too much rain water, air cannot reach the roots underground. This causes the cassava roots to suffocate and rot inside the wet soil before you can harvest them.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nu lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Where can I get reliable, high-quality seeds in Ghana if I want to expand my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɛji miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) office or Seed Production Directorate (SPDS) stations across Ghana, where extension officers provide certified, high-yielding seeds meant for strong crop growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara omaŋ ni ji Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) nitsumɔhe loo Dumɔwui Afeemɔ He Nitsumɔhe (SPDS) ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ. he ni shweremɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa.

english: Can I just use seeds saved from my previous harvest, or should I buy new ones from the agricultural office?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ atsu nii? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Getting fresh, certified seeds from an agricultural office yields much better results because saved seeds often lose their strength over time and can carry diseases from the previous season.
ga: Kɛ́ aná dumɔwui heei ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ, ebaaha yibii kpakpai babaoo aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why is it better for me to start my seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery protects young, delicate sprouts from intense sun, dry soil, and insects, allowing them to build strong root systems before facing harsh field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa amɛma shi dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa kpeɔ.

english: How do I know when my seedlings in the nursery are ready to be moved to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting when they have grown 3 to 4 strong leaves and a sturdy stem, which usually takes about 3 to 4 weeks after planting the seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui kɛji amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ tso ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my seedlings look weak and wilt right after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by root disruption during moving. Planting late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps seedlings recover quickly from heat and shock.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi lɛ amligbalamɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature and yield much faster than the ones I traditional use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specially bred to absorb soil nutrients efficiently and develop flowers and fruits quickly, reducing the time needed from planting to harvest.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai oya Enɛ haa be ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant a very large quantity of seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaa nibii bibii.

english: Why are young seedlings in my nursery attacked more easily by pests than full-grown plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants have soft leaves and tender stems that insects easily eat, and they lack the deep roots and energy reserves that mature plants use to survive pest damage.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kooloi yeɔ amɛ oya. ni amɛbɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni tsei ni eda lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which types of crops should I choose if I need quick money from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji akɛ shika he miihia mi oya kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Short-duration crops such as vegetables (tomatoes, pepper) or early-maturing maize give you quick yields within a few months, bringing faster economic returns to support your home.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai (tomato, peppers) loo ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa shika helɛtemɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo baa oya koni akɛha oshia lɛ niyenii.

english: How does using high-yielding crop varieties increase my total farm income?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ mli shika fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: High-yielding crop varieties produce far more bags of food per plot of land without requiring extra space, giving you more surplus produce to sell for gain at the local market.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ woɔ niyenii kotokui babaoo kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he kroko afata he. Enɛ haa onáa nibii babaoo ni fa fe nine ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I planted them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are old, damaged by heat or moisture during storage, planted too deep, or if the soil lacks enough moisture to activate the seed's growth.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji amɛgbɔ. Dɔlɛ loo fɛ̃i fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni adu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I check if my stored corn seeds are still alive before I go to plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo dani madu amɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a moist cloth or wet paper for 3 to 5 days. If 8 or more grow sprouts, your seeds are good to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ loo wolo ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai je kpo lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant corn seeds saved from my previous harvest instead of buying certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji oshara lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests often lose their strength over time, carry hidden diseases, or produce lower yields compared to fresh, certified seeds that are treated for high germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase ni atsa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo lɛ he lɛ yɛ.
