english: Is it good to plant my corn immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually risky because the first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch. If the soil dries out completely, the newly sprouted seeds will die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Oshara yɛ be fɛɛ mli ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gboiɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do seeds planted early in the year sometimes dry up inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ gbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early in the year, the soil top layer is very hot. If there is not enough steady rain, the high soil heat dries out the delicate root shoot as soon as it tries to open.
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli dɔɔ waa. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ faaa lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbele pɛ.

english: How deep should I put maize seeds into the ground when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (about the depth of your thumb knuckle). Planting too deep starves the seed of energy before it reaches sunlight, while planting too shallow exposes it to drying heat and birds.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee ŋmãa nineshi ŋmãa lɛ mlibotemɔ). Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye dumɔwui ni hewalɛ yeɔ amɛ lɛ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ okpoi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my corn seeds rot in the dirt when heavy rains fall right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need air in the soil to breathe and grow. Heavy rains can flood the soil, filling all air spaces with water, which suffocates and rots the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Okɛ nu awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do ants and birds dig up my corn seeds before they can grow into plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi shwieɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Planted seeds are a rich source of food for birds, ants, and rodents. Covering the seeds properly with soil and using recommended seed treatment chemicals keeps pests away.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ji niyenii ni jara wa kɛha okpoi, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ha dumɔwui ahe jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa dumɔwui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Can leaving my seed bag in direct sunlight ruin the seeds before planting day?
ga: Ani dumɔwui kotoku ko ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani dumɔ gbi lɛ aba?

english: Yes, direct heat from harsh sunlight bakes the seeds inside the bag, killing the living embryo inside so it will never sprout when planted.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Egbeɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛɛɛ.

english: Why do some seeds sprout weak and yellow even when they manage to grow out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Young plants turn weak and yellow if the soil lacks basic nutrients like nitrogen, or if the roots are damaged by bad soil conditions or underground insects early on.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii fite shishifãi lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, a main food crops need to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titri ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next crop grow bigger?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni efee tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial germs on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plants die, this nitrogen stays in the ground as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ helai fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot in the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When too much rainwater collects in the soil without draining away, the roots drown and fungi attack them, causing them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants droop during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant temporarily droops to protect itself from heat, but usually recovers in the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves catch sunlight to make food for the plant. When the vine climbs high on a stake, its leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to make big yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛyaa akulashiŋi kakadaji lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees give small bunches when I leave many young shoots growing around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Pruning extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the mother plant gets enough nutrients to grow a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they do not have enough water, shade, or soil nutrients to support full pods, or if tiny insects called midges did not visit the flowers to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha amɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ eyaaa fɔfɔi amli koni ekɛ pollination aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and curling like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves, or a plant virus spread by these insects that distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: What makes the bottom of my green tomato fruits turn black and flat before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ po?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It often happens when the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet, disturbing how the plant drinks up nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni trukaa lɛ, edɔ waa. ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa

english: Stored seeds can lose their life if kept in hot or damp places, or if weevils damage the tiny living embryo inside. Keeping seeds cool, dry, and sealed preserves their strength so they germinate properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kpata ŋmeii ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo lɛ ahiɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni oooha amɛhe ajɔɔ, amɛgbi, ni amɛtsi amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ ahi shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops no longer grow as big as they used to on this same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa dɔŋŋ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, farming the same piece of land continuously removes natural nutrients from the soil. Without giving the land time to rest or adding nutrients back, the soil loses its natural richness, causing crops to grow smaller and produce lower yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its natural richness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks essential nutrients, crops often look small or stunted, their leaves turn pale or yellow instead of deep green, and the overall harvest is significantly lower than in past years.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii loo amɛhe ejɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ.

english: Why does old farming land seem to lose its strength over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi shikpɔji momo lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Every crop planted on the land draws out essential nutrients to grow. When crops are harvested and removed, those nutrients go with them, gradually draining the soil's natural fertility unless it is replenished.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashɛrɛ ashwie lɛ Nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛ amɛ baaya, ni amɛbaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ fiofio. ja awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: What does fertilizer actually do to help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa yɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the plant and soil. It puts back essential nutrients that the soil is missing, giving crops the nourishment they need to grow strong stems, healthy leaves, and bigger produce.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa. baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni anáa babaoo

english: What is ammonia fertilizer, and why would my crops need it?
ga: Mɛni ji ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Ammonia fertilizer supplies crops with nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient that drives plant growth. It gives plants energy to build strong roots, grow rapidly, and maintain healthy green foliage.
ga: Ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. shwereɔ oya ni eha baai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are there different types of ammonia fertilizer available for farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ni okwaafoi baanyɛ aná lɛ?

english: Different types of ammonia fertilizer release nitrogen into the soil at different speeds and react differently to moisture and heat, allowing farmers to select the specific type that best suits their soil and crop needs.
ga: Ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. ni etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛji hulutsoo kɛ latsaa eba Enɛ haa okwaafoi halaa tso pɔtɛɛ ni sa amɛshikpɔŋ kɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiamɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can fertilizer restore the strength of my soil so crops grow well again?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, applying the right fertilizer replenishes missing nutrients in worn-out soil, giving new crops the immediate nourishment required to grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje yɛ sũ ni efite lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei heei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. When crops do not get enough nitrogen from the soil, they cannot produce the green color necessary to make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Crops that receive enough soil nutrients will have thick stems, vibrant deep green leaves, steady growth, and will produce full, healthy fruit or grains.
ga: Tsei ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni mli tse. baai eŋɔli ni mli tse ni yaa nɔ edaa ni ehaa aduawai loo ŋmaa ni eye emuu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will applying too much fertilizer harm my soil or my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ loo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn crop roots, cause leaf tip damage, and alter soil balance, which is why it is important to apply only the recommended amount for your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. fiteɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ pɛ atsu nii kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops need chemical spraying or 'medicine' even when I do not see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai loo ‘tsofai’ afɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi moŋ?

english: Preventative spraying acts like a protective shield for plants. Applying crop protection chemicals before pests or fungal diseases appear prevents infections from starting, keeping your crop healthy throughout the growing season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibi ni buɔ tsei ahe. Tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akɛwoɔ mli dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ tsiɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekaje shishi. ni oha onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How often should I apply protective chemical treatments to my cocoa trees before the main harvest in December?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he awo kookoo tsei ahe dani akpa ŋmaa titri lɛ yɛ December mli?

english: Cocoa trees usually require preventative fungicide spraying every three to four weeks during the wet season leading up to December to prevent black pod disease from destroying the pods before harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, biɔ ni afɔse tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ daa otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashi December. Bɔni afee ni black pod hela lɛ akafite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together to spray my maize field faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ afutu mli koni mikɛshwie ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli oya?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can cause reactions that burn plant leaves or render the treatment useless. Always check with an extension officer to confirm which products can be safely combined.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko aba ni shã tso lɛ baai lɛ loo eha tsofa lɛ afee yaka. Kwɛmɔ ohiɛyaa najiaŋdamɔlɔ be fɛɛ be koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nibii ni abaanyɛ akɛfata he shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it dangerous to harvest and sell my vegetables immediately after applying crop protection chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ makpa mi-vegetables lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: Yes, every crop chemical has a required waiting period after spraying. Harvesting too soon leaves toxic chemical residues on the food, making it unsafe for consumers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ. ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve internal water. The plant enters a resting state and will produce fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he. Tso lɛ baabote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli ni ebaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly into narrow tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to reduce their exposed surface area, which slows down water loss through evaporation during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa fe fɛɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ baa shi fioo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to protect them from heat stress during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can an extension officer help me create a schedule for spraying and caring for my crops?
ga: Te extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mato be ni akɛbaafɔse miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: An extension officer can assess your specific crop, soil, and local weather conditions to build a step-by-step application calendar that tells you exactly when and how much product to use.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi, shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Koni ofee shika helɛtemɔ kalanda ni tsɔɔ bo be pɔtɛɛ kɛ nibii abɔ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of a disease or simply because of a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigbo loo nu ni bɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Drought-stressed crops generally wilt together across the whole field during hot hours and recover at night, whereas diseased plants show dark spots, rotting stems, or stunted growth that remains even after rain.
ga: Tsei ni hɔmɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ gbee yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso ni egbo loo dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ.

english: Can I use household soap or human medicine to treat diseases on my crop leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shia samla loo gbɔmɔ tsofa atsa helai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: No, household soaps and human medicines contain ingredients that can damage plant tissues, alter soil chemistry, and leave harmful chemicals in the food you grow. Only use approved agricultural products.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni baanyɛ afite tsei amli fãji yɛ shia samlai kɛ adesai tsofai amli. Tsakemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsofai ni oshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ pɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I tell if the farm chemicals I buy in the market are good quality and safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Genuine farm chemicals come from certified distributors with clear seals, registration numbers, and proper packaging. Buying reliable, tested products protects your crops from damage caused by fake or ineffective chemicals.
ga: Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. kɛ stamp ni mli ka shi faŋŋ Registration number kɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli Nibii ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ahemɔ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ tsofai ni amalei loo tsofai ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ahe.

english: Is it really necessary to buy farming chemicals from approved companies instead of cheaper sellers in the market?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni ahe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe nii kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni jara waaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, approved companies supply genuine products that actually protect your plants. Cheap, unapproved chemicals are often diluted or fake, which can ruin your crops and waste your hard-earned money.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔhei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni buɔ otso lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ haa. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni jara waaa ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ nu mli loo afeeɔ amalei. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ, ni efite oshika ni okɛtsu nii waa lɛ.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my vegetables even after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi aduawai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects can survive if you use weak, fake, or incorrect chemicals, or if you spray at the wrong time. Using dependable, quality insecticides recommended for your specific crop ensures the pests are effectively controlled.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni bɛ hewalɛ, amale, loo ejaaa tsu nii. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal diseases like black pod or leaf blight that thrive in wet weather. Applying quality, approved fungicides helps protect your trees so your farm can stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli ewo diŋ loo baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ okɛ tsofa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I use weedkiller on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds return fast if the herbicide used is low quality, wrongly mixed, or not meant for that specific weed type. Using genuine, recommended herbicides kills weeds down to the roots and keeps your farm clean longer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ oya kɛji tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ehiii. Akɛfutumɔ ni ejaaa Aloo afeee nakai jwɛi pɔtɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yi, ni ji anɔkwale lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe jwɛi lɛ kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɔ̃ɔ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or the fertilizer applied was washed away or of poor quality. Applying dependable fertilizers gives your maize the strength to grow dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ efo loo ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha o-abele lɛ aná hewalɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when plants lack key nutrients or are stressed by pests and disease. Using proper foliage fertilizers and pest control products helps the plant retain flowers and produce plenty of healthy fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli kɛ nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my crops grow very slowly compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops grow slowly when the soil lacks food or when hidden pests damage the roots. Providing quality soil nutrients and plant protection products helps your farm flourish and grow at its best speed.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa fiofio kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni okɛaaha lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni eyaa hiɛ ni edaa oya.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical to mix so I don't burn my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛfutu mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, kaashã ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Every genuine chemical product comes with clear measurement instructions on the label. Following these instructions or asking an extension officer prevents chemical burn and keeps your crops healthy.
ga: Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ fɛɛ baaná susumɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji onyiɛ ŋaawoi nɛɛ asɛɛ loo obi o-extension nitsulɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofai akashã bo, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do to make sure the chemicals I use on my farm don't harm my soil for next year?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Using approved, high-quality products in the correct quantities ensures pests are controlled without leaving harmful toxins in the soil, allowing you to farm successfully year after year.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eshiuuu tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Yelikɛbuamɔ ni okɛyeɔ omanye yɛ okwaayeli mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life restores their healthy green color and helps them grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why does leaving dry leaves and weeds on top of my soil help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering your soil with dry leaves or plant grass acts like a protective blanket called mulch. It traps moisture in the ground so water doesn't evaporate quickly under the hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents the sun from baking your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo tsei jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa hulu la lɛ ashã otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land year after year without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural fertilizer and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: What causes small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa lɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the tender heart of the plant to feed. Spraying an approved insecticide directly into the leaf center early in the morning or late evening kills the worms before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ tsei atsuii ni mli jɔ lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown, rot, and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions with poor air movement. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into your farm, along with spraying copper fungicide, prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛfata akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap out of the young leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating your pepper garden with neem oil spray or an insecticide keeps these pests away so leaves can open flat and feed the fruits.
ga: Koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu o-pepper abɔɔ lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akaŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai lɛ agbele amɛhe ni amɛha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot in the ground when the rainfall is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because roots need air to breathe just like humans do. Planting your cassava stems on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ, tamɔ adesai lɛ, shishifãi lɛ hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: A plantain stem can only share a limited amount of water and food from the soil. Leaving too many small suckers forces the mother plant to fight for food, resulting in small bunches; keeping only one or two strong follow-up suckers guarantees large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ baanyɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ Shi babaoo lɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko Kɛ́ ajie tso kome loo enyɔ ni he wa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii baa.

english: Yam vines produce tubers using sunlight captured by their leaves. Staking lifts the vines high into the air so maximum leaf space hits the sun, boosting energy production into building large yam tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu lɛ ashɛ he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Ehaa hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn dark and rotten before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering or dry spells. Giving your tomato plants steady, even watering and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps the fruit grow firm without rotting from the bottom.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ. Tomato Tsei lɛ Ahe Shihilɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tso ashwishwɛ loo lime wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ adara be fɛɛ be ni amɛfiteee kɛjɛɛɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides them with vital shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cashew seedlings stop growing leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew plants naturally slow down their top growth during dry periods to save water and energy, focusing their strength on sending roots deeper into the ground to find moisture.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eyatao ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaves and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Amɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves and transmitting plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun, which helps the plant manufacture enough food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds germinate early without steady moisture, the tender roots dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ oya ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli daa. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: A good cassava cutting should come from a mature, healthy plant, be about thumb-thick, have visible eye buds, and show fresh moist wood inside when cut.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpai ni afo lɛ ajɛ tsei ni eda ni amɛhe wa amli. Eshɛɔ tamɔ tsitsi bibioo ko. yɛ hiŋmɛii ni baanyɛ ana ni etsɔɔ tso hee ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ mli kɛji afo

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, space, and fertilizer, effectively stealing the nourishment your crops need to produce well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu, hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves, but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling its roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye niyenii ni ekɛwo eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before tiny pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from dry soil, extreme heat, or attacks from tiny insects like capsids. Providing light shade and keeping the soil moist helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants bloom with plenty of flowers but fail to produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called thrips often attack cowpea flowers and destroy them from the inside before pods can form. Protecting the flowers during the early blooming stage allows pods to grow successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli dani ŋmeii feɔ. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease where bacteria block the tiny tubes inside the stem that carry water from roots to leaves. Rotating your field with non-susceptible crops like maize helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tsiɔ paipii bibii anaa. Yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli Kɛ akɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmɔji ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Why does my yam plant need a tall wooden stake to climb on to produce large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which travels down the stem to build heavy, thick tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni efee bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves develop dark brown spots and dry up early during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture creates an ideal environment for fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka to spread on plantain leaves. Spacing your plants properly allows airflow and sunlight to dry the leaves and slow down the disease.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka ni gbɛɔ eshwaa plantain baai lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni haa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa helai sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field make my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often because soil watering is uneven. Regular watering helps the roots absorb calcium steadily from the soil up into the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or gliricidia to protect them from heat stress and keep the soil moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If cassava stems are planted too close, the roots fight underground for space, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly—about one meter apart—gives each plant enough room to form big, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa Kɛ́ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by high heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Ensuring steady moisture and protecting the plants from pests helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpea under my maize crop help suppress weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akashɛ he?

english: Cowpea spreads quickly along the ground, creating a dense leafy cover that blocks sunlight from reaching the soil. Without direct sunlight, weed seeds cannot germinate and grow easily.
ga: Cowpea gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni mli tse ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ ni amɛdaraaa oya.

english: Why do I need to put stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can manufacture food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and increasing the overall size of your yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ebai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potato lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids, or a virus they carry. Spraying recommended organic treatments or mild chemical controls early stops these pests from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Akɛ organic spraying loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ he ŋaawoo haa mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the plant roots decay, that natural food remains behind to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji legumes ni yɔɔ nodes krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni tso shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the heat of the day. Watering during the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before roots can take it up, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch the plant.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, food, and energy from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains instead of many small ones.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo. Yɛ tsei bibii babaoo najiaŋ

english: What is the main reason I need to put wooden stakes in my farm to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch plenty of sunlight to produce food for the crop. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, preventing leaves from rotting on damp soil and allowing the tubers underground to grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why should I put my stakes in the ground right after planting yam tubers instead of waiting for the vines to grow first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni wain tso lɛ akwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ

english: Setting up stakes early prevents you from accidentally driving a stick through the delicate growing seed tuber or its fresh roots underneath the soil once growth begins.
ga: Okɛ ohe awo mli mra Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okatswa tsei niji kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi heei anɔ yɛ oshara mli kɛji amɛdalɛ je shishi pɛ.

english: Does the height of the stake I select for my climbing crops affect the harvest size?
ga: Ani tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mihalaa kɛha mi tsei ni mikɛkwɔɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ da ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, taller stakes (around 2 to 3 meters) give the vines more room to spread their foliage. More leaf area exposed to the sun translates directly to bigger, healthier roots and tubers at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kwɔlɔ (aaafee mitai 2 kɛyashi 3) lɛ haa wain tsei lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa. Baai babaoo ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How deep into the ground should I push a stake to support climbing crops against heavy winds?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi tso lɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ koni manyɛ mafi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɔɔ lɛ asɛɛ kɛshi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ?

english: Stakes should be driven firmly into the solid soil near the base of the mound, at least 30 to 40 centimeters deep, so strong rains and wind don't blow the stakes over and snap the fragile vines.
ga: Esa akɛ atswa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɛŋkɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eshishinumɔ ji sɛntimitai 30 kɛyashi 40, koni nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa tsei lɛ ni amɛkumɔ wain tsei ni waaa lɛ.

english: What type of string or material is best for guiding young crop vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛɛ kpãa loo nibii ni sa kɛha wain tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to use soft, natural materials like jute, banana fiber, or soft cotton twine. These natural materials do not trap high heat from the sun and will not slice into tender plant stems.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ jute, banana fiber, loo cotton kpãai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baatsu nii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni efoŋ tsei akutsei bibii lɛ amli

english: Why do the synthetic plastic strings I use to tie my yam vines to stakes seem to scorch and burn the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plastic kpã ni akɛfee nibii ni mikɛfiɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni eshãa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Dark or synthetic plastic strings heat up rapidly under intense tropical sunshine. When wrapped tightly against young, tender vine stems, the stored heat bakes the plant tissue, causing scorched or burnt spots.
ga: Plastic loo tsɔne ni akɛfee tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli edɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ abɔle wain tso bibioo ko tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni ato lɛ baashã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa shãa loo shãa baa.

english: How tightly should I tie a young crop vine to a support stake?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ miwein tsei bibii lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ ahe waa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ties should always be loose, ideally tied in a figure-eight loop. This leaves plenty of room for the vine stem to thicken as it grows without being choked or cut by the string.
ga: Esa akɛ tai lɛ afee mlɛo be fɛɛ be. Esa akɛ akpɛtɛ he yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ ŋmeii kpaanyɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo baaha wain tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni edaa lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko ŋmɛɛɛ lɛ loo efolɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Do crop vines climb up stakes on their own, or do I need to wrap them in a specific direction?
ga: Ani wain tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kwɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo esa akɛ mabɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ?

english: Vines will naturally twining upward, but guiding them helps. Different yam varieties twist naturally either clockwise or counter-clockwise; guiding them in their natural direction ensures they grip the stake firmly without snapping.
ga: Wein tsei lɛ baatsɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi amɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa. Atomɔ henɔi srɔtoi baatsɔ amɛhe kɛya ŋmɛlɛtswaa gbɛ nɔ loo yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa gbɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkuuu.

english: Why do the tips of my young crop vines wither and turn brown during very hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwein tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young vine tips are soft and hold lots of moisture. In extreme sun, heat radiating from bare dry soil or hot tying materials causes the shoot to lose water faster than the roots can supply it, causing scorched tips.
ga: Wein tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nibii krokomɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji naagbee ni eshã.

english: Is it safe to reuse old plastic ropes and dried branches from last season's crop for new yam vines?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ plastic tsɔne momo kɛ tsei niji ni egbi ni jɛ nyɔŋ ni ho lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛdu sweet potato wain tsei heei?

english: Old wooden stakes are fine if they are sturdy and free of termites, but old plastic strings often deteriorate under the sun and can harbor fungal diseases or pests from the previous crop that harm new shoots.
ga: Tsoi ni akɛfee ŋtayaai momo lɛ hi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wa ni ŋmeii bɛ mli. Shi plastic kpã momo lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei awui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tsei miida Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under young leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baa lɛ mligbalamɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. The plant becomes stressed and drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight in and helps keep the pods dry to prevent fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe ni aaafolɔ babaoo lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi koni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long due to poor drainage or heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised ridges helps excess water drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu yucca yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the hot ground and spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ ni egbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ aná nɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily as soon as the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛtsiimɔ pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily get damaged by underground worms or strong winds. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden pole supports the heavy weight of the growing bunch.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ shishitoo ni tsii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally traps nitrogen gas from the air and puts it back into the soil. Planting them restores soil fertility naturally for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that aggressively compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients. If weeds aren't removed, they steal the nutrients before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does my rice crop start turning pale green when the water level in the field drops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice roots rely on standing water to easily absorb nitrogen from the soil. When the soil dries out, the roots struggle to feed, causing the green color to fade.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ damɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna niyenii. fade ŋmɔ lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops wither and die after I water them with muddy stream water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji fɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dirty or silt-heavy water carries fine mud and chemicals that coat plant roots and block soil pores. This stops the roots from absorbing oxygen and clean moisture, causing the crops to choke and dry up even though they are wet.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo sũ ni tsii lɛ mli muji kpakpai kɛ tsofai ni haa tsei shishifãi ahe ni tsiɔ sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ.

english: Why are my crops growing so weakly on land where the topsoil was dug up and removed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa ŋwɛi sũ lɛ nɔ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Topsoil is the dark upper layer where almost all plant nutrients and organic matter live. When topsoil is removed, crops are left in deep subsoil or gravel that cannot hold water or feed the plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ji ŋwɛi fã ni yɔɔ duŋ ni tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Ashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ loo tɛ ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu loo aha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the plants look tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Nakai ŋmei tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ baai?

english: When soil is compacted or degraded, cassava plants spend all their energy just trying to survive above ground. Instead of storing extra food in plump tubers, the roots stay thin, hard, and woody.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etsilɛ loo efite lɛ Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛkɛ ni ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii krokomɛi baato bulbs ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe wa, ni amɛfeɔ tsei.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen. When the ground is depleted, the maize plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee lɛ, Abele juɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the base when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When heavy water sits on the field without draining, the roots drown and soil fungi attack the weak stem, causing the plant to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu afua nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ fitemɔ

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the land first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting like natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences severe heat or water stress, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying before conditions improve.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he dani shihilɛi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the roots of my cocoa trees starting to show above the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away bare topsoil if there are no cover crops or leaf mulch to break the force of the water droplets and hold the earth in place.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ ni baatsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewalɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the edges of my yam leaves turning brown and scorched even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shãa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Scorched leaf edges often mean the soil contains harmful toxins or high salt levels from environmental disturbance. The roots absorb these substances, which burn the edges of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmei ni jɛɔ shihilɛ mli nibii ni gbaa mɔ naa lɛ amli lɛ fa babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nibii nɛɛ, ni shãa baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and break easily when all the large shade trees around my farm are cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkuɔ oya be mli ni tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Ajie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii?

english: Plantains have soft, heavy leaves that need protection from harsh sunlight and strong winds. Shade trees create a moist, sheltered environment that keeps plantain leaves healthy and upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tsii ni he hiaa ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and scorch when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burnt under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh sun, cooling the soil, and keeping moisture in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Yellowing along the main stem of lower maize leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps fix this.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm during the first month make my crops grow so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops need all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients they can get to build strong roots. Weeds grow fast and steal these resources away, starving your crop during its most important growth period.
ga: Tsei bibii hia nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small fruits when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to gather sun and food to produce large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa hulu la kɛ niyenii anaa koni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko kɛmiitsɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Spraying an approved insecticide or neem extract early into the plant funnel stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ mli mra koni akɛkpa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This provides free natural plant food for your maize and keeps the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-corn. ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and uneven watering. Regular watering and adding organic compost or lime to the soil helps the fruit form properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ organic compost loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by them. Controlling these small insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant producing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to germinate if they absorb moisture or get damaged by insects like weevils during storage. Drying seeds thoroughly and keeping them in sealed containers with ash protects them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni akɛ sũ ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why is it better to clear my weed-covered land by hand instead of burning it before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ niji aaatsi shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaashã dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the soil that feed your crops. Clearing by hand and leaving the cleared plant matter to rot naturally creates a protective cover that traps soil moisture and acts as natural fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Nine ni akɛjieɔ tsei ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper crops very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and few fruits. Giving them enough space allows air to flow, reduces disease spread, and helps each plant grow larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ pepper tsei bua amɛhe naa lɛ, amɛshiɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua tso fɛɛ tso ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves regain their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense heat to protect themselves and reduce water evaporation. As long as the soil has sufficient moisture, the leaves will naturally relax and uncurl as the evening cools down.
ga: Shi oyitsɔi lɛ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ mli koni ebu ehe ni eha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛhaa amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: When is the safest and best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that rain doesn't waste it?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akafee yaka?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination. You should avoid putting fertilizer on dry soil or right before a heavy rainstorm, which can wash the nutrients away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba. ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ mli

english: What causes small green caterpillars to chew holes in the inner leaves of my maize, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize shoots. Applying recommended organic treatments or targeted sprays directly into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning kills the larvae before they ruin the farm.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni gbeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my green tomato fruits develop flat black rotten spots at the bottom end before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ dani ahoo.
