english: This problem is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding agricultural lime or wood ash improves calcium uptake and keeps fruits healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata he lɛ, ehaa calcium lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and quickly removing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are growing big tubers underground without digging them all up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: When cassava plants are healthy and mature, you will often see small cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem. These soil cracks indicate that the tubers underneath are expanding and filling out properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli wa ni edara jogbaŋŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmei bibii. Efeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmiiyi mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating holes in my harvested maize grains during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye bu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils attack stored maize if the grain is not fully dry or if air leaks into the storage container. Drying your maize until the kernels are rock-hard and storing them in hermetic (airtight) bags or clean drums prevents insects from surviving.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii baatutua ŋmaa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ eho kɛtee ŋmaa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala o-abele lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee tɛ ni wa ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo baagi ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Can I actually make a good living from farming if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ oyɔɔ lɛ, ani obaanyɛ oná shihilɛ kpakpa lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Yes, you can. By practicing intensive farming and planting high-value crops like vegetables or fruits that yield continuous harvests, even a half-acre or one-acre plot can generate steady income comparable to or higher than formal monthly salary jobs.
ga: Hɛɛ obaanyɛ, kɛtsɔ okwaayeli ni mli wa ni ooofee kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ aduawai loo aduawai ni woɔ yibii daa lɛ nɔ. Acre fã loo acre kome po baanyɛ aha shika ni yaa nɔ daa ni kɛ nitsumɔ ni awoɔ nyɔmɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why should I plant different crops like pawpaw and coconut on the same land instead of just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ papaya kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ

english: Mixing crops protects your income and maximizes your land space. Pawpaws grow fast and yield quick returns within a year, while long-term crops like coconuts take longer to mature but provide sustained income for decades without competing heavily for the same soil space when spaced properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ buɔ oshika he ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yaa hiɛ babaoo. Pawpaw daa oya ni ekuɔ esɛɛ oya yɛ afi kome mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ. Shi ehaa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ abɔ he akaŋ kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Which short-term crops can give me cash while I wait for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo baanyɛ aha mi shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ adara lɛ?

english: You can plant short-cycle crops like pawpaw, maize, pepper, or leafy vegetables between your young tree crops. These produce harvests within three to nine months, giving you regular income to support yourself and fund your farm work before the long-term trees start bearing.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ papaya, ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai yɛ odumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Enɛɛmɛi woɔ ŋmaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi nɛɛhu mli. Enɛ haa onáa shika daa ni okɛkwɛɔ ohe ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ dani tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi.

english: Are there crops that will allow me to harvest and make money every couple of weeks instead of once a year?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ko yɛ ni manyɛ makpa ni maná shika daa otsii fioo komɛi moŋ fe shikome yɛ afi mli?

english: Yes, crops like mature pawpaw, green coconuts, and vegetables can be harvested every 7 to 14 days throughout their fruiting season. This gives you regular, frequent cash flow rather than waiting for a single seasonal harvest like cocoa or grain.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ papaya ni eda, ŋmeii ni eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai daa gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha oná shika ni baa daa ni okɛbaatsu nii daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ be mli nibii ni akpaa tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmaa

english: How often can I harvest fresh coconuts once my trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmeii heei kɛji tsei lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Once mature coconut palms start bearing, new bunches ripen continuously. You can harvest mature green coconuts every 3 to 4 weeks (or roughly twice a month) year-round from the same tree.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso momo lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ, ŋmeii heei baaya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ daa otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 (loo aaafee shii enyɔ yɛ nyɔŋ mli) yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ.

english: How long does it take for a pawpaw tree to start producing fruits after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani papaya tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most improved pawpaw varieties start flowering within 4 to 5 months after transplanting and produce harvestable fruits between 8 to 11 months, making them one of the fastest fruit crops for earning income.
ga: Papaya henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaje fɔfɔii ashishi yɛ nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 5 mli beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. ni ewoɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 11 teŋ, ni no haa efeɔ yibii ni anáa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pawpaw plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-pawpaw tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pawpaw flowers may drop due to male plants that produce flowers but no fruit, lack of water during hot periods, or poor pollination. Ensuring you plant hermaphrodite (self-pollinating) varieties and watering during dry spells helps fruits form properly.
ga: Pawpaw fɔfɔi baanyɛ ajɛ tsei hii ni woɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ amli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo pollination ni ehiii Kwɛmɔ ni odu hermaphroditic henɔi. (Self-pollination) kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant pawpaw trees so they don't crowd each other out?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu pawpaw tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe?

english: Pawpaw trees should be planted about 2 meters by 2 meters (or 6 feet by 6 feet) apart. This spacing gives each tree enough room for sunlight, root growth, and air movement to prevent disease while maximizing how many plants fit on your land.
ga: Esa akɛ adu pawpaw tsei lɛ aaafee mitai 2 kɛ mitai 2 (loo ninetalɔi 6 kɛ ninetalɔi 6) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha hulu la. shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ koni helai akabote mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei ayibɔ aya hiɛ koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why are my young coconuts falling off the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Premature nut drop in coconuts is usually caused by sudden long dry spells, lack of nutrients (especially potassium), or attack by sucking bugs. Providing adequate water and mulching around the roots helps the tree hold onto its fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni egbiɔ trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ. niyenii ni esaaa (titri lɛ potassium) loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ nu mli Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil is suitable for growing fruit crops like pawpaw and coconut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ pawpaw kɛ ŋmeii adumɔ?

english: Both crops prefer deep, well-draining soil where water does not settle after heavy rain. Pawpaws suffer quickly from root rot in waterlogged land, while coconuts thrive in sandy or loamy soils with good drainage.
ga: Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni nu eshwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Pawpaws naa shishifãi ni fiteɔ oya yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ahe amanehulu. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã loo sũ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer gives the soil the food your maize needs to turn green and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmãa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker every year if I plant maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your crops by planting groundnuts or beans every other season helps the soil naturally rebuild its nutrients and stay healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ooodu yɛ be kroko mli lɛ nɔ. Be yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and turning soft under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the roots can breathe and stay dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ebɔle amɛhe. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants droop and wilt even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root diseases from fungus or bacteria in swampy soil. Planting in well-drained spots or raised beds prevents these microscopic organisms from attacking and destroying the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo bacteria shishifã hela ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ loo saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii bibii nɛɛ akatutua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkafite amɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes and powdery brown dirt in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the leaves. Inspecting your farm early in the season and applying suitable pest treatments early prevents these caterpillars from destroying the growing tips of your plants.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akafite otsei lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the plant sap, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early keeps the leaves flat, healthy, and able to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Tsei nɛɛ mra baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe awa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa plants from heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa.

english: Why do experience farmers tell me to plant cowpeas together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ afee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into soil food that maize can use. Planting them together feeds your maize naturally, covers the ground to stop weeds, and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ sũ ni ŋmãa baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Mulch koni egbe jwɛi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to clear tall grass and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Keeping vines on stakes off the wet ground also protects leaves from soil diseases and helps produce bigger yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to grow strong and produce large bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsoi krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara waa ni ewo tsei babaoo.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs from the soil to stay green and grow strong grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect attacks like mirids, causing the tree to save energy by shedding blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli haomɔ mli. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ tamɔ pollen Ha tsei lɛ ahere hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when fields stay waterlogged during heavy rains, allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hei komɛi edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over during high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that get weakened by pests like nematodes or stem borers, making the heavy plant lose its grip in the soil when strong winds blow.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus transmitted by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from young leaves, causing them to twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why are my planted yam setts taking so long to sprout out of the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-sweet potatoes ni midu lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam setts remain dormant underground until the soil receives enough rain and moisture to signal to the tuber that it is safe to break dormancy and sprout.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulb lɛ ale akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ebaafo wɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni pepper ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot temperatures combined with dry soil cause pepper plants stress, forcing them to drop flowers to preserve water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fata he. Nyɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ajie amɛ koni akɛto nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is a purple-flowered weed causing my maize crop to dry up and stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ miiha mi-ŋmã lɛ miigbi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: That purple weed is likely Striga (witchweed), a parasite that attaches its roots directly to maize roots to steal water and nutrients from your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji Striga (witchweed), ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In strong heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, so the plant temporarily droops to conserve moisture until the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are the bottom fronds of my oil palm trees turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom fronds on oil palms are a sign of potassium or magnesium deficiency in the soil, which the tree needs to build healthy green leaves and fruit bunches.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium loo magnesium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tso lɛ awo baai eŋɔli kɛ aduawai akui ni mli wa.

english: How much fertilizer do I actually need to put on my corn farm to get a good harvest?
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ enyiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe hiaa ni mikɛfata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Corn needs specific nutrients based on your soil type and growth stage. While standard advice often suggests 2 to 4 bags per acre, doing a quick soil check or consulting your local extension agent helps you apply just the right amount so you don't waste money.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ he miihia ŋmãa ni damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ bɔ ni edaa lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋaawoi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ awo kotokui 2 kɛyashi 4 yɛ acre kome mli moŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa oya loo mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooobi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okɛ nɔ ni sa lɛ atsu nii. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ofite shika

english: Is it true that using more bags of fertilizer will always give me a bigger corn yield?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba be fɛɛ be?

english: No, adding extra fertilizer does not automatically mean a bigger harvest. Crops can only absorb a certain amount of nutrients, and applying too much can actually burn the roots, pollute the soil, and waste your hard-earned money.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baajɛ mli aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mujiwoo ni okɛ shika ni okɛtsu nii waa lɛ baafite

english: Should I apply all my fertilizer at once when planting maize, or split it into different times?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ shikome kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo yɛ bei srɔtoi amli?

english: It is best to split your fertilizer application into at least two stages—a small amount at or shortly after planting to help roots grow, and a second application a few weeks later when the stalks grow rapidly to support strong cobs.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo fãi enyɔ mli. Eji nɔ ko fioo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ loo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa oya koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni he wa lɛ.

english: How do I know if the chemical seller's advice on fertilizer amounts is right for my specific land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsofa-kɛ-ŋma hɔlɔlɔ lɛ ŋaawoi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ he lɛ sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Chemical sellers often give general recommendations meant to sell inputs, but your land's fertility might be different. Your local extension officer can help tailor the input amount to your soil condition and budget so you avoid overusing fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma hɔɔlɔi haa ŋaawoo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ he. Shi ekolɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii babaoo ehaa lɛ yɛ srɔto. Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛtsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ kɛ shika ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee. Bɔni afee ni akakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo atsu nii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves start turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrients out of the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow better after I put it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants by supplying vital nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These nutrients help crops build strong roots, grow sturdy green stalks, and produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei, ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium haa. Nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ tsei eŋɔli ni mli wa. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin but end up producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Corn grows tall and thin with small cobs when plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen without enough sunlight and other balanced nutrients to support cob development.
ga: Abele daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛná nitrogen babaoo tsɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni ja bɛ mli. Koni eye ebua COB lɛ shweremɔ

english: Why do commercial farms seem to produce so much more corn than small family farms in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jarayeli ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe weku ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Commercial farms often achieve higher yields because they combine proper seed spacing, timely weed management, and correct fertilizer rates tailored to their soil, rather than relying on fertilizer alone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ejaakɛ amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ mli. Jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ nɔ

english: What happens to my maize crops if I apply fertilizer at the wrong time of the season?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli?

english: If you apply fertilizer too early or during heavy rainfall, the nutrients wash away before roots can grab them. If applied too late, the plant will use the energy for leaf growth instead of filling out the corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii blɛoo tsɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baa moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ baafata he.

english: Does spacing my corn seeds properly affect how well the crop uses fertilizer?
ga: Ani mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ he?

english: Yes, proper seed spacing ensures each plant has enough root space and light to absorb nutrients effectively. When crops are crowded, they compete for the fertilizer you applied, leading to weaker plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shishifãi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants recover their dark green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Koolooi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In very hot weather, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. As long as the soil is moist and the plants stand back up in the cool evening, they are just naturally protecting themselves from the heat.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛmiibu amɛhe kɛmiijɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. The plants waste all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of using that energy to produce big grains or fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ beni amɛdaraa koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ woɔ wuhi aloo yiblii nguanguahi.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, leaving extra plant food behind for your maize crop during the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ shĩɔ tsei niyenii yɛ sɛɛ kɛha o-maise lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves to drink the plant's juices. They leave behind a sugary liquid that attracts insects and causes mold to grow on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Amɛshiɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni gbalaa kooloi ni haa ŋmeii baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot move enough calcium from the soil into the growing fruit. Irregular watering causes this, so keeping the soil steadily moist helps the fruit develop normally.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat, sudden dry spells, or too much water. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its remaining energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo nu babaoo yɛ Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young mango trees drop many of their small fruits shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwo lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Trees produce thousands of flowers, but they often shed extra small fruits if they do not have enough water or nutrients to grow all of them. Watering the tree during the fruit-setting stage helps it hold onto more fruits.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛfɔɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ womɔ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii babaoo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry gap before the main rains begin. If your seeds sprout after that first rain and the soil dries up again, the delicate young sprouts will burn and die in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ekoŋŋ. Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil quickly when I leave them stacked together inside a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still alive and need cool, moving air to stay healthy. Stacking them in a hot, dark room traps heat and moisture, creating the perfect environment for rot and fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ehe miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ ehe koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, helping young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Look at the small buds or leaf nodes along the cassava stem. These nodes should always point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down prevents proper growth and lowers your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo baai lɛ. along the cassava stem Esa akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ odu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, etsĩɔ dalɛ ni sa naa, ni ehaa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to drive long wooden stakes into the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves toward the sun. Lifting the vines off the ground allows maximum sunlight contact, which helps the plant store energy and grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa enáa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ehaa bulb lɛ daa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or a deficiency in soil nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their flowers without producing pods when the dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers as a survival mechanism during sudden dry spells to conserve water. Maintaining soil moisture helps the flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) protects it from direct sun heat, holds moisture in the ground longer, and stops weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the main stem can burn the tender plant tissue and damage the feeding roots beneath the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi ni yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my crops give me smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing seedlings compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are small worms eating the rolled leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni abɔle amɛhe yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the leaf whorl of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves, which weakens the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Even with enough rain, plants cannot thrive if the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use poultry manure instead of buying expensive chemical fertilizers for my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Yes, poultry manure is a great low-cost alternative. It enriches the soil with essential nutrients and improves its ability to hold water, though it should be dried or rotted before application to avoid burning plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ashishifã ji nɔ ko ni jara waaa kwraa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ agbi loo egbo dani akɛtsu nii koni akashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ.

english: Is it effective to place a tiny bottle-cap amount of fertilizer directly next to each plant instead of spreading it across the whole field?
ga: Ani ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ni jɛɔ tɔ mli lɛ baawo emasɛi? tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, this method is called micro-dosing. It allows you to use much less fertilizer while ensuring the plant roots get the exact nutrients they need without wasting money on the spaces between crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mikrodosing. Enɛ haa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ohaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni ofiteee shika yɛ he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he.

english: Will planting my cassava or maize closer together give me a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Ani ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni madu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that stored nitrogen without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: How can I keep my vegetable soil moist during dry spells without buying expensive watering equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha aduawai ashikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni miheee nu ni jara wa?

english: You can cover the soil around your plants with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks. This technique, called mulching, shields the ground from direct sunlight and stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tso shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ ŋaa nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya

english: Why shouldn't I apply my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away expensive fertilizer from the root zone into streams or deep into the subsoil before plants can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the warm, wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive and reproduce rapidly in warm, humid conditions because tender plant growth and moisture provide abundant food and ideal breeding conditions for pests.
ga: Koolooi daraa ni amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my main crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to suck up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing the soil gives dormant weed seeds the light they need to sprout quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ woɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Eyɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or irregular feeding. When the plant feels stressed, it drops blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ ni esaaa lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why should I set aside some of my best harvested maize seeds to store for next season instead of selling everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato mi-ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ eko he gbɛjianɔ koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Saving high-quality seeds ensures you have reliable planting material for the next season without spending money. Healthy, mature saved seeds retain strong traits that help them germinate well and produce a good harvest when planted again.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtoɔ lɛ haa onáa dumɔ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni okɛ shikatoohe lɛ fiteee. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɛɔ sui ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I store my harvested grains so that insects do not destroy them before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite amɛ dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Drying your grains thoroughly in the sun until they are hard, then storing them in airtight containers or hermetic bags prevents moisture and air from getting in. This stops weevils and insects from breeding and destroying your food and seed supply.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛkafite oniyenii kɛ dumɔwui jɛɛhei lɛ.

english: If I only have a small amount of fertilizer, is it better to share it among all my crops or give a lot to just a few?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ Ani ehi akɛ majara miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ loo maha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛkɛ?

english: Giving a small, recommended amount to each plant gives all your crops an equal chance to grow well. Putting too much fertilizer on a few plants can burn their roots, while leaving the rest without nutrients lowers your total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ha fioo taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ aná hegbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei komɛi amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛshishifãi lɛ. yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ ashi fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is a natural reaction that helps the plant save water and protect itself during dry weather.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up when planted in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct, hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a shelter, protecting the young trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni ahiɔ Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow better when I plant cowpeas around them instead of leaving the soil bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Cowpeas act as a living blanket that covers the ground to trap soil moisture and stop weeds. They also fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the cassava plants and helps them form bigger tubers.
ga: Cowpeas tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. Ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ hu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛyitsei wuji.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures every plant gets enough food to grow strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer groundnuts when I plant them in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every year drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating groundnuts with crops like maize keeps the soil healthy and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra branches on my tomato plants when they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi dalɛ pɛ?

english: Pruning extra side branches directs the plant's energy and food into growing larger, healthier tomatoes rather than wasting energy on growing leaves that do not produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ aya hiɛ koni etsɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ baai ni wooo yibii lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yam tubers so they don't rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: When the leaves and vines of the yam plant turn yellow and dry up naturally, it means the tuber has finished growing and storing nutrients. Harvesting at this stage prevents the tubers from rotting or being eaten by pests in the soil.
ga: Beni sweet potato tso lɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, agbe ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni amɛto niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekafite loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ akaye amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a signal that the soil is running out of nitrogen. Maize plants move the remaining nitrogen to their newest top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Shi shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and big cobs, they stretch upwards competing for sunlight.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ a he kɛ ha hulu la ɔ he akaŋ.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells cause severe stress to tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and moisture for its own survival instead of making fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do the small green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: This is typically caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod Disease, which spreads easily in damp, shady conditions. It attacks the young cocoa pods and cuts off their nutrients, causing them to blacken and die.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela. Ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Etutuaa kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli. Enɛ haa efeɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy, water-filled stems. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the center of gravity shifts, easily pulling the shallow roots out of the soil unless supported with strong wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ, ŋwɛi hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baatsake. Ehaa anyɛɔ ajieɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ja tso nibii ni he wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why does my yam crop produce small tubers if I let the vines trail on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii kɛji miha wain tso lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ stake?

english: Yam leaves need to spread high up in full sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking holds the leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni akɛha sweet potato tso lɛ niyenii. Staking lɛ haa baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains creates a cool, humid environment that shields the young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying even though the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli efɔ lɛ?

english: Too much water in the soil drowns the plant roots by cutting off oxygen. Damp conditions also attract soil fungi that rot the roots, leaving the plant unable to drink water despite wet soil.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hu gbalaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni kɛ shishifãi fiteɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ anu nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain leaves soil waterlogged for long periods, micro-organisms multiply in the trapped water and decay the starch in the cassava tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baafa babaoo yɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli. ni efoɔ starch ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have larger, wild root systems that absorb water and plant food faster than cultivated crops. When you apply fertilizer, the weeds eat first unless you clear them out before feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni dara, ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baaye nii klɛŋklɛŋ. Ja ojie amɛ dani okɛ niyenii ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves their dark green color back so they can make energy for big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baatsake baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ ni ekɛbaahã ŋmɔtɔi wuji lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium or when watering is inconsistent. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots pull up calcium from the soil into the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya tomato ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft growing centers of maize plants. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended biopesticides into the central whorl of the leaf early on stops them before they ruin the crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni he wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes gives them maximum light and keeps leaves dry, which prevents leaves from rotting or catching diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ená la babaoo ni eha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite loo hela akamɔ amɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the roots cool, conserves moisture, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Koni nu akafee oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ Ekwɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the dry bush on my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei ni egbi ni yɔɔ midumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ?

english: Burning kills essential organisms in the soil and destroys organic matter that naturally feeds crops. Clearing without burning allows dead vegetation to rot back into the soil, keeping it rich and moist for longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni egboi lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ni oooha efee nii babaoo ni ehiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my plot before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same plot later, the maize feeds on this leftover natural fertilizer and grows much better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off without turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when trees are stressed by lack of water, too much sun, or a lack of soil nutrients. Shade trees and rich soil keep the tree cool and hydrated, giving the flowers a better chance to form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. hulu la ni fa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛfeɔ pods ni mli wa.

english: As cassava plants age past their ideal maturity point, they stop storing soft starch and begin converting it into tough wood fibers. Harvesting cassava at the right time—usually between 9 and 12 months—ensures roots stay soft and easy to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fe he ni sa akɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mlimɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa. Cassava ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli Be nɛɛ (bei pii lɛ, eyɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehoomɔ waaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to keep your harvest healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ anɔ.

english: Is it better to clear my land by burning the bush or by cutting it down?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaajie shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ashãa loo ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cutting the bush down and leaving it to rot naturally is much better for your farm. Burning destroys valuable organic nutrients in the topsoil, whereas decaying plant material acts as natural fertilizer.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni ooofo mli ni oha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ hi kwraa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: This is called Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady conditions. You can reduce it by pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods off the tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ okɛba shi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ooofolɔ koni hulu la aba mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when the seeds have sprouted, and the second round when the maize reaches knee-height. This ensures the plant gets nutrients exactly when it is growing fastest.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ beni amɛdaraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball. If it holds its shape slightly but crumbles easily when poked, it has the right balance of moisture and air for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ su ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fioo shi efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa baahi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Insects like weevils thrive in moist grain. Make sure your maize is fully dried in the sun before storing it in clean, sealed airtight bags or raised storage structures kept off the damp ground.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛwo vacuum bag ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni awo nɔ ni akɛtoɔ kpo nɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam seed tubers need continuous moisture to break out of dormancy and sprout roots. If you plant too early before steady rain, the hot, dry soil can cause the seed tuber to rot or dry out.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe miihia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛje shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings fall over and die shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil fungus disease known as 'damping-off', which happens when seedling beds are overwatered or planted too closely together. Giving seedlings space and avoiding excess water helps them stay upright.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping-off’ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa kɛji dumɔwui asaji lɛ amli nu fa tsɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any peppers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani eduɔ pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat and lack of water as a survival reaction. Watering them regularly at the roots during dry periods stops the flowers from falling off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he akɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shishigbɛ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans in the same field as my corn instead of planting corn alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa kɛkɛ?

english: Beans and corn are good partners because beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the corn. Planting them together gives you two harvests from one plot while keeping your soil healthy.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmãa ji hefatalɔi kpakpai ejaakɛ ŋmãa jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha oná nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do bean plants improve the soil for other crops growing next to them?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Bean plants have tiny bumps on their roots that work with natural soil organisms to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food. When the bean roots and leaves decay, that food stays in the soil for crops like corn to feed on.
ga: Bean tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Beni ŋmeii shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei tamɔ ŋmei aye.

english: Why is it harmful to grow the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to multiply in that field. Rotating different crops breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a corn plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Even if there is enough water, the plant turns yellow when the soil lacks the nutrients required to stay green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Kɛji nu ni fa yɛ po Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara.

english: What will happen to my corn plants if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If corn plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, tall, and weak, producing very small ears or no ears at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ, amɛkwɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛtoi bibii waa loo amɛbɛ toi kwraa.

english: Why do my corn plants stop producing good corn ears when a dry spell hits during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kpa ŋmãa toi kpakpai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ kɛ́ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flowering is the critical moment when corn forms silks and pollen to create grains. Drought at this stage stresses the plant, causing the silks to dry up before pollen can reach them, which leads to empty or incomplete cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be ni he hiaa waa ni ŋmãa feɔ siliki kɛ pollen ni ekɛfeɔ dumɔwui. Nɛkɛ hɔmɔ be nɛɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani pollen lɛ shɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ efolo loo eshɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted during the middle of a hot day even if the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: During peak heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily as a natural reaction to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers in the evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni baabu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to your local soil, so they absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds. They sprout quickly to cover the ground and steal sunlight before your crops get a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛju hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What causes small green worms to hide and eat inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Hiɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli.

english: Those are typically fall armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. The young caterpillars crawl deep into the tight funnel of the corn plant because it offers soft leaves to feed on and shelters them from heat and birds.
ga: Amɛ ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji ni ŋmeii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ baa nɔ lɛ mli. Kplukai bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is moist enough to plant seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil taken from a few inches deep into a ball. If it holds its shape comfortably without dripping water or crumbling into dry powder, the soil has the right amount of moisture for your seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni ajie kɛjɛ inchi fioo komɛi amli lɛ mli owo bɔɔlu mli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee shi loo efoŋ ni efee powda ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of rice seeds available in Ghana, and how do I choose the right one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ Ghana lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmaa ni sa?

english: Different rice varieties are bred for specific soil types, water levels, and weather conditions in Ghana. Choosing the right one depends on whether your land gets flooded, receives low rainfall, or if you want a variety that local buyers prefer for cooking.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli ŋmãa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ naa. Kɛji nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo, loo oosumɔ srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛhoo nii lɛ nɔ, ni obaahala nɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if a specific crop variety will grow well in the northern part of Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso pɔtɛɛ ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: Northern Ghana has a shorter rainy season and hotter conditions, so agricultural officers recommend crop varieties that are drought-tolerant and mature quickly before the dry season starts.
ga: Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be kuku kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ ahe ŋaa dani hɔmɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds every season instead of re-using seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i ngɔ ngɛ ye nyagbe ngmami ɔ mi ɔ tsu ní ekohu.

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred to produce uniform, high-yielding crops that resist local diseases. Re-using seeds from previous harvests causes the crop to lose those strong qualities, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be, ni helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛye nɔ lɛ aba. Dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ jeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some types of rice take longer to mature than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Rice varieties have different natural growth cycles. Quick-maturing varieties take about 90 to 100 days and help avoid dry spells, while longer-maturing varieties take up to 120 days or more but often yield more grains if rain is steady.
ga: Omɔ henɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoi srɔtoi. Nibii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ heɔ aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 100 ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ gbii 120 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Shi esumɔɔ ni ewo dumɔwui babaoo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ daa.

english: Why do my rice crops sometimes produce empty heads with no grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ woɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice grains, or chaffiness, usually happen when the plant experiences severe heat or dry weather right when it is flowering, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen during grain development.
