ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Rice plants fall over (called lodging) when their stems are too weak to support heavy grain heads. This happens if too much nitrogen fertilizer was used, if plants were sown too close together, or if you planted a tall variety in a windy area.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ shĩai) kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛji oodu tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa.

english: What causes the leaves of my young crops to turn yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that too much standing water is suffocating the roots. Poor root drainage stops the plant from absorbing nutrients, making the leaves lose their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do some rice varieties need a flooded field while others can grow on dry land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsɔ nu awo ŋmãa henɔi komɛi anɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ adu srɔtoi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties are built to survive in deep water and flooded valleys, whereas upland rice varieties have deep root systems designed to extract moisture from drier, rain-fed soil on higher ground.
ga: Abɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu ni mli kwɔ kɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa henɔi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee koni ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔji ni egbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can planting improved seed varieties help me deal with unpredictable rains in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni manyɛ madamɔ Ghana nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ naa?

english: Improved varieties are developed by scientists to withstand dry spells, so even if the rains stop unexpectedly for a few weeks, the crop can survive and still give you a decent harvest.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efee tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsii fioo komɛi po lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni eha bo yibii kpakpai lolo.

english: Why does my neighbor get a bigger yield than me even though we planted the exact same crop variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ tsei kome pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ?

english: Yield depends on more than just the seed variety; differences in soil fertility, water management, land preparation, and planting timing between farms strongly affect how much a crop produces.
ga: Yibiiwoo damɔ nɔ ni fe dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛkɛ nɔ. Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu he nitsumɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔ be mli yɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ waa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. Heavy rain can wash this nutrient away, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest groundnuts, that trapped food stays behind in the ground and acts as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle harsh, direct sun without getting scorched. Tall shade trees act as umbrellas to keep the cocoa cool and hold moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãaa amɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo koni eha kookoo lɛ mli ajɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni miida yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main trunk. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main plant to grow big bunches of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ plantains ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing big even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi miŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively take soil nutrients, sunlight, and space away from your crops. Even with enough rain, your crops will struggle because the weeds are stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii po miihoso ejaakɛ jwɛi miiju amɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight on their leaves to feed the growing yam tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and keeps them away from damp ground where pests and diseases live.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaa lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ebaaha tso lɛ akabote hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ ahi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed, usually due to irregular watering, extreme sun heat, or tiny insect attacks. Keeping the soil evenly damp and controlling pests helps the flowers form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ waa. aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ lɛ yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do many tiny cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still small on the cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods often blacken because of fungal diseases encouraged by too much shade and wet weather, or because the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot feed. Trimming thick branches helps air and sun dry out dampness that causes pod rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli baa lɛ hewɔ. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni adebɔɔ nyɛŋ aha niyenii aha lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni mli tse lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la, ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and shrinking during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. This weakens the leaves, which reduces the size of the cassava roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baa shi.

english: When water sits in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing them to suffocate and decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many thick leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse waa shi eshishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: When cowpea gets too much nitrogen from the soil, it spends all its energy growing green leaves instead of flowers and pods. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers encourages cowpea to produce more flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawo cowpea hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the canopy, which helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli gĩɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long or when fungal rot is present in damp soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, protecting the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji ŋmeii fite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. koni akɛbu shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a reaction to hot weather, irregular watering, or viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Putting straw mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and reduces heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa, jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells or when insects attack the young buds. Providing shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the cocoa tree retain its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa hiŋmɛii bibii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their tiny fruits before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Peppers drop young fruit when soil water levels change too drastically from dry to wet, or when temperatures get too high. Watering the plants consistently keeps the fruit attached to the plant.
ga: Chili ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ akpɛtɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why does my maize produce small cobs with missing grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni dumɔwui komɛi fataaa he?

english: Missing grains occur when dry weather or heat damages the silk during pollination, preventing fertilization. Planting seeds at the correct distance apart ensures adequate airflow and pollen transfer between plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ fite siliki lɛ yɛ pollination be mli. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni sa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pollen ni sa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil is packed too hard or contains stones that block the growing tuber. Clearing stones and loosening the soil deep into mounds gives the tubers space to stretch straight and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi tsi bulbs ni miida lɛ naa. Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni da ni ja.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up from the bottom moving upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: The yellowing of lower leaves can be a sign that the plant lacks potassium or is infected by a soil fungus affecting root intake. Clearing old yellow leaves and adding wood ash or potassium fertilizer strengthens the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni miigba shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ajie baai momo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ tso sũ loo potassium ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plants need sunlight, water, and food from the soil to grow well. If you plant them too close, they fight each other for these resources, leading to thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrition to produce full cobs.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ sũ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji odu amɛ obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi yɛ nibii nɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo cob ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant plantains on my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mikookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily scorched by harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves, providing temporary shade and keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Ha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks key nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color so the plant can make food and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are small worms eating the centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central leaf whorls of young maize. Catching them early and applying recommended pesticides or neem solutions prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa bibii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet and humid weather. Trimming extra branches to let in air and sunlight, removing infected pods, and spraying fungicides will help protect your healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my previous maize harvest to plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested seeds from hybrid crop varieties lose their yield potential in the second generation, producing weaker plants and smaller cobs. Purchasing fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong growth and higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the main stems become brown and thick. Digging up just one sample plant near the edges of your plot can help you confirm if the tubers are full and mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ otsa tso kome ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oma nɔ mi kɛji bulb lɛ edara ni edara.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruits when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper fertilization. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally sheds its flowers to save energy until temperatures become cooler.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to rapidly absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and fertilizer from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for crops. Adding fertilizer or animal manure restores soil nutrients so the plants can regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does fertilizer actually do for my crops, and why isn't standard soil enough?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works like food supplements for plants. Over time, soil loses its natural strength through repeated farming, so fertilizer replaces vital nutrients that crops need to yield healthy food.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni akɛfataa tsei ahe. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does leaving crop remains on the field after harvest help my next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving old stalks and leaves to rot naturally feeds organic matter back into the ground, restoring soil fertility and strength for the next crop without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei kɛ baai momoi lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ kɛba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my tomato leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Excess moisture creates wet conditions where fungal diseases easily infect plants. The black spots are a sign of fungal sickness, which can be controlled by proper plant spacing and fungicides.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yeɔ tsei anɔ oya. He ni yɔɔ diŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadi. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and get scorched by intense tropical sun. They require shade trees like plantains or bananas to act as protective umbrellas until their root systems grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do cassava leaves curl up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water and surviving drought. The plant goes quiet above ground while protecting its roots and tubers until the rain comes back.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashwieɔ lɛ ji ŋmei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he ni ejoɔ hɔmɔ naa foi. Tso lɛ baafee dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water directly from your crops' roots, effectively starving your plants of the food they need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply extra fertilizer beyond what the instruction guide recommends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ nii woɔ mli fe bɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ?

english: Just like taking too much human medicine causes sickness, applying excessive fertilizer burns plant roots and damages the soil structure instead of making crops grow faster.
ga: Taakɛ tsofai babaoo ni ayeɔ yɛ adesai amli lɛ kɛ hela baa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, eshãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei adara oya

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and lower leaves from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary leaves forces the plant to send its food strength directly into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra branches.
ga: Baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ niji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ

english: Why do crops planted from certified government seeds grow better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ amli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist local diseases, handle heat better, and use soil nutrients more efficiently, resulting in healthier plants and bigger yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. It can also happen when the soil stays too soaked after heavy rains, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Heavy rain will wash away your expensive fertilizer off the field or push it too deep into the dirt where your crop's roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist but heavy rain is not falling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ebaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo shi nugbɔ enɛko waa.

english: Why are there little caterpillars eating holes inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the young growing center of maize plants. They hide deep inside the leaves to feed on the tender growth, which can destroy the plant if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye gbekɛbii ni daraa lɛ, ni baanyɛ akpata tso lɛ hiɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that sit under the leaves and suck out the plant's juices. They can also pass viral diseases to the plant, which causes the foliage to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni shwereɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ hu amɛshwã tsei ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees provide natural shade and protect young cocoa from drying out in the heat until the plants are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ latsaa be mli kɛyashi tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: When too many small shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong ones, which helps the main tree produce much larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni bɔle dumɔwu kome he lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ niji ni dara kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant gets stressed by too much heat or dry soil, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Beni hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi fe nine lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their crop roots with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so the soil stays wet longer. It also blocks weeds from growing and slowly rots into natural food for the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ Decay ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots run out of air and suffocate. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni no haa amɛmuɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do I harvest less grain every year when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa ŋmaa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot season after season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the land and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why did my rice crop dry up and produce empty husks when the rains stopped early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa oya lɛ?

english: Rice plants need a steady supply of water, especially during the flowering and grain-filling stages. If the soil dries out during this critical period, the plant becomes stressed and stops forming grains in order to save itself, leaving you with empty husks.
ga: Nu he miihia omɔ tsei daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ be mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa dumɔwui ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa ehe lɛ feemɔ. Eshiɔ bo kɛ ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why am I getting a much smaller harvest from my land now than I used to get five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ nɔ babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bianɛ fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same land without adding nutrients or giving the soil a rest drains the earth of essential plant foods. Over time, the soil becomes tired and depleted, resulting in smaller harvests each year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo daa afi.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow before they even produce any food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ewo niyenii po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that its roots are being damaged by waterlogging or pests. Without green leaves, the plant cannot catch sunlight to make food for growth.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu loo kooloi ni yeɔ awui efite eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛji baai eŋɔli bɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over time and can carry hidden diseases from the previous season. Certified seeds are specially selected to grow strong, resist local diseases, tolerate dry spells better, and produce higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ Eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small grains when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛdumɔwui bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light instead of spending energy on growing thick stems and heavy grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why do insects attack my farm more during hot, dry weather than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dry weather weakens plants, making them less able to naturally defend themselves. In addition, many insects look for green crops as their main source of water during dry spells, leading to heavier pest damage on your farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii babaoo kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli akɛ amɛ nu jɛɛhe titri yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo fiteɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil and turn moldy after I store it in bags at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛwo baagi mli yɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If grain is bagged before it is completely dry, moisture gets trapped inside the bag. Damp grain creates a perfect environment for mold and insects to breed, destroying your food before you can use or sell it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Moisture baatsi kotoku lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi fɔmɔ. Fitemɔ oniyenii lɛ dani okɛtsu nii loo okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant legumes like beans along with my main food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ miniyenii titri ni miduɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes have roots that can take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil as natural fertilizer. This improves soil fertility and helps feed neighboring crops while giving you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ niyenii kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaakpa.

english: How can I protect my farm from failing completely if the rains come late this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekafite kwraa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be nɛɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: You can plant early-maturing crop varieties that need less time and water to produce a harvest. Covering the soil with organic matter like dry leaves (mulching) also helps trap moisture in the ground for your crops during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni biɔ be kɛ nu fioo dani okɛkpaa lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my farm than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food and water your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Smoothing and leveling your ground allows water to spread evenly across the field so that every plant gets equal moisture, preventing some areas from drowning while others stay thirsty.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei fɛɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ haaa hei komɛi atsɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kumai yeɔ hei komɛi.

english: I heard commercial farmers use laser tools on their field, how does that technology help a farm?
ga: Minu akɛ okwaafoi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ jarayeli mli lɛ kɛ laser nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋaalee ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔji?

english: Laser land leveling precise-flattens the field, which helps save a lot of irrigation water, stops soil erosion, and makes it easier for seeds to germinate uniformly.
ga: Laser shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni haa nu babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi Ekpaa shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Does using heavy machines to clear my bush affect how the soil holds water?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ brɔshi lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he?

english: Heavy machinery can press the soil too tightly, creating a hard layer that stops rain from soaking in easily, which means you may need to loosen the soil afterward.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa ni tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekabote mli mlɛo lɛ baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ sũ lɛ atsu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What can I do to keep my crops growing during the dry season when the nearby stream starts drying up?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: You can conserve water by applying mulch around plant bases to reduce evaporation, digging shallow water retention basins, or using drip irrigation to feed water directly to roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu akafite kɛtsɔ sũ ni okɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ nɔ. tso shishitoo koni ekɛba nu ni hoɔ lɛ shi Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mlifomɔ Aloo okɛ drip irrigation atsu nii ni okɛ nu aha shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does water gather in big pools on some parts of my field and rot my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu miibua ehe naa yɛ nubui wuji amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi ni ehaa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ?

english: Water pools in low spots or heavy clay soil that lacks drainage, causing roots to suffocate without oxygen; leveling the field or digging drainage channels solves this issue.
ga: Nubu ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu bɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛ́ afee ŋmɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ loo nu homɔ gbɛi ni atsa lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.
